faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso la passive voice en inglés?
faqs.answer: Cuando el receptor de la acción es más importante que el agente, o cuando el agente es desconocido o irrelevante: The defendant was convicted of fraud.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma el passive con diferentes tiempos?
faqs.answer: Subject + be (en el tiempo correspondiente) + past participle (V3). Ejemplos: is done, was done, has been done, will be done, would have been done.

faqs.question: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre reported speech y passive reporting?
faqs.answer: Reported speech transforma una cita directa (He said, "I am innocent" → He said he was innocent). Passive reporting atribuye información a una fuente general (It is believed that... / The man is believed to be...).

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso "it is said that" vs "the man is said to"?
faqs.answer: Ambas son correctas. La primera enfatiza la información; la segunda enfatiza a la persona. La forma con "to" necesita infinitivo: is said to have done (pasado).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 52?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 52 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones.

content:
La **Unidad 52** consolida la **passive voice** en todos los tiempos, la **passive reporting** (*It is believed that… / The suspect is believed to have…*) y el **reported speech** (*He said that… / She claimed to have…*) en el contexto de la **justicia y los derechos humanos**. Estas estructuras son esenciales para expresar quién realiza una acción cuando el foco está en el receptor, o para atribuir información a fuentes sin comprometer la neutralidad. En este artículo encontrarás teoría completa con ejemplos del ámbito legal y ejercicios progresivos para dominar estas construcciones. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 52](/curso-b2/unit-52)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 51 — Wish, If Only y Third Conditional](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-51-wish-third-conditional-economy)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 53 — Modals y Phrasal Verbs](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-53-modals-phrasal-verbs-career) --- # Parte I — Teoría ## Qué aprenderás en esta unidad - Usar la **passive voice** en presente simple, pasado, futuro, perfecto, condicional y con modales en contextos de justicia y derechos humanos. - Aplicar la **passive reporting** (*It is alleged that… / The suspect is alleged to have…*) para atribuir información a fuentes en un tono formal y periodístico. - Transformar citas directas en **reported speech** con backshift de tiempos, verbos de reporte variados y estructuras de órdenes, preguntas y peticiones. - Ampliar tu vocabulario de **justicia, derechos humanos, sistema legal e derecho internacional** con más de 20 términos clave. - Desarrollar habilidades de reading, listening, writing y speaking en un contexto de tribunales, constituciones y resoluciones internacionales. ![Passive Voice y Reported Speech en inglés B2 con vocabulario de justicia y derechos humanos](/blog/curso-b2/unit-52/passive-reported-speech-map.png) --- ## Sección 1 — Passive Voice: passive en todos los tiempos La **passive voice** se usa cuando el receptor de la acción es más importante que quien la realiza, o cuando el agente es desconocido, irrelevante o deliberadamente ocultado. En contextos legales y de derechos humanos, la passive es extremadamente frecuente porque los informes judiciales, las resoluciones de tribunales y los comunicados de prensa suelen centrarse en los hechos y sus víctimas, no en los agentes. ### Estructura general **Subject + to be (en el tiempo correspondiente) + past participle (V3)** ### Present simple passive Se usa para hechos generales, procedimientos habituales o leyes vigentes. - *The defendant **is charged** with fraud.* — El acusado es acusado de fraude. - *Human rights **are protected** by the constitution.* — Los derechos humanos son protegidos por la constitución. - *Evidence **is collected** at the crime scene.* — La evidencia es recolectada en la escena del crimen. ### Past simple passive Describe acciones completadas en el pasado, como veredictos o sentencias ya dictadas. - *The law **was passed** in 2015.* — La ley fue aprobada en 2015. - *The suspect **was arrested** on Monday.* — El sospechoso fue arrestado el lunes. - *Three witnesses **were called** to testify.* — Tres testigos fueron llamados a declarar. ### Present perfect passive Enfatiza el resultado actual de una acción pasada. Muy útil en informes legales actualizados. - *The evidence **has been examined** by the court.* — La evidencia ha sido examinada por el tribunal. - *The verdict **has been announced**.* — El veredicto ha sido anunciado. - *Several amendments **have been made** to the bill.* — Se han hecho varias enmiendas al proyecto de ley. ### Future simple passive Se usa para decisiones futuras, predicciones legales o pronunciamientos pendientes. - *The verdict **will be announced** tomorrow.* — El veredicto será anunciado mañana. - *The accused **will be sentenced** next week.* — El acusado será sentenciado la próxima semana. - *New regulations **will be enforced** from January.* — Nuevas regulaciones serán aplicadas desde enero. ### Modal passive Expresa posibilidad, obligación, permiso o capacidad en forma pasiva. - *The sentence **can be reduced** with good behaviour.* — La sentencia puede ser reducida con buen comportamiento. - *Corruption **must be investigated** thoroughly.* — La corrupción debe ser investigada a fondo. - *The prisoner **may be released** on parole.* — El prisionero puede ser liberado en libertad condicional. ### Past modal passive (modal + have been + V3) Habla de obligaciones, posibilidades o críticas sobre el pasado. - *The rights **should have been respected**.* — Los derechos deberían haber sido respetados. - *The case **could have been resolved** sooner.* — El caso podría haber sido resuelto antes. - *More evidence **might have been gathered**.* — Más evidencia podría haber sido recopilada. ### Conditional passive Expresa situaciones hipotéticas o consecuencias supuestas. - *The case **would be dismissed** without evidence.* — El caso sería desestimado sin evidencia. - *The defendant **would be acquitted** if new proof emerged.* — El acusado sería absuelto si surgiera nueva prueba. ### Perfect conditional passive Habla de hipótesis sobre resultados que no ocurrieron. - *The sentence **would have been reduced** if the defendant had cooperated.* — La sentencia habría sido reducida si el acusado hubiera cooperado. - *Justice **would have been served** if the trial had been fair.* — La justicia habría sido servida si el juicio hubiera sido justo. ### Errores comunes con la passive voice | # | Error | Corrección | Explicación | |---|-------|-----------|-------------| | 1 | *The law **was passed** by government in 2015.* (sin artículo) | *The law was passed by **the** government in 2015.* | Cuando el agente va con "by", se necesita el artículo definido si se refiere a una entidad concreta. | | 2 | *The evidence **has been examine** by the court.* | *The evidence has been **examined** by the court.* | Se necesita el past participle (V3), no el infinitivo. | | 3 | *Human rights **are protect** by the constitution.* | *Human rights **are protected** by the constitution.* | Falta el pasado participio; "protect" → "protected". | | 4 | *The verdict **will announced** tomorrow.* | *The verdict **will be announced** tomorrow.* | En future passive se necesita "will + be + V3". | | 5 | *The suspect **was arrest** on Monday.* | *The suspect **was arrested** on Monday.* | Falta el pasado participio; "arrest" → "arrested". | --- ## Sección 2 — Passive Reporting La **passive reporting** atribuye información a una fuente general o impersonal sin comprometer al hablante. Es fundamental en periodismo, informes legales y comunicados oficiales. En inglés se construye de dos formas principales: ### Estructura impersonal **It + is/was + reported/said/believed/claimed/thought/expected + that + clause** - *It is said that the suspect fled the country.* — Se dice que el sospechoso huyó del país. - *It was reported that three people were injured.* — Se reportó que tres personas resultaron heridas. - *It is believed that the crime was premeditated.* — Se cree que el crimen fue premeditado. ### Estructura personal (con "to") **Subject + is/was + said/believed/reported + to + infinitive / to have + V3** Cuando la acción es pasada, se usa **to have + past participle**. - *The suspect **is said to have fled** the country.* — Se dice que el sospechoso huyó del país. - *The man **is believed to be** connected to the crime.* — Se cree que el hombre está conectado con el crimen. - *The victim **was reported to have died** at the scene.* — Se reportó que la víctima murió en el lugar. ### Passive reporting en diferentes tiempos | Tiempo | Estructura | Ejemplo | |--------|-----------|---------| | Present simple | It is said that… | *It is said that the trial will be fair.* | | Past simple | It was reported that… | *It was reported that the jury reached a verdict.* | | Present perfect | It has been claimed that… | *It has been claimed that evidence was tampered with.* | | Future | It will be expected that… | *It will be expected that the defendant cooperates.* | | Past perfect | It had been alleged that… | *It had been alleged that the contract was signed under duress.* | ### Verbos de reporting habituales en passive reporting - **said** — dicho - **believed** — creído - **reported** — reportado - **claimed** — alegado - **expected** — esperado - **thought** — pensado - **known** — sabido - **alleged** — alegado - **suspected** — sospechado - **confirmed** — confirmado ### Errores comunes con la passive reporting | # | Error | Corrección | Explicación | |---|-------|-----------|-------------| | 1 | *It is believed **that him** to be guilty.* | *It is believed **that he is** guilty.* / *He is believed **to be** guilty.* | No se pueden mezclar ambas estructuras. Usar "that + clause" o "to + infinitive". | | 2 | *The man is said **having fled** the country.* | *The man is said **to have fled** the country.* | Después de "to" se usa el infinitivo perfecto, no el gerundio. | | 3 | *It was reported **him** to have been arrested.* | *It was reported **that he had been** arrested.* / ***He** was reported to have been arrested.* | El sujeto después de "it was reported" va en clause con "that", o como sujeto principal. | | 4 | *It is **say** that the law is effective.* | *It is **said** that the law is effective.* | Se necesita el past participle, no el infinitivo base. | | 5 | *He is believed **be** innocent.* | *He is believed **to be** innocent.* | Falta la preposición "to" antes del infinitivo. | --- ## Sección 3 — Reported Speech El **reported speech** (estilo indirecto) transforma una cita directa en una cláusula subordinada. En contextos legales, es indispensable para declaraciones de testigos, sentencias judiciales y comunicados de abogados. ### Backshift de tiempos Cuando el verbo de reporting está en pasado, los tiempos de la cita directa se desplazan hacia atrás (backshift): | Directo | Indirecto | |---------|-----------| | "I **am** innocent." | He said he **was** innocent. | | "I **was** at home." | She said she **had been** at home. | | "I **have seen** the evidence." | He said he **had seen** the evidence. | | "I **will testify**." | She said she **would testify**. | | "I **can help**." | He said he **could help**. | | "I **must leave**." | She said she **had to leave**. | ### Verbos de reporting En derecho y derechos humanos, los verbos de reporting más frecuentes son: - **say** — decir - **tell** — decir (a alguien) - **claim** — alegar - **alleg** — alegar (formal) - **insist** — insistir - **deny** — negar - **suggest** — sugerir - **report** — reportar ### Reporting de preguntas - Preguntas con auxiliary: *He asked **whether** the suspect **had been** arrested.* - Preguntas sin auxiliary: *She asked **where** the evidence **was**.* ### Reporting de órdenes y peticiones - Orden: *The judge ordered **that the jury be sequestered**.* / *The judge told them **to leave** the courtroom.* - Petición: *The lawyer requested **that the case be dismissed**.* ### Errores comunes con el reported speech | # | Error | Corrección | Explicación | |---|-------|-----------|-------------| | 1 | *He said that he **is** innocent.* | *He said that he **was** innocent.* | El backshift exige cambiar "is" a "was" cuando el verbo de reporting está en pasado. | | 2 | *She told **that** she had seen the evidence.* | *She said that she had seen the evidence.* / *She **told me** that she had seen the evidence.* | "Tell" requiere un objeto indirecto; "say" no lo necesita. | | 3 | *The witness claimed **to not have been** present.* | *The witness claimed **not to have been** present.* | La negación va antes del infinitivo: "not to + V". | | 4 | *He asked me **that** where I was.* | *He asked me **where I was**.* | En preguntas indirectas no se usa "that" ni se duplica la interrogación. | | 5 | *The lawyer insisted **to see** the documents.* | *The lawyer insisted **on seeing** the documents.* / *The lawyer insisted **that he be allowed** to see the documents.* | "Insist" no va seguido de infinitivo directo. Se usa "on + gerundio" o "that + clause". | --- ## Sección 4 — Vocabulario: Justicia y derechos humanos | Inglés | Español | Ejemplo | |--------|---------|---------| | human rights | derechos humanos | *Human rights are protected by international law.* | | civil rights | derechos civiles | *Civil rights were earned after decades of struggle.* | | rule of law | estado de derecho | *The rule of law must be upheld in every democracy.* | | due process | debido proceso | *Every defendant is entitled to due process.* | | freedom of speech | libertad de expresión | *Freedom of speech is a fundamental human right.* | | asylum | asilo | *The refugee was granted asylum in the host country.* | | deportation | deportación | *Deportation orders were issued against the suspects.* | | tribunal | tribunal | *The tribunal was established to investigate war crimes.* | | indictment | acusación formal | *The indictment was issued by a grand jury.* | | verdict | veredicto | *The verdict was announced after three weeks of deliberation.* | | sentence | sentencia | *The sentence was handed down by the presiding judge.* | | plaintiff | demandante | *The plaintiff filed a lawsuit against the corporation.* | | defendant | acusado / demandado | *The defendant pleaded not guilty to all charges.* | | habeas corpus | habeas corpus | *A habeas corpus petition was filed on behalf of the detainee.* | | habeas corpus | habeas corpus | *The writ of habeas corpus protects against unlawful detention.* | | genocide | genocidio | *The tribunal ruled that genocide had been committed.* | | war crimes | crímenes de guerra | *War crimes were documented by the United Nations.* | | extradition | extradición | *The suspect was extradited to face trial in another country.* | | acquittal | absolución | *The acquittal was met with widespread protest.* | | prosecution | fiscalía / persecución penal | *The prosecution presented compelling evidence.* | | amnesty | amnistía | *An amnesty was declared for political prisoners.* | | loophole | vacío legal | *A loophole in the law was exploited by the defence.* | | jurisdiction | jurisdicción | *The case falls under the jurisdiction of the ICC.* | | detention | detención | *Prolonged detention without trial violates human rights.* | --- ## Sección 5 — Reading: A landmark human rights case In 2010, a landmark case **was brought** before the International Criminal Court. The case **was filed** by a group of human rights organisations alleging that war crimes **had been committed** during an armed conflict. The evidence **was collected** over several years by independent investigators and **has been presented** to the court in a series of hearings. It **is believed** that the crimes **were planned** at the highest levels of government. Several high-ranking officials **are said to have ordered** attacks on civilian populations. It **was reported** that thousands of civilians **were displaced** as a result. After a lengthy trial, the court **ruled** that the evidence was sufficient to proceed. It **is expected** that the verdict **will be announced** early next year. Human rights groups have called the proceedings a milestone in international justice, and it **is hoped** that the case **will set** a precedent for future prosecutions. *(Approx. 150 words)* --- ## Sección 6 — Listening y diálogo **Context:** A courtroom scene where a judge addresses the defendant's lawyer. > **Judge:** It has been alleged that your client was present at the scene. Is that correct? > > **Lawyer:** My client has been wrongly accused, Your Honour. He is believed to have been at work at the time. > > **Judge:** The prosecution claims that evidence places him at the location. Were the security records examined? > > **Lawyer:** Yes, Your Honour. The security records have been reviewed and it is now confirmed that the timestamps were altered. It is thought that the footage was tampered with. > > **Judge:** Very well. The defence will be allowed to present its findings. The trial will resume on Monday. > > **Lawyer:** Thank you, Your Honour. Este diálogo ilustra passive voice (*were examined, have been reviewed*), passive reporting (*it has been alleged, is believed to have been, it is thought that*) y reported speech en un contexto judicial real. --- ## Sección 7 — Writing: Reports and legal documents La passive voice y la passive reporting son esenciales en la redacción formal de informes legales, resoluciones judiciales y documentos de derechos humanos. ### Consejos clave 1. **Usa passive cuando el agente es desconocido o irrelevante:** *The victim was found unconscious.* (no sabemos quién la encontró). 2. **Usa passive reporting para atribuir información sin compromiso:** *It is alleged that…* en vez de *People say that…* 3. **Mantén coherencia temporal:** Si el informe describe hechos pasados, usa past passive; si describe la situación actual, usa present passive. 4. **Evita el estilo periodístico informal:** Usa *It has been reported that* en lugar de *People have been saying that*. 5. **Cita testigos con reported speech:** *The witness stated that she had seen the defendant leaving the building.* 6. **Combina passive y reported speech:** *The documents were said to have been destroyed.* --- ## Sección 8 — Speaking Para discutir temas de justicia y derechos humanos en inglés B2: 1. **Prepara chunks de passive reporting:** *It is believed that…, The suspect is said to have…, It was reported that…* 2. **Usa passive para sonar objetivo:** En lugar de *They arrested him*, di *He was arrested*. Esto es más formal y neutral. 3. **Cita fuentes con reported speech:** *According to the report, the law was passed unanimously.* 4. **Practica opiniones con condicionales pasivos:** *More could have been done to prevent the crisis.* 5. **Vocabulario temático:** Domina los términos de la tabla de vocabulario para sonar preciso y profesional. --- ## Sección 9 — Errores cruzados y estrategia de examen | # | Error | Corrección | Tipo de error | |---|-------|-----------|---------------| | 1 | *The law is said **pass** last year.* | *The law is said **to have been passed** last year.* | Passive reporting + tiempo pasado | | 2 | *He said that he **will** testify.* | *He said that he **would** testify.* | Falta backshift en reported speech | | 3 | *It was believed **him to be** guilty.* | *It was believed **that he was** guilty.* | Mezcla incorrecta de estructuras | | 4 | *The verdict **will announced** tomorrow.* | *The verdict **will be announced** tomorrow.* | Falta "be" en future passive | | 5 | *She told **that** she had not seen the evidence.* | *She **said that** she had not seen the evidence.* / *She told **me that**…* | "Tell" necesita objeto indirecto | | 6 | *The rights should **been** respected.* | *The rights should **have been** respected.* | Falta "have" en past modal passive | --- ## Sección 10 — Del reconocimiento a la producción B2 El camino de B2 va del **reconocimiento pasivo** (identificar passive y reported speech cuando lees o escuchas) a la **producción activa** (usarlas espontáneamente al hablar y escribir). Para lograrlo: - **Lee informes legales y artículos de prensa** en inglés y subraya todas las construcciones pasivas y de reporting. - **Escucha debates parlamentarios o juicios** disponibles en YouTube para identificar passive reporting en tiempo real. - **Escribe resúmenes de noticias legales** usando al menos 5 construcciones passive/reporting por párrafo. - **Practica speaking** simulando una entrevista periodística o una declaración ante un tribunal. - **Corrige tus propios errores** usando la tabla de errores comunes como referencia. --- ## Sección 11 — Resumen rápido de teoría | Estructura | Forma | Ejemplo | |-----------|-------|---------| | Present simple passive | am/is/are + V3 | *Rights are protected by law.* | | Past simple passive | was/were + V3 | *The law was passed in 2015.* | | Present perfect passive | have/has been + V3 | *Evidence has been examined.* | | Future simple passive | will be + V3 | *The verdict will be announced.* | | Modal passive | modal + be + V3 | *The sentence can be reduced.* | | Past modal passive | modal + have been + V3 | *Rights should have been respected.* | | Conditional passive | would be + V3 | *The case would be dismissed.* | | Perfect conditional passive | would have been + V3 | *The sentence would have been reduced.* | | Passive reporting (impersonal) | It is said that… | *It is said that he fled.* | | Passive reporting (personal) | Subject + is said to… | *He is said to have fled.* | | Reported speech (statements) | Subject + said (that)… | *He said (that) he was innocent.* | | Reported speech (questions) | Subject + asked whether/if… | *She asked whether the law applied.* | | Reported speech (orders) | Subject + ordered/told + to V | *The judge ordered him to leave.* | --- ## Checklist - [ ] La passive voice se forma con **subject + to be (tiempo) + V3**. - [ ] En cada tiempo verbal, el verbo "be" se conjuga según el tiempo correspondiente. - [ ] La passive reporting impersonal usa **It is/was + V3 + that + clause**. - [ ] La passive reporting personal usa **Subject + is/was + V3 + to + infinitive**. - [ ] Para acciones pasadas en passive reporting se usa **to have + V3**. - [ ] El reported speech requiere **backshift** cuando el verbo de reporting está en pasado. - [ ] "Tell" necesita un objeto indirecto; "say" no. - [ ] Las preguntas indirectas usan **whether/if** (preguntas sí/no) o wh- words. - [ ] Las órdenes se reportan con **ordered/told + object + to + verb**. - [ ] En writing formal, la passive y passive reporting crean un tono objetivo y profesional. --- # Parte II — Ejercicios con soluciones Este cuaderno reúne los **ejercicios de la Unidad 52 del curso B2** (*Human Rights & Justice*). Practicarás reconocimiento, transformación y producción con tareas cerradas o criterios verificables. > **Guía teórica:** [Passive & Reported Speech B2](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-52-passive-reported-speech-human-rights)
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 52](/curso-b2/unit-52) **Contenido de los ejercicios:** 1. [Lección 1 — Gramática y chunks](#leccion-1--gramatica-y-chunks) 2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario](#leccion-2--vocabulario) 3. [Lección 3 — Reading](#leccion-3--reading) 4. [Lección 4 — Listening](#leccion-4--listening) 5. [Lección 5 — Writing y Speaking](#leccion-5--writing-y-speaking) --- ## Lección 1 — Gramática y chunks ### 1.1 Passive voice: completa el tiempo verbal Completa cada oración con la forma pasiva correcta del verbo entre paréntesis. **1.** The defendant __________ (charge) with fraud.
Ver solución **is charged** *The defendant **is charged** with fraud.* — Present simple passive.
**2.** The law __________ (pass) by parliament in 2018.
Ver solución **was passed** *The law **was passed** by parliament in 2018.* — Past simple passive.
**3.** The evidence __________ (examine) by the forensic team.
Ver solución **has been examined** *The evidence **has been examined** by the forensic team.* — Present perfect passive.
**4.** A new verdict __________ (announce) next week.
Ver solución **will be announced** *A new verdict **will be announced** next week.* — Future simple passive.
**5.** The rights __________ (should / respect) by all authorities.
Ver solución **should have been respected** *The rights **should have been respected** by all authorities.* — Past modal passive.
### 1.2 Passive reporting: transforma a passive reporting Transforma cada oración activa en passive reporting usando "It is/was said that…" o la estructura personal con "to". **1.** People say that the suspect fled the country.
Ver solución - **It is said that the suspect fled the country.** - **The suspect is said to have fled the country.**
**2.** Experts believe that the law is unconstitutional.
Ver solución - **It is believed that the law is unconstitutional.** - **The law is believed to be unconstitutional.**
**3.** Reports claim that evidence was destroyed.
Ver solución - **It is claimed that evidence was destroyed.** - **Evidence is claimed to have been destroyed.**
**4.** The media reported that the judge was biased.
Ver solución - **It was reported that the judge was biased.** - **The judge was reported to have been biased.**
**5.** Analysts expect that the verdict will be unanimous.
Ver solución - **It is expected that the verdict will be unanimous.** - **The verdict is expected to be unanimous.**
### 1.3 Reported speech: transforma a estilo indirecto Transforma cada cita directa en reported speech con backshift adecuado. **1.** "I am not guilty," said the defendant.
Ver solución **The defendant said (that) he was not guilty.**
**2.** "I saw the victim last week," the witness stated.
Ver solución **The witness stated (that) he/she had seen the victim the previous week.**
**3.** "I will cooperate fully with the investigation," the suspect promised.
Ver solución **The suspect promised (that) he/she would cooperate fully with the investigation.**
**4.** "Where is the evidence stored?" the lawyer asked.
Ver solución **The lawyer asked where the evidence was stored.**
**5.** "Give me access to the documents," the judge ordered.
Ver solución **The judge ordered (him/her) to give him/her access to the documents.**
### 1.4 Mixed: elige la forma correcta Selecciona la opción correcta (a o b) para completar cada oración. **1.** It __________ that the trial will be fair. a) is believed b) is believed to
Ver solución **a) is believed** *It is believed that the trial will be fair.* — Con "that + clause", se usa la estructura impersonal sin "to".
**2.** The man is said __________ the scene. a) to have left b) having left
Ver solução **a) to have left** *The man is said to have left the scene.* — Después de "is said" se usa "to + infinitive" (perfecto para pasado).
**3.** She said that she __________ the evidence. a) has seen b) had seen
Ver solução **b) had seen** *She said that she had seen the evidence.* — Backshift: present perfect → past perfect.
**4.** The law __________ in 2020. a) was being passed b) was passed
Ver solução **b) was passed** *The law was passed in 2020.* — Past simple passive para una acción puntual en el pasado.
**5.** It __________ that the evidence had been tampered with. a) was reported b) reported
Ver solução **a) was reported** *It was reported that the evidence had been tampered with.* — Passive reporting: "it + be + V3 + that".
--- ## Lección 2 — Vocabulario ### 2.1 Traducción precisa Empareja cada término en inglés con su traducción al español. **1.** verdict **2.** indictment **3.** habeas corpus **4.** extradition **5.** amnesty
Ver solución 1. **verdict** → veredicto 2. **indictment** → acusación formal 3. **habeas corpus** → habeas corpus (writ de hábeas corpus) 4. **extradition** → extradición 5. **amnesty** → amnistía
### 2.2 Elige por definición Elige el término correcto (a o b) para cada definición. **1.** "A legal principle that protects people from unlawful detention." a) due process b) jurisdiction
Ver solução **a) due process** *Due process* refers to the legal requirement to respect all legal rights of a person.
**2.** "The authority of a court to hear and decide a case." a) prosecution b) jurisdiction
Ver solução **b) jurisdiction** *Jurisdiction* is the official power to make legal decisions and judgments.
**3.** "An official order for someone to leave a country." a) deportation b) asylum
Ver solução **a) deportation** *Deportation* is the removal of a person from a country.
**4.** "The principle that all people and institutions are accountable to the law." a) rule of law b) freedom of speech
Ver solução **a) rule of law** *Rule of law* means no one is above the law.
**5.** "An acquittal means the defendant was found __________." a) guilty b) not guilty
Ver solução **b) not guilty** An *acquittal* is a formal declaration that someone is not guilty of a criminal charge.
### 2.3 Completa el chunk Completa cada chunk legal con la palabra correcta. **1.** The __________ was handed down by the judge. (sentencia)
Ver solução **sentence** *The sentence was handed down by the judge.*
**2.** War __________ were documented by the United Nations.
Ver solução **crimes** *War crimes were documented by the United Nations.*
**3.** The __________ presented compelling evidence in court.
Ver solução **prosecution** *The prosecution presented compelling evidence in court.*
**4.** A __________ in the law was exploited by the defence team.
Ver solução **loophole** *A loophole in the law was exploited by the defence team.*
**5.** The refugee was granted __________ in the host country.
Ver solução **asylum** *The refugee was granted asylum in the host country.*
### 2.4 Word formation Completa con la forma correcta de la palabra entre paréntesis. **1.** The __________ (try) lasted for six months.
Ver solução **trial** *The trial lasted for six months.* — Sustantivo formado de "try" → "trial".
**2.** __________ (free) of speech is a fundamental human right.
Ver solução **Freedom** *Freedom of speech is a fundamental human right.*
**3.** Several __________ (amend) were made to the constitution.
Ver solução **amendments** *Several amendments were made to the constitution.* — Plural de "amendment".
**4.** The defendant's __________ (defense) was well prepared.
Ver solução **defence** / **defense** *The defendant's defence was well prepared.* — Orthografía británica (defence) o americana (defense).
**5.** The __________ (govern) passed the law unanimously.
Ver solução **government** *The government passed the law unanimously.*
--- ## Lección 3 — Reading Lee el siguiente texto y responde las preguntas. In 2023, an international tribunal **was established** to investigate allegations of systematic human rights violations. The proceedings **were initiated** following a formal complaint filed by the United Nations Human Rights Council. It **is understood** that the violations **occurred** over a period of ten years and **affected** thousands of civilians. Testimony **has been collected** from over 200 witnesses. Several former officials **are alleged to have ordered** the attacks on civilian infrastructure. It **was revealed** during the proceedings that internal documents **had been destroyed** to conceal evidence. The tribunal **is expected to issue** its final ruling by the end of the year. It **is hoped** that the ruling **will establish** a legal precedent for holding individuals accountable for crimes against humanity. Human rights organisations have stated that the case represents a turning point in international justice. The proceedings have been **broadcast** worldwide, raising public awareness of the issues at stake. *(Approx. 150 words)* ### 3.1 Comprensión global Responde según el texto. **1.** When was the tribunal established? a) 2020 b) 2023 c) 2015
Ver solución **b) 2023** *In 2023, an international tribunal was established…*
**2.** Who filed the formal complaint? a) The tribunal b) The witnesses c) The United Nations Human Rights Council
Ver solução **c) The United Nations Human Rights Council** *…following a formal complaint filed by the United Nations Human Rights Council.*
**3.** How many witnesses testified? a) Over 100 b) Over 200 c) Over 500
Ver solução **b) Over 200** *Testimony has been collected from over 200 witnesses.*
**4.** What was destroyed to conceal evidence? a) Testimony records b) Internal documents c) External reports
Ver solução **b) Internal documents** *…internal documents had been destroyed to conceal evidence.*
**5.** What do human rights organisations say about the case? a) It is irrelevant b) It is too slow c) It represents a turning point in international justice
Ver solução **c) It represents a turning point in international justice** *Human rights organisations have stated that the case represents a turning point in international justice.*
### 3.2 Detalles y chunks exactos Completa las oraciones usando información exacta del texto. **1.** The tribunal __________ to investigate allegations of systematic human rights violations.
Ver solução **was established**
**2.** It is understood that the violations occurred over a period of __________.
Ver solução **ten years**
**3.** __________ from over 200 witnesses has been collected.
Ver solução **Testimony**
**4.** Several former officials are alleged to have __________ the attacks on civilian infrastructure.
Ver solução **ordered**
**5.** It is expected that the ruling will establish a legal __________ for holding individuals accountable.
Ver solução **precedent**
### 3.3 Forma, significado y secuencia Analiza las construcciones pasivas y de reporting del texto. **1.** Identify one example of past simple passive in the text and explain why past simple is used.
Ver solução *The proceedings were initiated following a formal complaint…* — Past simple passive because it describes a completed action in the past that triggered the tribunal.
**2.** What is the difference between "It is understood that" and "It was revealed that" in the text?
Ver solução *It is understood that* uses present passive reporting to state current general knowledge. *It was revealed that* uses past passive reporting to describe something disclosed during the proceedings.
**3.** Why does the text use present perfect passive: "Testimony has been collected"?
Ver solução Present perfect passive emphasises the result of an ongoing process — the testimony collection started in the past and is relevant to the current state of the proceedings.
**4.** Explain the structure: "are alleged to have ordered."
Ver solução Personal passive reporting in present tense + perfect infinitive (*to have ordered*) to refer to a past action attributed to the officials.
**5.** What passive construction appears in the last sentence? What is its function?
Ver solução *The proceedings have been broadcast worldwide.* — Present perfect passive to describe a completed action with present relevance (public awareness).
--- ## Lección 4 — Listening **Context:** A journalist interviews a human rights lawyer about a recent case. > **Journalist:** Can you tell us about the case? > > **Lawyer:** It was filed on behalf of several families who were displaced during the conflict. It is believed that the military targeted civilian areas deliberately. > > **Journalist:** What evidence has been presented? > > **Lawyer:** Satellite imagery has been examined, and it is said to confirm the attacks. Witness testimonies have also been collected from over 150 individuals. > > **Journalist:** Has the government responded? > > **Lawyer:** It was reported that the government denied all allegations. However, internal documents are said to have been leaked, which contradicts their official position. > > **Journalist:** What is expected to happen next? > > **Lawyer:** It is expected that a formal ruling will be issued next month. We are hopeful that justice will be served. ### 4.1 Comprensión global **1.** Who filed the case? a) The journalist b) Several displaced families c) The military
Ver solución **b) Several displaced families** *It was filed on behalf of several families who were displaced during the conflict.*
**2.** What evidence does the lawyer mention? a) DNA analysis only b) Satellite imagery and witness testimonies c) Financial records
Ver solução **b) Satellite imagery and witness testimonies** *Satellite imagery has been examined… Witness testimonies have also been collected…*
**3.** How did the government respond? a) They accepted responsibility b) They denied all allegations c) They cooperated fully
Ver solução **b) They denied all allegations** *It was reported that the government denied all allegations.*
**4.** What documents are said to have been leaked? a) Military orders b) Internal documents c) Financial statements
Ver solução **b) Internal documents** *Internal documents are said to have been leaked, which contradicts their official position.*
**5.** When is the formal ruling expected? a) Next week b) Next month c) Next year
Ver solução **b) Next month** *It is expected that a formal ruling will be issued next month.*
### 4.2 Detalles y chunks exactos **1.** The case was filed __________ of several families who were displaced.
Ver solução **on behalf**
**2.** It is believed that the military targeted __________ areas deliberately.
Ver solución **civilian**
**3.** Satellite imagery has been __________ by experts.
Ver solução **examined**
**4.** Internal documents are said to have been __________, which contradicts the official position.
Ver solução **leaked**
**5.** The lawyer expressed hope that __________ would be served.
Ver solução **justice**
### 4.3 Forma, significado y secuencia **1.** Identify all instances of passive reporting in the dialogue.
Ver solução - *It is believed that…* - *It is said to confirm…* - *It was reported that…* - *Internal documents are said to have been leaked…* - *It is expected that…*
**2.** Why does the lawyer use "It was reported that" instead of "They said"?
Ver solução *It was reported that* is more formal and impersonal, appropriate for legal and journalistic contexts. *They said* is informal and vague about the source.
**3.** What is the function of "has been examined" in the dialogue?
Ver solução Present perfect passive emphasises the result of the examination — the satellite imagery has been processed and the findings are relevant now.
**4.** Analyze: "are said to have been leaked." What tenses are combined?
Ver solução Present passive reporting (*are said*) + perfect passive infinitive (*to have been leaked*), referring to a past action (the leak) that is currently reported.
**5.** What is the difference between "We are hopeful" and "It is hoped" in legal language?
Ver solução *We are hopeful* is personal and informal. *It is hoped* is impersonal and formal, more appropriate for official statements.
--- ## Lección 5 — Writing y Speaking ### Writing **1.** Write a short news report (3–5 sentences) about a human rights case using at least 3 passive voice constructions.
Ver modelo A human rights tribunal **was convened** in Geneva to investigate allegations of abuse. Testimony **has been collected** from over 100 witnesses. It **is believed** that the crimes **were committed** over a period of five years. The tribunal **is expected to issue** its findings by the end of the month.
**2.** Rewrite the following active sentences in passive voice: "The police arrested the suspect. They charged him with theft. A judge will hear the case."
Ver modelo The suspect **was arrested** by the police. He **was charged** with theft. The case **will be heard** by a judge.
**3.** Transform this direct quote into reported speech: "I have committed no crime," the defendant told the court.
Ver modelo The defendant told the court that he **had committed** no crime.
**4.** Write a formal paragraph (50–70 words) about freedom of speech using at least 2 passive reporting structures.
Ver modelo Freedom of speech **is considered** a fundamental human right in democratic societies. It **is believed that** this right **is protected** by the constitutions of most nations. However, it **is reported that** in many countries, journalists **are persecuted** for expressing their opinions. It **is hoped that** international pressure **will lead** to greater protection.
**5.** Rewrite this informal sentence in formal legal style using passive reporting: "People think the government broke the law."
Ver modelo **It is believed that** the government **violated** the law. / The government is believed to have violated the law.
**6.** Write a sentence using past modal passive about a human rights violation: "should have been respected."
Ver modelo The fundamental rights of the detainees **should have been respected** by the authorities at all times.
**7.** Write a sentence using conditional passive about a legal scenario: "would be dismissed."
Ver modelo The case **would be dismissed** if insufficient evidence is presented to the court.
**8.** Transform this sentence into perfect conditional passive: "If the lawyer had objected, the jury would have been sequestered."
Ver modelo If the lawyer had objected, the jury **would have been sequestered**. (The sentence is already in correct perfect conditional passive form.)
**9.** Write a 3-sentence legal summary using: was established, has been alleged, is expected to be.
Ver modelo A special commission **was established** to investigate the matter. It **has been alleged** that funds were diverted from public accounts. The final report **is expected to be** published next quarter.
**10.** Write a formal complaint letter opening (2–3 sentences) using passive voice and reported speech: "We have been told that our complaint was ignored."
Ver modelo We **have been informed** that our initial complaint, filed on 15 March 2026, **was not addressed** by the relevant department. It **has been brought to our attention** that similar cases **have been overlooked** in the past. We respectfully request that this matter be reviewed immediately.
### Speaking **1.** Prepare a 1-minute monologue about a human rights topic. Use at least 5 passive/reporting constructions.
Consejos y modelo Suggested chunk list to include: - *It is believed that…* - *The law was passed in…* - *It is reported that…* - *Rights have been violated…* - *It is expected that…* Model opening: *Human rights are protected by international law, but it is believed that many countries violate these rights systematically. It is reported that thousands of people are detained without trial each year. It is hoped that international tribunals will hold perpetrators accountable.*
**2.** Role-play a courtroom dialogue (judge + lawyer). Use passive voice, passive reporting, and reported speech. (2–3 minutes)
Script sugerido > **Judge:** Has the evidence been examined? > **Lawyer:** Yes, Your Honour. It has been examined by two independent experts. > **Judge:** And what is the conclusion? > **Lawyer:** It is believed that the documents are authentic. > **Judge:** Was the defendant present when the evidence was collected? > **Lawyer:** The defendant was not present. He is said to have been abroad at the time.
**3.** Explain the difference between "It is said that he fled" and "He is said to have fled" in your own words.
Respuesta modelo Both convey the same meaning — that there is a claim that the man left the country. The first structure (*It is said that…*) emphasises the information, while the second (*He is said to have fled*) emphasises the person. Both are formal and appropriate for legal contexts.
**4.** Discuss with a partner: "Should human rights violations always be prosecuted, even years later?" Use passive reporting in your argument.
Puntos para tu respuesta Use chunks like: - *It is widely believed that…* - *It has been argued that…* - *Justice should not be delayed.* - *The rights of victims have been overlooked.* - *It is expected that courts will…*
**5.** Prepare a 30-second summary of the reading passage from Lección 3. Use passive constructions.
Modelo In 2023, an international tribunal was established to investigate human rights violations. Testimony has been collected from over 200 witnesses. Several officials are alleged to have ordered attacks on civilians. It is expected that the ruling will set a legal precedent.
--- ## Tip del profesor En inglés formal y periodístico, la passive voice y la passive reporting no son solo "opciones gramaticales": son herramientas de precisión y neutralidad. En un tribunal o en un informe de derechos humanos, el agente a menudo se omite deliberadamente para enfocarse en los hechos y las víctimas. Domina estas estructuras y tu inglés sonará profesional y creíble. --- ## Siguiente paso en el curso B2 Continúa con la **Unidad 53 del curso B2**: *Modals y Phrasal Verbs* con *Carrera Profesional y Mundo Laboral*. - [Unidad 52 del curso](/curso-b2/unit-52) - [Continuar con Unidad 53](/curso-b2/unit-53) ### Guías relacionadas - [U51 Wish, If Only y Third Conditional](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-51-wish-third-conditional-economy) - [U53 Modals & Phrasal Verbs](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-53-modals-phrasal-verbs-career) - [Inglés B2](/blog/metodos/ingles-b2) --- ## Preguntas frecuentes ### ¿Cuándo uso la passive voice en inglés? Cuando el receptor de la acción es más importante que el agente, o cuando el agente es desconocido: *The defendant was convicted.* ### ¿Cómo se forma el passive con diferentes tiempos? Subject + be (time) + past participle. *is done, was done, has been done, will be done.* ### ¿Qué diferencia hay entre reported speech y passive reporting? Reported speech transforms direct quotes. Passive reporting attributes information to sources. ### ¿Cuándo uso "it is said that" vs "the man is said to"? Both correct. First emphasizes information; second emphasizes person. Passive with "to" needs infinitive. ### ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 52? En la Unidad 52 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía. También puedes practicar con los [ejercicios y soluciones de la Unidad 52](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-52-passive-reported-speech-human-rights-ejercicios-soluciones). --- ## Fuentes - CEFR/MCER — Nivel B2: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages - British Council — B1–B2 grammar: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/b1-b2-grammar - Cambridge Dictionary — Grammar and vocabulary reference: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/
