faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre must, have to y need to?
faqs.answer: Must expresa obligación personal o deducción fuerte. Have to es obligación externa. Need to es necesidad subjetiva.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forman los phrasal verbs con separación?
faqs.answer: Si el objeto es un pronombre, siempre va entre verbo y partícula: pick it up. Si es un sustantivo, puede ir antes o después: pick up the phone / pick the phone up.

faqs.question: ¿Qué modals uso para deducción?
faqs.answer: Must (conclusión fuerte), might/could (posibilidad), can't (descarte fuerte). She must be working late. She might have left.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo aprendo phrasal verbs de forma natural?
faqs.answer: Aprende el verbo y la partícula como una unidad con su contexto: set up a business, take on responsibility, turn down an offer.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 53?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 53 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones.

content:
La **Unidad 53** consolida los **modals** de obligación, deducción y consejo junto con **phrasal verbs** frecuentes del ámbito laboral y profesional. Cada ejemplo conecta forma gramatical y vocabulario real del mundo del trabajo. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 53](/curso-b2/unit-53)
> **Antes:** [U52 — Passive & Reported Speech + Human Rights](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-52-passive-reported-speech-human-rights)
> **Siguiente:** [Unidad 54 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-54) --- # Parte I — Teoría ## Qué aprenderás en esta unidad - Usar los **modals de obligación** (*must, have to, need to, should, ought to, don't have to, mustn't*) para hablar de deberes, políticas de empresa y obligaciones profesionales. - Aplicar los **modals de deducción** en presente y pasado (*must, might, could, can't* + *must have + V3, might have + V3, can't have + V3*) para inferir situaciones de compañeros y decisiones de negocio. - Dominar más de 20 **phrasal verbs** del mundo laboral (*apply for, set up, take on, turn down, work out*, etc.) con su contexto natural. - Desarrollar las cuatro destrezas — reading, listening, writing y speaking — en un escenario profesional y de carrera. - Corregir los errores más comunes y aplicar una estrategia real de examen B2. ![Modals y Phrasal Verbs en inglés B2 con vocabulario de carrera profesional y mundo laboral](/blog/curso-b2/unit-53/modals-phrasal-verbs-map.png) --- ## 1. Modals of obligation: must, have to, need to, should, ought to, don't have to, mustn't Los **modals of obligation** expresan distintos grados de necesidad y deber. La elección entre ellos depende de quién impone la obligación, de la fuerza de la necesidad y del nivel de formalidad. En el mundo laboral, esta distinción es esencial para entender contratos, políticas de empresa y deberes profesionales. ### Must — obligación personal o fuerte - *I **must** finish this report before the meeting.* — Debo terminar este informe antes de la reunión. - *Employees **must** wear their ID badge at all times.* — Los empleados deben llevar su credencial en todo momento. - *You **must** attend the safety training.* — Debes asistir a la formación de seguridad. Must expresa una obligación que el hablante siente como propia o una norma clara. En presente no necesita "to" ni se conjuga: *He must work.* (no *He musts*). ### Have to — obligación externa - *I **have to** arrive at 9 a.m. because the office opens then.* — Tengo que llegar a las 9 porque la oficina abre entonces. - *She **has to** submit the invoice by Friday.* — Ella tiene que enviar la factura antes del viernes. - *They **had to** cancel the project.* — Tuvieron que cancelar el proyecto. Have to describe una obligación impuesta desde fuera: una norma, un jefe, una ley. A diferencia de must, sí cambia de forma: *I have to / she has to / I had to / I will have to*. ### Need to — necesidad subjetiva - *You **need to** update your CV before applying.* — Necesitas actualizar tu CV antes de postularte. - *We **need to** discuss the budget.* — Necesitamos discutir el presupuesto. Need to es más suave que must y expresa una necesidad práctica o personal, frecuente en consejos y recomendaciones laborales. ### Should y ought to — consejo y recomendación - *You **should** ask for a promotion.* — Deberías pedir un ascenso. - *He **should** negotiate a better salary.* — Debería negociar un mejor salario. - *We **ought to** review the contract carefully.* — Deberíamos revisar el contrato con cuidado. Should y ought to son prácticamente sinónimos y expresan recomendación (no obligación). Ought to es ligeramente más formal. *You should* en un trabajo de oficina suena como consejo amable, no como orden. ### Don't have to — ausencia de obligación - *You **don't have to** wear a suit on Fridays.* — No tienes que llevar traje los viernes. - *She **doesn't have to** work weekends.* — Ella no tiene que trabajar los fines de semana. Don't have to significa *no es necesario*: la obligación no existe. No confundir con *mustn't*. ### Mustn't — prohibición - *You **mustn't** share confidential files.* — No debes compartir archivos confidenciales. - *Employees **mustn't** use their mobile phones on the shop floor.* — Los empleados no deben usar sus móviles en la planta. Mustn't expresa **prohibición**. La diferencia con *don't have to* es crucial: *don't have to* = no es necesario; *mustn't* = está prohibido. ### Errores comunes con los modals of obligation | # | Error | Corrección | Explicación | |---|-------|-----------|-------------| | 1 | *She **musts** finish the report.* | *She must finish the report.* | Los modals no se conjugan ni llevan "-s" en tercera persona. | | 2 | *You **mustn't** to work today.* | *You **mustn't work** today.* | Después de un modal se usa el infinitivo sin "to". | | 3 | *He **have to** attend the meeting.* | *He **has to** attend the meeting.* | Con tercera persona singular, "have to" cambia a "has to". | | 4 | *You **don't must** leave early.* | *You **mustn't** leave early.* / *You **don't have to** leave early.* | "Must" no se niega con "don't"; se usa "mustn't" (prohibición) o "don't have to" (no necesario). | | 5 | *We **need** work overtime.* | *We **need to** work overtime.* | "Need to" necesita "to"; "need" solo se usa sin "to" como modal auxiliar en negativas y preguntas. | --- ## 2. Modals of deduction: must, might, could, can't Los **modals of deduction** expresan el grado de certeza que tenemos sobre una situación. En el trabajo los usamos constantemente para inferir lo que hace un compañero, por qué se retrasa un proyecto o qué decisión tomará la dirección. ### Deducción en presente - **Must** — conclusión lógica fuerte (estoy casi seguro). - *She **must** be working late — I can see her car.* — Debe de estar trabajando hasta tarde, veo su coche. - *The meeting **must** be cancelled — the manager hasn't arrived.* — La reunión debe de estar cancelada, el gerente no ha llegado. - **Might / Could** — posibilidad (no estoy seguro). - *He **might** be stuck in traffic.* — Puede que esté atascado en el tráfico. - *They **could** be negotiating a new deal.* — Podrían estar negociando un nuevo trato. - **Can't** — descarte fuerte (conclusión negativa). - *She **can't** be at the conference — she's in the office.* — No puede estar en la conferencia, está en la oficina. - *He **can't** have no experience — he has a great CV.* — No puede no tener experiencia, tiene un gran CV. La forma para deducción en presente es **modal + base form**: *must work, might be, can't earn.* No se usa "to": *He must to work* es incorrecto. ### Deducción en pasado Para hablar de deducciones sobre hechos pasados se usa **modal + have + past participle (V3)**. - **Must have + V3** — conclusión fuerte sobre el pasado. - *She **must have left** the office early.* — Debe de haberse marchado de la oficina temprano. - *They **must have missed** the deadline.* — Deben de haber incumplido el plazo. - **Might have + V3 / Could have + V3** — posibilidad en el pasado. - *He **might have forgotten** the presentation.* — Puede que haya olvidado la presentación. - *The company **could have lost** the client.* — La empresa podría haber perdido al cliente. - **Can't have + V3** — descarte sobre el pasado. - *She **can't have received** my email — she didn't reply.* — No puede haber recibido mi correo, no respondió. - *He **can't have worked** here for ten years — he's too young.* — No puede haber trabajado aquí diez años, es demasiado joven. ### Ejemplos en contexto de negocio - *The share price **must have fallen** because of the bad news.* — El precio de la acción debe de haber caído por las malas noticias. - *The manager **might have postponed** the launch.* — El gerente puede que haya pospuesto el lanzamiento. - *Our competitors **could be** preparing a new product.* — Nuestros competidores podrían estar preparando un nuevo producto. ### Errores comunes con los modals of deduction | # | Error | Corrección | Explicación | |---|-------|-----------|-------------| | 1 | *He **must to work** late.* | *He **must work** late.* | "Must" va seguido del infinitivo sin "to". | | 2 | *She **must worked** overtime.* | *She **must have worked** overtime.* | Para pasado se usa "must + have + V3". | | 3 | *He **can't** to be at home.* | *He **can't be** at home.* | "Can't" va seguido de la base form, sin "to". | | 4 | *She **might has** left.* | *She **might have** left.* | Después del modal se usa "have", no "has". | | 5 | *The company **can't lost** the client.* | *The company **can't have lost** the client.* | Para descartar algo pasado se usa "can't have + V3". | --- ## 3. Phrasal verbs: work and career Los **phrasal verbs** están formados por un verbo y una o dos partículas. En el ámbito laboral son extremadamente frecuentes y dan naturalidad al inglés. El truco es aprender el verbo y la partícula como una unidad con su contexto, no palabra por palabra. | Inglés | Español | Ejemplo | |--------|---------|---------| | apply for | solicitar, postularse para | *I'm going to **apply for** the marketing role.* | | set up | montar, crear | *She **set up** her own consultancy.* | | take on | asumir (responsabilidad/trabajo) | *He **took on** more responsibility.* | | bring up | sacar a colación, plantear | *We **brought up** the pay issue in the meeting.* | | carry out | llevar a cabo | *The team **carried out** a market analysis.* | | come up with | idear, proponer | *She **came up with** an excellent idea.* | | cut back on | recortar, reducir | *The firm **cut back on** travel expenses.* | | end up | acabar (haciendo algo) | *He **ended up** accepting the offer.* | | get along with | llevarse bien con | *I **get along with** my colleagues.* | | give in | ceder, rendirse | *Don't **give in** during the salary negotiation.* | | go through | pasar por, examinar | *We **went through** the budget line by line.* | | keep up with | seguir el ritmo de | *It's hard to **keep up with** new software.* | | look into | investigar, indagar | *HR is **looking into** the complaint.* | | put off | posponer, aplazar | *They **put off** the meeting until Friday.* | | run into | encontrarse con, toparse con | *I **ran into** my old boss at the conference.* | | take over | tomar el relevo, hacerse cargo | *She will **take over** the department.* | | turn down | rechazar (una oferta) | *He **turned down** the job offer.* | | work out | resolver, salir bien | *Things **worked out** in the end.* | | point out | señalar, destacar | *The manager **pointed out** a mistake.* | | get on | progresar, llevarse bien | *How are you **getting on** in your new job?* | ### El tema de la separación Si el objeto del phrasal verb es un **pronombre**, siempre se coloca entre el verbo y la partícula: *pick **it** up.* Si es un sustantivo, puede ir antes o después: *pick up the phone* / *pick the phone up.* Algunos phrasal verbs no se separan nunca (los intransitivos o los de tres palabras): *come up with ***it***, get along with ***him***.* --- ## 4. Reading: A career change After ten years in finance, María **decided to turn down** a big promotion and **set up** her own business. She had always wanted to **work out** how to combine her skills with her passion for design. Her colleagues thought she must be making a risky move, but María knew she **mustn't** regret not trying. She **applied for** a small business loan and **took on** a part-time role to pay the bills while she **carried out** market research. She soon **ran into** problems with suppliers, but she **came up with** creative solutions. Her old employer offered her a job back, but she turned it down because she wanted to **keep up with** her own growth. "I **had to** learn to trust myself," she says. "You **shouldn't** let fear **put off** your dreams. If you **get along with** the right people and never **give in**, things tend to **work out**." Today her studio employs eight people, and she **points out** that the best decision she ever made was **taking over** her own career. *(Approx. 150 words)* --- ## 5. Listening y diálogo **Context:** A team meeting where colleagues discuss a project delay. > **Manager:** We need to **look into** why the launch was postponed. The clients must **have come up with** concerns about the design. > > **Ana:** I think they might **have been** worried about the budget. We probably **should have** discussed costs earlier. > > **Manager:** You're right. We **shouldn't have** ignored their feedback. Now we **have to** find a solution before Friday. > > **Leo:** I can't **keep up with** all the changes. We **mustn't** make the same mistake twice. > > **Manager:** Exactly. Let's **work out** a plan. Ana, you **mustn't** leave this to the last minute. Leo, you **ought to** prepare the new figures. > > **Ana:** OK, I'll **carry out** the review and **come up with** a revised proposal tomorrow. Este diálogo integra modals of obligation (*must, have to, ought to, mustn't, shouldn't have*), modals of deduction (*must have been, might have been*) y phrasal verbs laborales (*look into, come up with, keep up with, work out, carry out*) en una conversación de oficina realista. --- ## 6. Writing — Professional emails Los modals y los phrasal verbs son clave para redactar **correos profesionales** en inglés. El tono depende del objetivo: una solicitud, un recordatorio, una disculpa o una propuesta. ### Consejos clave 1. **Usa *should / ought to* para sugerir respetuosamente:** *You should review the attached proposal.* 2. **Usa *must* solo para obligaciones claras:** *All staff must complete the training.* 3. **Usa *don't have to* para recalcar que algo no es necesario:** *You don't have to attend the Friday call.* 4. **Prefiere phrasal verbs formales en contexto:** *We need to carry out a review*, *I'd like to bring up a concern*, *Please look into this issue.* 5. **Sé cortés con *might / could* en peticiones:** *Could you look into the figures for me?* 6. **Para deducciones en informes:** *The delay might have been caused by a misunderstanding.* --- ## 7. Speaking Para discutir la carrera profesional y el mundo laboral en inglés B2: 1. **Usa modals para hablar de obligaciones y deberes:** *I have to attend training*, *I mustn't miss the deadline.* 2. **Aplica deducción a situaciones de trabajo:** *He must be in a meeting*, *She might have taken the day off.* 3. **Domina phrasal verbs laborales para sonar natural:** *set up, take on, turn down, work out.* 4. **Practica consejos con *should / ought to*:** *You should negotiate your salary.* 5. **Cuenta historias de carrera usando pasado:** *I ran into my old manager*, *I ended up changing jobs.* --- ## 8. Errores cruzados y estrategia de examen | # | Error | Corrección | Tipo de error | |---|-------|-----------|---------------| | 1 | *She **must to call** the client.* | *She must call the client.* | Modal + infinitivo sin "to" | | 2 | *He **have to** finish the report.* | *He **has to** finish the report.* | Con jugación de "have to" | | 3 | *You **don't must** be late.* | *You **mustn't** be late.* | Negación de "must" | | 4 | *She **must worked** overtime.* | *She **must have worked** overtime.* | Deducción pasada: modal + have + V3 | | 5 | *We need to **set down** a business.* | *We need to **set up** a business.* | Partícula incorrecta del phrasal verb | | 6 | *He **turned down** it.* | *He **turned it down**.* | Pronombre entre verbo y partícula | --- ## 9. Del reconocimiento a la producción B2 El camino hacia B2 va del **reconocimiento pasivo** (identificar modals y phrasal verbs cuando lees o escuchas) a la **producción activa** (usarlos espontáneamente). Para lograrlo: - **Escucha reuniones y podcasts de negocios** en inglés y anota cada modal y phrasal verb que detectes. - **Subraya los modals de obligación y deducción** en correos profesionales y contratos. - **Escribe tu propio correo o post laboral** usando al menos 5 modals y 3 phrasal verbs. - **Habla sobre tu jornada laboral** describiendo obligaciones (*I have to*), deducciones (*My boss must be…*) y consejos (*You should…*). - **Corrige tus propios errores** con la tabla de errores como guía. --- ## 10. Resumen rápido de teoría | Estructura | Uso | Ejemplo | |-----------|-----|---------| | must + base form | obligación personal / deducción fuerte | *You must finish the report.* | | have to + base form | obligación externa | *She has to arrive at 9.* | | need to + base form | necesidad subjetiva | *We need to update the CV.* | | should / ought to + base form | consejo, recomendación | *You should negotiate salary.* | | don't have to + base form | ausencia de obligación | *You don't have to wear a suit.* | | mustn't + base form | prohibición | *You mustn't share files.* | | must / might / could / can't + base form | deducción en presente | *She must be working.* | | modal + have + V3 | deducción en pasado | *He might have left.* | --- ## Checklist - [ ] Los modals van seguidos del **infinitivo sin "to"** (*must work, can't be*). - [ ] "Have to" sí se conjuga (*has to, had to, will have to*); "must" no. - [ ] "Don't have to" = no es necesario; "mustn't" = prohibido. - [ ] "Should" y "ought to" expresan consejo, no obligación. - [ ] La deducción en presente usa **modal + base form**. - [ ] La deducción en pasado usa **modal + have + V3** (*must have, might have, can't have*). - [ ] Con un pronombre, el phrasal verb se separa: *pick it up*. - [ ] Con un sustantivo, la partícula puede ir antes o después: *pick up the phone*. - [ ] Los phrasal verbs se aprenden como una unidad con su contexto. - [ ] Los modals de deduction y obligation son clave en el examen B2 (Use of English). --- --- # Parte II — Ejercicios con soluciones Este cuaderno reúne los **ejercicios de la Unidad 53 del curso B2** (*Career & Work*). Practicarás reconocimiento, transformación y producción con tareas cerradas o criterios verificables. > **Guía teórica:** [Modals & Phrasal Verbs B2](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-53-modals-phrasal-verbs-career)
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 53](/curso-b2/unit-53) **Contenido de los ejercicios:** 1. [Lección 1 — Gramática y chunks](#leccion-1--gramatica-y-chunks) 2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario](#leccion-2--vocabulario) 3. [Lección 3 — Reading](#leccion-3--reading) 4. [Lección 4 — Listening](#leccion-4--listening) 5. [Lección 5 — Writing y Speaking](#leccion-5--writing-y-speaking) --- ## Lección 1 — Gramática y chunks ### 1.1 Modals of obligation: elige la opción correcta Selecciona la opción correcta (must / have to / should / don't have to / mustn't) para completar cada oración. **1.** You __________ be late for the interview. It's really important. a) don't have to b) mustn't c) should
Ver solución **b) mustn't** Significa *no debes llegar tarde* (prohibición), dado que "It's really important" indica una norma estricta.
**2.** Employees __________ wear a suit on Fridays; it's casual day. a) don't have to b) mustn't c) must
Ver solución **a) don't have to** No es necesario llevar traje los viernes (ausencia de obligación), no es una prohibición.
**3.** I __________ finish this project today. My manager is waiting for it. a) should b) must c) might
Ver solución **b) must** Es una obligación personal fuerte ("My manager is waiting"), por lo que "must" es la opción natural.
**4.** She __________ knock before entering the director's office. a) ought to b) have to c) mustn't
Ver solución **a) ought to** "Ought to" expresa una recomendación o cortesía profesional, más apropiada que una prohibición u obligación externa aquí.
**5.** You __________ submit the form before Friday if you want to be considered. a) don't have to b) have to c) mustn't
Ver solución **b) have to** Es una obligación externa impuesta por el proceso de candidatura ("if you want to be considered").
### 1.2 Modals of deduction: presente y pasado Elige el modal de deducción correcto (must / might / could / can't) y la forma adecuada (base form o have + V3). **1.** She has her laptop open and is typing. She __________ work on the report. a) must be b) can't be c) must have been
Ver solución **a) must be** Deducción en presente con fuerte certeza: vemos la evidencia de que está escribiendo.
**2.** His desk is empty and it's only 10 a.m. He __________ left for the day. a) can't have b) might have c) mustn't have
Ver solución **b) might have** Es posible que se haya ido, pero no tenemos certeza; "might have + V3" expresa posibilidad en el pasado.
**3.** The manager never misses meetings. He __________ be at the conference. a) can't b) must c) could
Ver solución **b) must** Conclusión lógica en presente: conoce su hábito y deduce que está en la conferencia.
**4.** She just read the email and looks annoyed. She __________ received some bad news. a) must have b) can't have c) might be
Ver solución **a) must have** Deducción fuerte sobre un hecho pasado ("received") basada en la reacción visible.
**5.** He's too young for this role. He __________ have ten years of experience. a) might b) could c) can't
Ver solución **c) can't** Descarte lógico en presente: no puede tener diez años de experiencia.
### 1.3 Phrasal verbs: completa con el phrasal verb correcto Completa cada oración con el phrasal verb correcto (aplicar la forma verbal adecuada). **1.** She decided to __________ the senior position. a) apply for b) turn down c) give in
Ver solución **a) apply for** *Apply for* significa *solicitar, postularse para* un puesto.
**2.** They __________ the meeting until next week because of the conflict. a) brought up b) put off c) carried out
Ver solución **b) put off** *Put off* significa *posponer, aplazar*.
**3.** He had to __________ a lot of extra responsibility after the merger. a) take on b) work out c) go through
Ver solución **a) take on** *Take on* significa *asumir* responsabilidad o trabajo.
**4.** The team needs to __________ a solution to the budget problem. a) look into b) come up with c) run into
Ver solución **b) come up with** *Come up with* significa *idear, proponer* una solución.
**5.** I __________ my old colleague at the trade fair yesterday. a) took over b) gave in c) ran into
Ver solución **c) ran into** *Run into* significa *encontrarse con* alguien por casualidad.
### 1.4 Mixed: modals + phrasal verbs Completa cada oración combinando un modal y un phrasal verb correctos. **1.** You __________ (should / carry out) a full review before launching. a) should carry out b) should carrying out c) should to carry out
Ver solución **a) should carry out** "Should" va seguido de la base form: *should carry out*.
**2.** She __________ (must / turn down) the offer because it seemed too good. a) must turned down b) must have turned down c) must turn down it
Ver solución **b) must have turned down** Deducción pasada: *must have + V3*; con el phrasal verb *turn down*.
**3.** We __________ (have to / come up with) a new strategy before Friday. a) have to come up with b) have to coming up with c) have to come up it
Ver solución **a) have to come up with** "Have to" + base form y el phrasal verb de tres palabras *come up with* (no se separa).
**4.** Employees __________ (mustn't / bring up) confidential topics in public. a) mustn't bring up b) mustn't bringing up c) mustn't to bring up
Ver solución **a) mustn't bring up** "Mustn't" + base form; *bring up* significa *sacar a colación*.
**5.** Things __________ (might / work out) if we negotiate well. a) might to work out b) might work out c) might working out
Ver solución **b) might work out** "Modal" + base form: *might work out* (salir bien).
--- ## Lección 2 — Vocabulario ### 2.1 Traducción precisa Empareja cada phrasal verb en inglés con su traducción al español. **1.** take over **2.** turn down **3.** carry out **4.** keep up with **5.** cut back on
Ver solución 1. **take over** → hacerse cargo / tomar el relevo 2. **turn down** → rechazar (una oferta) 3. **carry out** → llevar a cabo 4. **keep up with** → seguir el ritmo de 5. **cut back on** → recortar, reducir
### 2.2 Elige por definición Elige el phrasal verb correcto (a o b) para cada definición. **1.** "To create or establish a business." a) set up b) put off
Ver solución **a) set up** *Set up a business* significa *montar/crear un negocio*.
**2.** "To get on well with someone at work." a) run into b) get along with
Ver solución **b) get along with** *Get along with* significa *llevarse bien con*.
**3.** "To refuse or reject an offer." a) give in b) turn down
Ver solución **b) turn down** *Turn down* significa *rechazar*. *Give in* es *ceder*.
**4.** "To investigate or examine something carefully." a) look into b) point out
Ver solución **a) look into** *Look into* significa *investigar, indagar*.
**5.** "To finish doing something in a particular way." a) work out b) end up
Ver solución **b) end up** *End up* significa *acabar (haciendo algo)*. *Work out* es *salir bien/resolver*.
### 2.3 Completa el chunk Completa cada frase profesional con el phrasal verb correcto. **1.** The HR department is __________ a complaint about the manager. (investigando)
Ver solución **looking into** *The HR department is looking into a complaint about the manager.*
**2.** She __________ a lot of responsibility when she was promoted. (asumió)
Ver solución **took on** *She took on a lot of responsibility when she was promoted.*
**3.** We need to __________ costs this quarter. (recortar)
Ver solución **cut back on** *We need to cut back on costs this quarter.*
**4.** The manager __________ a mistake in the report. (señaló)
Ver solución **pointed out** *The manager pointed out a mistake in the report.*
**5.** He __________ the job offer because the salary was too low. (rechazó)
Ver solución **turned down** *He turned down the job offer because the salary was too low.*
### 2.4 Word formation Completa con la forma correcta de la palabra entre paréntesis en un contexto laboral. **1.** She is a successful __________ (consult) who runs her own firm.
Ver solución **consultant** *She is a successful consultant who runs her own firm.*
**2.** The __________ (employ) offered him a generous package.
Ver solución **employer** *The employer offered him a generous package.* — Sustantivo de "employ" → "employer".
**3.** They accepted his __________ (resign) after a long discussion.
Ver solución **resignation** *They accepted his resignation after a long discussion.*
**4.** Networking is essential for career __________ (advance).
Ver solución **advancement** *Networking is essential for career advancement.* — Sustantivo de "advance".
**5.** The team celebrated their latest __________ (achieve).
Ver solución **achievement** *The team celebrated their latest achievement.* — Sustantivo de "achieve".
--- ## Lección 3 — Reading Lee el siguiente texto y responde las preguntas. After five years as an engineer, Daniel decided he **should** move into project management. At first, he was afraid he **might not** have the leadership skills required. "You **mustn't** let insecurity **hold back** your ambitions," his mentor told him. Daniel **took out** time to **carry out** a self-assessment and **came up with** a clear development plan. He **applied for** an internal role, but the manager **turned down** his first request, saying he **shouldn't** rush into the position. Daniel **went through** the feedback and enrolled in a leadership course. He soon realised he **didn't have to** abandon his technical role completely; he could combine both. "I **can't have** imagined how much I'd enjoy leading a team," he says. Six months later, Daniel **took over** the project and **set up** several improvements that reduced costs. He **points out** that asking for feedback was the best decision. "Things **tend to work out** when you keep an open mind and **get along with** the right people." *(Approx. 150 words)* ### 3.1 Comprensión global Responde según el texto. **1.** What did Daniel decide to move into? a) Engineering management b) Project management c) Sales
Ver solución **b) Project management** *After five years as an engineer, Daniel decided he should move into project management.*
**2.** What did his mentor tell him? a) To give up b) Not to let insecurity hold back his ambitions c) To stay in engineering
Ver solución **b) Not to let insecurity hold back his ambitions** *"You mustn't let insecurity hold back your ambitions," his mentor told him.*
**3.** What happened when he first applied for the internal role? a) He got the job b) His request was turned down c) He withdrew his application
Ver solución **b) His request was turned down** *…but the manager turned down his first request…*
**4.** What did Daniel realise about his technical role? a) He had to abandon it b) He didn't have to abandon it completely c) He should quit
Ver solución **b) He didn't have to abandon it completely** *He soon realised he didn't have to abandon his technical role completely.*
**5.** What happened six months later? a) He left the company b) He took over the project and set up improvements c) He returned to engineering only
Ver solución **b) He took over the project and set up improvements** *Six months later, Daniel took over the project and set up several improvements.*
### 3.2 Detalles y chunks exactos Completa las oraciones usando información exacta del texto. **1.** Daniel was afraid he __________ have the leadership skills required.
Ver solución **might not** *…he was afraid he might not have the leadership skills required.*
**2.** He took out time to __________ a self-assessment.
Ver solución **carry out** *He took out time to carry out a self-assessment.*
**3.** The manager turned __________ his first request.
Ver solución **down** *…the manager turned down his first request…*
**4.** Six months later, Daniel took __________ the project.
Ver solución **over** *Six months later, Daniel took over the project…*
**5.** Things tend to __________ out when you keep an open mind.
Ver solución **work** *Things tend to work out when you keep an open mind…*
### 3.3 Forma, significado y secuencia Analiza las construcciones del texto. **1.** Why is "might not have" used instead of "must not have" in the first paragraph?
Ver solución "*Might not have*" expresa posibilidad (no estar seguro de poseer las habilidades), mientras que "*must not have*" implicaría una conclusión o prohibición. Aquí el miedo es solo una posibilidad, por eso "might" es correcto.
**2.** Explain the difference between "turned down" and "took over" in the text.
Ver solución "*Turned down*" significa *rechazar* (el manager rechazó la solicitud). "*Took over*" significa *hacerse cargo* (Daniel asumió el proyecto). Son acciones opuestas: una rechazar y otra asumir.
**3.** What does "I can't have imagined" express in the text?
Ver solución Es una deducción en pasado con "can't have + past participle": expresa un descarte fuerte — no podría haber imaginado lo mucho que disfrutaría liderar un equipo.
**4.** Why does the author use "didn't have to" instead of "mustn't"?
Ver solución "*Didn't have to*" expresa *ausencia de obligación* (no era necesario abandonar el rol técnico), mientras que "*mustn't*" expresaría *prohibición*. El contexto habla de una necesidad, no de una regla.
**5.** Identify three phrasal verbs in the text and give their meanings.
Ver solución - *carry out* → llevar a cabo - *come up with* → idear, proponer - *take over* → hacerse cargo (Otras válidas: *applied for* = solicitar, *turned down* = rechazar, *went through* = repasar, *set up* = crear, *pointed out* = señalar, *work out* = salir bien, *get along with* = llevarse bien con.)
--- ## Lección 4 — Listening **Context:** A job interview where the candidate discusses her career decisions. > **Interviewer:** So, why did you decide to **apply for** this role? > > **Candidate:** I've spent five years in sales, but I realised I **should** move into account management. I **mustn't** stay in a role where I'm not learning. > > **Interviewer:** And how would you handle a difficult client? > > **Candidate:** I'd **work out** the root problem first. It might be a communication issue. I **wouldn't** give in to pressure; instead, I'd **look into** the facts and **come up with** a solution. > > **Interviewer:** Tell me about a time you took on extra responsibility. > > **Candidate:** Last year, my manager got sick, so I **had to** take over his accounts. I **couldn't have** managed without my team, but we **carried out** a full reorganisation and things **worked out**. > > **Interviewer:** You seem very calm under pressure. > > **Candidate:** I think you **have to** stay calm in this job. You **mustn't** let stress affect your judgement. ### 4.1 Comprensión global **1.** Why did the candidate decide to leave sales? a) She was fired b) She realised she should move into account management c) The salary was too low
Ver solución **b) She realised she should move into account management** *I've spent five years in sales, but I realised I should move into account management.*
**2.** How would she handle a difficult client? a) She would give in to pressure b) She would work out the root problem first c) She would ignore the client
Ver solución **b) She would work out the root problem first** *I'd work out the root problem first.*
**3.** What did she have to do when her manager got sick? a) Quit the company b) Take over his accounts c) Hire a new manager
Ver solución **b) Take over his accounts** *…I had to take over his accounts.*
**4.** Could she have managed without her team? a) Yes b) No c) It's not mentioned
Ver solución **b) No** *I couldn't have managed without my team.*
**5.** What does she say about calmness under pressure? a) It's not important b) You have to stay calm and mustn't let stress affect your judgement c) You should avoid difficult situations
Ver solución **b) You have to stay calm and mustn't let stress affect your judgement** *I think you have to stay calm in this job. You mustn't let stress affect your judgement.*
### 4.2 Detalles y chunks exactos **1.** I __________ stay in a role where I'm not learning. (prohibición)
Ver solución **mustn't** *I mustn't stay in a role where I'm not learning.*
**2.** I'd __________ out the root problem first.
Ver solución **work** *I'd work out the root problem first.*
**3.** I wouldn't __________ in to pressure.
Ver solución **give** *I wouldn't give in to pressure.* — *give in* = ceder.
**4.** I had to take __________ his accounts.
Ver solución **over** *I had to take over his accounts.*
**5.** I couldn't have __________ without my team.
Ver solución **managed** *I couldn't have managed without my team.* — Deducción pasada con "couldn't have + V3".
### 4.3 Forma, significado y secuencia **1.** List all the modals of obligation used by the candidate and classify them.
Ver solución - *should* → consejo/recomendación - *mustn't* → prohibición - *wouldn't* → voluntad/negación - *had to* → obligación externa en pasado - *have to* → obligación externa en presente
**2.** What is the function of "couldn't have managed" in the dialogue?
Ver solución Es una deducción negativa en pasado ("can't have + V3"): expresa el descarte de que pudiera haberlo hecho sin su equipo.
**3.** Why does the candidate use "work out" and "come up with" for problem-solving?
Ver solución "*Work out*" (resolver) describe el proceso de solucionar el problema; "*come up with*" (idear) describe la generación de una solución concreta. Juntos dan naturalidad al lenguaje de resolución de problemas.
**4.** Explain the difference between "had to take over" and "have to stay calm" in terms of obligation.
Ver solución "*Had to take over*" es una obligación externa en el pasado (una situación concreta). "*Have to stay calm*" es una obligación externa general en presente (norma del puesto).
**5.** What does the interviewer's question "Tell me about a time you took on extra responsibility" test about the candidate?
Ver solución Es una pregunta de comportamiento típica en entrevistas: evalúa experiencia real, iniciativa y capacidad para gestionar el cambio, usando phrasal verbs como *take on* (asumir).
--- ## Lección 5 — Writing y Speaking ### Writing **1.** Write a short professional email (3–5 sentences) to your manager requesting a meeting, using at least one modal of obligation and one modal of deduction.
Ver modelo Dear Ms. Carter, I **would like to bring up** a concern about the project deadline. I believe we **might have** underestimated the time required for the review. We **should** schedule a short meeting to **work out** a realistic plan. Please let me know when you are available.
**2.** Write a sentence using a modal of obligation to describe a workplace rule.
Ver modelo All employees **must** complete the annual safety training before the end of the month.
**3.** Write a sentence using a modal of deduction in the present about a colleague's situation.
Ver modelo He **must be** preparing the presentation, because his office door has been closed all morning.
**4.** Write a sentence using a modal of deduction in the past about a business decision.
Ver modelo The company **must have decided** to cut costs, given that they cancelled several large projects last quarter.
**5.** Rewrite this informal sentence in a more professional tone using a modal: "You can't be late for the meeting."
Ver modelo Please **make sure you don't arrive late** for the meeting. / You **shouldn't** be late for the meeting, as it affects the whole team.
**6.** Write to a friend advising them how to prepare for a job interview, using at least 3 phrasal verbs.
Ver modelo Before the interview, you **should look into** the company carefully. Prepare questions and **come up with** examples of your achievements. If they mention something you don't know, ask them to **point out** the details. Don't **give in** to nerves — stay confident and things will **work out**.
**7.** Write an email apologising for a delay, using "should have + V3" and "won't happen again."
Ver modelo Dear Mr. Ruiz, I apologise for the delay in submitting the report. I **should have** informed you earlier about the setback. It was an oversight, and it **won't happen again**. Thank you for your patience.
**8.** Write a sentence using "don't have to" to explain a workplace flexibility.
Ver modelo You **don't have to** come into the office on Fridays; we offer remote work that day.
**9.** Write a 3-sentence professional summary using: set up, take over, turn down.
Ver modelo After the merger, the regional office **set up** a new finance team. The lead manager agreed to **take over** the project, even though she had **turned down** a similar role last year.
**10.** Write a short paragraph (50–70 words) about your career goals, using at least 2 modals of obligation and 1 phrasal verb.
Ver modelo In the next few years, I **need to** develop my leadership skills and **take on** more responsibility. I **should** seek a mentor to guide my career, and I **don't have to** change jobs to grow. My goal is to **set up** a project that combines my technical and managerial experience.
### Speaking **1.** Prepare a 1-minute monologue about your ideal job, using at least 3 modals and 2 phrasal verbs.
Consejos y modelo Suggested chunks: - *I should…* - *I need to…* - *I mustn't…* - *set up, work out, take on* Model opening: *In my ideal job, I **need to** have creative freedom. I **should** work with a team I can **get along with**, and I **mustn't** feel stuck in a routine. I would love to **set up** new projects and **take on** challenging roles that help me grow.*
**2.** Role-play a salary negotiation (employee + manager). Use modals of obligation, advice, and deduction.
Script sugerido > **Employee:** I believe I **should** receive a raise given my recent performance. > **Manager:** I understand, but we **have to** stick to the budget this year. > **Employee:** You **might have** overlooked my extra responsibilities. I **had to** take over two projects. > **Manager:** That's true. Let's **work out** a compromise — perhaps a bonus instead of a raise.
**3.** Explain in your own words the difference between "mustn't" and "don't have to".
Respuesta modelo "*Mustn't*" means something is forbidden — you are not allowed to do it. "*Don't have to*" means something is not necessary — you are free to decide. For example, "You mustn't use your phone at work" (prohibited) vs "You don't have to wear a suit" (not necessary).
**4.** Discuss with a partner: "Is it better to stay in one company or change jobs to grow your career?" Use modals and phrasal verbs in your argument.
Puntos para tu respuesta Use chunks like: - *You should…* - *You don't have to…* - *You shouldn't…* - *take on, end up, give in, work out* Example: *You **should** consider changing jobs if you aren't learning, but you **don't have to** leave if you can **take on** new responsibilities. You might **end up** regretting a hasty decision.*
**5.** Prepare a 30-second summary of the reading passage from Lección 3. Use modals and phrasal verbs.
Modelo Daniel, an engineer, decided he **should** move into project management. His mentor told him he **mustn't** let insecurity hold him back. His first application was **turned down**, but he **went through** the feedback and improved. Six months later, he **took over** the project and things **worked out**.
--- ## Tip del profesor En el trabajo, la diferencia entre *mustn't* (prohibido) y *don't have to* (no necesario) puede decidir si entiendes bien una norma o un contrato: memoriza siempre los modals como un bloque junto a su phrasal verb favorito y el contexto laboral. --- ## Siguiente paso en el curso B2 Continúa con la **Unidad 54 del curso B2**: *Linkers y Collocations* con *Política y Relaciones Internacionales*. - [Unidad 53 del curso](/curso-b2/unit-53) - [Continuar con Unidad 54](/curso-b2/unit-54) ### Guías relacionadas - [U52 Passive & Reported Speech](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-52-passive-reported-speech-human-rights) - [U54 Linkers & Collocations](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-54-linkers-collocations-geopolitics) - [Inglés B2](/blog/metodos/ingles-b2) --- ## Preguntas frecuentes ### ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre must, have to y need to? *Must* expresa una obligación personal o una deducción fuerte: *You must finish the report.* *Have to* describe una obligación externa impuesta por otros: *She has to arrive at 9.* *Need to* expresa una necesidad subjetiva: *We need to update the CV.* Todos van seguidos de la base form (sin "to"), excepto "have to" y "need to" que ya llevan "to". ### ¿Cómo se forman los phrasal verbs con separación? Si el objeto es un pronombre, siempre va entre el verbo y la partícula: *pick it up, turn it down.* Si es un sustantivo, puede ir antes o después: *pick up the phone* o *pick the phone up.* Los phrasal verbs de tres palabras (*come up with, get along with, keep up with*) no se separan. ### ¿Qué modals uso para deducción? Para deducción en presente: *must* (conclusión fuerte), *might/could* (posibilidad), *can't* (descarte fuerte). Para el pasado: *must have + V3, might have + V3, can't have + V3.* Ejemplo: *She must be working late. She might have left.* ### ¿Cómo aprendo phrasal verbs de forma natural? Aprende el verbo y la partícula como una sola unidad con su contexto: *set up a business, take on responsibility, turn down an offer, work out a solution.* No los separe palabra por palabra; súbelos en frases completas y pratícalos en speaking y writing. ### ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 53? En la Unidad 53 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría completa y ejercicios con soluciones en formato interactivo. --- ## Fuentes - CEFR/MCER — Nivel B2: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages - British Council — B1–B2 grammar: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/b1-b2-grammar - Cambridge Dictionary — Grammar and vocabulary reference: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre although, despite y in spite of?
faqs.answer: Although va seguido de clause (sujeto + verbo). Despite e in spite of van seguidos de noun/gerund: Despite the crisis, the economy grew. Although the crisis hit, the economy grew.

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso so that vs in order to?
faqs.answer: Ambos expresan propósito. So that va seguido de clause (con modal): She studied hard so that she could pass. In order to va seguido de infinitivo: She studied hard in order to pass.

faqs.question: ¿Qué collocations son más frecuentes en política?
faqs.answer: Hold elections, impose sanctions, reach an agreement, sign a treaty, conduct negotiations, maintain stability, break down talks, bilateral relations.

faqs.question: ¿Puedo usar moreover y furthermore indistintamente?
faqs.answer: Sí, son sinónimos. Moreover añade información nueva; furthermore añade un argumento adicional más formal. Ambos son adecuados para writing académico y formal.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 54?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 54 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones.

content:
# Unidad 54 — Linkers y Collocations: Política y Relaciones Internacionales La **Unidad 54** integra **linkers** de contraste, causa, propósito y adición con **collocations** del ámbito de la política y las relaciones internacionales. Cada conector sitúa la información correctamente; cada colocación aporta precisión léxica al registro formal. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 54](/curso-b2/unit-54)
> **Antes:** [U53 — Modals & Phrasal Verbs + Career](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-53-modals-phrasal-verbs-career)
> **Siguiente:** [Unidad 55 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-55) --- ## 1. Linkers of Contrast Los linkers de contraste expresan oposición, concesión o diferencia entre dos ideas. En textos políticos son esenciales para presentar argumentos equilibrados y análisis críticos. ### 1.1 Although / Even though **Although** y **even though** introducen una clause (sujeto + verbo) que contrasta con la idea principal. *Even though* es más enfático. | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | **Although** the president promised reforms, no legislation was passed. | Aunque el presidente prometió reformas, no se aprobó ninguna ley. | | **Even though** the opposition boycotted the vote, the referendum went ahead. | Aunque la oposición boicoteó la votación, el referéndum siguió adelante. | | **Although** both nations signed the accord, implementation remains uncertain. | Aunque ambas naciones firmaron el acuerdo, la implementación sigue siendo incierta. | ### 1.2 Despite / In spite of **Despite** e **in spite of** van seguidos de un **noun** o un **gerund** (no de una clause completa). | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | **Despite** the economic sanctions, the regime continued its nuclear programme. | A pesar de las sanciones económicas, el régimen continuó su programa nuclear. | | **In spite of** diplomatic efforts, the peace talks broke down. | A pesar de los esfuerzos diplomáticos, las conversaciones de paz se rompieron. | | **Despite** mounting pressure, the government refused to hold elections. | A pesar de la creciente presión, el gobierno se negó a convocar elecciones. | > **Error común:** ~~Despite the government resigned~~ → **Despite the government's resignation** / **Although the government resigned** ### 1.3 Whereas / While **Whereas** y **while** comparan dos situaciones o destacan una diferencia. *Whereas* es más formal y habitual en writing académico. | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | **Whereas** the US favour free trade, the EU often promotes protectionist policies. | Mientras que EE.UU. favorece el libre comercio, la UE a menudo promueve políticas proteccionistas. | | **While** some delegates supported the resolution, others demanded amendments. | Mientras algunos delegados apoyaron la resolución, otros exigieron enmiendas. | ### 1.4 However / Nevertheless **However** y **nevertheless** conectan oraciones completas y expresan contraste. Van precedidos de punto y coma o punto, y seguidos de coma. | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | The treaty was widely praised; **however**, its enforcement mechanisms are weak. | El tratado fue ampliamente elogiado; sin embargo, sus mecanismos de cumplimiento son débiles. | | The sanctions have not achieved their goal. **Nevertheless**, they remain in place. | Las sanciones no han logrado su objetivo. No obstante, siguen en vigor. | ### 1.5 Errores frecuentes: Linkers de contraste | Error | Correcto | Explicación | | --- | --- | --- | | ~~Despite it was raining~~ | **Although it was raining** | *Despite* + noun/gerund; *although* + clause | | ~~Although of the crisis~~ | **Despite the crisis** | *Although* requires a clause, not a noun | | ~~Whereas he is poor, he is happy~~ | **Although he is poor, he is happy** | *Whereas* compara dos hechos; para concesión usa *although* | | ~~However the results~~ | **However, the results** | *However* lleva coma después | | ~~In spite of the treaty was signed~~ | **In spite of the treaty being signed** | *In spite of* + gerund, no clause | --- ## 2. Linkers of Reason, Purpose and Result Estos conectores establecen relaciones causales, de propósito o de consecuencia. Son indispensables en análisis políticos y editoriales. ### 2.1 Because / Since / As Introducen la **causa** o razón de algo. *Because* es el más directo; *since* y *as* son más formales. | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | **Because** the economy stagnated, the government introduced austerity measures. | Debido a que la economía se estancó, el gobierno introdujo medidas de austeridad. | | **Since** both parties refused to compromise, negotiations collapsed. | Dado que ambas partes se negaron a comprometerse, las negociaciones fracasaron. | | **As** public trust eroded, calls for early elections intensified. | Como la confianza pública se deterioró, las llamadas a elecciones anticipadas se intensificaron. | ### 2.2 So / So that **So** introduce una consecuencia. **So that** introduce un propósito (acompañado de *can/could/will/would*). | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | The president raised taxes, **so** public unrest grew. | El presidente subió impuestos, por lo que la inquietud pública creció. | | The delegation negotiated **so that** a ceasefire could be established. | La delegación negoció para que pudiera establecerse un alto el fuego. | | Funding was increased **so that** humanitarian aid could reach civilians. | Se aumentó el financiamiento para que la ayuda humanitaria pudiera llegar a los civiles. | ### 2.3 In order to Expresa propósito con infinitivo. Más formal que *so that*. | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | **In order to** stabilise the region, troops were deployed along the border. | Con el fin de estabilizar la región, se desplegaron tropas a lo largo de la frontera. | | **In order to** prevent further escalation, the UN sent envoys. | Con el fin de prevenir una mayor escalada, la ONU envió enviados. | ### 2.4 Therefore / Consequently / As a result Conectan una oración completa con su consecuencia lógica. Formalidad creciente. | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | The resolution was vetoed. **Therefore**, alternative measures were considered. | La resolución fue vetada. Por lo tanto, se consideraron medidas alternativas. | | Trade volumes dropped sharply. **Consequently**, unemployment rose. | Los volúmenes comerciales cayeron drásticamente. En consecuencia, el desempleo aumentó. | | The ceasefire collapsed. **As a result**, civilian casualties increased. | El alto el fuego colapsó. Como resultado, las bajas civiles aumentaron. | ### 2.5 Errores frecuentes: Linkers de causa, propósito y resultado | Error | Correcto | Explicación | | --- | --- | --- | | ~~Because of the economy collapsed~~ | **Because the economy collapsed** | *Because* + clause; *because of* + noun | | ~~So that to improve relations~~ | **In order to improve relations** | *So that* + clause con modal; no + infinitivo directo | | ~~Therefore, the government acted quickly~~ | **The government acted quickly. Therefore, ...** | *Therefore* conecta ideas; no inicia una oración que es causa | | ~~As a result of the talks failed~~ | **As a result, the talks failed** | *As a result* es linker entre cláusulas; *as a result of* + noun | | ~~Due to the minister resigned~~ | **Due to the minister's resignation** | *Due to* + noun; para clause usa *because* | --- ## 3. Linkers of Addition and Listing Añaden información, refuerzan argumentos o enumeran puntos. Clave en ensayos formales y discursos políticos. ### 3.1 Moreover / Furthermore / What's more Añaden información o argumentos adicionales. *Moreover* y *furthermore* son formales; *what's more* es ligeramente menos formal. | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | The country faces inflation. **Moreover**, its debt has reached record levels. | El país enfrenta inflación. Además, su deuda ha alcanzado niveles récord. | | The peace deal was fragile. **Furthermore**, neither side trusted the other. | El acuerdo de paz era frágil. Además, ninguna parte confiaba en la otra. | | The opposition won the popular vote. **What's more**, it secured a majority in parliament. | La oposición ganó el voto popular. Además, obtuvo mayoría en el parlamento. | ### 3.2 In addition / Besides **In addition** añade un punto nuevo de forma formal. **Besides** añade un argumento que refuerza la idea anterior. | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | **In addition** to trade tariffs, the US imposed travel restrictions. | Además de los aranceles comerciales, EE.UU. impuso restricciones de viaje. | | **Besides** the economic costs, the conflict caused a massive refugee crisis. | Además de los costes económicos, el conflicto causó una crisis migratoria masiva. | ### 3.3 Not only... but also / Both... and **Not only... but also** enfatiza una idea inesperada. **Both... and** iguala dos elementos. | Ejemplo | Traducción | | --- | --- | | **Not only** did the ambassador resign, **but also** the foreign minister stepped down. | No solo renunció el embajador, sino que también dimitió el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores. | | **Both** France **and** Germany supported the proposed sanctions. | Tanto Francia como Alemania apoyaron las sanciones propuestas. | ### 3.4 Errores frecuentes: Linkers de adición | Error | Correcto | Explicación | | --- | --- | --- | | ~~Moreover of the evidence~~ | **Moreover, the evidence** | *Moreover* es adverbio, va con coma, no + *of* | | ~~Not only the president but also~~ | **Not only did the president... but also** | *Not only* antepuesto invierte el orden (aux + sujeto) | | ~~Besides to the treaty~~ | **Besides the treaty** | *Besides* + noun; no + *to* | | ~~In addition for~~ | **In addition to** | La preposición correcta es *to* | | ~~Both the economy and is weak~~ | **Both the economy and the currency are weak** | *Both... and* enlaza elementos paralelos de misma categoría | --- ## 4. --- ## 7. Writing — Formal Essays and Reports En writing de nivel B2, los linkers son esenciales para conectar ideas de forma coherente. Ensayos y reportes sobre temas políticos requieren registro formal. ### Tips para writing formal - **Abre** con un linker de causa o concesión: *Although the issue is complex, several solutions have been proposed.* - **Desarrolla** párrafos con *moreover*, *furthermore* o *in addition* para añadir argumentos. - **Cierra** con *therefore*, *consequently* o *as a result* para sintetizar conclusiones. - Usa collocations precisas: *conduct negotiations*, *impose sanctions*, *reach an agreement*. ### Modelo de párrafo formal > Although the peace talks were initially promising, several obstacles emerged. Both sides refused to compromise on key territorial issues. Moreover, external actors complicated the process by funding opposing factions. Consequently, the negotiations broke down after three months. Nevertheless, diplomats remain committed to finding a solution, and further talks are expected to be conducted before the end of the year. ![Writing tips](/blog/curso-b2/unit-54/writing-tips.png) --- ## 8. Speaking En speaking de nivel B2, los linkers te permiten organizar tus ideas de forma fluida y convencer a tu interlocutor. ### Tips para speaking sobre política - **Opinión + linker + justificación:** *In my view, although sanctions are necessary, they should be proportionate.* - **Contraargumento:** *However, one could argue that diplomatic ties are more effective in the long run.* - **Enumerar:** *Furthermore, we should consider economic, social, and environmental factors.* - **Concluir:** *Therefore, a multilateral approach is essential.* ### Frases útiles - "What strikes me is that **although** the treaty was signed, implementation has been minimal." - "**Moreover**, the economic sanctions have not achieved their stated objectives." - "**In spite of** these setbacks, I believe **furthermore** negotiations could yield results." - "**Consequently**, the international community must adopt a more coordinated strategy." --- ## 9. Despite e in spite of van seguidos de noun/gerund: Despite the crisis, the economy grew. Although the crisis hit, the economy grew. **¿Cuándo uso so that vs in order to?** Ambos expresan propósito. So that va seguido de clause (con modal): She studied hard so that she could pass. In order to va seguido de infinitivo: She studied hard in order to pass. **¿Qué collocations son más frecuentes en política?** Hold elections, impose sanctions, reach an agreement, sign a treaty, conduct negotiations, maintain stability, break down talks, bilateral relations. **¿Puedo usar moreover y furthermore indistintamente?** Sí, son sinónimos. Moreover añade información nueva; furthermore añade un argumento adicional más formal. Ambos son adecuados para writing académico y formal. **¿Dónde practico la Unidad 54?** En la Unidad 54 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones. --- --- # Ejercicios — Unidad 54 ## Lección 1 — Gramática y Chunks ### 1.1 Linkers of Contrast **Elige el linker correcto: although / despite / whereas / however** 1. ______ the summit was a success, several delegates expressed frustration. 2. ______ the economic downturn, the government maintained its spending levels. 3. ______ the US promotes free trade, the EU tends to adopt protectionist measures. 4. The treaty was signed in 2015; ______, implementation has been disappointing. 5. ______ numerous calls for reform, the parliament took no action.
Ver solução 1. **Although** — *although* + clause (sujeto + verbo: *the summit was a success*) 2. **Despite** — *despite* + noun (*the economic downturn*) 3. **Whereas** — *whereas* compara dos situaciones 4. **however** — *however* conecta oraciones completas con punto y coma 5. **Despite** — *despite* + noun (*numerous calls for reform*)
### 1.2 Linkers of Reason / Purpose / Result **Elige el linker correcto: because / so that / therefore / as a result** 1. The economy contracted sharply; ______, unemployment reached 12%. 2. The ambassador was recalled ______ she publicly criticised the government. 3. Troops were deployed ______ violence could be contained. 4. The government raised taxes. ______, public trust declined further. 5. The UN imposed an arms embargo ______ the conflict was escalating rapidly.
Ver solução 1. **therefore** — *therefore* conecta consecuencia lógica entre oraciones 2. **because** — *because* + clause introduciendo la razón 3. **so that** — *so that* + clause con modal (*could*) para expresar propósito 4. **As a result** — *as a result* introduce la consecuencia 5. **because** — *because* + clause (razón: *the conflict was escalating*)
### 1.3 Linkers of Addition **Elige el linker correcto: moreover / furthermore / in addition / not only** 1. ______ the president refused to negotiate, ______ the opposition threatened to boycott. 2. The country faces rising inflation. ______, its national debt has doubled. 3. ______ to military intervention, economic sanctions were imposed. 4. The peace deal included territorial concessions. ______, it established a framework for power sharing. 5. ______ did the ambassador resign, but also the entire cabinet stepped down.
Ver solução 1. **Not only... but also** — estructura *not only* + inversión + *but also* 2. **Moreover** — *moreover* añade un argumento adicional con coma 3. **In addition** — *in addition to* + noun (*military intervention*) 4. **Furthermore** — *furthermore* añade información adicional formal 5. **Not only** — *Not only* + did + sujeto + verbo (inversión obligatoria)
### 1.4 Mixed Linkers **Elige el linker correcto: although / as a result / moreover / despite / in order to / nevertheless** 1. The talks collapsed. ______, both sides returned to their positions. 2. ______ the economic benefits, many residents opposed the construction. 3. The agreement was praised internationally. ______, critics warned it was unenforceable. 4. ______ several attempts at mediation, the conflict continued unabated. 5. The government increased border patrols ______ prevent illegal crossings.
Ver solução 1. **As a result** — *as a result* introduce consecuencia 2. **Despite** — *despite* + noun (*the economic benefits*) 3. **Nevertheless** — *nevertheless* expresa contraste entre oraciones completas 4. **Despite** — *despite* + noun (*several attempts at mediation*) 5. **in order to** — *in order to* + infinitivo para expresar propósito

**Ejercicio 4:** Escribe una oración de propósito usando *in order to*. Use: stabilise — region — deploy troops
Ver solução **In order to** stabilise the region, troops were deployed.
**Ejercicio 5:** Escribe una oración con *not only... but also* incluyendo inversión. Use: ambassador resign — foreign minister resign
Ver solução **Not only did the ambassador resign**, but the foreign minister also stepped down.
**Ejercicio 6:** Reescribe usando *consequently*. The ceasefire collapsed. Civilian casualties increased dramatically.
Ver solução The ceasefire collapsed. **Consequently**, civilian casualties increased dramatically.
**Ejercicio 7:** Escribe un párrafo de 40–60 palabras sobre por qué los acuerdos comerciales son importantes. Usa al menos 3 collocations y 2 linkers.
Ver solução **Modelo de respuesta:** International trade agreements are essential for economic growth. Moreover, they help maintain stability between neighbouring nations. When countries reach an agreement on tariffs, bilateral relations tend to improve. Furthermore, trade agreements create jobs and reduce poverty. Therefore, governments should prioritise diplomatic negotiations to reach mutually beneficial deals. *Collocations usadas:* trade agreements, maintain stability, reach an agreement, bilateral relations, diplomatic negotiations. *Linkers usadas:* moreover, furthermore, therefore.
**Ejercicio 8:** Corrige los 5 errores en este párrafo. > Despite it was a difficult time, the government held elections. Moreover of the protests, the referendum went ahead. Both the economy and is fragile. In addition for trade, diplomatic ties were strengthened. Therefore, the president acted quickly, so that public confidence could be restored.
Ver solução > **Although** it was a difficult time, the government held elections. **Despite** the protests, the referendum went ahead. **Both** the economy **and** the currency are fragile. **In addition to** trade, diplomatic ties were strengthened. **Therefore**, the president acted quickly **so that** public confidence could be restored. *Errores corregidos:* 1. ~~Despite it was~~ → **Although it was** (although + clause) 2. ~~Moreover of~~ → **Despite** (despite + noun) 3. ~~and is~~ → **and the currency are** (both... and parallel) 4. ~~In addition for~~ → **In addition to** (preposición correcta) 5. ~~Therefore,~~ before the cause → reordered (therefore conecta consecuencia)
**Ejercicio 9:** Escribe un informe formal de 80–100 palabras sobre una crisis diplomática. Usa: *despite*, *in order to*, *as a result*, *bilateral relations*, *impose sanctions*, *reach an agreement*.
Ver solução **Modelo de respuesta:** The diplomatic crisis between the two nations escalated rapidly in January. Despite several rounds of mediation, neither side was willing to compromise on territorial claims. In order to de-escalate tensions, the UN Security Council convened an emergency session. As a result, both countries agreed to a temporary ceasefire. However, reaching a lasting agreement will require sustained diplomatic engagement. The international community has called on both governments to maintain stability and avoid imposing sanctions that could further damage bilateral relations.
**Ejercicio 10:** Completa este email formal con los linkers y collocations correctos. > Dear Minister, > > I am writing to inform you that ______ [although/despite] our best efforts, the trade negotiations have ______ [broken down / hold elections]. ______ [Moreover / Despite] the economic benefits of a deal, both sides remain divided on key issues. ______ [In order to / Because of] prevent further escalation, I recommend that ______ [bilateral relations / trade agreement] be prioritised at the upcoming summit.
Ver solução > Dear Minister, > > I am writing to inform you that **although** our best efforts, the trade negotiations have **broken down**. **Despite** the economic benefits of a deal, both sides remain divided on key issues. **In order to** prevent further escalation, I recommend that **bilateral relations** be prioritised at the upcoming summit.
### Speaking (Ejercicios 11–15) **Ejercicio 11:** Prepárate para hablar durante 2 minutos sobre el siguiente tema. Usa al menos 3 collocations y 2 linkers. *"Should countries impose economic sanctions to resolve international conflicts?"* Estructura sugerida: - Opinión personal - Argumento a favor (con linker de adición) - Argumento en contra (con linker de contraste) - Conclusión (con linker de resultado)
Ver solução **Modelo de respuesta (guion):** In my opinion, economic sanctions can be an effective tool in international relations, although they must be used carefully. **Moreover**, they offer a non-violent alternative to military intervention. **For instance**, when the UN imposed sanctions on a regime that violated human rights, it sent a strong diplomatic message. **However**, I also believe that sanctions can disproportionately affect ordinary citizens. **Despite** their intended targets being governments, it is often civilians who suffer the most. **Furthermore**, history shows that sanctions rarely achieve their stated goals quickly. **Consequently**, I think sanctions should be part of a broader strategy that includes diplomatic ties and peace talks. **In order to** resolve conflicts effectively, nations must reach agreements through multilateral negotiations rather than relying solely on economic pressure.
**Ejercicio 12:** Practica esta respuesta exprés (30–45 segundos). Usa *although*, *therefore* y *reach an agreement*. *"What do you think is the biggest challenge in international diplomacy?"*
Ver solução **Modelo de respuesta:** The biggest challenge in international diplomacy is achieving consensus among nations with conflicting interests. Although organisations like the UN provide a platform for dialogue, reaching an agreement on issues such as climate change or nuclear disarmament remains extremely difficult. Different political systems, economic priorities, and cultural perspectives often create deadlocks. Therefore, I believe that patience, compromise, and sustained bilateral relations are essential to overcome these obstacles.
**Ejercicio 13:** Debate en pareja. Tema: *"Should the EU impose sanctions on countries that violate human rights?"* Usa estas frases en tu debate: - *"Not only... but also"* - *"Nevertheless"* - *"In order to"* - *"bilateral relations"*
Ver solução **Modelo de debate:** **A:** I think the EU should impose sanctions. Not only would this demonstrate a commitment to human rights, but it would also pressure violators to change their behaviour. **B:** I see your point. Nevertheless, history shows that sanctions often harm civilians more than governments. Moreover, they can damage bilateral relations. **A:** That's a fair point. In order to avoid that, perhaps the EU should impose targeted sanctions on specific individuals rather than broad economic measures. **B:** I agree. Furthermore, diplomatic ties should be maintained so that dialogue remains possible.
**Ejercicio 14:** Describe esta situación usando al menos 4 collocations. *"Two neighbouring countries have been in conflict for years. A mediator has been appointed to help them negotiate."*
Ver solução **Modelo de respuesta:** Two neighbouring countries have been in conflict for years, despite numerous attempts at mediation. The dispute has affected bilateral relations and led to the severing of diplomatic ties. Both nations have imposed economic sanctions on each other, which has damaged trade and increased instability. Recently, a mediator was appointed to conduct negotiations and help the parties reach an agreement. The ultimate goal is to establish power sharing arrangements and maintain stability in the region. Moreover, both governments have expressed willingness to sign a treaty if progress is made. *Collocations usadas:* bilateral relations, diplomatic ties, economic sanctions, conduct negotiations, reach an agreement, power sharing, maintain stability, sign a treaty, moreover.
**Ejercicio 15:** Graba una presentación de 2 minutos sobre un tratado internacional conocido (Paris,Geneva, etc.). Estructura: 1. Contexto histórico (although / despite) 2. Contenido principal (moreover / in order to) 3. Resultados (therefore / as a result) 4. Valoración personal (nevertheless)
Ver solução **Modelo de presentación:** The Geneva Conventions, signed in 1949, represent one of the most important achievements in international humanitarian law. Although warfare has evolved significantly since then, the conventions remain the foundation of the rules of armed conflict. Despite their age, they continue to provide essential protections for civilians and prisoners of war. Moreover, the conventions establish clear guidelines for the treatment of wounded soldiers and regulate the use of certain weapons. In order to ensure compliance, an international monitoring system was created. Furthermore, nations that violate the conventions can face diplomatic isolation and economic sanctions. As a result, the Geneva Conventions have saved countless lives. Therefore, they remain a cornerstone of international relations. Nevertheless, critics argue that enforcement mechanisms need to be strengthened to address modern challenges such as cyber warfare and asymmetric conflicts.
--- ## Fuentes - Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR/MCER) — Council of Europe - British Council — LearnEnglish: Linkers and connectors - Cambridge Dictionary — Linkers of contrast, addition, cause - Oxford Learner's Dictionary — Common collocations in English - United Nations Treaty Collection — International agreements database

faqs.answer: Integra U51–54: wish/if only + past perfect, third conditional, mixed conditional, passive all tenses, passive reporting, reported speech, modals of obligation/deduction, phrasal verbs, linkers y collocations.
