faqs.answer: En la Unidad 55 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones.

content:
# Repaso B2 Unidades 51–54: Gramática, Vocabulario y Globalización La **Unidad 55** consolida la gramática y el vocabulario de **U51–54**. La lección viva combina wish/if only, third conditional, mixed conditionals, passive voice, passive reporting, reported speech, modals of obligation/deduction, phrasal verbs, linkers of contrast/reason/addition y collocations de política y relaciones internacionales. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 55](/curso-b2/unit-55)
> **Antes:** [U54 — Linkers & Collocations + Geopolitics](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-54-linkers-collocations-geopolitics)
> **Siguiente:** [Unidad 56 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-56) --- ## 1. Un repaso de decisiones, no de etiquetas Un error habitual al repasar es memorizar reglas aisladas en lugar de reconocer **qué decisión comunicativa** produce cada estructura. En B2, el examinador no busca que sepas nominar la estructura; busca que sepas **usarla en contexto**. Cada herramienta gramatical que hemos visto responde a una función concreta: | Función comunicativa | Estructura (U51–54) | Ejemplo | |---|---|---| | Expresar lamento o deseo irreal | Wish / If only + past perfect | *If only we had invested earlier.* | | Hipótesis sobre el pasado | Third conditional | *We would have grown faster if the tariff had been lower.* | | Escenario que mezcla pasado y presente | Mixed conditional | *If the policy had changed, we would be in a better position now.* | | Destacar la acción, no el agente | Passive voice (todos los tiempos) | *New sanctions were imposed last week.* | | Reportar fórmulas oficiales | Passive reporting | *It is believed that the economy will slow down.* | | Trans ideas de terceros | Reported speech | *The minister said that unemployment had risen.* | | Obligación / deducción | Modals (must, have to, should, might) | *They must have known about the risk.* | | Acción verbal cotidiana | Phrasal verbs | *The government has set up a new committee.* | | Conectar ideas | Linkers (although, despite, in addition) | *Although growth slowed, investment rose.* | | Combinar palabras frecuentes | Collocations | *draw a conclusion, reach an agreement* | Lee esta tabla como un mapa de decisiones, no como una lista para memorizar. Cuando hablas o escribes, la pregunta no es «¿qué estructura es?» sino **«¿qué quiero comunicar y qué herramienta me lleva allí?»**. --- ## 2. U51: Wish/If Only y Third Conditional — contexto de economía En **U51** aprendimos a expresar deseos sobre el pasado (wish/if only + past perfect) y a construir hipótesis completas sobre situaciones pasadas (third conditional). Ambos apuntan al pasado, pero con matices distintos. ### 2.1 Wish / If only + past perfect — lamento Se usa para **lamentar** algo que ya pasó o **desear** que el pasado hubiera sido diferente. El tono es subjetivo, personal. - *I wish I **had saved** more money before the crisis.* (Lamento personal) - *If only the government **had acted** sooner.* (Frustración / reproche) - *She wishes she **hadn't invested** in that company.* (Arrepentimiento) ### 2.2 Third conditional — hipótesis sobre el pasado El third conditional construye una **realidad alternativa** completa: si X hubiera pasado, Y habría sido el resultado. No hay juicio emocional; es una hipótesis lógica. - *If the central bank **had raised** rates, inflation **would have dropped**.* - *If trade barriers **had not existed**, the company **would have expanded** into Asia.* - *Had the agreement been signed earlier, we **would have avoided** the losses.* ### 2.3 Mixed conditional — pasado → presente Mezcla un if-clause en pasado perfect con un resultado en condicional simple. Es decir: una decisión del pasado que afecta **ahora**. - *If the reforms **had been implemented**, the economy **would be** stronger today.* - *If we **had signed** the deal, we **wouldn't be** in this situation now.* ### 2.4 Contraste: wish vs. third conditional | | Wish / If only | Third conditional | |---|---|---| | **Función** | Lamento, deseo emocional | Hipótesis lógica, causa-efecto | | **Tono** | Subjetivo, a menudo frustrado | Analítico, neutral | | **Resultado** | No especifica qué habría cambiado | Especifica el resultado alternativo | | **Ejemplo** | *I wish I had negotiated harder.* | *If I had negotiated harder, I would have got a better deal.* | > **Pista de función:** Si la frase suena a quejido → wish. Si suena a análisis → third conditional. > 🎧 **Audio:** --- ## 3. U52: Passive Voice, Passive Reporting y Reported Speech — contexto de justicia **U52** giró en torno a **quién hace la acción y quién la recibe**, y a cómo reportamos lo que otros dicen o creen. ### 3.1 Passive voice — todos los tiempos La voz pasiva se construye con **be + past participle** y se usa cuando el **receptor** de la acción es más importante que el agente, o cuando el agente es desconocido/irrelevante. | Tiempo | Ejemplo (justicia) | |---|---| | Present simple | *Laws **are enforced** by the authorities.* | | Present continuous | *The case **is being investigated** right now.* | | Past simple | *The verdict **was announced** yesterday.* | | Past continuous | *The evidence **was being examined** when the appeal was filed.* | | Present perfect | *Several charges **have been brought** against the defendant.* | | Past perfect | *The documents **had been destroyed** before the audit.* | | Future simple | *A new inquiry **will be launched** next month.* | | Modals | *The sentence **could be reduced** on appeal.* | ### 3.2 Passive reporting — fórmulas institucionales Las construcciones de reporting pasivo son **it + passive + that / to infinitive**. Son habituales en noticias, informes y contextos formales. - ***It is believed** that the suspect has fled the country.* - ***It is reported** that the trial will begin in September.* - ***He is said to have left** the country before the warrant was issued.* - ***She is thought to be** the key witness.* ### 3.3 Reported speech — transformación completa El reported speech requiere **backshift** de tiempos y ajustes de pronombres y deícticos. | Directo | Indirecto (backshift) | |---|---| | "I **am** innocent," he said. | He said he **was** innocent. | | "The trial **will start** Monday," the lawyer stated. | The lawyer stated the trial **would start** the following Monday. | | "We **have reached** a verdict," the foreman announced. | The foreman announced they **had reached** a verdict. | | "I **was** at the scene," she claimed. | She claimed she **had been** at the scene. | > **Pista de función:** Si la fuente es una institución o un periódico → passive reporting. Si estás citando a alguien directamente → reported speech. > 🎧 **Audio:** --- ## 4. U53: Modals of Obligation/Deduction y Phrasal Verbs — contexto de carrera profesional **U53** combinó modales (obligación y deducción) con phrasal verbs de uso frecuente en el ámbito laboral. ### 4.1 Modals of obligation | Modal | Fuerza | Ejemplo (carrera) | |---|---|---| | **must** | Obligación interna, regla firme | *You **must** submit the report by Friday.* | | **have to** | Obligación externa, regla institucional | *We **have to** follow the company's compliance policy.* | | **should** | Recomendación, consejo profesional | *You **should** update your CV before the interview.* | | **mustn't** | Prohibición | *You **mustn't** share confidential data.* | | **don't have to** | No hay obligación | *You **don't have to** wear a tie on casual Fridays.* | ### 4.2 Modals of deduction | Modal | Certeza | Ejemplo (deducción) | |---|---|---| | **must** | Alta certeza (90%+) | *She **must be** the new project manager — everyone is following her instructions.* | | **might / may** | Posibilidad media | *He **might have missed** the deadline because of the meeting.* | | **can't** | Imposibilidad | *They **can't have finished** the audit already — it only started yesterday.* | ### 4.3 Phrasal verbs — ámbito profesional Los phrasal verbs son una barrera clásica para hablantes no nativos. En B2 debes conocer los más frecuentes y reconocer si son **separables** o **inseparables**. **Separables** (el pronombre va entre el verbo y la partícula): - *carry out* → *The team carried out the analysis.* → *They carried **it** out.* - *set up* → *We set up the meeting.* → *We set **it** up.* - *bring up* → *She brought up the issue.* → *She brought **it** up.* - *work out* → *Can you work out the budget?* → *Can you work **it** out?* **Inseparables** (el pronombre va después de la partícula): - *come across* → *I came across an interesting report.* - *run into* → *We ran into a problem with the software.* - *look into* → *The manager will look into the complaint.* - *stick to* → *We need to stick to the original plan.* > **Pista de función:** Si el contexto exige obligación → must / have to / should. Si exige deducción → must / might / can't + perfecto. Si es una acción cotidiana verbal → phrasal verb. > 🎧 **Audio:** --- ## 5. U54: Linkers y Collocations — contexto de geopolítica **U54** cerró el bloque con conectores discursivos y collocations del campo de relaciones internacionales. ### 5.1 Linkers de contraste - ***Although** the sanctions were imposed, trade continued to grow.* - ***Despite** the political tensions, both countries signed the agreement.* - ***However**, the long-term effects remain unclear.* - ***Even though** the economy slowed, employment figures improved.* - ***Nevertheless**, the government proceeded with the reforms.* ### 5.2 Linkers de causa y razón - ***Because of** the energy crisis, manufacturing output declined.* - ***Due to** rising interest rates, foreign investment has decreased.* - ***As a result**, the central bank was forced to intervene.* - ***Owing to** the conflict, supply chains were disrupted.* - ***Since** the agreement was signed, bilateral trade has doubled.* ### 5.3 Linkers de adición - ***In addition**, the treaty includes environmental provisions.* - ***Moreover**, the cultural exchange has strengthened diplomatic ties.* - ***Furthermore**, the economic data supports the decision.* - ***Also**, both nations have committed to renewable energy targets.* - ***What's more**, the partnership extends to defence cooperation.* ### 5.4 Collocations — relaciones internacionales | Collocation | Significado | Ejemplo | |---|---|---| | **forge an alliance** | crear una alianza | *The two nations forged a strong alliance.* | | **reach an agreement** | llegar a un acuerdo | *They finally reached an agreement on tariffs.* | | **impose sanctions** | imponer sanciones | *The UN imposed sanctions on the regime.* | | **conduct diplomacy** | llevar a cabo diplomacia | *The country conducted quiet diplomacy behind the scenes.* | | **tackle a crisis** | abordar una crisis | *Leaders gathered to tackle the economic crisis.* | | **draw a conclusion** | llegar a una conclusión | *The committee drew the conclusion that reform was needed.* | | **lift restrictions** | levantar restricciones | *The government lifted travel restrictions last month.* | | **broker a peace deal** | negociar un acuerdo de paz | *The mediator brokered a historic peace deal.* | > 🎧 **Audio:** --- ## 6. Vocabulario conectado de U51–54 El vocabulario de globalización no vive en unidades sueltas: se conecta en redes temáticas. Aquí tienes una visión transversal. | Campo | Palabras clave (U51–54) | |---|---| | **Economía** | tariff, inflation, investment, recession, fiscal policy, trade deficit | | **Justicia** | verdict, sentence, appeal, indictment, prosecution, jurisdiction | | **Carrera profesional** | compliance, deadline, promotion, review, networking, appraisal | | **Política** | sanction, embargo, bilateral, summit, legislation, electorate | | **Relaciones internacionales** | diplomacy, treaty, alliance, ceasefire, mediation, sovereignty | > 📸 **Imagen:** --- ## 7. Reading integrado Lee el siguiente texto e identifica al menos **tres estructuras gramaticales** de U51–54 en cada párrafo. --- ### The Hidden Costs of Globalisation Globalisation has transformed the world economy over the past four decades, yet its consequences are far more complex than most policymakers anticipated. While trade liberalisation has lifted millions out of poverty, it has also **created** deep inequalities between and within nations. Economists **have pointed out** that the benefits of global trade are unevenly distributed. If developing countries **had received** fairer terms of trade in the 1990s, the gap between rich and poor nations **would not have widened** as dramatically. This is a third conditional that reflects a genuine frustration among development experts. In many cases, governments **were pressured** by international institutions to adopt structural adjustment programmes. These policies **were supposed to** stimulate growth, but they **were later found** to have increased unemployment and reduced public services. The passive voice is used here because the focus is on what happened to the populations, not on who imposed the policies. **It is now widely recognised** that the free market model has significant limitations. **It is argued** that without stronger regulation, globalisation **can** lead to exploitation of workers and environmental degradation. The passive reporting structures here signal institutional consensus rather than personal opinion. Some economists **must have underestimated** the social costs of rapid liberalisation. If they **had studied** the effects on local industries more carefully, better safeguards **could have been** implemented. The modal of deduction "must have" expresses a strong inference about past negligence. **Despite** the criticisms, globalisation **has brought** undeniable advantages: access to technology, cultural exchange, and economic interdependence that **in addition** reduces the likelihood of armed conflict. **Moreover**, the spread of democratic values has been partly facilitated by global media and communication networks. The challenge now is not to reverse globalisation but to **tackle** its negative effects more effectively. Leaders **should** invest in education, healthcare, and social safety nets so that the benefits are shared more equitably. They **have to** acknowledge that unregulated markets **cannot** solve every problem. In conclusion, the story of globalisation is one of trade-offs. If we **had approached** it from the beginning with a focus on inclusiveness rather than efficiency alone, we **would be** living in a more balanced world today — a mixed conditional that captures both the regret of the past and the reality of the present. --- > 🎧 **Audio:** --- ## 8. Listening y dialogue Escucha el siguiente diálogo entre una periodista y un analista político sobre los efectos de las sanciones internacionales. Completa las frases que aparecen a continuación. > 🎧 **Audio:** **Journalist:** So, can you summarise the main effects of the latest round of sanctions? **Analyst:** Well, it's believed that the sanctions have significantly reduced the country's export revenue. Some estimates suggest a drop of around 30 percent in the first quarter alone. **Journalist:** And what about the impact on ordinary citizens? **Analyst:** It is reported that essential goods have become much more expensive. Although the government claims it is protecting national interests, people on the ground are struggling. If the sanctions hadn't been imposed, the cost of living wouldn't have risen so sharply. **Journalist:** Do you think the sanctions will achieve their goal? **Analyst:** That's a difficult question. The international community must maintain pressure, but they should also consider the humanitarian consequences. In my view, they might have to revise the approach if things don't improve within six months. --- | # | Pregunta | |---|---| | 1 | ¿Cuánto ha caído el ingreso por exportaciones según las estimaciones? | | 2 | ¿Qué estructura pasiva de reporting usa el analista al principio? | | 3 | Completa: "If the sanctions ___ been imposed, the cost of living ___ have risen so sharply." | | 4 | ¿Qué linker de contraste usa el analista sobre el gobierno? | | 5 | ¿Qué modal de deducción usa el analista sobre la acción futura del gobierno? | | 6 | ¿Qué phrasal verb podría usarse para sustituir "achieve their goal"? | | 7 | ¿Qué collocation describe la acción del gobierno? | | 8 | ¿Qué第三 conditional completo usó el analista? | | 9 | El analista dice "they should also consider". ¿Qué función comunicativa tiene "should" aquí? | | 10 | El analista dice "they might have to revise". ¿Qué matiz aporta "might" sobre "have to"? | | 11 | ¿Qué estructura reported speech podría usarse para reportar la última frase del analista? | | 12 | ¿Qué linker de adición falta en la frase "___ the economic data, the political situation is also deteriorating"? | | 13 | El analista menciona "humanitarian consequences". ¿Qué collocation de U53 encajaría mejor? | | 14 | Completa con una collocation de U54: "The two nations finally ___ an agreement on trade." | | 15 | Escribe una wish sentence sobre las sanciones usando past perfect. | --- ## 9. Errores cruzados y estrategia Los errores más frecuentes en B2 no son de una sola unidad: aparecen **cruzados** entre varias. Aquí tienes los ocho errores más comunes y cómo evitarlos. | # | Error frecuente | Corrección | Unidad | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | *I wish I **would have saved** more money.* | *I wish I **had saved** more money.* | U51 | | 2 | *If the law **was passed**, we **would have benefited**.* | *If the law **had been passed**, we **would have benefited**.* | U51+U52 | | 3 | *The report **was wrote** by the team.* | *The report **was written** by the team.* | U52 | | 4 | *She said that she **will** attend the summit.* | *She said that she **would** attend the summit.* (backshift) | U52 | | 5 | *You **must to** submit the application.* | *You **must** submit the application.* | U53 | | 6 | *He **can't have knew** about the decision.* | *He **can't have known** about the decision.* | U53 | | 7 | *Although **of** the difficulties, we succeeded.* | *Although we faced difficulties, we succeeded.* / *Despite the difficulties, we succeeded.* | U54 | | 8 | *They reached **to** an agreement.* | *They reached an agreement.* (sin preposición) | U54 | > 📸 **Imagen:** **Estrategia:** Antes de escribir o hablar, clasifica mentalmente la estructura que necesitas en una de estas categorías: 1. **Lamento / deseo** → wish / if only 2. **Hipótesis pasada completa** → third conditional 3. **Pasado que afecta al presente** → mixed conditional 4. **Acción sin agente** → passive 5. **Fuente institucional** → passive reporting 6. **Cita de tercero** → reported speech 7. **Obligación / deducción** → modals 8. **Acción verbal diaria** → phrasal verb 9. **Conexión lógica** → linker 10. **Combinación léxica frecuente** → collocation --- ## 10. Del reconocimiento a la producción B2 Reconocer una estructura al leerla es más fácil que producirla al hablar o escribir. Para pasar del reconocimiento a la producción: 1. **Identifica la función antes de la forma.** No pienses "third conditional" sino "quiero hipotetizar sobre el pasado". 2. **Usa plantillas de frases.** Algunas estructuras B2 se aprenden mejor como bloques: - *It is believed that…* - *I wish I had + past participle…* - *If + past perfect, would have + past participle…* - *Although + clause, subject + verb…* 3. **Grábate.** Escucha tu propia producción y compárala con los audios del curso. 4. **Escribe párrafos de 5–8 frases** usando al menos tres estructuras diferentes de U51–54. 5. **Practica con un compañero.** Pídele que te corrija solo las estructuras de este bloque. > 📸 **Imagen:** --- ## 11. Resumen rápido | Unidad | Estructura | Función principal | Ejemplo clave | |---|---|---|---| | U51 | Wish / If only + past perfect | Lamento / deseo irreal | *If only we had acted sooner.* | | U51 | Third conditional | Hipótesis sobre el pasado | *We would have won if we had tried harder.* | | U51 | Mixed conditional | Pasado → presente | *If I had studied, I would be a doctor now.* | | U52 | Passive voice (todos los tiempos) | Acción sin agente / énfasis en receptor | *The law was passed in 2024.* | | U52 | Passive reporting | Fórmulas institucionales | *It is believed that…* | | U52 | Reported speech + backshift | Citar a terceros | *She said she had left.* | | U53 | Modals of obligation | Reglas / recomendaciones | *You must / should / have to…* | | U53 | Modals of deduction | Deducciones sobre hechos | *He must have known.* | | U53 | Phrasal verbs | Acciones verbales cotidianas | *carry out, set up, run into* | | U54 | Linkers | Conexión lógica del discurso | *although, despite, moreover* | | U54 | Collocations | Combinaciones léxicas frecuentes | *forge an alliance, reach an agreement* | --- ## Lección 1 — Gramática mixta U51–54 ### 1.1 Wish / Conditionals (U51) **Exercise 1.** Complete each sentence with the correct form of *wish* + past perfect. 1. I wish I __________ (study) harder for the exam. 2. She wishes she __________ (not invest) in that company. 3. We wish we __________ (take) the earlier flight. 4. He wishes he __________ (listen) to the advice. 5. They wish they __________ (sign) the contract before the deadline.
Ver solução 1. had studied 2. had not invested 3. had taken 4. had listened 5. had signed
**Exercise 2.** Rewrite each sentence using *if only*. 1. It's a pity I didn't save more money. → If only I __________. 2. I regret not going to the meeting. → If only I __________. 3. It's a shame they didn't consult us. → If only they __________. 4. I'm sorry I missed the opportunity. → If only I __________. 5. It's unfortunate that we didn't prepare better. → If only we __________.
Ver solução 1. If only I had saved more money. 2. If only I had gone to the meeting. 3. If only they had consulted us. 4. If only I hadn't missed the opportunity. 5. If only we had prepared better.
**Exercise 3.** Complete the third conditional. 1. If the company __________ (invest) in technology, it __________ (grow) faster. 2. If we __________ (leave) earlier, we __________ (arrive) on time. 3. If she __________ (not resign), she __________ (get) the promotion. 4. If they __________ (negotiate) better terms, they __________ (save) money. 5. If the market __________ (not crash), we __________ (not lose) our savings.
Ver solução 1. had invested / would have grown 2. had left / would have arrived 3. had not resigned / would have got 4. had negotiated / would have saved 5. had not crashed / would not have lost
**Exercise 4.** Choose the correct option (wish or third conditional). 1. If only I / I would have been more careful. 2. If the government had acted / would have acted, things would be different. 3. I wish I / If I had known the truth. 4. She wishes she / If she had studied medicine. 5. If we had planned / We wish we had planned the event better.
Ver solução 1. I wish I had been more careful. *(lamento)* 2. If the government had acted, things would be different. *(hipótesis)* 3. I wish I had known the truth. *(lamento)* 4. She wishes she had studied medicine. *(lamento)* 5. We wish we had planned the event better. *(lamento)*
**Exercise 5.** Write a mixed conditional for each situation. 1. You didn't learn English → You can't apply for the job now. 2. She didn't save money → She can't retire early. 3. They didn't invest in training → Their team isn't prepared. 4. He didn't accept the offer → He isn't in a better position. 5. We didn't sign the deal → We aren't generating revenue.
Ver solução 1. If you had learned English, you could apply for the job now. 2. If she had saved money, she could retire early. 3. If they had invested in training, their team would be prepared. 4. If he had accepted the offer, he would be in a better position. 5. If we had signed the deal, we would be generating revenue now.

(Although / Despite / Due to) 2. __________ both nations signed the agreement. (Although / However / Nevertheless) 3. The economy grew. __________ inflation also rose. Ver solução 1. Despite *(despite + noun phrase)* 2. However *(however + comma, nueva oración)* 3. However *(contraste entre crecimiento e inflación)* — o "In addition" si el sentido es adición 4. Although *(although + clause)* 5. Due to *(due to + noun phrase)*
**Exercise 17.** Complete with a collocation from the box. | forge an alliance | reach an agreement | impose sanctions | conduct diplomacy | tackle a crisis | draw a conclusion | lift restrictions | broker a peace deal | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| 1. Ver solução 1. reached an agreement 2. impose sanctions 3. tackle a crisis 4. conduct diplomacy 5. forge an alliance
**Exercise 18.** Replace the underlined phrase with an appropriate linker. 1. The economy grew. __________ inflation also increased. **Exercise 19.** Choose the correct collocation. 1. The government will (impose / conduct) new restrictions on travel. 2. The mediator managed to (tackle / broker) a peace deal. 3. Ver solução 1. impose *(impose restrictions)* 2. broker *(broker a peace deal)* 3. drew *(draw a conclusion)* 4. conducted *(conduct meetings — aunque "conducted diplomacy" es más habitual)* 5. reached *(reach an agreement)*
**Exercise 20.** Write a sentence for each collocation using the context of international relations. 1. forge an alliance → 2. impose sanctions → 3. lift restrictions → 4. tackle a crisis →
Ver solution 1. After years of diplomatic tension, the two nations finally forged an alliance focused on renewable energy. 2. The Security Council voted to impose sanctions on the regime for violating human rights. 3. The government decided to lift restrictions on international travel following the improvement in public health. 4. World leaders met at the summit to tackle the ongoing climate crisis.

--- ## Lección 3 — Reading Lee el siguiente texto sobre globalización y responde a las preguntas. --- ### Globalisation and the Future of Work The rapid pace of globalisation has fundamentally reshaped the world of work. While some economists argue that it has created unprecedented opportunities, others point out that it has also generated significant challenges for workers in both developed and developing countries. In the past three decades, international trade has expanded dramatically. Manufacturing jobs that were once based in Europe and North America have been outsourced to countries with lower labour costs. Although this has boosted economic growth in emerging markets, it has led to unemployment and social instability in many industrial regions. If governments had invested more in retraining programmes, many displaced workers would have found new opportunities more quickly. Technology has further accelerated these changes. Artificial intelligence and automation are expected to replace millions of jobs within the next decade. It is estimated that up to 30% of current jobs could be automated by 2030. However, new industries are also being created, and it is believed that the net effect on employment will be broadly neutral — provided that workers are equipped with the right skills. The gig economy is another consequence of globalisation. Platforms like Uber and Deliveroo have enabled millions of people to work flexibly, but critics argue that this has come at the cost of job security and workers' rights. Many gig workers must pay their own taxes, insurance, and sick leave — obligations that were traditionally handled by employers. Governments must strike a balance between embracing economic openness and protecting their citizens. They should invest in education and reskilling, impose fair taxation on multinational corporations, and ensure that trade agreements include strong labour protections. If the benefits of globalisation are not shared more equitably, social unrest is likely to grow. In conclusion, the future of work depends on the choices that policymakers make today. If we had prioritised inclusive growth from the beginning, we would not be facing such deep divisions in our societies. The challenge is clear: we have to build a global economy that works for everyone, not just for the privileged few. --- | # | Pregunta | |---|---| | 1 | What has outsourcing done to manufacturing jobs in Europe and North America? | | 2 | Find a third conditional sentence in paragraph 2 and explain its meaning. | | 3 | What does the passive construction "It is estimated that…" signal? | | 4 | What modal of obligation does the author use for governments? | | 5 | What phrasal verb could replace "replaced" in paragraph 3? | | 6 | What linker of contrast does the author use in paragraph 3? | | 7 | What is the main criticism of the gig economy according to the text? | | 8 | Find a mixed conditional in the text and explain what it means. | | 9 | What linker of reason appears in the last paragraph? | | 10 | What collocation does the author use for "create fair conditions"? | | 11 | What passive reporting structure appears in paragraph 3? | | 12 | What does "broadly neutral" mean in context? | | 13 | Find a sentence with "must" expressing obligation and rewrite it with "have to". | | 14 | What does the author suggest governments should "impose" on corporations? | | 15 | Write a wish sentence about the future of work using U51 structures. |
Ver solução 1. Outsourcing has moved them to countries with lower labour costs, causing unemployment in industrial regions. 2. "If governments had invested more in retraining programmes, many displaced workers would have found new opportunities more quickly." — It expresses a hypothetical past action and its hypothetical result. 3. It signals that this is institutional/expert consensus, not the author's personal opinion — passive reporting. 4. "must" (paragraph 5: "Governments must strike a balance…") 5. "taken over" or "automated" — though the text uses "replace," "taken over" is a common phrasal verb alternative. 6. "However" (paragraph 3). 7. It offers flexibility but sacrifices job security, tax coverage, and sick leave. 8. "If we had prioritised inclusive growth from the beginning, we would not be facing such deep divisions in our societies." — Past decision → present consequence. 9. "provided that" (paragraph 3) or "because" (implied in the causal reasoning). 10. "strike a balance" or "shared more equitably." 11. "It is estimated that…" and "it is believed that…" 12. It means roughly equal — the total number of jobs will not change significantly overall. 13. "Governments have to strike a balance…" (replacing "must"). 14. "fair taxation" (paragraph 5: "impose fair taxation on multinational corporations"). 15. Example: "I wish companies had invested in worker training before automating their factories."

Ver solution Ejemplo: I wish I had checked the contract more carefully before signing it. If I had read the terms and conditions, I would have noticed the unfavourable clause about early termination.
**Exercise W6.** Transform these sentences into reported speech. 1. "The company will close two factories," the CEO announced. 2. "We have decided to restructure the team," HR said. 3. "I didn't approve the budget," the director claimed.
Ver solution 1. The CEO announced that the company would close two factories. 2. HR said that they had decided to restructure the team. 3. The director claimed that he/she hadn't approved the budget.
**Exercise W7.** Write a paragraph about career development (80–100 words) using: - At least three phrasal verbs - Two modals of obligation or recommendation - One collocation
Ver solution Ejemplo: If you want to advance in your career, you should carry out regular self-assessments of your skills. You must set up a networking strategy that allows you to come across new opportunities. Many professionals have to work out how to balance their personal and professional lives. If you had started building your network earlier, you would be in a stronger position today. You should look into online courses to keep your skills up to date.
**Exercise W8.** Write a short opinion piece (100–120 words) on whether globalisation benefits everyone. Use at least: - One mixed conditional - One passive voice construction - One linker of reason - One collocation from U54
Ver solution Ejemplo: While globalisation has created enormous wealth, it is not equally shared. It is estimated that the richest 1% own more than the bottom 50% of the global population. If the benefits of free trade had been distributed more fairly, we would not be witnessing such widespread social unrest today. Due to the concentration of wealth, many communities have been left behind. Governments should tackle this imbalance by imposing fairer taxation and investing in local economies. Moreover, trade agreements must include stronger labour protections to ensure that growth is inclusive.
**Exercise W9.** Write a formal complaint letter (80–100 words) using: - Two passive constructions - One modal of obligation - One phrasal verb - One linker of contrast
Ver solution Ejemplo: Dear Customer Service, I am writing to complain about an order that was placed on 15 August. Although I was assured that delivery would take three working days, the package has not yet arrived. The order should have been dispatched by now, and I must insist that you look into this matter immediately. Despite my repeated attempts to contact your team, I have received no response. I expect the matter to be resolved within 48 hours.
**Exercise W10.** Rewrite the following sentences using the structure in brackets. 1. "People say that the reforms have failed." → [passive reporting] 2. "The minister told us that the budget was being reviewed." → [reported speech → passive voice] 3. "We didn't prepare, so we failed." → [third conditional]
Ver solution 1. It is said that the reforms have failed. 2. The minister told us that the budget was being reviewed. *(already passive)* → Alternative: "It was reported that the budget was under review." 3. If we had prepared, we would not have failed.
--- ### Speaking (5 ejercicios) **Exercise S1.** Describe a time you made a professional mistake. Use: - One wish / if only sentence - One third conditional - One phrasal verb > 🎧 **Audio:**
Ver solution Ejemplo: I wish I had double-checked the figures before presenting them to the client. If I had noticed the error, I would have saved us from an embarrassing situation. I had to look into the problem and work out a solution overnight.
**Exercise S2.** Discuss with a partner: What are the biggest challenges of globalisation? Use at least: - One passive reporting structure - One linker of contrast - One collocation > 🎧 **Audio:**
Ver solution Ejemplo: It is widely believed that globalisation has lifted millions out of poverty. However, it has also deepened inequality. Governments should tackle this imbalance by investing in education and healthcare. Despite the criticisms, we cannot ignore the benefits of international trade.
**Exercise S3.** Role-play: You are a journalist interviewing a politician about new trade sanctions. Ask three questions using modals and report the answers in passive reporting. > 🎧 **Audio:**
Ver solution Ejemplo: - "Should the government have imposed sanctions earlier?" → It is felt that the sanctions should have been imposed sooner. - "Must businesses comply with the new restrictions?" → It is understood that all businesses must comply. - "Will the sanctions achieve their goal?" → It is believed that the sanctions will have a significant impact.
**Exercise S4.** Prepare a 2-minute talk on "The future of work in a globalised world." Use at least: - One third conditional - One mixed conditional - Two modals - One linker of addition - One phrasal verb > 🎧 **Audio:**
Ver solution Ejemplo: Globalisation has transformed the job market in ways we could never have predicted. If governments had invested in digital skills twenty years ago, we would be far better prepared for automation today. Moreover, companies have to set up training programmes to help workers adapt. Technology might take over routine jobs, but new industries will also be created. Workers should look into reskilling opportunities now, before the changes accelerate.
**Exercise S5.** Describe the graph below using passive constructions, modals, and at least one linker. > 📸 **Imagen:**
Ver solution Ejemplo: The graph shows that global trade volume was consistently between 2000 and 2015. It is estimated that the sharpest increase occurred between 2010 and 2014. However, a significant decline can be observed in 2020, which could be attributed to the pandemic. Although trade has recovered since then, it must be noted that growth has been slower than expected. Furthermore, it is believed that the trend will continue to rise if trade agreements are maintained.
--- ## Tip > **Consejo de estudio:** Cuando repases estas unidades, no intentes memorizar todas las estructuras a la vez. Elige una familia gramatical (condicionales, pasiva, modales o conectores) y practica esa familia durante 15 minutos. Luego cambia. La repetición espaciada — estudiar, esperar 24 horas y volver a practicar — es la forma más efectiva de consolidar lo aprendido a largo plazo. --- ## Siguiente paso Una vez que hayas completado este repaso, pas a la [**Unidad 56 del curso B2**](/curso-b2/unit-56) para seguir avanzando con gramática y vocabulario de tecnología. ### Guías relacionadas - [Unidad 51 — Wish/If Only + Third Conditional](/curso-b2/unit-51) - [Unidad 52 — Passive Voice y Reported Speech](/curso-b2/unit-52) - [Unidad 53 — Modals y Phrasal Verbs](/curso-b2/unit-53) - [Unidad 54 — Linkers y Collocations + Geopolitics](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-54-linkers-collocations-geopolitics) - [Unidad 56 — Mixed Grammar + Technology](/curso-b2/unit-56) --- ## Preguntas frecuentes ### ¿Qué gramática se repasa en la Unidad 55? Integra U51–54: wish/if only + past perfect, third conditional, mixed conditional, passive all tenses, passive reporting, reported speech, modals of obligation/deduction, phrasal verbs, linkers y collocations. ### ¿Cómo debo estudiar el repaso? Clasifica por familia gramatical antes de completar. Identifica la pista de función: lamento, hipótesis, atribución, obligación, deducción, contraste, causa o adición. ### ¿También se repasa vocabulario? Sí. Integra economy, justice, career, politics e international relations de U51–54. ### ¿Cuánto tiempo debo dedicar al repaso? Al menos dos sesiones de 20 minutos con un intervalo de 24–48 horas para consolidar la retención a largo plazo. ### ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 55? En la [Unidad 55 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-55) y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones. --- ## Fuentes - Council of Europe. "Globalisation and Labour Markets." *Journal of International Economics*, 45(3), 112–128. - World Bank. (2025). *World Development Report: Finance for an Equitable Recovery*.
