content:
La **Unidad 56** obliga a elegir entre múltiples estructuras gramaticales B2 en el contexto de la **tecnología e innovación digital**. Cada sección integra conditionals, passive voice, passive reporting, modals, phrasal verbs, linkers y cleft sentences en situaciones tecnológicas reales. Al finalizar, serás capaz de manejar todas estas estructuras de forma fluida en textos y conversaciones sobre tecnología. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 56](/curso-b2/unit-56)
> **Antes:** [U55 — Repaso 51–54 + Globalización](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-55-repaso-51-54-globalisation)
> **Siguiente:** [Unidad 57 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-57) --- ## 1. Mixed Conditionals in Technology Los **mixed conditionals** combinan tiempos diferentes en la cláusula if y la cláusula principal. Son esenciales para hablar de tecnología porque constantemente mezclamos pasado, presente y futuro. ### Tipo 1: Pasado → Presente Usamos esta estructura cuando una condición hipotética del pasado tiene un resultado en el presente. **Estructura:** `If + past perfect, ... would + infinitive` - *If AI had been developed earlier, healthcare **would be** more advanced now.* - *If cybersecurity had been prioritised in the 1990s, data breaches **wouldn't be** so common today.* - *If engineers had invested more in renewable energy tech, we **wouldn't face** so many environmental challenges now.* ### Tipo 2: Presente → Pasado Usamos esta estructura cuando una condición hipotética del presente tiene un resultado en el pasado. **Estructura:** `If + past simple, ... would have + past participle` - *If we **invested** more in cybersecurity, breaches **wouldn't have increased** last year.* - *If the company **had** better infrastructure, the server **wouldn't have crashed** during the launch.* - *If developers **tested** their code more thoroughly, that bug **wouldn't have affected** millions of users.* ### Consejo práctico Para identificar qué mixed conditional usar, pregunta: **¿El resultado es presente o pasado?** Si es presente → usa `would + infinitive`. Si es pasado → usa `would have + past participle`. --- ## 2. Passive Voice and Passive Reporting in Tech News El **passive voice** es frecuente en noticias tecnológicas porque el foco está en la acción, no en quién la realiza. El **passive reporting** se usa para atribuir información a fuentes generales. ### Passive voice — Estructuras | Tiempo | Estructura | Ejemplo tech | |--------|-----------|--------------| | Present simple | am/is/are + past participle | *The data **is encrypted** before transmission.* | | Past simple | was/were + past participle | *The algorithm **was designed** to detect fraud.* | | Present perfect | has/have been + past participle | *Several vulnerabilities **have been discovered** this quarter.* | | Future | will be + past participle | *New features **will be rolled out** next month.* | | Modal | modal + be + past participle | *This software **must be updated** immediately.* | ### Passive reporting El passive reporting permite informar sin comprometer la fuente. Es muy usado en periodismo tecnológico y reportes corporativos. **Estructuras comunes:** - *It is believed that the data **was compromised** by an internal employee.* - *It is reported that the company **has raised** $50 million in funding.* - *It is thought that the outage **was caused** by a cyberattack.* - *It is claimed that the new AI **can outperform** human doctors.* ### Diferencia entre passive voice y passive reporting El **passive voice** se centra en la acción: *The server was hacked.* El **passive reporting** atribuye la información a una fuente vaga: *It is believed that the server was hacked.* Ambos son pasivos, pero el reporting tiene una capa adicional de distancia con la información. --- ## 3. Modals of Deduction for Tech Speculation Los **modals of deduction** permiten especular sobre causas, consecuencias y estados de la tecnología con diferentes grados de certeza. ### Escala de certeza | Nivel | Modal | Ejemplo tech | |-------|-------|--------------| | Certeza (~95%) | must | *The system **must have crashed** due to the overload.* | | Probabilidad (~75%) | should / ought to | *The update **should have fixed** the security flaw.* | | Posibilidad (~50%) | might / could | *The breach **might have been** caused by a phishing attack.* | | Imposibilidad (~5%) | can't | *The breach **can't have been accidental** — too much data was stolen.* | ### Modals en contextos tecnológicos - *The new feature **could revolutionise** how we use smartphones.* - *AI **might eventually replace** certain types of manual labour.* - *This app **must have been** designed with accessibility in mind.* - *The company's security **can't have been** adequate — the breach was massive.* ### Consejo práctico Cuando escuches o leas una noticia tecnológica, fíjate en qué modal usa el autor para expresar certeza o duda. Esto te ayuda a entender la postura del hablante y a usar los modals correctamente en tus propios textos. --- ## 4. Phrasal Verbs for Technology Los **phrasal verbs** son frecuentes en conversaciones sobre tecnología. Aquí tienes los más importantes para el contexto B2. | Phrasal verb | Significado | Ejemplo | |-------------|-------------|---------| | **roll out** | lanzar, implementar progresivamente | *The company will **roll out** the new update next week.* | | **scale up** | ampliar, aumentar capacidad | *We need to **scale up** our servers to handle the traffic.* | | **phase out** | eliminar gradualmente | *They plan to **phase out** older devices by 2027.* | | **plug in** | conectar | *Just **plug in** the USB and the software will install automatically.* | | **sync up** | sincronizar | *Make sure your phone **syncs up** with the cloud before travelling.* | | **back up** | respaldar | *Always **back up** your data before updating the system.* | | **run into** | encontrar (un problema) | *We **ran into** some compatibility issues during testing.* | | **come up with** | idear, inventar | *The team **came up with** an innovative solution to the problem.* | | **break down** | averiarse, fallar | *The server **broke down** during peak hours.* | | **set up** | configurar, instalar | *It took hours to **set up** the new network infrastructure.* | ### Consejo práctico Los phrasal verbs tech suelen ser separables: *The update was rolled out gradually* / *They rolled the update out gradually.* Cuando el objeto es un pronombre, siempre va entre el verbo y la partícula: *They rolled it out.* --- ## 5. Linkers and Cleft Sentences in Technical Writing Los **linkers** conectan ideas y dan fluidez a textos técnicos. Los **cleft sentences** enfatizan información específica. ### Linkers esenciales para tecnología | Linker | Función | Ejemplo | |--------|---------|---------| | **furthermore** | añadir información | *The system is fast. **Furthermore**, it is highly secure.* | | **however** | contrastar | *The app is free. **However**, it contains ads.* | | **consequently** | consecuencia | *The server was overloaded. **Consequently**, it crashed.* | | **in addition** | añadir | *The software is reliable. **In addition**, it is open source.* | | **nevertheless** | concesión | *The product had bugs. **Nevertheless**, it was a success.* | | **as a result** | resultado | *Demand surged. **As a result**, the company expanded its team.* | ### Cleft sentences Las cleft sentences reestructuran una oración para enfatizar un elemento. Son muy útiles en textos técnicos y académicos. **Estructura:** `It + be + elemento enfatizado + that/who + resto de la oración` - *It was **the algorithm** that identified the security flaw.* (énfasis en qué descubrió el fallo) - *It is **data privacy** that concerns users the most.* (énfasis en qué preocupa) - *It was **during the launch** that the system crashed.* (énfasis en cuándo ocurrió) - *It was **the development team** who resolved the issue.* (énfasis en quién) ### Diferencia entre cleft y oración normal - Normal: *The team resolved the issue during the launch.* - Cleft: *It was **the team** who resolved the issue.* (énfasis en quién) - Cleft: *It was **during the launch** that the issue was resolved.* (énfasis en cuándo) --- ## 6. Vocabulario de Tecnología | English | Español | Ejemplo en contexto | |---------|---------|-------------------| | Artificial Intelligence (AI) | Inteligencia Artificial | *AI is transforming healthcare diagnostics.* | | Machine Learning | Aprendizaje automático | *Machine learning algorithms predict user behaviour.* | | Algorithm | Algoritmo | *The algorithm processes millions of data points per second.* | | Cybersecurity | Ciberseguridad | *Cybersecurity spending has increased by 40% this decade.* | | Blockchain | Cadena de bloques | *Blockchain technology ensures transparent transactions.* | | Cloud Computing | Computación en la nube | *Cloud computing allows remote access to powerful servers.* | | Internet of Things (IoT) | Internet de las Cosas | *IoT devices collect data from smart homes.* | | Automation | Automatización | *Automation has reduced manufacturing costs significantly.* | | Digital Transformation | Transformación digital | *Digital transformation is essential for business survival.* | | Data Privacy | Privacidad de datos | *Data privacy regulations protect user information.* | | Open Source | Código abierto | *The open source community contributed thousands of fixes.* | | Bandwidth | Ancho de banda | *Higher bandwidth enables faster streaming speeds.* | | Bug | Error de software | *A critical bug forced the company to issue a patch.* | | Deploy | Desplegar, implementar | *The team deployed the update across all servers.* | | Patch | Parche, actualización de seguridad | *A security patch was released to fix the vulnerability.* | | Firewall | Cortafuegos | *The firewall blocked unauthorised access attempts.* | | Malware | software malicioso | *The malware infected thousands of computers worldwide.* | | Phishing | suplantación de identidad | *Phishing attacks are becoming increasingly sophisticated.* | | Encryption | Cifrado | *End-to-end encryption protects message content.* | | Server | Servidor | *The server handles all incoming requests from users.* | --- ## 7. Reading: A Tech Startup's Story Lee el siguiente texto sobre una empresa emergente tecnológica. > **From Garage to Global: The Rise of NovaTech** > > NovaTech was founded in 2019 by two university graduates who wanted to make cybersecurity accessible to small businesses. In the early days, the founders had little funding and worked from a garage. However, their idea was innovative: a subscription-based firewall service powered by artificial intelligence. > > By 2021, the company had scaled up significantly. Over 10,000 small businesses had signed up for the service, and NovaTech had raised $12 million in venture capital. It was the AI-driven detection system that attracted most investors, as it could identify threats in real time. > > In 2023, the company rolled out a major update that included machine learning capabilities. Although the update was praised by experts, some users ran into compatibility issues with older operating systems. Fortunately, the development team came up with a patch within 48 hours. > > Today, NovaTech serves clients in over 30 countries. The founders believe that if they hadn't taken the risk of starting the company, thousands of small businesses would still lack affordable cybersecurity protection. **Vocabulario clave del texto:** | Palabra | Significado | |---------|------------| | venture capital | capital de riesgo | | subscription-based | basado en suscripción | | detection system | sistema de detección | | compatibility issues | problemas de compatibilidad | | affordable | asequible | --- ## 8. Listening Escucha el siguiente diálogo sobre transformación digital en una empresa. ![Diagrama de conversación sobre transformación digital](/blog/curso-b2/unit-56/digital-transformation-dialogue.png) **Transcripción del audio:** > **Sarah:** Have you heard about Meridian's digital transformation project? > > **James:** Yes, it's been all over the tech news. Apparently, they're automating their entire supply chain. > > **Sarah:** That's right. It is believed that the new system will reduce costs by 30%. They've already rolled out the first phase. > > **James:** Really? I thought they were still in the planning stages. > > **Sarah:** No, they started deploying AI-powered tools six months ago. The algorithm was designed to predict demand patterns. > > **James:** That sounds ambitious. Have there been any issues? > > **Sarah:** Well, the team ran into some data privacy concerns at first. But they came up with an encryption protocol that satisfied the regulators. > > **James:** It must have been a massive investment. > > **Sarah:** It was. But if they hadn't invested in the technology, they wouldn't have survived the market disruption last year. > > **James:** That's true. Traditional companies that didn't modernise have struggled. > > **Sarah:** Exactly. And what's interesting is that it was the CEO's decision to prioritise innovation that made it all possible. > > **James:** I suppose it shows that leadership is key when it comes to digital transformation. > > **Sarah:** Absolutely. The company should have made the change sooner, but at least they did it before it was too late. **Audio disponible:** `/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-56/digital-transformation-dialogue.mp3` --- ## 9. Writing — Technical Reports Un **technical report** en inglés sigue una estructura formal. Aquí tienes la plantilla y los linkers esenciales. ### Estructura de un reporte técnico 1. **Title** — Descriptive and clear 2. **Executive Summary** — Brief overview of findings 3. **Introduction** — Context and objectives 4. **Methodology** — How data was gathered 5. **Findings** — Results and data analysis 6. **Conclusions** — What the findings mean 7. **Recommendations** — Actionable next steps ### Linkers para reportes | Sección | Linkers recomendados | |---------|---------------------| | Executive Summary | *In summary, ...* / *Overall, ...* | | Findings | *Furthermore, ...* / *In addition, ...* / *It was observed that ...* | | Conclusions | *Consequently, ...* / *As a result, ...* / *Therefore, ...* | | Recommendations | *It is recommended that ...* / *It is suggested that ...* / *Nevertheless, ...* | ### Ejemplo de cleft sentence en un reporte - Normal: *The firewall prevented the attack.* - Cleft: *It was **the firewall** that prevented the attack.* (énfasis en el elemento clave) --- ## 10. Speaking ### Temas de conversación B2 sobre tecnología Practica estos temas usando las estructuras de la unidad: 1. **AI and the future of work:** *If AI had been developed earlier, how would the job market be different today?* 2. **Cybersecurity:** *It is believed that cyberattacks will increase in the next decade. Do you agree?* 3. **Digital privacy:** *Should governments regulate data collection more strictly?* 4. **Tech ethics:** *If companies invested more in ethical AI, would we have fewer problems with bias?* ### Phrasal verbs en conversación Usa estos phrasal verbs en tus respuestas: - *The government needs to **phase out** outdated technology in public services.* - *We **came up with** a solution during the meeting.* - *The system **broke down** because nobody had **backed up** the data.* - *Once you **set up** the firewall, you should **sync up** all your devices.* --- ## 11. Common Errors — Errores Comunes Evita estos errores frecuentes al usar las estructuras B2 de esta unidad. | # | Estructura | Error | Corrección | Explicación | |---|-----------|-------|-----------|-------------| | 1 | Mixed conditional | *If AI had developed earlier, healthcare **would have been** more advanced now.* | *If AI had developed earlier, healthcare **would be** more advanced now.* | El resultado es presente, no pasado: usa `would + infinitive`. | | 2 | Passive voice | *The data has been compromise by hackers.* | *The data **has been compromised** by hackers.* | El pasado participio de "compromise" es "compromised". | | 3 | Passive reporting | *It is believe that the system was hacked.* | *It is **believed** that the system was hacked.* | El participio es "believed", no "believe". | | 4 | Modals of deduction | *The server must crashed due to overload.* | *The server **must have crashed** due to overload.* | Después de "must" para deduction en pasado, usa `have + past participle`. | | 5 | Phrasal verb | *They rolled out the update it gradually.* | *They rolled the update out gradually.* | El pronombre va entre el verbo y la partícula: `rolled it out`. | | 6 | Linker | *The software is fast. Furthermore, it is cheap. Furthermore, it is easy to use.* | *The software is fast. **Furthermore**, it is cheap. **In addition**, it is easy to use.* | No repitas el mismo linker dos veces seguidas. | | 7 | Cleft sentence | *It was during the launch when the system crashed.* | *It was during the launch **that** the system crashed.* | En cleft sentences se usa "that", no "when". | | 8 | Mixed conditional | *If we invested more, breaches **wouldn't increase** last year.* | *If we invested more, breaches **wouldn't have increased** last year.* | El resultado es pasado (last year): usa `would have + past participle`. | --- ## 12. Resumen Rápido | Estructura | Uso principal | Ejemplo clave | |-----------|--------------|--------------| | Mixed conditionals | Mezclar tiempos en hipótesis | *If AI had been developed earlier, healthcare would be more advanced now.* | | Passive voice | Enfocar la acción, no el agente | *The algorithm was designed to detect fraud.* | | Passive reporting | Atribuir información a fuentes generales | *It is believed that the data was compromised.* | | Modals of deduction | Especificar nivel de certeza | *The breach can't have been accidental.* | | Phrasal verbs | Verbos coloquiales frecuentes en tech | *They rolled out the new update.* | | Linkers | Conectar ideas en textos formales | *Furthermore, the system is highly secure.* | | Cleft sentences | Enfocar un elemento específico | *It was the algorithm that identified the flaw.* | --- ## Lección 1 — Gramática Mixta ### Subsección 1: Mixed Conditionals — Elige la forma correcta **Instrucciones:** Elige la opción correcta (a o b) para completar cada oración. **1.** If cybersecurity had been a priority in the 1990s, data breaches ______ so common today. - a) wouldn't be - b) wouldn't have been
Ver solução **a) wouldn't be** — El resultado es presente ("today"), así que usamos `would + infinitive`.
**2.** If the company ______ better infrastructure, the server wouldn't have crashed during the launch. - a) had - b) would have
Ver solução **a) had** — En mixed conditionals, la cláusula if usa el pasado simple (no "would").
**3.** If engineers had invested more in renewable energy tech, we ______ so many environmental challenges now. - a) wouldn't face - b) wouldn't have faced
Ver solução **a) wouldn't face** — El resultado es presente ("now"), así que usamos `would + infinitive`.
**4.** If developers tested their code more thoroughly, that bug ______ millions of users last year. - a) wouldn't have affected - b) wouldn't affect
Ver solução **a) wouldn't have affected** — El resultado es pasado ("last year"), así que usamos `would have + past participle`.
**5.** If AI ______ developed earlier, healthcare would be more advanced now. - a) had been - b) was
Ver solução **a) had been** — La cláusula if se refiere a una condición hipotética del pasado, así que usamos past perfect.
--- ### Subsección 2: Passive + Reporting — Transforma o identifica **Instrucciones:** Transforma las oraciones al passive voice o identifica la estructura correcta. **1.** Transforma al passive: *The team designed the algorithm to detect fraud.*
Ver solução *The algorithm was designed to detect fraud.*
**2.** Transforma al passive: *Hackers compromised the data last week.*
Ver solução *The data was compromised by hackers last week.*
**3.** Completa el passive reporting: *It is ______ that the server was hacked by an insider.*
Ver solução *It is **believed** that the server was hacked by an insider.*
**4.** Transforma al passive: *The company has raised $50 million in funding.*
Ver solução *$50 million has been raised in funding by the company.*
**5.** Identifica el error: *It is report that several vulnerabilities have been discover.*
Ver solução *It is **reported** that several vulnerabilities have been **discovered**.* — Faltan los participios: "reported" y "discovered".
--- ### Subsección 3: Modals + Phrasal Verbs — Completa o corrige **Instrucciones:** Completa con el modal correcto o corrige el error. **1.** The system ______ have crashed due to the overload. (Certeza ~95%)
Ver solução *The system **must** have crashed due to the overload.* — "Must" indica certeza casi total.
**2.** The breach ______ have been accidental — too much data was stolen. (Imposibilidad)
Ver solução *The breach **can't** have been accidental.* — "Can't" indica imposibilidad.
**3.** Corrige: *The new update could have rolled out next month.*
Ver solução *The new update **could be rolled out** next month.* — "Rolled out" necesita la estructura pasiva: `could be + past participle`.
**4.** Complete: *We ______ into some compatibility issues during testing.*
Ver solução *We **ran** into some compatibility issues during testing.* — El phrasal verb es "run into" (encontrar un problema).
**5.** Corrige: *The team came up an innovative solution.*
Ver solução *The team **came up with** an innovative solution.* — El phrasal verb es "come up with" (idear/inventar).
--- ### Subsección 4: Linkers + Cleft Sentences — Elige o corrige **Instrucciones:** Elige el linker correcto o corrige la cleft sentence. **1.** The software is fast. ______, it is highly affordable. - a) However - b) Furthermore
Ver solução **b) Furthermore** — Se añade información positiva, no se contrasta.
**2.** The server was overloaded. ______, it crashed during peak hours. - a) Consequently - b) Nevertheless
Ver solução **a) Consequently** — Se expresa una consecuencia lógica.
**3.** Completa la cleft: ______ the algorithm that identified the security flaw. - a) It is - b) It was
Ver solução **b) It was** — El evento pasó en el pasado, así que usamos "was".
**4.** Corrige: *It was during the launch when the system crashed.*
Ver solução *It was during the launch **that** the system crashed.* — En cleft sentences se usa "that", no "when".
**5.** The product had bugs. ______, it was a commercial success. - a) As a result - b) Nevertheless
Ver solução **b) Nevertheless** — Se expresa concesión: a pesar de los bugs, tuvo éxito.
--- ## Lección 2 — Vocabulario Tech ### Subsección 1: Definiciones — Empareja **Instrucciones:** Empareja cada término tech con su definición. | # | Término | | # | Definición | |---|---------|---|---|------------| | 1 | Algorithm | | a | Software diseñado para dañar sistemas | | 2 | Firewall | | b | Proceso de volver a configurar algo en un sistema | | 3 | Malware | | c | Conjunto de reglas que resuelven un problema | | 4 | Encryption | | d | Dispositivo que recopila datos del entorno | | 5 | IoT device | | e | Sistema de protección contra accesos no autorizados |
Ver solução 1-c, 2-e, 3-a, 4-**, 5-d
### Subsección 2: Completar con vocabulario **Instrucciones:** Completa cada oración con la palabra correcta del banco. **Banco:** *phishing, bandwidth, patch, deploy, open source* **1.** A critical ______ was released to fix the security vulnerability. **2.** ______ attacks are becoming increasingly sophisticated. **3.** The company plans to ______ the new software across all offices. **4.** Higher ______ enables faster streaming speeds. **5.** The ______ community contributed thousands of code improvements.
Ver solução 1. patch, 2. Phishing, 3. deploy, 4. bandwidth, 5. open source
### Subsección 3: Uso correcto — Elige **Instrucciones:** Elige la opción que usa correctamente el término. **1.** ¿Cuál es correcto? - a) *The AI uses machine learning to learning patterns.* - b) *The AI uses machine learning to learn patterns.*
Ver solução **b)** — Después de "to" se usa el infinitivo: "to learn".
**2.** ¿Cuál es correcto? - a) *Blockchain ensures transparent and immutable transactions.* - b) *Blockchain ensures transparent and mutable transactions.*
Ver solução **a)** — Blockchain garantiza transacciones **inmutables** (no cambiables).
**3.** ¿Cuál es correcto? - a) *The data privacy was violated by the company.* - b) *Data privacy was violated by the company.*
Ver solução **b)** — "Data privacy" como concepto general no lleva artículo definido.
**4.** ¿Cuál es correcto? - a) *Cloud computing allows to access remote servers.* - b) *Cloud computing allows remote access to powerful servers.*
Ver solução **b)** — "Allow" no permite un sujeto explícito con "to": se usa `allow + noun`.
**5.** ¿Cuál es correcto? - a) *The automation has reduced significantly manufacturing costs.* - b) *The automation has significantly reduced manufacturing costs.*
Ver solução **b)** — El adverbio "significantly" va antes del verbo principal, no entre el verbo y su complemento.
### Subsección 4: Traducción tech **Instrucciones:** Traduce al inglés usando el vocabulario de la unidad. **1.** La inteligencia artificial está transformando los diagnósticos médicos.
Ver solução *Artificial intelligence is transforming healthcare diagnostics.*
**2.** Siempre debes respaldar tus datos antes de actualizar el sistema.
Ver solução *You should always back up your data before updating the system.*
**3.** Los dispositivos IoT recopilan datos de los hogares inteligentes.
Ver solução *IoT devices collect data from smart homes.*
**4.** La empresa planea eliminar gradualmente los dispositivos más antiguos para 2027.
Ver solução *The company plans to phase out older devices by 2027.*
**5.** El cifrado de extremo a extremo protege el contenido de los mensajes.
Ver solução *End-to-end encryption protects message content.*
--- ## Lección 3 — Reading Lee el siguiente texto sobre ciberseguridad y responde las preguntas. > **The Rise of AI-Powered Cybersecurity** > > In recent years, artificial intelligence has revolutionised the field of cybersecurity. Traditional firewalls and antivirus software, which relied on known threat signatures, are no longer sufficient. Modern cyberattacks are too sophisticated for these conventional tools. > > AI-driven security systems, on the other hand, can analyse millions of data points in real time. The algorithm was designed to identify patterns that human analysts might miss. Furthermore, machine learning allows these systems to improve over time, adapting to new types of threats. > > It is reported that companies using AI-powered cybersecurity have reduced their breach response time by 60%. Nevertheless, experts warn that AI can also be used by hackers to create more advanced malware. It is therefore essential that organisations invest in both offensive and defensive AI capabilities. > > One of the biggest challenges in cybersecurity is data privacy. While AI systems need vast amounts of data to function effectively, collecting and processing this data raises significant ethical concerns. It is believed that stricter regulations will be necessary to balance innovation with user protection. > > Looking ahead, the development of quantum computing could both strengthen and undermine encryption. If quantum computers become widely available, current encryption methods would need to be completely redesigned. Consequently, researchers are already working on quantum-resistant encryption protocols. ### Preguntas **1.** According to the text, why are traditional firewalls no longer sufficient? - a) They are too expensive - b) Modern attacks are too sophisticated for them - c) They have been banned by regulations - d) They only work with old operating systems
Ver solução **b)** — *Modern cyberattacks are too sophisticated for these conventional tools.*
**2.** What can AI-driven security systems analyse? - a) Only known threat signatures - b) Employee emails only - c) Millions of data points in real time - d) Physical security cameras
Ver solução **c)** — *AI-driven security systems can analyse millions of data points in real time.*
**3.** How much have companies reduced their breach response time using AI? - a) 30% - b) 50% - c) 60% - d) 80%
Ver solução **c)** — *Companies using AI-powered cybersecurity have reduced their breach response time by 60%.*
**4.** What is one concern experts have about AI in cybersecurity? - a) It is too slow for real-time analysis - b) It can be used by hackers to create advanced malware - c) It requires too much electricity - d) It cannot detect phishing attacks
Ver solução **b)** — *Experts warn that AI can also be used by hackers to create more advanced malware.*
**5.** What ethical concern does the text mention about AI and data privacy? - a) AI systems collect data without consent - b) AI systems need vast amounts of data, raising ethical concerns - c) AI systems sell data to third parties - d) AI systems cannot protect personal data
Ver solução **b)** — *While AI systems need vast amounts of data to function effectively, collecting and processing this data raises significant ethical concerns.*
**6.** What could quantum computing do to encryption? - a) Make it completely unnecessary - b) Both strengthen and undermine it - c) Replace it with blockchain - d) Make it faster and cheaper
Ver solução **b)** — *The development of quantum computing could both strengthen and undermine encryption.*
**7.** What structure does the sentence "It is reported that companies using AI-powered cybersecurity have reduced..." use? - a) Passive voice - b) Passive reporting - c) Mixed conditional - d) Cleft sentence
Ver solução **b)** — Passive reporting: "It is reported that..."
**8.** What modal of deduction does "It is believed that stricter regulations will be necessary" express? - a) Certainty - b) Possibility - c) Obligation - d) Ability
Ver solução **b)** — "It is believed" indica posibilidad, no certeza absoluta.
**9.** Find the phrasal verb in: "Modern cyberattacks are no longer sufficient." What is the synonym? - a) They are no longer adequate - b) They are no longer expensive - c) They are no longer popular - d) They are no longer legal
Ver solução **a)** — "Sufficient" means "adequate" (suficiente/adecuado).
**10.** Which linker is used to add information in the text? - a) Nevertheless - b) Consequently - c) Furthermore - d) On the other hand
Ver solução **c)** — "Furthermore" adds information (the third paragraph begins with it).
**11.** Which linker shows contrast in the text? - a) Furthermore - b) Consequently - c) It is reported that - d) Nevertheless
Ver solução **d)** — "Nevertheless" shows contrast/concession.
**12.** What is the main topic of the text? - a) The history of computers - b) AI's role in modern cybersecurity - c) How to build a firewall - d) The dangers of social media
Ver solução **b)** — The text discusses how AI has revolutionised cybersecurity.
**13.** Complete: If quantum computers become widely available, current encryption methods ______ need to be redesigned. - a) would - b) will - c) can - d) must
Ver solução **a)** — Second conditional: "would" for hypothetical future.
**14.** What does "adapt" mean in "adapting to new types of threats"? - a) Ignoring - b) Changing to suit new conditions - c) Copying - d) Destroying
Ver solução **b)** — "Adapt" means to change to suit new conditions (adaptarse).
**15.** According to the text, why are researchers working on quantum-resistant encryption? - a) Because current encryption is too slow - b) Because quantum computers could undermine current encryption - c) Because governments require it - d) Because it is cheaper than traditional encryption
Ver solução **b)** — *If quantum computers become widely available, current encryption methods would need to be completely redesigned.*
--- ## Lección 4 — Listening Escucha el audio de la sección 8 y responde las preguntas. **Audio:** `/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-56/digital-transformation-dialogue.mp3` **1.** What is Meridian automating? - a) Their customer service - b) Their entire supply chain - c) Their marketing department - d) Their hiring process
Ver solução **b)** — *Apparently, they're automating their entire supply chain.*
**2.** How much cost reduction is the new system expected to achieve? - a) 20% - b) 25% - c) 30% - d) 50%
Ver solução **c)** — *It is believed that the new system will reduce costs by 30%.*
**3.** When did Meridian start deploying AI-powered tools? - a) Three months ago - b) Six months ago - c) One year ago - d) Two years ago
Ver solução **b)** — *They started deploying AI-powered tools six months ago.*
**4.** What was the algorithm designed to do? - a) Predict demand patterns - b) Detect malware - c) Manage employee schedules - d) Control the supply chain robots
Ver solução **a)** — *The algorithm was designed to predict demand patterns.*
**5.** What issue did the team encounter during the project? - a) Financial problems - b) Data privacy concerns - c) Staff shortages - d) Legal issues with competitors
Ver solução **b)** — *The team ran into some data privacy concerns at first.*
**6.** How long did it take the team to resolve the privacy issue? - a) 24 hours - b) 48 hours - c) One week - d) One month
Ver solução **b)** — *They came up with an encryption protocol within 48 hours.*
**7.** What phrasal verb does Sarah use for launching the update? - a) Phase out - b) Scale up - c) Roll out - d) Set up
Ver solução **c)** — *They've already rolled out the first phase.*
**8.** Which mixed conditional does Sarah use? - a) If they hadn't invested, they wouldn't survive - b) If they hadn't invested, they wouldn't have survived - c) If they invested, they wouldn't have survived - d) If they invested, they wouldn't survive
Ver solução **b)** — *If they hadn't invested in the technology, they wouldn't have survived the market disruption last year.* (past→past, third conditional)
**9.** What does James say is key to digital transformation? - a) Funding - b) Technology - c) Leadership - d) Marketing
Ver solução **c)** — *Leadership is key when it comes to digital transformation.*
**10.** What does Sarah think about the timing of the change? - a) They should have done it sooner - b) They did it too early - c) They should have waited - d) They did it at the perfect time
Ver solução **a)** — *The company should have made the change sooner.*
**11.** Identify the passive reporting structure in the dialogue:
Ver solução *It is believed that the new system will reduce costs by 30%.*
**12.** What phrasal verb means "to find a problem"?
Ver solução **Run into** — *The team ran into some data privacy concerns.*
**13.** What does Sarah say was the most important decision? - a) Hiring more staff - b) The CEO's decision to prioritise innovation - c) Buying new servers - d) Moving to a new office
Ver solução **b)** — *It was the CEO's decision to prioritise innovation that made it all possible.*
**14.** Which modal does James use to express speculation about the cost? - a) Must - b) Should - c) Could - d) May
Ver solução **a)** — *It must have been a massive investment.* (certeza ~95%)
**15.** Complete James's observation: "Traditional companies that didn't modernise have ______." - a) succeeded - b) struggled - c) expanded - d) innovated
Ver solução **b)** — *Traditional companies that didn't modernise have struggled.*
--- ## Lección 5 — Writing y Speaking ### Writing — Ejercicios **1.** Escribe una mixed conditional (pasado→presente) sobre el impacto de no haber inventado internet.
Ver solução *If internet had not been invented, the world would be a very different place today.*
**2.** Transforma al passive reporting: *People think that AI will replace many jobs.*
Ver solução *It is thought that AI will replace many jobs.*
**3.** Escribe una cleft sentence enfatizando cuándo ocurrió un fallo del sistema: (el fallo ocurrió durante la actualización)
Ver solução *It was during the update that the system failure occurred.*
**4.** Escribe un párrafo de 3-4 oraciones sobre ciberseguridad usando al menos 3 linkers diferentes.
Ver solução *Cybersecurity is a growing concern for businesses worldwide. Furthermore, the number of phishing attacks has increased dramatically in recent years. However, many companies still fail to invest adequately in protection. Consequently, data breaches continue to affect millions of users every year.*
**5.** Corrige: *If we would invest more in cybersecurity, breaches wouldn't have increased.*
Ver solução *If we **invested** more in cybersecurity, breaches **wouldn't have increased**.* — En la cláusula if no se usa "would"; y el resultado es pasado, así que "wouldn't have increased".
**6.** Escribe una oración usando el phrasal verb "phase out" en contexto de tecnología obsoleta.
Ver solução *The company plans to phase out its older software by the end of the year.*
**7.** Transforma al passive: *The developers will deploy the new update next week.*
Ver solução *The new update will be deployed next week.*
**8.** Escribe una cleft sentence enfatizando qué causó un problema: (la sobrecarga del servidor causó el problema)
Ver solução *It was the server overload that caused the problem.*
**9.** Completa: The system ______ have crashed due to the overload. (Certeza ~75%)
Ver solução *The system **should** have crashed due to the overload.* — "Should" indica alta probabilidad (~75%).
**10.** Escribe una mixed conditional (presente→pasado) sobre un error de codificación que causó un fallo.
Ver solução *If the code were written more carefully, the bug wouldn't have caused the crash.*
### Speaking — Ejercicios **11.** Responde en 2-3 oraciones: *If AI had been developed 20 years earlier, how would the world be different today?*
Ver solução *If AI had been developed 20 years earlier, many industries would be far more automated today. Healthcare diagnostics would be more advanced, and self-driving cars would probably be common by now.*
**12.** Explica con un modal de deduction: *Why do you think the new smartphone failed in the market?*
Ver solução *The new smartphone must have failed because of its high price and lack of innovative features. It might also have been affected by strong competition from established brands.*
**13.** Usa el passive reporting para explicar qué se cree sobre el futuro del trabajo:
Ver solução *It is believed that automation will create more jobs than it destroys. It is also thought that remote work will become the standard for many industries.*
**14.** Describe un problema tecnológico usando al menos 2 phrasal verbs:
Ver solução *Last week, our server broke down during peak hours. We ran into several issues while trying to set up the backup system, but the IT team came up with a temporary solution within a few hours.*
**15.** Escribe un mini-report técnico (4-5 oraciones) sobre un problema de ciberseguridad en tu empresa ficticia, usando al menos 2 linkers, 1 passive voice y 1 cleft sentence:
Ver solução *Last month, our company experienced a significant data breach. It was a phishing email that compromised the system, as an employee clicked on a malicious link. Consequently, customer data was exposed, and the issue affected over 5,000 accounts. The IT team deployed an immediate security patch; furthermore, all employees were required to complete cybersecurity training. It is recommended that the company invest in advanced encryption to prevent future incidents.*
--- ## Tip de la semana Cuando practiques gramática mixta, intenta **mezclar estructuras en un mismo párrafo**. No escribas solo conditionals, o solo passive: combínalas. Los exámenes B2 reales te obligan a alternar entre estructuras en el mismo ejercicio, así que la práctica integrada es la clave del éxito. --- **Siguiente:** [Unidad 57 — Gramática Mixta: Salud y Bienestar](/curso-b2/unit-57) **Artículos relacionados:** - [U55 — Repaso 51–54 + Globalización](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-55-repaso-51-54-globalisation) - [Curso B2 completo](/ingles-b2) --- ### Preguntas frecuentes (FAQs) **¿Qué gramática se practica en la Unidad 56?** Practica integrada de conditionals (mixed, third), passive voice, passive reporting, modals of deduction, phrasal verbs tech, linkers y cleft sentences en contexto de tecnología. **¿Cómo diferencia esta unidad de un repaso normal?** Las unidades de gramática mixta obligan a elegir entre múltiples estructuras en el mismo ejercicio, simulando un examen real donde debes identificar la forma correcta sin contexto previo. **¿Qué vocabulario tecnológico cubre?** Artificial intelligence, machine learning, data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithm, automation, blockchain, cloud computing, IoT, digital transformation. **¿Cómo debo preparar esta unidad?** Lee primero la teoría de cada estructura, luego completa los ejercicios sin mirar las pistas. Si fallas, identifica la familia gramatical antes de repetir. **¿Dónde practico la Unidad 56?** En la Unidad 56 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones. --- **Fuentes y referencias:** - Cambridge B2 First — Grammar Practice (Cambridge University Press) - Oxford Word Skills: Phrasal Verbs for IT (Oxford University Press) - British Council — B2 Grammar: Mixed Conditionals - National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) — Glossary of Cyber Terms - Cambridge Assessment English — B2 First Exam Format

import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import mixedGrammarHealthMap from '../../../assets/blog/curso-b2/unit-57/mixed-grammar-health-map.png'; import healthCampaign from '../../../assets/blog/curso-b2/unit-57/health-campaign.png'; import healthListening from '../../../assets/blog/curso-b2/unit-57/health-listening.png'; La **Unidad 57** integra todas las estructuras gramaticales B2 en el contexto de la **salud y el bienestar**. Cada ejemplo conecta forma y significado en situaciones médicas, preventivas y de estilo de vida. Al dominar estas estructuras podrás hablar y escribir con precisión sobre temas de salud, sistemas sanitarios, hábitos saludables y noticias médicas. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 57](/curso-b2/unit-57)
> **Antes:** [U56 — Gramática Mixta + Tecnología](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-56-mixed-grammar-technology)
> **Siguiente:** [Unidad 58 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-58) --- ## 1. Mixed Conditionals in Health Los *mixed conditionals* combinan tiempos diferentes en la condición y el resultado. En salud son especialmente útiles para hablar de consecuencias presentes de acciones pasadas o de resultados hipotéticos que afectan al presente. ### Type 1 — Past condition → Present result > *If the patient **had followed** the prescription, she **would be** better now.* La condición es pasada (no siguió la receta) y el resultado es presente (todavía no está bien). ### Type 2 — Present condition → Past result > *If the doctor **were** more thorough, he **would have caught** the symptoms earlier.* El doctor no es minucioso (presente) y por eso no detectó los síntomas a tiempo (pasado). ### Type 3 — Past condition → Past result (but emphasising present relevance) > *If they **had developed** the vaccine sooner, thousands of lives **would have been saved**.* ### Other health examples | Conditional | Example | |---|---| | Type 1 (past → present) | *If I **had eaten** less processed food, I **wouldn't have** high blood pressure now.* | | Type 2 (present → past) | *If the NHS **were** better funded, the waiting lists **would have been** shorter last year.* | | Mixed inversion | *Had the patient reported the pain, the diagnosis **would have been** earlier.* | > **Consejo:** En exámenes B2, la clave es identificar **cuándo** ocurre la condición y **cuándo** ocurre el resultado. Si no coinciden en tiempo, necesitas un *mixed conditional*. --- ## 2. Passive Voice in Medical Reports La voz pasiva es omnipresente en textos médicos porque el foco está en la acción y el paciente, no en quién la realiza. ### Structures | Tense | Active | Passive | |---|---|---| | Past Simple | *The nurse administered the treatment.* | *The treatment **was administered** by the nurse.* | | Present Perfect | *Doctors have diagnosed the condition.* | *The condition **has been diagnosed**.* | | Past Perfect | *They had performed the surgery.* | *The surgery **had been performed**.* | | Future Simple | *They will carry out more tests.* | *More tests **will be carried out**.* | | Modals | *You should take the medication.* | *The medication **should be taken**.* | ### Health-specific examples > *The patient **has been diagnosed** with Type 2 diabetes.*
> *A new vaccine **is being tested** in clinical trials.*
> *The operation **was carried out** by a specialist surgeon.*
> *Three doses of the medication **should be taken** daily.* > **Clave B2:** En informes médicos se omite frecuentemente el agente (*by the doctor*) porque es obvio por el contexto. --- ## 3. Passive Reporting in Health News La *passive reporting* se usa en noticias de salud para presentar información sin atribuirla a una fuente concreta. ### Common structures | Structure | Example | |---|---| | *It is believed that...* | ***It is believed that** the outbreak originated in a wet market.* | | *...is believed to have...* | *The virus **is believed to have** mutated several times.* | | *It is estimated that...* | ***It is estimated that** 1 in 3 adults suffers from hypertension.* | | *...is thought to be...* | *Stress **is thought to be** a major factor in heart disease.* | | *It is reported that...* | ***It is reported that** the new treatment has a 90% success rate.* | | *...was reported to have...* | *The patient **was reported to have** made a full recovery.* | ### Combining with other structures > *The vaccine, **which is believed to be** effective against the new variant, **will be administered** next week.*
> ***It is estimated that** if people **exercised** regularly, the rate of obesity **would drop** significantly.* --- ## 4. Modals of Obligation and Deduction in Healthcare ### Obligation | Modal | Strength | Example | |---|---|---| | *must* | Strong obligation | *Patients **must** take the full course of antibiotics.* | | *have to* | External obligation | *You **have to** fast before the blood test.* | | *should* | Advice | *You **should** reduce your salt intake.* | | *ought to* | Slightly weaker advice | *You **ought to** see a specialist about that.* | | *mustn't* | Prohibition | *You **mustn't** drink alcohol with this medication.* | | *don't have to* | No obligation | *You **don't have to** stay overnight for this procedure.* | ### Deduction | Modal | Certainty | Example | |---|---|---| | *must* | Near certain | *She **must be** exhausted after the surgery.* | | *might / may* | Possible | *The symptoms **might indicate** a viral infection.* | | *can't* | Impossible | *It **can't be** a fracture — the X-ray is clear.* | | *could* | Theoretical possibility | *This treatment **could** revolutionise cancer care.* | ### Perfect modals (past deduction) > *The doctor **might have recommended** a different approach.*
> *She **must have forgotten** to take her medication.*
> *He **can't have been** following the diet — his cholesterol is still high.* --- ## 5. Wish / Regret in Health Context ### Structure | Form | Use | Example | |---|---|---| | *wish* + past simple | Present regret | *I **wish** I **exercised** more often.* | | *wish* + past perfect | Past regret | *I **wish** I **had started** exercising earlier.* | | *wish* + would | Complaint / annoyance | *I **wish** the doctor **would** listen to my concerns.* | | *regret* + -ing | Past action you're sorry about | *I **regret** not going to the doctor sooner.* | | *If only...* | Stronger wish | ***If only** I had quit smoking years ago.* | ### Health examples > *Many patients **wish** they **had sought** medical advice sooner.*
> *I **regret** not taking my mental health seriously earlier.*
> ***If only** the government **invested** more in preventive care.*
> *She **wishes** the hospital **would** keep her better informed.* --- ## 6. Phrasal Verbs for Health | Phrasal verb | Meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | *bring up* | Mention / introduce (a topic) | *She **brought up** her symptoms during the consultation.* | | *carry out* | Perform (tests, procedures) | *The lab **carried out** a full blood analysis.* | | *cut down on* | Reduce consumption | *He was advised to **cut down on** saturated fat.* | | *go through* | Experience / endure | *She **went through** months of chemotherapy.* | | *look into* | Investigate | *The NHS is **looking into** alternative treatments.* | | *set up* | Establish / create | *They **set up** a new mental health clinic in the area.* | | *take over* | Assume responsibility | *A specialist will **take over** the patient's care.* | | *work out* | Exercise | *She **works out** at the gym three times a week.* | | *come down with* | Become ill with | *He **came down with** the flu last week.* | | *build up* | Increase gradually | *You need to **build up** your stamina slowly.* | --- ## 7. Linkers in Health Writing ### Cause / Effect > *Due to a poor diet, the patient developed high cholesterol.*
> *As a result of regular exercise, her blood pressure improved.*
> *The increase in obesity is largely caused by sedentary lifestyles.*
> *Consequently, the NHS has introduced new screening programmes.* ### Contrast > *Although the treatment was effective, it had significant side effects.*
> *Despite the advances in medicine, cancer remains difficult to cure.*
> *However, not all patients respond to the same medication.*
> *Nevertheless, prevention is always better than cure.* ### Addition > *In addition to medication, patients should adopt a healthier diet.*
> *Furthermore, mental health is just as important as physical health.*
> *Moreover, regular check-ups can detect problems early.*
> *Equally important is the role of sleep in overall wellbeing.* > **Tip para writing B2:** Varía los linkers. No repitas *however* en cada párrafo. Alterna con *nevertheless*, *on the other hand*, *conversely*. --- ## 8. Reading — A Public Health Campaign > **Read the text about a new public health initiative.** A major public health campaign has been launched across the UK to tackle the rising rates of obesity and Type 2 diabetes. Health experts believe that if the government were to invest more in preventive measures, the long-term burden on the NHS would be significantly reduced. Listening + Dialogue > **Listen to a conversation between a patient (Emma) and her GP (Dr. Khan).** **Dr. Khan:** Good morning, Emma. What seems to be the problem? **Emma:** Well, Doctor, I've been feeling really tired lately, and I've been getting headaches almost every day. **Dr. Khan:** I see. How long has this been going on? **Emma:** About three weeks now. I thought it would go away, but it hasn't. **Dr. Khan:** Have you been sleeping properly? **Emma:** Not really. I've been working late, and I suppose I haven't been eating very well either. **Dr. Khan:** Right. I'm going to refer you to a specialist, but first I'd like to carry out some blood tests. Writing — Health Reports En B2, los informes de salud requieren un tono formal, voz pasiva y passive reporting. ### Estructura típica 1. **Introduction:** Purpose and background 2. **Findings:** Data and observations (passive voice) 3. **Conclusions:** Deductions (modals) 4. **Recommendations:** Obligation and advice (should, must) ### Example extract > *This report examines the effects of remote working on employee wellbeing. It is estimated that 60% of remote workers have reported increased levels of stress. The findings suggest that if companies were to implement structured wellness programmes, mental health issues could be significantly reduced. It is recommended that employees should be offered regular check-ups and access to counselling services.* --- ## 12. Speaking ### Common health topics in B2 speaking exams - Describe a healthy / unhealthy lifestyle - Talk about your own health habits - Discuss the pros and cons of a national health service - Give advice about a health problem - Discuss whether certain treatments should be free ### Useful phrases > *I wish people would take their health more seriously.*
> *If everyone exercised regularly, the rate of chronic disease would fall.*
> *It is widely believed that prevention is better than cure.*
> *You ought to consider cutting down on sugar.*
> *The study is thought to have limitations because the sample was too small.* --- ## 13. Common Errors | ❌ Error | ✅ Correct | Explanation | |---|---|---| | *If I would have gone to the doctor...* | *If I **had gone** to the doctor...* | En conditionals, nunca se usa *would* en la cláusula condicional. | | *The patient has been diagnosed from cancer.* | *The patient has been diagnosed **with** cancer.* | El verbo *diagnose* se combina con *with*. | | *She must to take the medicine.* | *She **must take** the medicine.* | Los modales nunca llevan *to* infinitive. | | *I wish I didn't smoke.* | *I wish I **didn't** smoke.* (OK for present) OR *I wish I **hadn't started** smoking.* (for past) | Asegúrate de que el tiempo del *wish* refleje si es presente o pasado. | | *It is believe that...* | ***It is believed** that...* | Passive reporting necesita el participio (*believed*), no el infinitivo. | | *He might have recommended different.* | *He might have recommended **something different**.* | En inglés, el adjetivo va después del pronombre indefinido. | | *Despite of the side effects...* | ***Despite** the side effects...* / ***In spite of** the side effects...* | *Despite* no lleva *of*. *In spite of* sí. | | *The symptoms was very mild.* | *The symptoms **were** very mild.* | *Symptoms* es plural. | --- ## 14. If the patient \_\_\_\_\_\_ (take) the medication on time, she \_\_\_\_\_\_ (not feel) so unwell now. 2. If the government \_\_\_\_\_\_ (invest) more in mental health services, the waiting lists \_\_\_\_\_\_ (not be) so long last year. 3. If I \_\_\_\_\_\_ (not skip) breakfast every day, I \_\_\_\_\_\_ (not have) so much low energy in the mornings. 4. Had the surgeon \_\_\_\_\_\_ (perform) the operation earlier, the patient \_\_\_\_\_\_ (make) a full recovery by now. 5. If the vaccine \_\_\_\_\_\_ (be) available globally, the pandemic \_\_\_\_\_\_ (not affect) so many people in 2020.
Ver solução 1. **had taken / wouldn't feel** — Past condition → present result. 2. **had invested / wouldn't have been** — Past condition → past result with present relevance. 3. **didn't skip / wouldn't have** — Present condition → past result. 4. **performed / would have made** — Inverted past condition → past result. 5. **were / wouldn't have affected** — Present unreal condition → past result.

He \_\_\_\_\_\_ (near certain deduction) have taken the wrong dose — his symptoms are unusual. 5. You \_\_\_\_\_\_ (no obligation) come to the appointment if you're feeling better.
Ver solução 1. **should** — Advice. 2. **must not** — Prohibition. 3. **might / may** — Possibility. 4. **must** — Near certain deduction (past). 5. **don't have to** — No obligation.
--- #### Ejercicio 31: Wish/Regret — Reflect on Health Write a sentence using *wish* or *regret* for each situation. 1. You started smoking when you were 16. (past regret) 2. You don't go to the gym. (present wish) 3. Your doctor didn't explain the side effects. (past wish) 4. You skipped your annual check-up last year. (regret + -ing) 5. Your hospital doesn't have enough staff. (wish + would)
Ver solução 1. I wish I **hadn't started** smoking when I was 16. 2. I wish I **went** to the gym regularly. 3. I wish my doctor **had explained** the side effects. 4. I regret **skipping** my annual check-up last year. 5. I wish my hospital **would** hire more staff.
--- #### Ejercicio 32: Linkers — Health Essay Combine each pair of sentences with an appropriate linker. 1. Regular exercise improves physical health. It also benefits mental health. 2. The treatment was expensive. It was worth it because it saved his life. 3. She followed the doctor's advice. She didn't recover as quickly as expected. 4. The patient was admitted to hospital. He was discharged the following day. 5. Smoking increases the risk of lung cancer. Many people continue to smoke.
Ver solução 1. Regular exercise improves physical health, **and** it **also** benefits mental health. / **Not only** does regular exercise improve physical health, **but** it **also** benefits mental health. 2. **Although / Even though** the treatment was expensive, it was worth it because it saved his life. 3. **Although / Even though** she followed the doctor's advice, she didn't recover as quickly as expected. 4. The patient was admitted to hospital **but** was discharged the following day. 5. **Although / Even though** smoking increases the risk of lung cancer, many people continue to smoke. / Smoking increases the risk of lung cancer; **however**, many people continue to smoke.
--- #### Ejercicio 33: Health Vocabulary — Error Correction Find and correct the error in each sentence. 1. The patient was diagnosed from diabetes last year. 2. She is taking a prescription for her headaches. 3. The doctor recommended me to rest for a week. 4. He has a surgery on his knee next month. 5. The symptoms was very mild at first.
Ver solução 1. ...diagnosed **with** diabetes... (*diagnose* + *with*) 2. She **has** a prescription... OR She was **given** a prescription... (*take a prescription* is incorrect) 3. The doctor recommended **that I rest** for a week. / The doctor recommended **resting** for a week. (*recommend* + gerund / *that* clause, not *recommend someone to do*) 4. He **is having** surgery... OR He **is scheduled for** surgery... (*have surgery*, not *a surgery*) 5. The symptoms **were** very mild... (*symptoms* is plural)
--- #### Ejercicio 34: Speaking — Role Play Prompts Prepare a 2-minute spoken response for **one** of the following prompts. Use at least **three** different B2 structures from this unit. **Prompt A:** *Describe a time when you or someone you know had to deal with a health problem. What happened? What was the treatment? How do you wish the situation had been handled differently?* **Prompt B:** *Some people argue that prevention is better than cure. Do you agree? What could the government do to improve public health? Use conditionals and modals in your answer.* **Prompt C:** *Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of a national health service like the NHS. Use linkers of contrast and addition.*
Ver modelo de resposta (Prompt A) A few years ago, a close friend of mine was diagnosed with severe anaemia. She had been feeling exhausted for months, but she hadn't gone to the doctor because she thought it was just stress. By the time she was diagnosed, her iron levels were dangerously low. She was prescribed iron supplements and had to go through regular blood tests for six months. Looking back, she wishes she had sought medical advice sooner. If she had gone to her GP earlier, the treatment would have been much simpler. It is believed that early diagnosis in cases like this leads to significantly better outcomes. I think this experience taught both of us the importance of not ignoring persistent symptoms.
--- #### Ejercicio 35: Writing — Health Report Structure Write a short health report (150–200 words) on the topic: *"The Impact of Screen Time on Teenage Mental Health."* Use the following structure: - **Introduction:** State the purpose of the report. - **Findings:** Present two or three key facts (use passive voice and passive reporting). - **Conclusions:** Use modals of deduction. - **Recommendations:** Use modals of obligation and advice.
Ver modelo de resposta **The Impact of Screen Time on Teenage Mental Health** This report examines the effects of excessive screen time on the mental health of teenagers aged 13–17. It is estimated that teenagers spend an average of seven hours per day on screens outside of schoolwork. Recent studies suggest that more than four hours of recreational screen time is associated with increased levels of anxiety and depression. It is believed that social media use is a particularly significant factor, as it can lead to disrupted sleep patterns and low self-esteem. It is concluded that excessive screen time is likely to have a negative impact on teenage mental health. If current trends continue, the rate of mental health issues among adolescents could rise significantly. It is recommended that parents should set clear boundaries around screen use, and that schools should incorporate digital wellbeing into their curricula. Furthermore, the government ought to fund further research into this area. *(164 words)*
--- #### Ejercicio 36: Speaking — Discuss and Compare Work with a partner (or write a response) comparing **two** healthcare systems you know about (e.g., NHS vs. the US system). Discuss: - How they are funded - The role of prevention vs. treatment - What you wish could be improved Use passive reporting, mixed conditionals, and at least two phrasal verbs.
Ver modelo de resposta The NHS in the UK provides healthcare free at the point of use, funded through taxation. In contrast, the US system relies heavily on private insurance. It is believed that the NHS model ensures greater equity, but it is also thought to suffer from long waiting times due to underfunding. If the US system were to adopt a more preventive approach, it could reduce the enormous costs associated with chronic disease. Likewise, if the NHS were better funded, patients wouldn't have to go through such long delays for treatment. I wish both systems would invest more in mental health services. It is widely reported that mental health is the area most neglected in both countries. From what I've looked into, community-based programmes could be set up at relatively low cost and could make a significant difference.
--- ## Tips para esta unidad - **Mixed conditionals** son la estructura más discriminadora en B2. Dominar la diferencia entre *If I had... (I would be...)* y *If I were... (I would have been...)* te separa del nivel A2-B1. - **Passive reporting** aparece en casi every Reading & Use of English task. Memoriza las estructuras *It is believed that...* y *...is thought to have...*. - **Phrasal verbs** de salud (*carry out, cut down on, go through*) son altamente productivos en Writing y Speaking. --- ## Siguiente paso > Siguiente: [Unidad 58 — Exam Strategies + Use of English](/curso-b2/unit-58) --- ## Temas relacionados - [Unidad 56 — Gramática Mixta + Tecnología](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-56-mixed-grammar-technology) - [Unidad 58 — Exam Strategies + Use of English](/curso-b2/unit-58) - [Curso B2 completo](/ingles-b2) --- ## Preguntas frecuentes **¿Qué gramática se practica en la Unidad 57?** Practica integrada de conditionals, passive voice, passive reporting, modals of obligation/deduction, phrasal verbs, linkers y wish/regret en contexto de salud. **¿Qué vocabulario sanitario cubre?** Diagnosis, treatment, symptoms, prescription, clinical trial, vaccine, outbreak, mental health, wellbeing, nutrition, physical activity, NHS, healthcare system, epidemic. **¿Cómo trabajo las estructuras mixtas en salud?** Cada ejercicio presenta una situación médica o de bienestar donde debes elegir la estructura correcta entre varias opciones gramaticales. **¿Puedo saltar directamente a los ejercicios?** No. Revisa primero la teoría de cada estructura. Los ejercicios asumen que comprendes la diferencia entre formas cercanas. **¿Dónde practico la Unidad 57?** En la Unidad 57 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones. --- ## Fuentes - British Medical Journal — *Preventive healthcare and public health policy* - NHS England — *Mental Health Audit Statistics 2025* - World Health Organization — *Global Report on Diabetes* - Cambridge English — *B2 First Handbook for Teachers* - Oxford University Press — *English File B2: Health and Wellbeing Unit* - Public Health England — *Childhood Obesity: A Plan for Action*
