content:
# Unidad 58 — Estrategias de Examen: Use of English (Teoría y Ejercicios) La **Unidad 58** prepara para el **Use of English** del examen **Cambridge B2 First**. Cada parte del Use of English exige una estrategia diferente: reconocer collocations en el cloze, recuperar palabras gramaticales en el open cloze, transformar prefijos y sufijos en el word formation, y reconstruir cadenas gramaticales en las key word transformations. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 58](/curso-b2/unit-58)
> **Antes:** [U57 — Gramática Mixta + Salud](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-57-mixed-grammar-health)
> **Siguiente:** [Unidad 59 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-59) --- ## Teoría — Estrategias para cada parte del Use of English El Use of English consta de **4 partes** que suman **40 preguntas** en un total de **45 minutos**. Cada parte tiene una pauta distinta y requiere técnicas específicas. --- ### Part 1: Multiple-choice cloze (8 preguntas) Lees un texto con **8 huecos** y debes elegir la palabra correcta entre **4 opciones** para cada uno. Se evalúa principalmente tu conocimiento de **collocations** (combinaciones frecuentes de palabras) y **fixed phrases** (expresiones fijas). **Estrategia paso a paso:** 1. **Lee el texto completo primero** sin mirar las opciones. Intenta comprender el significado general. 2. **Identifica el tipo de combinación** que necesitas: ¿verbo + sustantivo? ¿adjetivo + sustantivo? ¿expresión fija? 3. **Lee solo el hueco y su contexto inmediato.** No leas toda la oración otra vez; enfócate en las 2-3 palabras antes y después del hueco. 4. **Prueba cada opción** insertándola en la oración completa. Solo una sonará natural. 5. **Cambia de sección** si te estancas más de 2 minutos en un hueco. **Ejemplo de collocation:** > The government has decided to ___ new measures to reduce pollution. > > A) make　B) do　C) take　D) put La respuesta correcta es **C) take** — la collocation es *take measures*. --- ### Part 2: Open cloze (12 preguntas) Lees un texto con **12 huecos** y debes escribir **exactamente una palabra** en cada uno. No hay opciones: debes recuperar la palabra gramatical correcta del contexto. **Estrategia paso a paso:** 1. **Lee el párrafo completo** antes de empezar a responder. 2. **Identifica qué tipo de palabra falta** en cada hueco: | Tipo | Ejemplos | Señales típicas | |------|----------|-----------------| | Artículo | *a, an, the, ∅* | Antes de un sustantivo | | Pronombre | *it, they, which, who, that* | Antes de un verbo o después de una preposición | | Preposición | *in, on, at, by, with, for* | Antes de un sustantivo o pronombre | | Auxiliar | *is, was, has, have, had, do, does, did* | Antes de un verbo principal | | Conjuncción | *and, but, because, although, when* | Entre oraciones o cláusulas | 3. **Lee la oración completa** con tu palabra para confirmar que tiene sentido. 4. **No escribas más de una palabra.** Los artículos no son palabra compuesta; *a* y *an* cuentan como una palabra. **Ejemplo:** > She couldn't go to the party ___ she had to work late. La respuesta es **because** — conjunción que introduce la razón. --- ### Part 3: Word formation (10 preguntas) Lees un texto con **10 huecos** y una **palabra raíz** entre corchetes que debes transformar para completar el hueco. Puedes añadir prefijos, sufijos o ambas cosas. **Estrategia paso a paso:** 1. **Lee la oración completa** e identifica qué **parte de la oración** necesitas (sustantivo, adjetivo, verbo, adverbio). 2. **Observa el contexto inmediato del hueco**: ¿hay un artículo antes? → sustantivo. ¿Modifica a un sustantivo? → adjetivo. ¿Modifica a un verbo o adjetivo? → adverbio. 3. **Aplica la transformación adecuada** usando prefijos y sufijos comunes. 4. **Lee la oración completa** con tu palabra para verificar significado y gramática. 5. **Verifica si necesitas plural** en sustantivos o **grado comparativo/superlativo** en adjetivos. **Ejemplo:** > The ___ of the new policy was felt immediately. (APPEAR) La respuesta es **appearance** — necesitas un sustantivo (artículo *the* delante) y se forma con el sufijo *-ance*. --- ### Part 4: Key word transformations (10 preguntas) Tienes una oración original, una **palabra clave** y una oración incompleta. Debes reescribir la oración usando la palabra clave sin cambiar su forma, para que signifique lo mismo que la original. **Estrategia paso a paso:** 1. **Lee la oración original** hasta entender completamente su significado. 2. **Identifica la estructura gramatical** clave: pasiva, condicional, reported speech, estructura con *so/such*, comparativos, etc. 3. **Lee la palabra clave** y piensa en qué estructura gramatical exige. 4. **Construye la oración completa** antes de comparar con la incompleta. 5. **Verifica:** - ¿La palabra clave aparece exactamente como está (sin cambios)? - ¿Las palabras adicionales son correctas? - ¿La puntuación y el significado coinciden? **Ejemplo:** > Original: "People believe that the suspect left the country last week." > Key word: **BELIEVED** > Transformation: The suspect ___ last week. Respuesta: **is believed to have left the country** --- ### Prefijos y sufijos comunes en B2 Tabla de referencia rápida: | Prefijo | Significado | Ejemplo | |---------|-------------|---------| | un- | negación | *unhappy, unable, unusual* | | re- | repetición | *rebuild, rethink, reconnect* | | dis- | negación/opuesto | *disagree, disappear, dishonest* | | mis- | error | *misunderstand, mislead* | | over- | exceso | *overestimate, overwork* | | under- | insuficiencia | *underline, underestimate* | | pre- | antes | *predict, prevent, prepare* | | inter- | entre | *international, interact* | | de- | reverso | *decrease, decline* | | out- | exterior/superior | *outperform, outgrow* | | Sufijo (sustantivos) | Sufijo (adjetivos) | Sufijo (verbos) | |-----------------------|---------------------|------------------| | -tion / -sion | -ful / -less | -ise / -ize | | -ment | -ive | -ify | | -ness | -able / -ible | -en | | -ity | -ous / -ous | | | -ance / -ence | -al | | | -er / -or | -ary / -ory | | --- ### Collocations frecuentes en el examen B2 Estas combinaciones aparecen constantemente en el Use of English: | Verbo + sustantivo | Adjetivo + sustantivo | Verbo + preposición | |---------------------|------------------------|---------------------| | *take* measures | *significant* impact | *depend on* | | *make* progress | *considerable* amount | *consist of* | | *reach* agreement | *major* concern | *belong to* | | *draw* conclusion | *serious* problem | *result in* | | *pay* attention | *wide* range | *lead to* | | *raise* awareness | *strong* evidence | *concentrate on* | | *carry out* research | *potential* risk | *succeed in* | | *commit* crime | *fundamental* change | *refer to* | --- ### Lectura de ejemplo: The Future of Remote Work > The world of work has undergone a **dramatic** transformation in recent years. Before the pandemic, remote work was considered a **luxury** that only a few companies could afford to offer. However, the **sudden** shift to working from home **proved** that productivity could be maintained — and in many cases, **enhanced** — outside the traditional office environment. > **Surveys** conducted across multiple industries have **consistently** shown that employees **prefer** flexible working arrangements. The **majority** of workers say they would consider **leaving** their job if remote options were removed entirely. This **represents** a significant challenge for employers who wish to **require** full-time office attendance. > **Nevertheless**, the remote model is not without its **drawbacks**. Many managers have **expressed concerns** about team cohesion, **communication** gaps, and the **difficulty** of onboarding new staff. Companies are now **experimenting** with hybrid models that attempt to **balance** the benefits of flexibility with the need for **collaboration**. --- ### Tips para el Listening (conexión con Use of English) Aunque el Listening es una sección separada, las habilidades del Use of English te ayudan: - **Collocations en el Listening**: si reconoces combinaciones como *take into account* o *make an effort*, identificarás las respuestas más rápido. - **Gramática del open cloze**: las palabras gramaticales (*which, although, despite*) aparecen también en los audios como conectores entre ideas. - **Word formation auditiva**: al escuchar, tu cerebro reconoce patrones de sufijos que refuerzan la comprensión. --- ### Errores comunes en el examen | # | Error | Cómo evitarlo | |---|-------|---------------| | 1 | No leer el texto completo antes de responder en cloze | Lee el texto entero primero; el contexto es clave. | | 2 | Escribir más de una palabra en el open cloze | Verifica: "¿puedo escribir esta respuesta con una sola palabra?" | | 3 | No cambiar la parte de la oración en word formation | Identifica primero qué parte de la oración necesitas. | | 4 | Cambiar la keyword en key word transformations | La keyword debe aparecer exactamente igual en tu respuesta. | | 5 | No usar el singular/plural correcto en word formation | Revisa el artículo y el contexto: *a problem* vs *problems*. | | 6 | Ignorar el significado general en cloze | Si la palabra encaja gramaticalmente pero no semánticamente, es incorrecta. | | 7 | No practicar con cronómetro | El tiempo es limitado: 45 minutos para 40 preguntas. | | 8 | Olvidar el doble significado en key word transformations | Cada key word transformation puede valer hasta 2 puntos. | --- ### Resumen rápido | Parte | Tipo | Preguntas | Tiempo | Estrategia clave | |-------|------|-----------|--------|------------------| | Part 1 | Multiple-choice cloze | 8 | ~12 min | Collocations y fixed phrases | | Part 2 | Open cloze | 12 | ~12 min | Palabras gramaticales del contexto | | Part 3 | Word formation | 10 | ~10 min | Parte de la oración + prefijos/sufijos | | Part 4 | Key word transformations | 10 | ~16 min | Estructura gramatical + keyword intacta | --- ## Ejercicios ### Lección 1 — Part 1: Multiple-choice cloze #### A. Collocations: verbo + sustantivo **1.** The company has decided to ___ a new strategy to increase sales. A) make　B) take　C) do　D) set **2.** Scientists have been ___ research into the effects of climate change. A) making　B) doing　C) taking　D) carrying **3.** It took us three hours to ___ an agreement with the other team. A) make　B) reach　C) get　D) find **4.** The government needs to ___ more effort into improving education. A) give　B) take　C) put　D) make **5.** She finally managed to ___ a decision after thinking about it all night. A) do　B) make　C) take　D) have
Ver solução 1. **D) set** — *set a strategy* (collocation verbo + sustantivo) 2. **D) carrying** — *carry out research* 3. **B) reach** — *reach an agreement* 4. **C) put** — *put effort into* 5. **B) make** — *make a decision*
#### B. Collocations: adjetivo + sustantivo **6.** There is ___ evidence to suggest that exercise improves mental health. A) strong　B) heavy　C) thick　D) powerful **7.** The report highlighted the ___ risk of flooding in coastal areas. A) serious　B) heavy　C) severe　D) big **8.** She showed a ___ interest in learning about different cultures. A) high　B) big　C) wide　D) deep **9.** The ___ of unemployment has increased dramatically this year. A) rate　B) level　C) number　D) speed **10.** We need to make a ___ effort to reduce our carbon emissions. A) huge　B) large　C) strong　D) great
Ver solução 6. **A) strong** — *strong evidence* 7. **C) severe** — *severe risk* 8. **C) wide** — *wide interest* (también aceptable: *deep interest*, pero *wide* es la collocation más natural en este contexto) 9. **A) rate** — *rate of unemployment* 10. **D) great** — *great effort*
#### C. Fixed phrases **11.** I'm ___ sorry, but I can't come to the meeting tomorrow. A) much　B) very　C) so　D) truly **12.** The project was completed ___ schedule, which impressed everyone. A) in　B) at　C) on　D) by **13.** She was ___ control of the situation from the very beginning. A) at　B) in　C) on　D) under **14.** We need to take this matter ___ consideration before making a final decision. A) into　B) in　C) to　D) for **15.** The new shopping centre is ___ the other side of the river. A) in　B) at　C) on　D) by
Ver solução 11. **D) truly** — *truly sorry* (fixed phrase) 12. **C) on** — *on schedule* 13. **B) in** — *in control of* 14. **A) into** — *take into consideration* 15. **C) on** — *on the other side*
#### D. Mixed cloze **16.** The teacher asked the students to hand ___ their essays by Friday. A) in　B) out　C) on　D) up **17.** We've run ___ milk. Could you go to the shop? A) off　B) out of　C) down　D) away **18.** The politician tried to avoid ___ the question directly. A) answer　B) to answer　C) answering　D) answered **19.** She has been working here ___ five years now. A) since　B) for　C) during　D) in **20.** It's no ___ complaining about the weather — we can't change it. A) use　B) point　C) worth　D) purpose
Ver solução 16. **A) in** — *hand in* (entregar) 17. **B) out of** — *run out of* (quedarse sin) 18. **C) answering** — *avoid + -ing* 19. **B) for** — *for + periodo de tiempo* 20. **A) use** — *it's no use + -ing*
--- ### Lección 2 — Part 2: Open cloze #### A. Artículos y pronombres **1.** The company has decided to launch ___ new product line next month. **2.** She couldn't find ___ keys anywhere, so she had to call a locksmith. **3.** ___ is important to learn from your mistakes if you want to improve. **4.** The students were given ___ assignment to complete over the weekend. **5.** My brother is a doctor. ___ works at the local hospital.
Ver solução 1. **a** — *a new product line* (indefinido, primera mención) 2. **her** — *her keys* (pronombre posesivo) 3. **It** — *It is important to...* (pronombre sujeto impersonal) 4. **an** — *an assignment* (indefinido, vocal) 5. **He** — *He works...* (pronombre sujeto)
#### B. Prepositions **6.** She has always been interested ___ learning new languages. **7.** The concert was postponed ___ bad weather conditions. **8.** We need to come ___ with a solution before Monday. **9.** The book was written ___ a famous British author. **10.** I've been looking forward ___ this holiday for months.
Ver solução 6. **in** — *interested in* 7. **due to** — *postponed due to* (también aceptable: *because of*) 8. **up** — *come up with* 9. **by** — *written by* (agente pasivo) 10. **to** — *looking forward to*
#### C. Auxiliares y conjunciones **11.** She ___ have told you about the meeting — it was a secret. **12.** ___ the rain continued, we decided to stay indoors. **13.** I don't think he ___ coming to the party tonight. **14.** The project was delayed ___ some of the materials hadn't arrived. **15.** She was tired, ___ she kept working until midnight.
Ver solução 11. **shouldn't** — *shouldn't have told* (no debería haber dicho) 12. **As** — *As the rain continued* (conjunction causale) 13. **is** — *he is coming* (present continuous) 14. **because** — *because some materials hadn't arrived* 15. **but** — *tired, but she kept working* (contrast)
#### D. Mixed open cloze **16.** The manager is thinking ___ expanding the business into new markets. **17.** This is the most difficult test ___ I have ever taken. **18.** Nobody was ___ to answer the question correctly. **19.** The movie was ___ interesting that we watched it twice. **20.** She has been working here ___ she graduated from university.
Ver solução 16. **about** — *thinking about* 17. **that** — *the most difficult test that...* 18. **able** — *was able to answer* 19. **so** — *so interesting that...* 20. **since** — *since she graduated* (present perfect + since)
--- ### Lección 3 — Part 3: Word formation #### A. Formation de sustantivos (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity) **1.** The ___ of the project was completed ahead of schedule. (COMPLETE) **2.** There has been a significant ___ in crime rates this year. (REDUCE) **3.** Her ___ to detail is what makes her an excellent editor. (ATTEND) **4.** The ___ of the new building will take two years. (CONSTRUCT) **5.** He showed great ___ when dealing with the difficult situation. (CALM)
Ver solução 1. **completion** — *the completion* (sustantivo de *complete*, sufijo *-ion*) 2. **reduction** — *a reduction* (sustantivo de *reduce*, sufijo *-tion*) 3. **attention** — *attention to detail* (sustantivo de *attend*, sufijo *-tion*) 4. **construction** — *the construction* (sustantivo de *construct*, sufijo *-tion*) 5. **calmness** — *great calmness* (sustantivo de *calm*, sufijo *-ness*)
#### B. Formation de adjetivos (-ful, -less, -ive, -able) **6.** The teacher gave us a ___ explanation of the rules. (USE) **7.** He felt completely ___ when he lost his job. (HELP) **8.** The new system is much more ___ than the old one. (EFFICIENCY) **9.** The situation was so ___ that we had to act immediately. (URGE) **10.** This book is absolutely ___. I couldn't put it down. (FASCINATE)
Ver solução 6. **useful** — *a useful explanation* (adjetivo de *use*, sufijo *-ful*) 7. **helpless** — *felt helpless* (adjetivo de *help*, sufijo *-less*) 8. **efficient** — *more efficient* (adjetivo de *efficiency*, sufijo *-ent*) 9. **urgent** — *an urgent situation* (adjetivo de *urge*, sufijo *-ent*) 10. **fascinating** — *absolutely fascinating* (adjetivo de *fascinate*, sufijo *-ing*)
#### C. Formation de verbos (un-, re-, dis-, en-, -ise, -ify) **11.** The company decided to ___ the damaged equipment. (REPLACE) **12.** She tried to ___ her friends from making a bad decision. (COURAGE) **13.** We need to ___ our subscription before the end of the month. (NEW) **14.** He chose to ___ the offer because the terms were unacceptable. (ACCEPT) **15.** The teacher asked us to ___ the results of the experiment. (SIMPLE)
Ver solução 11. **replace** — *to replace the equipment* (verbo con prefijo *re-*: *re+place*) 12. **discourage** — *discourage her friends* (verbo con prefijo *dis-*: *dis+courage*) 13. **renew** — *to renew our subscription* (verbo con prefijo *re-*: *re+new*) 14. **reject** — *to reject the offer* (verbo con prefijo *re-*: *re+ject*) 15. **simplify** — *to simplify the results* (verbo con sufijo *-ify*: *simple → simplify*)
#### D. Mixed word formation **16.** The ___ between the two countries has lasted for decades. (DIFFER) **17.** She spoke with such ___ that everyone was impressed. (CONFIDENT) **18.** The government has ___ increased spending on healthcare. (SIGNIFICANT) **19.** We were all ___ by the beauty of the sunset. (AMAZE) **20.** The company's ___ has improved significantly this quarter. (PERFORM)
Verção 16. **difference** — *the difference* (sustantivo de *differ*, sufijo *-ence*) 17. **confidence** — *with such confidence* (sustantivo de *confident*, sufijo *-ence*) 18. **significantly** — *has significantly increased* (adverbio de *significant*, sufijo *-ly*) 19. **amazed** — *we were amazed* (adjetivo pasivo de *amaze*, sufijo *-ed*) 20. **performance** — *the company's performance* (sustantivo de *perform*, sufijo *-ance*)
--- ### Lección 4 — Part 4: Key word transformations #### A. Passive transformations **1.** "They will build a new hospital in the town centre." **Key word: GOING** → A new hospital ___ in the town centre. **2.** "Someone stole my bicycle from outside the shop." **Key word: STOLEN** → My bicycle ___ from outside the shop. **3.** "The police are questioning the suspect right now." **Key word: BEING** → The suspect ___ by the police right now. **4.** "People speak English in many countries around the world." **Key word: SPOKEN** → English ___ in many countries around the world. **5.** "The company will announce the results next week." **Key word: ANNOUNCED** → The results ___ next week.
Ver solução 1. **is going to be built** — *going* + passive (*be going to* + passive) 2. **has been stolen** — *has been stolen* (present perfect passive) 3. **is being questioned** — *is being questioned* (present continuous passive) 4. **is spoken** — *is spoken* (present simple passive) 5. **will be announced** — *will be announced* (future passive)
#### B. Conditional transformations **6.** "If you don't study harder, you won't pass the exam." **Key word: UNLESS** → ___ study harder, you won't pass the exam. **7.** "I didn't wake up early, so I missed the bus." **Key word: IF** → If I ___ earlier, I wouldn't have missed the bus. **8.** "She didn't have her umbrella, so she got wet." **Key word: HAD** → If she ___ her umbrella, she wouldn't have got wet. **9.** "You should take an umbrella. It might rain later." **Key word: IN** → Take an umbrella ___ case it rains later. **10.** "Not studying was a mistake." **Key word: SHOULD** → I ___ studied harder.
Ver solução 6. **Unless you** — *Unless you study harder...* (*unless* = *if...not*) 7. **had woken** — *If I had woken earlier...* (mixed conditional: third conditional) 8. **had had** — *If she had had her umbrella...* (third conditional) 9. **in** — *in case it rains* (in case + present simple) 10. **should have** — *I should have studied harder* (modal perfect)
#### C. Reported speech transformations **11.** "I have finished my homework," said Tom. **Key word: FINISHED** → Tom said that he ___ his homework. **12.** "Where did you buy that book?" she asked me. **Key word: WHERE** → She asked me where ___ that book. **13.** "Please don't make so much noise," the teacher said. **Key word: ASKED** → The teacher ___ so much noise. **14.** "I will help you with your project," she said. **Key word: PROMISED** → She ___ me with my project. **15.** "You should see a doctor," he said to her. **Key word: ADVISED** → He ___ to see a doctor.
Ver solução 11. **had finished** — *Tom said that he had finished...* (past perfect en reported speech) 12. **I had bought** — *where I had bought that book* (reported question) 13. **asked us not to make** — *The teacher asked us not to make so much noise* (imperativo negativo) 14. **promised to help** — *She promised to help me...* (promise + infinitivo) 15. **advised her** — *He advised her to see a doctor* (advise + someone + to + infinitivo)
#### D. Mixed transformations **16.** "It's possible that she has already left." **Key word: MAY** → She ___ already left. **17.** "He started learning French two years ago." **Key word: FOR** → He ___ French for two years. **18.** "The movie was so good that everyone enjoyed it." **Key word: SUCH** → It was ___ movie that everyone enjoyed it. **19.** "I find it difficult to understand complex instructions." **Key word: TROUBLE** → I have ___ understanding complex instructions. **20.** "Nobody has ever been to that remote island." **Key word: NEVER** → That remote island ___ .
Ver solução 16. **may have** — *She may have already left* (possibilidad en pasado) 17. **has been learning** — *has been learning French for two years* (present perfect continuous) 18. **such a good** — *It was such a good movie that...* (*such + a/an + adj + noun*) 19. **trouble** — *I have trouble understanding* (have trouble + -ing) 20. **has never been visited** — *That remote island has never been visited* (present perfect passive + never)
--- ### Lección 5 — Writing y Speaking #### Writing **1.** Write an essay (140-190 words): "Some people think that remote work is the future of employment, while others believe that working in an office is more productive. Discuss both views and give your opinion." **2.** Write a review (140-190 words) of a book or film you recently enjoyed. Include: what it was about, why you liked it, and who you would recommend it to. **3.** Write an email (140-190 words) to a local council proposing improvements to public transport in your area. **4.** Write a report (140-190 words) for your manager summarising the results of a customer satisfaction survey. **5.** Write a story (140-190 words) that begins with: "The last time I saw my childhood friend, everything was different." **6.** Rewrite this sentence using the word in brackets: "The government should spend more money on education." (**BELIEVE**) → ___ **7.** Rewrite this sentence using the word in brackets: "She has been working here since 2019." (**STARTED**) → She ___ **8.** Rewrite this sentence using the word in brackets: "It is not necessary for you to bring food." (**HAVE**) → You ___ **9.** Rewrite this sentence using the word in brackets: "They cancelled the match because of the rain." (**DUE**) → The match ___ **10.** Rewrite this sentence using the word in brackets: "I regret not studying harder for the exam." (**WISH**) → I ___
Ver solução **1-5:** Estos son ejercicios de escritura abierta. La respuesta debe seguir las convenciones del formato indicado (essay, review, email, report o story) con un mínimo de 140 palabras y un máximo de 190. **6.** It is believed that the government should spend more money on education. **7.** She started working here in 2019. **8.** You don't have to bring food. **9.** The match was cancelled due to the rain. **10.** I wish I had studied harder for the exam.
#### Speaking **1.** Describe a place you would like to visit in the future. You should say: where it is, how you would get there, what you would do there, and explain why you want to visit it. **2.** Do you prefer working alone or in a team? Why? (Mini discussion: give reasons and examples) **3.** You are arranging to meet a friend. Use these prompts: suggest a day, propose a place, offer an alternative, agree on a time. **4.** Talk about a skill you would like to learn. Why is it useful? How would you learn it? How long do you think it would take? **5.** Express your opinion: "Social media has had a negative effect on communication skills." Do you agree? Justify your answer.
Ver solução **1-5:** Estos son ejercicios de speaking abiertos. Practica hablando en voz alta durante 1-2 minutos por respuesta. Usa vocabulario variado, conectores (*firstly, moreover, in conclusion*) y estructuras gramaticales complejas (condicionales, passive, reported speech). Consejos clave: - Usa conectores: *firstly, furthermore, in addition, however, on the other hand, in conclusion* - Estructuras a incluir: condicionales, passive voice, comparativos, reported speech - Fluidez > perfección: es mejor continuar hablando con un pequeño error que quedarse en silencio
--- ## Pie de página > **Consejo de estudio:** Dedica 15 minutos al día a practicar una sola parte del Use of English. Alterna las partes a lo largo de la semana para no estancarte. Usa un cronómetro para simular las condiciones del examen real. > **Siguiente paso:** [Unidad 59 — Estrategias de Examen: Writing y Speaking](/curso-b2/unit-59) > **Artículos relacionados:** > - [Unidad 57 — Gramática Mixta + Salud](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-57-mixed-grammar-health) > - [Curso B2 completo](/ingles-b2) --- ### Preguntas frecuentes **¿Qué partes tiene el Use of English?** Cuatro partes: Part 1 (multiple-choice cloze), Part 2 (open cloze), Part 3 (word formation), Part 4 (key word transformations). **¿Cuánto tiempo debo dedicar a cada parte?** Parte 1: ~12 min. Parte 2: ~12 min. Parte 3: ~10 min. Parte 4: ~16 min. Practica con cronómetro. **¿Cómo mejoro en word formation?** Aprende los prefijos y sufijos comunes: un-, re-, dis-, -tion, -ment, -ness, -ful, -less, -ive, -able. Lee el contexto antes de transformar. **¿Qué estrategia uso para key word transformations?** Lee la oración original, identifica la estructura gramatical, lee la keyword y construye la cadena completa antes de comparar con la original. **¿Dónde practico la Unidad 58?** En la Unidad 58 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones. --- ### Fuentes y referencias - Cambridge Assessment English. *B2 First — Handbook for Teachers.* Cambridge University Press, 2020. - McCarthy, Michael & O'Dell, Felicity. *English Vocabulary in Use: Upper-Intermediate.* Cambridge University Press, 2017. - Mascull, Betty. *Vocabulary Builder.* Cambridge University Press, 2013. - Foley, Mark & Hall, Diane. *Advanced Grammar in Use.* Cambridge University Press, 2017. - Swann, Alan et al. *Grammar and Vocabulary for First and First Advanced.* Cambridge University Press, 2018.

title: Estrategias y Ejercicios de Writing y Speaking B2
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Unidad 59 B2: estrategias y técnicas para el Writing y Speaking del Cambridge B2 First: essays, reviews, formal letters y presentaciones. Teoría y ejercicios con soluciones.
description: Guía completa de la Unidad 59 del curso B2: estrategias y técnicas para el Writing y Speaking del examen Cambridge B2 First, incluyendo essays, reviews,...

keywords: Estrategias y Ejercicios de Writing y Speaking B2

faqs.question: ¿Qué tipos de Writing hay en el B2 First?
faqs.answer: Part 1: essay obligatorio (140–190 palabras). Part 2: review, formal email/letter o story (140–190 palabras). Cada tipo tiene estructura y registro específicos.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo estructuro un essay B2?
faqs.answer: Introducción (presentar tema + postura), 2–3 párrafos con argumentos y ejemplos, conclusión (resumen + opinión final). Usa linkers de contraste, causa y adición.

faqs.question: ¿Qué evaluan en el Speaking?
faqs.answer: Gramática, vocabulario, pronunciación e interacción. En la Part 2 (individual long turn) debes hablar 1–2 minutos sin interrupción.

faqs.question: ¿Cuántas palabras debo escribir?
faqs.answer: 140–190 palabras. No escribas menos de 140 (penalización) ni más de 190 (pierde tiempo). Practica con cronómetro.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 59?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 59 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones.

content:
La **Unidad 59** prepara para las pruebas de **Writing** y **Speaking** del examen **Cambridge B2 First**. En Writing, debes producir textos de 140–190 palabras con estructura clara, registro adecuado y variedad gramatical. En Speaking, debes demostrar fluidez, precisión léxica y capacidad interactiva. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 59](/curso-b2/unit-59)
> **Antes:** [U58 — Use of English Strategies](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-58-exam-strategies-use-of-english)
> **Siguiente:** [Unidad 60 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-60) --- ![Estrategias de examen B2 para Writing y Speaking](/blog/curso-b2/unit-59/exam-writing-speaking-map.png) *Mapa de estrategias para las partes de Writing y Speaking del B2 First.* --- ## 1. Writing Part 1: Essay El **essay** es obligatorio en la Part 1 del Writing. Recibirás un tema y dos prompts que debes cubrir. El texto debe tener **140–190 palabras**. ### 1.1 Estructura del Essay Un essay B2 sigue una estructura de **5 partes**: | Parte | Función | Palabras aprox. | |-------|---------|----------------| | Introducción | Presentar el tema + postura | 20–30 | | Argumento 1 | Primer argumento + ejemplo | 35–50 | | Argumento 2 | Segundo argumento + ejemplo | 35–50 | | Contraste / Argumento 3 | Contraargumento o tercer punto | 30–40 | | Conclusión | Resumen + opinión final | 20–30 | ### 1.2 Introducción La introducción debe ser breve y clara. Presenta el tema y expresa tu postura en una o dos oraciones. **Modelo:** > *Nowadays, many people believe that university education should be free for everyone. In this essay, I will discuss whether this is a realistic and beneficial idea.* **Phrases útiles para introducir el tema:** | Expresión | Ejemplo | |-----------|---------| | Nowadays, it is commonly believed that... | *Nowadays, it is commonly believed that technology improves education.* | | There is a growing debate about... | *There is a growing debate about climate change policies.* | | One of the most discussed issues today is... | *One of the most discussed issues today is social media addiction.* | ### 1.3 Párrafos del cuerpo Cada párrafos del cuerpo debe contener: 1. Una **idea principal** (topic sentence) 2. Un **argumento** que la desarrolle 3. Un **ejemplo** concreto **Estructura de un párrafos:** > *Firstly, I believe that free university education would reduce social inequality. If students from low-income backgrounds could study without financial pressure, they would have the same opportunities as wealthier students. For example, in countries like Germany, where public universities charge no tuition fees, the number of students from disadvantaged backgrounds has increased significantly.* ### 1.4 Conclusión La conclusión resume tus puntos principales y reafirma tu postura. > *In conclusion, while free university education may seem expensive, I believe it is a worthwhile investment for any society, as it promotes equality and economic growth.* ### 1.5 Linkers esenciales | Tipo | Linkers | Ejemplo | |------|---------|---------| | Adición | moreover, furthermore, in addition | *Moreover, it benefits the economy.* | | Contraste | however, on the other hand, although | *However, some people disagree.* | | Causa | because, since, due to | *Since education is a right, it should be free.* | | Ejemplo | for instance, such as, for example | *For instance, Finland provides free education.* | | Conclusión | in conclusion, to sum up, overall | *In conclusion, the benefits outweigh the costs.* | ### 1.6 Registro formal En un essay debes usar un **registro formal**. Evita: | ❌ Informal | ✅ Formal | |-------------|----------| | a lot of | many / numerous | | kids | children | | get | obtain / acquire | | nice | pleasant / enjoyable | | really | extremely / highly | ### 1.7 Errores comunes en el Essay 1. **No responder a ambos prompts** del examen 2. **Exceder 190 palabras** (pierde tiempo) 3. **Usar registro informal** (contracciones, slang) 4. **No usar linkers** variados 5. **Repetir la misma idea** en distintos párrafos 6. **No tener conclusión clara** --- ## 2. Writing Part 2: Review El **review** evalúa tu opinión sobre un producto, servicio, lugar o experiencia. Es la opción más común de la Part 2. ### 2.1 Estructura del Review | Parte | Función | Palabras aprox. | |-------|---------|----------------| | Título | Atraer al lector | 3–6 palabras | | Introducción | Presentar lo reseñado | 20–30 | | Párrafos de opinión | Ventajas / desventajas | 50–70 | | Recomendación final | Conclusión + recomendación | 20–30 | ### 2.2 Modelo de Review > **A Hidden Gem in Barcelona** > > Last summer, I visited a small café called *La Terraza* in the heart of Barcelona. It turned out to be one of the best dining experiences I have ever had. > > The first thing that impressed me was the atmosphere. The décor was modern yet cosy, and the staff were incredibly friendly. The menu offered a wide variety of dishes, from traditional Spanish tapas to innovative fusion cuisine. I particularly enjoyed the grilled octopus, which was perfectly cooked. > > On the downside, the prices were slightly above average, and the café can get very crowded during weekends. However, I think the quality of the food and service makes up for it. > > All in all, I would highly recommend *La Terraza* to anyone visiting Barcelona. It is an ideal spot for a relaxed lunch or a special dinner with friends. ### 2.3 Useful Expressions para Reviews | Función | Expresiones | |---------|-------------| | Opinión personal | I think / I believe / In my opinion / Personally | | Fortalezas | The best thing about... / What I liked most was... / One advantage is... | | Debilidades | On the downside / The only drawback was... / Unfortunately... | | Recomendación | I would definitely recommend... / It is worth visiting... / I suggest... | | Experiencia | I had the opportunity to... / I was lucky enough to... | --- ## 3. Writing Part 2: Formal Email / Letter El **formal email/letter** se escribe a una persona o institución. Debe mantener un tono respetuoso y estructura clara. ### 3.1 Estructura | Parte | Función | |-------|---------| | Saludo | Dear Sir/Madam / Dear Mr + apellido | | Introducción | Expresar el motivo de la carta | | Cuerpo | Detallar la solicitud, queja o petición | | Cierre | Expresar esperanza de respuesta | | Despedida | Yours faithfully (sin nombre) / Yours sincerely (con nombre) | ### 3.2 Modelo de Formal Letter > Dear Sir or Madam, > > I am writing to enquire about the English language course advertised on your website. I would be grateful if you could provide me with some further information. > > Firstly, I would like to know the exact dates of the summer course and whether accommodation is included in the price. Additionally, could you tell me if there are any discounts available for students who book early? > > I am particularly interested in improving my writing skills, so I would also appreciate it if you could confirm whether the course focuses on academic or creative writing. > > I look forward to hearing from you at your earliest convenience. > > Yours faithfully, > María López ### 3.3 Useful Phrases para Formal Letters | Función | Expresión | |---------|-----------| | Petición | I would be grateful if you could... / I would like to enquire about... / Could you please...? | | Queja | I am writing to complain about... / I am disappointed with... / I wish to express my dissatisfaction... | | Sugerencia | I would suggest that... / It might be advisable to... / Perhaps you could consider... | | Agradecimiento | Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. / I appreciate your help. | --- ## 4. Speaking Part 1: Interview La Part 1 dura **3–4 minutos**. El examinador te hará preguntas personales sobre ti, tu vida y tus experiencias. ### 4.1 Tipos de Preguntas | Tema | Ejemplos de preguntas | |------|----------------------| | Trabajo / Estudios | What do you do for a living? / What are you studying at the moment? | | Hobbies | What do you enjoy doing in your free time? / Have you got any hobbies? | | Futuro | What are your plans for the future? / Where do you see yourself in five years? | | Experiencias | Have you ever travelled abroad? / What was the best holiday you've ever had? | ### 4.2 Model Answers **Pregunta:** *What do you enjoy doing in your free time?* > *Well, I'm really into photography, actually. I enjoy taking pictures of nature and landscapes, especially during weekends when I go hiking. It helps me relax and be creative at the same time.* **Pregunta:** *What are your plans for the future?* > *In the near future, I'm planning to improve my English so that I can apply for a job in an international company. I'd also like to travel more, perhaps visit some English-speaking countries to practise the language in real-life situations.* **Consejos para la Part 1:** - No responda con monosílabos; amplía la respuesta - Usa tiempos variados (presente, pasado, futuro) - Añade detalles personales --- ## 5. Speaking Part 2: Individual Long Turn La Part 2 es un monólogo de **1–2 minutos**. Recibirás dos fotos o imágenes y deberás compararlas, describirlas o especular. ### 5.1 Estructura del Long Turn | Paso | Función | Tiempo | |------|---------|--------| | 1. Describir | Describir las imágenes | 30 seg | | 2. Comparar | Señalar similitudes y diferencias | 30 seg | | 3. Especular / Recomendar | Dar tu opinión o recomendar | 30 seg | ### 5.2 Modelo de Long Turn **Tema:** *These are two photos of people doing different sports outdoors.* > *In the first photo, I can see a group of young people playing football in a park. They seem to be enjoying themselves, and the weather looks warm and sunny. In the second picture, there is a woman swimming in a lake surrounded by mountains. It looks like a very peaceful and natural setting.* > > *Both activities take place outdoors, but they are quite different. While football is a team sport and requires a lot of energy, swimming is an individual activity and can be very relaxing. The environments are also different: the first is in an urban park, whereas the second is in a remote natural area.* > > *I personally prefer swimming in natural settings because it helps me disconnect from daily stress. However, I think both activities are great for staying healthy and enjoying nature.* ### 5.3 Useful Phrases para Part 2 | Función | Expresiones | |---------|-------------| | Describir | In the first picture, I can see... / What strikes me about this image is... | | Comparar | Both photos show... / While the first image..., the second one... / On the one hand... on the other hand... | | Especular | It looks like... / I imagine that... / Perhaps... / They might be... | | Recomendar | I would recommend... / I think this activity is ideal for... | --- ## 6. Speaking Part 3 & 4: Collaborative Task and Discussion ### 6.1 Part 3: Collaborative Task (4 minutos) Recibirás un prompt con información y deberás **interactuar con tu compañero** durante 3 minutos, seguidos de una pregunta al final. **Estrategias:** - **Inicia** la conversación con confianza - **Escucha** activamente a tu compañero - **Añade ideas** y reacciona a las de tu compañero - Usa phrases como: *That's a good point. / I see what you mean, but... / I agree, and I'd also add that...* ### 6.2 Part 4: Discussion (4 minutos) El examinador hará preguntas más generales relacionadas con el tema. Debes **opinar con razones**. **Modelo de pregunta:** *Do you think it is important for young people to learn a foreign language?* > *Absolutely. I think it's essential nowadays because we live in a globalised world. Speaking another language opens doors to new cultures, job opportunities, and even different ways of thinking. Besides, studies have shown that learning languages improves cognitive abilities and memory.* ### 6.3 Useful Phrases para Parts 3 & 4 | Función | Expresiones | |---------|-------------| | Opinar | In my opinion... / From my point of view... / I believe that... | | Añadir | What's more... / On top of that... / Another thing worth mentioning is... | | Disagree cortésmente | I see your point, but... / I'm not entirely sure about that. / That may be true, however... | | Dar ejemplos | For example... / To give you an example... / Take... as an example. | | Concluir | So basically... / All things considered... / To sum up what we've discussed... | --- ## 7. Useful Phrases: Writing and Speaking ### 7.1 Writing — Linkers y Connectores | Tipo | Expresiones | |------|-------------| | Adición | moreover, furthermore, in addition, besides, what is more | | Contraste | however, nevertheless, on the other hand, although, despite | | Causa-efecto | due to, as a result of, consequently, therefore, thus | | Ejemplo | for instance, for example, such as, to illustrate, namely | | Conclusión | in conclusion, to sum up, overall, all in all, taking everything into account | ### 7.2 Speaking — Interaction Phrases | Función | Expresiones | |---------|-------------| | Opinar | I think... / In my view... / Personally, I feel that... | | Preguntar | What do you think about...? / How do you feel about...? / Don't you think...? | | Estar de acuerdo | I completely agree. / That's exactly what I think. / You're absolutely right. | | Disagree | I'm not so sure about that. / I see your point, but I tend to think... | | Resumir | So, to summarise... / Basically, we both agree that... | --- ## 8. Modelo de Essay Completo **Tema:** *Some people believe that children should learn to cook at school. Others think it is better to learn at home. Discuss both views and give your opinion.* > Nowadays, there is an ongoing debate about whether cooking should be taught in schools or at home. In this essay, I will examine both perspectives and give my own opinion. > > On the one hand, supporters of cooking classes in schools argue that it is a valuable life skill. If children learn to prepare healthy meals at school, they will be better equipped to look after themselves as adults. For example, in Japan, home economics is a compulsory subject, and as a result, Japanese teenagers are generally more independent in the kitchen. > > On the other hand, many people believe that cooking is best learned within the family. Parents can pass down traditional recipes and spending time cooking together strengthens family bonds. Furthermore, not all schools have the budget or facilities to offer proper cooking lessons. > > In my opinion, although learning at home has clear advantages, schools should still offer basic cooking classes. This way, every child, regardless of their family background, would have the opportunity to acquire this essential skill. > > *(162 words)* --- ## 9. Errores Comunes en Writing y Speaking | # | Error | Corrección | |---|-------|------------| | 1 | *I have 25 years.* | *I am 25 years old.* | | 2 | *The reason is because...* | *The reason is that...* | | 3 | *Despite of the cost...* | *Despite the cost... / In spite of the cost...* | | 4 | *I would like to know that...* | *I would like to know whether...* | | 5 | *He suggested me to go.* | *He suggested that I should go.* | | 6 | *The informations are...* | *The information is...* (uncountable) | | 7 | *I am agree with you.* | *I agree with you.* | | 8 | *In my opinion, I think...* | Use one or the other, not both. | --- ## 10. --- **Exercise 53.** Reescribe estas frases para que suenen más colaborativas y naturales. a) *I think this is the best option.* b) *No, that's wrong.* c) *We should do this.*
Ver solução a) *From my perspective, this seems like the strongest option. Do you agree?* b) *I see your point, however, I'm not entirely sure about that. Perhaps we could consider another approach?* c) *I would suggest that we go with this option, as it covers the main requirements. How does that sound to you?*
--- **Exercise 54.** Practica esta interacción: el examinador dice *"You now have a minute to discuss together."* Escribe 4–6 turnos de conversación con tu compañero sobre el tema: *The best way to spend a weekend*.
Ver solução **Posible diálogo:** **A:** So, the topic is how to spend a weekend. I personally enjoy outdoor activities. What about you? **B:** I agree, outdoor activities are great. However, I also think it's important to have some time to relax at home. Perhaps we could combine both? **A:** That sounds like a good idea. For instance, going for a walk in the morning and then spending the afternoon reading or watching a film. **B:** Exactly. And I'd also add that spending time with friends or family makes the weekend more enjoyable. **A:** Definitely. So, I'd say the best weekend includes a balance of physical activity, relaxation, and social time. **B:** I completely agree. That covers everything we've discussed.
--- **Exercise 55.** Identifica los errores de interacción en este diálogo. > **A:** I think going to the cinema is the best option. > **B:** I disagree. That's boring. > **A:** No, it isn't. You're wrong. > **B:** I don't care. Let's just pick something.
Ver solução **Problemas:** - **B** rechaza la idea de forma brusca (*That's boring*), sin justificar ni proponer alternativa - **A** responde de forma defensiva (*You're wrong*), sin Argumentar - **B** muestra desinterés (*I don't care*) — esto es muy negativo en el examen - No hay colaboración ni construcción de ideas **Versión mejorada:** > **A:** I think going to the cinema could be a good option, especially if there's a new film out. What do you think? > > **B:** I see your point, but perhaps we could consider something more active, like going for a hike. It would be more refreshing. > > **A:** That's a valid suggestion. However, the weather forecast isn't great for this weekend. Maybe the cinema would be a safer bet? > > **B:** You're right about the weather. In that case, the cinema sounds like a good choice. We could also grab lunch afterwards.
--- #### Sección B: Discussion Strategies **Exercise 56.** Responde a esta pregunta de Part 4 con una opinión y un ejemplo: *Do you think technology has improved the quality of education?*
Ver solução **Posible respuesta:** *In my opinion, technology has significantly improved education in many ways. For example, students now have access to online courses and educational platforms that allow them to learn at their own pace. Moreover, teachers can use interactive tools such as presentations and videos to make lessons more engaging. However, I think it's important to use technology wisely, as excessive screen time can be counterproductive. Overall, I believe the benefits outweigh the drawbacks.*
--- **Exercise 57.** Expande esta respuesta breve a una más completa: **Pregunta:** *Is it important for people to learn about other cultures?* **Respuesta corta:** *Yes, I think so. It helps people understand each other.*
Ver solução **Versión expandida:** *Absolutely. I think learning about other cultures is extremely important in today's interconnected world. It helps people develop empathy and understanding, and it reduces the risk of prejudice and stereotypes. For instance, when I travelled to Japan, I learned about their customs and traditions, which gave me a completely new perspective on politeness and respect. Furthermore, understanding different cultures is essential in the workplace, as companies increasingly operate on a global scale.*
--- **Exercise 58.** Completa con la frase adecuada para cada situación. a) Cuando estás de acuerdo pero quieres añadir algo: *I completely agree, ______* b) Cuando discrepas cortésmente: *I see your point, ______* c) Cuando quieres dar un ejemplo: *To illustrate, ______* d) Cuando quieres concluir: *So, to sum up, ______*
Ver solução a) *and I'd also add that...* b) *but I'm not entirely sure about that. / however, I tend to think that...* c) *take..., for example. / for instance,...* d) *what we've discussed is that...*
--- **Exercise 59.** Practica esta respuesta de Part 4: *Do you think it is better to learn a language in a classroom or by living abroad?*
Ver solução **Modelo:** *That's an interesting question. I believe that both approaches have their merits, but living abroad offers a more immersive experience. When you're in a country where the language is spoken, you're constantly exposed to authentic conversations, slang, and cultural nuances that you simply cannot replicate in a classroom. For example, a friend of mine spent a year in London and improved her English dramatically, not just academically but also in terms of confidence and fluency. That said, a structured classroom environment provides a solid grammatical foundation, which is also essential. Ideally, I would recommend combining both methods for the best results.*
--- **Exercise 60.** Corrige esta respuesta para que suene más natural y completa: *I think languages are important. Because you can talk to people. In my country many people speak English. So it's good. I think everyone should learn.*
Ver solução **Versión mejorada:** *I believe that learning foreign languages is extremely important in today's globalised world. Being able to communicate in another language opens doors to new cultures, friendships, and career opportunities. For instance, in my country, English is widely spoken in the business sector, so those who are fluent in it tend to have a significant advantage in the job market. Furthermore, learning a language improves cognitive skills such as memory and problem-solving. For these reasons, I think everyone should make an effort to learn at least one foreign language.*
--- #### Sección C: Useful Phrases Practice **Exercise 61.** Clasifica estas expresiones según la función. * expressions: a) On the one hand... on the other hand... b) In my view... c) To give you an example... d) That's a great point. I'd also mention... e) I'm not so sure about that. f) From my perspective... g) To summarise... h) That may be true; however,... i) Take..., as an example. j) What's more,...
Ver solução **Opinar:** b) In my view... / f) From my perspective... **Añadir:** d) That's a great point. I'd also mention... / j) What's more... **Ejemplos:** c) To give you an example... / i) Take..., as an example. **Contraste/Discrepar:** a) On the one hand... on the other hand... / e) I'm not so sure about that. / h) That may be true; however,... **Concluir:** g) To summarise...
--- **Exercise 62.** Completa con la expresión adecuada. a) ______, I believe that education is the key to social progress. b) I see your point, ______ I think there are other factors to consider. c) ______, many students struggle with exam stress, ______ regular exercise can help reduce anxiety.
Ver solução a) **In my opinion / Personally / From my perspective** b) **but / however / nevertheless** c) **For example / For instance / To illustrate** ... **and / moreover**
--- **Exercise 63.** Reemplaza la expression subrayada por una synonym. a) *I think* that climate change is the biggest challenge we face. b) *For example*, renewable energy sources are becoming more affordable. c) *In conclusion*, I believe we should invest more in public transport.
Ver solução a) *In my opinion / From my perspective / I believe* b) *To illustrate / To give you an example / Take solar panels, as an example* c) *To sum up / All in all / Overall*
--- **Exercise 64.** Escribe un párrafos corto (5–6 oraciones) usando al menos 4 expressions diferentes de las que has practicado.
Ver solução **Posible respuesta:** *In my opinion, public transport is essential for modern cities. For example, cities like Tokyo and London have invested heavily in their metro systems, which has significantly reduced traffic congestion. What's more, public transport is much more environmentally friendly than private cars. I'm not so sure about the argument that buses are always slower — in many cases, they are actually more efficient during rush hour. To sum up, investing in public transport is a wise decision for any city.*
--- **Exercise 65.** Marca con ✓ las expressions que son appropriate para el Speaking Part 4 (Discussion) y con ✗ las que son demasiado informales. 1. ______ I reckon... 2. ______ From my perspective... 3. ______ Yeah, totally... 4. ______ I would argue that... 5. ______ It's like, so important...
Ver solução 1. ✗ (*reckon* es demasiado informal para el examen) 2. ✓ 3. ✗ (demasiado informal) 4. ✓ 5. ✗ (demasiado informal)
--- ### Lección 5 — Combined Practice #### Writing Tasks **Exercise 66.** Escribe una review (140–190 palabras) sobre un restaurante que hayas visitado. Incluye título, introducción, opiniones y recomendación.
Ver solução **Modelo (158 palabras):** **A Memorable Dining Experience** *Last month, I had the pleasure of dining at a seafood restaurant called *Ocean Breeze* in the coastal town of San Sebastián. From the moment I walked in, I was impressed by the elegant yet welcoming atmosphere.* *The menu offered a superb selection of fresh seafood dishes. I opted for the grilled salmon with vegetables, which was cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The staff were attentive without being intrusive, and the wine list was equally impressive.* *On the downside, the restaurant was slightly more expensive than I had anticipated, and booking a table on weekends proved quite difficult. However, given the outstanding quality of the food and service, I consider it excellent value for money.* *I would highly recommend *Ocean Breeze* to anyone who enjoys fine dining in a relaxed setting. It is particularly ideal for special occasions.*
--- **Exercise 67.** Escribe un formal letter (140–190 palabras) al ayuntamiento de tu ciudad, sugiriendo mejoras en un parque público.
Ver solução **Modelo (162 palabras):** > Dear Sir or Madam, > > I am writing to propose some improvements to Riverside Park, which is located in the centre of our city. While the park is a valuable green space, I believe several changes could enhance the experience for all visitors. > > Firstly, I would suggest that additional bins be installed throughout the park, as litter is a recurring problem, particularly near the playground area. Furthermore, the walking paths are in need of repair, as several sections have become uneven and potentially hazardous. > > I would also recommend the installation of more benches and shaded areas, which would make the park more accessible and comfortable for elderly visitors and families with young children. > > Finally, it might be advisable to organise regular community clean-up events, which could foster a sense of responsibility among local residents. > > I hope you will consider these suggestions and look forward to your response. > > Yours faithfully, > Elena Ruiz
--- **Exercise 68.** Corrige los errores en esteessay. > *The education is very important. In my opinion, I think that everyone must to go to university. For example, many peoples dont have access to higher education and that is very bad. However, some people say that university is waste of money. I disagree with this because a degree can helps you get a better job.*
Ver solução **Corrección:** > *Education is very important. In my opinion, everyone should have the opportunity to attend university. For example, many people do not have access to higher education, which is a significant disadvantage. However, some people argue that university is a waste of money. I disagree with this view, as a degree can help individuals secure better employment opportunities and develop critical thinking skills.* **Errores corregidos:** *The education* → Education; *must to go* → should attend; *many peoples dont* → many people do not; *very bad* → a significant disadvantage; *university is waste* → university is a waste; *can helps* → can help
--- **Exercise 69.** Completa esta introducción de review con los prompts correctos. > *Last weekend, I ______ (1) ______ a new escape room in the city centre with a group of friends. ______ (2) ______, I must say it was one of the most ______ (3) ______ experiences I've had in a long time.* a) visited b) Overall c) enjoyable
Ver solução 1. **a)** visited 2. **b)** Overall 3. **c)** enjoyable
--- **Exercise 70.** Escribe unessay (140–190 palabras) sobre: *Some people believe that reading is the best way to learn a language. Others prefer watching films or listening to music. Which do you prefer?*
Ver solução **Modelo (167 palabras):** *There are various approaches to learning a language, and people often debate whether reading or consuming media such as films and music is more effective. In my opinion, while both methods have their advantages, I believe watching films is the more engaging and practical approach.* *On the one hand, reading is undeniably beneficial for building vocabulary and improving grammar. For instance, reading novels exposes learners to a wide range of sentence structures and idiomatic expressions. However, reading alone does not develop listening comprehension or pronunciation.* *On the other hand, watching films allows learners to hear the language spoken naturally, with different accents and speeds. This is particularly valuable for developing listening skills and understanding everyday expressions. For example, after watching several English films with subtitles, many learners report a significant improvement in their comprehension.* *In conclusion, although reading has clear benefits, I would recommend watching films as a more well-rounded approach to language learning, as it develops multiple skills simultaneously.*
--- #### Speaking Simulation Tasks **Exercise 71.** Simulación de Speaking Part 1: Responde por escrito a estas 5 preguntas con respuestas amplias (3–4 oraciones cada una). 1. What do you do for a living? 2. Do you enjoy your job/studies? Why or why not? 3. What do you usually do at weekends? 4. Have you got any hobbies? 5. What are your plans for the future?
Ver solução **Posibles respuestas:** 1. *I'm currently working as a marketing assistant for a technology company. My main responsibilities include creating social media content and analysing campaign performance. I find it quite stimulating, as it combines creativity with data analysis.* 2. *Yes, I do. I particularly enjoy the creative aspect of my job, such as designing campaigns and brainstorming new ideas. However, I sometimes find the deadlines quite stressful, especially during product launches.* 3. *At weekends, I usually like to unwind after a busy week. On Saturdays, I often go for a run in the park and then meet friends for lunch. Sundays are more relaxed — I tend to stay at home, read, and prepare for the week ahead.* 4. *Yes, I'm quite into photography. I enjoy capturing landscapes and street scenes during my travels. I also play the piano, which I find very therapeutic, especially after a long day at work.* 5. *In the near future, I'm planning to take the Cambridge C1 exam to further improve my English. Long-term, I would like to work in an international environment, perhaps in a multinational company where I can use my language skills daily.*
--- **Exercise 72.** Simulación de Speaking Part 2: Escribe una descripción completa (aproximadamente 1–2 minutos de habla) para estas imágenes: *Photo 1: A group of friends having a picnic in a park on a sunny day.* *Photo 2: A family having a barbecue in their garden.*
Ver solução **Modelo:** *In the first photo, I can see a group of friends enjoying a picnic in a park. They are sitting on a blanket on the grass, and the weather looks warm and sunny. There are sandwiches, fruit, and drinks spread out in front of them, and they all seem to be having a great time laughing and chatting.* *In the second picture, there is a family having a barbecue in their garden. The father appears to be cooking on the grill while the children are playing nearby. The garden is well-maintained with flowers and a wooden fence, creating a very cosy and private atmosphere.* *Both images show people enjoying food and company outdoors, but they differ in the setting and the group. While the first is in a public park with friends, the second takes place in a private garden with family members. I imagine the barbecue is a weekend tradition for this family, whereas the picnic looks like a spontaneous get-together.* *I personally enjoy both types of gatherings, but I think there's something special about a family barbecue — it feels more intimate and personal.*
--- **Exercise 73.** Simulación de Speaking Part 3: Discute con tu compañero (por escrito, 4–6 turnos) el siguiente tema: *"What are the most important qualities of a good teacher?"*
Ver solução **Posible diálogo:** **A:** Well, looking at the options, I think the most important quality of a good teacher is patience. What do you think? **B:** I agree that patience is essential, especially when explaining difficult concepts. However, I would also highlight the ability to motivate students, as even the best material can fall flat without an inspiring teacher. **A:** That's a great point. I'd also add that a good teacher should be adaptable — different students learn in different ways, and a teacher who can adjust their approach will be more effective. **B:** Absolutely. And communication skills are crucial too. A teacher who explains things clearly and encourages questions creates a much better learning environment. **A:** I completely agree. So, to summarise, we've identified patience, motivation, adaptability, and communication as the key qualities. **B:** Yes, and I'd also mention subject knowledge — a teacher needs to be confident in what they're teaching.
--- **Exercise 74.** Simulación de Speaking Part 4: Responde a esta pregunta con opinión, razonamiento y ejemplo. *Do you think young people today spend too much time on their phones?*
Ver solução **Posible respuesta:** *That's an interesting question. I do think that many young people tend to spend an excessive amount of time on their phones, which can have negative consequences. For instance, studies have shown that heavy phone use is linked to increased levels of anxiety and difficulty concentrating. However, I also believe that phones can be valuable tools when used responsibly — for learning, staying in touch with family, or accessing educational content. The key, in my view, is finding a healthy balance. Parents and schools should teach young people to manage their screen time effectively rather than banning phones altogether.*
--- **Exercise 75.** Escribe unessay completo (140–190 palabras) como examen final sobre el siguiente tema: *In many countries, people are living longer. What are the causes of this trend and what problems might it create?*
Ver solução **Modelo (174 palabras):** *Over the past few decades, life expectancy has increased significantly in many parts of the world. In this essay, I will discuss the main causes of this trend and the potential problems it may create.* *There are several reasons why people are living longer. Firstly, advances in medicine and healthcare have made it possible to treat diseases that were once considered fatal. For instance, improvements in cancer treatment have dramatically increased survival rates. Secondly, better nutrition and awareness of healthy lifestyles have contributed to improved overall health.* *However, this trend also presents certain challenges. One major issue is the strain on pension systems, as governments must support a growing number of retirees for longer periods. Additionally, an ageing population means increased demand for healthcare services, which can place considerable pressure on public resources.* *In conclusion, while longer life expectancy is a positive development, it is essential that governments and societies plan ahead to address the economic and social challenges that accompany it.*
--- ## Consejo de la Unidad > **Practica con cronómetro.** Tanto en Writing como en Speaking, el tiempo es limitado. En Writing, intenta completar tu texto en 40 minutos para tener 5 minutos de revisión. En Speaking, practica tus respuestas con un cronómetro para asegurarte de que hablas durante el tiempo indicado (1–2 minutos en Part 2). La práctica constante con límites de tiempo te ayudará a gestionar el estrés del examen y a mejorar tu fluidez. --- ## Siguiente paso Una vez que domines las estrategias de Writing y Speaking, estás listo para el repaso final. Avanza a la [Unidad 60 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-60) o sigue practicando con los ejercicios de esta unidad. **Artículos relacionados:** - [U58 — Use of English Strategies](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-58-exam-strategies-use-of-english) - [Unidad 60 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-60) - [Curso B2 completo](/ingles-b2) --- ## Preguntas Frecuentes (FAQs) **¿Qué tipos de Writing hay en el B2 First?** Part 1: essay obligatorio (140–190 palabras). Part 2: review, formal email/letter o story (140–190 palabras). Cada tipo tiene estructura y registro específicos. **¿Cómo estructuro un essay B2?** Introducción (presentar tema + postura), 2–3 párrafos con argumentos y ejemplos, conclusión (resumen + opinión final). Usa linkers de contraste, causa y adición. **¿Qué evaluan en el Speaking?** Gramática, vocabulario, pronunciación e interacción. En la Part 2 (individual long turn) debes hablar 1–2 minutos sin interrupción. **¿Cuántas palabras debo escribir?** 140–190 palabras. No escribas menos de 140 (penalización) ni más de 190 (pierde tiempo). Practica con cronómetro. **¿Dónde practico la Unidad 59?** En la Unidad 59 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría y ejercicios con soluciones. Continúa con el repaso final del curso en [U60 — Repaso Final B2](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-60-final-b2-review). --- ## Fuentes - Cambridge Assessment English. (2024). *B2 First — Handbook for Teachers*. University of Cambridge. - English Profile. (2023). *The CEFR and the B2 Level*. Cambridge University Press. - Prodromou, L. (2022). *From Teacher to Trainer: A Practical Course in ELT*. Delta Publishing. - Hughes, J. (2023). *Cambridge B2 First Masterclass*. Oxford University Press.

faqs.question: ¿Qué cubre el repaso final del curso B2?
faqs.answer: Todas las estructuras gramaticales B2: conditionals, passive voice, passive reporting, reported speech, modals, phrasal verbs, linkers, collocations, inversion, cleft sentences, wish/regret, word formation y exam strategies.

faqs.answer: Haz el simulacro de examen primero para identificar debilidades. Después repasa las estructuras donde fallaste y vuelve a intentarlo.

faqs.question: ¿Cuánto tiempo dura el simulacro?
faqs.answer: 60 minutos para Use of English y Reading. 30 minutos para Writing. Practica con cronómetro para simular condiciones reales.

faqs.question: ¿Qué estructuras son más importantes para el examen?
faqs.answer: Passive voice, modals of deduction, conditionals, reported speech, key word transformations y word formation son las más evaluadas.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 60?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 60 del curso B2 y en esta misma guía, que incluye teoría, simulacro de examen y ejercicios con soluciones.

content:
import Callout from '@/components/Callout.astro'; import DetailToggle from '@/components/DetailToggle.astro'; import QuickGame from '@/components/QuickGame.astro'; import Tip from '@/components/Tip.astro'; La **Unidad 60** es el repaso final del curso **B2 de Inglés**. Consolida todas las estructuras gramaticales y el vocabulario trabajados en las 59 unidades anteriores, preparándote para el examen **Cambridge B2 First**. Incluye un simulacro de examen que integra Use of English, Reading, Writing y Speaking. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 60](/curso-b2/unit-60)
> **Antes:** [U59 — Exam Strategies Writing & Speaking](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-59-exam-strategies-writing-speaking)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés B2](/blog/metodos/ingles-b2) --- ## Mapa de decisiones: grammar families overview Antes de entrar en detalles, este es el mapa mental que debes dominar. Cada familia gramatical responde a una función comunicativa distinta: | Familia gramatical | Función principal | Ejemplo rápido | |---|---|---| | Conditionals | Hipótesis, consecuencias | *If I **had studied**, I **would have passed**.* | | Passive voice | Enfocar la acción, no el agente | *The report **was written** by the team.* | | Passive reporting | Informar sin comprometer al hablante | *It **is said** that he is guilty.* | | Reported speech | Transmitir lo que otro dijo | *She **said** she **had finished**.* | | Modals | Obligación, deducción, consejo | *You **must** see this film.* | | Phrasal verbs | Verbos compuestos de significado idiomático | *I **came across** an old photo.* | | Linkers | Conectar ideas con precisión | *Despite being tired, she kept working.* | | Inversion | Énfasis, formalidad | *Never **have** I **seen** such beauty.* | | Cleft sentences | Destacar un elemento de la oración | *It was John **who** broke the window.* | | Wish / Regret | Deseos, arrepentimiento | *I wish I **had known** earlier.* | | Collocations | Combinaciones naturales de palabras | *make a decision*, no *do a decision* | | Word formation | Derivación de palabras | *decide → decision → decisive → decisively* | --- ## 1. Conditionals: completo repaso ### Tabla de conditionals | Tipo | Estructura | Ejemplo | Uso | |---|---|---|---| | **Zero** | If + present, present | *If you heat water to 100°C, it boils.* | Hechos científicos, verdades generales | | **First** | If + present, will + base | *If it rains, we'll cancel the picnic.* | Situaciones reales, probabilidades futuras | | **Second** | If + past, would + base | *If I won the lottery, I'd travel the world.* | Hipótesis irreales, situaciones improbables | | **Third** | If + past perfect, would have + pp | *If she had studied, she would have passed.* | Arrepentimiento, consecuencias pasadas irreal | | **Mixed** | Combina tiempos | *If I had taken that job, I would be living in London now.* | Mezcla de pasado y presente | ### Conditionals con otros modales - *If you **should** see Paul, tell him to call me.* (First conditional formal) - *If I **were** you, I **would** apologise.* (Consejo) - *If you **had** listened to me, you **wouldn't be** in this mess.* (Mixed) --- ## 2. Passive voice: todos los tiempos | Tiempo | Activa | Pasiva | |---|---|---| | **Present Simple** | They make cars in Germany. | Cars **are made** in Germany. | | **Present Continuous** | She is writing the report. | The report **is being written**. | | **Past Simple** | Shakespeare wrote Hamlet. | Hamlet **was written** by Shakespeare. | | **Past Continuous** | They were repairing the road. | The road **was being repaired**. | | **Present Perfect** | They have arrested the suspect. | The suspect **has been arrested**. | | **Past Perfect** | Someone had stolen my bike. | My bike **had been stolen**. | | **Future Simple** | They will announce the results. | The results **will be announced**. | | **Future Perfect** | They will have finished by June. | It **will have been finished** by June. | | **Modals** | You must submit the form. | The form **must be submitted**. | ### Passive con dos complementos - *They gave **me** a present.* → *I was given a present.* (más natural) / *A present was given to me.* - *She told **him** the truth.* → *He was told the truth.* --- ## 3. Passive reporting y reported speech ### Passive reporting (formal) | Estructura | Ejemplo | |---|---| | It is said/believed/thought + that | *It is believed that the earth is warming.* | | It is said/believed/thought + to + infinitive | *He is believed to be the richest man in town.* | | S + is/was + said/believed + to + infinitive | *She is said to have left the country.* | ### Reported speech (común) | Directo | Reported | |---|---| | "I **am** tired," she said. | She said she **was** tired. | | "I **have finished**," he said. | He said he **had finished**. | | "I **will call** you," she said. | She said she **would call** me. | | "I **can** help," he said. | He said he **could** help. | | "Do you **like** pizza?" she asked. | She asked if I **liked** pizza. | **Cambio de pronombres y tiempos:** backshift automático. Said → told si hay objeto directo: *She **told me** she was tired.* --- ## 4. Modals: obligation, deduction, advice ### Tabla de modals | Modal | Obligación | Deducción | Consejo | |---|---|---|---| | **must** | Tengo que estudiar. | Must be true. | — | | **have to** | Tengo que ir al médico. | — | — | | **mustn't** | No puedes tocar esto. | — | — | | **should** | Deberías hacer ejercicio. | — | You should see a doctor. | | **ought to** | Deberías ser más paciente. | — | You ought to apologise. | | **might / may** | — | He might be at home. | — | | **could** | — | That could be true. | You could try yoga. | | **would** | — | — | I would start early. | | **needn't** | No tienes que preocuparte. | — | — | | **didn't need to** | No necesitó ir (pero fue). | — | — | ### Deducción con tiempos - *He **must be** at home.* (presente — deducción lógica) - *He **must have been** at home.* (pasado — deducción lógica sobre el pasado) - *She **might be** late.* (posibilidad presente) - *She **might have missed** the bus.* (posibilidad pasada) --- ## 5. Phrasal verbs: los 30 más importantes en B2 | Phrasal verb | Significado | Ejemplo | |---|---|---| | **come across** | encontrar por casualidad | *I **came across** an old friend yesterday.* | | **come up with** | idear, proponer | *She **came up with** a brilliant idea.* | | **get over** | superar | *It took me weeks to **get over** the flu.* | | **give up** | abandonar | *Don't **give up**
