Linkers: contrast, reason, addition, purpose ### Tabla de linkers | Función | Linkers formales | Linkers informales | |---|---|---| | **Contraste** | however, nevertheless, although, despite, whereas | but, though, even though | | **Razón** | because, since, as, due to, owing to | 'cause | | **Adición** | furthermore, moreover, in addition, what's more | also, and, besides | | **Propósito** | in order to, so as to, with the aim of | to, so that | | **Resultado** | therefore, consequently, as a result, thus | so | | **Concesión** | although, even though, despite, in spite of | even if | | **Comparación** | similarly, likewise, in the same way | just like, just as | | **Ejemplo** | for example, for instance, such as, namely | like | ### Errores comunes con linkers - ~~Despite~~ **he was tired**, he kept working. → **Despite being tired**, he kept working. / **Although he was tired**, he kept working. - **Due to** ~~that~~ the rain, the match was cancelled. - She is not only intelligent **but also** hardworking. (correlativo) --- ## 7. Inversion, cleft sentences, wish / regret ### Inversion Se invierte el orden auxiliar-sujeto después de adverbios negativos o restrictivos: | Expresión | Ejemplo con inversión | |---|---| | Never | Never **have** I **seen** such a mess. | | Rarely / Seldom | Rarely **does** he **arrive** on time. | | Not only... but also | Not only **did** she **win**, but she also broke the record. | | Hardly / Scarcely... when | Hardly **had** I **sat down** when the phone rang. | | No sooner... than | No sooner **had** they **left** than it started raining. | | Under no circumstances | Under no circumstances **should** you **open** that door. | | Only then | Only then **did** he **realise** his mistake. | | So + adjective + be | So beautiful **was** the sunset **that** we stopped to watch. | ### Cleft sentences Para enfatizar un elemento de la oración: | Tipo | Ejemplo | |---|---| | **It is/was + énfasis + who/that** | *It was John **who** broke the window.* | | **What + sujeto + verb + es** | *What I need **is** a holiday.* | | **The thing/person + that** | *The person **that** I admire most is my mother.* | ### Wish / Regret | Estructura | Uso | Ejemplo | |---|---|---| | Wish + past simple | Deseo presente irreal | *I wish I **had** more free time.* | | Wish + past perfect | Arrepentimiento pasado | *I wish I **had studied** harder.* | | Wish + would | Queja / cambio futuro | *I wish you **would stop** making noise.* | | Regret + gerund | Arrepentimiento por algo hecho | *I regret **telling** her the secret.* | | Regret + to infinitive | Noticia desagradable formal | *I regret **to inform** you that your application has been refused.* | --- ## 8. Collocations y redes de vocabulario ### Collocations esenciales B2 | Verbo | Collocations | |---|---| | **make** | a decision, a mistake, progress, an effort, a difference | | **do** | homework, exercise, research, a job, damage | | **take** | a photo, notes, a break, a chance, action | | **have** | a look, a chat, an effect, an influence, a problem | | **give** | advice, a speech, a chance, permission, an example | ### Redes de vocabulario: feelings - **Positive:** delighted, thrilled, pleased, content, relieved, grateful - **Negative:** frustrated, devastated, overwhelmed, anxious, exhausted - **Intensity scale:** annoyed → irritated → furious / happy → ecstatic ### Redes de vocabulario: work & business - **Verbs:** recruit, promote, resign, retire, sack, lay off - **Nouns:** colleague, employer, employee, boss, manager, CEO - **Adjectives:** qualified, experienced, reliable, ambitious, competent --- ## 9. Reading: simulated exam passage **Read the text below and answer the questions that follow.** > **The Art of Slowing Down** > > In a world that celebrates productivity and speed, choosing to slow down can feel almost rebellious. Yet research consistently shows that the quality of our experiences improves dramatically when we resist the urge to rush. A 2023 study at the University of Cambridge found that participants who were asked to eat a chocolate bar slowly reported 40% more enjoyment than those who ate it at their normal pace. The implications extend far beyond chocolate. People who walk slowly through a city notice architectural details that speed-walkers miss entirely. Musicians who practise deliberately — focusing on one passage at a time — advance faster than those who simply repeat pieces from start to finish. Slowness, it turns out, is not the enemy of efficiency but often its secret ally. The challenge is not to eliminate busyness from our lives, but to ensure that when we do move quickly, it is by choice rather than compulsion. **Questions:** 1. What is the main idea of the text? 2. According to the Cambridge study, what happened to participants who ate slowly? 3. What does the author compare eating chocolate to? 4. The word "compulsion" in the last sentence is closest in meaning to ___ 5. What tone does the author adopt throughout the text? --- ## 10. Listening: simulated exam task **Listen to the audio and complete the notes below.** 🎧 Audio: [final-review-listening.mp3](/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-60/final-review-listening.mp3) **Topic: The history of public libraries** | Detail | Answer | |---|---| | The first public library in the world opened in… | (1) _______ | | The British Library was founded in… | (2) _______ | | The biggest library today is in… | (3) _______ | | Libraries now offer services such as… | (4) _______ and (5) _______ | --- ## 11. Errores más comunes en B2 | # | Error | Correction | Regla | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | ~~If I would have known~~ | If I **had known** | Third conditional: past perfect, no "would" en la cláusula if | | 2 | ~~He suggested me to go~~ | He suggested **I (should) go** / He suggested **going** | Suggest + that + subjuntivo / gerundio | | 3 | ~~Despite of being tired~~ | **Despite being tired** | Despite + gerund / noun, nunca "despite of" | | 4 | ~~The music was being listened~~ | The music **was being listened to** | Phrasal verb pasivo: la preposición se queda al final | | 5 | ~~I wish I would have more time~~ | I wish I **had** more time | Wish + past simple para deseos presentes | | 6 | ~~He is believed being rich~~ | He is believed **to be** rich | Passive reporting + infinitivo | | 7 | ~~Although it rained, but we went out~~ | **Although** it rained, we went out | Although y but no se usan juntos | | 8 | ~~The number of students are~~ | The number of students **is** | "The number of" es singular | | 9 | ~~I used to go often to school~~ | I used to **often go** to school | Frecuencia: adverbio entre "used to" y el verbo | | 10 | ~~She told me that had she finished~~ | She told me that **she had finished** | Reported speech: no inversión en cláusulas that | --- ## 12. Simulacro de examen: overview | Paper | Parts | Ejercicios | Tiempo | |---|---|---|---| | **Use of English** | 4 parts | 20 ejercicios | 40 min | | **Reading** | 3 texts | 15 ejercicios | 40 min | | **Writing** | 2 tareas | 2 ejercicios | 40 min | | **Listening** | 4 partes | 30 ejercicios | 40 min | | **Speaking** | 4 partes | 14 minutos | 14 min | --- ## 13. Resumen rápido: master summary table | Estructura | Clave para recordar | Ejemplo | |---|---|---| | **Conditionals** | Backshift en tipos 2 y 3 | If I were you, I'd go. | | **Passive** | Agente con "by" opcional | It was built in 1900. | | **Passive reporting** | Said + to + infinitive | He is said to be a genius. | | **Reported speech** | Backshift automático | She said she was tired. | | **Modals** | Must = deducción; have to = obligación | He must be tired. | | **Phrasal verbs** | Separables e inseparables | Turn it off. / I ran into her. | | **Linkers** | Although + clause; despite + gerund | Although tired, I worked. | | **Inversion** | Never + aux + suj + verbo | Never have I seen this. | | **Cleft** | It was X who/that Y | It was John who said it. | | **Wish** | Past simple = presente; past perfect = pasado | I wish I knew. | | **Collocations** | make vs do por convención | Make a decision. | | **Word formation** | Prefijos y sufijos B2 | un-, re-, -tion, -ness, -ful | --- # Simulacro de Examen — Use of English ## Part 1: Multiple-choice cloze (5 ejercicios) **For questions 1–5, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap.** > Last summer, I decided to take a sabbatical from work. I had been feeling (1) _______ for months, and I knew something had to change. I booked a one-way ticket to Thailand, (2) _______ I hoped would help me rediscover my passion for life. The first few days were (3) _______ — I barely knew anyone and I missed my routine terribly. But gradually, I began to (4) _______ myself. I joined a cooking class, met travellers from all over the world, and for the first time in years, I felt genuinely (5) _______. The experience taught me that sometimes you need to leave everything behind to find what truly matters. 1. **A** burning out   **B** running out   **C** making out   **D** carrying out 2. **A** what   **B** which   **C** that   **D** where 3. **A** frightening   **B** daunting   **C** shocking   **D** astonishing 4. **A** enjoy   **B** amuse   **C** entertain   **D** adapt 5. **A** fulfilled   **B** satisfied   **C** completed   **D** achieved
Ver solución 1. **A — burning out**. "Burn out" = agotarse. "Running out" = quedarse sin algo; "making out" = besarse/deducir; "carrying out" = ejecutar. 2. **B — which**. Relative pronoun referring to the whole clause: "a one-way ticket to Thailand, **which** I hoped would help…" 3. **B — daunting**. Daunting = intimidante, desalentador. Es la palabra más natural para describir algo que genera inseguridad al principio. 4. **D — adapt**. "Adapt oneself" = adaptarse. En el contexto de un viaje, es la opción correcta. 5. **A — fulfilled**. Fulfilled = realizado. Complementa la idea de "encontrar lo que realmente importa".
## Part 2: Open cloze (5 ejercicios) **For questions 6–10, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap.** > Learning a foreign language is one of the most rewarding things you can do. It opens doors (6) _______ new cultures, friendships and career opportunities. However, it requires (7) _______ and persistence. Many people start enthusiastically but give (8) _______ after a few weeks when progress seems slow. The key is to set realistic goals and celebrate small (9) _______ along the way. Remember: fluency is not (10) _______ you arrive, but the journey itself.
Ver solución 6. **to** — "open doors to" = collocación fija. 7. **patience** — La oración requiere un sustantivo abstracto que搭配 con "persistence". 8. **up** — "give up" = abandonar. 9. **victories / wins** — "small victories" o "small wins" = logros pequeños. 10. **where** — "Fluency is not where you arrive" = la fluidez no es un destino, sino un proceso.
## Part 3: Word formation (5 ejercicios) **Read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of some lines to form a word that fits in the gap.** > Environmental protection has become one of the most (11) _______ issues of our time. Scientists have been warning for decades that our planet is in (12) _______. The (13) _______ of plastic in the oceans is particularly alarming. Despite growing (14) _______ among the public, governments have been slow to act. It is (15) _______ that we change our habits before it is too late. 11. URGENT 12. DANGER 13. POLLUTE 14. AWARE 15. ESSENTIAL
Ver solución 11. **urgent** — Forma adjetivo de "urgency": *most urgent issues*. 12. **danger** — "In danger" = en peligro. 13. **pollution** — Sustantivo de "pollute": *the pollution of the oceans*. 14. **awareness** — Sustantivo de "aware": *growing awareness among the public*. 15. **essential** — Adjetivo de "essence": *It is essential that…*
## Part 4: Key word transformations (5 ejercicios) **Complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between two and five words, including the word given.** 16. "I haven't seen you for ages!" she said. → She said she **(NOT SEE)** me for ages. 17. People believe that the CEO is resigning. → The CEO **(SAID)** to be resigning. 18. If I were you, I would accept the offer. → If I **(IN)** your shoes, I would accept the offer. 19. She finished the project and then left the office. → She didn't leave the office **(UNTIL)** she had finished the project. 20. "You must not park here," the sign said. → The sign said that parking **(FORBIDDEN)**.
Ver solución 16. **hadn't seen** — Reported speech: present perfect → past perfect. 17. **is said** — Passive reporting: "is said to be". 18. **were in** — "If I were in your shoes" = variante de "if I were you". 19. **until** — "didn't leave until" = no se fue hasta que. 20. **was forbidden** — Passive + past simple. "Parking was forbidden" = el estacionamiento estaba prohibido.
--- # Simulacro de Examen — Reading ## Text 1: Multiple choice (5 ejercicios) **Read the text about public libraries and answer questions 21–25.** > Public libraries have undergone a remarkable transformation in recent decades. Once seen primarily as repositories of books, they have evolved into vibrant community hubs that offer far more than lending services. Today's libraries provide free access to the internet, digital literacy courses, language workshops, and even creative spaces equipped with 3D printers. Far from becoming obsolete in the digital age, libraries have reinvented themselves. A 2024 report found that library usage among young adults increased by 25% over the past five years, driven partly by the demand for quiet study spaces and partly by the expansion of digital services. Libraries also play a crucial role in social inclusion, offering support to immigrants, elderly people, and those without access to technology at home. 21. What does the author suggest about libraries? - A) They are outdated institutions. - B) They have successfully adapted to modern needs. - C) They should focus only on books. - D) They are less popular than they used to be. 22. The word "repositories" in line 2 is closest in meaning to: - A) shops - B) storages - C) classrooms - D) offices 23. Library usage among young adults has increased because of: - A) cheaper book prices - B) the closure of other community centres - C) the availability of study spaces and digital services - D) new library buildings 24. Which group is NOT mentioned as benefiting from libraries? - A) immigrants - B) elderly people - C) children under five - D) people without home technology 25. What is the overall tone of the passage? - A) critical - B) nostalgic - C) optimistic - D) sarcastic
Ver solución 21. **B** — The text emphasises adaptation and growth, not obsolescence. 22. **B** — Repositories = almacenes/lugares de almacenamiento. 23. **C** — Explicitly stated: "driven partly by the demand for quiet study spaces and partly by the expansion of digital services." 24. **C** — Children under five are not mentioned. 25. **C** — The author presents libraries positively: "remarkable transformation", "vibrant community hubs".
## Text 2: Matching (5 ejercicios) **Read the five short texts (26–30). What is each person mainly expressing? Match each text with the correct option (A–H).** 26. "I was convinced the presentation went terribly, but my manager praised me afterwards. I guess we're always our own harshest critics." 27. "The flight was delayed by six hours, which meant I missed the opening ceremony. I tried to make the best of it, but honestly, I was furious." 28. "I've been offered a promotion, but it means relocating to another city. I'm torn — it's a great opportunity, but my family is here." 29. "My colleague always takes credit for my ideas in meetings. I've decided to speak up next time it happens." 30. "I used to think working from home was the dream, but now I realise I miss the social interaction of the office." **Options:** A. Expressing frustration B. Reflecting on a past assumption C. Showing determination D. Feeling conflicted E. Admitting self-criticism F. Complaining about unfairness G. Celebrating success H. Expressing regret
Ver solución 26. **E** — "We're always our own harshest critics" = autocrítica. 27. **A** — "I was furious" = frustración. 28. **D** — "I'm torn" = dividido/conflictuado. 29. **C** — "I've decided to speak up" = determinación. 30. **B** — "I used to think… but now I realise" = suposición pasada.
## Text 3: True / False / Not Given (5 ejercicios) **Read the text and decide if the statements are True, False or Not Given.** > Artificial intelligence has been making headlines for several years now. While proponents argue that AI will revolutionise healthcare, education and transportation, critics warn of job displacement and ethical concerns. One area where AI has already made significant inroads is in medical diagnostics. Studies have shown that AI systems can detect certain cancers with accuracy comparable to — and sometimes exceeding — that of human doctors. However, the technology is not without limitations. AI systems are only as good as the data they are trained on, and biased data can lead to biased outcomes. Furthermore, the "black box" problem — the difficulty of understanding how AI reaches its conclusions — remains a significant barrier to trust. 31. AI has been a topic of public interest for many years. — **True / False / Not Given** 32. Everyone agrees that AI will have a positive impact on society. — **True / False / Not Given** 33. AI is better than doctors at detecting all types of cancer. — **True / False / Not Given** 34. AI systems can produce unfair results if trained on biased data. — **True / False / Not Given** 35. Scientists have fully solved the "black box" problem. — **True / False / Not Given**
Ver solución 31. **True** — "has been making headlines for several years". 32. **False** — Critics are mentioned: "critics warn of job displacement and ethical concerns". 33. **False** — The text says "certain cancers", not all. 34. **True** — "biased data can lead to biased outcomes". 35. **False** — The text says it "remains a significant barrier", meaning it has not been solved.
--- # Simulacro de Examen — Writing ## Task 1: Essay (220–260 words) **Topic:** Some people believe that university education should be free for everyone. Others argue that students should pay for their own education. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. **Useful expressions:** - *It is often argued that…* - *On the other hand…* - *From my perspective…* - *A compelling argument in favour of…* - *To sum up…*
Ver modelo de respuesta > It is often argued that higher education should be funded entirely by the state, while others believe that students should bear the cost themselves. This essay will discuss both perspectives before presenting my own view. > > Those in favour of free university education contend that it promotes equality and social mobility. If students do not have to worry about tuition fees, individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds are more likely to pursue a degree. Furthermore, an educated population benefits society as a whole, as graduates tend to contribute more in taxes and civic engagement. > > On the other hand, opponents argue that making education free places an unfair burden on taxpayers who did not attend university. They also suggest that students who pay for their own education tend to be more motivated and take their studies more seriously. Moreover, governments have limited budgets and must prioritise spending on healthcare and infrastructure. > > From my perspective, a balanced approach is the most sensible solution. Governments could offer means-tested grants to students from low-income families while allowing those who can afford it to pay tuition fees. This would ensure that financial barriers do not prevent talented students from accessing education, while still maintaining a sense of personal responsibility. > > In conclusion, while free education has clear advantages, a hybrid model that combines public funding with personal contribution is likely to be the fairest and most sustainable option. *(238 words)*
## Task 2: Review (220–260 words) **Topic:** You recently stayed at a hotel. Write a review for a travel website describing your experience, what you liked and what could be improved.
Ver modelo de respuesta > **Grand Horizon Hotel — A Mixed Experience** > > Last month, I spent four nights at the Grand Horizon Hotel in Barcelona, and while there were some highlights, the experience was not without its drawbacks. > > On the positive side, the location was unbeatable. The hotel is situated just a five-minute walk from La Rambla, which made it incredibly easy to explore the city on foot. The lobby was modern and stylish, and the staff at reception were genuinely friendly and helpful. Our room had a stunning view of the harbour, which made the mornings particularly enjoyable. > > However, there were several areas that fell short of expectations. The breakfast buffet, while extensive, was often crowded, and the food was lukewarm at best. More concerning was the noise from the street below, which made it difficult to sleep before midnight. For a hotel in this price range, better soundproofing would be expected. Additionally, the Wi-Fi was frustratingly slow, which was a real inconvenience for a business traveller like myself. > > In summary, the Grand Horizon Hotel offers a fantastic location and charming staff, but the noisy rooms and poor dining experience let it down. I would recommend it for a short city break, provided you bring earplugs and are prepared for the occasional inconvenience. *(208 words)*
--- # Simulacro de Examen — Speaking ## Part 1: Interview (2 minutes) **Practice answering these questions:** 1. What do you do in your free time? 2. Have you ever travelled abroad? Where? 3. What would you like to improve about yourself?
Ver pistas de respuesta 1. *In my free time, I enjoy… / I'm quite keen on… / I tend to…* 2. *Yes, I've been to… / I went to… last year. It was… / I haven't had the chance yet, but I'd love to…* 3. *I'd like to become more… / I think I need to work on… / If I could change one thing, it would be…*
## Part 2: Long turn (1 minute per photo) **You see two photos showing people doing sports. Say which sport you think is more popular and why.**
Ver modelo > *I think the first photo, which shows people playing football, depicts a more popular sport. Football is by far the most widely played sport in the world, with millions of fans and players across every continent. It's also relatively cheap — all you need is a ball and some open space. The second photo shows people playing tennis, which is also popular, but it requires more equipment and access to a court, which limits who can play. Personally, I prefer football because it's more social and you can play it almost anywhere.*
## Part 3: Collaborative task (2 minutes) **Your friend says: "I think learning online is better than learning in a classroom." Discuss and decide.**
Ver guion - *I see your point, but…* - *That's true, although I also think…* - *I agree that… However, don't you think…?* - *Let me put it another way…* - *I'm not sure I agree with that, because…* - *So, in conclusion, we both agree that…*
## Part 4: Discussion (2 minutes) 1. Do you think technology has changed the way we learn languages? 2. Is it important for young people to learn a foreign language? Why?
Ver pistas de respuesta 1. *Absolutely. Apps like Duolingo have made it… / I'd say technology has been a double-edged sword… / On the one hand… on the other hand…* 2. *I think it's essential, because… / It depends on the country, but in general… / From a personal perspective, learning a language has helped me…*
## Part 5: Photo description (1 minute) **Describe this photo: a busy open-plan office.** ![Open-plan office](/blog/curso-b2/unit-60/open-plan-office.png)
Ver modelo > *In this photo, I can see a large open-plan office with several employees working at their desks. The space is bright and modern, with large windows letting in natural light. Most people appear to be focused on their computer screens, though two colleagues seem to be having a discussion in the background. There are also some plants scattered around, which add a nice touch to the otherwise functional environment. I imagine it could be quite noisy, which is one of the drawbacks of this kind of workspace.*

¿Qué cubre el repaso final del curso B2? Todas las estructuras gramaticales B2: conditionals, passive voice, passive reporting, reported speech, modals, phrasal verbs, linkers, collocations, inversion, cleft sentences, wish/regret, word formation y exam strategies.

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 10 del curso B1** (*Repaso 6–9*) con **soluciones comentadas**.

> **Guía teórica:** [Repaso 6–9 B1](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-10-repaso-6-9)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 10 — Repaso 6–9](/curso-b1/unit-10)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

**Foco de esta unidad:** *futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to*. Si dudas, abre primero la [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-10-repaso-6-9).

![Repaso 6–9](/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/review-map.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática](#leccion-1--gramatica)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario](#leccion-2--vocabulario)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Mixed review paragraph](#leccion-3--reading)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Emma's mixed plans](#leccion-4--listening)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing](#leccion-5--writing)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

Elige la opción correcta. Solo una es válida.

1. I ___ visit my parents next weekend. (plan) → *am going to / will / was going to*
2. She ___ be happy — she got promoted. → *must / might / can't*
3. I ___ play football when I was young. → *used to / am used to / get used to*
4. They ___ travel last summer but cancelled. → *were going to / are going to / will*
5. That ___ be him — he's in Paris. → *can't / must / might*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am going to** · 2. **must** · 3. **used to** · 4. **were going to** · 5. **can't**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

Completa cada frase con la forma correcta.

1. Wait — I ___ help you. → *will / am going to / used to*
2. She ___ living in a big city. → *is used to / used to / was going to*
3. I ___ have left my keys at work. → *might / must / can't*
4. She ___ meeting her boss at 3. → *is / will / used to*
5. It took months to ___ living here. → *get used to / used to / must*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **will** · 2. **is used to** · 3. **might** · 4. **is** · 5. **get used to**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige el error

Cada frase tiene **un** error. Reescribe la frase correcta.

1. *I am going to call you yesterday.*
2. *That mustn't be him.* (imposible)
3. *I am used to play tennis.*
4. *Look! It will rain.* (nubes negras)
5. *They was going to come.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **was going to** call you yesterday.
2. That **can't** be him.
3. I am used to **playing** / I **used to play**…
4. It **is going to** rain.
5. They **were going to** come.

</details>

---


## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

**Objetivo:** travel, plans, feelings, habits (mix).

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja / elige

Elige la **traducción o significado correcto** (ignora las distracciones).

1. postpone → *posponer · must · continuous*
2. relieved → *aliviado · despegar · pueblo*
3. commuting → *ir/venir al trabajo · cancelar · anillo*
4. engaged → *prometido/a · horario · campo*
5. arrangement → *arreglo fijo · hábito pasado · imposibilidad*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **posponer** · 2. **aliviado** · 3. **ir/venir al trabajo** · 4. **prometido/a** · 5. **arreglo fijo**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa / significado

Elige la opción que completa o explica mejor cada ítem.

1. was going to = ___ → *plan fallido / hábito pasado / casi seguro*
2. used to = ___ → *hábito pasado / arreglo fijo / evidencia*
3. must = ___ → *casi seguro / posible / imposible*
4. can't = ___ → *imposible / plan / rutina*
5. get used to = ___ → *acostumbrarse / cancelar / despegar*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **plan fallido** · 2. **hábito pasado** · 3. **casi seguro** · 4. **imposible** · 5. **acostumbrarse**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — En contexto

Completa con una de estas palabras: *postpone* · *relieved* · *commuting* · *engaged* · *arrangement*

11. Write a short sentence with **postpone** and the grammar focus (*futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to*).  
12. Write a short sentence with **relieved**.  
13. Write a short sentence with **commuting**.  
14. Choose the best word for this idea: «prometido» → **engaged** / other. Confirm in the [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-10-repaso-6-9).  
15. Practise aloud, then continue in the [Unidad 10 del curso](/curso-b1/unit-10).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. Modelo: usa **postpone** en una frase natural con *futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to*.  
12. Modelo: usa **relieved** en una frase corta.  
13. Modelo: usa **commuting** en una frase corta.  
14. **engaged** (comprueba la tabla de vocabulario en la teoría).  
15. Continúa en **/curso-b1/unit-10**.

</details>

## Lección 3 — Reading: Mixed review paragraph

**Objetivo:** comprender un texto con *practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.*.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Mixed review paragraph"></audio>

Lee el texto (puedes escuchar el audio). Las respuestas salen **del texto**.

> I used to live in a small town but now I live in London. I am meeting my sister at the airport next Saturday — she is flying from Spain. I have already booked my flight to Tokyo for next month. I was going to go last year but I cancelled because of work. My neighbour must be happy — he just moved into a new house. I am getting used to the busy city lifestyle.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión literal

Completa con la palabra que falta (según el texto).

1. I used to live in a small town but now I live in ___.
2. I am meeting my sister at the airport next ___ — she is flying from Spain.
3. I have ___ booked my flight to Tokyo for next month.
4. I was going to go last year but I ___ because of work.
5. My ___ must be happy — he just moved into a new house.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **London** · 2. **Saturday** · 3. **already** · 4. **cancelled** · 5. **neighbour**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Busca en el texto

Responde con palabras o frases **copiadas del texto**.

6. ¿De qué trata el texto en una frase? (idea principal)
7. ¿Qué estructura gramatical practicas? → *practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.*
8. Copia una frase (o trozo) con **going**.
9. Copia una frase (o trozo) con **used**.
10. Copia una frase (o trozo) con **used**.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. Modelo: resume el texto en tus palabras (tema + *practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.*).  
7. **practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.**  
8. Copia del texto algo con *going* (ej.: «I used to live in a small town but now I live in London.»).  
9. Copia del texto algo con *used*.  
10. Copia del texto algo con *used*.

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma y significado

11. Reescribe una frase del texto usando *practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.*.  
12. Nombra 2 palabras de vocabulario útiles del texto.  
13. ¿Es correcto *He must to be tired*? → True / False. Si es False, corrígelo.  
14. Enlace del curso: [/curso-b1/unit-10](/curso-b1/unit-10)  
15. Compara con la [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-10-repaso-6-9) y marca 1 duda.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. Modelo: toma una frase del texto y mantenla con *practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.*.  
12. Elige 2 palabras clave del texto (nombres, verbos o adjetivos).  
13. **False** (corrige la forma típica de error con *practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.*).  
14. **/curso-b1/unit-10**  
15. Anota tu duda y revísala en la teoría.

</details>


## Lección 4 — Listening: Emma's mixed plans

**Objetivo:** escuchar *practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.* en contexto.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/listening-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Emma's mixed plans"></audio>

Escucha primero **sin leer**. Luego puedes usar el guion para comprobar.

> Hi, I am Emma. I used to work in an office but now I work from home. I am going to travel to Italy next month. I was going to go last year but I had to cancel because of work. My friend must be happy — she just got engaged. I am used to early flights now because I travel a lot.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. ¿Quién habla?  
2. Completa según el audio: Hi, I am ___.  
3. Completa: I used to work in an ___ but now I work from home.  
4. Completa: I am going to ___ to Italy next month.  
5. Completa: I was going to go last year but I had to cancel ___ of work.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Emma**  
2. **Emma**  
3. **office**  
4. **travel**  
5. **because**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Completa: My friend must be happy — she just got ___.  
7. ¿Cuál es el foco gramatical del audio?  
8. Copia una frase del guion con el foco gramatical.  
9. Copia otra frase útil del guion.  
10. Resume en una frase lo que dice Emma.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **engaged**  
7. **practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.**  
8. «I used to work in an office but now I work from home.»  
9. «I am going to travel to Italy next month.»  
10. Modelo: Emma habla usando *practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.* sobre el tema del audio.

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Práctica oral y forma

11. Escribe una frase nueva con *practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.* (tema libre).  
12. Di en voz alta 4–5 palabras clave del audio.  
13. Escucha otra vez e imita (shadowing) una frase completa.  
14. ¿Es correcto *He must to be tired*? → True / False  
15. Abre «Ver solución» solo cuando hayas intentado 11–14.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. Modelo: crea una frase natural con *practicar futuros, was/were going to, modales, used to.*.  
12. Pronunciación libre — revisa la [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-10-repaso-6-9).  
13. Elige una frase del guion e imítala.  
14. **False**  
15. ✓

</details>

title: Repaso B1 unidades 6–9: futuros, deducción y used to
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía completa de la Unidad 10 del curso B1: repaso integrado de futuros, was/were going to, modales de deducción y used to, con diagnóstico, vocabulario mixto, reading, diálogo y ejercicios.
description: Repasa de forma integrada will/going to, was/were going to, must/might/can't y used to / be used to / get used to. Guía completa de la Unidad 10 del curso...
alt: Mapa de repaso B1 unidades 6 a 9
keywords: was going to must used to

faqs.question: ¿Qué gramática repasa exactamente la Unidad 10?
faqs.answer: Los cuatro bloques del segundo tramo del curso: **futuros** (will, going to, present continuous, Present Simple para horarios) de la Unidad 6, **was/were going to** para planes pasados no cumplidos de la Unidad 7, los **modales de deducción** (must, might, can't) de la Unidad 8, y el trío **used to / be used to / get used to** de la Unidad 9. Además, incluye vocabulario mixto de travel, plans, feelings y habits, y un diagnóstico para elegir la estructura correcta cuando aparecen mezcladas.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo elijo entre will, going to y was/were going to en una misma conversación?
faqs.answer: Pregúntate primero de qué **momento** hablas: si es futuro y ya tienes el plan decidido, usa *going to*; si es futuro y es solo una opinión o decisión espontánea, usa *will*; si es un arreglo confirmado con hora y lugar, usa el present continuous. Si en cambio hablas de un plan del **pasado** que finalmente no se cumplió, necesitas *was/were going to*, casi siempre acompañado de *but* y una razón.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia clave entre was going to y used to?
faqs.answer: **Was/were going to** describe una **intención concreta** que tenías para un momento futuro (desde el punto de vista del pasado) y que no se cumplió: *I was going to call you but I forgot*. **Used to** describe un **hábito o estado habitual** que se repetía en el pasado y que ya no es así: *I used to call my grandmother every Sunday*. La diferencia está en si hablas de una intención puntual no realizada o de una costumbre repetida que sí ocurría.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo distingo must de might en la práctica?
faqs.answer: **Must** se usa cuando la evidencia es muy clara y estás casi seguro: *She must be happy — she just got promoted*. **Might** se usa cuando la evidencia es más débil o incompleta, y solo puedes decir que algo es posible: *She might be at home — I'm not sure*. Y **can't** se reserva para cuando la evidencia contradice completamente esa posibilidad, haciendo que sea prácticamente imposible.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde puedo practicar el repaso de la Unidad 10 del curso B1?
faqs.answer: En la [Unidad 10 del curso B1 de Linguafly](/curso-b1/unit-10) tienes gramática mixta, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing, y en el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-10-repaso-6-9-ejercicios-soluciones) puedes comprobar cada respuesta con explicación. También puedes revisar las guías teóricas de las Unidades 6 a 9 enlazadas más abajo si necesitas repasar algún punto concreto.

content:
La **Unidad 10 del curso B1** (*Repaso 6–9*) integra todo lo aprendido desde los futuros hasta *used to*, cerrando el segundo tramo del curso antes de entrar en el Módulo 2 (condicionales). Igual que en la [Unidad 5](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-5-repaso-1-4), aquí no hay gramática nueva: el objetivo es que reconozcas, sin dudar, qué estructura corresponde a cada situación cuando las cuatro unidades aparecen mezcladas en el mismo texto o la misma conversación, tal como ocurre en la vida real.

Vas a repasar el contraste de **futuros** con *will*, *going to* y *present continuous* (Unidad 6), la estructura **was/were going to** para planes pasados que no se cumplieron (Unidad 7), los **modales de deducción** *must*, *might* y *can't* (Unidad 8), y el trío **used to / be used to / get used to** (Unidad 9). Además, incluye un apartado de diagnóstico con preguntas concretas para decidir rápidamente qué estructura necesitas, vocabulario mixto de las cuatro unidades, un texto de lectura, un diálogo modelo, un plan de práctica y ocho ejercicios con soluciones comentadas.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 10 — Repaso 6–9](/curso-b1/unit-10)  
> **Cuaderno de ejercicios (con soluciones):** [Ejercicios Unidad 10 B1](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-10-repaso-6-9-ejercicios-soluciones)  
> **Guías:** [U6](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-6-future-will-going-to) · [U7](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-7-was-were-going-to) · [U8](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-8-modals-deduction) · [U9](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-9-used-to-be-get-used-to)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 10 (B1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Repasar y consolidar **will, going to, present continuous** y el Present Simple para horarios.
- Repasar y consolidar **was/were going to** para planes pasados no cumplidos.
- Repasar y consolidar los modales de deducción **must, might, can't**.
- Repasar y consolidar el trío **used to / be used to / get used to**.
- Aplicar un **diagnóstico rápido** para elegir la estructura correcta en frases mixtas.
- Usar vocabulario combinado de travel, plans, feelings y habits en un mismo texto o conversación.

![Mapa de repaso](/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/review-map.png)

---

## 1. Mapa del repaso

Antes de entrar en detalle, conviene ver el conjunto completo de las cuatro unidades y su vocabulario asociado, para entender cómo se conectan entre sí.

| Unidad | Gramática | Vocabulario |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [U6](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-6-future-will-going-to) | will / going to / present continuous | Travel & transport |
| [U7](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-7-was-were-going-to) | was/were going to | Plans & intentions |
| [U8](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-8-modals-deduction) | must / might / can't | Personal feelings |
| [U9](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-9-used-to-be-get-used-to) | used to / be used to / get used to | Habits & lifestyle |

Fíjate en la progresión: la Unidad 6 mira hacia el **futuro**, la Unidad 7 mira hacia un **futuro que ya no se cumplió**, la Unidad 8 razona sobre el **presente y el pasado con evidencia**, y la Unidad 9 mira hacia **hábitos y adaptación**. Juntas cubren casi todos los matices temporales que necesitas para hablar con naturalidad de tu vida pasada, presente y futura.

---

## 2. Repaso: Futuros (U6)

Recuerda el criterio de elección: *will* para opinión, promesa o decisión espontánea; *going to* para plan o evidencia visible; present continuous para un arreglo confirmado con hora y lugar; Present Simple para horarios oficiales.

> I **am going to** visit my parents next weekend. *(plan)*  
> Wait, I **will** help you. *(espontáneo)*  
> She **is meeting** her boss at 3 PM. *(arreglo)*  
> Look at the clouds! It **is going to** rain. *(evidencia)*  
> We **are flying** to Rome on Friday. *(viaje fijo)*

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/future-review.mp3" title="🔊 Future forms review"></audio>

---

## 3. Repaso: Was/were going to (U7)

Recuerda el patrón típico: *was/were going to + verbo* + *but* + razón, para explicar un plan pasado que finalmente no se cumplió.

> I **was going to** call you yesterday but I forgot.  
> They **were going to** travel to Spain last summer but cancelled.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/was-going-to-review.mp3" title="🔊 Was/were going to review"></audio>

---

## 4. Repaso: Deducción (U8)

Recuerda la escala de certeza: *must* (≈90%, evidencia fuerte), *might* (≈50%, posibilidad), *can't* (≈0%, imposibilidad según la evidencia).

> She **must** be happy — she just got promoted.  
> That **can't** be him — he is in Paris this week.  
> I **might** have left my keys at the office.  
> They **must** be at home — the lights are on.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/modals-review.mp3" title="🔊 Modals of deduction review"></audio>

---

## 5. Repaso: Used to trio (U9)

Recuerda las tres ideas: *used to* (hábito pasado que ya terminó), *be used to* (acostumbrado ahora), *get used to* (proceso de adaptación).

> I **used to** play football when I was young.  
> She **is used to** living in a big city.  
> It took me a few months to **get used to** living here.  
> They **got used to** the cold weather after a few months.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/used-to-review.mp3" title="🔊 Used to trio review"></audio>

---

## 6. Diagnóstico mixto: cómo elegir la estructura correcta

Cuando te enfrentes a una frase y no sepas qué estructura necesitas, sigue este proceso de decisión, en orden:

1. **¿Hablas de una intención pasada que no se cumplió?** Si sí → **was/were going to** (+ *but* + razón).
2. **¿Hablas del futuro?** Si sí → decide entre *will* (opinión/espontáneo), *going to* (plan/evidencia) o present continuous (arreglo confirmado).
3. **¿Estás razonando sobre algo a partir de una evidencia?** Si sí → decide entre *must* (casi seguro), *might* (posible) o *can't* (imposible), según lo fuerte que sea esa evidencia.
4. **¿Hablas de un hábito del pasado que ya no es verdad?** Si sí → **used to**.
5. **¿Hablas de estar acostumbrado ahora, o del proceso de acostumbrarte?** Si sí → **be used to** (estado) o **get used to** (proceso).

Con este proceso, mira este ejemplo mixto: *"I was going to visit Japan last year, but I cancelled my trip. I used to dream about it every day, and I might go next year instead. My friend, who has already been there twice, must be a real expert on Japanese culture by now, and she says you get used to the time difference after just a few days."* Contiene *was going to*, *used to*, *might*, *must* y *get used to* — las cuatro unidades trabajando juntas en un solo párrafo, tal como ocurre en una conversación real.

---

## 7. Vocabulario mixto: las cuatro unidades

![Ejemplos rápidos](/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/review-examples.png)

| Palabra | Unidad | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| flight | U6 — Travel | We are booking the **flight** next week. |
| delay | U6 — Travel | There was a two-hour **delay** at the airport. |
| postpone | U7 — Plans | They had to **postpone** the wedding. |
| change your mind | U7 — Plans | She decided to **change her mind** at the last minute. |
| relieved | U8 — Feelings | They must feel very **relieved** after the good news. |
| confident | U8 — Feelings | He looks much more **confident** these days. |
| lifestyle | U9 — Habits | She has a very active **lifestyle** now. |
| adjustment period | U9 — Habits | Every big change has an **adjustment period**. |

---

## 8. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes (repaso mixto)

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Unidad |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I will to go.* | *I **will go**.* | U6 |
| *I am going to call you yesterday.* | *I **was going to** call you yesterday.* | U7 |
| *They was going to travel.* | *They **were** going to travel.* | U7 |
| *That mustn't be him.* (imposible) | *That **can't** be him.* | U8 |
| *He must to be tired.* | *He **must be** tired.* | U8 |
| *I am used to play tennis.* | *I am used to **playing** tennis.* | U9 |
| *I didn't used to smoke.* | *I **didn't use** to smoke.* | U9 |
| *The flight is depart at 10.* | *The flight **departs** at 10.* | U6 |

---

## 9. Reading mixto: un año de cambios

![Ejemplos rápidos](/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/review-examples.png)

> Last year I was going to travel to Japan for my birthday, but I had to cancel because I got a new job that started earlier than expected. I used to dream about that trip every single day, so it was a difficult decision, but I think it must have been the right one, because I love my new job. I am used to the new schedule now, although it took me a few months to get used to waking up so early every morning. My colleague must be really experienced with international trips, because she has already visited more than twenty countries. She might be able to give me some tips before I finally travel to Japan next year. I am going to start saving money again soon, and this time nothing will stop me from getting on that plane.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: a year of changes"></audio>

Identifica las cuatro estructuras del repaso en el texto: *was going to* (U7), *used to* y *get used to* (U9), *must have been* y *might* (U8), y *am going to* (U6).

---

## 10. Diálogo: repasando antes del Módulo 2

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/listening-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: mixed review"></audio>

> **Nadia:** Were you going to travel to Japan last year?  
> **Hugo:** Yes, but I cancelled because I got a new job.  
> **Nadia:** Do you regret it? You used to talk about that trip all the time.  
> **Hugo:** A little, but it must have been the right decision. I love my job.  
> **Nadia:** Are you used to the new schedule now?  
> **Hugo:** Yes, although it took a while to get used to waking up so early.  
> **Nadia:** Do you think you'll travel to Japan next year instead?  
> **Hugo:** I hope so. I am going to start saving money again soon.  
> **Nadia:** Your colleague might have some good tips, right?  
> **Hugo:** Definitely. She must be an expert — she's visited over twenty countries.

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (10–15 minutos)

1. **3 min — Repaso auditivo.** Escucha los audios de las secciones 2 a 5 en orden y, antes de cada uno, intenta predecir qué estructura vas a escuchar.
2. **4 min — Lectura activa.** Lee el reading mixto y clasifica cada estructura subrayada en una de las cuatro unidades (U6, U7, U8 o U9).
3. **4 min — Producción oral.** Practica el diálogo con otra persona y después cámbialo para hablar de un cambio real en tu propia vida durante el último año.
4. **4 min — Autoevaluación.** Escribe una frase por cada unidad (cuatro en total) sobre tu propia vida, y después una quinta frase que combine dos estructuras distintas en la misma oración.

### Practica con el audio de la unidad

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-10/practice-mix.mp3" title="🔊 Mixed practice"></audio>

Escucha este audio de práctica mixta dos veces: la primera solo para identificar de oído qué estructura aparece en cada frase; la segunda repitiendo cada frase completa en voz alta.

> I am going to visit my parents next weekend. She must be happy. I used to play football. I was going to call you but I forgot. We are flying to Rome on Friday. That can't be him.

---

## 12. Ejercicios integrados

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige la forma

1. I \_\_\_\_ visit my parents next weekend. *(plan)*
2. She \_\_\_\_ be happy — she got promoted.
3. I \_\_\_\_ play football when I was young.
4. They \_\_\_\_ travel last summer but cancelled.
5. That \_\_\_\_ be him — he's in Paris.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am going to** · 2. **must** · 3. **used to** · 4. **were going to** · 5. **can't**

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Más contraste

1. Wait — I \_\_\_\_ help you.
2. She \_\_\_\_ living in a big city for years. *(is used to)*
3. I \_\_\_\_ have left my keys at work.
4. She \_\_\_\_ meeting her boss at 3.
5. It took months to \_\_\_\_ living here.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **will** · 2. **is used to** · 3. **might** · 4. **is** · 5. **get used to**

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Corrección

1. *I am going to call you yesterday.* → \_\_\_\_
2. *That mustn't be him* (imposible) → \_\_\_\_
3. *I am used to play tennis.* → \_\_\_\_
4. *Look! It will rain* (nubes negras) → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **was going to** call you yesterday…
2. That **can't** be him.
3. I am used to **playing** / I **used to play**…
4. It **is going to** rain.

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Matching rápido

A. arrangement fijo · B. plan fallido · C. hábito pasado · D. deducción fuerte

1. We are flying on Friday. → \_\_\_\_
2. I was going to go but cancelled. → \_\_\_\_
3. I used to live in a village. → \_\_\_\_
4. She must be relieved. → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **A** · 2. **B** · 3. **C** · 4. **D**

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading (a year of changes)

1. The trip to Japan was planned for last \_\_\_\_.
2. The person got a new \_\_\_\_.
3. It took a few months to get used to waking up \_\_\_\_.
4. The colleague has visited more than \_\_\_\_ countries.
5. The person is going to start \_\_\_\_ money again.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **year** · 2. **job** · 3. **early** · 4. **twenty** · 5. **saving**

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Listening extra (diálogo)

Escucha el diálogo de la sección 10 y anota qué estructura de cada unidad (U6, U7, U8, U9) aparece en cada turno de la conversación.

<details>
<summary>Modelo de respuesta</summary>

"Were you going to travel…?" (U7) · "I am going to start saving…" (U6) · "It must have been the right decision" (U8) · "It took a while to get used to…" (U9).

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Traducción al inglés (mezcla las cuatro unidades)

1. Iba a viajar a Japón, pero lo cancelé.
2. Debe de estar muy orgullosa de su trabajo.
3. Solía vivir en un pueblo pequeño.
4. Voy a empezar a ahorrar dinero de nuevo.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I was going to travel to Japan, but I cancelled.**
2. **She must be very proud of her job.**
3. **I used to live in a small village.**
4. **I am going to start saving money again.**

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Produce un párrafo de repaso

Escribe una frase con cada estructura: *going to*, *was going to*, *must*, *can't*, *used to*, *get used to*.

<details>
<summary>Modelo</summary>

I **am going to** study tonight. I **was going to** go out, but I was tired. She **must** be pleased. That **can't** be true. I **used to** hate mornings. I am **getting used to** waking up early.

</details>

---

## 13. Checklist antes del Módulo 2

- [ ] Distingo *will / going to / continuous* según opinión, plan o arreglo.
- [ ] Sé narrar un plan cancelado con *was/were going to… but…*.
- [ ] Uso *must / might / can't* con la evidencia adecuada en cada caso.
- [ ] No confundo *used to* con *be used to*.
- [ ] Puedo hablar con naturalidad de travel, plans, feelings y habits.

Si falla algún punto, vuelve a su unidad correspondiente y repasa de nuevo la teoría y los ejercicios antes de continuar en el [curso](/curso-b1/unit-10).

---

## Tip del profesor

En el repaso, **no memorices tablas de memoria**: inventa mini-historias que combinen varias estructuras (un viaje cancelado, seguido de deducciones sobre un amigo, seguido de un cambio de hábitos). La gramática de nivel B1 se fija mucho mejor con contexto real que con listas aisladas, y este tipo de historias cortas es exactamente lo que necesitarás producir en una conversación o en un examen oral.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Unidad | Estructura clave | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U6 | will / going to / present continuous | I am going to visit my parents. |
| U7 | was/were going to + but + razón | I was going to call you but I forgot. |
| U8 | must / might / can't | She must be happy. |
| U9 | used to / be used to / get used to | I used to live in a village. |
| Diagnóstico | intención pasada → evidencia → hábito | Combina las cuatro según el contexto. |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso B1

Tras este repaso, continuarás con el **Módulo 2** del curso B1: la Unidad 11 profundiza en el **first conditional** y las *future time clauses*, con vocabulario del tiempo atmosférico (*weather*).

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 10 B1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-10-repaso-6-9-ejercicios-soluciones)

1. Relee las guías de U6–U9 en veinte minutos (solo mapas rápidos y ejemplos).
2. Haz los ocho ejercicios de esta página en voz alta.
3. Completa la [Unidad 10 del curso B1](/curso-b1/unit-10).

Curso:

- [Unidad 11 — First conditional](/curso-b1/unit-11) *(siguiente módulo)*

Guía teórica siguiente:

- [U11 — First conditional & Weather](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-11-first-conditional-weather)

Guías relacionadas:

- [U6 — Future forms](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-6-future-will-going-to)
- [U7 — Was/were going to](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-7-was-were-going-to)
- [U8 — Modals of deduction](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-8-modals-deduction)
- [U9 — Used to trio](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-9-used-to-be-get-used-to)
- [Inglés B1: guía del nivel](/blog/metodos/cursos-online-ingles-b1)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel B1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- Cambridge English — B1 Preliminary: https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/preliminary/
- British Council — B1 grammar reference: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/b1-b2-grammar

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 11 del curso B1** (*First Conditional & Weather*) con **soluciones comentadas**.

> **Guía teórica:** [First conditional & Weather B1](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-11-first-conditional-weather)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 11 — First conditional & Weather](/curso-b1/unit-11)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

**Foco de esta unidad:** *first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until)*. Si dudas, abre primero la [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-11-first-conditional-weather).

![First conditional & Weather](/blog/curso-b1/unit-11/first-conditional.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática](#leccion-1--gramatica)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario](#leccion-2--vocabulario)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Weekend weather plans](#leccion-3--reading)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Anna's weather plans](#leccion-4--listening)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing](#leccion-5--writing)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** practicar first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until).

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

Elige la opción correcta. Solo una es válida.

1. If it ___ tomorrow, I will stay at home. → *rains / will rain / rained*
2. When I ___, I will call you. → *arrive / will arrive / arrived*
3. As soon as the storm ___, I will call. → *passes / will pass / passed*
4. We will stay indoors until the rain ___. → *stops / will stop / stopped*
5. If it's sunny, we ___ have a barbecue. → *will / would / are*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **rains** · 2. **arrive** · 3. **passes** · 4. **stops** · 5. **will**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

Completa cada frase con la forma correcta.

1. If you ___ early, we will have time for coffee. → *come / will come / came*
2. Before we leave, I ___ check the forecast. → *will / would / am*
3. After the storm, we ___ go for a walk. → *will / would / are*
4. If there ___ a storm, we will stay indoors. → *is / will be / was*
5. I will tell you when I ___ the forecast. → *see / will see / saw*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **come** · 2. **will** · 3. **will** · 4. **is** · 5. **see**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige el error

Cada frase tiene **un** error. Reescribe la frase correcta.

1. *If it will rain, I stay home.*
2. *When I will arrive, I call you.*
3. *As soon as it will pass…*
4. *Until the rain will stop…*
5. *If it's sunny, we would have a barbecue.* (plan real)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. If it **rains**, I **will** stay home.
2. When I **arrive**, I **will** call you.
3. As soon as it **passes**…
4. Until the rain **stops**…
5. If it's sunny, we **will** have a barbecue.

</details>

---


## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

**Objetivo:** weather.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja / elige

Elige la **traducción o significado correcto** (ignora las distracciones).

1. sunny → *soleado · lluvioso · nublado*
2. storm → *tormenta · niebla · brisa*
3. forecast → *pronóstico · temperatura · humedad*
4. temperature → *temperatura · clima · granizo*
5. drizzle → *llovizna · aguacero · sequía*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **soleado** · 2. **tormenta** · 3. **pronóstico** · 4. **temperatura** · 5. **llovizna**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa / significado

Elige la opción que completa o explica mejor cada ítem.

1. Day with no clouds = ___ → *sunny / rainy / foggy*
2. Strong rain + thunder = ___ → *storm / drizzle / mild*
3. How hot/cold = ___ → *temperature / forecast / climate*
4. Pronóstico = ___ → *forecast / humidity / hail*
5. Relámpago = ___ → *lightning / thunder / wind*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **sunny** · 2. **storm** · 3. **temperature** · 4. **forecast** · 5. **lightning**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — En contexto

Completa con una de estas palabras: *sunny* · *storm* · *forecast* · *temperature* · *drizzle*

11. Write a short sentence with **sunny** and the grammar focus (*first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until)*).  
12. Write a short sentence with **storm**.  
13. Write a short sentence with **forecast**.  
14. Choose the best word for this idea: «temperatura» → **temperature** / other. Confirm in the [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-11-first-conditional-weather).  
15. Practise aloud, then continue in the [Unidad 11 del curso](/curso-b1/unit-11).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. Modelo: usa **sunny** en una frase natural con *first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until)*.  
12. Modelo: usa **storm** en una frase corta.  
13. Modelo: usa **forecast** en una frase corta.  
14. **temperature** (comprueba la tabla de vocabulario en la teoría).  
15. Continúa en **/curso-b1/unit-11**.

</details>

---


## Lección 3 — Reading: Weekend weather plans

**Objetivo:** comprender un texto con *practicar first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until).*.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-11/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Weekend weather plans"></audio>

Lee el texto (puedes escuchar el audio). Las respuestas salen **del texto**.

> Tomorrow the weather forecast says it will be sunny in the morning but cloudy in the afternoon. If it rains, we will stay at home and watch a film. When the sun comes out, we will go for a walk in the park. As soon as the storm passes, I will call you to arrange our picnic. We will stay indoors until the rain stops. The temperature will be mild, around twenty degrees.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión literal

Completa con la palabra que falta (según el texto).

1. Tomorrow the weather forecast says it will be sunny in the morning but cloudy in the ___.
2. If it ___, we will stay at home and watch a film.
3. When the sun ___ out, we will go for a walk in the park.
4. As soon as the storm passes, I will call you to ___ our picnic.
5. We will stay ___ until the rain stops.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **afternoon** · 2. **rains** · 3. **comes** · 4. **arrange** · 5. **indoors**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Busca en el texto

Responde con palabras o frases **copiadas del texto**.

6. ¿De qué trata el texto en una frase? (idea principal)
7. ¿Qué estructura gramatical practicas? → *practicar first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until).*
8. Copia una frase (o trozo) con **when**.
9. Copia una frase (o trozo) con **soon**.
10. Copia una frase (o trozo) con **until**.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. Modelo: resume el texto en tus palabras (tema + *practicar first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until).*).  
7. **practicar first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until).**  
8. Copia del texto algo con *when* (ej.: «Tomorrow the weather forecast says it will be sunny in the morning but cloudy in the afternoon.»).  
9. Copia del texto algo con *soon*.  
10. Copia del texto algo con *until*.

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma y significado

11. Reescribe una frase del texto usando *practicar first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until).*.  
12. Nombra 2 palabras de vocabulario útiles del texto.  
13. ¿Es correcto *If I will see her, I will call you*? → True / False. Si es False, corrígelo.  
14. Enlace del curso: [/curso-b1/unit-11](/curso-b1/unit-11)  
15. Compara con la [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-11-first-conditional-weather) y marca 1 duda.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. Modelo: toma una frase del texto y mantenla con *practicar first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until).*.  
12. Elige 2 palabras clave del texto (nombres, verbos o adjetivos).  
13. **False** (corrige la forma típica de error con *practicar first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until).*).  
14. **/curso-b1/unit-11**  
15. Anota tu duda y revísala en la teoría.

</details>


## Lección 4 — Listening: Anna's weather plans

**Objetivo:** escuchar *practicar first conditional + future time clauses (when, as soon as, until).* en contexto.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-11/listening-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Anna's weather plans"></audio>

Escucha primero **sin leer**. Luego puedes usar el guion para comprobar.

> Hi, I am Anna. If it rains tomorrow, I will stay at home and watch a film. When I see the forecast, I will tell you. As soon as the storm passes, I will call you to arrange our picnic. Until the rain stops, we will stay indoors. If it's sunny on Saturday, we will have a barbecue in the garden.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. ¿Quién habla?  
2. Completa según el audio: Hi, I am ___.  
3. Completa: If it rains ___, I will stay at home and watch a film.  
4. Completa: When I see the ___, I will tell you.  
5. Completa: As soon as the storm passes, I will call you to ___ our picnic.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Anna**  
2. **Anna**  
3. **tomorrow**  
4. **forecast**  
5. **arrange**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Completa: Until the rain stops, we will stay ___.  
7. ¿Cuál es el foco gramatical del audio?  
8. Copia una frase del guion con el foco gramatical.  
9. Copia otra frase útil del guion.  
10. Resume en una frase lo que dice Anna.

<details>

faqs.question: ¿Qué es el first conditional?
faqs.answer: Es la estructura If + present simple, will + infinitivo que usamos para hablar de situaciones reales o posibles en el futuro: If it rains, I will stay at home. La condición es realista, no una fantasía — podrías comprobarla mañana mismo.

faqs.question: ¿Qué son future time clauses?
faqs.answer: Son cláusulas de tiempo como when, as soon as, until, before y after que anuncian una acción futura pero llevan el verbo en presente, nunca en will: When I arrive, I will call you. As soon as the storm passes, we will leave.

faqs.question: ¿Puedo poner will en el if?
faqs.answer: No, en el first conditional estándar de B1 la if-clause nunca lleva will: *If it will rain* ✗ → If it rains ✓. Will solo aparece en la parte del resultado (main clause).

faqs.question: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre if y when con el tiempo futuro?
faqs.answer: If introduce una condición incierta (puede pasar o no): If it rains… When introduce algo que sabes que va a pasar, solo falta el momento exacto: When it gets dark… (sabemos que oscurecerá; if implicaría duda).
