## Diálogo: hablando de sentimientos

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-6/dialogue-u6.mp3" title="🔊 Diálogo: expressing feelings"></audio>

> **A:** You look anxious. Is everything okay?
> **B:** I am, actually. I wish I weren't so nervous about the presentation tomorrow.
> **A:** I understand. If only you had practised with me last night!
> **B:** I know. I wish I had asked for your help earlier.
> **A:** Well, it's not too late. We could still rehearse tonight.
> **B:** That would be great. I wish I could feel more confident about it.
> **A:** You will. And if only more people admitted they get nervous too!
> **B:** True. I wish people would talk more openly about their feelings.
> **A:** Exactly. Let's practise now — you'll feel more relieved afterwards.
> **B:** Thanks. I already feel less overwhelmed just talking about it.

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa con wish + past simple o past perfect

### Ejercicio 9 — Escribe tu propio texto

Escribe 8–10 frases sobre ti mismo/a. Incluye:

- 2 frases con **wish + past simple / were** (presente).
- 2 frases con **wish / if only + past perfect** (pasado).
- 1 frase con **wish + could**.
- 1 frase con **wish + would** (queja sobre otra persona).
- Al menos 4 palabras de vocabulario de feelings.

**Modelo:** usa el texto de la sección de reading como referencia de estilo.

## Tip del profesor

La clave para no confundirte con wish e if only es hacerte siempre la misma pregunta: **¿el problema es ahora o fue en el pasado?** Si es ahora, usa pasado simple / were / could. Si fue en el pasado, usa past perfect. Y si lo que quieres es que **otra persona cambie de comportamiento**, entonces —y solo entonces— usa would. Practicar esta pregunta mental antes de hablar te ahorrará la mayoría de los errores típicos de esta unidad.

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| wish + past simple / were | deseo sobre el presente | I wish I had more time. |
| wish + could | habilidad/posibilidad presente | I wish I could play well. |
| wish / if only + past perfect | arrepentimiento pasado | If only you had told me. |
| wish + would | queja sobre otra persona | I wish they would stop. |
| Vocabulario | feelings & emotions | anxious, relieved, overwhelmed... |

content:
## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 7 (B2)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar **would rather + infinitivo sin *to*** para expresar tus propias preferencias.
- Usar **would rather + sujeto + pasado** para expresar preferencias sobre lo que hace otra persona.
- Usar **would prefer + to infinitivo** (o + sustantivo + to + sustantivo) como alternativa más formal.
- Usar **it's (high/about) time + pasado** para decir que ya deberíamos estar haciendo algo.
- Formar la negación correcta con **would rather not** y **would prefer not to**.
- Nombrar y usar en contexto vocabulario de **family**: sibling, in-laws, extended family, gathering y más.

![Esquema de would rather, would prefer e it's time en inglés B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/would-rather-prefer.png)

---

## Gramática: Would Rather, Would Prefer & It's Time

### 1. Would rather + infinitivo sin *to*: tu propia preferencia

Para decir qué preferirías hacer **tú mismo/a**, usamos **would rather + infinitivo sin *to***. Es una de las formas más comunes en inglés hablado para expresar preferencia, y suena más natural que *I prefer to* en la conversación diaria. Por ejemplo, si prefieres comprar por internet antes que ir a una tienda física, dices *I would rather shop online*.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/rather-shop.mp3" title="🔊 would rather + infinitivo: I would rather shop online"></audio>

La forma contraída *I'd rather* es extremadamente frecuente en el habla informal. Recuerda que, como con los modales, **rather nunca lleva *to*** antes del verbo: no decimos *I would rather to shop*, sino *I would rather shop*.

### 2. Would rather + sujeto + pasado: preferencias sobre otra persona

Cuando quieres expresar una preferencia sobre lo que **hace o hará otra persona**, la estructura cambia: **would rather + sujeto + pasado simple**. Aunque el verbo esté en pasado, el significado es sobre el presente o el futuro — funciona igual que el pasado irreal que ya viste con wish en la Unidad 6. Por ejemplo, *I'd rather you came early* significa que ahora mismo preferirías que la otra persona llegara pronto, no que ya haya ocurrido en el pasado.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/rather-you-came.mp3" title="🔊 would rather + subject + past: I'd rather you came early"></audio>

Esta es probablemente la estructura más difícil de la unidad porque contradice la intuición: no hay ningún "pasado real" en la frase, solo una forma verbal de pasado usada para señalar irrealidad o hipótesis, tal como ocurre en el segundo condicional y con wish.

### 3. Would prefer + to infinitivo: la alternativa más formal

**Would prefer** expresa el mismo tipo de preferencia que would rather, pero requiere **to + infinitivo** después: *He would prefer to buy local products*. También puede usarse con dos sustantivos unidos por *to*: **would prefer + sustantivo + to + sustantivo**, como en *I would prefer tea to coffee* (prefiero el té al café).

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/prefer-to-buy.mp3" title="🔊 would prefer + to: He would prefer to buy local"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/prefer-not.mp3" title="🔊 would prefer not to"></audio>

La negación se forma con **would prefer not to + infinitivo**: *I would prefer not to travel alone*. Would prefer se usa con más frecuencia en contextos formales, escritos o cuando queremos sonar especialmente educados, por ejemplo al rechazar una invitación con delicadeza.

### 4. It's (high/about) time + pasado: ya deberíamos hacerlo

**It's time** (o las versiones más enfáticas **it's high time** / **it's about time**) seguido de **sujeto + pasado simple** se usa para decir que **ya deberíamos estar haciendo algo** que hemos estado posponiendo. De nuevo, el pasado no indica tiempo pasado real, sino urgencia sobre el presente. Por ejemplo, si una familia lleva meses sin controlar sus gastos, puedes decir *It's time he got his budget under control*.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/its-time-got.mp3" title="🔊 it's time + past: It's time he got his budget under control"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/high-time.mp3" title="🔊 it's high time + past: It's high time they started apologising"></audio>

Cuanto más añades *high* o *about*, más fuerte es la sensación de urgencia o incluso de reproche. *It's high time they apologised* suena más a "ya iba siendo hora, ¡y tarde!" que un simple *it's time*.

### 5. Cómo elegir entre rather, prefer e it's time

Estas tres estructuras se confunden porque todas hablan de preferencias o de lo que "debería" pasar, pero cada una responde a una pregunta distinta. **Would rather** responde a "¿qué preferirías hacer tú (o que hiciera otra persona)?" en un registro informal. **Would prefer** responde a la misma pregunta, pero en un registro más cuidado y con *to* obligatorio. **It's (high) time**, en cambio, no habla de preferencia sino de **urgencia o retraso**: algo que ya debería haber pasado y no ha pasado. Antes de construir la frase, decide primero qué mensaje quieres dar — preferencia informal, preferencia formal, o urgencia — y elige la estructura correspondiente.

---

## Vocabulario: Family

![Vocabulario de family en inglés B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/family-vocab.png)

| Palabra | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **sibling** | hermano/a | I have two siblings, a brother and a sister. |
| **cousin** | primo/a | My cousin lives in Canada. |
| **in-laws** | suegros / familia política | We're having dinner with my in-laws tonight. |
| **household** | hogar / unidad familiar | Our household has five people. |
| **get along (with)** | llevarse bien (con) | I get along really well with my grandparents. |
| **reunion** | reunión familiar | The family reunion happens every summer. |
| **grandparents** | abuelos | My grandparents live in the countryside. |
| **extended family** | familia extendida | We invited our extended family to the wedding. |
| **nuclear family** | familia nuclear | A nuclear family usually means parents and children. |
| **relative** | pariente | Several relatives came from abroad for the party. |
| **gathering** | reunión / encuentro | We're organising a family gathering next month. |
| **decorate** | decorar | The children love decorating the house for the holidays. |
| **celebrate** | celebrar | We always celebrate birthdays together. |
| **only child** | hijo/a único/a | She's an only child, so she loves spending time with cousins. |
| **stepbrother / stepsister** | hermanastro/a | My stepbrother moved in with us last year. |
| **twins** | gemelos/as, mellizos/as | My aunt is expecting twins. |

Combina este vocabulario con la gramática: *I would rather spend time with my siblings than with strangers* o *It's time our extended family had a proper reunion*.

---

## Errores típicos con would rather, would prefer e it's time

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I would rather to stay home. | I would rather **stay** home. | Rather + infinitivo sin *to*. |
| She would prefer travel by bus. | She would prefer **to travel** by bus. | Prefer + to + infinitivo. |
| I would rather my brother comes early. | I would rather my brother **came** early. | Sujeto distinto → pasado, no presente. |
| It is time we leave. | It is time we **left**. | It's time + pasado, no presente. |
| Would you rather to cook? | Would you rather **cook**? | Sin *to* en preguntas también. |
| I don't would rather go. | I would rather **not go**. | La negación va con "rather not", no "don't would rather". |
| I would prefer staying home. | I would prefer **to stay** home. | Prefer + to-infinitivo, no gerundio, en esta estructura. |
| It's high time we are leaving. | It's high time we **left**. | Pasado también con "high time". |
| I would rather not to travel alone. | I would rather **not travel** alone. | "Not" va antes del infinitivo sin *to*. |

---

## Reading: Tom's family plans

![Escena de family en contexto en inglés B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/family-scene.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/reading-u7.mp3" title="🔊 Escucha las frases clave del reading"></audio>

> Family gatherings need planning, and Tom's family is no exception. Tom would rather cook at home than eat in a noisy restaurant, especially now that his household includes three young children. He would prefer to celebrate his birthday with close relatives only, rather than inviting the whole extended family. It is high time they called their cousins in Canada — it has been three years since they last spoke, and everyone keeps saying they will do it "soon". Tom would rather his brother helped with the decorations this year, because last time nobody organised anything until the last minute. His mother, meanwhile, would prefer to have the party in the garden instead of the crowded living room, weather permitting. Balancing everyone's preferences is never simple, but Tom believes that a little planning — and a few honest conversations about what each person would rather do — makes family celebrations far more enjoyable for everyone involved.

**Comprueba tu comprensión:** ¿qué preferiría Tom sobre la fiesta de cumpleaños? ¿Y qué preferiría su madre?

---

## Diálogo: preferencias en una reunión familiar

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/dialogue-u7.mp3" title="🔊 Diálogo: family preferences"></audio>

> **A:** Should we stay in tonight or go out with the family?
> **B:** I'd rather stay with my siblings, if that's okay.
> **A:** Sure. Would you prefer to order pizza or cook something?
> **B:** I'd rather cook, actually — the kids love helping in the kitchen.
> **A:** Good idea. By the way, it's time we called your cousins abroad.
> **B:** You're right, it's been far too long. It's high time we did.
> **A:** I'd rather you called them this weekend, not next month.
> **B:** Fair enough. I would prefer to call on Sunday afternoon, though.
> **A:** That works for me. Should we invite the in-laws too?
> **B:** I'd rather keep it small this time — just close relatives.

---

## Plan de práctica (10–15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Repasa las cinco secciones de gramática y practica en voz alta un ejemplo de cada una.
2. **4 min** — Escucha los audios de rather, prefer e it's time y repite cada frase, prestando atención a si va con *to* o no.
3. **4 min** — Lee el texto sobre Tom y anota qué estructura usa en cada frase (rather, prefer o it's time).
4. **3–4 min** — Practica el diálogo y después crea tres frases propias sobre preferencias familiares reales.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso would rather + infinitivo sin *to*.
- [ ] Uso would rather + sujeto + pasado para hablar de otra persona.
- [ ] Uso would prefer + to + infinitivo correctamente.
- [ ] Uso it's (high) time + pasado para expresar urgencia.
- [ ] Nombro al menos 6 palabras de vocabulario de family.

---

## Practica en el curso B2

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/practice-u7.mp3" title="🔊 Practica: repite y responde"></audio>

Escucha el audio de práctica y repite cada frase antes de continuar. Después, responde en voz alta: *Would you rather spend a weekend with your family or with friends? Is there anything it's time you started doing at home?* Intenta usar al menos una de las tres estructuras de la unidad en cada respuesta.

## Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Would rather / would prefer

1. I would rather ___ (shop) online tonight.
2. He would prefer ___ (buy) local.
3. I would rather my sister ___ (come) early.
4. She would prefer tea ___ coffee.
5. I would rather ___ (not travel) alone.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **shop** · 2. **to buy** · 3. **came** · 4. **to** · 5. **not travel**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — It's time

1. It's time he ___ (get) his budget under control.
2. It's high time they ___ (start) apologising.
3. It's about time we ___ (call) our cousins.
4. It's time you ___ (learn) to cook.
5. It's time the children ___ (go) to bed.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **got** · 2. **started** · 3. **called** · 4. **learned** · 5. **went**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Corrige el error

1. *I would rather to stay home.*
2. *She would prefer travel by bus.*
3. *It is time we leave.*
4. *I would rather my brother comes early.*
5. *Would you rather to cook?*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I would rather **stay** home.
2. She would prefer **to travel** by bus.
3. It is time we **left**.
4. I would rather my brother **came** early.
5. Would you rather **cook**?
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Elige la opción correcta

1. Would you rather ___ or fly? → *drive / to drive / driving*
2. I would prefer tea ___ coffee. → *to / than / over*
3. It is about time he ___ a job. → *find / found / finding*
4. She would rather her parents ___ with them. → *stay / stayed / staying*
5. I'd rather you ___ tell anyone yet. → *don't / didn't / not*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **drive** · 2. **to** · 3. **found** · 4. **stayed** · 5. **didn't**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Vocabulario: empareja

1. sibling
2. in-laws
3. gathering
4. extended family
5. only child
6. get along

a) llevarse bien · b) hermano/a · c) suegros · d) familia extendida · e) reunión · f) hijo/a único/a

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **c** · 3 → **e** · 4 → **d** · 5 → **f** · 6 → **a**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el diálogo

A: Should we stay in or go out with the ___?
B: I'd ___ stay with my siblings.
A: Would you prefer to order pizza or ___ something?
B: I'd rather ___, actually.
A: It's time we ___ your cousins abroad.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**family** · **rather** · **cook** · **cook** · **called**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Completa el texto

Tom would rather ___ (cook) at home than eat in a noisy restaurant. He would prefer ___ (celebrate) his birthday with close relatives. It is high time they ___ (call) their cousins in Canada. Tom would rather his brother ___ (help) with the decorations.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**cook** · **to celebrate** · **called** · **helped**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Traduce

1. Preferiría quedarme en casa.
2. Preferiría viajar en tren. (would prefer)
3. Ya es hora de que llamemos a nuestros primos.
4. Preferiría que mi hermano llegara temprano.
5. No me gustaría viajar solo/a.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I would rather stay at home.
2. She would prefer to travel by train.
3. It's time we called our cousins.
4. I would rather my brother came early.
5. I would rather not travel alone.
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Escribe tu propio texto

Escribe 8–10 frases sobre tu propia familia. Incluye:

- 2 frases con **would rather + infinitivo**.
- 1 frase con **would rather + sujeto + pasado**.
- 2 frases con **would prefer + to + infinitivo**.
- 2 frases con **it's (high) time + pasado**.
- Al menos 4 palabras de vocabulario de family.

**Modelo:** usa el texto sobre Tom como referencia de estilo.

---

## Tip del profesor

Antes de hablar, pregúntate: ¿estoy expresando **mi** preferencia (would rather + infinitivo), la preferencia sobre **otra persona** (would rather + sujeto + pasado), lo mismo en registro más formal (would prefer + to), o **urgencia** por algo que llevamos posponiendo (it's time + pasado)? Practicar esta clasificación mental antes de construir la frase evita casi todos los errores de esta unidad, especialmente la tentación de añadir *to* después de rather.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Estructura | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| would rather | + infinitivo sin *to* | I would rather shop online. |
| would rather | + sujeto + pasado | I'd rather you came early. |
| would prefer | + to + infinitivo | He would prefer to buy local. |
| it's (high) time | + sujeto + pasado | It's time he got control. |
| Vocabulario | family | sibling, in-laws, gathering... |

# Parte II — Ejercicios

Este artículo incluye también los **ejercicios de la Unidad 7** con soluciones comentadas. Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.
## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** would rather + inf; would rather + subject + past; would prefer; It's time + past

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I would rather ___ at home this year. → *stay / to stay / staying*
2. She would prefer ___ by train. → *travel / to travel / travelling*
3. It is high time we ___ our cousins. → *visit / visited / visiting*
4. I would rather my sister ___ early. → *comes / came / come*
5. He would rather not ___ abroad alone. → *travel / to travel / travelling*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **stay** · 2. **to travel** · 3. **visited** · 4. **came** · 5. **travel**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. Would you rather ___ or fly? → *drive / to drive / driving*
2. I would prefer tea ___ coffee. → *to / than / over*
3. It is about time he ___ a job. → *find / found / finding*
4. She would rather her parents ___ with them. → *stay / stayed / staying*
5. I'd rather you ___ tell anyone yet. → *don't / didn't / not*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **drive** · 2. **to** · 3. **found** · 4. **stayed** · 5. **didn't**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *I would rather to stay home.*
2. *She would prefer travel by bus.*
3. *It is time we leave.*
4. *I would rather my brother comes early.*
5. *Would you rather to cook?*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I would rather **stay** home.
2. She would prefer **to travel** by bus.
3. It is time we **left**.
4. I would rather my brother **came** early.
5. Would you rather **cook**?

</details>

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

**Objetivo:** family

2. gathering → *reunión familiar · vuelo · maleta*

4. decorate → *decorar · cancelar · posponer*

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

## Lección 4 — Listening: Tom on preferences

**Objetivo:** escuchar el foco gramatical en contexto.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-7/listening-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Tom on preferences"></audio>

> Hi, I am Tom. I would rather spend the holiday with my grandparents than fly abroad. I would prefer to stay at home this year. It is high time we visited my aunt — we have not seen her for two years. I would rather my sister came early to help with the cooking.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Who speaks? → *Tom / Leo / Ben*
2. Would rather spend holiday with ___ → *grandparents / boss / strangers*
3. Would prefer to stay ___ → *at home / abroad / at office*
4. It is high time they ___ aunt → *visited / visit / visiting*
5. Not seen aunt for ___ years → *two / ten / zero*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Tom** · 2. **grandparents** · 3. **at home** · 4. **visited** · 5. **two**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Would rather sister came to help with ___ → *cooking / flying / reporting*
7. Rather + bare inf? → *yes / no*
8. Prefer + to? → *yes / no*
9. It's time + past? → *yes / no*
10. Already visited aunt? → *False / True*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **cooking** · 7. **stay** · 8. **to stay** · 9. **visited** · 10. **False**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Write would rather + inf.
12. Write it's time + past.
13. Shadow audio.
14. Family vocab? → *yes / none*
15. Would rather my sister ___
16. Open Ver solución. → *yes*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **Model OK** · 12. **Model OK** · 13. **done** · 14. **grandparents, aunt, sister** · 15. **came** · 16. **yes**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

1. Escribe would rather, would prefer e It's time en contexto familiar.
2. Completa: I would rather ___ (stay) at home.
3. Completa: She would prefer ___ (travel) by train.
4. Completa: It is high time we ___ (visit) our cousins.
5. Completa: I would rather my brother ___ (help) me.
6. Would rather not + inf.
7. Prefer tea ___ coffee.
8. Corrige: *I would rather to cook.*
9. Corrige: *It is time we leave.*
10. Párrafo sobre preferencias familiares.
11. Traduce: Preferiría quedarme en casa.
12. Traduce: Ya es hora de que llamemos a mi tía.
13. I'd rather you didn't…
14. Diálogo en una reunión familiar.
15. Autochequeo: rather (sin to) vs prefer (con to).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Open — three structures in family context.
2. **stay**
3. **to travel**
4. **visited**
5. **helped**
6. I would rather not **go** abroad alone.
7. I would prefer tea **to** coffee.
8. I would rather **stay** at home.
9. It is time we **left**.
10. Open family paragraph.
11. I would rather **stay** at home.
12. It is high time we **called** my aunt.
13. I'd rather you **didn't** drive so fast.
14. Open dialogue.
15. Self-check.

</details>

content:
## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 8 (B2)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Formar mixed conditionals de tipo **pasado → presente** (if + past perfect, would + infinitivo).
- Formar mixed conditionals de tipo **pasado → futuro** con la misma estructura verbal.
- Formar mixed conditionals de tipo **presente → pasado** (if + past simple/were, would have + participio).
- Distinguir un mixed conditional del segundo y del tercer condicional "puros".
- Reconocer mixed conditionals en preguntas y frases negativas.
- Nombrar y usar en contexto vocabulario de **travel**: itinerary, layover, delay, destination y más.

![Esquema de mixed conditionals en inglés B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-conditionals.png)

---

## Gramática: Mixed Conditionals

### 1. Pasado → presente: la combinación más frecuente

El tipo de mixed conditional más común combina una **causa en el pasado** (que ya no se puede cambiar) con un **resultado que se siente ahora, en el presente**. La estructura es **if + past perfect** en la condición y **would + infinitivo** (sin *to*) en el resultado. Por ejemplo, *If he had caught the bus, he would be here now*: no cogió el autobús (pasado), y por eso no está aquí ahora (presente).

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-bus.mp3" title="🔊 pasado → presente: If he had caught the bus, he would be here now"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-booked.mp3" title="🔊 pasado → presente: If we had booked the hotel, we would have a room"></audio>

Fíjate en que el resultado (*would be here*, *would have a room*) describe una situación **actual**, no una acción puntual pasada; por eso no lleva *have + participio*, como sí ocurriría en un tercer condicional puro.

### 2. Pasado → futuro: la misma estructura, resultado futuro

La misma combinación verbal (**if + past perfect**, **would + infinitivo**) también sirve cuando el resultado se proyecta hacia el **futuro cercano**, no solo hacia el presente inmediato. Por ejemplo, *If he had passed the interview, he would start next week*: aprobar la entrevista es un evento pasado (hipotético), pero el resultado — empezar a trabajar — pertenece al futuro.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-interview.mp3" title="🔊 pasado → futuro: If he had passed the interview, he would start next week"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-tickets.mp3" title="🔊 pasado → presente: If we had bought the tickets, we would be attending tonight"></audio>

La clave para reconocer este tipo es preguntarte si el resultado apunta a "ahora" o a "un poco más adelante", en vez de estar completamente terminado en el pasado.

### 3. Presente → pasado: cuando una característica estable explica el pasado

Este tipo, menos frecuente pero igualmente importante para el B2, combina una **condición general y estable del presente** con un **resultado que ya ocurrió (o no ocurrió) en el pasado**. Se forma con **if + past simple / were** en la condición y **would have + participio** en el resultado. Por ejemplo, *If I were taller, I would have joined the basketball team [last year]*: ser alto es una característica que sigue siendo cierta ahora, y explica por qué algo no sucedió en el pasado.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-spanish.mp3" title="🔊 pasado → presente: If I had learned Spanish, I would speak fluently now"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-warning.mp3" title="🔊 presente → pasado: If she were more organised, she would have caught the earlier flight"></audio>

Distingue bien entre esta combinación y la del punto 1: aquí la condición no es un evento puntual del pasado, sino un rasgo o estado que **sigue siendo verdad** en el presente.

### 4. Mixed conditionals en preguntas y frases negativas

Los mixed conditionals mantienen su estructura habitual también en preguntas y negaciones. En preguntas, el orden habitual de would + sujeto se mantiene: *Would you be here now if you had caught the bus?* En negativas, el *not* se coloca junto al verbo correspondiente en cada cláusula: *If we hadn't bought the tickets, we wouldn't be attending tonight*. Practicar estas variantes es importante porque los exámenes B2 suelen pedir transformar frases afirmativas en preguntas o negativas manteniendo el mismo tipo de condicional.

### 5. Cómo no confundir mixed conditionals con el 2.º y el 3.er condicional

La mejor forma de identificar un mixed conditional es fijarte en si **ambas partes de la frase pertenecen al mismo momento temporal** o no. Si la condición y el resultado están completamente en el pasado (*If I had studied, I would have passed*), es un **tercer condicional puro**. Si ambas están en un presente/futuro hipotético (*If I had more time, I would travel more*), es un **segundo condicional puro**. Pero si una parte está en el pasado y la otra en el presente o futuro —o viceversa—, entonces necesitas un **mixed conditional**, combinando los tiempos verbales de cada bloque temporal por separado.

---

## Vocabulario: Travel

![Vocabulario de travel en inglés B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/travel-vocab.png)

| Palabra | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **itinerary** | itinerario | Our itinerary includes three cities in ten days. |
| **layover** | escala | We have a two-hour layover in Madrid. |
| **check-in** | registro / facturación | Check-in opens three hours before the flight. |
| **check-out** | salida (hotel) | Check-out time is 11 a.m. |
| **delay** | retraso | The flight had a two-hour delay. |
| **destination** | destino | Our final destination is Lisbon. |
| **connecting flight** | vuelo de conexión | She missed her connecting flight. |
| **excess baggage** | equipaje de más | They had to pay for excess baggage. |
| **embassy** | embajada | He went to the embassy for a new passport. |
| **forecast** | previsión (del tiempo) | Check the forecast before you pack. |
| **boarding** | embarque | Boarding starts at gate 12. |
| **lounge** | sala VIP | We waited in the airport lounge. |
| **queue** | cola / fila | There was a long queue at security. |
| **souvenir** | recuerdo (de viaje) | I bought a souvenir for my sister. |

Combina este vocabulario con la gramática de mixed conditionals: *If we had checked the forecast, we would have packed differently* o *If the flight weren't delayed, we would be boarding now*.

---

## Errores típicos con mixed conditionals

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| If he caught the bus, he would be here now. | If he **had caught** the bus, he would be here now. | La condición pasada necesita past perfect. |
| If we had booked the hotel, we would have had a room. | If we had booked the hotel, we **would have** a room [now]. | Resultado presente → would + infinitivo, no would have + pp. |
| If I were taller, I would join the team last year. | If I were taller, I **would have joined** the team last year. | Resultado pasado → would have + participio. |
| If he had passed, he would started next week. | If he had passed, he **would start** next week. | Would + infinitivo, sin -ed. |
| If I had learned Spanish, I would spoke fluently now. | If I had learned Spanish, I would **speak** fluently now. | Would + infinitivo, no pasado. |
| If we had bought tickets, we will be attending tonight. | If we had bought tickets, we **would be** attending tonight. | Will no aparece en el resultado condicional. |
| We would be at the beach now if the ferry didn't cancel. | We would be at the beach now if the ferry **hadn't been cancelled**. | La condición pasada exige past perfect (pasivo aquí). |
| If she were more careful, she would avoid the accident. | If she were more careful, she **would have avoided** the accident [yesterday]. | Resultado pasado → would have + participio. |

---

## Reading: Clara's travel troubles

![Escena de travel en contexto en inglés B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/travel-scene.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/reading-u8.mp3" title="🔊 Escucha las frases clave del reading"></audio>

> Travel plans rarely go perfectly, and Clara's latest trip proves it. If she had left the airport lounge earlier, she would be boarding the plane right now instead of running through the terminal. If she had double-checked her passport before leaving home, she would not be waiting at the embassy today to sort out the paperwork. If her partner were better at packing light, they would have avoided the excess baggage fee at check-in — a rule she keeps forgetting every single trip. They would be hiking in the mountains this afternoon if the tour company had not cancelled the excursion due to unexpected snow. Clara admits that most of her travel disasters share the same pattern: small decisions in the past that keep affecting the present. Next time, she promises, she will plan her itinerary a little more carefully — starting with checking the forecast before booking anything at all.

**Comprueba tu comprensión:** ¿por qué está Clara en la embajada? ¿Qué tipo de mixed conditional usa la frase sobre el equipaje de más?

---

## Diálogo: contratiempos en el aeropuerto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/dialogue-u8.mp3" title="🔊 Diálogo: airport mixed conditionals"></audio>

> **A:** Did you hear? He missed the bus this morning.
> **B:** Oh no. If he had caught it, he would be here with us now.
> **A:** Have you booked the hotel yet?
> **B:** Not yet, but if we had booked last week, we would have a room by the pool now.
> **A:** What about the connecting flight?
> **B:** If we had checked the schedule, we wouldn't be waiting in this queue.
> **A:** True. And if I were more organised, I would have printed the boarding passes already.
> **B:** Don't worry, we still have time before boarding.
> **A:** I hope so. If the forecast is right, our flight might be delayed anyway.
> **B:** Then it wouldn't matter if we had rushed or not!

---

## Plan de práctica (10–15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Repasa las tres combinaciones de mixed conditional (pasado→presente, pasado→futuro, presente→pasado) con un ejemplo de cada una.
2. **4 min** — Escucha los seis audios de la sección de gramática y repite cada frase, identificando el tiempo de la condición y del resultado.
3. **4 min** — Lee el texto de Clara y subraya cada mixed conditional; clasifícalo según el tipo.
4. **3–4 min** — Practica el diálogo del aeropuerto y crea dos frases propias sobre un viaje real (o imaginado) que salió mal.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso if + past perfect / would + infinitivo para pasado → presente o futuro.
- [ ] Uso if + past simple (were) / would have + participio para presente → pasado.
- [ ] Distingo el mixed conditional del 2.º y el 3.er condicional puros.
- [ ] Formo correctamente preguntas y negativas con mixed conditionals.
- [ ] Nombro al menos 6 palabras de vocabulario de travel.

---

## Practica en el curso B2

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/practice-u8.mp3" title="🔊 Practica: repite y responde"></audio>

Escucha el audio de práctica y repite cada frase antes de continuar. Después, responde en voz alta: *Is there a decision in the past that still affects your life today? What would be different now if you had made a different choice?* Intenta construir tu respuesta con un mixed conditional completo, no solo con una frase suelta.

---

## Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Pasado → presente

1. If he ___ (catch) the bus, he would be here now.
2. If we ___ (book) the hotel, we would have a room.
3. If I ___ (check) the forecast, I would have the right clothes now.
4. If they ___ (leave) earlier, they would be at the gate already.
5. If she ___ (bring) her passport, she wouldn't be at the embassy now.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **had caught** · 2. **had booked** · 3. **had checked** · 4. **had left** · 5. **had brought**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Presente → pasado

1. If I ___ (be) taller, I would have joined the team.
2. If she ___ (be) more organised, she would have caught the flight.
3. If he ___ (not be) so nervous, he would have spoken up.
4. If we ___ (have) more money, we would have booked business class.
5. If they ___ (like) adventure, they would have gone hiking.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **were** · 2. **were** · 3. **weren't** · 4. **had** · 5. **liked**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Corrige el error

1. *If he caught the bus, he would be here now.*
2. *If we had booked the hotel, we would have had a room.*
3. *If she was organised, she would have caught it.*
4. *If he had booked, he isn't waiting.*
5. *If I am taller, I would have joined.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. If he **had caught** the bus, he would be here now.
2. If we had booked the hotel, we **would have** a room.
3. If she **were** organised, she would have caught it.
4. If he had booked, he **wouldn't be** waiting.
5. If I **were** taller, I would have joined.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Elige la opción correcta

1. If I had checked the forecast, I ___ a raincoat. → *pack / would pack / would have packed*
2. If she ___ more organised, she would have caught the flight. → *is / were / had been*
3. We ___ at the beach now if the ferry hadn't been cancelled. → *are / would be / will be*
4. Mixed: past → present uses ___ in the if-clause. → *past perfect / past simple / will*
5. If he were braver, he ___ asked for help yesterday. → *will / would / would have*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **would have packed** · 2. **were** · 3. **would be** · 4. **past perfect** · 5. **would have**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Vocabulario: empareja

1. layover
2. excess baggage
3. embassy
4. forecast
5. boarding
6. queue

a) previsión del tiempo · b) embajada · c) escala · d) equipaje de más · e) cola/fila · f) embarque

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **d** · 3 → **b** · 4 → **a** · 5 → **f** · 6 → **e**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el diálogo

A: Did you hear? He ___ the bus this morning.
B: If he had caught it, he would be here ___ now.
A: Have you ___ the hotel yet?
B: If we had booked last week, we would have a ___ by the pool.
A: What about the connecting ___?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**missed** · **with us** · **booked** · **room** · **flight**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Completa el texto

If Clara ___ (leave) the lounge earlier, she would be boarding now. If she ___ (check) her passport, she would not be at the embassy today. If her partner ___ (be) better at packing, they would have avoided the excess baggage fee.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**had left** · **had double-checked** · **were**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Traduce

1. Si hubiéramos salido antes, no estaríamos atrapados ahora.
2. Si fuera más alto, habría entrado en el equipo.
3. Si hubiéramos reservado, tendríamos una habitación ahora.
4. Si comprobara el pronóstico, empacaría mejor.
5. Si él hubiera aprobado, empezaría la próxima semana.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. If we had left earlier, we wouldn't be stuck now.
2. If I were taller, I would have joined the team.
3. If we had booked, we would have a room now.
4. If I checked the forecast, I would pack better. *(2.º condicional, no mixed)*
5. If he had passed, he would start next week.
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Mixed vs. 2.º / 3.er condicional puro

Clasifica cada frase: **mixed**, **2.º condicional** o **3.er condicional**.

1. If I had more time, I would travel more.
2. If he had caught the bus, he would be here now.
3. If I had studied, I would have passed the exam.
4. If she were taller, she would have joined the team last year.
5. If we had booked earlier, we would be relaxing on the beach now.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **2.º condicional** (presente hipotético → presente hipotético) · 2. **mixed** (pasado → presente) · 3. **3.er condicional** (pasado → pasado) · 4. **mixed** (presente → pasado) · 5. **mixed** (pasado → presente)
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tu propio texto

Escribe 8–10 frases sobre un viaje (real o imaginario) que no salió como esperabas. Incluye:

- 3 frases con **mixed conditional pasado → presente**.
- 2 frases con **mixed conditional presente → pasado**.
- Al menos 5 palabras de vocabulario de travel.

**Modelo:** usa el texto sobre Clara como referencia de estilo.

---

## Tip del profesor

Para identificar qué tipo de mixed conditional necesitas, dibuja mentalmente una línea de tiempo con dos puntos: el momento de la **causa** y el momento del **resultado**. Si la causa está antes en el tiempo que el resultado, y el resultado es "ahora" o "pronto", usa **had + participio → would + infinitivo**. Si la causa es un rasgo estable que sigue siendo cierto, pero el resultado ya ocurrió en el pasado, usa **past simple/were → would have + participio**. Esta línea de tiempo mental es más fiable que memorizar reglas sueltas.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tipo | If-clause | Resultado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Pasado → presente | past perfect | would + infinitivo | If he had caught the bus, he would be here now. |
| Pasado → futuro | past perfect | would + infinitivo | If he had passed, he would start next week. |
| Presente → pasado | past simple / were | would have + participio | If I were taller, I would have joined. |
| Vocabulario | travel | itinerary, layover, delay... | |

# Parte II — Ejercicios

Este artículo incluye también los **ejercicios de la Unidad 8** con soluciones comentadas. Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.
## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** if + past perfect → would + base (now); if + past simple → would have + pp

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. If we had left earlier, we ___ stuck now. → *aren't / wouldn't be / won't be*
2. If I had checked the forecast, I ___ a raincoat. → *pack / would pack / would have packed*
3. If she ___ more organised, she would have caught the flight. → *is / were / had been*
4. We ___ at the beach now if the ferry hadn't been cancelled. → *are / would be / will be*
5. If he had booked online, he ___ waiting in the queue. → *isn't / wouldn't be / won't be*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **wouldn't be** · 2. **would have packed** · 3. **were** · 4. **would be** · 5. **wouldn't be**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. If I ___ taller, I would have joined the team. → *am / were / had been*
2. If they had taken a taxi, they ___ here by now. → *are / would be / will be*
3. If she ___ the alarm, she wouldn't be late now. → *sets / set / had set*
4. Mixed: past → present uses ___ in the if-clause. → *past perfect / past simple / will*
5. If he were braver, he ___ asked for help yesterday. → *will / would / would have*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **were** · 2. **would be** · 3. **had set** · 4. **past perfect** · 5. **would have**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *If we left earlier, we wouldn't be stuck.* (mixed)
2. *If I checked the forecast, I would pack a coat.*
3. *If she was organised, she would have caught it.*
4. *If he had booked, he isn't waiting.*
5. *If I am taller, I would have joined.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. If we **had left** earlier, we wouldn't be stuck.
2. If I **had checked** the forecast, I **would have packed** a coat.
3. If she **were** organised, she **would have caught** it.
4. If he **had booked**, he **wouldn't be** waiting.
5. If I **were** taller, I **would have joined**.

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

**Objetivo:** travel

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja / elige

1. connecting flight → *vuelo de conexión · beca · tesis*
2. excess baggage → *equipaje de más · ascenso · nómina*
3. embassy → *embajada · aeropuerto · sendero*
4. forecast → *previsión (tiempo) · billete · maleta*
5. cancelled → *cancelado · aprobado · reservado*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **vuelo de conexión** · 2. **equipaje de más** · 3. **embajada** · 4. **previsión (tiempo)** · 5. **cancelado**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

1. boarding ≈ ___ → *embarque / equipaje / pasaporte*
2. lounge ≈ ___ → *sala VIP / calle / bosque*
3. delay ≈ ___ → *retraso / ascenso / beca*
4. mixed conditional ≈ ___ → *mezcla de tiempos condicionales / solo presente*
5. if + past perfect → would + base = ___ → *pasado irreal → presente / futuro real*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **embarque** · 2. **sala VIP** · 3. **retraso** · 4. **mezcla de tiempos condicionales** · 5. **pasado irreal → presente**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — En contexto

11. Usa 3 palabras nuevas en frases con el foco gramatical.
12. Di en voz alta el vocabulario de la unidad.
13. Empareja cada palabra con un ejemplo personal.
14. Revisa la tabla de vocabulario de la [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-8-mixed-conditionals-travel).
15. Continúa en la [Unidad 8 del curso](/curso-b2/unit-8).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11–13. Open answers — check meaning in theory. · 14. Theory vocab section. · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-8**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Clara's travel troubles

**Objetivo:** comprender un texto con el foco de la unidad.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Clara's travel troubles"></audio>

> Travel plans rarely go perfectly. If Clara had left the airport lounge earlier, she would be boarding the plane now. If she had double-checked her passport, she would not be waiting at the embassy today. If her partner were better at packing, they would have avoided the excess baggage fee. They would be hiking in the mountains now if the tour had not been cancelled due to snow.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. If Clara had left lounge earlier, she would be ___ → *boarding / hiking / cooking*
2. If she had checked passport, she wouldn't wait at ___ → *embassy / gym / library*
3. If partner were better at packing, they'd avoid ___ fee → *excess baggage / tuition / scholarship*
4. Would be hiking if tour hadn't been cancelled due to ___ → *snow / sun / wind*
5. Mixed: past perfect → ___ → *present result / past only / zero*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **boarding** · 2. **embassy** · 3. **excess baggage** · 4. **snow** · 5. **present result**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. If she were better at packing = ___ conditional mix → *present → past / past → present*
7. Travel problems? → *yes / none*
8. At the beach now? → *False / True*
9. Underline mixed conditionals.
10. Write If I had…, I would… now.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **present → past** · 7. **passport, queue, cancellation** · 8. **False** · 9. **See text** · 10. **Model OK**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Travel vocab? → *yes / none*
12. Main idea? → *travel / education / family*
13. Second part uses would + ? → *base (now)*
14. Course link → */curso-b2/unit-8*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **boarding, embassy, baggage** · 12. **travel gone wrong** · 13. **base / have + pp** · 14. **/curso-b2/unit-8**

</details>

## Lección 4 — Listening: Clara at the airport

**Objetivo:** escuchar el foco gramatical en contexto.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/listening-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Clara at the airport"></audio>

> Hi, I am Clara. If we had left the hotel earlier, we would not be stuck in traffic now. If I had checked the forecast, I would have packed a raincoat. If she were more organised, she would have caught the connecting flight yesterday. We would be at the beach now if the ferry had not been cancelled.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Who speaks? → *Clara / Olivia / Emma*
2. If had left hotel earlier, wouldn't be stuck in ___ → *traffic / snow / class*
3. If had checked forecast, would have packed ___ → *raincoat / thesis / map*
4. If she were organised, would have caught ___ → *connecting flight / bus / meal*
5. Would be at beach if ferry not ___ → *cancelled / approved / booked*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Clara** · 2. **traffic** · 3. **raincoat** · 4. **connecting flight** · 5. **cancelled**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Mixed conditional focus? → *past → present / only second*
7. Travel context? → *yes / no*
8. At beach now? → *False / True*
9. Write If I had…, I would… now.
10. Write If she were…, she would have…

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **past → present** · 7. **yes** · 8. **False** · 9. **Model OK** · 10. **Model OK**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Shadow audio.
12. Travel vocab? → *yes / none*
13. Past perfect in if-clause? → *yes / no*
14. Open Ver solución. → *yes*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **done** · 12. **traffic, raincoat, ferry** · 13. **yes** · 14. **yes**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

1. Escribe 2 mixed: pasado → presente y presente → pasado.
2. Completa: If we had left earlier, we ___ (not be) stuck now.
3. Completa: If I had checked the forecast, I ___ (pack) a coat.
4. Completa: If she ___ (be) organised, she would have caught the flight.
5. Completa: We ___ (be) at the beach now if the tour hadn't been cancelled.
6. Explica pasado → presente en 1 frase.
7. Corrige: *If we leave early, we wouldn't be stuck.*
8. Corrige: *If I checked the forecast, I would pack a coat.*
9. Párrafo sobre un viaje que salió mal.
10. Traduce: Si hubiéramos salido antes, no estaríamos atrapados.
11. Traduce: Si fuera más alto, habría entrado en el equipo.
12. Usa vocabulario travel: boarding, delay, luggage.
13. Diálogo en el aeropuerto.
14. Autochequeo: tiempos en if y result clauses.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Open — one past→present and one present→past mixed.
2. **wouldn't be**
3. **would have packed**
4. **were**
5. **would be**
6. Past unreal condition → present unreal result.
7. If we **had left** earlier, we wouldn't be stuck.
8. If I **had checked** the forecast, I **would have packed** a coat.
9. Open travel paragraph.
10. If we **had left** earlier, we **wouldn't be** stuck.
11. If I **were** taller, I **would have joined** the team.
12. Open with travel vocabulary.
13. Open airport dialogue.
14. Self-check.

</details>

content:
## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 9 (B2)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Formar cláusulas de participio **-ing** para acciones activas y simultáneas.
- Formar cláusulas de participio **-ed** para significados pasivos.
- Usar **having + past participle** para mostrar que una acción terminó antes que otra.
- Evitar el error del "dangling participle" (participio sin sujeto claro).
- Reconocer participle clauses como reducción de oraciones relativas o subordinadas.
- Nombrar y usar en contexto vocabulario de **environment**: pollution, recycling, sustainable, biodiversity y más.

![Esquema de participle clauses en inglés B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/participle-clauses.png)

---

## Gramática: Participle Clauses

### 1. Cláusulas -ing: cuando el sujeto hace la acción

Cuando el sujeto de la cláusula reducida **realiza** la acción de forma activa y, normalmente, simultánea a la acción principal, usamos el **gerundio (-ing)**. Por ejemplo, *Walking along the beach, he found a shell*: caminar y encontrar la concha ocurren casi al mismo tiempo, y es la misma persona (he) quien hace ambas cosas.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/walking-beach.mp3" title="🔊 -ing: Walking along the beach, he found a shell"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/waiting-train.mp3" title="🔊 -ing: Waiting for the train, she read her book"></audio>

Esta estructura equivale a decir *While he was walking along the beach, he found a shell*, pero de forma mucho más compacta — una de las razones por las que las participle clauses son tan habituales en textos escritos con estilo cuidado.

### 2. Cláusulas -ed: cuando el sujeto recibe la acción

Cuando el significado es **pasivo** — es decir, el sujeto **recibe** la acción en lugar de realizarla — usamos el **participio pasado (-ed** o forma irregular**)**. Por ejemplo, *Disturbed by the news, she couldn't sleep*: ella no molesta a nadie, sino que **es molestada** por la noticia; por eso usamos la forma pasiva -ed, no -ing.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/disturbed-news.mp3" title="🔊 -ed: Disturbed by the news, she couldn't sleep"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/built-bridge.mp3" title="🔊 -ed: The bridge built in 1950 is still in use"></audio>

Este segundo ejemplo, *The bridge built in 1950 is still in use*, muestra otro uso muy común de las cláusulas -ed: como versión reducida de una oración relativa pasiva (*the bridge that was built in 1950*), colocada justo después del sustantivo al que modifica.

### 3. Having + past participle: una acción completada antes que otra

**Having + participio** se usa para mostrar que la acción de la cláusula reducida se **completó antes** de la acción de la cláusula principal — es, en esencia, una versión compacta de *after + past perfect*. Por ejemplo, *Having finished the tasks, we went home* significa lo mismo que *After we had finished the tasks, we went home*, pero con un registro más formal y una estructura más económica.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/having-finished.mp3" title="🔊 Having + pp: Having finished the tasks, we went home"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/having-completed.mp3" title="🔊 Having + pp: Having completed the report, she sent it"></audio>

Esta estructura es especialmente útil para narrar secuencias de acciones en informes, artículos o narraciones, donde queremos dejar clara la relación temporal entre dos eventos sin recurrir a conjunciones repetitivas.

### 4. Participle clauses como reducción de oraciones más largas

Las participle clauses no son una estructura aislada: son, en realidad, una forma **reducida** de oraciones subordinadas más largas que ya conoces. Una cláusula con *because* (*Because she was disturbed by the news, she couldn't sleep*) se puede reducir a una cláusula -ed (*Disturbed by the news, she couldn't sleep*). Una cláusula relativa pasiva (*The bridge that was built in 1950...*) se reduce a una cláusula -ed pospuesta (*The bridge built in 1950...*). Y una cláusula con *after* + past perfect se reduce con having + participio. Entender esta relación te ayuda a producir participle clauses a partir de ideas que ya sabes expresar de forma más larga.

### 5. El error del "dangling participle": mismo sujeto obligatorio

El error más grave con las participle clauses ocurre cuando el sujeto implícito de la cláusula reducida **no coincide** con el sujeto de la cláusula principal, produciendo una frase confusa o incluso cómica sin querer. Por ejemplo, *Walking along the beach, a shell was found* sugiere (incorrectamente) que la concha caminaba por la playa, porque el sujeto gramatical de la oración principal es *a shell*, no la persona que camina. La solución es siempre asegurarte de que el sujeto de la cláusula principal sea también quien realiza (o recibe) la acción de la participle clause: *Walking along the beach, he found a shell*.

---

## Vocabulario: Environment

![Vocabulario de environment en inglés B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/environment-vocab.png)

| Palabra | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **pollution** | contaminación | Air pollution is a serious problem in big cities. |
| **recycling** | reciclaje | Recycling reduces the amount of waste we produce. |
| **sustainable** | sostenible | We need more sustainable transport options. |
| **renewable** | renovable | Solar power is a renewable energy source. |
| **biodiversity** | biodiversidad | The rainforest has incredible biodiversity. |
| **habitat** | hábitat | Deforestation destroys natural habitats. |
| **single-use** | de un solo uso | Many countries are banning single-use plastics. |
| **carbon footprint** | huella de carbono | Flying increases your carbon footprint significantly. |
| **solar panels** | paneles solares | They installed solar panels on the roof. |
| **audit** | auditoría | The energy audit revealed several problems. |
| **volunteer** | voluntario/a | Volunteers collected litter along the river. |
| **litter** | basura tirada | Please don't leave litter on the beach. |
| **eco-friendly** | ecológico | We chose an eco-friendly hotel for our holiday. |
| **conservation** | conservación | The organisation focuses on wildlife conservation. |

Combina este vocabulario con la gramática de participle clauses: *Encouraged by local volunteers, the council installed more recycling bins* o *Having reduced their carbon footprint, the school won an award*.

---

## Errores típicos con participle clauses

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Disturbing by the noise, they protested. | **Disturbed** by the noise, they protested. | Significado pasivo → -ed, no -ing. |
| Walked along the beach, I noticed birds. | **Walking** along the beach, I noticed birds. | Acción activa/simultánea → -ing. |
| Having finish the tasks, we went home. | Having **finished** the tasks, we went home. | Having + participio, no infinitivo. |
| Have finished the report, she sent it. | **Having** finished the report, she sent it. | Se necesita "having", no "have". |
| The bridge building in 1950 is still in use. | The bridge **built** in 1950 is still in use. | Significado pasivo → participio -ed. |
| Walking along the beach, a shell was found. | **Walking along the beach, he found a shell.** | Dangling participle: el sujeto no coincide. |
| Encourage by the reports, the mayor acted. | **Encouraged** by the reports, the mayor acted. | Participio pasado, no infinitivo. |
| Having completed report, she sent it. | Having completed **the** report, she sent it. | No se puede omitir el artículo necesario. |

---

## Reading: Green city action

![Escena de environment en contexto en inglés B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/environment-scene.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/reading-u9.mp3" title="🔊 Escucha las frases clave del reading"></audio>

> Environmental action often starts locally, and Ben's town is a good example. Disturbed by rising pollution levels, citizens demanded cleaner public transport at the last council meeting, and the local government finally listened. Having installed solar panels on the school roof, the head teacher reported that energy bills dropped by almost forty percent within a year. Walking along the river every weekend, a group of volunteers now collects several bags of litter, slowly restoring the local habitat for birds and fish. Encouraged by international reports on biodiversity loss, the mayor promised to ban single-use plastics in all public buildings by next year. Having finished a full environmental audit of the town, experts recommended stricter recycling rules and more investment in renewable energy. None of these changes happened overnight, but together they show how small, connected actions — each one reducing the town's carbon footprint a little more — can add up to something genuinely sustainable.

**Comprueba tu comprensión:** ¿qué tipo de participle clause usa la frase sobre los paneles solares? ¿Y la frase sobre los ciudadanos molestos por la contaminación?

---

## Diálogo: hablando del medio ambiente

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/dialogue-u9.mp3" title="🔊 Diálogo: talking about the environment"></audio>

> **A:** Did you hear about the new recycling scheme?
> **B:** Yes! Encouraged by the results, more schools are joining every month.
> **A:** That's great. Have you finished the audit for our building yet?
> **B:** Having finished it yesterday, I can tell you we waste a lot of energy.
> **A:** I'm not surprised. Walking through the office at night, I always see the lights on.
> **B:** Disturbed by that, I already reported it to the manager.
> **A:** Good. What about the volunteers by the river?
> **B:** Having collected litter every weekend, they say the water looks much cleaner now.
> **A:** Maybe we should join them one Saturday.
> **B:** I'd like that — reducing our carbon footprint starts with small actions, right?

---

## Plan de práctica (10–15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Repasa las tres formas (-ing, -ed, having + participio) con un ejemplo de cada una en voz alta.
2. **4 min** — Escucha los seis audios de la sección de gramática y decide, antes de escuchar la respuesta, si cada cláusula es -ing, -ed o having + participio.
3. **4 min** — Lee el texto sobre la acción medioambiental local y subraya cada participle clause; identifica el sujeto implícito.
4. **3–4 min** — Practica el diálogo y crea dos frases propias sobre el medio ambiente usando -ing y -ed.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso -ing cuando el sujeto realiza la acción.
- [ ] Uso -ed (o forma irregular) cuando el sujeto recibe la acción.
- [ ] Uso having + participio para una acción completada antes que otra.
- [ ] Compruebo que el sujeto de la cláusula reducida coincide con el de la principal.
- [ ] Nombro al menos 6 palabras de vocabulario de environment.

---

## Practica en el curso B2

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/practice-u9.mp3" title="🔊 Practica: repite y responde"></audio>

Escucha el audio de práctica y repite cada frase antes de continuar. Después, responde en voz alta usando una participle clause: *What is one small change you have made (or could make) to reduce your carbon footprint? Describe a moment when you were disturbed or encouraged by some environmental news.*

---

## Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — -ing o -ed

1. ___ by the noise, residents protested. (Disturb)
2. ___ along the river, volunteers collected litter. (Walk)
3. ___ by the results, more schools joined. (Encourage)
4. ___ for the bus, she read the news on her phone. (Wait)
5. The report ___ last year is now out of date. (write)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Disturbed** · 2. **Walking** · 3. **Encouraged** · 4. **Waiting** · 5. **written**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Having + participio

1. ___ (finish) the audit, experts made recommendations.
2. ___ (install) solar panels, the school cut its bills.
3. ___ (complete) the report, she sent it immediately.
4. ___ (plant) hundreds of trees, the council improved air quality.
5. ___ (read) the results, the mayor decided to act.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Having finished** · 2. **Having installed** · 3. **Having completed** · 4. **Having planted** · 5. **Having read**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Corrige el error

1. *Disturbing by noise, they protested.*
2. *Having plant trees, air improved.*
3. *Walked through the park, I noticed birds.*
4. *Encouraging by reports, the mayor acted.*
5. *Having finish the audit, they left.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Disturbed** by noise, they protested.
2. Having **planted** trees, air improved.
3. **Walking** through the park, I noticed birds.
4. **Encouraged** by reports, the mayor acted.
5. Having **finished** the audit, they left.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Elige la opción correcta

1. -ing clause = usually ___ meaning. → *active / passive / past*
2. -ed clause = usually ___ meaning. → *passive / active / future*
3. Having + pp = action ___ the main verb. → *before / after / during*
4. Same ___ in both clauses. → *subject / object / tense*
5. Disturbed by… = cláusula ___ → *-ed / -ing / infinitive*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **active** · 2. **passive** · 3. **before** · 4. **subject** · 5. **-ed**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Vocabulario: empareja

1. pollution
2. sustainable
3. carbon footprint
4. litter
5. biodiversity
6. eco-friendly

a) huella de carbono · b) contaminación · c) sostenible · d) basura tirada · e) ecológico · f) biodiversidad

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **c** · 3 → **a** · 4 → **d** · 5 → **f** · 6 → **e**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el diálogo

A: Did you hear about the new ___ scheme?
B: Encouraged by the results, more schools are ___ every month.
A: Have you finished the ___ for our building?
B: Having finished it, I can tell you we ___ a lot of energy.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**recycling** · **joining** · **audit** · **waste**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Completa el texto

___ by rising pollution levels, citizens demanded cleaner transport. ___ installed solar panels, the school cut its bills. ___ along the river, volunteers collected litter. ___ finished the audit, experts recommended stricter rules.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Disturbed** · **Having** · **Walking** · **Having**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Traduce

1. Al terminar la auditoría, publicaron el informe.
2. Caminando por el río, recogieron basura.
3. Molestos por el ruido, los vecinos protestaron.
4. El puente construido en 1950 sigue en uso.
5. Animados por los resultados, más escuelas se unieron.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Having finished the audit, they published the report.
2. Walking along the river, they collected litter.
3. Disturbed by the noise, the neighbours protested.
4. The bridge built in 1950 is still in use.
5. Encouraged by the results, more schools joined.
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Reescribe usando participle clauses

Reescribe cada frase con una cláusula de participio.

1. Because she was disturbed by the noise, she couldn't concentrate.
2. After we had finished the meeting, we went for lunch.
3. The report that was written last year is now out of date.
4. While he was walking to work, he saw an accident.
5. Because they were encouraged by the good news, they celebrated.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Disturbed by the noise, she couldn't concentrate.
2. Having finished the meeting, we went for lunch.
3. The report written last year is now out of date.
4. Walking to work, he saw an accident.
5. Encouraged by the good news, they celebrated.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tu propio texto

Escribe 8–10 frases sobre una acción medioambiental (real o imaginaria) en tu barrio o ciudad. Incluye:

- 2 frases con **cláusula -ing**.
- 2 frases con **cláusula -ed**.
- 2 frases con **having + participio**.
- Al menos 5 palabras de vocabulario de environment.

**Modelo:** usa el texto de Ben como referencia de estilo.

---

## Tip del profesor

Antes de construir una participle clause, hazte tres preguntas en este orden: primero, **¿el sujeto hace la acción o la recibe?** (activa → -ing; pasiva → -ed). Segundo, **¿la acción reducida ocurrió antes que la principal?** (si es así, usa having + participio). Y tercero, siempre al final, **¿el sujeto de mi cláusula principal es el mismo que el de la cláusula reducida?** Esta última pregunta evita el error más grave de toda la unidad: el dangling participle.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Forma | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **-ing** | activa / simultánea | Walking along the beach, he found a shell. |
| **-ed** | pasiva / causa | Disturbed by the news, she couldn't sleep. |
| **Having + pp** | completada antes | Having finished the tasks, we went home. |
| Vocabulario | environment | pollution, recycling, sustainable... |
