content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 56 del curso A1** (*At the Restaurant*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Restaurante A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-56-restaurante-pedidos)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 56 — At the Restaurant](/curso-a1/unit-56)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![I would like](/blog/curso-a1/unit-56/a1-unit56-polite-orders.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: pedidos educados](#leccion-1--gramatica-pedidos-educados)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: restaurante](#leccion-2--vocabulario-restaurante)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Tonight at a restaurant](#leccion-3--reading-tonight-at-a-restaurant)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Are you ready to order?](#leccion-4--listening-are-you-ready-to-order)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: My order](#leccion-5--writing-my-order)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: pedidos educados

**Objetivo:** *I would like…*, *Can I have…?*, *would like to + verb*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I ____ like the soup please. → *would / will / want*  
2. Can I ____ the bill please? → *have / to have / having*  
3. I would like ____ order a starter. → *to / for / –*  
4. We ____ like to see the menu. → *would / will / can*  
5. For dessert I ____ like ice cream. → *would / will / want*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **would** — *I would like* = forma educada.  
2. **have** — *Can I have…?*  
3. **to** — *would like to* + verbo.  
4. **would**  
5. **would**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige

6. Polite way to order = ____. → a) I would like… · b) I want… · c) Give me…  
7. *Can I have the bill?* = ____. → a) a polite request for the bill · b) order food · c) see the menu  
8. After *would like* we use ____. → a) *to* + verb or a noun · b) verb only · c) *-ing* only  
9. *Starter* = ____. → a) first course before main · b) dessert · c) drink  
10. *Main course* = ____. → a) the main dish of the meal · b) starter · c) dessert

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) I would like…**  
7. **a) a polite request for the bill**  
8. **a) *to* + verb or a noun**  
9. **a) first course before main**  
10. **a) the main dish of the meal**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Ordena

11. I / would like / the / chicken / please.  
12. Can / I / have / the / menu / please?  
13. For / dessert / I would like / ice cream.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. I would like the chicken please.  
12. Can I have the menu please?  
13. For dessert I would like ice cream.

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. *I would like* is more polite than *I want*. → True / False  
15. At a restaurant we say *Can I have the bill?* to pay. → True / False

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **True**  
15. **True**

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: restaurante

**Objetivo:** *menu, starter, main course, dessert, bill, waiter*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige el significado

1. *Menu* = ____. → a) a list of food and drinks · b) the bill · c) the table  
2. *Starter* = ____. → a) first course, e.g. soup or salad · b) main dish · c) dessert  
3. *Main course* = ____. → a) the main dish of the meal · b) starter · c) dessert  
4. *Dessert* = ____. → a) a sweet dish at the end · b) starter · c) drink  
5. *Bill* = ____. → a) the paper showing what you must pay · b) menu · c) starter

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) a list of food and drinks**  
2. **a) first course, e.g. soup or salad**  
3. **a) the main dish of the meal**  
4. **a) a sweet dish at the end**  
5. **a) the paper showing what you must pay**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–7 — Empareja

6. Empareja: menu / starter / main course / dessert / bill → list of dishes · first course · main dish · sweet at end · what you pay  
7. Empareja: soup / chicken / ice cream / waiter / table → often a starter · main course · dessert · serves food · where you sit

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **menu → list of dishes** · **starter → first course** · **main course → main dish** · **dessert → sweet at end** · **bill → what you pay**  
7. **soup → often a starter** · **chicken → main course** · **ice cream → dessert** · **waiter → serves food** · **table → where you sit**

</details>

### Ejercicios 8–13 — Completa / elige

8. Can I see the ____ please? → *menu / bill / dessert*  
9. For ____ I would like soup. → *starter / main course / dessert*  
10. I would like the ____ please. → *bill / menu / starter*  
11. Order of courses: ____. → a) starter, main course, dessert · b) dessert, main, starter · c) main, starter, dessert  
12. *Waiter* = ____. → a) a person who serves food in a restaurant · b) chef · c) customer  
13. To pay at a restaurant you ask for ____. → a) the bill · b) the menu · c) the starter

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

8. **menu**  
9. **starter**  
10. **bill**  
11. **a) starter, main course, dessert**  
12. **a) a person who serves food in a restaurant**  
13. **a) the bill**

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. Dessert comes after the main course. → True / False  
15. The menu shows what food you can order. → True / False

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **True**  
15. **True**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Tonight at a restaurant

**Objetivo:** leer sobre una comida en el restaurante.

### Texto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-56/reading-restaurant.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Tonight at a restaurant"></audio>

> We are at a restaurant tonight. The waiter brings the menu. I would like a soup for starter. My friend wants salad. For main course I order chicken and rice. We have water to drink. After dinner we would like dessert. I have ice cream. Then we ask for the bill and pay.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. Where are they tonight? → a) At a restaurant · b) At home · c) At a cafe  
2. What does the waiter bring? → a) The menu · b) The bill · c) The food  
3. What starter does the writer want? → a) Soup · b) Salad · c) Chicken  
4. What main course does he/she order? → a) Chicken and rice · b) Soup · c) Ice cream  
5. What do they drink? → a) Water · b) Coffee · c) Juice

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) At a restaurant**  
2. **a) The menu**  
3. **a) Soup**  
4. **a) Chicken and rice**  
5. **a) Water**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Comprensión

6. What dessert does the writer have? → a) Ice cream · b) Salad · c) Soup  
7. After dessert they ____. → a) ask for the bill and pay · b) order more food · c) leave without paying  
8. *Starter* means ____. → a) first course · b) main dish · c) dessert  
9. *Bill* means ____. → a) what you pay · b) menu · c) starter  
10. *I would like* means ____. → a) a polite way to order · b) I want now · c) give me

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) Ice cream**  
7. **a) ask for the bill and pay**  
8. **a) first course**  
9. **a) what you pay**  
10. **a) a polite way to order**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Detalles

11. The text is about ____. → a) a meal at a restaurant · b) cooking at home · c) a supermarket  
12. *Main course* means ____. → a) main dish · b) starter · c) dessert  
13. Who wants salad for starter? → a) The friend · b) The writer · c) The waiter  
14. *Dessert* means ____. → a) sweet at the end of the meal · b) starter · c) drink  
15. What is the order of the meal? → a) Starter, main course, dessert · b) Dessert, main, starter · c) Main, bill, dessert

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) a meal at a restaurant**  
12. **a) main dish**  
13. **a) The friend**  
14. **a) sweet at the end of the meal**  
15. **a) Starter, main course, dessert**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Are you ready to order?

**Objetivo:** escuchar un diálogo de pedido en el restaurante.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-56/listening-restaurant.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Are you ready to order?"></audio>

> **Waiter:** Are you ready to order?  
> **Customer:** Yes. I would like the soup for starter please.  
> **Waiter:** And for main course?  
> **Customer:** I would like the fish please.  
> **Waiter:** Anything to drink?  
> **Customer:** Water please.  
> **Waiter:** Dessert?  
> **Customer:** No thank you. Can I have the bill please?  
> **Waiter:** Of course.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. What does the customer order for starter? → a) Soup · b) Salad · c) Fish  
2. What main course does the customer want? → a) Fish · b) Chicken · c) Soup  
3. What does the customer drink? → a) Water · b) Coffee · c) Wine  
4. Does the customer want dessert? → a) No · b) Yes · c) The dialogue doesn't say  
5. What does the customer ask for at the end? → a) The bill · b) The menu · c) More water

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Soup**  
2. **a) Fish**  
3. **a) Water**  
4. **a) No**  
5. **a) The bill**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. *I would like* means ____. → a) a polite way to order · b) I want now · c) give me  
7. *Starter* means ____. → a) first course · b) main course · c) dessert  
8. The dialogue is at ____. → a) a restaurant · b) a cafe · c) home  
9. *Can I have the bill?* means ____. → a) a request to pay · b) order food · c) ask for the menu  
10. *Main course* means ____. → a) main dish · b) starter · c) dessert

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) a polite way to order**  
7. **a) first course**  
8. **a) a restaurant**  
9. **a) a request to pay**  
10. **a) main dish**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Who says *Are you ready to order?* → a) The waiter · b) The customer · c) Both  
12. *Bill* means ____. → a) what you pay · b) menu · c) starter  
13. *Of course* means ____. → a) yes, certainly · b) no · c) maybe  
14. *Dessert* means ____. → a) sweet at the end · b) starter · c) drink  
15. The dialogue is about ____. → a) ordering food and asking for the bill · b) cooking at home · c) buying at the supermarket

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) The waiter**  
12. **a) what you pay**  
13. **a) yes, certainly**  
14. **a) sweet at the end**  
15. **a) ordering food and asking for the bill**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: My order

**Objetivo:** escribir pedidos educados en el restaurante.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I ____ like the soup please. → *would / will / want*  
2. Can I ____ the bill? → *have / to have / having*  
3. For ____ I would like salad. → *starter / main course / dessert*  
4. We would like ____ see the menu. → *to / for / –*  
5. For dessert I ____ like ice cream. → *would / will / can*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **would**  
2. **have**  
3. **starter**  
4. **to**  
5. **would**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. I / would like / the / chicken / please.  
7. Can / I / have / the / menu / please?  
8. For / dessert / I would like / ice cream.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. I would like the chicken please.  
7. Can I have the menu please?  
8. For dessert I would like ice cream.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Pedir la carta de forma educada.  
10. Qué quisieras de entrante (*I would like…*).  
11. Dos frases: plato principal y postre.  
12. Pedir la cuenta de forma educada.  
13. Párrafo corto (3–4 frases): pedido completo.  
14. Diferencia *I want* e *I would like* en 2–3 frases.  
15. Diálogo corto: carta → platos → cuenta.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. Can I have the menu please?  
10. I would like the soup for starter please.  
11. For main course I would like the fish. For dessert I would like ice cream.  
12. Can I have the bill please?  
13. I would like the soup for starter. For main course I would like the chicken. Water please. Can I have the bill please?  
14. I would like is more polite than I want. At a restaurant we say I would like the soup please.  
15. Customer: Can I have the menu please? Waiter: Here you are. Customer: I would like the chicken and the bill please.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **I would like** | I **would like** the soup please. |
| **Can I have…?** | Can I **have** the bill please? |
| **starter / main / dessert** | soup → chicken → ice cream |
| **menu / bill** | Can I see the **menu**? / the **bill** |
| **waiter** | The **waiter** brings the menu. |

---

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 57 del curso A1** (*Cooking & Recipes*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Cocina A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-57-cocina-recetas)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 57 — Cooking & Recipes](/curso-a1/unit-57)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![First Then Finally](/blog/curso-a1/unit-57/a1-unit57-first-then-finally.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: First, Then, Finally](#leccion-1--gramatica-first-then-finally)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: cocina y recetas](#leccion-2--vocabulario-cocina-y-recetas)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Today I cook pasta](#leccion-3--reading-today-i-cook-pasta)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Wash the vegetables](#leccion-4--listening-wash-the-vegetables)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: My recipe](#leccion-5--writing-my-recipe)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: First, Then, Finally

**Objetivo:** secuenciadores e imperativos en recetas.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. ____ cut the vegetables. → *First / Finally / Mix*  
2. First cut. ____ mix the ingredients. → *Then / Finally / Bake*  
3. Then fry the onion. ____ add the salt. → *Finally / First / Cut*  
4. ____ boil the water. → *First / Finally / Mix*  
5. First mix. ____ bake for twenty minutes. → *Then / First / Cut*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **First** — primer paso.  
2. **Then** — paso siguiente.  
3. **Finally** — último paso.  
4. **First**  
5. **Then**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige

6. Correct order = ____. → a) First, Then, Finally · b) Finally, Then, First · c) Then, First, Finally  
7. Recipe instructions use ____. → a) imperative (base verb) · b) *to* + verb · c) *-ing* only  
8. *Finally* means ____. → a) last step · b) first step · c) never  
9. *First boil the water* is ____. → a) correct · b) needs *to* · c) needs subject *you*  
10. After *Then* we often use ____. → a) a base verb · b) *to* + verb · c) *will*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) First, Then, Finally**  
7. **a) imperative (base verb)**  
8. **a) last step**  
9. **a) correct**  
10. **a) a base verb**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

11. *Finally cut the vegetables. First bake.* (ordena)  
12. *To mix the eggs.* (imperativo)  
13. *You should to boil the water.* → usa imperativo de receta  
14. *Then first add salt.*  
15. *Bake the onion in a pan.* (elige el verbo correcto)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **First** cut the vegetables. **Finally** bake.  
12. **Mix** the eggs.  
13. **Boil** the water.  
14. **Then** add salt. / **First** add salt.  
15. **Fry** the onion in a pan.

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: cocina y recetas

**Objetivo:** *cut, mix, fry, boil, bake* + *pan, pot, oven, recipe, ingredients*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja

1. cut  
2. mix  
3. fry  
4. boil  
5. bake  

a) cook in hot oil in a pan · b) cook in the oven · c) use a knife · d) combine ingredients · e) cook in hot water

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **d** · 3 → **a** · 4 → **e** · 5 → **b**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

6. Use a ____ to fry onions. → *pan / pot / oven*  
7. Boil water in a ____. → *pot / oven / knife*  
8. Bake bread in the ____. → *oven / pan / pot*  
9. A ____ is a list of steps. → *recipe / pan / salt*  
10. ____ are what you need for a recipe. → *Ingredients / Ovens / Finally*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **pan**  
7. **pot**  
8. **oven**  
9. **recipe**  
10. **Ingredients**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Elige

11. Fry = ____. → a) cook in oil in a pan · b) cook in the oven · c) cut  
12. Boil = ____. → a) cook in hot water · b) mix · c) bake  
13. Bake = ____. → a) cook in the oven · b) fry · c) cut  
14. *Knife* goes with ____. → a) cut · b) bake · c) boil  
15. *Serve* means ____. → a) put food on a plate for people · b) cut · c) boil

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) cook in oil in a pan**  
12. **a) cook in hot water**  
13. **a) cook in the oven**  
14. **a) cut**  
15. **a) put food on a plate for people**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Today I cook pasta

**Objetivo:** leer una receta simple con secuenciadores.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-57/reading-cooking.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Today I cook pasta"></audio>

> Today I cook pasta. First, I boil water. Then I put the pasta in the water. Next, I cook the sauce. After that, I mix the pasta and the sauce. Finally, I eat it. It is delicious!

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. What does the person cook? → a) Pasta · b) Bread · c) Eggs  
2. What is the first step? → a) Boil water · b) Eat · c) Mix the sauce  
3. When does the person mix pasta and sauce? → a) After cooking the sauce · b) First · c) Never  
4. What is the last step? → a) Eat it · b) Boil water · c) Cut tomatoes  
5. Is the pasta delicious? → a) Yes · b) No · c) The text doesn't say

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Pasta**  
2. **a) Boil water**  
3. **a) After cooking the sauce**  
4. **a) Eat it**  
5. **a) Yes**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. *First* appears with ____. → a) boil water · b) eat · c) mix  
7. *Finally* appears with ____. → a) eat it · b) boil · c) put pasta  
8. *Next* and *After that* mean something like ____. → a) Then · b) First · c) Never  
9. The person puts pasta ____. → a) in the water · b) in the oven · c) in a pan with oil  
10. The main topic is ____. → a) cooking pasta step by step · b) a restaurant · c) a supermarket

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) boil water**  
7. **a) eat it**  
8. **a) Then**  
9. **a) in the water**  
10. **a) cooking pasta step by step**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *Boil* here means ____. → a) cook in hot water · b) fry · c) bake  
12. *Mix* means ____. → a) combine · b) cut · c) serve only  
13. *Finally* = ____. → a) last · b) first · c) never  
14. Imperative example from recipes = ____. → a) Boil the water · b) I am boiling · c) To boil  
15. The text uses sequence words like ____. → a) First, Then, Next, Finally · b) only Finally · c) only because

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) cook in hot water**  
12. **a) combine**  
13. **a) last**  
14. **a) Boil the water**  
15. **a) First, Then, Next, Finally**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Wash the vegetables

**Objetivo:** escuchar pasos de una receta.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-57/listening-cooking.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Wash the vegetables"></audio>

> First, wash the vegetables. Then, cut them. Next, put oil in the pan. After that, cook the vegetables. Finally, add salt.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. What is the first step? → a) Wash the vegetables · b) Add salt · c) Put oil  
2. What do you do after washing? → a) Cut them · b) Eat them · c) Bake them  
3. Where do you put the oil? → a) In the pan · b) In the oven · c) In a pot  
4. What is the last step? → a) Add salt · b) Wash · c) Cut  
5. Do you cook the vegetables? → a) Yes · b) No · c) The audio doesn't say

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Wash the vegetables**  
2. **a) Cut them**  
3. **a) In the pan**  
4. **a) Add salt**  
5. **a) Yes**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. *Cut* comes ____ washing. → a) after · b) before · c) never  
7. *Finally* is used with ____. → a) add salt · b) wash · c) put oil  
8. The cooking happens ____. → a) in a pan · b) in the oven · c) in water only  
9. *Next* and *After that* are like ____. → a) Then · b) First · c) Finally only  
10. The listening is about ____. → a) cooking vegetables · b) ordering food · c) buying clothes

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) after**  
7. **a) add salt**  
8. **a) in a pan**  
9. **a) Then**  
10. **a) cooking vegetables**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *Wash* is ____. → a) an imperative · b) past tense · c) a noun  
12. *Pan* goes with ____. → a) fry / cook with oil · b) bake · c) only boil  
13. *Add salt* = ____. → a) put salt in the food · b) cut salt · c) boil salt  
14. *Vegetables* are ____. → a) ingredients · b) ovens · c) recipes  
15. Correct order starts with ____. → a) First · b) Finally · c) After that

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) an imperative**  
12. **a) fry / cook with oil**  
13. **a) put salt in the food**  
14. **a) ingredients**  
15. **a) First**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: My recipe

**Objetivo:** escribir una receta corta con secuenciadores y verbos de cocina.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. ____ cut the onions. → *First / Finally / Oven*  
2. Then ____ the eggs and flour. → *mix / pan / recipe*  
3. ____ the water in a pot. → *Boil / Bake / Cut*  
4. ____ the cake in the oven. → *Bake / Fry / Boil*  
5. ____ add salt and serve. → *Finally / First / Knife*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **First**  
2. **mix**  
3. **Boil**  
4. **Bake**  
5. **Finally**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. First / boil / the water.  
7. Then / mix / the ingredients.  
8. Finally / bake / for twenty minutes.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. First boil the water.  
7. Then mix the ingredients.  
8. Finally bake for twenty minutes.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Primero corta las verduras.  
10. Luego mezcla los ingredientes.  
11. Finalmente hornea durante veinte minutos.  
12. Primero hierve el agua. Luego fríe la cebolla.  
13. Párrafo corto (4–6 frases): pasta o verduras con *First / Then / Finally*.  
14. Usa *pan* o *pot* o *oven* en una frase.  
15. Termina con *serve* o *eat*.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. First cut the vegetables.  
10. Then mix the ingredients.  
11. Finally bake for twenty minutes.  
12. First boil the water. Then fry the onion.  
13. First boil water in a pot. Then add the pasta. Next cook the sauce. Finally mix and serve.  
14. Fry the onion in a pan. / Bake the bread in the oven.  
15. Finally serve on a plate. / Finally eat it.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **First** | First **cut** the vegetables. |
| **Then** | Then **mix** the ingredients. |
| **Finally** | Finally **bake** for twenty minutes. |
| **Verbos** | cut · mix · fry · boil · bake |
| **Herramientas** | pan · pot · oven |

---

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 58 del curso A1** (*Health & Illness*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Salud A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-58-salud-should)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 58 — Health & Illness](/curso-a1/unit-58)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![should / shouldn't](/blog/curso-a1/unit-58/a1-unit58-should-shouldnt.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: should / shouldn't](#leccion-1--gramatica-should--shouldnt)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: salud y farmacia](#leccion-2--vocabulario-salud-y-farmacia)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: I feel ill today](#leccion-3--reading-i-feel-ill-today)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: I have a bad headache](#leccion-4--listening-i-have-a-bad-headache)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: Advice for a friend](#leccion-5--writing-advice-for-a-friend)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: should / shouldn't

**Objetivo:** consejos con *should / shouldn't* + verbo base.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. You ____ see a doctor if you have a fever. → *should / shouldn't / to*  
2. You ____ go to work if you are very ill. → *shouldn't / should / must to*  
3. He ____ go to the pharmacy for medicine. → *should / shouldn't / to*  
4. You should ____ a lot of water. → *drink / to drink / drinking*  
5. You shouldn't ____ on the computer all day. → *work / to work / working*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **should** — consejo.  
2. **shouldn't** — consejo negativo.  
3. **should**  
4. **drink** — *should* + verbo base (sin *to*).  
5. **work** — *shouldn't* + verbo base.

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige

6. *Should* is used for ____. → a) advice · b) past facts · c) only questions about food  
7. After *should* we use ____. → a) base verb · b) *to* + verb · c) *-ing* only  
8. *You shouldn't go* is ____. → a) correct · b) needs *to* · c) needs *-s*  
9. *He shoulds rest* is ____. → a) wrong (*should* has no *-s*) · b) correct · c) past tense  
10. *You should to rest* is ____. → a) wrong · b) correct · c) better than *should rest*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) advice**  
7. **a) base verb**  
8. **a) correct**  
9. **a) wrong (*should* has no *-s*)**  
10. **a) wrong**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

11. *You should to rest.*  
12. *He shoulds see a doctor.*  
13. *You shouldn't to go to work.*  
14. *I have headache.*  
15. *Go to pharmacy.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. You should **rest**.  
12. He **should** see a doctor.  
13. You shouldn't **go** to work.  
14. I have **a** headache.  
15. Go to **the** pharmacy.

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: salud y farmacia

**Objetivo:** *headache, fever, cold, medicine, pharmacy, doctor, rest, ill*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja

1. headache  
2. fever  
3. cold  
4. pharmacy  
5. medicine  

a) place to buy medicine · b) pain in your head · c) something you take when ill · d) high body temperature · e) illness with cough / runny nose

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **d** · 3 → **e** · 4 → **a** · 5 → **c**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

6. I have a ____. (dolor de cabeza) → *headache / fever / pharmacy*  
7. I have a ____. (fiebre) → *fever / cut / oven*  
8. I think I have a ____. (resfriado) → *cold / pan / bill*  
9. Buy medicine at the ____. → *pharmacy / restaurant / oven*  
10. You should ____ at home. → *rest / fry / bake*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **headache**  
7. **fever**  
8. **cold**  
9. **pharmacy**  
10. **rest**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Elige

11. *Ill / sick* means ____. → a) not well · b) hungry · c) happy  
12. *Doctor* = ____. → a) a person who helps when you are ill · b) a chef · c) a waiter  
13. *Pill* is a type of ____. → a) medicine · b) food · c) clothes  
14. *I feel ill* = ____. → a) I don't feel well · b) I am hungry · c) I am at work  
15. *See a doctor* means ____. → a) visit a doctor · b) buy clothes · c) cook pasta

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) not well**  
12. **a) a person who helps when you are ill**  
13. **a) medicine**  
14. **a) I don't feel well**  
15. **a) visit a doctor**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: I feel ill today

**Objetivo:** leer un texto con síntomas y consejos.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-58/reading-health.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: I feel ill today"></audio>

> I feel ill today. I have a headache and a slight fever. I think I have a cold. I should rest at home and drink a lot of water. I should take some medicine from the pharmacy. I shouldn't go to work today. If the fever gets worse I should see a doctor.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. How does the person feel? → a) Ill · b) Great · c) Hungry  
2. What symptoms does the person have? → a) Headache and slight fever · b) Only a cough · c) No symptoms  
3. What does the person think they have? → a) A cold · b) A broken leg · c) Nothing  
4. Should the person go to work? → a) No · b) Yes · c) The text doesn't say  
5. When should they see a doctor? → a) If the fever gets worse · b) Never · c) Only for food

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Ill**  
2. **a) Headache and slight fever**  
3. **a) A cold**  
4. **a) No**  
5. **a) If the fever gets worse**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. The person should ____ at home. → a) rest · b) work · c) fry  
7. Medicine comes from the ____. → a) pharmacy · b) bakery · c) cinema  
8. The person should drink ____. → a) a lot of water · b) oil · c) coffee only  
9. *Slight fever* means ____. → a) a little fever · b) no fever · c) a big party  
10. The main topic is ____. → a) feeling ill and what you should do · b) cooking · c) shopping

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) rest**  
7. **a) pharmacy**  
8. **a) a lot of water**  
9. **a) a little fever**  
10. **a) feeling ill and what you should do**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *I have a headache* needs ____. → a) *a* · b) no article · c) *the* only  
12. *Should* is followed by ____. → a) base verb · b) *to* + verb · c) past  
13. *Shouldn't go* is ____. → a) correct · b) needs *to* · c) wrong  
14. *Take some medicine* means ____. → a) use medicine · b) cook medicine · c) sell medicine  
15. *See a doctor* = ____. → a) visit a doctor · b) phone a chef · c) go shopping

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) *a***  
12. **a) base verb**  
13. **a) correct**  
14. **a) use medicine**  
15. **a) visit a doctor**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: I have a bad headache

**Objetivo:** escuchar un diálogo de salud y consejos.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-58/listening-health.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: I have a bad headache"></audio>

> **A:** I have a bad headache.  
> **B:** You should take some medicine.  
> **A:** Where can I get it?  
> **B:** At the pharmacy. Or if you have a fever you should see a doctor.  
> **A:** I don't have a fever. Just a headache.  
> **B:** Then you should rest and drink water. You shouldn't work on the computer all day.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. What is A's problem? → a) A bad headache · b) A broken arm · c) No problem  
2. What does B suggest first? → a) Take some medicine · b) Go to work · c) Cook pasta  
3. Where can A get medicine? → a) At the pharmacy · b) At the cinema · c) At school  
4. Does A have a fever? → a) No · b) Yes · c) The dialogue doesn't say  
5. Should A work on the computer all day? → a) No · b) Yes · c) Only at night

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) A bad headache**  
2. **a) Take some medicine**  
3. **a) At the pharmacy**  
4. **a) No**  
5. **a) No**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. If you have a fever you should ____. → a) see a doctor · b) fry onions · c) buy clothes  
7. B also says A should ____. → a) rest and drink water · b) run a marathon · c) bake bread  
8. *Bad headache* means ____. → a) a strong headache · b) no pain · c) a cold only  
9. The dialogue is about ____. → a) health advice · b) a restaurant order · c) a recipe  
10. *Shouldn't* appears with ____. → a) work on the computer · b) take medicine · c) rest

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) see a doctor**  
7. **a) rest and drink water**  
8. **a) a strong headache**  
9. **a) health advice**  
10. **a) work on the computer**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *You should take* uses ____. → a) base verb · b) *to take* · c) *taking* only  
12. *Pharmacy* is where you buy ____. → a) medicine · b) tickets · c) shoes  
13. *Just a headache* means ____. → a) only a headache · b) fever and cold · c) nothing  
14. *Rest* means ____. → a) relax / not work hard · b) cook · c) pay  
15. The dialogue practices ____. → a) should / shouldn't · b) First / Then / Finally · c) too / enough

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) base verb**  
12. **a) medicine**  
13. **a) only a headache**  
14. **a) relax / not work hard**  
15. **a) should / shouldn't**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: Advice for a friend

**Objetivo:** escribir consejos de salud con *should / shouldn't*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. You ____ rest at home. → *should / shouldn't / to*  
2. You ____ go to work today. → *shouldn't / should / must to*  
3. I have ____ headache. → *a / – / the*  
4. Go to ____ pharmacy. → *the / – / a*  
5. You should ____ some medicine. → *take / to take / taking*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **should**  
2. **shouldn't**  
3. **a**  
4. **the**  
5. **take**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. You / should / see / a doctor.  
7. You / shouldn't / go / to work.  
8. I / have / a / fever.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. You should see a doctor.  
7. You shouldn't go to work.  
8. I have a fever.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Tienes dolor de cabeza: consejo con *should*.  
10. Estás enfermo: no vayas al trabajo (*shouldn't*).  
11. Pregunta dónde comprar medicina.  
12. Di que debes beber agua y descansar.  
13. Párrafo corto (4–6 frases): síntomas + *should* / *shouldn't*.  
14. Usa *pharmacy* y *doctor* en dos frases.  
15. Si la fiebre empeora, ve al médico.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. You should take some medicine. / You should rest.  
10. You shouldn't go to work.  
11. Where can I get medicine? / Where is the pharmacy?  
12. You should drink water and rest.  
13. I feel ill. I have a headache and a cold. I should rest at home. I should take medicine. I shouldn't go to work.  
14. Go to the pharmacy for medicine. You should see a doctor.  
15. If the fever gets worse, you should see a doctor.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **should + base** | You should **rest**. |
| **shouldn't + base** | You shouldn't **go** to work. |
| **síntomas** | a headache · a fever · a cold |
| **ayuda** | medicine · pharmacy · doctor · rest |

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 59 del curso A1** (*Money & Currency*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Dinero A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-59-dinero-pay-for-spend-on)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 59 — Money & Currency](/curso-a1/unit-59)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![pay for / spend on](/blog/curso-a1/unit-59/a1-unit59-pay-spend.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: pay for / spend on](#leccion-1--gramatica-pay-for--spend-on)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: dinero y caja](#leccion-2--vocabulario-dinero-y-caja)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: When I go shopping](#leccion-3--reading-when-i-go-shopping)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: That is twenty pounds please](#leccion-4--listening-that-is-twenty-pounds-please)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: My purchase](#leccion-5--writing-my-purchase)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: pay for / spend on

**Objetivo:** *pay for*, *spend on*, *paid*, *spent*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I paid ____ the dinner with cash. → *for / on / to*  
2. She spends money ____ clothes. → *on / for / at*  
3. We ____ too much on food last month. → *spent / spend / paid*  
4. Yesterday I ____ for the book. → *paid / payed / spent*  
5. Can I ____ for this with credit card? → *pay / spend / change*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **for** — *pay for* + cosa.  
2. **on** — *spend on* + categoría.  
3. **spent** — pasado de *spend*.  
4. **paid** — pasado de *pay* (no *payed*).  
5. **pay**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige

6. *Pay for* = ____. → a) pay for a specific thing · b) spend in a category · c) get change only  
7. *Spend on* = ____. → a) use money on a category · b) only ask for receipt · c) cook  
8. Past of *pay* = ____. → a) paid · b) payed · c) paying  
9. Past of *spend* = ____. → a) spent · b) spended · c) spend  
10. *I paid on the coffee* is ____. → a) wrong (*pay for*) · b) correct · c) better

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) pay for a specific thing**  
7. **a) use money on a category**  
8. **a) paid**  
9. **a) spent**  
10. **a) wrong (*pay for*)**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

11. *I paid on the coffee.*  
12. *She spends money for books.*  
13. *I payed for dinner.*  
14. *We spended too much.*  
15. *Can I to pay with card?*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. I paid **for** the coffee.  
12. She spends money **on** books.  
13. I **paid** for dinner.  
14. We **spent** too much.  
15. Can I **pay** with card?

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: dinero y caja

**Objetivo:** *cash, credit card, change, receipt, pounds*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja

1. cash  
2. credit card  
3. change  
4. receipt  
5. pounds  

a) paper proof of payment · b) money back when you pay more · c) plastic card to pay · d) British money · e) notes and coins

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **e** · 2 → **c** · 3 → **b** · 4 → **a** · 5 → **d**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

6. I prefer to pay with ____. → *cash / receipt / spend*  
7. Can I pay with ____ card? → *credit / change / boil*  
8. Here is your ____ — ten pounds. → *change / recipe / fever*  
9. Can I have the ____ please? → *receipt / pan / cold*  
10. That is twenty ____ please. → *pounds / pharmacies / ovens*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **cash**  
7. **credit**  
8. **change**  
9. **receipt**  
10. **pounds**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Elige

11. *Change* in a shop = ____. → a) money you get back · b) clothes size · c) a recipe  
12. *Receipt* = ____. → a) proof of payment · b) medicine · c) a starter  
13. *Cash or card?* asks about ____. → a) payment method · b) food · c) health  
14. *Shop assistant* = ____. → a) person who works in a shop · b) doctor · c) chef  
15. *Note* (twenty-pound note) = ____. → a) paper money · b) a recipe · c) a cold

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) money you get back**  
12. **a) proof of payment**  
13. **a) payment method**  
14. **a) person who works in a shop**  
15. **a) paper money**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: When I go shopping

**Objetivo:** leer un texto sobre compras y pago.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-59/reading-money.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: When I go shopping"></audio>

> When I go shopping I usually take both cash and my credit card. Yesterday I bought a book for ten pounds. I paid for it with cash. The total was ten pounds so I gave a twenty-pound note. The shop assistant gave me my change — ten pounds back — and a receipt. I spend a lot of money on books every month.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. What did the person buy yesterday? → a) A book · b) Clothes · c) Medicine  
2. How much was the book? → a) Ten pounds · b) Twenty pounds · c) Thirty pounds  
3. How did they pay? → a) With cash · b) Only with credit card · c) They didn't pay  
4. How much change did they get? → a) Ten pounds · b) Twenty pounds · c) No change  
5. What do they spend money on every month? → a) Books · b) Cars · c) Only food

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) A book**  
2. **a) Ten pounds**  
3. **a) With cash**  
4. **a) Ten pounds**  
5. **a) Books**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. They usually take ____. → a) cash and credit card · b) only receipts · c) only change  
7. They gave a ____ note. → a) twenty-pound · b) five-pound · c) fifty-pound  
8. The shop assistant gave ____. → a) change and a receipt · b) only medicine · c) pasta  
9. *Paid for* appears with ____. → a) the book / it · b) clothes only · c) fever  
10. The main topic is ____. → a) shopping and paying · b) cooking · c) health advice

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) cash and credit card**  
7. **a) twenty-pound**  
8. **a) change and a receipt**  
9. **a) the book / it**  
10. **a) shopping and paying**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *I paid for it* uses ____. → a) *pay for* in the past · b) *spend on* · c) *should*  
12. *I spend … on books* uses ____. → a) *spend on* · b) *pay for* only · c) *too*  
13. *Change* here means ____. → a) money back · b) clothes · c) recipe  
14. *Receipt* means ____. → a) proof of payment · b) headache · c) starter  
15. Past of *buy* in the text idea = ____. → a) bought · b) buyed · c) buys

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) *pay for* in the past**  
12. **a) *spend on***  
13. **a) money back**  
14. **a) proof of payment**  
15. **a) bought**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: That is twenty pounds please

**Objetivo:** escuchar un diálogo en la caja.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-59/listening-money.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: That is twenty pounds please"></audio>

> **Shop assistant:** That is twenty pounds please.  
> **Customer:** Can I pay for this with credit card?  
> **Shop assistant:** Yes of course.  
> **Customer:** I prefer to pay with cash. Here you are.  
> **Shop assistant:** You gave me thirty pounds. Here is your change — ten pounds — and your receipt.  
> **Customer:** Thank you.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. How much is the total? → a) Twenty pounds · b) Ten pounds · c) Thirty pounds  
2. Does the shop take credit card? → a) Yes · b) No · c) The dialogue doesn't say  
3. How does the customer prefer to pay? → a) With cash · b) Only with card · c) Not at all  
4. How much did the customer give? → a) Thirty pounds · b) Twenty pounds · c) Ten pounds  
5. How much change does the customer get? → a) Ten pounds · b) Twenty pounds · c) Thirty pounds

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Twenty pounds**  
2. **a) Yes**  
3. **a) With cash**  
4. **a) Thirty pounds**  
5. **a) Ten pounds**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. The customer also gets a ____. → a) receipt · b) fever · c) recipe  
7. *Pay for this* means ____. → a) pay for this thing · b) spend on clothes in general · c) rest  
8. The dialogue is at ____. → a) a shop checkout · b) a hospital · c) a kitchen  
9. *Here you are* means ____. → a) giving the money · b) saying goodbye forever · c) ordering food  
10. *Yes of course* means ____. → a) yes, no problem · b) no · c) maybe later

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) receipt**  
7. **a) pay for this thing**  
8. **a) a shop checkout**  
9. **a) giving the money**  
10. **a) yes, no problem**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *Can I pay* uses ____. → a) base verb after *can* · b) *to pay* · c) *paying* only  
12. *Change* and *receipt* are ____. → a) different things · b) the same word · c) cooking verbs  
13. *Credit card* is a ____. → a) payment method · b) symptom · c) sequencer  
14. *Prefer to pay with cash* = ____. → a) like cash more · b) only use card · c) need medicine  
15. The dialogue practices ____. → a) paying, change, receipt · b) First/Then/Finally · c) should/shouldn't only

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) base verb after *can***  
12. **a) different things**  
13. **a) payment method**  
14. **a) like cash more**  
15. **a) paying, change, receipt**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: My purchase

**Objetivo:** escribir sobre una compra con *pay for / spend on*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I paid ____ the book with cash. → *for / on / to*  
2. I spend money ____ books. → *on / for / at*  
3. Here is your ____. → *change / fever / pan*  
4. Can I have the ____ please? → *receipt / cold / oven*  
5. Can I pay with ____ card? → *credit / boil / cut*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **for**  
2. **on**  
3. **change**  
4. **receipt**  
5. **credit**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. I / paid / for / the dinner / with cash.  
7. She / spends / money / on / clothes.  
8. Can I / have / the receipt / please?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. I paid for the dinner with cash.  
7. She spends money on clothes.  
8. Can I have the receipt please?

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Pagué la cena en efectivo.  
10. Gasto mucho dinero en ropa.  
11. ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?  
12. Aquí tienes el cambio y el recibo.  
13. Párrafo corto (4–6 frases): compra + *paid for* + *spend on* + *change/receipt*.  
14. Usa *cash* y *credit card* en dos frases.  
15. Pregunta el recibo de forma educada.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. I paid for the dinner with cash.  
10. I spend a lot of money on clothes.  
11. Can I pay with credit card? / Can I pay for this with credit card?  
12. Here is your change and your receipt.  
13. Yesterday I bought a book. I paid for it with cash. I gave twenty pounds. I got ten pounds change and a receipt. I spend money on books every month.  
14. I prefer cash. Sometimes I use my credit card.  
15. Can I have the receipt please?

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **pay for** | I paid **for** the book. |
| **spend on** | I spend money **on** books. |
| **pasados** | paid · spent |
| **caja** | cash · credit card · change · receipt |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Continúa con la [**Unidad 60 — Module 6 Review**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-60-repaso-modulo-6): repaso de compras, comida, *should* y *pay for*.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe 6–8 frases reales sobre una compra con *pay for*, *spend on*, *change* y *receipt*.

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 60 del curso A1** (*Module 6 Review — Shopping & Food*) con **soluciones comentadas**.

> **Guía teórica:** [Repaso Módulo 6 A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-60-repaso-modulo-6)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 60 — Module 6 Review](/curso-a1/unit-60)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Module 6 map](/blog/curso-a1/unit-60/a1-unit60-module-map.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: repaso](#leccion-1--gramatica-repaso)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: repaso](#leccion-2--vocabulario-repaso)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Last week at the supermarket](#leccion-3--reading-last-week-at-the-supermarket)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Review dialogue](#leccion-4--listening-review-dialogue)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: My shopping day](#leccion-5--writing-my-shopping-day)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: repaso

**Objetivo:** *some/any*, *much/many*, *too/enough*, *would like*, *First/Then/Finally*, *should*, *pay for / spend on*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I have ____ apples. → *some / any / much*  
2. I don't have ____ milk. → *any / some / many*  
3. How ____ water do you want? → *much / many / some*  
4. How ____ apples do you need? → *many / much / any*  
5. This shirt is ____ small. → *too / enough / some*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **some** — afirmativa.  
2. **any** — negativa.  
3. **much** — incontable.  
4. **many** — contable.  
5. **too** — *too* + adjetivo.

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

6. It isn't big ____. → *enough / too / some*  
7. I would ____ the chicken please. → *like / likes / liking*  
8. ____ boil the water. Then add the pasta. → *First / Finally / Any*  
9. You ____ rest when you are ill. → *should / shouldn't / to*  
10. I paid ____ dinner with cash. → *for / on / to*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **enough** — adj. + *enough*.  
7. **like** — *I would like*.  
8. **First**  
9. **should** + verbo base.  
10. **for** — *pay for*.

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Elige / corrige

11. Correct: ____. → a) I spend money on food · b) I spend money for food · c) I pay on food  
12. Correct: ____. → a) You should rest · b) You should to rest · c) You shoulds rest  
13. Correct order: ____. → a) First, Then, Finally · b) Finally, First, Then · c) Then, Finally, First  
14. *I have any milk* (afirmativa) → corrige  
15. *How many water?* → corrige

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) I spend money on food**  
12. **a) You should rest**  
13. **a) First, Then, Finally**  
14. I have **some** milk.  
15. How **much** water?

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: repaso

**Objetivo:** supermercado, ropa, restaurante, cocina, salud, dinero.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja

1. aisle  
2. changing room  
3. bill  
4. pharmacy  
5. receipt  

a) place to try clothes · b) supermarket corridor · c) restaurant account · d) proof of payment · e) place to buy medicine

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **a** · 3 → **c** · 4 → **e** · 5 → **d**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

6. Apples are ____. → *countable / uncountable / too*  
7. Milk is ____. → *uncountable / countable / receipt*  
8. Starter comes ____ the main course. → *before / after / never*  
9. Fry in a ____. Bake in the ____. → *pan / oven · pot / pharmacy*  
10. Cash or ____ card? → *credit / fever / boil*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **countable**  
7. **uncountable**  
8. **before**  
9. **pan** · **oven**  
10. **credit**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Elige

11. *Headache* = ____. → a) pain in your head · b) a receipt · c) a recipe  
12. *Change* (in a shop) = ____. → a) money you get back · b) a cold · c) an aisle  
13. *Ingredients* = ____. → a) what you need for a recipe · b) the bill · c) size M  
14. *Dessert* = ____. → a) sweet course at the end · b) starter · c) medicine  
15. *Sale* = ____. → a) reduced prices · b) pharmacy · c) fever

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) pain in your head**  
12. **a) money you get back**  
13. **a) what you need for a recipe**  
14. **a) sweet course at the end**  
15. **a) reduced prices**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Last week at the supermarket

**Objetivo:** leer un texto que une el Módulo 6.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-60/reading-review.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Last week at the supermarket"></audio>

> Last week I went to the supermarket and bought some apples, some milk and bread. I don't have much money this month so I didn't buy any dessert. On Saturday I cooked pasta. First I boiled the water. Then I added the pasta. Finally I served it with sauce. I feel a bit ill today — I have a headache. I should rest and take some medicine.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Where did the person go last week? → a) The supermarket · b) The cinema · c) The airport  
2. What did they buy? → a) Apples, milk and bread · b) Only clothes · c) Only medicine  
3. Why didn't they buy dessert? → a) Not much money · b) They hate dessert · c) The shop was closed  
4. What did they cook on Saturday? → a) Pasta · b) Cake only · c) Nothing  
5. How do they feel today? → a) A bit ill / headache · b) Great · c) Hungry only

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) The supermarket**  
2. **a) Apples, milk and bread**  
3. **a) Not much money**  
4. **a) Pasta**  
5. **a) A bit ill / headache**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. *Some* appears with ____. → a) apples and milk · b) only dessert · c) only headache  
7. *Any* appears with ____. → a) dessert (negative) · b) apples (affirmative) · c) pasta only  
8. Recipe order uses ____. → a) First, Then, Finally · b) only Finally · c) only should  
9. Advice uses ____. → a) should rest · b) pay for · c) too small  
10. The main topic is ____. → a) a shopping/cooking/health day · b) only weather · c) only travel

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) apples and milk**  
7. **a) dessert (negative)**  
8. **a) First, Then, Finally**  
9. **a) should rest**  
10. **a) a shopping/cooking/health day**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *Much money* is correct because *money* is ____. → a) uncountable · b) countable · c) a verb  
12. *Didn't buy any dessert* uses ____. → a) any in negative · b) some in negative · c) many water  
13. *Boiled* is past of ____. → a) boil · b) bake · c) cut  
14. *I have a headache* needs ____. → a) *a* · b) no article · c) *any*  
15. *Take some medicine* uses ____. → a) some · b) any · c) too

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) uncountable**  
12. **a) any in negative**  
13. **a) boil**  
14. **a) *a***  
15. **a) some**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Review dialogue

**Objetivo:** escuchar un diálogo que une restaurante, dinero y salud.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-60/listening-review.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Review dialogue"></audio>

> **A:** I would like the chicken for main course please.  
> **B:** Anything else?  
> **A:** Can I have the bill please? I paid for dinner with cash yesterday but today I only have credit card.  
> **B:** No problem. Here is your receipt.  
> **A:** I feel a bit ill — headache.  
> **B:** You should rest and take medicine.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. What does A order? → a) Chicken for main course · b) Only dessert · c) Only water  
2. What does A ask for? → a) The bill · b) A changing room · c) An aisle  
3. How did A pay yesterday? → a) With cash · b) Only with card · c) Not at all  
4. How does A pay today? → a) Credit card · b) Only cash · c) Nothing  
5. What advice does B give? → a) Rest and take medicine · b) Go to work · c) Fry onions

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Chicken for main course**  
2. **a) The bill**  
3. **a) With cash**  
4. **a) Credit card**  
5. **a) Rest and take medicine**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. B gives A a ____. → a) receipt · b) fever · c) pan  
7. A has a ____. → a) headache · b) recipe · c) sale  
8. *I would like* is ____. → a) a polite order · b) a past tense · c) a superlative  
9. *Paid for dinner* uses ____. → a) pay for · b) spend on · c) too enough  
10. The dialogue reviews ____. → a) restaurant + money + health · b) only weather · c) only packing

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) receipt**  
7. **a) headache**  
8. **a) a polite order**  
9. **a) pay for**  
10. **a) restaurant + money + health**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *Can I have the bill?* is ____. → a) a polite request · b) a recipe step · c) a size  
12. *Should* + ____. → a) base verb · b) *to* + verb · c) *-ing* only  
13. *Main course* = ____. → a) the main dish · b) starter · c) receipt  
14. *No problem* means ____. → a) it's OK · b) never · c) too small  
15. The listening mixes Module 6 topics: ____. → a) yes · b) no · c) only Unit 41

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) a polite request**  
12. **a) base verb**  
13. **a) the main dish**  
14. **a) it's OK**  
15. **a) yes**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: My shopping day

**Objetivo:** escribir un día que una el Módulo 6.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I bought ____ apples. → *some / any / much*  
2. I don't have ____ dessert. → *any / some / many*  
3. This shirt is ____ big. → *too / enough / some*  
4. ____ boil water. Then cook the pasta. → *First / Finally / Any*  
5. I paid ____ the dinner with cash. → *for / on / to*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **some**  
2. **any**  
3. **too**  
4. **First**  
5. **for**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. I / would like / the chicken / please.  
7. You / should / rest.  
8. Can I / have / the receipt / please?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. I would like the chicken please.  
7. You should rest.  
8. Can I have the receipt please?

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Compra con *some* y negativa con *any*.  
10. Pregunta *how much* y *how many*.  
11. Ropa con *too* / *enough*.  
12. Pedido educado + la cuenta.  
13. Receta corta con *First / Then / Finally*.  
14. Consejo con *should / shouldn't*.  
15. Párrafo (6–8 frases) que una supermercado + cocina + salud o pago.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. I bought some apples. I didn't buy any dessert.  
10. How much milk? How many apples?  
11. This shirt is too small. It isn't big enough.  
12. I would like the chicken please. Can I have the bill please?  
13. First boil the water. Then add the pasta. Finally serve.  
14. You should rest. You shouldn't go to work.  
15. Last week I went to the supermarket. I bought some milk and bread. On Saturday I cooked pasta. First I boiled water. Then I added the pasta. I feel ill today. I should rest. Yesterday I paid for dinner with cash.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Bloque | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Cantidad | some · any · much · many |
| Ropa | too · enough |
| Restaurante | I would like · the bill |
| Cocina | First · Then · Finally |
| Salud | should · shouldn't |
| Dinero | pay for · spend on · receipt |

---

## Siguiente paso tras el curso A1

Con la Unidad 60 cierras el **Módulo 6** y el recorrido A1 del blog. Consolida con el [índice del curso A1](/curso-a1) y la guía [Inglés A1 vs A2](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1-vs-a2).

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 1 del curso A2** (*Greetings & Introductions — repaso*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Saludos e introducciones A2](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-1-saludos-introducciones-repaso)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 1 — Saludos e introducciones](/curso-a2/unit-1)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Fórmula A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-1/a2-unit1-intro-formula.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: to be y Present Simple](#leccion-1--gramatica-to-be-y-present-simple)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: hometown y hobbies](#leccion-2--vocabulario-hometown-y-hobbies)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Hello! My name is Maria](#leccion-3--reading-hello-my-name-is-maria)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Hi! My name is Carlos](#leccion-4--listening-hi-my-name-is-carlos)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: My introduction](#leccion-5--writing-my-introduction)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: to be y Present Simple

**Objetivo:** *I am / you are / he-she is* y *live / lives*, *teach / teaches*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa (*to be*)

1. I ____ from Spain. → *am / is / are*  
2. You ____ a student. → *are / am / is*  
3. She ____ twenty-eight years old. → *is / am / are*  
4. My hometown ____ Madrid. → *is / are / am*  
5. I ____ happy to be here. → *am / is / are*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am**  
2. **are**  
3. **is**  
4. **is**  
5. **am**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa (Present Simple)

6. I ____ in a quiet neighbourhood. → *live / lives / living*  
7. She ____ in a small flat. → *lives / live / living*  
8. He ____ in London. → *lives / live / is live*  
9. They ____ near the beach. → *live / lives / living*  
10. Maria ____ English at a small school. → *teaches / teach / teaching*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **live**  
7. **lives** — 3.ª persona singular.  
8. **lives**  
9. **live**  
10. **teaches**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

11. *You am a teacher.*  
12. *She live near the beach.*  
13. *My hometown are Madrid.*  
14. *My favourite hobby is play football.*  
15. *I live in quiet neighbourhood.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. You **are** a teacher.  
12. She **lives** near the beach.  
13. My hometown **is** Madrid.  
14. My favourite hobby is **playing** football.  
15. I live in **a** quiet neighbourhood.

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: hometown y hobbies

**Objetivo:** *hometown, neighbourhood, hobby, favourite, Nice to meet you*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja

1. hometown  
2. neighbourhood  
3. hobby  
4. favourite  
5. Nice to meet you  

a) pasatiempo · b) favorito · c) ciudad natal · d) primera vez · e) barrio

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **e** · 3 → **a** · 4 → **b** · 5 → **d**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

6. My ____ is Madrid. → *hometown / hobby / teacher*  
7. I live in a quiet ____. → *neighbourhood / favourite / age*  
8. My favourite ____ is reading. → *hobby / hometown / am*  
9. My ____ colour is blue. → *favourite / neighbourhood / teach*  
10. Nice to ____ you! → *meet / live / teach*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **hometown**  
7. **neighbourhood**  
8. **hobby**  
9. **favourite**  
10. **meet**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Elige

11. *Hometown* = ____. → a) the city where you grew up · b) your job · c) your age  
12. *Neighbourhood* = ____. → a) the area where you live · b) a country · c) a school subject  
13. *Hobby is* + ____. → a) *-ing* / noun · b) past tense · c) *to* + base only  
14. *Nice to meet you* is for ____. → a) the first time · b) every morning with friends · c) only emails  
15. *I am a student* tells ____. → a) occupation · b) hometown · c) colour

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) the city where you grew up**  
12. **a) the area where you live**  
13. **a) *-ing* / noun**  
14. **a) the first time**  
15. **a) occupation**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Hello! My name is Maria

**Objetivo:** leer una presentación A2 completa.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-1/reading-intro.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Hello! My name is Maria"></audio>

> Hello! My name is Maria. I am twenty-eight years old. My hometown is Madrid, Spain. I live in a quiet neighbourhood with many parks and cafes. My favourite hobby is reading books. I also love walking in my neighbourhood. I am a teacher. I teach English at a small school. Nice to meet you!

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. How old is Maria? → a) Twenty-eight · b) Twenty-five · c) Thirty  
2. Where is her hometown? → a) Madrid · b) Barcelona · c) London  
3. What is her favourite hobby? → a) Reading books · b) Football · c) Cooking only  
4. What is her job? → a) Teacher · b) Student · c) Doctor  
5. Does she close with *Nice to meet you*? → a) Yes · b) No · c) The text doesn't say

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Twenty-eight**  
2. **a) Madrid**  
3. **a) Reading books**  
4. **a) Teacher**  
5. **a) Yes**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Her neighbourhood has ____. → a) parks and cafes · b) only a beach · c) no parks  
7. She also loves ____. → a) walking in her neighbourhood · b) flying · c) skiing only  
8. She teaches English at ____. → a) a small school · b) a big hospital · c) a museum  
9. *Hometown* in the text = ____. → a) Madrid, Spain · b) Barcelona · c) London  
10. The main topic is ____. → a) Maria's introduction · b) a trip to London · c) past holidays

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) parks and cafes**  
7. **a) walking in her neighbourhood**  
8. **a) a small school**  
9. **a) Madrid, Spain**  
10. **a) Maria's introduction**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *I am a teacher* uses ____. → a) *to be* · b) Past Simple · c) *will*  
12. *I teach English* uses ____. → a) Present Simple · b) Past Continuous · c) *going to*  
13. *Quiet neighbourhood* needs ____. → a) *a* · b) no article · c) *any*  
14. *Favourite hobby is reading* uses ____. → a) *-ing* · b) past *-ed* · c) *to read* only  
15. *Nice to meet you* is a ____. → a) closing greeting · b) past time marker · c) superlative

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) *to be***  
12. **a) Present Simple**  
13. **a) *a***  
14. **a) *-ing***  
15. **a) closing greeting**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Hi! My name is Carlos

**Objetivo:** escuchar una presentación A2 y comparar con Maria.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-1/listening-intro.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Hi! My name is Carlos"></audio>

> Hi! My name is Carlos. I am from Barcelona, Spain. I am twenty-five years old. My hometown is Barcelona. I live in a nice neighbourhood near the beach. My favourite hobby is playing football. I am a student. I study at the university. I am happy to be here. Nice to meet you!

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Where is Carlos from? → a) Barcelona · b) Madrid · c) Valencia  
2. How old is he? → a) Twenty-five · b) Twenty-eight · c) Thirty  
3. Where does he live? → a) Near the beach · b) Near a hospital · c) In London  
4. What is his favourite hobby? → a) Playing football · b) Reading books · c) Cooking  
5. Is he a student or a teacher? → a) Student · b) Teacher · c) Doctor

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Barcelona**  
2. **a) Twenty-five**  
3. **a) Near the beach**  
4. **a) Playing football**  
5. **a) Student**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. He studies at ____. → a) the university · b) a small school · c) home only  
7. He says ____. → a) I am happy to be here · b) Goodbye forever · c) See you yesterday  
8. Compared with Maria, Carlos is ____. → a) a student · b) a teacher · c) older than Maria  
9. His neighbourhood is ____. → a) nice / near the beach · b) quiet with parks · c) not mentioned  
10. The listening is about ____. → a) Carlos's introduction · b) past irregular verbs · c) weather

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) the university**  
7. **a) I am happy to be here**  
8. **a) a student**  
9. **a) nice / near the beach**  
10. **a) Carlos's introduction**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *Playing football* after *hobby is* is ____. → a) correct · b) needs *play* · c) past tense  
12. *I study* is ____. → a) Present Simple · b) Past Simple · c) Future  
13. *I am from Barcelona* uses ____. → a) *to be* · b) *did* · c) *will*  
14. *Nice to meet you* appears ____. → a) at the end · b) only in the middle · c) never  
15. A2 introductions add ____. → a) hometown, neighbourhood, hobby · b) only name · c) only past verbs

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) correct**  
12. **a) Present Simple**  
13. **a) *to be***  
14. **a) at the end**  
15. **a) hometown, neighbourhood, hobby**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: My introduction

**Objetivo:** escribir tu presentación A2.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. My ____ is Valencia. → *hometown / meet / teach*  
2. I live in a quiet ____. → *neighbourhood / ago / yesterday*  
3. My favourite ____ is swimming. → *hobby / bill / fever*  
4. I ____ a student. → *am / is / are*  
5. Nice to ____ you! → *meet / live / walk*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **hometown**  
2. **neighbourhood**  
3. **hobby**  
4. **am**  
5. **meet**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. My / hometown / is / Madrid.  
7. I / live / in / a quiet neighbourhood.  
8. My / favourite hobby / is / reading.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. My hometown is Madrid.  
7. I live in a quiet neighbourhood.  
8. My favourite hobby is reading.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Di tu nombre y edad.  
10. Di tu *hometown*.  
11. Describe tu *neighbourhood* en una frase.  
12. Di tu *favourite hobby*.  
13. Di si eres *student* o tu trabajo.  
14. Cierra con *Nice to meet you!* o *I am happy to be here!*  
15. Párrafo completo (8–10 frases) con todos los puntos anteriores.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. Hello! My name is Ana. I am twenty-two years old.  
10. My hometown is Valencia.  
11. I live in a quiet neighbourhood.  
12. My favourite hobby is swimming.  
13. I am a student. / I am a teacher.  
14. Nice to meet you! / I am happy to be here!  
15. Hello! My name is Ana. I am twenty-two years old. My hometown is Valencia. I live in a quiet neighbourhood. My favourite hobby is swimming. I am a student. I study at the university. Nice to meet you!

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **to be** | I **am** / you **are** / she **is** |
| **Present Simple** | I **live** / she **lives** |
| **Vocabulario** | hometown · neighbourhood · hobby · favourite |
| **Cierre** | Nice to meet you! |

---

Continúa con la [**Unidad 2 — Past Simple: verbos regulares**](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-2-past-simple-verbos-regulares): *-ed*, *yesterday*, *last week*, *ago*.

Antes de pasar de unidad, graba tu presentación de 1 minuto en voz alta.
