faqs.question: ¿Qué es la word formation y por qué importa en C1?
faqs.answer: La word formation es el proceso de crear nuevas palabras mediante afijos (prefijos y sufijos) y conversión de categoría. En C1 importa porque permite generar el sustantivo, adjetivo o verbo correcto a partir de una raíz, una destreza evaluada directamente en el CAE (use of English) e indirectamente en toda escritura académica.

faqs.question: ¿Cuáles son los sufijos nominalizadores más importantes en C1?
faqs.answer: Los sufijos que forman sustantivos: -tion/-sion (creation, decision), -ment (development), -ness (happiness), -ity (complexity), -ance/-ence (importance, existence), -ship (relationship), -hood (childhood), -al (refusal), -er/-or (researcher, director). Su dominio permite nominalizar verbos y adjetivos con precisión.

faqs.question: ¿Qué prefijos negativos existen y cuándo se usa cada uno?
faqs.answer: Los principales son un- (unhappy), in-/im-/il-/ir- (invisible, impossible, illegal, irregular), dis- (disagree), non- (non-negotiable) y mis- (misunderstand). La elección depende de la raíz y la convención: im- ante p/b, il- ante l, ir- ante r. No son intercambiables.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es la conversión de categoría y por qué es típica del inglés?
faqs.answer: La conversión consiste en cambiar la categoría gramatical de una palabra sin alterar su forma: to google (sustantivo a verbo), a run (verbo a sustantivo), to clean (adjetivo a verbo). Es muy productiva en inglés y una marca de fluidez idiomática en C1.

content:
La formación de palabras, o word formation, es el motor morfológico del inglés. A partir de una raíz, los afijos generan sustantivos, adjetivos, verbos y adverbios con significados precisos, y la conversión de categoría permite que una misma forma funcione en distintas clases gramaticales. A nivel C1, dominar este proceso no es un lujo sino una necesidad: la sección use of English del CAE lo evalúa directamente, y la escritura académica exige la precisión nominal que solo la word formation adecuada confiere. Esta unidad del Language Lab aísla el fenómeno y lo entrena en sus patrones más rentables. Cada concepto se presenta en tres niveles. El A2 ofrece la versión más sencilla, el B2 añade complejidad operativa y el C1 presenta la formación de palabras con sus matices de precisión nominal y registro. A2: We can make new words by adding small parts. "Happy" + "ness" = "happiness." B2: Word formation creates new words through affixes and category conversion. Suffixes like -tion, -ment and -ness form nouns; prefixes like un- and in- form negatives. C1 mastery means generating the correct noun, adjective or verb from a root with precision. C1: Word formation, the morphological engine of English, generates nominals, adjectivals, verbals and adverbials from a root via affixation and category conversion. At C1, its mastery is not optional but obligatory: the CAE use of English component assesses it directly, and academic writing demands the nominal precision that only calibrated word formation confers. This Language Lab unit isolates the phenomenon and drills its most discursively productive patterns to automaticity. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 63 C1](/curso-c1/unit-63)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 62 C1: Language Lab — Verbo/adjetivo + preposición](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-62-language-lab-verbo-adjetivo-preposicion)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 64 C1: Language Lab — Fórmulas fijas y stems académicos](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-64-language-lab-formulas-fijas-stems-academicos)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría: Formación de palabras y precisión nominal ### 1. La arquitectura morfológica de la palabra Una palabra inglesa se compone de raíz (root), prefijo y sufijo. La raíz porta el significado léxico; los afijos modifican la categoría o el significado. Understandable se descompone en under (prefijo) + stand (raíz) + able (sufijo). Comprender esta arquitectura permite analizar palabras desconocidas y generar las formas correctas a partir de una raíz dada, destreza central del C1. A2: A word can have a main part and small parts before and after it. B2: An English word comprises a root, a prefix and a suffix. The root carries the lexical meaning; affixes modify the category or meaning. Understandable decomposes into under + stand + able. Understanding this architecture lets you analyse unknown words and generate correct forms. C1: The morphological architecture of an English word comprises a root, which ports the lexical semantics, together with prefixes and suffixes which modulate category or meaning. The item understandable decomposes into the prefix under, the root stand and the suffix able. Internalising this architecture enables the decomposition of unfamiliar lexemes and the generative production of the correct derivative from a given root, a competence central to C1 morphological agility. ### 2. Sufijos nominalizadores: -tion, -ment, -ness, -ity Los sufijos nominalizadores transforman verbos o adjetivos en sustantivos. -tion/-sion (creation, decision), -ment (development, achievement), -ness (happiness, awareness), -ity (complexity, validity), -ance/-ence (importance, existence), -ship (relationship, leadership), -hood (childhood, likelihood), -al (refusal, proposal), -er/-or (researcher, director). Su dominio permite nominalizar con precisión. A2: We can make nouns by adding endings like "-tion" or "-ness." B2: Nominalising suffixes transform verbs or adjectives into nouns: -tion/-sion (creation, decision), -ment (development), -ness (happiness), -ity (complexity), -ance/-ence (importance), -ship (relationship), -hood (childhood), -al (refusal), -er/-or (researcher). Their mastery enables precise nominalisation. C1: Nominalising suffixes effect the categorial transposition of verbs or adjectives into nouns: -tion/-sion (creation, decision), -ment (development, achievement), -ness (happiness, awareness), -ity (complexity, validity), -ance/-ence (importance, existence), -ship (relationship, leadership), -hood (childhood, likelihood), -al (refusal, proposal) and -er/-or (researcher, director). Their calibrated deployment enables the precise nominalisation that is a diagnostic of C1 academic prose, where nominal density outranks verbal proliferation. ### 3. Sufijos adjetivizadores: -able, -ous, -ive, -ful, -less Los sufijos adjetivizadores forman adjetivos a partir de sustantivos o verbos. -able/-ible (reliable, visible), -ous (hazardous, courageous), -ive (effective, productive), -ful (meaningful, useful), -less (meaningless, useless), -al (cultural, accidental), -ic (strategic, economic), -y (risky, wealthy). La elección del sufijo correcto es convencional y debe memorizarse por raíz. A2: We can make describing words with endings like "-able" or "-ful." B2: Adjectivising suffixes form adjectives from nouns or verbs: -able/-ible (reliable, visible), -ous (hazardous), -ive (effective), -ful (meaningful), -less (meaningless), -al (cultural), -ic (strategic), -y (risky). The correct suffix is conventional and must be memorised by root. C1: Adjectivising suffixes generate adjectives from nominal or verbal bases: -able/-ible (reliable, visible), -ous (hazardous, courageous), -ive (effective, productive), -ful (meaningful, useful), -less (meaningless, useless), -al (cultural, accidental), -ic (strategic, economic) and -y (risky, wealthy). The selection of the correct suffix is conventionally determined and must be memorised per root, since the distribution is idiosyncratic and not predictable from semantics, a memorisation burden intrinsic to C1 morphological mastery. ### 4. Sufijos verbales: -ise, -ate, -en, -ify Los sufijos verbales forman verbos a partir de sustantivos o adjetivos. -ise/-ize (realise, emphasise), -ate (activate, formulate), -en (widen, strengthen), -ify (simplify, justify). La diferencia entre -ise (británico) e -ize (americano) es ortográfica pero convencional. Estos sufijos son rentables en la prosa académica, donde la verbalización densifica la expresión. A2: We can make verbs with endings like "-ise" or "-en." B2: Verbal suffixes form verbs from nouns or adjectives: -ise/-ize (realise, emphasise), -ate (activate, formulate), -en (widen, strengthen), -ify (simplify, justify). The difference between -ise (British) and -ize (American) is orthographic but conventional. These suffixes are useful in academic prose. C1: Verbal suffixes generate verbs from nominal or adjectival bases: -ise/-ize (realise, emphasise), -ate (activate, formulate), -en (widen, strengthen) and -ify (simplify, justify). The alternation between -ise (British) and -ize (American) is orthographically conventional rather than semantically motivated. These suffixes are discursively productive in academic prose, where verbalisation contributes to the lexical density that characterises the C1 register. ### 5. Prefijos negativos: un-, in-, dis-, non-, mis- Los prefijos negativos invierten o matizan el significado. un- (unhappy, unlikely), in-/im-/il-/ir- (invisible, impossible, illegal, irregular), dis- (disagree, dissatisfied), non- (non-negotiable, non-existent), mis- (misunderstand, misrepresent). La distribución alomórfica de in- (im- ante p/b, il- ante l, ir- ante r) es convencional y debe respetarse. A2: We can make words negative with beginnings like "un-" or "dis-." B2: Negative prefixes invert or nuance meaning: un- (unhappy), in-/im-/il-/ir- (invisible, impossible, illegal, irregular), dis- (disagree), non- (non-negotiable), mis- (misunderstand). The allomorphic distribution of in- (im- before p/b, il- before l, ir- before r) is conventional and must be respected. C1: Negative prefixes effect semantic inversion or attenuation: un- (unhappy, unlikely), in-/im-/il-/ir- (invisible, impossible, illegal, irregular), dis- (disagree, dissatisfied), non- (non-negotiable, non-existent) and mis- (misunderstand, misrepresent). The allomorphic distribution of the in- allomorph, im- before bilabial onsets, il- before lateral onsets and ir- before rhotic onsets, is phonologically conditioned yet conventionally fixed, and its violation, such as irpossible for impossible, constitutes an orthographic error diagnostically incompatible with C1 competence. ### 6. Prefijos de grado e intensidad: over-, under-, out-, sub- Los prefijos de grado matizan la intensidad o el exceso. over- (overestimate, overcomplicated), under- (underestimate, underdeveloped), out- (outperform, outnumber), sub- (substandard, subcommittee), super- (superhuman, supervise). Su uso en prosa académica permite expresar matices cuantitativos con precisión y concisión. A2: Some beginnings change how much something is: "over-" means too much, "under-" means too little. B2: Degree prefixes nuance intensity or excess: over- (overestimate), under- (underestimate), out- (outperform), sub- (substandard), super- (superhuman). Their use in academic prose expresses quantitative nuances with precision and concision. C1: Degree prefixes modulate quantitative or intensive magnitude: over- (overestimate, overcomplicated), under- (underestimate, underdeveloped), out- (outperform, outnumber), sub- (substandard, subcommittee) and super- (superhuman, supervise). Their deployment in academic prose enables the concise expression of quantitative nuances that would otherwise require periphrastic formulation, a concision that is itself a marker of C1 lexical economy. ### 7. Prefijos de actitud y postura: pro-, anti-, counter-, co- Los prefijos de actitud expresan postura o alineación. pro- (pro-European, proactive), anti- (anti-war, antisocial), counter- (counter-argument, counterproductive), co- (coexist, cooperate), mis- (misaligned), pre- (predetermine). En la argumentación académica, estos prefijos compactan relaciones de postura que de otro modo requerirían circunloquios. A2: Some beginnings show what side you are on: "pro-" means for, "anti-" means against. B2: Attitude prefixes express stance or alignment: pro- (pro-European), anti- (anti-war), counter- (counter-argument), co- (coexist), pre- (predetermine). In academic argumentation, these prefixes compact stance relations that would otherwise need circumlocution. C1: Attitudinal prefixes encode stance or alignment: pro- (pro-European, proactive), anti- (anti-war, antisocial), counter- (counter-argument, counterproductive), co- (coexist, cooperate) and pre- (predetermine, precondition). In academic argumentation, these prefixes compactly encode relational stances that would otherwise demand periphrastic exposition, a lexical economy that contributes to the informational density diagnostic of C1 scholarly register. ### 8. Conversión de categoría: la productividad del inglés La conversión consiste en cambiar la categoría gramatical de una palabra sin alterar su forma. to google (sustantivo a verbo), a run (verbo a sustantivo), to clean (adjetivo a verbo), a must (verbo modal a sustantivo). Es muy productiva en inglés y una marca de fluidez idiomática en C1, donde permite expresar ideas con economía. A2: Sometimes we use the same word as a noun or a verb, like "a run" and "to run." B2: Conversion changes a word's grammatical category without altering its form: to google (noun to verb), a run (verb to noun), to clean (adjective to verb), a must (modal to noun). It is very productive in English and a marker of idiomatic fluency at C1. C1: Conversion effects categorial transposition without morphological alteration: to google instantiates noun-to-verb conversion, a run instantiates verb-to-noun conversion, to clean instantiates adjective-to-verb conversion, and a must instantiates modal-to-noun conversion. Its productivity in English is exceptionally high, and its idiomatic deployment constitutes a marker of C1 fluency, enabling the economical expression of ideas that a more morphologically conservative language would require periphrastic means to convey. ### 9. Nominalización en prosa académica: densidad informativa La nominalización, la conversión de verbos o cláusulas en sustantivos, es un rasgo distintivo de la prosa académica inglesa. The decision was made to revise the policy se densifica en the policy revision decision. The fact that the data were analysed carefully se densifica en the careful analysis of the data. Esta densidad nominal es lo que distingue el registro académico C1 del coloquial. A2: In academic writing, we can use nouns instead of long phrases to be shorter. B2: Nominalisation, converting verbs or clauses into nouns, is a distinctive feature of academic English. The decision was made to revise the policy becomes the policy revision decision. The fact that the data were analysed carefully becomes the careful analysis of the data. This nominal density distinguishes C1 academic register from colloquial. C1: Nominalisation, the conversion of verbal or clausal constructions into nominal counterparts, constitutes a diacritic feature of English academic prose. The clausal the decision was made to revise the policy condenses into the nominal the policy revision decision, and the clausal the fact that the data were analysed carefully condenses into the careful analysis of the data. This nominal density is what distinguishes the C1 academic register from the colloquial, and its calibrated deployment is a reliable index of scholarly registeral control. ### 10. Compuestos: noun + noun y adjetivo + noun La formación de compuestos, dos palabras unidas para formar una nueva, es muy productiva en inglés. Noun + noun (decision-making process, research findings, policy framework), adjetivo + noun (long-term effect, high-quality evidence). Los compuestos densifican la expresión y son característicos de la prosa académica C1, donde aparecen con frecuencia diagnóstica. A2: We can join two words to make a new one, like "research findings." B2: Compounding, joining two words to form a new one, is very productive in English. Noun + noun (decision-making process, research findings, policy framework), adjective + noun (long-term effect, high-quality evidence). Compounds densify expression and are characteristic of C1 academic prose. C1: Compounding, the lexical fusion of two bases into a novel unit, is exceptionally productive in English. Noun-plus-noun compounding (decision-making process, research findings, policy framework) and adjective-plus-noun compounding (long-term effect, high-quality evidence) densify expression and are diacritically characteristic of C1 academic prose, where their diagnostic frequency furnishes a reliable index of registeral elevation and lexical sophistication. ### 11. Errores frecuentes en word formation: sufijos espurios Los errores más comunes incluyen sufijos espurios: importance no importancy, development no developement, happiness no happyness, reliable no relyable. La ortografía de los sufijos tiene irregularidades (y se convierte en i ante -ness: happy → happiness) que deben memorizarse. El C1 no puede permitirse estos errores en escritura formal. A2: Some word endings are spelled in special ways. "Happy" becomes "happiness," not "happyness." B2: Common errors include spurious suffixes: importance not importancy, development not developement, happiness not happyness, reliable not relyable. Suffix spelling has irregularities (y becomes i before -ness: happy → happiness) that must be memorised. C1 cannot afford these errors in formal writing. C1: The most prevalent word-formation errors involve spurious suffixal spellings: importance, not importancy, development, not developement, happiness, not happyness, and reliable, not relyable. Suffixal orthography harbours idiosyncratic irregularities, such as the y-to-i mutation ante -ness (happy → happiness), whose memorisation is non-negotiable. The commission of such errors in formal writing is diagnostically incompatible with C1 certification, their persistence signalling a morphological control beneath the target threshold. ### 12. Word formation en el CAE: la sección use of English La sección use of English del CAE incluye ejercicios de word formation donde se da una raíz y se debe generar la forma correcta según el contexto. La estrategia exige analizar la categoría requerida por el hueco (sustantivo, adjetivo, adverbio, verbo), aplicar el sufijo o prefijo adecuado y verificar la ortografía. Practicar con cronómetro es esencial. A2: In the CAE exam, you get a word and change it to fit the sentence. B2: The CAE use of English includes word formation exercises where a root is given and the correct form must be generated. The strategy requires analysing the category needed by the gap (noun, adjective, adverb, verb), applying the correct suffix or prefix and checking spelling. Timed practice is essential. C1: The CAE use of English component incorporates word-formation items in which a root is supplied and the contextually correct derivative must be generated. The strategic protocol demands the analysis of the categorial slot required by the gap, nominal, adjectival, adverbial or verbal, the application of the diacritically correct affix and the verification of orthographic accuracy. Timed practice is indispensable, since the examination rewards both accuracy and velocity, and the candidate must internalise the derivational pathways to automaticity. ### 13. Adverbios en -ly y sus irregularidades La mayoría de los adverbios se forman con -ly: carefully, effectively, significantly. Pero hay irregularidades: los adjetivos terminados en -y cambian a -ily (happy → happily), los terminados en -ble cambian a -bly (probable → probably), y algunos adjetivos no admiten -ly (fast, hard, early son ya adverbios). Conocer estas reglas evita errores ortográficos. A2: Many adverbs end in "-ly," like "carefully." B2: Most adverbs are formed with -ly: carefully, effectively. But there are irregularities: adjectives ending in -y change to -ily (happy → happily), those ending in -ble change to -bly (probable → probably), and some adjectives do not take -ly (fast, hard, early are already adverbs). C1: The majority of English adverbs are -ly derivatives: carefully, effectively, significantly. The formation, however, harbours systematic irregularities: adjectival bases terminating in -y undergo y-to-i mutation ante the suffix (happy → happily), those terminating in -ble contract to -bly (probable → probably), and a delimited class of adjectives, fast, hard and early, function adverbially without morphological marking. Internalising these rules precludes the orthographic errors whose commission would attenuate the impression of C1 morphological control. ### 14. Falsos amigos morfológicos: sufijos que engañan Ciertos sufijos generan falsos amigos morfológicos. -ly no siempre forma adverbios: lonely es adjetivo, likely es adjetivo o adverbio. -ful no siempre significa lleno de: dreadful significa terrible, no lleno de terror. -ish puede indicar aproximación (greenish) o actitud (childish). El C1 debe reconocer estos matices para no interpretar literalmente. A2: Sometimes word endings do not mean what you think. "Lonely" is not an adverb. B2: Some suffixes generate morphological false friends. -ly does not always form adverbs: lonely is an adjective, likely is an adjective or adverb. -ful does not always mean full of: dreadful means terrible. -ish can indicate approximation (greenish) or attitude (childish). C1 must recognise these nuances. C1: A subset of suffixes generates morphological false friends whose literal interpretation would produce semantic distortion. The -ly suffix does not invariably derive adverbs: lonely is adjectival and likely is ambiguously adjectival or adverbial. The -ful suffix does not invariably encode repletion: dreadful denotes terribleness rather than fullness of dread. The -ish suffix ambigates between approximation (greenish) and attitudinal characterisation (childish). The C1 user must recognise these non-compositional nuances to preclude literal misinterpretation. ### 15. Estrategias de consolidación de la word formation La consolidación exige practicar la derivación sistemática: partir de una raíz y generar todas las formas posibles (noun, adjective, verb, adverb), crear tarjetas con las familias de palabras y practicar con ejercicios tipo CAE cronometrados. La lectura abundante de prosa académica, donde las formas derivadas aparecen en contexto, es insustituible. La atención a la ortografía de los sufijos es crucial. A2: To learn word formation, practice making different words from one root. B2: Consolidation requires systematic derivation practice: starting from a root, generate all possible forms (noun, adjective, verb, adverb), create cards with word families, and practise with timed CAE-style exercises. Abundant reading of academic prose is irreplaceable. Attention to suffix spelling is crucial. C1: The consolidation of word formation necessitates systematic derivational practice: commencing from a root, the learner generates all categorially admissible derivatives, nominal, adjectival, verbal and adverbial, constructs flashcards encoding word families and practises with timed CAE-prototype exercises. Abundant immersion in academic prose, wherein derived forms arise in natural context, remains the irreplaceable substrate of acquisition. Scrupulous attention to suffixal orthography is pivotal, since orthographic error is the most prevalent manifestation of incomplete morphological automation at the C1 threshold. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 Forma el sustantivo a partir de DECIDE: The committee's ______ was controversial.
Ver solución decision
### Ejercicio 2 Forma el adjetivo a partir de RELY: The data are not sufficiently ______.
Ver solución reliable
### Ejercicio 3 Añade el prefijo negativo correcto: The treaty was ______legal and therefore void.
Ver solución il (illegal — il- before l)
### Ejercicio 4 Forma el adverbio a partir de HAPPY: She smiled ______ at the news.
Ver solución happily (y → i + ly)
### Ejercicio 5 Forma el sustantivo a partir de DEVELOP: The ______ of the region has been rapid.
Ver solución development
### Ejercicio 6 Forma el verbo a partir de SIMPLE: The new procedure will ______ the workflow.
Ver solución simplify
### Ejercicio 7 Añade el prefijo de grado adecuado: The report ______estimated the costs, causing a budget shortfall.
Ver solución under (underestimated)
### Ejercicio 8 Nominaliza: The fact that the policy was revised → The policy ______.
Ver solución revision
### Ejercicio 9 Forma el adjetivo a partir of HAZARD: The conditions were extremely ______.
Ver solución hazardous
### Ejercicio 10 Corrige el error ortográfico: The happyness of the team was evident.
Ver solución The happiness of the team was evident. (y → i before -ness)
### Ejercicio 11 Forma el sustantivo a partir of COMPLEX: The ______ of the problem is daunting.
Ver solución complexity
### Ejercicio 12 Añade el prefijo de postura adecuado: He presented a ______-argument to the main thesis.
Ver solución counter (counter-argument)
### Ejercicio 13 Forma el adverbio a partir de PROBABLE: The project will ______ be delayed.
Ver solución probably (-ble → -bly)
### Ejercicio 14 Conversión de categoría: usa RUN como sustantivo en una frase.
Ver solución She went for a run in the park. (run used as a noun, unchanged in form)
### Ejercicio 15 Forma el adjetivo a partir de MEANING: The results were statistically ______.
Ver solución meaningful
### Ejercicio 16 Explica en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) por qué la nominalización es característica de la prosa académica.
Ver solución Nominalisation is characteristic of academic prose because it densifies information, packing clausal content into compact nominal structures. Instead of writing the fact that the data were analysed carefully, the academic writer writes the careful analysis of the data, foregrounding the process as an abstract entity. This nominal density conveys authority and concision, hallmarks of the scholarly register, and its calibrated deployment distinguishes C1 academic writing from the more verbal, clause-heavy style of informal discourse.
### Ejercicio 17 Forma el verbo a partir de ACTIVE: The sensor will ______ when motion is detected.
Ver solución activate
### Ejercicio 18 Añade el prefijo negativo correcto: The gesture was ______appropriate for the occasion.
Ver solución in (inappropriate — in- before a)
### Ejercicio 19 Redacta en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) un breve párrafo académico que use al menos cuatro formas derivadas de raíces distintas (noun, adjective, verb, adverb).
Ver solución The government's decision to revise the policy was driven by the unreliable findings of the initial inquiry. By simplifying the regulatory framework, the committee sought to clarify procedures that had previously been characterised by excessive complexity. The resulting reforms, implemented carefully, were broadly welcomed, though their long-term effectiveness remains to be fully evaluated in the coming years.
## Resumen de la unidad En esta unidad del Language Lab has entrenado la formación de palabras, el motor morfológico del inglés C1. Has consolidado los sufijos nominalizadores (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance, -ship, -hood, -al), los adjetivizadores (-able, -ous, -ive, -ful, -less, -al, -ic), los verbales (-ise, -ate, -en, -ify) y los prefijos negativos (un-, in-/im-/il-/ir-, dis-, non-, mis-). Has aprendido la conversión de categoría, tan productiva en inglés, y la nominalización como rasgo distintivo de la prosa académica. Has identificado los errores ortográficos más comunes (happiness no happyness, development no developement) y los falsos amigos morfológicos (lonely, dreadful, -ish). Los 19 ejercicios te han entrenado en la word formation tipo CAE con la precisión que exige el nivel C1. En la siguiente unidad, la 64, el Language Lab aborda las fórmulas fijas y los stems académicos, otro pilar de la escritura formal avanzada.

title: Ejercicios de Verbos y Adjetivos con Preposición C1
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Domina los patrones preposicionales de verbos y adjetivos en inglés C1: depend on, consist of, result in, rely on, prone to, conducive to. Teoría sobre interferencias de la lengua materna, alternancias preposicionales y colocaciones formales, más 19 ejercicios inglés C1 gratis.
description: En esta unidad del curso de inglés C1 gratis del Language Lab aprendes a dominar los patrones preposicionales de verbos y adjetivos, a evitar las...
alt: Tablero con tarjetas de verbos y adjetivos conectados por flechas preposicionales sobre un fondo de pizarra oscura
keywords: Ejercicios de Verbos y Adjetivos con Preposición C1
verbos con preposición en inglés C1

faqs.question: ¿Por qué los patrones preposicionales son difíciles en inglés C1?
faqs.answer: Porque la elección de la preposición no es lógica sino convencional: depende de la lengua y debe memorizarse. Decimos 'depend on' pero en español 'depender de'; 'consist of' pero en español 'consistir en'. Las interferencias de la lengua materna causan errores que delatan un nivel inferior.

faqs.question: ¿Qué verbos C1 toman 'on' y cuáles 'in' o 'of'?
faqs.answer: Con 'on': depend on, rely on, build on, draw on, insist on. Con 'in': result in, engage in, specialise in, consist in (significar). Con 'of': consist of, dispose of, conceive of, beware of. La asociación verbo-preposición es arbitraria y debe aprenderse caso por caso.

faqs.question: ¿Qué adjetivos C1 toman preposiciones específicas?
faqs.answer: Ejemplos: 'dependent on', 'independent of', 'consistent with', 'compatible with', 'prone to', 'conducive to', 'reliant on', 'averse to', 'conversant with', 'conducive to'. Cada adjetivo tiene su preposición fija y cambiarla produce errores de registro.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es la alternancia preposicional y cuándo cambia el significado?
faqs.answer: Algunos verbos cambian de significado según la preposición: 'agree with' (estar de acuerdo con una persona) vs 'agree to' (aceptar una propuesta); 'consist of' (estar compuesto de) vs 'consist in' (consistir en, significar). Reconocer estos matices es una marca del C1.

content:
Los patrones preposicionales son uno de los territorios donde el inglés C1 se gana o se pierde. La dificultad no reside en reglas lógicas sino en convenciones arbitrarias: cada verbo y cada adjetivo exigen una preposición concreta que no se deduce del significado y que a menudo difiere de la lengua materna, generando interferencias. Esta unidad del Language Lab aísla este fenómeno, lo examina en sus patrones más rentables y lo entrena hasta la automatización, con especial atención a las colocaciones formales que la prosa académica C1 requiere. Cada concepto se presenta en tres niveles. El A2 ofrece la versión más sencilla, el B2 añade complejidad operativa y el C1 presenta los patrones preposicionales con sus matices de registro, alternancia y colocación. A2: Some words in English need a small word after them, like "depend on" or "interested in." B2: Prepositional patterns are conventional, not logical. Each verb and adjective takes a specific preposition that must be memorised: depend on, consist of, result in, rely on, prone to. Interference from your native language causes errors that signal a lower level. C1: Prepositional patterning constitutes a domain in which C1 proficiency is won or forfeited through the mastery of arbitrary convention. The selection of the complement preposition is irreducible to semantic logic and frequently divergent from the candidate's native language, engendering transfer-induced errors that diagnostically signal sub-C1 competence. This Language Lab unit isolates the phenomenon, scrutinises its most discursively productive patterns and drills them to automaticity, with particular attention to the formal collocations that C1 academic prose demands. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 62 C1](/curso-c1/unit-62)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 61 C1: Language Lab — Phrasal verbs en argumento](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-61-language-lab-phrasal-verbs-argumento)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 63 C1: Language Lab — Formación de palabras](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-63-language-lab-formacion-palabras)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría: Patrones preposicionales de verbo y adjetivo ### 1. La arbitrariedad del patrón preposicional La elección de la preposición tras un verbo o un adjetivo no se rige por la lógica sino por la convención. Decimos depend on pero en español dependemos de; consist of pero en español consistimos en; result in pero en español resulta en. Estas asociaciones son arbitrarias y deben aprenderse como unidades fijas, porque la interferencia de la lengua materna es la fuente más frecuente de error. A2: The little word after a verb is not always logical. You must learn it. B2: The choice of preposition after a verb or adjective is governed by convention, not logic. We say depend on (not depend of), consist of (not consist in, though consist in exists with a different meaning), result in. These associations are arbitrary and must be learned as fixed units. C1: The complement preposition selected by a verb or adjective is determined by convention rather than semantic logic, rendering the patterns irreducible to inferential acquisition. The English depend on diverges from the Spanish depender de; consist of diverges from consistir en; result in converges superficially but masks deeper distributional divergences. These associations are categorically arbitrary and must be internalised as indivisible lexical units, since cross-linguistic interference constitutes the most prolific source of prepositional error at the C1 threshold. ### 2. Verbos que toman on: depend, rely, build, draw, insist Un grupo numeroso de verbos C1 toma la preposición on: depend on (depender de), rely on (confiar en), build on (desarrollar a partir de), draw on (recurrir a), insist on (insistir en), focus on (centrarse en), elaborate on (desarrollar, ampliar), deliberate on (deliberar sobre), expand on (ampliar). Su consolidación es fundamental porque aparecen con frecuencia en prosa académica. A2: Some verbs use "on" after them, like "depend on" and "rely on." B2: A large group of C1 verbs takes the preposition on: depend on, rely on, build on, draw on, insist on, focus on, elaborate on, deliberate on, expand on. Their consolidation is essential because they appear frequently in academic prose. C1: A sizeable cohort of C1 verbs selects the preposition on: depend on, rely on, build on, draw on, insist on, focus on, elaborate on, deliberate on and expand on. Their consolidation is foundational, given their diagnostic frequency in academic expository prose, and their mis-prepositioning, such as depend of, constitutes an error whose persistence would conspicuously undermine a candidate's C1 credential. ### 3. Verbos que toman in: result, engage, specialise, culminate Otro grupo toma in: result in (dar como resultado), engage in (participar en), specialise in (especializarse en), culminate in (culminar en), consist in (consistir en, significar), participate in (participar en), succeed in (tener éxito en), confide in (confiar en alguien). La distinción entre consist of y consist in es crucial: el primero indica composición, el segundo significa consistir en el sentido de equivaler a. A2: Some verbs use "in," like "result in" and "participate in." B2: Another group takes in: result in, engage in, specialise in, culminate in, consist in, participate in, succeed in, confide in. The distinction between consist of and consist in is crucial: the first indicates composition, the second means to consist in the sense of to amount to. C1: A further verbal cohort selects in: result in, engage in, specialise in, culminate in, consist in, participate in, succeed in and confide in. The discrimination between consist of and consist in is pivotal: the former encodes part-whole composition, the latter encodes definitional equivalence, as in leadership consists in inspiring others. Their conflation would generate a semantic distortion diagnostically incompatible with C1 precision. ### 4. Verbos que toman of: consist, dispose, conceive, beware Los verbos que toman of son menos pero importantes: consist of (estar compuesto de), dispose of (desechar, desprenderse de), conceive of (concebir, imaginar), beware of (cuidado con), acquit of (absolver de), boast of (jactarse de). La interferencia con el español consistir en es una trampa recurrente que el C1 debe erradicar. A2: A few verbs use "of," like "consist of" and "beware of." B2: Verbs taking of are fewer but important: consist of, dispose of, conceive of, beware of, acquit of, boast of. Interference with Spanish consistir en is a recurrent trap that C1 must eradicate. C1: The verbal cohort selecting of, though less populous, is functionally significant: consist of, dispose of, conceive of, beware of, acquit of and boast of. The cross-linguistic interference with the Spanish consistir en constitutes a recurrent trap whose eradication is non-negotiable for C1 certification, the error consist in of being a paradigmatic fossilisation diagnostic of insufficient prepositional automation. ### 5. Verbos que toman with: comply, align, associate, reconcile Los verbos que toman with incluyen comply with (cumplir con), align with (alinearse con), associate with (asociarse con), reconcile with (reconciliar con), cope with (lidiar con), contend with (hacer frente a), coincide with (coincidir con), part company with (separarse de). Muchos de estos son de registro formal y propios de la prosa académica y administrativa. A2: Some verbs use "with," like "comply with" and "cope with." B2: Verbs taking with include comply with, align with, associate with, reconcile with, cope with, contend with, coincide with, part company with. Many of these are formal and typical of academic and administrative prose. C1: The verbal cohort selecting with encompasses comply with, align with, associate with, reconcile with, cope with, contend with, coincide with and part company with, the majority inhabiting the formal register characteristic of academic and administrative prose. Their correct deployment, particularly comply with and contend with, functions as a registeral marker whose absence would attenuate the impression of C1 formality. ### 6. Adjetivos que toman on, of, with, to: el mapa preposicional adjetival Los adjetivos C1 también rigen preposiciones específicas: dependent on (dependiente de), independent of (independiente de), consistent with (consistente con), compatible with (compatible con), prone to (propenso a), conducive to (propicio a), averse to (reacio a), reliant on (dependiente de), conversant with (familiarizado con), mindful of (consciente de). Cada adjetivo tiene su preposición fija y cambiarla produce errores de registro. A2: Adjectives also need small words after them: "dependent on," "prone to." B2: C1 adjectives also govern specific prepositions: dependent on, independent of, consistent with, compatible with, prone to, conducive to, averse to, reliant on, conversant with, mindful of. Each adjective has its fixed preposition, and changing it produces register errors. C1: C1 adjectives likewise govern complement prepositions with categorical fixity: dependent on, independent of, consistent with, compatible with, prone to, conducive to, averse to, reliant on, conversant with and mindful of. Each adjective contracts an idiosyncratic prepositional bond whose violation, such as dependent of or prone for, generates an error whose registeral dissonance would diagnostically undermine a candidate's C1 presentation, particularly in written production. ### 7. La trampa de dependent on e independent of Una de las trampas más frecuentes es la aparente asimetría entre dependent on e independent of. Lógicamente cabría esperar independent on, pero la convención fija independent of. Esta asimiedad refleja la arbitrariedad del patrón preposicional y debe memorizarse sin buscar justificación lógica. Lo mismo ocurre con reliant on pero free of o free from. A2: We say "dependent on" but "independent of." This is not logical, but it is correct. B2: One of the most frequent traps is the asymmetry between dependent on and independent of. Logically one might expect independent on, but convention fixes independent of. This asymmetry reflects the arbitrariness of prepositional patterning and must be memorised without seeking logical justification. C1: Among the most prolific traps is the apparent asymmetry between dependent on and independent of. Logical expectation would project independent on by analogical extension, yet convention categorically fixes independent of. This asymmetry, emblematic of the arbitrary character of prepositional patterning, must be memorised without the quest for rational motivation, a discipline that runs counter to the inferential habits of the proficient learner but that is indispensable for prepositional accuracy at C1. ### 8. Alternancia preposicional con cambio de significado Algunos verbos cambian de significado según la preposición. Agree with significa estar de acuerdo con una persona u opinión; agree to significa aceptar una propuesta o condición; agree on significa ponerse de acuerdo sobre un tema. Look at significa mirar; look into significa investigar; look after significa cuidar. Reconocer estos matices es una marca distintiva del C1. A2: Some verbs change meaning with the little word: "agree with" is different from "agree to." B2: Some verbs change meaning with the preposition. Agree with means to share an opinion; agree to means to accept a proposal; agree on means to reach agreement on a topic. Look at means to watch; look into means to investigate; look after means to care for. Recognising these nuances distinguishes C1. C1: A subset of verbs undergoes semantic modulation as a function of the complement preposition. Agree with encodes opinion-sharing with a person or proposition; agree to encodes acceptance of a proposal or condition; agree on encodes negotiated convergence on a topic. Similarly, look at encodes visual perception, look into encodes investigative scrutiny, and look after encodes custodial care. The diagnostic recognition of these prepositional semantic nuances is a distinguishing marker of C1 lexical precision, their conflation being a hallmark of insufficient differentiation. ### 9. Verbos sin preposición: el error de la preposición espuria Un error frecuente es añadir una preposición donde el inglés no la admite. Discuss something (no discuss about something), emphasise something (no emphasise on something), consider something (no consider about something), approach someone (no approach to someone). Esta preposición espuria refleja la interferencia del español y debe erradicarse. A2: Some verbs do not need a little word after them: "discuss the problem," not "discuss about the problem." B2: A frequent error is adding a preposition where English does not allow one: discuss something (not discuss about), emphasise something (not emphasise on), consider something (not consider about), approach someone (not approach to). This spurious preposition reflects Spanish interference and must be eradicated. C1: A high-frequency error consists in the insertion of a preposition where English categorically precludes one: discuss something, not discuss about something; emphasise something, not emphasise on something; consider something, not consider about something; approach someone, not approach to someone. These spurious prepositions are unambiguous artefacts of Spanish transfer and their eradication is a prerequisite for C1 certification, their persistence being a fossilisation diagnostic of sub-C1 syntactic control. ### 10. Patrones preposicionales en la escritura académica La prosa académica C1 despliega patrones preposicionales formales con frecuencia: to account for a phenomenon, to stem from a cause, to culminate in a result, to be consistent with evidence, to be conducive to innovation, to be reliant on funding, to be averse to risk. Dominar estas colocaciones preposicionales eleva la densidad y la precisión léxica del ensayo académico. A2: In academic writing, some word combinations sound professional, like "account for" and "consistent with." B2: C1 academic prose deploys formal prepositional patterns frequently: to account for a phenomenon, to stem from a cause, to culminate in a result, to be consistent with evidence, to be conducive to innovation, to be reliant on funding, to be averse to risk. Mastering these collocations raises lexical density and precision. C1: C1 academic prose exhibits a diagnostic frequency of formal prepositional collocations: to account for a phenomenon, to stem from a cause, to culminate in a result, to be consistent with evidence, to be conducive to innovation, to be reliant on funding and to be averse to risk. The idiomatic assimilation of these prepositional collocations elevates both the lexical density and the precisional granularity of the academic essay, their conspicuous absence conversely attenuating the impression of scholarly register. ### 11. Verbos de opinión y postura con preposición Los verbos de opinión y postura rigen preposiciones específicas: to subscribe to a view (suscribir una opinión), to allude to something (aludir a), to point to evidence (indicar), to object to a proposal (oponerse a), to allude to a study (aludir a), to dissent from a view (disentir de), to defer to an authority (deferir a). Su uso preciso en la argumentación académica es esencial. A2: Some verbs about opinions use specific words: "object to" and "point to." B2: Opinion and stance verbs govern specific prepositions: to subscribe to a view, to allude to something, to point to evidence, to object to a proposal, to dissent from a view, to defer to an authority. Their precise use in academic argumentation is essential. C1: Opinion and stance predicates select prepositions with categorical fixity: to subscribe to a view, to allude to something, to point to evidence, to object to a proposal, to dissent from a view and to defer to an authority. Their precise deployment within academic argumentation is indispensable, the substitution of one preposition for another, such as object at for object to, generating a registeral and semantic infraction that would diagnostically compromise C1 credibility. ### 12. Adjetivos de evaluación y crítica con preposición Los adjetivos evaluativos también rigen preposiciones: critical of (crítico con), indicative of (indicativo de), suggestive of (sugerente de), contemptuous of (despreciativo de), dismissive of (despectivo con), wary of (receloso de), conversant with (familiarizado con), averse to (reacio a). Su uso en reseñas y críticas académicas es recurrente y debe dominarse. A2: Some describing words use specific words too: "critical of" and "wary of." B2: Evaluative adjectives also govern prepositions: critical of, indicative of, suggestive of, contemptuous of, dismissive of, wary of, conversant with, averse to. Their use in academic reviews and critiques is recurrent and must be mastered. C1: Evaluative adjectives likewise govern complement prepositions: critical of, indicative of, suggestive of, contemptuous of, dismissive of, wary of, conversant with and averse to. Their recurrent deployment in academic reviews and critiques necessitates mastery, the prepositional error critical with for critical of being a fossilisation that would conspicuously attenuate the impression of C1 evaluative precision. ### 13. La alternancia entre gerundio y that-clause Algunos verbos admiten tanto un gerundio como una that-clause tras la preposición o directamente: to insist on leaving / to insist that he leave; to result in the policy being revised / to result in the policy being revised (gerundio); to acknowledge that / to acknowledge doing. La elección codifica matices de estructura y énfasis que el C1 debe manejar. A2: Some verbs can be followed by an -ing word or by "that." B2: Some verbs admit both a gerund and a that-clause: to insist on leaving / to insist that he leave; to acknowledge that / to acknowledge doing. The choice encodes structural and emphasis nuances that C1 must handle. C1: A class of verbs admits both gerundial and finite-clausal complementation: to insist on leaving alternates with to insist that he leave, and to acknowledge doing alternates with to acknowledge that he did. The selection encodes structural and focal nuances, the gerundial variant foregrounding process and the finite variant foregrounding propositional content, whose calibrated manipulation is a diagnostic of C1 syntactic sophistication. ### 14. Errores por interferencia de la lengua materna: catálogo El catálogo de errores por interferencia es amplio: depend of (de depender de, correcto depend on), consist in (de consistir en, correcto consist of para composición), think in (de pensar en, correcto think about), marry with (de casarse con, correcto marry sin preposición), listen music (de escuchar música, correcto listen to music). Identificar el origen del error acelera su erradicación. A2: Some mistakes come from your own language. For example, "depend of" is wrong; say "depend on." B2: The catalogue of interference errors is large: depend of (correct: depend on), consist in for composition (correct: consist of), think in (correct: think about), marry with (correct: marry), listen music (correct: listen to music). Identifying the source of the error accelerates eradication. C1: The catalogue of transfer-induced errors is extensive: depend of, projected from the Spanish depender de, versus the correct depend on; consist in projected from consistir en versus the correct consist of for compositional readings; think in projected from pensar en versus the correct think about; marry with projected from casarse con versus the correct marry without preposition; listen music projected from escuchar música versus the correct listen to music. The diagnostic identification of the transfer source accelerates the targeted eradication of each fossilisation. ### 15. Estrategias de consolidación de patrones preposicionales La consolidación exige agrupar los patrones por preposición y por campo semántico, crear tarjetas con verbo o adjetivo, preposición, colocación y frase de ejemplo, y practicar la reformulación activa. La exposición abundante a prosa académica auténtica, donde los patrones aparecen en contexto, es insustituible. La práctica de la traducción inversa, del español al inglés, expone las trampas de interferencia de manera directa. A2: To learn these patterns, group them and practice a lot. Read a lot of English. B2: Consolidation requires grouping patterns by preposition and semantic field, creating cards with verb or adjective, preposition, collocation and example sentence, and practising active reformulation. Abundant exposure to authentic academic prose is irreplaceable. Practising translation from Spanish to English exposes interference traps directly. C1: The consolidation of prepositional patterns necessitates their taxonomic organisation by preposition and semantic field, the construction of flashcards encoding the verb or adjective, its preposition, its canonical collocation and a contextually situated exemplar sentence, and the practice of active reformulation. Abundant immersion in authentic academic prose, wherein the patterns arise in natural context, remains the irreplaceable substrate of acquisition. The practice of inverse translation, from Spanish to English, directly exposes the interference traps whose navigation is constitutive of C1 prepositional mastery. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 Completa con la preposición correcta: The outcome will depend ______ the level of funding.
Ver solución on
### Ejercicio 2 Corrige el error de interferencia: The report consists in three sections.
Ver solución The report consists of three sections. ("Consist in" means to consist in the sense of to amount to; for composition, "consist of" is correct.)
### Ejercicio 3 Completa con la preposición: The investigation culminated ______ the resignation of the minister.
Ver solución in
### Ejercicio 4 Elige la preposición correcta: She is independent ______ her family's financial support.
Ver solución of (independent of, not independent on, despite the logical asymmetry with dependent on)
### Ejercicio 5 Completa con la preposición: The findings are consistent ______ the hypothesis.
Ver solución with
### Ejercicio 6 Corrige la preposición espuria: We discussed about the proposal for an hour.
Ver solución We discussed the proposal for an hour. ("Discuss" does not take a preposition.)
### Ejercicio 7 Completa con la preposición: The new policy is conducive ______ innovation.
Ver solución to
### Ejercicio 8 Distingue el significado: "agree with" vs "agree to" vs "agree on" — completa: I agree ______ you that we should agree ______ the terms and then agree ______ a date.
Ver solución I agree with you that we should agree to the terms and then agree on a date. (agree with = share opinion; agree to = accept terms; agree on = reach agreement on a topic)
### Ejercicio 9 Completa con la preposición: The committee must comply ______ the new regulations.
Ver solución with
### Ejercicio 10 Corrige el error: She is prone for making mistakes under pressure.
Ver solución She is prone to making mistakes under pressure. (prone to, not prone for)
### Ejercicio 11 Completa con la preposición: The theory stems ______ a misunderstanding of the data.
Ver solución from
### Ejercicio 12 Elige la preposición correcta: The reviewer was critical ______ the methodology.
Ver solución of (critical of, not critical with)
### Ejercicio 13 Completa con la preposición: He objected ______ the proposal on procedural grounds.
Ver solución to
### Ejercicio 14 Corrige el error de interferencia: I am thinking in changing jobs.
Ver solución I am thinking about changing jobs. (think about, not think in)
### Ejercicio 15 Completa con la preposición: The evidence is indicative ______ a deeper problem.
Ver solución of
### Ejercicio 16 Explica en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) la diferencia entre consist of y consist in, con un ejemplo de cada uno.
Ver solución Consist of denotes composition, the parts that make up a whole: The committee consists of ten members. Consist in, by contrast, denotes definitional equivalence, what something essentially amounts to: True leadership consists in inspiring others to exceed themselves. The former answers the question what is it made of, the latter answers what does it amount to. Conflating the two generates a semantic distortion incompatible with C1 precision.
### Ejercicio 17 Completa con la preposición: The company is heavily reliant ______ government contracts.
Ver solución on
### Ejercicio 18 Corrige el error: She married with a lawyer last year.
Ver solución She married a lawyer last year. ("Marry" does not take a preposition in this sense.)
### Ejercicio 19 Redacta en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) un breve párrafo académico que use al menos cuatro patrones preposicionales formales distintos.
Ver solución The current crisis stems from a decade of regulatory neglect and culminates in a loss of public trust. The proposed reforms, though consistent with the evidence, are not conducive to swift recovery, as they remain heavily reliant on political will. The government must comply with international standards and dispose of the dilatory compromises that have long obstructed progress, lest the opportunity for meaningful change be forfeited.
## Resumen de la unidad En esta unidad del Language Lab has entrenado los patrones preposicionales de verbos y adjetivos, uno de los territorios más exigentes del inglés C1. Has consolidado verbos con on (depend on, rely on, insist on), con in (result in, culminate in, consist in), con of (consist of, dispose of, conceive of) y con with (comply with, contend with, coincide with). Has dominado adjetivos como dependent on, independent of, consistent with, prone to y conducive to. Has aprendido a distinguir alternancias preposicionales con cambio de significado (agree with / agree to / agree on) y a erradicar preposiciones espurias por interferencia (discuss about, think in, marry with). Los 19 ejercicios te han entrenado en la precisión preposicional que define el registro académico C1. En la siguiente unidad, la 63, el Language Lab aborda la formación de palabras, donde la precisión nominal se convierte en el foco.

author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Domina los phrasal verbs de registro formal en contextos argumentativos: to bring about, to put forward, to rule out, to stem from, to account for. Teoría sobre separabilidad, colocación y alternancia con sinónimos latinos, más 19 ejercicios inglés C1 gratis para consolidar el uso argumentativo preciso.
