faqs.question: ¿Qué es un phrasal verb y por qué importa en C1?
faqs.answer: Un phrasal verb combina un verbo con una partícula (preposición o adverbio) cuyo significado conjunto no es literal: 'to bring about' significa 'causar', no 'traer alrededor'. En C1 importa porque muchos phrasal verbs son de registro formal y aparecen en ensayos y debates, mientras que otros son informales y deben evitarse en contextos académicos.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre phrasal verb separable e inseparable?
faqs.answer: Los separables permiten intercalar el objeto entre el verbo y la partícula: 'turn the offer down' o 'turn down the offer'. Los inseparables no lo permiten: 'look into the matter' (no 'look the matter into'). Con pronombres, los separables obligan a la separación: 'turn it down' (no 'turn down it').

faqs.question: ¿Qué phrasal verbs son apropiados en un ensayo académico C1?
faqs.answer: Son apropiados los de registro formal: 'to account for' (explicar), 'to bring about' (causar), 'to put forward' (proponer), 'to rule out' (descartar), 'to set out' (exponer), 'to stem from' (derivarse de), 'to point to' (indicar), 'to boil down to' (reducirse a). Los informales como 'chuck out' o 'put up with' deben evitarse.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es la colocación de un phrasal verb?
faqs.answer: La colocación es la combinación habitual y natural del phrasal verb con ciertos sustantivos. Decimos 'to mount an argument', 'to put forward a proposal', 'to account for a discrepancy'. Aprender estas combinaciones fijas es lo que hace que el uso suene natural y preciso en C1.

content:
El Language Lab es el espacio del curso donde la gramática se vuelve laboratorio: se aísla un fenómeno, se examina bajo la lupa y se entrena hasta la automatización. En esta unidad el foco son los phrasal verbs de registro formal en contextos argumentativos. A nivel C1, el dominio de los phrasal verbs no consiste en memorizar listas, sino en saber cuándo un phrasal verb eleva el registro y cuándo un sinónimo latino es más apropiado, y en conocer las colocaciones que hacen que cada uso suene natural. Cada concepto se presenta en tres niveles. El A2 ofrece la versión más sencilla, el B2 añade complejidad operativa y el C1 presenta el uso formal y argumentativo con sus matices de registro y colocación. A2: Phrasal verbs are verbs with small words like "up" or "out." For example, "give up" means to stop trying. B2: Phrasal verbs combine a verb with a particle whose joint meaning is not literal. At C1, you learn which phrasal verbs suit formal argumentation and which are too informal for academic writing. C1: The phrasal verb, a verb-particle compound whose composite meaning is non-compositional, constitutes a diagnostic feature of idiomatic English. C1 mastery resides not in rote memorisation but in the register-sensitive deployment of formal phrasal verbs within argumentative discourse, coupled with the strategic capacity to alternate them with their Latinate synonyms according to the stylistic demands of the context. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 61 C1](/curso-c1/unit-61)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 60 C1: Preparación examen CAE/IELTS/TOEFL](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-60-preparacion-examen)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 62 C1: Language Lab — Verbo/adjetivo + preposición](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-62-language-lab-verbo-adjetivo-preposicion)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría: Phrasal verbs en argumento ### 1. La anatomía del phrasal verb Un phrasal verb combina un verbo léxico con una partícula (preposición o adverbio) cuyo significado conjunto no se deduce literalmente de sus partes. To bring about significa causar, no traer alrededor; to put forward significa proponer, no poner adelante. Esta no composicionalidad es la marca definitoria del phrasal verb y la razón por la que deben aprenderse como unidades léxicas completas. A2: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a small word. Together they mean something new. B2: A phrasal verb combines a lexical verb with a particle whose joint meaning is not literal. To bring about means to cause, not to bring around. This non-compositionality is what makes phrasal verbs learned as whole units. C1: The phrasal verb fuses a lexical verb with a particle, prepositional or adverbial, whose composite semantics are irreducible to the sum of the constituent meanings. To bring about denotes causation rather than literal circumferential conveyance; to put forward denotes propositional advancement rather than literal spatial relocation. This semantic non-compositionality is the defining diacritic of the phrasal verb and the rationale for its acquisition as an indivisible lexical unit. ### 2. Phrasal verbs separables e inseparables Los phrasal verbs separables permiten intercalar el objeto entre el verbo y la partícula: turn the offer down o turn down the offer. Los inseparables no lo permiten: look into the matter (no look the matter into). Con pronombres, los separables obligan a la separación: turn it down, nunca turn down it. Conocer esta distinción evita errores sintácticos que delatan un nivel inferior. A2: Some phrasal verbs can be split: "turn down the offer" or "turn the offer down." With words like "it," you must split: "turn it down." B2: Separable phrasal verbs allow the object between the verb and the particle: turn the offer down or turn down the offer. Inseparable ones do not: look into the matter. With pronouns, separables must split: turn it down, never turn down it. C1: Separable phrasal verbs license the interpolation of the direct object between the verb and the particle, yielding alternants such as turn the offer down and turn down the offer. Inseparable phrasal verbs preclude such interpolation, look into the matter being the only admissible ordering. A further constraint is that pronominal objects obligatorily trigger separation in separable verbs, turn it down being grammatical and turn down it ungrammatical, a distinction whose mastery precludes a syntactic error that would conspicuously signal sub-C1 competence. ### 3. Phrasal verbs de tres partes Algunos phrasal verbs constan de verbo más dos partículas: to come up with (idear), to get away with (salirse con la suya), to look down on (despreciar), to put up with (tolerar), to get back to (volver a un tema). Estos son siempre inseparables y suelen ser de registro informal o neutro, por lo que su uso en ensayos académicos debe ponderarse. A2: Some phrasal verbs have two small words: "come up with" means to think of an idea. B2: Three-part phrasal verbs consist of verb plus two particles: to come up with, to get away with, to look down on, to put up with, to get back to. They are always inseparable and tend to be informal or neutral, so their use in academic essays should be weighed carefully. C1: A subset of phrasal verbs comprises verb plus two particles, to come up with, to get away with, to look down on, to put up with, to get back to, and these are categorically inseparable. Their register distribution skews toward the informal or neutral, and consequently their inclusion in academic prose warrants judicious calibration, with formal Latinate alternatives preferred where the stylistic stakes are high. ### 4. Phrasal verbs formales para la argumentación Ciertos phrasal verbs son de registro formal y encajan en ensayos y debates: to account for (explicar), to bring about (causar), to put forward (proponer), to rule out (descartar), to set out (exponer), to stem from (derivarse de), to point to (indicar), to boil down to (reducirse a), to spell out (explicitar), to bear out (confirmar). Su uso adecuado en contextos argumentativos es un indicador fiable del C1. A2: Some phrasal verbs sound formal and are good for essays, like "to bring about" (cause) and "to put forward" (propose). B2: Certain phrasal verbs are formal and fit essays and debates: to account for, to bring about, to put forward, to rule out, to set out, to stem from, to point to, to boil down to, to spell out, to bear out. Using them correctly in argumentation signals C1. C1: A delineable subset of phrasal verbs possesses the register elevation requisite for argumentative and expository prose: to account for, to bring about, to put forward, to rule out, to set out, to stem from, to point to, to boil down to, to spell out and to bear out. Their idiomatic integration within argumentative discourse functions as a diagnostically reliable index of C1 competence, their conspicuous absence conversely indicative of a lexical plateau beneath the target proficiency. ### 5. Alternancia con sinónimos latinos: la dialéctica del registro El inglés C1 exige saber alternar entre phrasal verbs y sus sinónimos latinos según el registro. To bring about / to cause; to put forward / to propose; to rule out / to exclude; to stem from / to originate in; to point to / to indicate; to spell out / to elucidate. En un ensayo denso, el sinónimo latino puede ser más apropiado; en un debate oral, el phrasal verb aporta fluidez y naturalidad. A2: Many phrasal verbs have longer words that mean the same thing. "Bring about" and "cause" are similar. B2: C1 English requires alternating between phrasal verbs and their Latinate synonyms by register. To bring about / to cause; to put forward / to propose; to rule out / to exclude; to stem from / to originate in; to point to / to indicate; to spell out / to elucidate. In a dense essay, the Latinate synonym may be more apt; in oral debate, the phrasal verb adds fluency. C1: C1 English demands the register-sensitive alternation between phrasal verbs and their Latinate equivalents. The paradigmatic pairings, to bring about and to cause, to put forward and to propose, to rule out and to exclude, to stem from and to originate in, to point to and to indicate, to spell out and to elucidate, instantiate a stylistic duality whose exploitation is itself a marker of proficiency. In lexically dense expository prose, the Latinate variant may be preferred for its morphological compactness; in extemporaneous oral debate, the phrasal verb confers a fluency and idiomaticity that the Latinate alternative cannot replicate. ### 6. Colocaciones argumentativas con phrasal verbs La colocación es la combinación habitual del phrasal verb con ciertos sustantivos. To mount an argument, to put forward a proposal, to account for a discrepancy, to rule out a possibility, to bring about a change, to set out the reasons, to point to evidence, to bear out a hypothesis. Aprender estas combinaciones fijas es lo que separa el uso correcto del uso idiomático. A2: Some words go together naturally. We say "put forward a proposal," not "put forward a cat." B2: Collocation is the habitual combination of a phrasal verb with certain nouns. To mount an argument, to put forward a proposal, to account for a discrepancy, to rule out a possibility, to bring about a change, to set out the reasons, to point to evidence, to bear out a hypothesis. Learning these fixed combinations separates correct from idiomatic usage. C1: Collocation denotes the statistically conventionalised co-occurrence of a phrasal verb with a delimited class of nominal complements. The entrenched pairings, to mount an argument, to put forward a proposal, to account for a discrepancy, to rule out a possibility, to bring about a change, to set out the reasons, to point to evidence and to bear out a hypothesis, constitute the idiomatic bedrock of argumentative phrasal usage. Their assimilation is what bifurcates the merely correct from the authentically idiomatic C1 user. ### 7. To bring about: causación y cambio To bring about significa causar o provocar un cambio, especialmente significativo. Se coloca con change, reform, transformation, revolution, shift, collapse. Su sinónimo latino es to cause o to effect. En un ensayo sobre política, to bring about lasting reform es más idiomático que to cause lasting reform, aunque ambos son correctos. A2: "Bring about" means to make something happen, like a big change. B2: To bring about means to cause or provoke a significant change. It collocates with change, reform, transformation, revolution, shift and collapse. Its Latinate synonym is to cause or to effect. In a politics essay, to bring about lasting reform is more idiomatic than to cause lasting reform. C1: To bring about encodes the causation of a significant change or transformation, and collocates with change, reform, transformation, revolution, shift and collapse. Its Latinate equivalents are to cause and to effect, the latter a markedly formal variant. In political expository prose, to bring about lasting reform exhibits an idiomaticity that to cause lasting reform, though grammatically impeccable, lacks, illustrating the registeral subtlety that distinguishes C1 lexical selection. ### 8. To put forward: proposición y argumentación To put forward significa proponer o presentar una idea, argumento o candidatura. Se coloca con proposal, argument, theory, candidate, suggestion, hypothesis. Su sinónimo latino es to propose, to present o to advance. En un debate, to put forward a compelling argument es la formulación natural; en un artículo académico denso, to advance a compelling argument puede ser preferible. A2: "Put forward" means to suggest an idea or a plan. B2: To put forward means to propose or present an idea, argument or candidacy. It collocates with proposal, argument, theory, candidate, suggestion and hypothesis. Its Latinate synonym is to propose, to present or to advance. In a debate, to put forward a compelling argument is natural; in a dense academic article, to advance a compelling argument may be preferable. C1: To put forward encodes the propositional or presentational advancement of an idea, argument or candidacy, collocating with proposal, argument, theory, candidate, suggestion and hypothesis. Its Latinate congeners are to propose, to present and to advance. In oral debate, to put forward a compelling argument constitutes the unmarked formulation; in lexically dense academic prose, to advance a compelling argument may be stylistically preferred, a registeral alternation that the proficient C1 user navigates with reflexive ease. ### 9. To rule out: exclusión y refutación To rule out significa descartar o excluir una posibilidad. Se coloca con possibility, option, scenario, explanation, candidate. Su sinónimo latino es to exclude o to preclude. En argumentación, to rule out an alternative explanation es una jugada retórica poderosa que estrecha el espacio de hipótesis competidoras. A2: "Rule out" means to say something is not possible. B2: To rule out means to discard or exclude a possibility. It collocates with possibility, option, scenario, explanation and candidate. Its Latinate synonym is to exclude or to preclude. In argumentation, to rule out an alternative explanation is a powerful rhetorical move that narrows the space of competing hypotheses. C1: To rule out encodes the eliminative exclusion of a possibility, collocating with possibility, option, scenario, explanation and candidate. Its Latinate equivalents are to exclude and to preclude, the latter encoding a stronger logical preemption. In argumentative discourse, to rule out an alternative explanation constitutes a rhetorically potent manoeuvre that contracts the space of competing hypotheses, a discursive function central to the logic of refutation at C1. ### 10. To account for: explicación y rendición de cuentas To account for significa explicar o dar razón de algo, especialmente una discrepancia, un fenómeno o un resultado. Se coloca con discrepancy, phenomenon, variance, behaviour, outcome, failure. Su sinónimo latino es to explain o to elucidate. Es uno de los phrasal verbs más rentables en ensayos académicos. A2: "Account for" means to explain why something happened. B2: To account for means to explain or give a reason for something, especially a discrepancy, phenomenon or result. It collocates with discrepancy, phenomenon, variance, behaviour, outcome and failure. Its Latinate synonym is to explain or to elucidate. It is one of the most useful phrasal verbs in academic essays. C1: To account for encodes the provision of an explanatory rationale for a phenomenon, particularly a discrepancy, variance or outcome, collocating with discrepancy, phenomenon, variance, behaviour, outcome and failure. Its Latinate equivalents are to explain and to elucidate, the latter imparting a more formal explanatory register. It ranks among the most discursively productive phrasal verbs in academic expository prose, its versatility rendering it indispensable to the C1 argumentative repertoire. ### 11. To stem from y to boil down to: origen y esencia To stem from significa derivarse de o tener su origen en. Se coloca con problem, criticism, confusion, inequality, discrepancy. To boil down to significa reducirse a o consistir esencialmente en. Se coloca con question, issue, matter, debate. Ambos son formales y útiles para la síntesis argumentativa. A2: "Stem from" means to come from. "Boil down to" means to be really about one main thing. B2: To stem from means to derive from or originate in. It collocates with problem, criticism, confusion, inequality and discrepancy. To boil down to means to reduce to or essentially consist in. It collocates with question, issue, matter and debate. Both are formal and useful for argumentative synthesis. C1: To stem from encodes derivational origin, collocating with problem, criticism, confusion, inequality and discrepancy, and admits the Latinate equivalent to originate in. To boil down to encodes reductive essentialisation, the compression of a complex matter to its constitutive core, collocating with question, issue, matter and debate. Both occupy the formal register and are instrumentally valuable for argumentative synthesis, the former tracing aetiology, the latter distilling essence. ### 12. To set out y to spell out: exposición y explicitación To set out significa exponer o presentar de manera estructurada. Se coloca con reasons, arguments, proposals, plan, stall. To spell out significa explicitar o detallar punto por punto. Se coloca with implications, consequences, details, terms. Ambos son formales y propios de la prosa académica y administrativa. A2: "Set out" means to explain something in a clear order. "Spell out" means to explain in a lot of detail. B2: To set out means to lay out or present in a structured manner. It collocates with reasons, arguments, proposals and plan. To spell out means to make explicit or detail point by point. It collocates with implications, consequences, details and terms. Both are formal and typical of academic and administrative prose. C1: To set out encodes the structured exposition of content, collocating with reasons, arguments, proposals, plan and stall, and admits the Latinate equivalent to expound. To spell out encodes the explicit articulation of content point by point, collocating with implications, consequences, details and terms, and admits the Latinate equivalent to elucidate. Both inhabit the formal register characteristic of academic and administrative prose, the former supplying structural scaffolding, the latter supplying granular explicitness. ### 13. Phrasal verbs que deben evitarse en registro formal Ciertos phrasal verbs son demasiado informales para la prosa académica: to chuck out (descartar), to put up with (tolerar), to bottle up (reprimir), to boss around (mandonear), to chicken out (acobardarse), to pig out (atracarse). En su lugar, el C1 prefiere to discard, to tolerate, to repress, to dominate, to withdraw, to overeat. La conciencia de esta frontera de registro es esencial. A2: Some phrasal verbs are too casual for formal writing. Use longer words instead. B2: Certain phrasal verbs are too informal for academic prose: to chuck out, to put up with, to bottle up, to boss around, to chicken out, to pig out. C1 prefers to discard, to tolerate, to repress, to dominate, to withdraw, to overeat. Awareness of this register boundary is essential. C1: A delimitable class of phrasal verbs is registerally inappropriate for academic prose: to chuck out, to put up with, to bottle up, to boss around, to chicken out and to pig out all occupy the informal register and would, if deployed in scholarly writing, constitute a registeral infraction. The C1 user accordingly deploys their Latinate equivalents, to discard, to tolerate, to repress, to dominate, to withdraw and to overeat, a registeral policing whose reflexive execution is a diagnostic of advanced competence. ### 14. Phrasal verbs en el speaking formal: debate y presentación En el speaking formal, como un debate o una presentación académica, los phrasal verbs aportan naturalidad y fluidez sin sacrificar el registro. To put forward a point, to build on an argument, to draw on evidence, to put across an idea, to follow through on a commitment son formulaciones idiomáticas que suenan persuasivas. La clave es combinar phrasal verbs formales con estructuras complejas. A2: When you speak formally, phrasal verbs can make you sound natural and clear. B2: In formal speaking, like a debate or academic presentation, phrasal verbs add naturalness and fluency without sacrificing register. To put forward a point, to build on an argument, to draw on evidence, to put across an idea and to follow through on a commitment are idiomatic and persuasive. Combine formal phrasal verbs with complex structures. C1: In formal oral discourse, such as competitive debate or academic presentation, phrasal verbs confer idiomatic naturalness and fluency without compromising registeral elevation. The formulations to put forward a point, to build on an argument, to draw on evidence, to put across an idea and to follow through on a commitment instantiate the persuasive idiomaticity that characterises proficient oral argumentation. The strategic synthesis of formal phrasal verbs with complex syntactic structures, inversion, mixed conditionals and concessive clauses, is what distinguishes the C1 oral performance. ### 15. Estrategias de aprendizaje y consolidación de phrasal verbs La consolidación de phrasal verbs exige agruparlos por registro y por campo semántico, no alfabéticamente. Crear tarjetas con el phrasal verb, su sinónimo latino, su colocación y una frase de ejemplo en contexto argumentativo es eficaz. Practicar la reformulación, parafraseando un texto reemplazando sinónimos latinos por phrasal verbs y viceversa, entrena la alternancia de registro. La exposición abundante a prosa académica auténtica es insustituible. A2: To learn phrasal verbs, group them by topic. Make cards with an example sentence. B2: Consolidating phrasal verbs requires grouping them by register and semantic field, not alphabetically. Create cards with the phrasal verb, its Latinate synonym, its collocation and an example sentence in argumentative context. Practice reformulation, paraphrasing a text by swapping Latinate synonyms for phrasal verbs and vice versa. Abundant exposure to authentic academic prose is irreplaceable. C1: The consolidation of phrasal verbs necessitates their taxonomic organisation by register and semantic field rather than alphabetical ordering, a structuring that mirrors their functional distribution. The construction of flashcards encoding the phrasal verb, its Latinate synonym, its canonical collocation and a contextually argumentative exemplar sentence is empirically efficacious. The practice of bidirectional reformulation, paraphrasing a source text by substituting Latinate synonyms for phrasal verbs and conversely, trains the registeral alternation that is the hallmark of C1 lexical agility. Abundant immersion in authentic academic prose remains the irreplaceable substrate of acquisition. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 Sustituye el sinónimo latino por el phrasal verbal formal adecuado: The reforms caused a profound transformation of the sector.
Ver solución The reforms brought about a profound transformation of the sector.
### Ejercicio 2 Completa la colocación: The committee will ______ a proposal at the next meeting.
Ver solución put forward
### Ejercicio 3 Reescribe con to rule out: The detective excluded the possibility of suicide.
Ver solución The detective ruled out the possibility of suicide.
### Ejercicio 4 Elige la opción gramaticalmente correcta (separabilidad): The committee turned ______ the proposal. / The committee turned the proposal ______.
Ver solución Both are correct: "The committee turned down the proposal" and "The committee turned the proposal down." However, with a pronoun, only "The committee turned it down" is correct (not "turned down it").
### Ejercicio 5 Completa con to account for: How do you ______ the discrepancy between the two datasets?
Ver solución account for
### Ejercicio 6 Sustituye por el phrasal verb formal: The problem originates in a lack of regulation.
Ver solución The problem stems from a lack of regulation.
### Ejercicio 7 Reescribe con to spell out: The report did not make the implications explicit.
Ver solución The report did not spell out the implications.
### Ejercicio 8 Identifica el phrasal verb inapropiado para un ensayo académico y propón una alternativa formal: The government chucked out the proposal.
Ver solución "Chuck out" is too informal for academic prose. Formal alternative: The government discarded the proposal (or: The government rejected the proposal).
### Ejercicio 9 Completa con to boil down to: The whole debate ______ a question of priorities.
Ver solución boils down to
### Ejercicio 10 Reescribe con to set out: The minister presented the reasons for the policy in a structured manner.
Ver solución The minister set out the reasons for the policy.
### Ejercicio 11 Completa con el pronombre correcto (separabilidad obligatoria): They put the offer forward → They put ______ forward.
Ver solución it (They put it forward. Separable phrasal verbs must split with pronouns: not "put forward it.")
### Ejercicio 12 Sustituye por el phrasal verb formal: The evidence confirmed the hypothesis.
Ver solución The evidence bore out the hypothesis.
### Ejercicio 13 Completa con to point to: Several indicators ______ a forthcoming recession.
Ver solución point to
### Ejercicio 14 Reescribe con un phrasal verb de tres partes (formal-neutro): The team could not devise a solution in time.
Ver solución The team could not come up with a solution in time.
### Ejercicio 15 Elige entre el phrasal verb y el sinónimo latino según el registro (ensayo académico denso): "The findings ___ a reconsideration of the theory." a) point to b) indicate
Ver solución Both are acceptable, but in a lexically dense academic essay, "indicate" (b) may be stylistically preferred for its compactness. In oral debate, "point to" (a) would be more idiomatic. Either is grammatically correct at C1.
### Ejercicio 16 Explica en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) cuándo preferirías to put forward sobre to propose.
Ver solución I would prefer to put forward in oral debate or semi-formal discussion, where its idiomatic fluency lends the argument a natural, persuasive rhythm without sacrificing register. To propose, by contrast, carries a more markedly formal, even bureaucratic tone, better suited to dense academic prose or official documentation. The choice is ultimately registeral: to put forward for spoken fluency, to propose for written formality, though both remain grammatically impeccable at C1.
### Ejercicio 17 Completa con to build on o to draw on: The second study ______ the findings of the first.
Ver solución builds on (to build on = to extend or develop further; to draw on = to use as a resource. "Builds on" fits extending findings; "draws on" would fit using findings as a resource.)
### Ejercicio 18 Reescribe con to follow through on: The government did not complete its commitment to reform.
Ver solución The government did not follow through on its commitment to reform.
### Ejercicio 19 Redacta en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) un breve argumento que use al menos tres phrasal verbs formales distintos.
Ver solución The current crisis stems from a decade of regulatory neglect, and no partial measure can bring about the transformation required. The government must put forward a comprehensive proposal that sets out the reasons for reform and rules out the dilatory compromises of the past. Unless policymakers spell out the implications of inaction, the public will not grasp the stakes, and the opportunity for meaningful change will be forfeited.
## Resumen de la unidad En esta unidad del Language Lab has entrenado el uso de phrasal verbs de registro formal en contextos argumentativos. Has aprendido la anatomía del phrasal verb, la distinción entre separables e inseparables, la existencia de phrasal verbs de tres partes y la frontera entre phrasal verbs formales e informales. Has consolidado colocaciones como to bring about a change, to put forward a proposal, to rule out a possibility, to account for a discrepancy y to stem from a problem. Has practicado la alternancia con sinónimos latinos (to bring about / to cause, to put forward / to propose, to rule out / to exclude) según el registro, una habilidad distintiva del C1. Los 19 ejercicios te han entrenado en la reformulación y el uso idiomático. En la siguiente unidad, la 62, el Language Lab se centra en los patrones preposicionales de verbo y adjetivo, otro territorio donde la precisión C1 se gana o se pierde.

title: Ejercicios y Estrategias para CAE, IELTS y TOEFL C1
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Prepárate estratégicamente para los exámenes CAE, IELTS y TOEFL con esta unidad C1: gestión del tiempo por sección, skimming y scanning, estructuras y léxico que los examinadores esperan, y las trampas más comunes a evitar. Teoría detallada y 19 ejercicios inglés C1 gratis orientados a la estrategia.
description: En esta unidad del curso de inglés C1 gratis aprendes a prepararte estratégicamente para los exámenes CAE, IELTS y TOEFL, a gestionar el tiempo en cada...

keywords: preparación examen CAE IELTS TOEFL C1

faqs.question: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre CAE, IELTS y TOEFL?
faqs.answer: El CAE (C1 Advanced) de Cambridge certifica el nivel C1 de por vida. El IELTS evalúa inglés académico o general y su validez es de dos años; es requisito común para universidades angloparlantes. El TOEFL, también válido dos años, es un examen principalmente académico y muy usado en Estados Unidos. Los tres exigen un dominio C1 para las puntuaciones más altas.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se gestiona el tiempo en la sección de escritura del IELTS?
faqs.answer: En el IELTS Academic Writing tienes 60 minutos para dos tareas: Task 1 (150 palabras, descripción de gráfico) y Task 2 (250 palabras, ensayo argumentativo). Se recomienda dedicar unos 20 minutos a Task 1 y 40 a Task 2, dejando 2-3 minutos finales para revisar gramática y coherencia.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es el 'skimming' y el 'scanning' en la comprensión lectora?
faqs.answer: El skimming es la lectura rápida para captar la idea general de un texto; el scanning es la búsqueda de información específica, como un nombre o una fecha. En exámenes como CAE e IELTS, combinar ambas técnicas permite responder con eficacia dentro del tiempo límite sin leer cada palabra.

faqs.question: ¿Qué errores frecuentes restan puntos en el speaking del CAE?
faqs.answer: Los más comunes son las pausas prolongadas por falta de fluidez, el uso repetitivo de vocabulario básico en lugar de sinónimos C1, la ausencia de estructuras complejas (inversión, condicionales mixtas) y no interactuar con el interlocutor en la fase colaborativa. Evitar estos errores eleva notablemente la puntuación.

content:
Llegar al final del curso C1 significa haber consolidado gramática, léxico y destrezas; pero el examen exige una dimensión adicional: la estrategia. Saber gestionar el tiempo, reconocer las trampas de los distractores, desplegar las estructuras que los examinadores esperan y mantener la compostura bajo presión es lo que separa una puntuación sobresaliente de una meramente aprobada. Esta unidad integra todo lo aprendido en el curso y lo orienta hacia los tres exámenes de referencia del nivel C1: CAE, IELTS y TOEFL. Cada concepto se presenta en tres niveles. El A2 ofrece la idea esencial, el B2 añade complejidad operativa y el C1 presenta el léxico y las estrategias avanzadas que distinguen a los candidatos con puntuaciones altas. A2: When you take an exam, you need to be ready. You must use your time well and not panic. B2: Exam preparation is not only about language but also about strategy. You must manage your time across sections, spot distractors in reading tasks, and display the advanced structures examiners look for. Calm under pressure is essential. C1: Examination at C1 level constitutes a high-stakes performance in which linguistic competence and strategic acumen must converge. The candidate must calibrate time allocation per section, circumvent the distractor traps embedded in multiple-choice items, and strategically showcase the complex grammatical structures and lexical range that examiners diagnostic of C1 proficiency reward. Composure under temporal pressure is itself a criterion-referenced competency. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 60 C1](/curso-c1/unit-60)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 59 C1: Consolidación gramatical global](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-59-consolidacion-gramatical-global)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 61 C1: Language Lab — Phrasal verbs en argumento](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-61-language-lab-phrasal-verbs-argumento)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría: Estrategia y tiempo en CAE, IELTS y TOEFL ### 1. Los tres exámenes: estructura y filosofía El CAE (C1 Advanced) de Cambridge certifica el nivel C1 de manera vitalicia y evalúa reading, writing, listening, speaking y use of English. El IELTS mide inglés académico o general con validez de dos años; es requisito habitual de universidades angloparlantes. El TOEFL, también válido dos años, es un examen principalmente académico muy usado en Estados Unidos. Comprender la filosofía de cada examen orienta toda la preparación. A2: There are three famous English exams. They check your reading, writing, listening and speaking. Each one is a little different. B2: The CAE certifies C1 level for life and tests reading, writing, listening, speaking and use of English. The IELTS measures academic or general English with two-year validity. The TOEFL is mainly academic and popular in the USA. Understanding each exam's philosophy guides preparation. C1: The CAE (C1 Advanced), administered by Cambridge, confers lifetime certification of C1 proficiency across reading, writing, listening, speaking and use of English components. The IELTS, with a two-year validity window, gauges academic or general English and constitutes a gatekeeping requirement for numerous anglophone universities. The TOEFL, likewise valid for two years, is a predominantly academic instrument favoured by US institutions. Internalising the distinctive philosophy and architecture of each examination calibrates the entirety of one's preparatory strategy. ### 2. Gestión del tiempo por sección: el plan maestro La gestión del tiempo es la habilidad estratégica más decisiva. En el CAE Reading, se recomienda dedicar unos 50 minutos al texto largo y 30 al resto. En el IELTS Writing, 20 minutos para Task 1 y 40 para Task 2. En el TOEFL Reading, aproximadamente 18 minutos por pasaje. Un cronómetro mental y la disciplina de no atascarse en una pregunta son esenciales. A2: In an exam, do not spend too much time on one question. If a question is hard, move on and come back later. B2: Time management is the most decisive strategic skill. In CAE Reading, allocate about 50 minutes to the long text and 30 to the rest. In IELTS Writing, spend 20 minutes on Task 1 and 40 on Task 2. A mental stopwatch and the discipline not to get stuck are essential. C1: Temporal management constitutes the single most decisive strategic competency in high-stakes examination. In CAE Reading, the prescribed allocation approximates 50 minutes to the extended text and 30 to the remaining items. In IELTS Writing, the optimal partition is 20 minutes for Task 1 and 40 for Task 2, with a two-to-three-minute terminal buffer for proofreading. In TOEFL Reading, approximately 18 minutes per passage is advisable. A disciplined refusal to become mired in any single item is the sine qua non of section completion. ### 3. Skimming y scanning en comprensión lectora El skimming es la lectura rápida para captar la idea general; el scanning, la búsqueda de información específica como nombres o fechas. En CAE e IELTS, combinar ambas permite responder con eficacia sin leer cada palabra. El skimming se aplica primero al pasaje completo; el scanning, después, a las preguntas individuales para localizar párrafos relevantes. A2: You can read fast to get the main idea. You can also look for a specific word or number quickly. B2: Skimming is fast reading for the main idea; scanning is searching for specific information like names or dates. In CAE and IELTS, combining both lets you answer efficiently without reading every word. Skim the passage first, then scan to locate relevant paragraphs. C1: Skimming, the rapid traversal of a text for its global gist, and scanning, the targeted retrieval of discrete informational items such as names or dates, constitute the twin methodologies of efficient reading comprehension. In CAE and IELTS, their synergistic deployment enables accurate response formulation without exhaustive per-word processing. The prescribed sequence is an initial skim of the passage in its entirety, followed by question-driven scanning to triangulate the pertinent paragraphs. ### 4. Distractores y trampas en multiple choice Los distractores son opciones incorrectas diseñadas para parecer plausibles. A menudo parafrasean el texto de manera casi correcta pero introducen un matiz falso, una generalización indebida o una inversión de sentido. La estrategia C1 exige volver siempre al texto y verificar que la opción no contradiga ni extienda lo afirmado. A2: In multiple choice, some wrong answers look right. You must check the text before you choose. B2: Distractors are wrong options designed to look plausible. They often paraphrase the text almost correctly but introduce a false nuance, an undue generalisation or an inversion of meaning. The C1 strategy is always to return to the text and verify the option. C1: Distractors are incorrect options engineered to mimic plausibility, typically via near-faithful paraphrase that nonetheless introduces a subtle falsification, an unwarranted generalisation or an inversion of the source proposition. The C1-grade counterstrategy mandates a reflexive return to the text to verify that the selected option neither contradicts nor extrapolates beyond what is explicitly or defensibly inferable from the passage, a discipline that neutralises the most common source of avoidable error. ### 5. La escritura del ensayo: coherencia, cohesión y registro En IELTS Task 2 y en el ensayo del CAE, los examinadores evalúan coherencia, cohesión, léxico y gramática. La coherencia exige una tesis clara y argumentos lógicos; la cohesión, conectores variados y referencia anafórica precisa; el léxico, sinónimos y colocaciones; la gramática, estructuras complejas sin errores que impidan la comprensión. A2: When you write an essay, you need a clear main idea, good linking words and correct grammar. B2: In IELTS Task 2 and the CAE essay, examiners assess coherence, cohesion, vocabulary and grammar. Coherence requires a clear thesis and logical arguments; cohesion needs varied connectors and precise reference; vocabulary needs synonyms and collocations; grammar needs complex structures without blocking errors. C1: In IELTS Task 2 and the CAE essay, the assessment criteria triangulate coherence, cohesion, lexical resource and grammatical range and accuracy. Coherence demands an explicit thesis scaffolded by logically sequenced arguments; cohesion requires a diversified connector inventory and precise anaphoric reference; lexical resource is calibrated by synonymic flexibility and collocational idiomaticity; grammatical range is evidenced by the deployment of complex structures, inversion, mixed conditionals and reduced relatives, unmarred by error of a severity that impedes intelligibility. ### 6. Léxico de alta rentabilidad para el examen Ciertos campos léxicos aparecen recurrentemente en los exámenes C1: el de la opinión y la postura (to contend, to maintain, to posit, to argue that), el de la causa y el efecto (to stem from, to give rise to, to bring about, to result in), el de la concesión (albeit, notwithstanding, granted) y el de la evaluación (to be of the opinion that, to be inclined to, it is arguable that). Dominarlos eleva las puntuaciones. A2: Learn useful words for giving opinions, like "I think" and "I believe." B2: Certain lexical fields recur in C1 exams: opinion and stance (to contend, to maintain, to argue that); cause and effect (to stem from, to give rise to, to result in); concession (albeit, notwithstanding, granted); evaluation (to be of the opinion that, it is arguable that). Mastering them raises your score. C1: Certain lexical domains recur with diagnostic frequency in C1 examinations and merit targeted acquisition: the stance field (to contend, to maintain, to posit, to argue that), the causation field (to stem from, to give rise to, to bring about, to result in), the concession field (albeit, notwithstanding, granted, for all that) and the evaluation field (to be of the opinion that, to be inclined to, it is arguable that). Their idiomatic deployment functions as a reliable proxy for C1 lexical range in the examiner's judgement. ### 7. Estructuras gramaticales de exhibición Los examinadores buscan evidencia de estructuras complejas. Mostrar, no solo evitar errores: una inversión emphática, una condicional mixta, una cláusula partitiva o un subjuntivo mandativo en el ensayo demuestran rango gramatical. La clave es insertarlas de manera natural, no forzada, donde el contenido las justifique. A2: Use some hard grammar in your writing, like "Never have I seen" or "If I had known, I would have done it." B2: Examiners look for evidence of complex structures. Show, do not just avoid errors: an emphatic inversion, a mixed conditional, a partitive clause or a mandative subjunctive in the essay demonstrates grammatical range. Insert them naturally where the content justifies them. C1: Examiners diagnosticise C1 grammatical range through the opportunistic deployment of complex structures. The imperative is to exhibit, not merely to avoid error: a well-placed emphatic inversion, a mixed conditional, a partitive relative or a mandative subjunctive within the essay furnishes tangible evidence of range. The critical caveat is organic insertion, the structure must be semantically motivated by the content rather than mechanically grafted, lest the prose betray artificiality. ### 8. El speaking: fluidez, interacción y pronunciación En el speaking del CAE y el IELTS, se evalúa fluidez, léxico, gramática, pronunciación e interacción. La fluidez no es velocidad sino continuidad sin pausas disruptivas. La interacción, en las fases colaborativas, exige responder al interlocutor y construir sobre sus puntos. La pronunciación inteligible pesa más que un acento nativo inalcanzable. A2: In the speaking test, try to speak smoothly. Listen to the other person and answer them well. B2: In CAE and IELTS speaking, fluency, vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation and interaction are assessed. Fluency is not speed but continuity without disruptive pauses. Interaction, in collaborative phases, requires responding to the interlocutor and building on their points. Intelligible pronunciation matters more than a native accent. C1: In the CAE and IELTS speaking components, the assessed criteria encompass fluency, lexical resource, grammatical range and accuracy, pronunciation and interactive communication. Fluency denotes continuous articulation unmarred by disruptive hesitation rather than mere velocity. Interactive communication, operative in the collaborative phases, demands responsive engagement with the interlocutor and the constructive elaboration of co-participants' contributions. Intelligible pronunciation, achievable by non-native speakers, outweighs the chimera of a native accent in the examiner's calibration. ### 9. El listening: predicción y anotación estratégica En el listening, la predicción es clave: antes de cada extracto, leer las preguntas e inferir el tema y el tipo de respuesta esperada reduce la carga cognitiva. La anotación estratégica, jotting down palabras clave durante la escucha, ayuda en los formatos de completar huecos. En CAE e IELTS, la información suele parafrasearse entre el audio y las preguntas. A2: Before you listen, read the questions. This helps you know what to listen for. B2: In listening, prediction is key: reading the questions before each extract and inferring the topic and expected answer reduces cognitive load. Strategic note-taking, jotting down keywords, helps in gap-fill formats. In CAE and IELTS, the audio information is often paraphrased in the questions. C1: In the listening component, anticipatory prediction is pivotal: pre-reading the questions and inferring both the topical domain and the anticipated response type attenuates cognitive load during the extract. Strategic annotation, the real-time jotting of keywords, augments performance in gap-fill formats. A further diagnostic nuance is that CAE and IELTS systematically paraphrase the auditory content in the question stems, so lexical recognition of synonyms and reformulations is as critical as literal comprehension. ### 10. El use of English: transformations y gap-fills El CAE incluye una sección de use of English con transformaciones (key word transformations) donde se debe reformular una frase usando una palabra clave. La estrategia exige dominar patrones: it's high time + past subjunctive, no sooner... than inversion, despite + gerund. El TOEFL no incluye esta sección, pero el IELTS sí tiene gap-fills en el listening. A2: Some exams ask you to rewrite a sentence using a special word. You must learn common patterns. B2: The CAE includes use of English with key word transformations, where you reformulate a sentence using a given word. The strategy is to master patterns: it's high time + past subjunctive, no sooner... than inversion, despite + gerund. The TOEFL lacks this section, but IELTS has gap-fills in listening. C1: The CAE use of English component features key word transformations, requiring the reformulation of a gapped sentence around a prescribed lexical anchor. Strategic competence resides in the internalisation of a repertoire of diagnostic patterns, it's high time + past subjunctive, no sooner... than with inversion, despite + gerund, such... that with fronting. The TOEFL omits this section entirely, whilst the IELTS incorporates analogous gap-fill formats within its listening paper, underscoring the cross-examinational utility of reformulation skills. ### 11. Evitar errores de FCE que cuestan el C1 Muchos candidatos retienen errores de nivel B2 que impiden alcanzar el C1: uso excesivo de will donde se requiere going to o present continuous, omisión del artículo en contextos definidos, confusión entre lend y borrow, o uso de very donde C1 exige considerably o profoundly. Identificar y erradicar estos errores es prioritario. A2: Some small mistakes can stop you from getting a high score. Check your old mistakes and fix them. B2: Many candidates retain B2 errors that block the C1: overusing will where going to or present continuous is needed, omitting the article in definite contexts, confusing lend and borrow, or using very where C1 demands considerably or profoundly. Identifying and eradicating these errors is a priority. C1: A cohort of candidates retain fossilised B2-stage errors that function as a ceiling precluding C1 certification: the overextension of will into contexts requiring the going-to or present-continuous prospective aspect, the systematic omission of the definite article in anaphoric contexts, the lend/borrow confusion and the default to the intensifier very where the C1 register demands considerably, profoundly or markedly. The diagnostic identification and targeted eradication of these fossilisations is a preparatory priority of the first order. ### 12. La psicología del examen: nervios y concentración El estado mental afecta el rendimiento. Los nervios excesivos reducen el acceso a léxico y estructuras consolidadas. Técnicas como la respiración controlada antes del speaking, la aceptación de preguntas difíciles sin pánico y la concentración segmentada (foco total en una sección, sin anticipar la siguiente) mejoran el desempeño. La preparación mental es tan estratégica como la lingüística. A2: When you feel nervous, take a deep breath. Do not worry about the whole exam at once. B2: Mental state affects performance. Excessive nerves reduce access to consolidated vocabulary and structures. Techniques like controlled breathing before speaking, accepting difficult questions without panic, and segmented concentration improve performance. Mental preparation is as strategic as linguistic preparation. C1: Psychological state exerts a measurable effect on examination performance. Excessive arousal degrades retrieval of consolidated lexical and structural resources, a phenomenon well-documented in cognitive psychology. Mitigative techniques include controlled diaphragmatic breathing prior to the speaking component, the acceptance of difficult items without panic-driven disengagement and segmented concentration, the allocation of total focal resources to the section in progress without anticipatory rehearsal of subsequent components. Psychological preparation is as strategically consequential as its linguistic counterpart. ### 13. Plantillas y anti-plantillas para el writing Las plantillas (templates) de ensayo son útiles como andamiaje, pero copiarlas de manera rígida penaliza la originalidad. La estrategia C1 consiste en internalizar estructuras, no memorizar frases. Una introducción que parafrasea el enunciado y enuncia la postura, dos párrafos de argumentación con conectores variados y una conclusión que sintetiza sin repetir literalmente es la arquitectura segura. A2: You can use a plan for your essay, but do not copy exactly. Use your own words. B2: Essay templates are useful as scaffolding, but copying them rigidly penalises originality. The C1 strategy is to internalise structures, not memorise phrases. An introduction paraphrasing the prompt and stating your stance, two argument paragraphs with varied connectors and a conclusion that synthesises without literal repetition is the safe architecture. C1: Essay templates function productively as provisional scaffolding but, deployed rigidly, they incur penalties for formulaic unoriginality. The C1-grade strategy is the internalisation of structural architecture rather than the memorisation of verbatim phrases. The reliable blueprint comprises an introduction that reformulates the prompt and enunciates the thesis, two argumentative body paragraphs deploying a diversified connector inventory and a conclusion that synthesises the antecedent argumentation without literal repetition, thereby demonstrating both structural control and discursive autonomy. ### 14. Colocaciones y phrasal verbs de alta frecuencia en el examen Los exámenes C1 recompensan el dominio de colocaciones (heavily reliant, widely acknowledged, deeply entrenched, broadly consistent) y phrasal verbs de registro formal (to account for, to bring about, to put forward, to rule out, to set out, to stem from). Su uso adecuado en writing y speaking es un indicador fiable del nivel C1. A2: Learn some common word pairs and phrases that native speakers use a lot. B2: C1 exams reward mastery of collocations (heavily reliant, widely acknowledged, deeply entrenched) and formal phrasal verbs (to account for, to bring about, to put forward, to rule out, to stem from). Using them in writing and speaking is a reliable C1 indicator. C1: C1 examinations remunerate the idiomatic command of entrenched collocations (heavily reliant, widely acknowledged, deeply entrenched, broadly consistent) and register-appropriate phrasal verbs (to account for, to bring about, to put forward, to rule out, to set out, to stem from). Their judicious deployment in the writing and speaking components functions as a diagnostically reliable index of C1 proficiency, their conspicuous absence conversely signalling a sub-C1 lexical plateau. ### 15. Repaso final y simulacros cronometrados La fase final de la preparación debe incluir simulacros cronometrados completos en condiciones reales. Hacer al menos dos simulacros íntegros de cada examen, revisar los errores sistemáticamente y ajustar la estrategia de tiempo según los resultados es el camino más eficaz hacia la puntuación objetivo. La práctica deliberada supera al estudio pasivo. A2: Before the real exam, practice the whole test with a clock. Check your mistakes and try again. B2: The final preparation phase should include full timed mock exams under real conditions. Do at least two complete mocks of each exam, review errors systematically and adjust time strategy based on the results. Deliberate practice outperforms passive study. C1: The culminatory preparatory phase should incorporate full-length timed mock examinations conducted under authentic conditions. The execution of a minimum of two complete mocks per examination, the systematic post-hoc review of errors and the iterative recalibration of temporal strategy in light of the results constitute the most efficacious pathway to the target score. Deliberate practice, characterised by targeted repetition with immediate corrective feedback, reliably outperforms passive study in the consolidation of examination-ready competence. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 Completa la transformación (CAE key word transformation) con la palabra HAVE: It's a pity I didn't revise more. → I wish ______ more.
Ver solución I wish I had revised
### Ejercicio 2 Reescribe con inversión emphática: She had never encountered such a demanding test before.
Ver solución Never before had she encountered such a demanding test.
### Ejercicio 3 Elige el conector C1 adecuado: The policy is popular; ______, its long-term effects remain uncertain.
Ver solución albeit (also acceptable: granted / however / nevertheless, depending on the intended nuance). "Albeit" or "granted" work best for concession.
### Ejercicio 4 Completa con una colocación de alta frecuencia: The theory is ______ acknowledged, though recent evidence has challenged it.
Ver solución widely
### Ejercicio 5 Identifica el distractor trampa: El texto dice "The decline began in 2008, though it accelerated after 2012." ¿Cuál de estas opciones es correcta? a) The decline started after 2012. b) The decline began in 2008 and sped up after 2012. c) The decline was caused by events in 2012.
Ver solución b is correct. Option a is a distractor that confuses "began" with "accelerated"; option c is a distractor that infers causation not stated in the text.
### Ejercicio 6 Completa con la condicional mixta adecuada: If I ______ (start) revising earlier, I ______ (be) better prepared now.
Ver solución had started ... would be
### Ejercicio 7 Reescribe con un phrasal verb formal (to bring about): The reform caused significant improvements.
Ver solución The reform brought about significant improvements.
### Ejercicio 8 Completa la transformación con SO + inversión: The impact was so significant that the committee reconsidered. → ______ that the committee reconsidered.
Ver solución So significant was the impact that the committee reconsidered.
### Ejercicio 9 Elige el léxico C1 adecuado para sustituir "very important": The findings are ______ important for future research.
Ver solución profoundly (also acceptable: considerably, markedly)
### Ejercicio 10 Completa con la preposición correcta (to stem from): Many of these problems ______ poor regulation.
Ver solución stem from
### Ejercicio 11 Reescribe con un subjuntivo mandativo: The examiner insists that every candidate ______ (arrive) ten minutes early.
Ver solución arrive
### Ejercicio 12 Elige la técnica de lectura adecuada: Para localizar el año en que se fundó una empresa en un texto largo, debes usar...
Ver solución scanning. Skimming is for the general idea; scanning is for specific information like a date or name.
### Ejercicio 13 Completa con no sooner... than + inversión: He had no sooner finished speaking than the audience erupted.
Ver solución No sooner had he finished speaking than the audience erupted.
### Ejercicio 14 Reescribe con un conector de evaluación C1: Some people believe that the exam is unfair. → ______ that the exam is unfair.
Ver solución It is arguable (also acceptable: Some are of the opinion)
### Ejercicio 15 Completa con la colocación: The two studies are broadly ______, despite minor methodological differences.
Ver solución consistent
### Ejercicio 16 Explica en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) cómo gestionarías el tiempo en la sección de escritura del IELTS.
Ver solución In the IELTS Academic Writing paper, I would allocate twenty minutes to Task 1 and forty to Task 2, reserving two to three terminal minutes for proofreading. Task 2 carries more weight, so the imbalance is justified. During Task 1, I would analyse the visual data, draft a concise overview and select key features. For Task 2, I would outline my thesis and arguments before writing, ensuring each paragraph develops a single coherent point.
### Ejercicio 17 Reescribe con una cláusula concesiva formal (albeit): The proposal was accepted, although with reservations.
Ver solución The proposal was accepted, albeit with reservations.
### Ejercicio 18 Completa con el phrasal verb adecuado (to rule out): The investigators could not ______ foul play.
Ver solución rule out
### Ejercicio 19 Redacta en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) un breve plan de estrategia para los tres días previos al examen CAE.
Ver solución In the three days preceding the CAE, I would taper active study and prioritise consolidation and rest. Day one: a full timed mock under authentic conditions, followed by systematic error review. Day two: targeted revision of fossilised errors and high-yield collocations, with light speaking practice. Day three: minimal review, mental rehearsal of time-management strategy and controlled breathing exercises, ensuring cognitive freshness. Deliberate practice gives way to psychological readiness.
## Resumen de la unidad En esta unidad has integrado toda la preparación lingüística del curso C1 en una estrategia orientada a los exámenes CAE, IELTS y TOEFL. Has aprendido a gestionar el tiempo por sección, a combinar skimming y scanning en la comprensión lectora, a identificar y evitar distractores y a exhibir las estructuras complejas (inversión, condicionales mixtas, subjuntivo mandativo) que los examinadores esperan. Has consolidado léxico de alta rentabilidad (to stem from, to bring about, broadly consistent, widely acknowledged) y conectores formales (albeit, notwithstanding, it is arguable that). Has comprendido la psicología del examen y la importancia de los simulacros cronometrados. Los 19 ejercicios te han entrenado en transformaciones, colocaciones y redacción estratégica. Con esta unidad cierras el bloque temático del curso; en la siguiente, la 61, el Language Lab te llevará a perfeccionar los phrasal verbs en contextos argumentativos, un registro esencial para la excelencia C1.
