faqs.question: ¿Qué es la inversión emphática y cuándo se usa en C1?
faqs.answer: La inversión emphática coloca el adverbio negativo o restrictivo al inicio de la oración, seguido de inversión del sujeto y el auxiliar: 'Never had she seen such beauty'. Se usa para dar énfasis retórico y es una marca distintiva del registro formal C1.

faqs.question: ¿Qué son las condicionales mixtas?
faqs.answer: Las condicionales mixtas combinan tiempos que no corresponden al mismo tipo. Por ejemplo, 'If I had studied medicine (pasado), I would be a doctor now (presente)' mezcla el tipo 3 con el tipo 2. Reflejan que la condición y la consecuencia se sitúan en tiempos distintos.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre although, despite e in spite of?
faqs.answer: Although va seguido de una cláusula con sujeto y verbo (Although it rained). Despite e in spite de van seguidos de un sintagma nominal o gerundio (Despite the rain / In spite of raining). Todos expresan concesión pero con estructuras distintas.

faqs.question: ¿Qué son los patrones de subordinación compleja en C1?
faqs.answer: Incluyen cláusulas de relativo reducidas (the book written by...), cláusulas nominales con what y whatever, construcciones partitivas (some of which) y cláusulas con before, until y once con valores temporales matizados. Permiten compactar información con precisión sintáctica.

content:
La consolidación gramatical es el momento en que los contenidos dispersos del curso se integran en un sistema coherente. A nivel C1, esto significa no solo conocer cada estructura de manera aislada, sino entender sus relaciones, sus intercambios de registro y los matices que distinguen una forma de otra. Esta unidad repasa de manera sistémica las estructuras más exigentes del nivel: los tiempos narrativos, las condicionales mixtas, la inversión emphática, las cláusulas concesivas y los patrones de subordinación compleja. Cada estructura se presenta en tres niveles. El A2 ofrece la versión más sencilla, el B2 añade complejidad gradual y el C1 presenta la forma avanzada con sus matices de registro y precisión sintáctica. A2: In English we can talk about the past, the present and the future. We can also say what we think and what we want. B2: At an intermediate-advanced level, you combine tenses to narrate, hypothesise and concede. You use conditional sentences, concessive clauses and complex subordination to express nuanced relationships between ideas. C1: C1 grammatical consolidation entails the systemic integration of previously discrete structures into a coherent syntactic repertoire. Mastery resides not in the isolated deployment of individual forms but in the calibrated selection among near-synonymous constructions according to register, emphasis and rhetorical effect, a competence that distinguishes proficient from competent users. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 59 C1](/curso-c1/unit-59)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 58 C1: Futuro de la humanidad](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-58-futuro-humanidad)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 60 C1: Preparación examen CAE/IELTS/TOEFL](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-60-preparacion-examen)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría: Consolidación gramatical global C1 ### 1. Los tiempos narrativos: past perfect, past perfect continuous y el uso del simple past La narración en inglés C1 requiere combinar con precisión el simple past, el past perfect y el past perfect continuous. El past perfect marca acciones anteriores a otro punto del pasado; el past perfect continuous enfatiza la duración o continuidad hasta ese punto. La elección entre ambos matiza el foco narrativo. A2: We use the past to tell stories. We say what happened first and what happened next. B2: Narrative tenses combine the simple past, the past perfect and the past perfect continuous. The past perfect marks actions before another past point; the past perfect continuous emphasises duration up to that point. C1: C1 narrative competence resides in the triadic orchestration of the simple past, the past perfect and the past perfect continuous. The past perfect encodes anteriority relative to a reference point in the past, whilst the past perfect continuous foregrounds the durative or iterative dimension of a process extending up to that reference point. The selection among the three encodes subtle focal distinctions that proficient narrators exploit for rhetorical effect. ### 2. Futuro perfecto y futuro perfecto continuo para la prospectión El future perfect (will have done) proyecta una acción como completada en un punto futuro; el future perfect continuous (will have been doing) la proyecta como en progreso hasta ese punto. Ambos son indispensables para la especulación temporal del nivel C1 y para describir trayectorias acumulativas. A2: We can say what will be finished before a time in the future. We can also say how long something will have been happening. B2: The future perfect projects an action as completed by a future point. The future perfect continuous projects it as ongoing up to that point. Both are useful for speculating about cumulative processes. C1: The future perfect encodes completion prior to a prospective temporal reference point, whilst the future perfect continuous encodes the durative continuity of a process extending up to that point. Both are indispensable instruments of C1 prospective reasoning, enabling precise articulation of cumulative trajectories and anticipatory states of affairs that simpler future forms cannot capture. ### 3. Condicionales mixtas: combinando tipos Las condicionales mixtas combinan estructuras de distintos tipos cuando la condición y la consecuencia se sitúan en tiempos distintos. If I had studied medicine (pasado, tipo 3), I would be a doctor now (presente, tipo 2) mezcla ambos. El dominio C1 requiere identificar qué combinación refleja cada relación temporal. A2: Sometimes the "if" part is about the past and the result is about now. We can mix them. B2: Mixed conditionals combine structures from different types when the condition and the consequence sit in different times. 'If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now' mixes type 3 (past) with type 2 (present). C1 mastery means identifying which combination fits each temporal relationship. C1: Mixed conditionals interleave conditional architectures when the protasis and the apodosis are temporally dislocated. The type 3/type 2 blend (If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now) encodes a counterfactual past condition yielding a counterfactual present consequence, whilst the type 2/type 3 blend (If she were more diligent, she would have finished by now) encodes a present dispositional condition yielding a past counterfactual outcome. C1 mastery demands the diagnostic identification of which temporal configuration each discourse context requires. ### 4. Inversión emphática con adverbios negativos y restrictivos La inversión emphática desplaza al inicio de la oración un adverbio negativo o restrictivo, seguido de la inversión del auxiliar y el sujeto. Never had she seen such beauty, Rarely do we encounter, Not until he arrived did she relax, Only after the meeting did they understand. Esta estructura confiere énfasis retórico y es marca del registro formal C1. A2: Sometimes we put a word like "never" at the start to make the sentence stronger. B2: Emphatic inversion places a negative or restrictive adverb at the front, followed by auxiliary-subject inversion: Never had she seen such beauty. This structure adds rhetorical emphasis and signals a formal register. C1: Emphatic inversion displaces a negative or restrictive adverb, never, rarely, seldom, not until, only after, to sentence-initial position, triggering auxiliary-subject inversion. The construction confers marked rhetorical prominence upon the displaced element and constitutes a diagnostic feature of the formal C1 register, exploited strategically in expository and literary prose alike to foreground salience. ### 5. Cláusulas concesivas: although, despite, whereas, while y much as Las cláusulas concesivas expresan contraste o concesión. Although va seguido de una cláusula con sujeto y verbo (Although it rained). Despite e in spite of van seguidos de un sintagma nominal o gerundio (Despite the rain). Whereas y while introducen contraste entre dos proposiciones. Much as es una forma formal y literaria. A2: We can say "but" in different ways. "Although" and "despite" show that something is surprising. B2: Concessive clauses express contrast or concession. Although is followed by a clause with subject and verb (Although it rained). Despite and in spite of are followed by a noun phrase or gerund (Despite the rain). Whereas and while introduce contrast between two propositions. C1: Concessive clauses encode contrast or concession with structurally differentiated complementation patterns. Although and even though select finite clauses, despite and in spite of select non-finite nominals or gerundive complements, whilst whereas and while introduce bipropositional contrast. Much as, a markedly formal and literary variant, selects a finite clause and is characteristic of elevated written registers, the correct distribution of which is a hallmark of C1 syntactic precision. ### 6. Cláusulas de propósito y resultado: so that, in order that, such that Las cláusulas de propósito (so that, in order that) expresan la finalidad de una acción y suelen llevar verbos modales como can, could, may, might. Las cláusulas de resultado (so... that, such... that) expresan la consecuencia y pueden emplear inversión con so o such al inicio. La distinción entre propósito y resultado es esencial para el registro C1. A2: We can say why we do things: "I went to the shop so that I could buy bread." We can also say the result: "It was so cold that I stayed home." B2: Purpose clauses (so that, in order that) express why an action is done and often take modal verbs. Result clauses (so... that, such... that) express consequence. Distinguishing purpose from result is essential for C1 accuracy. C1: Purpose clauses, introduced by so that and in order that, encode telic relations and characteristically select modal auxiliaries such as can, could, may and might in their complement. Result clauses, encoded by the so... that and such... that correlative constructions, express consequence and admit emphatic inversion when the degree adverbial is fronted. The scrupulous demarcation of purpose from result, and of their respective complementation requirements, is a diagnostic of C1 syntactic control. ### 7. Cláusulas de relativo reducidas y no reducidas Las cláusulas de relativo reducidas omiten el relativo y el auxiliar be: the book written by Smith (the book which was written by Smith). Las no reducidas (non-defining) aportan información adicional entre comas: My brother, who lives in Madrid, is a doctor. El dominio C1 requiere distinguir cuándo la reducción es posible y cuándo la coma cambia el significado. A2: We can shorten descriptions: "the book written by Smith" instead of "the book which was written by Smith." B2: Reduced relative clauses omit the relative pronoun and the auxiliary be: the book written by Smith. Non-defining clauses add extra information between commas: My brother, who lives in Madrid, is a doctor. C1 mastery means knowing when reduction is possible and when the comma changes meaning. C1: Reduced relative clauses, generated by deleting the relative pronoun and the auxiliary be, yield participial post-modifiers such as the book written by Smith from the book which was written by Smith. Non-defining relatives, set off by commas, supply appositive rather than restrictive information, and the comma's presence or absence can decisively alter semantic import. C1 competence demands diagnostic awareness of the conditions under which reduction is licensed and of the semantic consequences of comma placement. ### 8. Cláusulas nominales con what, whatever y whichever Las cláusulas nominales introducidas por what, whatever y whichever funcionan como sujeto u objeto. What she said surprised everyone (sujeto). I will support whatever you decide (objeto). La elección entre what y whatever codifica el grado de especificidad o de generalidad, un matiz característico del registro C1. A2: We can use "what" to talk about a thing: "What she said was interesting." B2: Nominal clauses with what, whatever and whichever function as subjects or objects: What she said surprised everyone. I will support whatever you decide. The choice between what and whatever encodes specificity versus generality. C1: Nominal clauses introduced by what, whatever and whichever occupy argument positions as subjects or objects. What she said surprised everyone instantiates a nominal clause in subject position, whilst I will support whatever you decide instantiates one in object position. The alternation between the specific what and the free-choice whatever encodes the speaker's stance regarding the determinacy of the referent, a C1-grade pragmatic distinction. ### 9. Construcciones partitivas: some of which, many of whom Las construcciones partitivas combinan un cuantificador con un relativo precedido de preposición: the students, many of whom failed, the proposals, some of which were accepted. Estas estructuras permiten integrar información cuantificada en cláusulas no restrictivas y son típicas del registro académico C1. A2: We can say "many of the students" to talk about part of a group. B2: Partitive constructions combine a quantifier with a prepositional relative: the students, many of whom failed; the proposals, some of which were accepted. They embed quantified information in non-restrictive clauses and are typical of academic C1. C1: Partitive constructions fuse a quantifier with a prepositional relative pronoun, yielding structures such as the students, many of whom failed, and the proposals, some of which were accepted. These constructions enable the integration of quantificational information within non-restrictive relatives and are diacritically characteristic of the C1 academic register, where their absence often signals a less proficient writer. ### 10. El uso matizado de before, until, once y as soon as Las conjunciones temporales before, until, once y as soon as introducen matices distintos. Until enfatiza la continuidad hasta un punto; before marca anterioridad; once indica que una condición se cumple y a partir de ahí cambia la situación; as soon as marca inmediatez. La distinción es crucial para la narración precisa. A2: We can say "before," "until," and "as soon as" to talk about time and order. B2: Temporal conjunctions before, until, once and as soon as introduce distinct nuances. Until emphasises continuity up to a point; before marks anteriority; once indicates a condition is met and the situation changes; as soon as marks immediacy. The distinction is crucial for precise narration. C1: The temporal conjunctions before, until, once and as soon as encode subtly distinct aspectual relations. Until encodes durative continuity terminated at a reference point; before encodes simple anteriority; once encodes a punctual condition the satisfaction of which inaugurates a new state of affairs; as soon as encodes maximal temporal proximity between triggering event and consequence. The calibrated selection among these is indispensable for the fine-grained temporal articulation that distinguishes C1 narrative control. ### 11. Inversión con so y such en cláusulas de resultado Cuando so o such se desplazan al inicio de la oración para enfatizar el grado, se produce la inversión del auxiliar y el sujeto: So profound was the impact that the policy was revised, Such was the outcry that the minister resigned. Esta inversión confiere fuerza retórica y pertenece al registro formal C1. A2: We can make a sentence stronger by putting "so" at the start: "So big was the dog that I was afraid." B2: When so or such is moved to the front for emphasis, auxiliary-subject inversion occurs: So profound was the impact that the policy was revised. This inversion adds rhetorical force and belongs to the formal C1 register. C1: Fronting the degree adverbials so and such in resultative constructions triggers auxiliary-subject inversion: So profound was the impact that the policy was revised, Such was the outcry that the minister resigned. This inversion confers marked rhetorical emphasis and is a diacritic of the formal C1 register, strategically deployed in argumentative and expository prose to invest a proposition with heightened salience. ### 12. El subjuntivo en inglés: mandative y formulaico El subjuntivo mandativo aparece tras verbos de sugerencia o exigencia (suggest, demand, insist) en cláusulas con that: I insist that he be present. El subjuntivo formulaico sobrevive en expresiones fijas como be that as it may, suffice it to say, heaven forbid. Ambos son marcas del registro formal C1. A2: Sometimes after words like "suggest" we use a special form: "I suggest that he be careful." B2: The mandative subjunctive appears after suggestion or demand verbs in that-clauses: I insist that he be present. The formulaic subjunctive survives in fixed expressions like be that as it may and suffice it to say. Both mark formal C1 register. C1: The mandative subjunctive, selected by directive predicates such as suggest, demand, insist and require in that-complements (I insist that he be present), encodes obligatory or recommended states of affairs without modal mediation. The formulaic subjunctive persists in fossilised expressions including be that as it may, suffice it to say and heaven forbid. Both constitute diagnostic features of the formal C1 register, their deployment signalling an advanced command of register-sensitive syntax. ### 13. Verbos modales en pasado para especulación y deducción Los modales en pasado (must have done, might have done, could have done, should have done, can't have done) expresan deducción, especulación o crítica sobre eventos pasados. Must have done indica deducción de certeza; can't have done, deducción de imposibilidad; should have done, crítica retrospectiva. Su uso preciso es central en el C1. A2: We can guess about the past: "He must have been tired" means I am sure he was tired. B2: Past modals (must have done, might have done, can't have done, should have done) express deduction, speculation or criticism about past events. Must have done indicates certainty; can't have done indicates impossibility; should have done expresses retrospective criticism. C1: Past modal configurations, must have done, might have done, could have done, should have done and can't have done, encode epistemic, deontic or evaluative stance toward past eventualities. Must have done encodes deductive certainty; can't have done encodes deductive impossibility; should have done encodes retrospective deontic critique. Their calibrated deployment, distinguishing epistemic from deontic readings, is central to C1 expressive precision in conjectural discourse. ### 14. Conectores discursivos de contraste, adición y reformulación El registro C1 emplea conectores variados más allá de but y however: nevertheless, nonetheless, conversely, on the contrary, by contrast (contraste); furthermore, moreover, additionally, in addition (adición); in other words, namely, to put it differently, that is to say (reformulación). Su elección codifica el tipo de relación lógica con precisión. A2: We can use words like "however" and "also" to connect ideas. B2: C1 uses varied connectors beyond but and however: nevertheless, conversely, on the contrary (contrast); furthermore, moreover, additionally (addition); in other words, namely, to put it differently (reformulation). Their choice encodes the logical relationship precisely. C1: The C1 register exploits a diversified connector inventory extending well beyond the elementary but and however: nevertheless, nonetheless, conversely, on the contrary and by contrast encode contrastive relations; furthermore, moreover, additionally and in addition encode additive relations; in other words, namely, to put it differently and that is to say encode reformulative relations. The calibrated selection among these encodes the specific logical relation with a granularity unavailable to less proficient users. ### 15. El artículo cero, el y a/an: precisión determinativa El uso avanzado del artículo distingue contextos donde el artículo cero es obligatorio (institutional reference: go to hospital, at school) de los que requieren the (specific reference) o a/an (classificatory). Las diferencias entre in hospital e in the hospital, o entre go to church y go to the church, codifican distinciones funcionales que el C1 debe dominar. A2: Sometimes we use "the," sometimes "a," and sometimes no word before a noun. It depends on what we mean. B2: Advanced article use distinguishes contexts requiring the zero article (go to hospital, at school) from those needing the (specific reference) or a/an (classificatory). The difference between in hospital and in the hospital encodes functional distinctions. C1: Advanced article deployment hinges on the diagnostic discrimination of contexts licensing the zero article, institutional or atelic reference such as go to hospital and at school, from those requiring the definite article for specific reference or the indefinite article for classificatory reference. The contrast between in hospital and in the hospital, or between go to church and go to the church, encodes functionally consequential distinctions between institutional role and mere locative reference that C1 users must command with reflexive precision. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 Completa con el tiempo narrativo correcto: By the time the ambulance arrived, the patient ______ (lose) consciousness for several minutes.
Ver solución had been losing (also acceptable: had lost). "had been losing" foregrounds the durative continuity up to the arrival; "had lost" foregrounds the completed state.
### Ejercicio 2 Reescribe con inversión emphática: She had never seen such devastation before.
Ver solución Never before had she seen such devastation.
### Ejercicio 3 Completa la condicional mixta: If she ______ (take) that job offer last year, she ______ (live) in Berlin now.
Ver solución had taken ... would be living
### Ejercicio 4 Transforma con despite: Although the evidence was weak, the jury convicted him.
Ver solución Despite the weak evidence, the jury convicted him. (Also acceptable: Despite the evidence being weak, the jury convicted him.)
### Ejercicio 5 Completa con una cláusula partitiva: The committee rejected the proposals, ______ (many of which / many of that) were politically sensitive.
Ver solución many of which
### Ejercicio 6 Reescribe con so... that invertido: The impact was so profound that the policy was revised.
Ver solución So profound was the impact that the policy was revised.
### Ejercicio 7 Completa con el subjuntivo mandativo: The board insists that every employee ______ (be) present at the meeting.
Ver solución be
### Ejercicio 8 Elige el conector adecuado y completa: The model is theoretically elegant; ______, it fails to account for the empirical anomalies.
Ver solución nevertheless (also acceptable: nonetheless). A contrastive connector is required.
### Ejercicio 9 Reescribe con una cláusula nominal con what: Her sudden resignation surprised everyone.
Ver solución What surprised everyone was her sudden resignation. (Or: Her sudden resignation was what surprised everyone.)
### Ejercicio 10 Completa con el modal pasado adecuado (deducción de imposibilidad): He ______ (can't have / mustn't have) known about the meeting; he was abroad that day.
Ver solución can't have
### Ejercicio 11 Transforma con un relativo reducido: The bridge which was built in 1890 is still in use.
Ver solución The bridge built in 1890 is still in use.
### Ejercicio 12 Completa con until, once o as soon as: ______ the new legislation takes effect, all existing permits will lapse.
Ver solución Once
### Ejercicio 13 Reescribe con such... that invertido: The outcry was such that the minister resigned.
Ver solución Such was the outcry that the minister resigned.
### Ejercicio 14 Completa la condicional mixta (presente → pasado): If he ______ (be) more disciplined, he ______ (finish) the project by now.
Ver solución were ... would have finished
### Ejercicio 15 Reescribe con un conector reformulativo C1: The theory is wrong. In other words, it cannot explain the data.
Ver solución The theory is untenable; to put it differently, it cannot account for the data.
### Ejercicio 16 Elige el artículo correcto (the, a, o cero): She went to ______ university to study law, and later spent three months in ______ hospital after an accident.
Ver solución zero article ... the (or zero article in British English for institutional reference: "She went to university to study law, and later spent three months in hospital after an accident." The first blank is zero; the second is zero in BrE institutional use or "the" if referring to a specific building.)
### Ejercicio 17 Completa con future perfect o future perfect continuous: By 2050, the company ______ (operate) in over fifty countries for three decades.
Ver solución will have been operating
### Ejercicio 18 Reescribe con much as: Although I sympathise with your position, I cannot support the motion.
Ver solución Much as I sympathise with your position, I cannot support the motion.
### Ejercicio 19 Redacta en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) un breve párrafo narrativo que combine past perfect, past perfect continuous, inversión emphática y una cláusula concesiva.
Ver solución Never before had the village witnessed such flooding. For three days the rain had been falling without relent, and by dawn the river had burst its banks. Although the townsfolk had reinforced the levee the previous summer, the waters overwhelmed it within hours. Despite their preparations, the destruction was total.
## Resumen de la unidad En esta unidad has consolidado de manera sistémica las estructuras gramaticales más exigentes del nivel C1. Has repasado los tiempos narrativos (simple past, past perfect, past perfect continuous) y los futuros perfectos para la prospectión. Has dominado las condicionales mixtas que combinan tipos distintos, la inversión emphática con adverbios negativos y con so y such, las cláusulas concesivas con although, despite y much as, las cláusulas de relativo reducidas y partitivas, el subjuntivo mandativo y los modales en pasado para la deducción. A nivel discursivo, has refinado el uso de conectores de contraste, adición y reformulación, y la precisión determinativa del artículo. Los 19 ejercicios te han permitido integrar estas estructuras en un repertorio coherente. En la siguiente unidad, la 60, aplicarás esta consolidación gramatical a la preparación estratégica para los exámenes CAE, IELTS y TOEFL, donde la gestión del tiempo y la estrategia son tan importantes como el dominio lingüístico.

title: Ejercicios sobre el Futuro de la Humanidad C1
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Domina la especulación prudente sobre el futuro de la humanidad en inglés C1: riesgos existenciales, longtermism, hedging y léxico futurológico. Teoría profunda y 19 ejercicios inglés C1 gratis para consolidar el razonamiento sobre el largo plazo con el rigor del nivel avanzado.
description: En esta unidad del curso de inglés C1 gratis aprendes a especular de manera prudente en inglés sobre el futuro de la humanidad, a usar el hedging y los...
alt: Silueta humana frente a un horizonte con una ciudad futurista, un planeta y líneas temporales divergentes en tonos azul y dorado
keywords: Ejercicios sobre el Futuro de la Humanidad C1
hedging para especular sobre el futuro

faqs.question: ¿Qué es un riesgo existencial y por qué importa?
faqs.answer: Un riesgo existencial (existential risk) es aquel que amenaza con extinguir a la humanidad o destruir su potencial a largo plazo de manera irreversible. Nick Bostrom argumenta que, dado que afecta a todas las generaciones futuras, su reducción tiene una utilidad esperada extraordinariamente alta, incluso si la probabilidad es baja.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es el longtermism y qué crítica recibe?
faqs.answer: El longtermism sostiene que influir positivamente en el largo plazo es una prioridad moral clave, dado el enorme número de vidas futuras posibles. Sus críticos objetan que puede descuidar los sufrimientos presentes y que las predicciones a muy largo plazo son demasiado inciertas para guiar decisiones éticas.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es el hedging y por qué es esencial al especular sobre el futuro?
faqs.answer: El hedging consiste en matizar las afirmaciones para indicar incertidumbre o probabilidad (it is plausible that, may, could, is likely to). Al especular sobre el futuro, donde la evidencia es limitada, el hedging evita aseveraciones dogmáticas y refleja honestidad intelectual, una marca del registro C1.

faqs.question: ¿Qué son las curvas de Kuznets y la paradoja de Jevons?
faqs.answer: La curva de Kuznets ambiental sugiere que la contaminación primero sube y luego baja con el desarrollo económico. La paradoja de Jevons observa que aumentar la eficiencia de un recurso puede elevar su consumo total, un argumento clave al especular sobre el futuro energético.

content:
El futuro de la humanidad es el territorio donde la especulación se encuentra con la responsabilidad moral. Razonar sobre él en inglés C1 exige más que imaginación: requiere hedging, es decir, matizar las afirmaciones según el grado de incertidumbre, y un léxico preciso para hablar de riesgos existenciales, trayectorias civilizatorias y largo plazo. Esta unidad te prepara para especular con prudencia, ni dogmático ni evasivo, sobre los escenarios que configuran el porvenir humano. Cada concepto clave se presenta en tres niveles. El A2 fija la idea esencial, el B2 añade matices y conectores, y el C1 presenta el léxico futurológico y las estructuras de hedging avanzadas que necesitas dominar. A2: We can think about the future. Some things might happen. We are not sure, but we can guess carefully. B2: Speculating about the future requires caution. We must distinguish likely trends from mere possibilities, using hedging language such as may, could and is likely to. Responsible futurology avoids both alarmism and complacency. C1: Speculation concerning humanity's long-run trajectory demands calibrated hedging, the judicious deployment of modal markers and probabilistic qualifiers that calibrate claims to the available evidence. Responsible futurology neither collapses into alarmist determinism nor retreats into complacent agnosticism; instead, it triangulates between divergent scenarios by foregrounding the epistemic uncertainty inherent in long-range projection. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 58 C1](/curso-c1/unit-58)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 57 C1: Ética y filosofía moral](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-57-etica-filosofia-moral)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 59 C1: Consolidación gramatical global](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-59-consolidacion-gramatical-global)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría: Futuro de la humanidad y especulación prudente ### 1. La futurología como disciplina cautelosa La futurología o futures studies no pretende predecir el futuro sino mapear los escenarios plausibles. Los futurólogos distinguen entre predicciones, proyecciones y proyecciones condicionales. La especulación prudente reconoce que el futuro es radicalmente incierto y que nuestra tarea es reducir la incertidumbre, no eliminarla. A2: People who study the future do not say exactly what will happen. They think about different possible futures. B2: Futures studies, or futurology, does not aim to predict but to map plausible scenarios. Futurologists distinguish predictions from projections and conditional forecasts. Prudent speculation accepts that the future is radically uncertain. C1: Futures studies eschews the chimera of deterministic prediction in favour of scenario mapping across a distribution of plausible trajectories. Practitioners rigorously demarcate unconditional predictions from conditional projections, acknowledging that the epistemic warrant for long-range claims attenuates sharply with temporal distance. Prudent speculation thus consists not in extinguishing uncertainty but in rendering it tractable for decision-making under radical Knightian uncertainty. ### 2. Hedging: el corazón lingüístico de la especulación C1 El hedging es el conjunto de recursos lingüísticos que matizan las afirmaciones para indicar incertidumbre, probabilidad o tentatividad. A nivel C1, domina expresiones como it is plausible that, the evidence tentatively suggests, may well, cannot be ruled out, there are grounds for supposing, in all likelihood, it is conceivable that, on present trends, barring unforeseen developments. A2: When we are not sure, we say "maybe" or "I think." We do not say things are certain if we are not sure. B2: Hedging means softening claims to reflect uncertainty. Useful C1 phrases include it is plausible that, the evidence tentatively suggests, may well, and cannot be ruled out. Hedging signals intellectual honesty when speculating. C1: Hedging constitutes the linguistic infrastructure of calibrated speculation, deploying an array of modal auxiliaries, evidential adverbs and tentative predicates to modulate the force of propositions in proportion to their evidential support. C1 mastery encompasses formulations such as it is plausible that, the evidence tentatively suggests, may well, cannot be ruled out, there are grounds for supposing, in all likelihood, it is conceivable that, on present trends, and barring unforeseen developments. ### 3. Riesgos existenciales: el marco de Bostrom Nick Bostrom clasifica los riesgos existenciales en categorías: naturales (asteroides, supervolcanes, pandemias), antropogénicos (guerra nuclear, cambio climático extremo) y emergentes (inteligencia artificial general, ingeniería biológica maliciosa). Su argumento central es que, dado el número de vidas futuras posibles, la reducción de riesgos existenciales tiene una utilidad esperada extraordinariamente alta. A2: Some things could end humanity, like big rocks from space or very bad diseases. We should try to stop them. B2: Nick Bostrom categorises existential risks as natural (asteroids, pandemics), anthropogenic (nuclear war, extreme climate change), and emerging (advanced AI, engineered pathogens). He argues that reducing these risks has enormous expected value because of the vast number of future lives at stake. C1: Bostrom's taxonomy partitions existential risks into natural hazards (asteroidal impacts, supervolcanic eruptions, naturally arising pandemics), anthropogenic catastrophes (nuclear exchange, runaway climate change) and emerging technological threats (unaligned artificial general intelligence, malevolent bioengineering). His central contention is that, given the astronomical cardinality of possible future lives, the expected utility of existential-risk mitigation vastly dominates that of comparatively near-term interventions. ### 4. Longtermism y sus críticas El longtermism sostiene que influir positivamente en el largo plazo es una prioridad moral clave. Sus defensores, asociados al movimiento de altruismo eficaz, argumentan que las generaciones futuras merecen igual consideración moral. Los críticos objetan que el largo plazo es demasiado incierto para guiar decisiones y que el longtermism puede descuidar los sufrimientos presentes. A2: Some people think we should care a lot about people who will live far in the future. Other people think we should focus on people who need help now. B2: Longtermism holds that positively shaping the long-run future is a key moral priority. Its proponents, linked to effective altruism, argue that future generations deserve equal moral consideration. Critics counter that the distant future is too uncertain to guide action and that longtermism can neglect present suffering. C1: Longtermism, as articulated within the effective altruism movement, maintains that positively influencing the long-run trajectory of civilisation constitutes a paramount moral priority, grounded in the equal moral considerability of future persons. Its detractors retort that the epistemic opacity of the distant future precludes action-guiding predictions and that longtermist reasoning risks instrumentalising present suffering in service of speculative downstream benefits. ### 5. Trayectorias civilizatorias: colapso, estancamiento y florecimiento Los futurólogos describen tres grandes trayectorias: el colapso (civilización que se autodestruye), el estancamiento (civilización que sobrevive sin avanzar) y el florecimiento (civilización que realiza su potencial). La probabilidad relativa de cada trayectoria es objeto de intenso debate, y el hedging es indispensable al discutirlas. A2: The future could go three ways: things get very bad, things stay the same, or things get much better. B2: Futurologists sketch three macro-trajectories: collapse, in which civilisation destroys itself; stagnation, in which it survives without progressing; and flourishing, in which it realises its potential. Estimating the relative likelihood of each trajectory remains deeply contested. C1: Futurologists delineate three canonical macro-trajectories: collapse, wherein civilisation precipitates its own disintegration; stagnation, wherein it subsists without substantive advancement; and flourishing, wherein it approximates its developmental potential. The conditional probabilities assigned to each trajectory remain acutely contested, and calibrated hedging is indispensable when adjudicating among them. ### 6. Singularidad tecnológica y superinteligencia La hipótesis de la singularidad tecnológica sostiene que el progreso tecnológico se acelerará de manera incontrolable tras la creación de inteligencia general artificial. I. J. Good y posteriormente Ray Kurzweil argumentan que una máquina que se mejora a sí misma podría superar rápidamente la inteligencia humana. La especulación prudente reconoce tanto la posibilidad como la profunda incertidumbre de este escenario. A2: Some people think machines could get very smart, smarter than us. Then things might change very fast. B2: The technological singularity hypothesis holds that progress will accelerate uncontrollably once artificial general intelligence is created. I. J. Good and Ray Kurzweil argue that a self-improving machine could swiftly surpass human intelligence. Prudent speculation acknowledges both the possibility and the deep uncertainty of this scenario. C1: The technological singularity hypothesis posits an irrevocable acceleration of technological change precipitated by the advent of artificial general intelligence. Good and, latterly, Kurzweil contend that a recursively self-improving intelligence could, via an intelligence explosion, comprehensively eclipse human cognitive capacities. Calibrated speculation demands that one hold this scenario neither as imminent certainty nor as dismissable fantasy, but as a high-stakes low-confidence prospect warranting serious preparatory analysis. ### 7. Colonización espacial y multiplanetariedad La colonización espacial se propone como mitigación de riesgos existenciales: una civilización multiplanetaria sobreviviría a catástrofes que aniquilaran un único planeta. Elon Musk y otros defensores argumentan que convertirse en especie multiplanetaria reduce la fragilidad existencial. Los escépticos cuestionan la viabilidad técnica, el coste de oportunidad y la prioridad moral frente a problemas terrestres urgentes. A2: If humans live on more than one planet, we are safer. If something bad happens to Earth, we still survive. B2: Space colonisation is proposed as a hedge against existential risk: a multiplanetary civilisation would survive a catastrophe that destroyed a single planet. Proponents like Elon Musk argue it reduces existential fragility. Skeptics question its feasibility, opportunity cost, and moral priority over urgent terrestrial problems. C1: Space colonisation is advanced as an existential-risk mitigant, the rationale being that a multiplanetary civilisation would be robust to single-planet annihilation. Proponents such as Musk contend that achieving multiplanetary status constitutes civilisational redundancy against catastrophic fragility. Skeptics counter on grounds of prohibitive technical intractability, formidable opportunity cost, and contested moral prioritisation relative to exigent terrestrial welfare deficits. ### 8. Cambio climático: escenarios y hedging El cambio climático ilustra la especulación prudente en acción. Los modelos climáticos proyectan rangos de calentamiento, no valores únicos, porque dependen de supuestos sobre emisiones y retroalimentaciones. El lenguaje científico emplea hedging sistemáticamente: likely, very likely, cannot be excluded, consistent with. Distinguir between projections and predictions es esencial. A2: The climate is getting warmer, but we do not know exactly how much. Scientists give a range, not one number. B2: Climate change illustrates prudent speculation. Models project warming ranges, not single values, because outcomes depend on emission scenarios and feedback loops. Scientific language uses systematic hedging: likely, very likely, cannot be excluded. Distinguishing projections from predictions is essential. C1: Anthropogenic climate change exemplifies calibrated speculation in practice. Climate models yield probabilistic distributions of warming rather than point estimates, contingent on emission pathways and feedback parameterisations. The associated scientific register deploys systematic hedging, likely, very likely, cannot be excluded, consistent with, and scrupulously distinguishes conditional projections from unconditional predictions, a demarcation indispensable to responsible communication. ### 9. Demografía: el declive poblacional y el envejecimiento Las proyecciones demográficas sugieren que la población humana podría estabilizarse o incluso declinar durante este siglo, con profundo envejecimiento en muchas economías desarrolladas. Las implicaciones para el crecimiento económico, los sistemas de pensiones y la innovación son objeto de especulación cautelosa. El hedging es crucial porque las tendencias pueden revertirse. A2: The number of people in the world might stop growing soon. Many countries have more old people than before. B2: Demographic projections suggest the global population may stabilise or decline this century, with profound ageing in many developed economies. The implications for growth, pensions and innovation are debated with caution. Hedging is crucial because trends may reverse. C1: Demographic projections intimate that the global population may plateau or contract during the present century, accompanied by pronounced ageing transitions across numerous developed economies. The downstream implications for aggregate economic growth, pension-system solvency and innovation rates are subject to calibrated conjecture, hedging being indispensable in light of the demonstrable reversibility of erstwhile secular trends. ### 10. La paradoja de Jevons y la eficiencia La paradoja de Jevons observa que aumentar la eficiencia en el uso de un recurso puede elevar su consumo total, porque el uso efectivo se abarata. Esta paradoja complica las proyecciones sobre el futuro energético y desafía la intuición de que la eficiencia reduce automáticamente el consumo. Es un ejemplo paradigmático de por qué la especulación sobre el futuro requiere humildad. A2: Sometimes when we use something better, we end up using more of it, not less. This is surprising. B2: The Jevons paradox observes that improving the efficiency of a resource can increase its total consumption, because effective use becomes cheaper. This complicates projections about the energy future and challenges the intuition that efficiency automatically reduces consumption. C1: The Jevons paradox, or rebound effect, observes that augmenting the efficiency of resource utilisation may paradoxically escalate aggregate consumption, as the effective price of use-dependent services declines. This complication bedevils energy-future projections and frustrates the intuitive supposition that efficiency gains mechanically curtail consumption, illustrating why futurological reasoning demands epistemic humility. ### 11. Bioética del futuro: edición genética y extensión de la vida La edición genética con CRISPR y las terapias de extensión de vida plantean dilemas futuros. ¿Deberíamos editar el genoma germline, transmitiendo cambios a las generaciones futuras? ¿La extensión radical de la vida agravaría las desigualdades? La especulación prudente requiere distinguir entre lo técnicamente posible, lo probablemente próximo y lo meramente concebible. A2: In the future, we might change genes to make people healthier. We might help people live much longer. But we must think carefully about what is fair. B2: Gene editing with CRISPR and life-extension therapies pose future dilemmas. Should we edit the germline, passing changes to future generations? Could radical life extension worsen inequality? Prudent speculation distinguishes the technically possible from the soon probable and the merely conceivable. C1: Germline CRISPR editing and life-extension interventions furnish a proliferating class of future-facing bioethical dilemmas. Whether to authorise heritable genomic modification, with its cascading intergenerational ramifications, and whether radical longevity amplification would exacerbate distributive inequity, are questions that demand a tripartite distinction between the technically feasible, the proximately probable and the merely conceivable. ### 12. Gobernanza global y cooperación a largo plazo Los retos de largo plazo, desde el cambio climático hasta los riesgos de la IA, sobrepasan la capacidad de los estados individuales. La especulación prudente sobre el futuro de la gobernanza global contempla escenarios de fragmentación, de cooperación reforzada y de nuevas instituciones transnacionales. El hedging es esencial porque las trayectorias institucionales son notoriamente difíciles de predecir. A2: Big problems need all countries to work together. But we do not know if they will. B2: Long-term challenges like climate change and AI risk exceed any single state's capacity. Prudent speculation about global governance considers scenarios of fragmentation, strengthened cooperation, and novel transnational institutions. Hedging is essential because institutional trajectories are hard to predict. C1: Long-horizon challenges, spanning climate destabilisation to AI-related existential risk, decisively outrun the jurisdictional competence of individual states. Calibrated speculation concerning the evolution of global governance encompasses scenarios of institutional fragmentation, reinforced multilateral cooperation and the emergence of qualitatively novel transnational architectures. Given the notorious unpredictability of institutional trajectories, robust hedging is non-negotiable. ### 13. Modales de probabilidad en inglés C1 A nivel C1, debes dominar los modales de probabilidad: it is highly probable that, there is a non-negligible chance, the probability is not negligible, it would be rash to conclude, the evidence is suggestive but not conclusive, we cannot discount the possibility. Estas formulaciones cuantifican verbalmente la incertidumbre, un rasgo distintivo del registro académico-futuroológico. A2: We can say "it is very likely" or "maybe it will happen" when we talk about what could be. B2: Useful probability phrases include it is highly probable that, there is a non-negligible chance, and the evidence is suggestive but not conclusive. These formulations verbalise uncertainty, a hallmark of academic futurology. C1: C1 proficiency in futurological discourse entails mastery of calibrated probability expressions: it is highly probable that, there is a non-negligible chance, the probability is not negligible, it would be rash to conclude, the evidence is suggestive but not conclusive, and we cannot discount the possibility. These formulations verbalise uncertainty with granular precision, a distinguishing register of academic futurology. ### 14. Conectores para el razonamiento prospectivo El razonamiento sobre el futuro emplea conectores específicos: assuming that, in the event that, should current trends persist, were this scenario to materialise, even granting that, for the sake of argument, conditional on, subject to the caveat that. Estos conectores anclan las especulaciones a supuestos explícitos, una práctica esencial del pensamiento cauteloso. A2: When we guess about the future, we can say "if this happens" or "let's imagine that." B2: Speculative reasoning uses connectors like assuming that, in the event that, should current trends persist, and were this scenario to materialise. These anchor speculation to explicit assumptions, a hallmark of careful thinking. C1: Prospective reasoning deploys a distinctive connector set, assuming that, in the event that, should current trends persist, were this scenario to materialise, even granting that, for the sake of argument, conditional on, and subject to the caveat that, each of which tethers speculative claims to explicitly articulated suppositions, an indispensable discipline of epistemically responsible futurology. ### 15. Léxico y colocaciones futuroológicas El léxico futuroológico del inglés C1 incluye colocaciones estables: to map plausible scenarios, to hedge one's bets, to avert an existential catastrophe, to reap the dividends of, to plateau and decline, to overshoot a threshold, to precipitate a collapse, to instrumentalise future persons, to discount the distant future, to foreground epistemic uncertainty, to calibrate claims to the evidence. A2: Useful phrases: to think about the future, to be careful, to try to avoid bad things. B2: Useful collocations include to map plausible scenarios, to hedge one's bets, to avert an existential catastrophe, and to plateau and decline. These fixed expressions make your futurological vocabulary precise. C1: The C1 futurological lexicon comprises entrenched collocations essential for idiomatic speculative discourse: to map plausible scenarios, to hedge one's bets, to avert an existential catastrophe, to reap the dividends of, to plateau and decline, to overshoot a threshold, to precipitate a collapse, to instrumentalise future persons, to discount the distant future, to foreground epistemic uncertainty, and to calibrate claims to the evidence. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 Completa con una expresión de hedging C1: ______ artificial general intelligence will be developed within the next fifty years, though the evidence is far from conclusive.
Ver solución It is conceivable that (also acceptable: It is plausible that / There are grounds for supposing that)
### Ejercicio 2 Traduce al inglés con hedging: "Es probable que la población mundial se estabilice durante este siglo, aunque no puede descartarse un declive."
Ver solución It is likely that the global population will stabilise this century, though a decline cannot be ruled out.
### Ejercicio 3 Reescribe con un conector prospectivo C1: If current trends continue, warming could exceed 2 degrees.
Ver solución Should current trends persist, warming could exceed 2 degrees.
### Ejercicio 4 Completa con la colocación correcta: The longtermist argues that we have a moral duty to ______ existential catastrophes.
Ver solución avert
### Ejercicio 5 Identifica la categoría de riesgo existencial según Bostrom: Una pandemia provocada por un patógeno ingenierizado en un laboratorio.
Ver solución It is an emerging technological risk (anthropogenic, specifically an engineered pathogen), as opposed to a naturally arising pandemic, which would be a natural existential risk.
### Ejercicio 6 Reescribe con hedging más fuerte: Artificial intelligence will definitely destroy humanity.
Ver solución It is conceivable that advanced artificial intelligence could pose an existential threat to humanity, though the evidence is suggestive but far from conclusive. (The key change: replace the dogmatic "will definitely" with calibrated hedging.)
### Ejercicio 7 Traduce al inglés: "Bostrom sostiene que la reducción de los riesgos existenciales tiene una utilidad esperada extraordinariamente alta."
Ver solución Bostrom argues that mitigating existential risks has an extraordinarily high expected utility.
### Ejercicio 8 Completa la frase: The Jevons paradox observes that improving resource efficiency may ______ total consumption rather than reduce it.
Ver solución increase (also acceptable: escalate)
### Ejercicio 9 Construye una frase C1 usando "subject to the caveat that" sobre el futuro de la energía.
Ver solución Renewable energy could plausibly meet the bulk of global demand by mid-century, subject to the caveat that battery storage scales faster than current trajectories suggest.
### Ejercicio 10 Reescribe con un modulador de probabilidad C1: Maybe space colonisation will reduce existential risk.
Ver solución There is a non-negligible chance that space colonisation would meaningfully reduce existential risk.
### Ejercicio 11 Traduce al inglés: "Una civilización multiplanetaria sería robusta frente a catástrofes de un solo planeta."
Ver solución A multiplanetary civilisation would be robust to single-planet catastrophes.
### Ejercicio 12 Identifica el error de razonamiento: "No podemos predecir el futuro a largo plazo, por tanto no debemos preocuparnos por él."
Ver solución This commits a non sequitur: the inability to predict the long-term future with precision does not entail that we should disregard it. Longtermists argue that even under radical uncertainty, some interventions (such as existential-risk reduction) have sufficiently high expected value to warrant prioritisation.
### Ejercicio 13 Completa con el conector adecuado: ______ this scenario were to materialise, the downstream consequences would be profound.
Ver solución Were
### Ejercicio 14 Reescribe con registro C1: We don't know if people will live much longer, but it might happen.
Ver solución Whether radical life extension will materialise remains uncertain, though it cannot be discounted. (Also acceptable: The prospect of radical life extension is speculative but not dismissable.)
### Ejercicio 15 Traduce al inglés con hedging: "La evidencia sugiere tentativamente que la curva de Kuznets ambiental podría no generalizarse a todos los contaminantes."
Ver solución The evidence tentatively suggests that the environmental Kuznets curve may not generalise across all pollutants.
### Ejercicio 16 Explica en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) por qué el hedging es esencial al especular sobre los riesgos de la inteligencia artificial general.
Ver solución Hedging is indispensable when speculating about artificial general intelligence because the relevant evidence is sparse, the timelines are deeply contested and the underlying mechanisms remain theoretically unsettled. Asserting that catastrophe is imminent would overstate the warrant; dismissing the risk entirely would understate it. Calibrated formulations, it is conceivable that, there is a non-negligible chance, preserve epistemic honesty while still licensing serious preparatory action under uncertainty.
### Ejercicio 17 Completa con la colocación: The futurologist attempts to ______ plausible scenarios rather than predict a single outcome.
Ver solución map
### Ejercicio 18 Reescribe con un conector concesivo C1: Longtermism has powerful arguments. Many ethicists remain unconvinced.
Ver solución Notwithstanding the powerful arguments advanced for longtermism, a substantial number of ethicists remain unconvinced.
### Ejercicio 19 Redacta en inglés C1 (60-80 palabras) un breve argumento sobre si la colonización espacial debería ser una prioridad moral frente a los problemas terrestres.
Ver solución Whether space colonisation merits moral prioritisation over terrestrial welfare deficits turns on contested empirical and normative assumptions. Proponents argue that existential-risk mitigation via multiplanetary redundancy safeguards an astronomical number of possible future lives, yielding extraordinary expected value. Critics counter that the opportunity costs are prohibitive and the technical feasibility uncertain, whilst present suffering commands more immediate moral salience. A defensible position may hedge: pursue both, but not at the expense of urgent welfare today.
## Resumen de la unidad En esta unidad has aprendido a especular con prudencia sobre el futuro de la humanidad en inglés C1. Has explorado el marco de los riesgos existenciales de Bostrom, el debate entre longtermism y sus críticos, las trayectorias civilizatorias y la singularidad tecnológica. A nivel lingüístico, has consolidado el hedging con expresiones como it is plausible that, cannot be ruled out y there are grounds for supposing, junto con conectores prospectivos como should current trends persist y were this scenario to materialise. Has dominado colocaciones futuroológicas como to map plausible scenarios, to avert an existential catastrophe y to foreground epistemic uncertainty. Los 19 ejercicios te han entrenado en el razonamiento prospectivo con la humildad epistémica que define el registro avanzado. En la siguiente unidad, la 59, consolidarás de manera sistémica toda la gramática del nivel C1 en un repaso global antes de la preparación para el examen.
