faqs.question: ¿Qué es la síntesis argumentativa en inglés C1?
faqs.answer: Es la capacidad de integrar múltiples fuentes, perspectivas y temas en un discurso coherente que muestra las relaciones entre ellos —convergencias, tensiones, jerarquías— sin perder el hilo argumental. Es la destreza culminante del bloque temático, que combina el léxico de las unidades anteriores con conectores de síntesis.

faqs.question: ¿Qué conectores de síntesis usa un hablante C1?
faqs.answer: Conectores como taken together, in sum, what emerges from this, viewed holistically, the through-line that connects these, seen in this light, against this backdrop, at the intersection of, alongside this, y expressions de jerarquización como the more fundamental point is.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se integra el léxico de medios, privacidad, IA y ética en un mismo discurso?
faqs.answer: Identificando el hilo conductor (por ejemplo, la confianza como recurso del ecosistema mediático) y usando conectores que muestren cómo la desinformación, la vigilancia, los sesgos algorítmicos y los dilemas deontológicos convergen en una misma pregunta sobre la credibilidad de la información.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es el 'through-line' y por qué es clave en la síntesis C1?
faqs.answer: El through-line es el hilo argumental que recorre y conecta temas aparentemente dispersos. En la síntesis C1, identificar el through-line permite presentar medios, privacidad, IA y ética no como temas separados sino como facetas de una misma transformación del ecosistema informativo.

content:
La consolidación es la destreza culminante de todo bloque temático: el momento en que los hilos dispersos se tejen en un tapiz coherente y el hablante demuestra que no solo sabe manejar cada tema por separado, sino integrarlos en un discurso que revela las relaciones entre ellos. En esta unidad del curso de inglés C1 gratis cerramos el bloque dedicado a los medios, la información y la transformación digital sintetizando los temas de las unidades anteriores \u2014medios tradicionales frente a digitales, desinformación, privacidad y vigilancia, IA y sociedad, ética periodística\u2014 en un marco unificado. No se trata de repetir lo aprendido, sino de elevarlo: de mostrar cómo la *trust crisis* del ecosistema mediático, la *surveillance capitalism* de la economía de datos, el *alignment problem* de la IA y los dilemas deontológicos del periodismo no son temas yuxtapuestos sino facetas de una misma transformación. El instrumento lingüístico de esa elevación es la síntesis argumentativa \u2014*taken together*, *what emerges from this*, *the through-line that connects these*\u2014, y su dominio es lo que distingue al hablante que acumula conocimiento del que lo integra. Para situar el nivel, observa cómo la misma síntesis se expresa en tres niveles. En **A2** diríamos: *We learned about media, privacy, AI and journalism. They are all important. The internet changes everything.* Es claro pero plano, sin integración ni vocabulario de síntesis. En **B2** subiríamos un peldaño: *Traditional media and digital media are different. Privacy is a problem online. AI has implications. Journalists have ethical rules. All these things are connected.* Aquí ya hay enumeración y conexión, pero le falta densidad analítica y verdadera integración. En **C1** alcanzamos la síntesis necesaria: *Taken together, the transformations examined across these units \u2014 the migration of authority from institutional gatekeepers to algorithmic curators, the commodification of attention that surveillance capitalism presupposes, the epistemic challenges that generative AI introduces, and the deontological strains that the attention economy places on the profession of verification \u2014 converge on a single question whose stakes are arguably higher than any of the individual phenomena suggests: whether the informational ecosystem on which democratic self-governance depends can retain enough shared trust to function, or whether the very mechanisms that have democratised access to information have, in the same motion, eroded the conditions under which that information can be collectively relied upon.* Esta unidad te enseña a producir ese tercer nivel de forma natural. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 54 C1](/curso-c1/unit-54)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 53 C1: Ética periodística](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-53-etica-periodistica)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 55 C1: Libre albedrío y determinismo](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-55-libre-albedrio-determinismo)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. La síntesis como destreza discursiva del C1 La síntesis (*synthesis*) es la destreza discursiva que integra múltiples elementos en un todo coherente que revela relaciones no evidentes en las partes. Se distingue del *summary* (resumen, que enumera) en que no se limita a yuxtaponer sino que muestra *convergences* (convergencias), *tensions* (tensiones), *hierarchies* (jerarquías) y *through-lines* (hilos conductores). Un hablante C1 escribe *whereas a summary would note that the units examined media transformation, privacy, AI and journalistic ethics in turn, a synthesis asks what these phenomena share, and the answer that emerges \u2014 that each represents a vector through which the relationship between information and trust is being renegotiated \u2014 is a claim that none of the individual analyses makes on its own but that all of them, taken together, substantiate.* La síntesis produce conocimiento que no está en las partes: es aditiva, no solo recapitulativa. ### 2. Conectores de síntesis Los conectores de síntesis son el andamiaje lingüístico de la integración: *taken together* (en conjunto), *in sum* (en suma), *what emerges from this* (lo que emerge de esto), *viewed holistically* (visto de forma holística), *the through-line that connects these* (el hilo que conecta estos), *seen in this light* (visto así), *against this backdrop* (contra este telón de fondo), *at the intersection of* (en la intersección de), *alongside this* (junto a esto), *the overarching point* (el punto que lo engloba). Un hablante C1 escribe *taken together, the erosion of gatekeeping authority, the rise of surveillance capitalism, the epistemic challenges of generative AI and the deontological strains on verification converge on a question that none of them poses in isolation: whether the informational commons can sustain the shared trust that democratic deliberation requires.* Estos conectores no decoran: construyen la arquitectura de la integración. ### 3. El through-line: el hilo conductor El *through-line* (hilo conductor) es el argumento que recorre y conecta temas aparentemente dispersos. Identificarlo es el acto central de la síntesis. En este bloque, un through-line posible es la *trust* (confianza) como recurso del ecosistema mediático: los medios tradicionales la erosionaron con su pérdida de autoridad, las plataformas la mercantilizaron con el engagement, la desinformación la ataca directamente, la IA la complica con lo sintético, y la ética periodística es el intento de preservarla. Un hablante C1 escribe *the through-line that connects these otherwise disparate phenomena is trust \u2014 its withdrawal from institutional gatekeepers, its monetisation by platforms whose business model treats it as an externality, its direct assault by disinformation, its complication by synthetic media, and its preservation as the explicit object of journalistic ethics \u2014 and seen in this light, the units of this block are not five topics but five perspectives on a single transformation.* El through-line convierte la enumeración en narrativa. ### 4. Jerarquización en la síntesis La síntesis jerarquiza: distingue lo fundamental de lo derivado. *The more fundamental point is* (el punto más fundamental es), *beneath these specifics lies* (debajo de estos detalles subyace), *the deeper question is* (la pregunta más profunda es), *what is at stake, ultimately, is* (lo que está en juego, en última instancia, es), *the root issue* (la cuestión de raíz), *the underlying dynamic* (la dinámica subyacente). Un hablante C1 escribe *beneath the specifics of platform design, data collection, algorithmic bias and editorial ethics lies a more fundamental question about the conditions under which a society can sustain a shared informational reality, and it is at that level \u2014 rather than at the level of any individual remedy \u2014 that the most consequential decisions about the future of the public sphere will, in all likelihood, be taken.* La jerarquización evita el flatten de todos los temas al mismo nivel. ### 5. Síntesis de medios tradicionales y digitales La síntesis de la transformación mediática integra *gatekeeping* (control de acceso), *disintermediation* (desintermediación), *attention economy* (economía de la atención), *platformisation* (plataformización), *audience fragmentation* (fragmentación de audiencias), *content moderation* (moderación de contenidos). Un hablante C1 escribe *the migration of authority from editorial gatekeepers to algorithmic curators is not, as the nostalgic framing would have it, a simple displacement of judgement by automation, but a restructuring of the conditions under which information achieves visibility, for whereas the gatekeeper's selection was at least legible as a human editorial choice, the curator's ranking is opaque in its criteria and optimised for an outcome \u2014 engagement \u2014 whose relationship to informational quality is, at best, contingent.* La síntesis muestra que la transformación no es pérdida sino reestructuración de las condiciones de visibilidad. ### 6. Síntesis de desinformación y verificación La síntesis de la desinformación integra *fake news* (noticias falsas), *misinformation* vs *disinformation* (información errónea vs deliberadamente falsa), *filter bubbles* (burbujas de filtro), *echo chambers* (cámaras de eco), *verification* (verificación), *source literacy* (alfabetización sobre fuentes). Un hablante C1 escribe *viewed holistically, the disinformation challenge is not adequately framed as a problem of individual credulity correctable by better fact-checking, for the structural conditions \u2014 algorithmic curation that rewards engagement, filter bubbles that insulate belief from contestation, and the collapse of shared gatekeeping that once supplied a common baseline of verified fact \u2014 interact in ways that make the individual-psychology framing a diagnosis of symptoms rather than of the disease.* La síntesis eleva el diagnóstico de lo individual a lo estructural. ### 7. Síntesis de privacidad y vigilancia La síntesis de privacidad integra *surveillance capitalism* (capitalismo de vigilancia), *behavioural surplus* (excedente conductual), *data extraction* (extracción de datos), *targeted advertising* (publicidad dirigida), *contextual integrity* (integridad contextual), *right to be forgotten* (derecho al olvido). Un hablante C1 escribe *the synthesis of the privacy and media transformations reveals a connection that neither analysis foregrounds on its own: the same extraction of behavioural surplus that funds the platforms to which editorial authority has migrated means that the economic model of the new information ecosystem is one in which the user is simultaneously the audience and the raw material, a dual role whose tension the advertising model of the legacy press, for all its limitations, did not embody.* La síntesis revela una conexión que las partes no muestran solas. ### 8. Síntesis de IA y ecosistema informativo La síntesis de la IA integra *algorithmic curation* (curaduría algorítmica), *generative AI* (IA generativa), *synthetic media* (medios sintéticos), *alignment problem* (problema de alineación), *algorithmic bias* (sesgo algorítmico), *hedging* (matización epistémica). Un hablante C1 escribe *at the intersection of the AI and media transformations lies a complication that compounds the trust crisis: the prospect that synthetic media, by eroding the commonsense presumption that audiovisual evidence is by default trustworthy, could undermine the very evidentiary foundation on which verification \u2014 the discipline that distinguishes journalism from assertion \u2014 has historically rested, a degradation whose full consequences may, over time, prove more corrosive than any single fabricated clip.* La síntesis identifica una intersección con consecuencias compuestas. ### 9. Síntesis de ética periodística bajo presión La síntesis de la ética bajo presión integra *duty to inform* (deber de informar), *minimisation of harm* (minimización del daño), *engagement metrics* (métricas de engagement), *church-state separation* (separación redacción-publicidad), *verification under speed* (verificación bajo presión temporal), *right of reply* (derecho de réplica). Un hablante C1 escribe *seen in this light, the deontological strains on journalism are not an independent crisis but the ethical expression of the same transformation that has restructured the economic and technological conditions of the profession, for the pressure of engagement metrics on editorial decisions, the erosion of the church-state separation by native advertising, and the compression of verification time by the demand for immediacy are all manifestations of a single dynamic in which the economic model of the attention economy is misaligned with the deontological duty to inform.* La síntesis muestra que las presiones éticas son expresión de la misma transformación estructural. ### 10. La convergencia: la confianza como recurso común La convergencia de todos los temas en la *trust* (confianza) como recurso común: *informational commons* (procomún informativo), *shared reality* (realidad compartida), *epistemic commons* (procomún epistémico), *trust as a commons* (la confianza como bien común), *collective sense-making* (construcción colectiva de sentido), *social capital* (capital social), *institutional legitimacy* (legitimidad institucional). Un hablante C1 escribe *the overarching point is that trust functions in the informational ecosystem as a commons \u2014 a resource that each actor draws upon but that none alone can sustain \u2014 and the tragedy that the convergence of these transformations risks producing is the tragedy of that commons: a situation in which the rational individual incentives of platforms, outlets and users combine, without any of them intending it, to degrade the very shared reality on which all of them, including the individual rational actors, ultimately depend.* La confianza como bien común es el marco unificador. ### 11. Tensiones y trade-offs en la síntesis La síntesis honesta reconoce tensiones: *on the one hand* (por una parte), *on the other hand* (por otra parte), *the tension between* (la tensión entre), *the trade-off* (el intercambio), *in tension with* (en tensión con), *not without cost* (no sin coste), *cuts both ways* (es de doble filo). Un hablante C1 escribe *the synthesis must hold the tension between two truths that the individual analyses each lean towards: that the democratisation of publishing has, on the one hand, given voice to perspectives that the gatekeeping model excluded, and that it has, on the other hand, removed the filtering that, for all its biases, supplied a common baseline of verified fact \u2014 a trade-off whose net effect on the public sphere is not captured by narratives that celebrate only the first or lament only the second.* La síntesis sostiene la tensión sin resolverla falsamente. ### 12. Léxico de la evaluación integrada La evaluación integrada emplea léxico de juicio calibrado: *arguably* (arguibilmente), *in all likelihood* (con toda probabilidad), *the evidence, taken together, suggests* (la evidencia, en conjunto, sugiere), *it is plausible that* (es plausible que), *the cumulative effect* (el efecto acumulado), *the net effect* (el efecto neto), *on balance* (en conjunto). Un hablante C1 escribe *the evidence, taken together, suggests that the net effect of these transformations on the capacity of the public sphere to sustain informed deliberation is, on balance, more ambiguous than either the celebratory or the catastrophic narrative allows, for the same mechanisms that have democratised access have, in the same motion, eroded the conditions of shared trust under which that access translates into collective sense-making.* La evaluación integrada es calibrada, no polarizada. ### 13. De la descripción a la prescripción La síntesis madura pasa de la *description* (descripción) a la *prescription* (prescripción): *what follows from this* (lo que se sigue de esto), *the implication is that* (la implicación es que), *this points towards* (esto apunta hacia), *the policy consequence* (la consecuencia política), *if this analysis is correct* (si este análisis es correcto), *the remedy, then, is not* (el remedio, entonces, no es), *but rather* (sino más bien). Un hablante C1 escribe *if this analysis is correct, the remedy is not to restore the gatekeeping model whose biases the democratisation of publishing rightly contested, but rather to build the institutional and architectural conditions under which the benefits of open access and the discipline of verification can coexist \u2014 a project whose difficulty is, admittedly, considerable, but whose necessity the synthesis of these transformations makes difficult to deny.* La síntesis madura genera prescripción, no solo diagnóstico. ### 14. Conectores de recapitulación jerárquica Los conectores de recapitulación jerárquica estructuran el cierre de la síntesis: *to recapitulate* (para recapitular), *in the final analysis* (en última instancia), *what this comes down to* (a lo que esto se reduce), *the thread that runs through all of this* (el hilo que recorre todo esto), *pulling these threads together* (juntando estos hilos), *the net conclusion* (la conclusión neta). Un hablante C1 escribe *pulling these threads together, what this comes down to is that the transformations examined across this block are not five crises but one \u2014 a restructuring of the relationship between information and trust \u2014 and that the adequacy of any response to it will be measured not by how well it addresses any single vector but by whether it grasps the underlying dynamic that connects them.* La recapitulación jerárquica cierra la síntesis sin perder el hilo. ### 15. Cohesión en ensayos de síntesis La cohesión en ensayos de síntesis combina conectores de integración y jerarquización en una arquitectura que avanza: *having examined X, we are in a position to* (habiendo examinado X, estamos en condiciones de), *this in turn* (esto a su vez), *it is against this backdrop that* (es contra este telón de fondo que), *the cumulative picture is one of* (el cuadro acumulado es de), *what unifies these* (lo que unifica estos). Un hablante C1 escribe *having examined the transformation of media, the challenge of disinformation, the economics of surveillance, the implications of AI and the strains on journalistic ethics, we are in a position to see that what unifies these is not a shared topic but a shared question \u2014 the question of whether the informational commons can sustain the trust that democratic deliberation requires \u2014 and it is against this backdrop that the adequacy of any proposed remedy must, in the final analysis, be assessed.* La cohesión de síntesis es arquitectónica: cada conector coloca una pieza en el edificio. ## Parte II — Ejercicios **Ejercicio 1.** Completa con conectores de síntesis: *taken together*, *what emerges from this*, *the through-line*, *seen in this light*. 1. ______, the phenomena examined are not separate crises but facets of one transformation. 2. ______ that connects these otherwise disparate units is the renegotiation of trust. 3. ______, the deontological strains are not an independent crisis but the ethical expression of the same dynamic. 4. ______ is a claim that none of the individual analyses makes on its own.
Ver solución 1. Taken together 2. The through-line 3. Seen in this light 4. What emerges from this These connectors do not merely link sentences; they perform the intellectual work of synthesis \u2014 showing convergence (*taken together*), identifying the connecting thread (*the through-line*), reframing a phenomenon (*seen in this light*), and naming the emergent claim (*what emerges from this*).
**Ejercicio 2.** Reescribe esta enumeración plana como una síntesis C1: "We studied media, privacy, AI and journalism. They are all about information and trust."
Ver solución *Taken together, the transformations examined across this block \u2014 the restructuring of media authority, the rise of surveillance capitalism, the epistemic challenges of generative AI, and the deontological strains on verification \u2014 converge on a single question that none of them poses in isolation: whether the informational commons can sustain the shared trust on which democratic deliberation depends, a through-line that recasts what might appear as four separate crises as four perspectives on one underlying renegotiation of the relationship between information and credibility.* The rewrite performs three synthesising moves: it names the convergence (*taken together... converge on*), identifies the through-line (trust as the common question), and reframes the four as perspectives on one transformation rather than separate crises.
**Ejercicio 3.** Escribe una frase en C1 que jerarquice \u2014que muestre qué es lo fundamental debajo de los detalles\u2014 usando al menos una expresión de jerarquización.
Ver solución *Beneath the specifics of platform design, data collection, algorithmic bias and editorial ethics lies a more fundamental question about the conditions under which a society can sustain a shared informational reality, and it is at that level \u2014 rather than at the level of any individual remedy \u2014 that the most consequential decisions about the future of the public sphere will, in all likelihood, be taken.* The hierarchising expression *beneath the specifics... lies a more fundamental question* does the synthesis work: it distinguishes the surface phenomena from the underlying dynamic and asserts that the latter is where the stakes are highest.
**Ejercicio 4.** Traduce al inglés C1: "En conjunto, la transformación de los medios, la desinformación, el capitalismo de vigilancia y la IA convergen en una pregunta que ninguno plantea aislado: si el procomún informativo puede sostener la confianza compartida."
Ver solución *Taken together, the transformation of the media, the challenge of disinformation, the rise of surveillance capitalism and the implications of AI converge on a question that none of them poses in isolation: whether the informational commons can sustain the shared trust on which democratic deliberation depends.* Key synthesising vocabulary: *taken together*, *converge on*, *none of them poses in isolation*, *informational commons*, *shared trust*. The construction *converge on a question that none poses alone* is the signature move of synthesis: the whole produces a question the parts do not.
**Ejercicio 5.** Reescribe esta afirmación dual como una síntesis que sostenga la tensión: "Democratising publishing is good. But it also removed filtering."
Ver solución *The synthesis must hold the tension between two truths that the individual analyses each lean towards: that the democratisation of publishing has, on the one hand, given voice to perspectives that the gatekeeping model excluded, and that it has, on the other hand, removed the filtering that, for all its biases, supplied a common baseline of verified fact \u2014 a trade-off whose net effect on the public sphere is not captured by narratives that celebrate only the first or lament only the second.* The synthesising moves: *hold the tension between*, *on the one hand / on the other hand*, *for all its biases* (concession that the filtering was imperfect), *a trade-off whose net effect... is not captured by narratives that...*. The sentence refuses to resolve the tension falsely.
**Ejercicio 6.** Completa con léxico de evaluación integrada: *arguably*, *on balance*, *the net effect*, *in all likelihood*. 1. ______, the cumulative impact is more ambiguous than either narrative allows. 2. The evidence, taken together, suggests that ______ is a restructuring of the conditions of trust. 3. ______, the same mechanisms that democratised access have eroded the conditions of shared credibility. 4. ______, the most consequential decisions will be taken at the structural rather than the individual level.
Ver solución 1. On balance 2. the net effect 3. arguably (or in all likelihood) 4. in all likelihood These expressions calibrate the integrated judgement: *on balance* weighs competing considerations, *the net effect* names the cumulative outcome, *arguably* signals a defensible but contestable claim, and *in all likelihood* signals probability without certainty. Synthesis without calibration becomes assertion.
**Ejercicio 7.** Escribe una frase en C1 que integre la transformación mediática y la economía de la vigilancia, revelando una conexión que ninguna muestra sola.
Ver solución *The synthesis of the privacy and media transformations reveals a connection that neither analysis foregrounds on its own: the same extraction of behavioural surplus that funds the platforms to which editorial authority has migrated means that the economic model of the new information ecosystem is one in which the user is simultaneously the audience and the raw material, a dual role whose tension the advertising model of the legacy press, for all its limitations, did not embody.* The synthesising move is to identify the *connection that neither foregrounds on its own* \u2014 that the platform economy fuses the audience and the raw material in a way the legacy press did not. This is emergent insight: a claim produced by the integration, not present in either part.
**Ejercicio 8.** Reescribe con síntesis jerárquica: "Fact-checking won't solve disinformation. Algorithms cause it. Bubbles reinforce it."
Ver solución *Viewed holistically, the disinformation challenge is not adequately framed as a problem of individual credulity correctable by better fact-checking, for the structural conditions \u2014 algorithmic curation that rewards engagement, filter bubbles that insulate belief from contestation, and the collapse of shared gatekeeping that once supplied a common baseline of verified fact \u2014 interact in ways that make the individual-psychology framing a diagnosis of symptoms rather than of the disease, which is to say that the remedy, if this analysis is correct, lies at the structural level rather than at the level of correcting any single falsehood.* The synthesising moves: *viewed holistically* reframes, the list of structural conditions shows interaction, *diagnosis of symptoms rather than of the disease* hierarchises, and *the remedy... lies at the structural level* moves from description to prescription. The rewrite integrates three claims into one structural diagnosis.
**Ejercicio 9.** Escribe una frase en C1 que muestre cómo la IA y la ética periodística se intersectan en el problema de la verificación, usando vocabulario de síntesis.
Ver solución *At the intersection of the AI and media transformations lies a complication that compounds the trust crisis: the prospect that synthetic media, by eroding the commonsense presumption that audiovisual evidence is by default trustworthy, could undermine the very evidentiary foundation on which verification \u2014 the discipline that distinguishes journalism from assertion \u2014 has historically rested, a degradation whose full consequences may, over time, prove more corrosive than any single fabricated clip.* The synthesising expression *at the intersection of* identifies the point where two transformations compound each other, and the sentence shows how the AI challenge (synthetic media) attacks the foundation (evidentiary trust) on which the ethical discipline (verification) rests. This is synthesis as the identification of compounding effects.
**Ejercicio 10.** Traduce al inglés C1: "Lo que une a estos no es un tema compartido sino una pregunta compartida: si el procomún informativo puede sostener la confianza."
Ver solución *What unifies these is not a shared topic but a shared question \u2014 the question of whether the informational commons can sustain the trust that democratic deliberation requires \u2014 and it is against this backdrop that the adequacy of any proposed remedy must, in the final analysis, be assessed.* The key construction *what unifies these is not a shared topic but a shared question* performs the synthesising move of distinguishing surface commonality (topic) from deep commonality (question). The phrase *against this backdrop* then uses the synthesis as the frame for evaluating remedies.
**Ejercicio 11.** Reescribe esta conclusión plana como una síntesis C1 que pase de la descripción a la prescripción: "Things are bad. We should do something."
Ver solución *If this analysis is correct, the remedy is not to restore the gatekeeping model whose biases the democratisation of publishing rightly contested, but rather to build the institutional and architectural conditions under which the benefits of open access and the discipline of verification can coexist \u2014 a project whose difficulty is, admittedly, considerable, but whose necessity the synthesis of these transformations makes difficult to deny.* The synthesising moves: *if this analysis is correct* (grounds the prescription in the synthesis), *the remedy is not... but rather...* (distinguishes false remedy from genuine one), and *whose necessity the synthesis... makes difficult to deny* (closes the loop by deriving the prescription from the integrated analysis). The move from description to prescription is the hallmark of mature synthesis.
**Ejercicio 12.** Completa con conectores de recapitulación jerárquica: *pulling these threads together*, *in the final analysis*, *what this comes down to*, *the thread that runs through*. 1. ______, these are not five crises but one restructuring of trust. 2. ______ all of this is a renegotiation of the information-credibility relationship. 3. ______, the adequacy of any remedy will be measured by whether it grasps the underlying dynamic. 4. ______ these units is the question of shared informational reality.
Ver solución 1. Pulling these threads together 2. What this comes down to 3. In the final analysis 4. The thread that runs through These connectors close the synthesis by recapitulating at a higher level: *pulling these threads together* gathers, *what this comes down to* distils, *in the final analysis* delivers the ultimate judgement, and *the thread that runs through* names the through-line in closing. Together they form the architecture of a synthesising conclusion.
**Ejercicio 13.** Escribe una frase en C1 que use la metáfora de la confianza como bien común (*commons*) para unificar los temas del bloque.
Ver solución *The overarching point is that trust functions in the informational ecosystem as a commons \u2014 a resource that each actor draws upon but that none alone can sustain \u2014 and the tragedy that the convergence of these transformations risks producing is the tragedy of that commons: a situation in which the rational individual incentives of platforms, outlets and users combine, without any of them intending it, to degrade the very shared reality on which all of them, including the individual rational actors, ultimately depend.* The metaphor of the *commons* (and the *tragedy of the commons*) unifies the block by providing a single explanatory frame: each transformation (media, privacy, AI, ethics) is a vector through which individual rational incentives degrade a shared resource. The synthesising expression *the overarching point is* introduces the unifying frame.
**Ejercicio 14.** Reescribe con evaluación integrada calibrada: "The internet destroyed journalism and democracy. Everything is worse now."
Ver solución *The evidence, taken together, suggests that the net effect of these transformations on the capacity of the public sphere to sustain informed deliberation is, on balance, more ambiguous than either the celebratory or the catastrophic narrative allows, for the same mechanisms that have democratised access have, in the same motion, eroded the conditions of shared trust under which that access translates into collective sense-making \u2014 a dual character that a synthesis, unlike a polemic, is bound to hold rather than resolve.* The calibration moves: *the evidence, taken together, suggests* (grounded, not asserted), *more ambiguous than either narrative allows* (rejects both poles), *on balance* (weighs), *a dual character that a synthesis... is bound to hold rather than resolve* (names the discipline of synthesis). The rewrite replaces polemic with calibrated integrated judgement.
**Ejercicio 15.** Escribe una frase en C1 que muestre cómo las presiones éticas sobre el periodismo son expresión de la misma transformación estructural, usando vocabulario de síntesis.
Ver solución *Seen in this light, the deontological strains on journalism are not an independent crisis but the ethical expression of the same transformation that has restructured the economic and technological conditions of the profession, for the pressure of engagement metrics on editorial decisions, the erosion of the church-state separation by native advertising, and the compression of verification time by the demand for immediacy are all manifestations of a single dynamic in which the economic model of the attention economy is misaligned with the deontological duty to inform.* The synthesising moves: *seen in this light* reframes, *not an independent crisis but the ethical expression of the same transformation* identifies the unity, and the list of three manifestations shows they are *all manifestations of a single dynamic*. The sentence integrates ethical, economic and technological phenomena under one structural diagnosis.
**Ejercicio 16.** Usa la estructura *having examined X, we are in a position to Y* para sintetizar el bloque entero en una frase.
Ver solución *Having examined the transformation of media, the challenge of disinformation, the economics of surveillance, the implications of AI and the strains on journalistic ethics, we are in a position to see that what unifies these is not a shared topic but a shared question \u2014 the question of whether the informational commons can sustain the trust that democratic deliberation requires \u2014 and it is against this backdrop that the adequacy of any proposed remedy must, in the final analysis, be assessed.* The structure *having examined X, we are in a position to Y* performs the synthesising move of deriving the conclusion from the cumulative examination: the list acknowledges the parts, *we are in a position to see* signals the emergent insight, and *what unifies these* names the through-line that the integration reveals.
**Ejercicio 17.** Reescribe esta afirmación sobre remedios con la precisión sintetizadora de un C1: "We need to fix the internet. Regulation will solve everything."
Ver solución *If the foregoing synthesis is correct, the adequacy of any remedy will be measured not by how well it addresses any single vector \u2014 disinformation, surveillance, algorithmic bias or editorial pressure \u2014 but by whether it grasps the underlying dynamic that connects them, which is to say that a regulatory response confined to individual symptoms, however well-intentioned, risks reproducing the fragmentation that the diagnosis identifies as the problem, for a structural condition is not adequately addressed by a catalogue of unrelated fixes.* The synthesising moves: *if the foregoing synthesis is correct* (grounds the claim in the integration), *not by how well it addresses any single vector... but by whether it grasps the underlying dynamic* (hierarchises remedy by structural grasp), and *a structural condition is not adequately addressed by a catalogue of unrelated fixes* (derives the prescription from the diagnosis). The rewrite replaces slogan with structurally grounded prescription.
**Ejercicio 18.** Escribe un párrafo breve (4-5 frases) en C1 que sintetice el bloque entero \u2014medios, desinformación, privacidad, IA y ética\u2014 identificando el through-line y moviéndose hacia una prescripción.
Ver solución *Taken together, the transformations examined across this block \u2014 the restructuring of media authority, the challenge of disinformation, the rise of surveillance capitalism, the epistemic implications of AI and the deontological strains on verification \u2014 converge on a question that none of them poses in isolation: whether the informational commons can sustain the shared trust on which democratic deliberation depends. The through-line that connects these is not a shared topic but a shared dynamic \u2014 the renegotiation of the relationship between information and credibility \u2014 and seen in this light, what might appear as five separate crises are more adequately understood as five perspectives on a single transformation. To be sure, the synthesis must hold the tension between the democratisation that these mechanisms have enabled and the erosion of shared trust they have, in the same motion, produced, for a narrative that celebrates only the former or laments only the latter fails to capture the dual character that the evidence, on balance, sustains. If this analysis is correct, the remedy is not to restore a gatekeeping model whose biases the democratisation of publishing rightly contested, but rather to build the institutional and architectural conditions under which open access and the discipline of verification can coexist \u2014 a project whose difficulty is, admittedly, considerable, but whose necessity the synthesis makes difficult to deny.* Synthesising features: *taken together... converge on*, *the through-line that connects these*, *seen in this light*, *the synthesis must hold the tension*, *on balance*, *if this analysis is correct... the remedy is not... but rather*. The paragraph moves from convergence to through-line to tension to prescription \u2014 the full arc of a synthesising argument.
**Ejercicio 19.** Escribe un párrafo breve (4-5 frases) en inglés C1 que evalúe de forma integrada el estado del ecosistema mediático, usando al menos tres conectores de síntesis y la metáfora de la confianza como bien común.
Ver solución *The overarching point that emerges from pulling these threads together is that trust functions in the informational ecosystem as a commons \u2014 a resource that each actor draws upon but that none alone can sustain, and whose degradation, once it passes a certain threshold, is liable to become self-reinforcing. Against this backdrop, the convergence of the transformations examined across this block takes on a character that the individual analyses do not fully convey: the migration of authority to platforms whose business model treats trust as an externality, the assault of disinformation on the presumption of good faith, the complication of evidentiary reliability by synthetic media, and the ethical strains on the profession of verification are, in the final analysis, not parallel phenomena but mutually reinforcing vectors of a single erosion. What this comes down to is that the adequacy of any response will be measured not by its effect on any one vector but by whether it grasps the dynamic that connects them, for a commons cannot be defended by measures that address its depletion in one quadrant while leaving the mechanisms of its depletion in the others intact. The honest synthesis, then, is neither the celebratory narrative that counts the gains of democratisation and stops there, nor the catastrophic one that counts the losses and stops there, but the more demanding recognition that the same transformation has produced both \u2014 and that the question of whether the net effect can be made to favour the public is one that the architecture of the ecosystem, not the goodwill of any individual actor within it, will ultimately decide.* Synthesising connectors: *the overarching point that emerges from pulling these threads together*, *against this backdrop*, *in the final analysis*, *what this comes down to*. Metaphor: *trust as a commons*, *self-reinforcing degradation*, *mutually reinforcing vectors of a single erosion*, *defended by measures that address its depletion in one quadrant*. The paragraph enacts the culminating C1 skill: integrated evaluation that refuses both polemic and complacency, and grounds its prescription in the structural diagnosis that the synthesis produces.
## Resumen de la unidad En esta unidad hemos consolidado el andamiaje lingüístico del bloque dedicado a los medios, la información y la transformación digital, elevando las destrezas de las unidades anteriores al nivel de la síntesis argumentativa. Has aprendido a manejar los conectores de síntesis \u2014*taken together*, *what emerges from this*, *the through-line that connects these*, *seen in this light*\u2014, las expresiones de jerarquización \u2014*beneath the specifics lies*, *the more fundamental point is*, *the underlying dynamic*\u2014 y las de evaluación integrada \u2014*on balance*, *the net effect*, *the evidence, taken together, suggests*\u2014. Has incorporado el léxico de la convergencia \u2014*informational commons*, *shared reality*, *trust as a commons*, *mutually reinforcing vectors*\u2014 y el de la prescripción madura \u2014*the remedy is not... but rather*, *if this analysis is correct*, *the adequacy of any remedy will be measured by*\u2014. Has ejercitado la identificación del *through-line* que convierte la enumeración en narrativa, el sostén de las tensiones sin resolución falsa, y el paso de la descripción a la prescripción que la síntesis madura sustenta. La destreza central de esta unidad es la integración: la capacidad de mostrar cómo los temas aparentemente dispersos del bloque convergen en una pregunta compartida, de jerarquizar lo fundamental debajo de los detalles, y de derivar del análisis integrado una prescripción que ningún análisis individual habría fundamentado. Esa arquitectura sintetizadora es la marca distintiva del hablante C1 cuando cierra un bloque temático: no quien acumula, sino quien integra; no quien enumera, sino quien revela las relaciones que la enumeración oculta.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es la deontología periodística y qué léxico asocia en inglés?
faqs.answer: La deontología periodística es el conjunto de principios y códigos que rigen la conducta profesional. Su léxico incluye accuracy, fairness, impartiality, right of reply, off the record, attribution, sourcing, verification, public interest y code of ethics.

faqs.question: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre 'off the record', 'on background' y 'on the record'?
faqs.answer: On the record significa que la información puede citarse con atribución; on background permite usar la información pero sin atribuir la fuente directamente; off the record significa que la información no puede publicarse, solo sirve para orientar al periodista.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se cita correctamente una fuente en inglés periodístico C1?
faqs.answer: Con verbos de atribución variados (said, stated, argued, acknowledged, conceded), atribución clara de la fuente, comillas para citas directas y paráfrasis para indirectas, distinguiendo siempre lo dicho de lo interpretado.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es el 'public interest' y cómo se distingue de 'public curiosity'?
faqs.answer: Public interest es el interés legítimo de la ciudadanía en información que afecta al bien común (corrupción, salud pública); public curiosity es el mero interés morboso por la vida privada. La deontología exige publicar según el primero, no el segundo.

content:
La ética periodística es el terreno donde el oficio de informar se encuentra con la responsabilidad de hacerlo bien, y debatirla con propiedad exige un léxico que combine la deontología profesional con la técnica de la atribución. No basta con decir que *journalists should be fair*; hay que distinguir *accuracy* de *fairness*, *off the record* de *on background*, *public interest* de *public curiosity*, y citar fuentes con la precisión que la credibilidad del discurso exige. En esta unidad del curso de inglés C1 gratis exploramos cómo los hablantes avanzados manejan el léxico de la deontología periodística \u2014desde *right of reply* hasta *code of ethics*\u2014, cómo citan con verbos de atribución matizados y cómo debaten los dilemas éticos del periodismo con un rigor que reconoce tanto la presión comercial como el deber de servir al público. Es un terreno donde el lenguaje construye confianza: *stated*, *acknowledged*, *conceded* y *argued* no son sinónimos intercambiables, sino instrumentos que señalan al lector exactamente qué dijo la fuente, cómo lo dijo y qué peso otorgarle. Para situar el nivel, observa cómo el mismo tema se expresa en tres niveles. En **A2** diríamos: *Journalists must tell the truth. They should not lie. It is important to be honest.* Es claro pero plano, sin vocabulario técnico ni matices. En **B2** subiríamos un peldaño: *Journalists have to check their sources. They should give both sides of the story. Sometimes it is hard to balance privacy and the public interest.* Aquí ya hay problema y principios, pero le falta densidad deontológica y precisión en la cita. En **C1** alcanzamos la precisión necesaria: *While the insistence on balance \u2014 that perennial touchstone of journalistic self-regulation \u2014 may, in its aspiration to fairness, serve as a guard against the covert insertion of editorial opinion, its uncritical application risks producing a false equivalence in which the measured consensus of the scientific community and the marginal dissent of a vested interest are afforded equal weight, a practice that, in the name of impartiality, arguably does more to mislead the public than the partisanship it was designed to prevent.* Esta unidad te enseña a producir ese tercer nivel de forma natural. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 53 C1](/curso-c1/unit-53)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 52 C1: IA y sociedad](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-52-ia-sociedad)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 54 C1: Consolidación de medios](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-54-consolidacion-medios)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. Los principios deontológicos fundamentales La deontología periodística (*journalistic ethics* o *professional ethics*) se articula en torno a principios fundamentales: *accuracy* (exactitud, la fidelidad a los hechos), *fairness* (equidad, trato justo de las partes), *impartiality* (imparcialidad, ausencia de sesgo), *objectivity* (objetividad, la aspiración a separar hecho de opinión), *independence* (independencia, libertad de presiones comerciales o políticas), *accountability* (rendición de cuentas), *transparency* (transparencia sobre métodos y fuentes), *minimisation of harm* (minimización del daño). Un hablante C1 escribe *the tension between accuracy and speed \u2014 between getting it right and getting it first \u2014 is not a dilemma that a code of ethics can resolve in the abstract, for it is constitutive of the profession itself, and the mark of an ethically serious newsroom is not that it never errs but that its error-correction practices are robust enough to make the cost of a mistake a stimulus to accuracy rather than a precedent for its erosion.* Estos principios no son adornos sino el fundamento de la credibilidad. ### 2. Léxico de la atribución y la cita La atribución (*attribution*) es el mecanismo mediante el cual el periodista señala la fuente de una afirmación. Sus verbos son matizados: *said* (dijo, neutro), *stated* (manifestó, formal), *claimed* (afirmó, con matiz de reserva), *argued* (argumentó), *acknowledged* (reconoció, admisión), *conceded* (concedió, reticente), *asserted* (aseveró, con fuerza), *maintained* (sostuvo, con persistencia), *denied* (negó), *admitted* (admitió), *noted* (observó), *warned* (advirtió), *insisted* (insistió). Un hablante C1 escribe *whereas the minister *stated* that the policy had reduced waiting times, the leaked internal memo *acknowledged* that the figures conflated two categories in a manner that the opposition *claimed* was designed to flatter the headline statistic, a characterisation the government *denied* while *conceding* that the methodology would be reviewed.* Cada verbo posiciona al lector respecto a la credibilidad y la actitud de la fuente. ### 3. On the record, off the record, on background La gestión de las fuentes exige distinguir niveles de atribución: *on the record* (en el registro, información atribuible con nombre), *off the record* (fuera del registro, no publicable, solo orienta al periodista), *on background* o *not for attribution* (en segundo plano, publicable pero sin atribuir la fuente), *deep background* (fondo profundo, publicable sin atribución y sin especificar siquiera que es una fuente), *embargo* (embargo, información publicable solo a partir de una fecha), *anonymous sourcing* (fuentes anónimas). Un hablante C1 escribe *the reliance on background sourcing, while sometimes indispensable in reporting on matters where named sources would face reprisal, carries a cost that the casual use of the construction *sources said* tends to obscure, for it asks the reader to extend trust to a source whose motives and reliability the journalist, by withholding identity, has not enabled them to assess.* La transparencia sobre el nivel de atribución es una obligación deontológica. ### 4. Verificación y sourcing La verificación (*verification*) es el núcleo del oficio: *sourcing* (localización de fuentes), *corroboration* (corroboración, confirmación por fuentes independientes), *single-source reporting* (reportaje de fuente única, de riesgo controvertido), *triangulation* (triangulación, cruzar varias fuentes), *fact-checking* (comprobación de hechos), *primary source* (fuente primaria), *secondary source* (fuente secundaria), *documentary evidence* (evidencia documental), *anonymous source* (fuente anónima). Un hablante C1 escribe *the distinction between a story that has been corroborated by two independent sources and one that rests on a single anonymous account is not a nicety of editorial pedantry but a structural difference in epistemic standing, since the former permits the reader to weigh convergent testimony while the latter asks them to extend trust that the journalist's verification \u2014 invisible to them \u2014 was as rigorous as the convention of single-sourcing demands.* La verificación es lo que separa el periodismo del rumor. ### 5. Public interest vs public curiosity La distinción entre *public interest* (interés público, el bien común de la información) y *public curiosity* (curiosidad pública, el mero interés morboso) es central en la deontología: *right to privacy* (derecho a la privacidad), *public figure* (figura pública), *private individual* (particular), *newsworthy* (digno de noticia), *legitimate public concern* (preocupación pública legítima), *voyeurism* (voyeurismo), *prurience* (morbosidad). Un hablante C1 escribe *the tendency of certain outlets to invoke the public interest as a post hoc justification for coverage that serves principally the public curiosity is a rhetorical manoeuvre that erodes the very concept it appropriates, for if every story that attracts readers can be retroactively deemed in the public interest, the term ceases to function as a constraint and becomes instead a license whose only limit is the market's appetite.* Mantener viva esta distinción es defender la integridad del concepto. ### 6. Right of reply y el trato justo de las partes El *right of reply* (derecho de réplica) es el principio de ofrecer a las partes afectadas la oportunidad de responder antes de la publicación: *right of reply*, *right to respond*, *fairness to all sides*, *no-condemnation-unheard* (nadie es condenado sin ser escuchado), *adversarial journalism* (periodismo adversarial), *due prominence* (prominencia debida, dar la rectificación el mismo espacio que el error). Un hablante C1 escribe *the right of reply, when treated as a formality to be discharged rather than a genuine opportunity for the subject to correct the record, becomes a procedural shell that satisfies the letter of the code while undermining its spirit, since a reply buried on page twelve while the accusation led page one is, in any meaningful sense, no reply at all.* El derecho de réplica es sustantivo, no ritual. ### 7. Independencia y conflictos de interés La independencia (*independence*) exige gestionar *conflicts of interest* (conflictos de interés): *disclosure* (declaración), *recusal* (abstención), *financial interest* (interés financiero), *sponsorship* (patrocinio), *advertorial* (publirreportaje), *native advertising* (publicidad nativa), *church-state separation* (separación entre redacción y publicidad), *lobbying* (cabildeo). Un hablante C1 escribe *the erosion of the church-state separation \u2014 the firewall between editorial and commercial operations \u2014 through the proliferation of native advertising that mimics the format of reportage risks a form of contamination more insidious than overt bias, for it asks the reader to apply the trust they have learned to extend to journalism to content whose production was governed by commercial rather than editorial priorities.* La transparencia sobre los conflictos es una obligación, no una opción. ### 8. Minimización del daño y temas sensibles El principio de *minimisation of harm* (minimización del daño) rige la cobertura de temas sensibles: *vulnerable sources* (fuentes vulnerables), *victims of crime* (víctimas de delitos), *grief intrusion* (intrusión en el duelo), *identification of minors* (identificación de menores), *sexual assault reporting* (cobertura de agresiones sexuales), *suicide reporting guidelines* (directrices sobre el suicidio), *stigmatisation* (estigmatización). Un hablante C1 escribe *the ethical weight of a decision to name a victim of sexual assault, or to identify a minor involved in a crime, is one that the calculus of newsworthiness alone cannot bear, since the reputational and psychological consequences for the individual are likely to outlast the news cycle that the publication will serve, a temporal asymmetry that the principle of minimisation of harm exists precisely to counterweight.* La minimización del daño contrarresta la tiranía del ciclo informativo. ### 9. Corrección y rectificación La gestión del error es parte de la deontología: *correction* (corrección), *retraction* (retractación), *clarification* (aclaración), *editor's note* (nota del editor), *due prominence* (prominencia debida), *accountability mechanism* (mecanismo de rendición de cuentas), *ombudsman* (defensor del lector), *readers' editor* (editor del lector). Un hablante C1 escribe *the practice of burying corrections in a角落 of the paper while the original error occupied the front page is one that treats the rectification as a regulatory inconvenience rather than an ethical obligation, whereas a genuinely accountable newsroom would insist on due prominence \u2014 the principle that the correction should be as visible as the mistake \u2014 not because the regulator demands it but because the credibility of the record depends on it.* La corrección visible es un indicador de seriedad ética. ### 10. Léxico del bias y la perspectiva El debate sobre el sesgo (*bias*) y la perspectiva: *bias* (sesgo), *partisanship* (parcialidad partidista), *editorial stance* (postura editorial), *framing* (encuadre), *selection bias* (sesgo de selección), *confirmation bias* (sesgo de confirmación), *false balance* o *false equivalence* (falso equilibrio), *he-said-she-said journalism* (periodismo de él-dijo-ella-dijo). Un hablante C1 escribe *the reflex of he-said-she-said reporting, by outsourcing the work of adjudication to a reader who has not been given the means to perform it, abdicates a responsibility that is properly the journalist's, for the distinction between reporting that two parties disagree and reporting on which of their claims the evidence supports is the distinction between stenography and journalism.* El periodismo no es taquigrafía. ### 11. Ética digital y nuevas plataformas La ética en el entorno digital: *clickbait* (cebo de clics), *engagement metrics* (métricas de engagement), *virality* (viralidad), *attention economy* (economía de la atención), *slow news* (noticias lentas), *live blogging ethics* (ética del blog en vivo), *social media sourcing* (fuentes en redes sociales), *unpublished material* (material no publicado). Un hablante C1 escribe *the pressure to optimise for engagement metrics \u2014 which reward the provocative and the emotive disproportionately \u2014 introduces an incentive structure whose alignment with the duty to inform is, at best, contingent, and a newsroom that allows that incentive to shape editorial decisions without explicit counterweight has, in effect, outsourced its news values to an algorithm it did not design and whose objectives it did not set.* Las métricas de engagement pueden erosionar el deber de informar. ### 12. Cita directa vs paráfrasis La distinción entre *direct quotation* (cita directa) y *paraphrase* (paráfrasis) es técnica: *verbatim* (literal), *ellipsis* (elipsis, omisión marcada con [...]), *brackets* (corchetes para aclaraciones), *quote marks* (comillas), *attribution tag* (etiqueta de atribución), *partial quote* (cita parcial), *out of context* (fuera de contexto), *misquotation* (cita errónea). Un hablante C1 escribe *the distinction between quoting a source verbatim within its original context and extracting a partial quote whose surrounding sentences would alter its meaning is the distinction between faithful reporting and a form of selective quotation that, while technically accurate in the words it reproduces, functions as a misrepresentation by omission.* La precisión técnica de la cita es una cuestión ética. ### 13. Protección de fuentes La protección de las fuentes (*source protection*): *confidential source* (fuente confidencial), *whistleblower* (denunciante), *source confidentiality* (confidencialidad de la fuente), *shield law* (ley de escudo), *contempt of court* (desacato al tribunal), *forced disclosure* (divulgación forzada), *chilling effect* (efecto disuasorio), *anonymous tip* (pista anónima). Un hablante C1 escribe *the journalist's obligation to protect a confidential source is not a personal preference but a structural precondition of the profession, for without credible assurance that the identity of sources will not be disclosed, the flow of information on which accountability journalism depends would, over time, attenuate to the point where the watchdog function becomes largely ceremonial.* La protección de fuentes sostiene el periodismo de investigación. ### 14. Dilemas éticos: privacidad vs revelación El dilema entre privacidad y revelación: *invasion of privacy* (invasión de la privacidad), *public interest override* (excepción de interés público), *legitimate expectation of privacy* (expectativa legítima de privacidad), *surveillance journalism* (periodismo de vigilancia), *sting operation* (operación trampa), *entrapment* (inducción), *hidden camera* (cámara oculta), *undercover reporting* (reportaje de incógnito). Un hablante C1 escribe *the use of undercover methods, while occasionally indispensable to expose wrongdoing that no source would volunteer, carries a cost to the profession's credibility that is rarely acknowledged in the moment of the scoop, since the precedent it sets \u2014 that deception is an acceptable tool when the end is sufficiently weighty \u2014 is one whose application to less meritorious cases the same logic will, in time, be invoked to justify.* El cálculo de medios y fines es el núcleo del dilema. ### 15. Cohesión en ensayos sobre ética periodística La cohesión en ensayos de ética periodística emplea conectores que articulan la tensión: *on the one hand* (por una parte), *on the other hand* (por otra parte), *that said* (dicho esto), *to be sure* (ciertamente), *at the same time* (al mismo tiempo), *in practice* (en la práctica), *in principle* (en principio), *in the final analysis* (en última instancia). Un hablante C1 escribe *on the one hand, the duty to inform the public of matters of legitimate concern is a foundational principle of the profession; on the other hand, the licence that duty grants is not unbounded, and in the final analysis the test is not whether a story is interesting but whether its publication serves a public interest weighty enough to override the privacy it intrudes upon.* Estos conectores sostienen la arquitectura del dilema ético. ## Parte II — Ejercicios **Ejercicio 1.** Completa con el principio deontológico correcto: *accuracy*, *fairness*, *impartiality*, *independence*. 1. The duty to report facts as they occurred, verified and unembellished, is ______. 2. The obligation to represent all relevant sides of a story without stacking the deck is ______. 3. The commitment to keep editorial decisions free from commercial or political pressure is ______. 4. The aspiration to separate fact from opinion and present neither as the other is ______.
Ver solución 1. accuracy 2. fairness 3. independence 4. impartiality These four principles form the core of most codes of ethics, though their application often involves trade-offs: accuracy may conflict with speed, fairness with the duty to expose wrongdoing, and impartiality with the journalist's responsibility to adjudicate competing claims.
**Ejercicio 2.** Elige el verbo de atribución que mejor captura la actitud de la fuente en cada caso. 1. The minister ______ that the figures had been presented in a flattering light, but denied deliberate intent. 2. The whistleblower ______ that the programme had been operating without oversight for years. 3. The CEO ______ the allegations of fraud, calling them baseless. 4. The scientist ______ that the early results were less conclusive than initially reported.
Ver solución 1. conceded — implies reluctant admission of a point that does not favour one's position. 2. asserted (or claimed) — signals a strong statement that the journalist is reporting but not necessarily endorsing. 3. denied — flat rejection of the allegations. 4. acknowledged — admission of a limitation, more neutral than *conceded*. The choice of attribution verb positions the reader: *conceded* signals reluctance, *asserted* signals force without journalist endorsement, *denied* signals flat rejection, and *acknowledged* signals a measured admission.
**Ejercicio 3.** Completa con el nivel de atribución correcto: *on the record*, *off the record*, *on background*, *embargo*. 1. Information that may be published but not attributed to the source by name is ______. 2. Information that may not be published at all and only guides the journalist's understanding is ______. 3. Information that may be quoted and attributed to the named source is ______. 4. Information released in advance on condition it is not published before a stated time is under ______.
Ver solución 1. on background (or not for attribution) 2. off the record 3. on the record 4. embargo The levels form a gradient of attribution. A C1 journalist manages these explicitly, and a C1 reader understands that *sources said* signals background sourcing whose verification the reader cannot independently assess.
**Ejercicio 4.** Reescribe esta afirmación excesivamente categórica sobre el equilibrio periodístico con la precisión deontológica de un C1: "Journalists must always give both sides equal weight."
Ver solución *While the principle of balance \u2014 that perennial touchstone of journalistic self-regulation \u2014 may, in its aspiration to fairness, serve as a guard against the covert insertion of editorial opinion, its uncritical application risks producing a false equivalence in which the measured consensus of the scientific community and the marginal dissent of a vested interest are afforded equal weight, a practice that, in the name of impartiality, arguably does more to mislead the public than the partisanship it was designed to prevent.* The revision distinguishes the legitimate aspiration of balance from its uncritical application, and introduces the concept of false equivalence to show that "both sides" is not always a neutral framing.
**Ejercicio 5.** Traduce al inglés C1: "El derecho de réplica, cuando se trata como una formalidad en lugar de una oportunidad genuina, se convierte en un procedimiento vacío que satisface la letra del código pero socava su espíritu."
Ver solución *The right of reply, when treated as a formality to be discharged rather than a genuine opportunity for the subject to correct the record, becomes a procedural shell that satisfies the letter of the code while undermining its spirit, since a reply buried on page twelve while the accusation led page one is, in any meaningful sense, no reply at all.* The key deontological vocabulary: *right of reply*, *formality to be discharged*, *letter of the code*, *undermining its spirit*, *due prominence* (implied by the page-twelve/front-page contrast).
**Ejercicio 6.** Completa con léxico de verificación: *corroboration*, *single-source reporting*, *triangulation*, *fact-checking*. 1. Confirming a claim through independent sources is ______. 2. Relying on one account without independent confirmation is ______. 3. Cross-referencing multiple sources and types of evidence is ______. 4. The systematic checking of factual claims before publication is ______.
Ver solución 1. corroboration 2. single-source reporting 3. triangulation 4. fact-checking These terms map the epistemic rigour of journalism: corroboration and triangulation strengthen a claim, single-sourcing carries acknowledged risk, and fact-checking is the systematic pre-publication discipline that distinguishes journalism from assertion.
**Ejercicio 7.** Escribe una frase en C1 que distinga *public interest* de *public curiosity*, usando vocabulario deontológico.
Ver solución *The tendency of certain outlets to invoke the public interest as a post hoc justification for coverage that serves principally the public curiosity is a rhetorical manoeuvre that erodes the very concept it appropriates, for if every story that attracts readers can be retroactively deemed in the public interest, the term ceases to function as a constraint and becomes instead a licence whose only limit is the market's appetite.* The distinction does the ethical work: *public interest* is a constraint that justifies intrusion; *public curiosity* is an appetite that does not. Conflating them turns the constraint into a licence.
**Ejercicio 8.** Reescribe con precisión deontológica: "The newspaper made a small mistake but fixed it later."
Ver solución *The newspaper issued a correction, though one whose due prominence \u2014 buried in a footnote on an inside page \u2014 fell considerably short of the visibility the original error had commanded, a discrepancy that, while technically discharging the obligation to rectify, arguably treated the correction as a regulatory inconvenience rather than an ethical duty to set the record as visibly as it had been distorted.* The revision introduces *correction*, *due prominence*, and the concept that the visibility of the rectification should match the visibility of the error \u2014 a substantive, not merely procedural, understanding of accountability.
**Ejercicio 9.** Completa con léxico de independencia y conflictos de interés: *native advertising*, *disclosure*, *church-state separation*, *advertorial*. 1. The firewall between editorial and commercial operations is the ______. 2. Content that mimics editorial format but is paid for by an advertiser is ______. 3. The transparent declaration of a journalist's financial or personal interest is ______. 4. A paid promotional feature presented in the style of editorial content is an ______.
Ver solución 1. church-state separation 2. native advertising 3. disclosure 4. advertorial Native advertising and advertorial both blur the editorial-commercial boundary; disclosure is the ethical counterweight, and the church-state separation is the structural firewall whose erosion is one of the principal contemporary threats to editorial independence.
**Ejercicio 10.** Reescribe este titular sensacionalista con el lenguaje ético de un C1: "SHOCKING SCANDAL: Politician's secret affair revealed!"
Ver solución *While the private life of a public figure may, in certain circumstances, bear a legitimate relationship to their public role \u2014 for instance, where it bears on their advocacy of family-values legislation \u2014 the publication of details that serve no evident public interest beyond the satisfaction of curiosity raises questions about whether the story's prominence reflects a judgement of newsworthiness or a calculation of engagement, a distinction that the code of ethics exists precisely to compel.* The revision reframes the question from sensation to the deontological test: does the private life bear a *legitimate relationship to the public role*? Without that relationship, the story serves curiosity, not interest.
**Ejercicio 11.** Escribe una frase en C1 sobre la protección de fuentes que explique por qué es una condición estructural del periodismo, no una preferencia personal.
Ver solución *The journalist's obligation to protect a confidential source is not a personal preference but a structural precondition of the profession, for without credible assurance that the identity of sources will not be disclosed, the flow of information on which accountability journalism depends would, over time, attenuate to the point where the watchdog function becomes largely ceremonial.* The key move is reframing source protection from an individual choice to a *structural precondition*: the argument is not that the journalist *wants* to protect sources but that the profession's function *depends* on it.
**Ejercicio 12.** Traduce al inglés C1: "El uso de métodos de incógnito, aunque ocasionalmente indispensable para exponer irregularidades que nadie denunciaría, conlleva un coste para la credibilidad de la profesión rara vez reconocido en el momento del exclusiva."
Ver solución *The use of undercover methods, while occasionally indispensable to expose wrongdoing that no source would volunteer, carries a cost to the profession's credibility that is rarely acknowledged in the moment of the scoop, since the precedent it sets \u2014 that deception is an acceptable tool when the end is sufficiently weighty \u2014 is one whose application to less meritorious cases the same logic will, in time, be invoked to justify.* Key vocabulary: *undercover methods*, *indispensable*, *wrongdoing*, *credibility*, *scoop*, *precedent*. The hedging (*while occasionally indispensable*, *rarely acknowledged*, *in time*) sustains the tension between the immediate justification and the long-term cost.
**Ejercicio 13.** Completa con léxico de cita: *verbatim*, *ellipsis*, *out of context*, *partial quote*. 1. Reproducing a source's words exactly as spoken is quoting ______. 2. The omission of words from a quotation, marked with [...], is an ______. 3. A quotation that reproduces only part of what was said is a ______. 4. Presenting a quote without the surrounding sentences that give it meaning is quoting ______.
Ver solución 1. verbatim 2. ellipsis 3. partial quote 4. out of context The ethical point: a partial quote that is technically verbatim but whose meaning changes without its context functions as misrepresentation by omission, even though the words reproduced are accurate. Precision in quotation is an ethical, not merely technical, matter.
**Ejercicio 14.** Reescribe esta afirmación sobre el sesgo con la precisión de un C1: "That newspaper is totally biased, it always supports one side."
Ver solución *While the newspaper's editorial stance is, on the available evidence, consistently aligned with one end of the political spectrum, the more analytically useful distinction is not between biased and unbiased outlets \u2014 a binary that flatters the self-image of those who claim neutrality \u2014 but between those that disclose their framing and those that present a perspective as the absence of one, since transparency about standpoint is arguably a more honest service to the reader than the performance of an objectivity that no human institution fully embodies.* The revision distinguishes *editorial stance* (disclosed) from *bias* (hidden), and argues that transparency about perspective is more honest than the performance of neutrality. This is the C1 move: from accusation to analysis.
**Ejercicio 15.** Escribe una frase en C1 sobre el efecto de las métricas de engagement en los valores editoriales, usando vocabulario deontológico.
Ver solución *The pressure to optimise for engagement metrics \u2014 which reward the provocative and the emotive disproportionately \u2014 introduces an incentive structure whose alignment with the duty to inform is, at best, contingent, and a newsroom that allows that incentive to shape editorial decisions without explicit counterweight has, in effect, outsourced its news values to an algorithm it did not design and whose objectives it did not set.* Key vocabulary: *engagement metrics*, *duty to inform*, *news values*, *editorial decisions*. The argument is that the incentive structure may be *misaligned* with the deontological duty, and that *outsourcing* news values to an algorithm is an abdication of editorial responsibility.
**Ejercicio 16.** Usa conectores de tensión (*on the one hand*, *on the other hand*, *in the final analysis*, *that said*) para articular el dilema entre el deber de informar y el respeto a la privacidad.
Ver solución *On the one hand, the duty to inform the public of matters of legitimate concern is a foundational principle of the profession, and the journalist who shrinks from it out of an excess of caution serves neither the public nor the truth; on the other hand, the licence that duty grants is not unbounded, and the fact that a story is interesting is not, in itself, sufficient warrant for the intrusion it may entail. That said, the line between the two is rarely self-evident in the moment of decision, and in the final analysis the test is not whether a story attracts readers but whether its publication serves a public interest weighty enough to override the privacy it intrudes upon \u2014 a judgement that, precisely because it cannot be reduced to a rule, remains the irreducible ethical core of the editor's responsibility.* The connectors orchestrate the dilemma: *on the one hand / on the other hand* present the two poles, *that said* acknowledges the difficulty of applying them, and *in the final analysis* delivers the synthesising test. This architecture is the hallmark of C1 ethical reasoning.
**Ejercicio 17.** Reescribe usando verbos de atribución matizados en lugar de *said*: "The minister said the policy worked. The report said it didn't. The opposition said it was a lie."
Ver solución *The minister *stated* that the policy had delivered the promised outcomes, while the independent report *acknowledged* that the headline figures concealed a deterioration in several underlying metrics, a characterisation the opposition *claimed* amounted to deliberate misrepresentation \u2014 a charge the government *denied* while *conceding* that the methodology would be reviewed.* The maturation from *said* to *stated / acknowledged / claimed / denied / conceded* does the analytical work: *stated* signals official assertion, *acknowledged* signals reluctant admission, *claimed* signals a charge the journalist is reporting without endorsing, *denied* signals flat rejection, and *conceded* signals a partial yielding. Each verb positions the reader.
**Ejercicio 18.** Escribe un párrafo breve (4-5 frases) en C1 que argumente sobre si el periodismo debe ser imparcial o transparente sobre su perspectiva, usando vocabulario deontológico y al menos dos conectores de tensión.
Ver solución *The debate between impartiality and transparency-about-perspective is often framed as a choice between two ideals, but the more honest framing may be that they are responses to different failures. On the one hand, impartiality, as an aspiration to separate fact from opinion and to weigh evidence without favour, remains a discipline whose abandonment would leave the public with no common informational ground; on the other hand, the performance of an objectivity that no human institution fully embodies can, when it conceals a standpoint that is in fact present, become a form of covert persuasion more misleading than openly declared opinion. That said, the two are not necessarily incompatible, and in the final analysis the ethically serious position may be one that pursues impartiality in method while being transparent about the perspective that the method is applied from \u2014 a synthesis that asks more of the journalist than either pure neutrality or pure disclosure, but that arguably serves the reader better than the false choice between them.* Deontological vocabulary: *impartiality*, *transparency*, *separate fact from opinion*, *objectivity*, *standpoint*, *perspective*. Connectors of tension: *on the one hand*, *on the other hand*, *that said*, *in the final analysis*. The paragraph models the C1 capacity to hold two principles in productive tension rather than collapsing one into the other.
**Ejercicio 19.** Escribe un párrafo breve (4-5 frases) en inglés C1 sobre un dilema ético del periodismo digital, usando al menos tres términos deontológicos y dos conectores de concesión.
Ver solución *The ethical challenges of digital journalism are, in several respects, continuations of old questions under new conditions rather than wholly novel dilemmas. Granted, the speed of publication and the pressure of engagement metrics have intensified the tension between accuracy and immediacy that has always defined the profession; that said, the underlying principle \u2014 that a story should be verified to the extent the timescale permits, and that the limits of that verification should be transparent to the reader \u2014 is not different in kind from the one that governed print. To be sure, the architecture of the attention economy, by rewarding the emotive and the polarising disproportionately, introduces an incentive whose misalignment with the duty to inform is, on the available evidence, more acute than anything the advertising model of the twentieth century produced. The honest position, then, is that the digital era has not invented new ethics so much as it has stress-tested the old ones \u2014 and that the newsroom whose code survives that test is the one whose commitment to accuracy, fairness and minimisation of harm is robust enough to hold even when the metrics whisper that a less scrupulous approach would, in the short term, pay.* Deontological terms: *accuracy*, *fairness*, *minimisation of harm*, *duty to inform*, *verified*, *transparent*. Concession connectors: *granted*, *that said*, *to be sure*.
