# Unidad 31 C1: modalidad y discurso profesional, carreras y ambición laboral Hablar de carrera profesional es, casi siempre, hablar de obligación, expectativa y elección: lo que *debes* hacer, lo que *se supone* que harás, lo que *conviene* evitar. El inglés C1 distingue estos matices con un repertorio de **modales** y **semi-modales** que ningún otro nivel maneja con la misma precisión. Comparemos tres versiones sobre la misma situación: - *You should update your CV and you must go to the interview.* - *You really ought to revise your CV before sending it, and you'll have to attend the interview in person.* - *Given the seniority of the role, you are expected to tailor your CV to each application; moreover, you would be well advised to prepare competency-based answers, since candidates are supposed to evidence leadership rather than merely claim it.* La primera usa modales básicos; la segunda ya introduce *ought to* y *have to* con sus matices; la tercera despliega el aparato completo: expectativa (*are expected to*), recomendación tentativa (*would be well advised to*), presión social (*are supposed to*), un conector formal (*moreover*) y un registro profesional denso. La Unidad 31 C1 desarrolla estos recursos en el contexto de **careers and career ambition**: *career path, promotion, appraise, relocate, headhunt, succession planning, plateau, upskill, pipeline, remuneration* y *benchmark*. El tema encaja de forma natural porque el discurso laboral gira en torno a lo que un profesional *debe*, *puede* y *conviene* hacer: cumplir criterios, demostrar competencias, gestionar expectativas. Dominar la modalidad es, en este registro, tan decisivo como el léxico sectorial. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 31 C1](/curso-c1/unit-31)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 30 C1: patrimonio y preservación](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-30-patrimonio-preservacion)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 32 C1: negocios y tendencias](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-32-negocios-tendencias)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. La modalidad: por qué importa en el discurso profesional La **modalidad** es la gramática de la obligación, el permiso, la posibilidad y la recomendación. En el mundo laboral, donde las jerarquías, las normas y las expectativas estructuran cada interacción, la modalidad es el motor del matiz: decir *you must* no es lo mismo que *you should*, ni *you are supposed to* que *you are expected to*. El C1 domina no solo los modales canónicos, sino los **semi-modales** y las **construcciones de expectativa** que calibran la fuente y la fuerza de la presión. ### 2. Must y have to: obligación interna vs. externa - **Must** expresa obligación que proviene del hablante o de una necesidad interna: *I must update my CV this weekend.* También inferencia fuerte: *She must be the new hire — I saw her badge.* - **Have to** expresa obligación externa, regla o circunstancia: *I have to submit the application by Friday.* Es la forma de pasado (*had to*) y futuro léxico (*will have to*), pues *must* carece de ellas. En registro profesional, *must* suena autoritario y se reserva para instrucciones directas (*All candidates must arrive ten minutes early*); *have to* es más neutro y ubícuo (*You'll have to complete a technical assessment*). ### 3. Should y ought to: recomendación y consejo moral - **Should** es la recomendación neutra y ubícua: *You should tailor your CV to each role.* - **Ought to** añade un tono moral o de obligación ideal: *You ought to inform your referee before naming them.* Es más formal y menos frecuente en habla, pero aparece en registro escrito y consejo serio. Ambos admiten perfective con *have*: *You should have / ought to have prepared more for that interview* (reproche sobre el pasado). ### 4. Need to y don't need to: necesidad objetiva - **Need to** señala necesidad objetiva, no obligación moral: *You need to demonstrate quantifiable impact.* - **Don't need to / needn't** indica ausencia de necesidad: *You needn't list every short course you've ever taken.* - *Needn't have* + participio: hiciste algo que no era necesario — *You needn't have worried; the panel was friendly.* ### 5. Be supposed to y be to: expectativa e instrucción - **Be supposed to** marca expectativa social, regla o norma percibida, a menudo incumplida: *Candidates are supposed to dress formally, but some don't.* En pasado: *I was supposed to hear back by Tuesday* (y no pasó). - **Be to** marca instrucción oficial, plan o arreglo: *The panel is to convene at noon.* En pasado narrativo (*was/were to*): *She was later to become VP of Sales.* La diferencia clave: *be supposed to* es expectativa percibida (que puede quebrarse); *be to* es directriz acordada (más formal y vinculante). ### 6. Be expected to y be required to: presión institucional - **Be expected to** señala lo que el entorno profesional presupone: *Senior managers are expected to mentor junior staff.* - **Be required to** es más fuerte: obligación vinculante, casi reglamentaria: *Applicants are required to provide three references.* Estas construcciones, típicas de descripciones de puesto y políticas de empresa, son la firma del registro profesional moderno y deben manejarse con soltura en C1. ### 7. Would y could en el discurso tentativo - **Would** suaviza consejo y oferta: *I would suggest highlighting your metrics.* *I would be happy to relocate.* - **Could** abre posibilidades sin comprometer: *You could frame that gap as a sabbatical.* - **Would have / could have** evalúan el pasado: *You could have negotiated a higher starting salary.* El discurso profesional recurrió abundantemente a estas formas tentativas para no sonar dogmáticos en feedback, coaching y entrevistas. ### 8. Modales en pasado y reproche - **Should have / ought to have + participio:** reproche o arrepentimiento — *I should have asked about the promotion criteria earlier.* - **Could have + participio:** posibilidad no realizada — *She could have applied for the VP role.* - **Needn't have + participio:** acción innecesaria realizada — *I needn't have prepared slides; they only wanted a conversation.* - **Was/were supposed to + infinitivo:** expectativa incumplida — *The decision was supposed to be communicated last week.* ### 9. Vocabulario de carreras y ambición - **Career path** — trayectoria profesional. - **Promotion / be promoted** — ascenso / ascender. - **Appraise / appraisal** — evaluar / evaluación de desempeño. - **Relocate / relocation** — reubicarse / reubicación. - **Headhunt / headhunter** — cazar talentos / cazatalentos. - **Succession planning** — planificación de sucesión. - **Plateau / career plateau** — estancamiento profesional. - **Upskill / reskill** — mejorar competencias / reciclar profesionalmente. - **Pipeline (talent pipeline)** — canal de talentos. - **Remuneration / compensation** — remuneración. - **Benchmark** — punto de referencia, comparar con un estándar. - **Competency** — competencia (habilidad demostrable). - **KPI** — indicador clave de desempeño. - **Probation (period)** — periodo de prueba. - **Notice (period) / serve notice** — preaviso / dar preaviso. ### 10. Colocaciones profesionales - *climb the ladder* — ascender en la jerarquía. - *make a lateral move* — cambiar de puesto sin ascender. - *step down / step aside* — dimitir, dejar el puesto. - *hand in one's notice* — entregar la renuncia. - *land a job / land a role* — conseguir un puesto. - *negotiate a salary / a package* — negociar salario / paquete. - *demonstrate impact* — demostrar impacto. - *evidence leadership* — evidenciar liderazgo. - *fill a vacancy* — cubrir una vacante. - *meet the criteria* — cumplir los criterios. ### 11. Errores frecuentes con modales y registro laboral - **Confundir must y have to en pasado:** *I must submit it yesterday* → *I **had to** submit it yesterday.* - **Usar to de más con modales:** *You should to update your CV* → *You should update.* - **Confundir be supposed to con be to:** *The offer is supposed to be signed by both parties* (expectativa) vs *The offer is to be signed by both parties* (instrucción vinculante). - **Sobrecargar con modales:** *You should could must prepare* → un modal por cláusula. - **Usar ought to en habla muy informal:** suena a sermón; en feedback escrito es adecuado. - **Olvidar el perfecto modal:** *I should prepare more* (presente) vs *I should have prepared more* (reproche pasado). ### 12. Registro: el perfil de CV Un perfil de CV en C1 omite el pronombre sujeto, usa verbos de acción orientados a logros y cuantifica resultados: > *Results-driven product manager with eight years' experience scaling SaaS platforms across three markets. Spearheaded a cross-functional initiative that lifted retention by 23% and streamlined onboarding, cutting time-to-value by six weeks. Adept at aligning product strategy with commercial goals; proven track record of mentoring high-potential teams.* Nótese: sin *I*, nominalizaciones (*onboarding, time-to-value*), verbos fuertes (*spearheaded, streamlined, lifted*), resultados medidos (*23%, six weeks*). Es el patrón que el C1 debe reproducir. ### 13. Registro: el lenguaje de entrevista - **Competency-based questions:** *Tell me about a time when you led a team through ambiguity.* → Respuesta con método STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result). - **Hypotheticals:** *How would you approach a stakeholder who resists change?* → *I would first seek to understand their concerns, then...* - **Strengths/weaknesses:** *My strength is building consensus; an area I'm actively developing is delegating earlier in the project lifecycle.* - **Closing questions del candidato:** *What does success look like in this role in the first year?* ### 14. Diferencias de registro: CV, carta, entrevista - **CV:** registro formal escrito, sin pronombre, verbos de acción, cuantificación. - **Cover letter:** registro formal escrito con pronombre (*I am writing to...*), cohesión narrativa, registro cálido pero profesional. - **Entrevista:** registro oral formal pero conversacional, modales tentativos (*I would, I tend to*), respuestas estructuradas (STAR). El C1 debe moverse entre los tres sin mezclar sus convenciones: el CV no lleva *I*, la carta sí, y la entrevista combina formalidad con oralidad. ### 15. Síntesis: modular el discurso profesional El discurso profesional combina tres capas: **modales canónicos** (*must, should, can, could*) para obligación y posibilidad; **semi-modales y construcciones de expectativa** (*have to, need to, be supposed to, be to, be expected to, be required to*) para graduar la fuente y fuerza de la presión; y **modales tentativos** (*would, could, would be well advised to*) para suavizar consejo y feedback. A esto se suman los **perfectos modales** (*should have, could have, needn't have*) para evaluar el pasado, y un **léxico profesional** preciso que permite hablar de carreras con la autoridad y el matiz que el nivel exige. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 — Must vs. have to Elige la forma correcta y justifica brevemente. 1. I really ______ update my CV this weekend. (obligación interna del hablante) 2. You ______ submit the application by Friday. (regla externa) 3. Last year I ______ relocate for the role. (pasado) 4. All candidates ______ arrive ten minutes early. (instrucción directa)
Ver solución 1. **must** (obligación interna del hablante). 2. **have to** (obligación externa, plazo impuesto). 3. **had to** (pasado; must no tiene forma de pasado léxico). 4. **must** (instrucción directa y autoritaria, típica de normas).
### Ejercicio 2 — Should vs. ought to Reescribe con *should* o *ought to* según el tono. 1. It's a good idea to tailor your CV to each role. (recomendación neutra) 2. You have a moral duty to inform your referee before naming them. (tono moral)
Ver solución 1. You **should** tailor your CV to each role. 2. You **ought to** inform your referee before naming them.
### Ejercicio 3 — Be supposed to vs. be to Elige la construcción adecuada (expectativa percibida vs. instrucción acordada). 1. Candidates ______ dress formally, but some show up in jeans. (expectativa que se incumple) 2. The panel ______ convene at noon sharp. (instrucción oficial) 3. I ______ hear back by Tuesday, but nobody called. (expectativa incumplida)
Ver solución 1. Candidates **are supposed to** dress formally, but some show up in jeans. 2. The panel **is to** convene at noon sharp. 3. I **was supposed to** hear back by Tuesday, but nobody called.
### Ejercicio 4 — Be expected to / be required to Completa con la forma más fuerte (required) o de expectativa (expected). 1. Senior managers ______ mentor junior staff. (presupuesto por el entorno) 2. Applicants ______ provide three references. (obligación vinculante, reglamento)
Ver solución 1. Senior managers **are expected to** mentor junior staff. (presupuesto del entorno) 2. Applicants **are required to** provide three references. (obligación vinculante)
### Ejercicio 5 — Would y could (discurso tentativo) Reescribe suavizando con *would* o *could*. 1. I suggest highlighting your metrics. → I ______ suggest... 2. You can frame that gap as a sabbatical. → You ______ frame... 3. I am happy to relocate. → I ______ be happy to relocate.
Ver solución 1. I **would** suggest highlighting your metrics. 2. You **could** frame that gap as a sabbatical. 3. I **would** be happy to relocate.
### Ejercicio 6 — Perfectos modales (reproche y posibilidad) Reescribe con el perfecto modal adecuado. 1. It was a mistake not to ask about the promotion criteria earlier. → I ______ ... 2. It was possible for her to apply for the VP role (but she didn't). → She ______ ... 3. I prepared slides, but they only wanted a conversation (unnecessary). → I ______ ...
Ver solución 1. I **should have asked** about the promotion criteria earlier. 2. She **could have applied** for the VP role. 3. I **needn't have prepared** slides; they only wanted a conversation.
### Ejercicio 7 — Corrige los errores Cada frase tiene un error. Corrígelo. 1. You should to update your CV. 2. I must submit it yesterday. 3. You should could must prepare. 4. The offer is to be signed, but they haven't yet. (contexto: expectativa que se incumple) 5. You ought to updating your LinkedIn profile.
Ver solución 1. You should **update** your CV. (sin *to* tras modal) 2. I **had to** submit it yesterday. (pasado) 3. Un solo modal por cláusula: *You should prepare.* (o *You must prepare.*) 4. The offer **is supposed to be** signed, but they haven't yet. (expectativa incumplida, no instrucción) 5. You ought to **update** your LinkedIn profile. (infinitivo sin *-ing*)
### Ejercicio 8 — Transformación (CAE-style) Reescribe empezando con las palabras dadas. 1. "It would be a good idea to prepare competency-based answers." → *You would be well advised...* 2. "They expect senior managers to mentor juniors." → *Senior managers are expected...* 3. "I regret not negotiating a higher salary." → *I should have...* 4. "It wasn't necessary to worry; the panel was friendly." → *I needn't have...*
Ver solución 1. You would be well advised **to prepare competency-based answers**. 2. Senior managers are expected **to mentor juniors**. 3. I should have **negotiated a higher salary**. 4. I needn't have **worried; the panel was friendly**.
### Ejercicio 9 — Vocabulario de carreras Relaciona cada término con su definición. 1. Plateau a. Canales de candidatos potenciales. 2. Upskill b. Estancamiento profesional. 3. Pipeline c. Mejorar competencias. 4. Headhunt d. Cazar talentos activamente. 5. Appraisal e. Evaluación de desempeño.
Ver solución 1-b, 2-c, 3-a, 4-d, 5-e.
### Ejercicio 10 — Colocaciones profesionales Completa con el verbo adecuado (climb / land / hand in / negotiate / demonstrate). 1. ______ the ladder to reach senior management. 2. ______ a role at a leading firm. 3. ______ one's notice and leave on good terms. 4. ______ a competitive salary package. 5. ______ quantifiable impact in your CV.
Ver solución 1. **Climb** the ladder to reach senior management. 2. **Land** a role at a leading firm. 3. **Hand in** one's notice and leave on good terms. 4. **Negotiate** a competitive salary package. 5. **Demonstrate** quantifiable impact in your CV.
### Ejercicio 11 — Perfil de CV Mejora este perfil débil con registro C1 (sin pronombre, verbos de acción, cuantificación). > *I am a marketing person. I have done marketing for a while. I like working with teams and I am good at social media.*
Ver solución Modelo: *Data-driven marketing manager with seven years' experience scaling B2B SaaS brands across EMEA. Orchestrated a multi-channel campaign that grew qualified leads by 41% and reduced cost-per-acquisition by 18%. Skilled at aligning brand strategy with revenue goals; proven track record of building and mentoring high-performing teams.*
### Ejercicio 12 — Lenguaje de entrevista (STAR) Estructura una respuesta STAR a: *"Tell me about a time when you led a team through ambiguity."*
Ver solución Modelo: **(Situation)** *In my previous role, a key product launch was thrown into uncertainty when our lead engineer left three weeks before release.* **(Task)** *I needed to stabilise the team and keep the launch on track.* **(Action)** *I redistributed responsibilities transparently, introduced daily stand-ups to surface blockers, and negotiated a two-week extension with stakeholders by presenting a revised risk plan.* **(Result)** *We launched on the new date with zero critical bugs, and team morale, measured in our pulse survey, recovered to pre-departure levels within a month.*
### Ejercicio 13 — Reading Lee el extracto y responde. > *The role requires a candidate who is expected to evidence leadership at every level. Applicants must demonstrate quantifiable impact, and they are supposed to have managed cross-functional teams of at least eight. You would be well advised to frame any career gap as intentional development; moreover, candidates need to provide three references, one of which ought to be a former direct report.* 1. Which three obligations/expectations are listed? 2. Which modal signals the strongest obligation? Which signals a recommendation? 3. Rewrite "they are supposed to have managed cross-functional teams" with *be expected to*.
Ver solución 1. Evidence leadership, demonstrate quantifiable impact, have managed cross-functional teams of 8+, provide three references (one a former direct report). 2. Strongest: **must** (demonstrate). Recommendation: **would be well advised to** / **ought to**. 3. They **are expected to have managed** cross-functional teams.
### Ejercicio 14 — Listening (paráfrasis) Parafrasea esta declaración del reclutador en registro C1. > "You've gotta send the CV by Friday, and you should really prep for the interview. We expect you to know the company."
Ver solución Modelo: *Applications must be submitted by Friday, and you would be well advised to prepare thoroughly for the interview. Candidates are expected to demonstrate a solid understanding of the company.*
### Ejercicio 15 — Writing Escribe una cover letter (80–100 palabras) para un puesto de *Senior Project Manager*. Usa al menos: un modal de obligación, una construcción de expectativa, un modal tentativo y un conector formal.
Ver solución Modelo: *Dear Ms. Alvarez, I am writing to express my interest in the Senior Project Manager position. Having led cross-functional teams of up to twelve across three markets, I am confident I can deliver the impact you require. Senior project managers are expected to align delivery with commercial strategy, and I have consistently done so, most recently cutting time-to-market by eight weeks. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my approach to stakeholder management could benefit your roadmap; moreover, I would be happy to provide references from former direct reports. Yours sincerely, ...* (94 palabras)
### Ejercicio 16 — Speaking (monólogo) Prepara un monólogo de 2 minutos en el que expliques tu trayectoria profesional y ambición, usando modales y registro profesional.
Ver solución Modelo de inicio: *I began my career in operations, where I quickly realised that I had to develop a stronger commercial lens to progress. Over the next five years I upskilled through a part-time MBA while leading two regional rollouts; I would say that experience taught me to evidence impact rather than effort alone. I am expected, in my current role, to mentor juniors, and I've come to see that as the most rewarding part of the job. Looking ahead, I would like to step into a director-level position within three years...*
### Ejercicio 17 — Registro: CV, carta o entrevista Clasifica cada extracto. 1. *Results-driven analyst with six years' experience in fintech.* 2. *I am writing to apply for the Data Lead role.* 3. *I would say my biggest strength is building consensus across silos.*
Ver solución 1. **CV** (sin pronombre, verbos de acción implícitos). 2. **Cover letter** (pronombre *I*, registro formal escrito). 3. **Entrevista** (oral, modal tentativo *I would say*).
### Ejercicio 18 — Consolidación Completa el párrafo con una palabra por hueco. > *Senior managers are (1)______ to mentor junior staff, and applicants (2)______ demonstrate quantifiable impact. You (3)______ be well advised to tailor your CV; (4)______, you (5)______ to provide three references. Last year I (6)______ to relocate for the role.*
Ver solución 1. **expected** (be expected to) 2. **must** (obligación fuerte) 3. **would** (would be well advised to) 4. **moreover** (conector formal) 5. **need** (need to) 6. **had** (had to, pasado)
### Ejercicio 19 — Reescribe el párrafo con discurso profesional Eleva el registro del párrafo coloquial con modales, construcciones de expectativa y léxico profesional. > *You've gotta fix your CV and you should go to the interview. They expect you to know the company and you have to show you're a leader. I think you could ask for more money.*
Ver solución Modelo: *You must revise your CV before submitting it, and you would be well advised to prepare thoroughly for the interview. Candidates are expected to demonstrate a deep understanding of the company, and you are required to evidence leadership with quantifiable results. Furthermore, you could consider negotiating a more competitive remuneration package, particularly given the seniority of the role.*
## Resumen de la unidad - La **modalidad** es la gramática de la obligación, el permiso, la posibilidad y la recomendación; en el discurso profesional calibra la fuente y la fuerza de la presión. - **Must** (obligación interna, inferencia) frente a **have to** (obligación externa, regla; única forma de pasado y futuro léxico); **should** (recomendación neutra) frente a **ought to** (tono moral); **need to** (necesidad objetiva) y **needn't / don't need to** (ausencia de necesidad). - Las **construcciones de expectativa** gradúan la presión institucional: *be supposed to* (expectativa percibida, a menudo incumplida), *be to* (instrucción acordada), *be expected to* (presupuesto del entorno), *be required to* (obligación vinculante). - Los **modales tentativos** (*would, could, would be well advised to*) suavizan consejo y feedback; los **perfectos modales** (*should have, could have, needn't have, was supposed to*) evalúan el pasado con reproche, posibilidad o innecesariedad. - El **vocabulario de carreras** (*career path, promotion, appraise, relocate, headhunt, succession planning, plateau, upskill, pipeline, remuneration, benchmark, competency, KPI, probation, notice*) y sus colocaciones (*climb the ladder, make a lateral move, hand in one's notice, land a role, negotiate a package, demonstrate impact, evidence leadership*) permiten hablar de trayectorias y ambición con la autoridad y el matiz que el C1 exige, tanto en CV (sin pronombre, verbos de acción, cuantificación), en cover letter (con pronombre, cohesión narrativa) como en entrevista (oral, modales tentativos, método STAR).

title: Ejercicios de Informes y Comparativos en Inglés C1
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía C1 sobre informes de negocios y comparativos avanzados aplicados a tendencias de mercado, con vocabulario, teoría y ejercicios resueltos.
description: Aprende a redactar informes de negocios en inglés C1 con comparativos avanzados (far/considerably/marginally + comparativo, the more... the more...
alt: Informes y comparativos avanzados aplicados a negocios y tendencias en inglés C1
keywords: Ejercicios de Informes y Comparativos en Inglés C1
comparativos avanzados inglés the more the more
the more the more business reports
cómo redactar un informe formal C1

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se estructura un informe de negocios en inglés C1?
faqs.answer: Con encabezado (To/From/Date/Subject), introducción con propósito, secciones con subencabezados, cuerpo con datos y comparativos, conclusiones numeradas y recomendaciones accionables. El registro es formal, impersonal, con pasiva, nominalización y comparativos para contrastar periodos, mercados o productos.

faqs.question: ¿Qué modificadores refuerzan y atenúan el comparativo en C1?
faqs.answer: Intensificadores: far, considerably, substantially, much, a lot, even, still (far more profitable). Atenuadores: marginally, slightly, narrowly, only modestly (marginally higher). La elección calibra la magnitud de la diferencia que el informe comunica.

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo se usa la estructura the more... the more... en informes?
faqs.answer: Para expresar proporcionalidad entre dos variables: The more we automate, the faster we scale. Cada cláusula empieza con the + comparativo y mantiene el orden sujeto-verbo; es ideal para mostrar correlaciones en datos de mercado.

faqs.question: ¿La Unidad 32 incluye ejercicios resueltos?
faqs.answer: Sí. Incluye práctica de comparativos y modificadores, the more... the more..., conectores de informe, vocabulario de tendencias, reading, listening, writing de informe y speaking con soluciones y modelos.

content:
# Unidad 32 C1: informes y comparativos, negocios y tendencias El informe de negocios es el género donde los datos se vuelven argumento: una serie de cifras se transforma en una conclusión accionable porque el texto las compara, las matiza y las encadena. Para hacerlo con precisión, el inglés C1 refina los **comparativos** (con modificadores y la estructura *the more... the more...*) y despliega el **registro formal del informe**. Comparemos tres versiones sobre el mismo dato: - *Sales went up. Costs went up too. We did better than last year.* - *Sales grew considerably faster than costs, and margins improved markedly on the previous year.* - *The more aggressively we expanded into emerging markets, the more our customer acquisition costs fell, so that operating margins outperformed the prior year by a substantial margin; by contrast, domestic growth remained only marginally positive.* La primera yuxtapone; la segunda compara con modificador; la tercera combina *the more... the more...*, un comparativo reforzado (*substantial margin*) y un contraste formal (*by contrast*, *only marginally*). La Unidad 32 C1 desarrolla estos recursos en el contexto de **business and market trends**: *revenue, margin, forecast, downturn, scale, disrupt, benchmark, leverage, streamlined, volatile, resilient* y *stagnant*. El tema encaja de forma natural porque los informes de negocios son comparativos por naturaleza: contrastan trimestres, mercados, productos y escenarios. Aprender a matizar la magnitud de una diferencia y a estructurar un informe con el registro justo es, en este género, tan importante como el análisis numérico. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 32 C1](/curso-c1/unit-32)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 31 C1: carreras y ambición laboral](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-31-carreras-ambicion-laboral)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 33 C1: emprendimiento e innovación](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-33-emprendimiento-innovacion)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. El informe de negocios: por qué importan los comparativos Un informe no solo presenta datos; **los interpreta** comparándolos. Decir *revenue increased* es insuficiente; el lector necesita saber *cuánto más*, *respecto a qué* y *con qué matiz*. Los comparativos refinados y sus modificadores son la herramienta que convierte una cifra suelta en una conclusión argumentada. Sin ellos, el informe se queda en *sales went up*; con ellos, llega a *sales grew considerably faster than costs, lifting margins by a substantial margin*. ### 2. Comparativos y sus modificadores de gradación El comparativo básico se forma con *-er* o *more* + adjetivo. En C1, lo que distingue el nivel es el uso de **modificadores** que cuantifican la diferencia: - **Intensificadores:** *far, considerably, substantially, much, a lot, even, still* — *far more profitable, considerably higher, even faster to scale*. - **Atenuadores:** *marginally, slightly, narrowly, only modestly, a little* — *marginally higher, slightly less volatile, only modestly positive*. La elección calibra la magnitud: *marginally* sugiere una diferencia apenas perceptible; *substantially*, una diferencia notable y relevante para la decisión. ### 3. Comparativos con sustantivos y as...as - **Sustantivos contables e incontables:** *more/less/fewer ... than* — *more revenue than projected, fewer churn events than Q1, less volatility than expected.* - **as...as reforzado:** *not nearly as, nothing like as, almost as, twice as* — *almost as resilient as the market leader, not nearly as volatile as last quarter, twice as efficient as the legacy system.* ### 4. La estructura the more... the more... La estructura **the + comparativo ... the + comparativo** expresa proporcionalidad entre dos variables, manteniendo el orden sujeto-verbo en cada cláusula: - *The more we automate, the faster we scale.* - *The earlier we enter, the cheaper the acquisition cost.* - *The less we invest in R&D, the harder it becomes to stay competitive.* Es ideal para mostrar correlaciones en datos de mercado y es una de las construcciones más características del informe analítico en C1. ### 5. Superlativos reforzados - *by far the most profitable segment.* - *one of the fastest-growing markets in the region.* - *the single largest contributor to revenue.* - *among the least volatile categories.* El superlativo reforzado sitúa un dato en el extremo de la distribución y es útil para destacar el hallazgo clave del informe. ### 6. Contraste en informes: whereas, by contrast, conversely - **Subordinado:** *whereas, while, whilst* (con cláusula con verbo) — *Domestic growth stagnated, whereas international revenue surged.* - **Adverbial independiente:** *by contrast, in contrast, conversely* (punto y coma + cláusula nueva) — *Domestic growth stagnated; by contrast, international revenue surged.* - **Argumentativo:** *on the other hand, however, nevertheless* — *The forecast is optimistic; however, headwinds remain.* ### 7. Concesivas en análisis de negocio - **Con cláusula:** *although, even though* — *Although the market contracted, we gained share.* - **Con sustantivo o -ing:** *despite, in spite of* — *Despite the downturn, margins held. In spite of rising costs, we remained profitable.* Las concesivas introducen el obstáculo que no impidió el resultado, un matiz esencial en el análisis de negocio donde rara vez todo es lineal. ### 8. Estructura del informe formal Un informe C1 típico sigue esta arquitectura: 1. **Encabezado:** *To: / From: / Date: / Subject:* 2. **Introducción:** propósito y alcance — *This report examines Q3 performance across three regions and recommends...* 3. **Secciones con subencabezados:** *Findings, Analysis, Comparison, Risks.* 4. **Cuerpo:** datos con comparativos y conectores. 5. **Conclusiones:** numeradas — *1. Margins improved considerably...* 6. **Recomendaciones:** accionables — *It is recommended that...* El registro es **formal, impersonal y denso**: pasiva (*it is projected that*), nominalización (*the contraction of the market*), y comparativos para interpretar datos. ### 9. Conectores de causa y consecuencia en informes - **Causa:** *owing to, due to, on account of, given* (con sustantivo) — *Owing to supply-chain disruptions, revenue fell.* - **Consecuencia:** *consequently, accordingly, therefore, as a result, hence* — *Costs rose; consequently, margins narrowed.* - **Propósito:** *so as to, in order to, with a view to* — *We diversified suppliers in order to reduce single-point risk.* ### 10. Vocabulario de negocios y tendencias - **Revenue** — ingresos. - **Margin / profit margin** — margen. - **Forecast** — pronóstico, previsión. - **Downturn** — recesión, contracción. - **Scale / scalable** — escalar / escalable. - **Disrupt / disruption** — disruptir / disrupción. - **Benchmark** — punto de referencia, comparar. - **Leverage** — aprovechar, palanquear. - **Streamlined** — optimizado, simplificado. - **Volatile** — volátil. - **Resilient** — resiliente, resistente. - **Stagnant** — estancado. - **Headwind / tailwind** — viento en contra / a favor (factor adverso / favorable). - **Churn (rate)** — tasa de cancelación o abandono. - **YoY / QoQ** — interanual / trimestral. ### 11. Colocaciones de informe - *revenue surged / climbed / edged up* — los ingresos se dispararon / subieron / rozaron la subida. - *margins narrowed / widened* — los márgenes se estrecharon / ensancharon. - *gain / lose market share* — ganar / perder cuota. - *outperform / underperform the market* — superar / quedarse por debajo del mercado. - *bear the brunt* — soportar lo peor. - *offset the decline* — compensar la caída. - *weather the downturn* — resistir la recesión. - *rebound from a low* — rebotar desde un mínimo. - *flat year-on-year* — plano interanual. - *a fraction of the cost* — una fracción del coste. ### 12. Errores frecuentes con comparativos en informes - **Olvidar el modificador graduado:** *Sales are more than last year* → *Sales are **considerably higher** than last year.* - **Confundir fewer y less:** *less customers* → *fewer customers* (contable); *less revenue* (incontable) es correcto. - **Mal formar the more... the more...:** *More we automate, faster we scale* → *The more we automate, the faster we scale.* - **Confundir whereas y by contrast:** *whereas* lleva cláusula con verbo; *by contrast* abre cláusula nueva tras punto y coma. - **Mezclar registro:** *Sales are like way up* → *Sales rose substantially.* - **Sobrecargar de modificadores:** *far considerably much higher* → uno por comparativo. ### 13. Registro: párrafo de informe modelo > *Q3 revenue grew 14% year-on-year, considerably outpacing the sector average of 6%. The more aggressively we expanded into emerging markets, the more our blended acquisition cost fell, so that operating margins widened by 230 basis points. Domestic growth, by contrast, remained only marginally positive, stagnant amid pricing pressure. Although headwinds persist in supply, international momentum is expected to offset the domestic shortfall; consequently, it is recommended that investment be reallocated toward high-growth territories.* Nótese: comparativo con modificador (*considerably outpacing*), *the more... the more...*, contraste formal (*by contrast*), concesiva (*although*), conector de consecuencia (*consequently*) y recomendación con subjuntivo mandativo (*be reallocated*). ### 14. Diferencias de registro: informe, memo, email - **Informe:** formal, impersonal, estructurado con secciones, comparativos densos, pasiva y nominalización. - **Memo:** formal-corto, propósito único, más directo, menos seccionado. - **Email profesional:** semiformal, conciso, puede usar primera persona, registro cálido pero profesional. El C1 debe adaptar el registro al género: el informe admite densidad analítica; el email exige concisión y claridad inmediata. ### 15. Síntesis: comparar para concluir El informe de negocios combina cuatro motores: **comparativos con modificadores** (graduar la diferencia), **the more... the more...** (proporcionalidad), **contraste formal** (*whereas, by contrast, conversely, however*) y **concesivas** (*although, despite*). A esto se suman conectores de causa y consecuencia (*owing to, consequently*), la **estructura canónica del informe** (encabezado, intro, secciones, conclusiones, recomendaciones) y un **léxico de tendencias** preciso que permite convertir datos en argumento accionable. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 — Modificadores del comparativo Añade un intensificador o atenuador adecuado. 1. Sales grew ______ faster than costs. (intenso) 2. Margins were ______ higher than last quarter. (apenas perceptible) 3. The new system is ______ more efficient than the legacy one. (notable) 4. Domestic growth was ______ positive. (muy modesto)
Ver solución 1. Sales grew **considerably / far / substantially** faster than costs. 2. Margins were **marginally / slightly** higher than last quarter. 3. The new system is **far / substantially / much** more efficient than the legacy one. 4. Domestic growth was **only marginally / slightly** positive.
### Ejercicio 2 — as...as reforzado Reescribe con una forma reforzada de *as...as*. 1. Domestic growth is not as volatile as international. (casi nada) 2. The churn rate is not as high as feared. (ni mucho menos) 3. The cloud platform is as efficient as the market leader. (el doble)
Ver solución 1. Domestic growth is **not nearly as** volatile as international. 2. The churn rate is **nothing like as** high as feared. 3. The cloud platform is **twice as** efficient as the market leader.
### Ejercicio 3 — La estructura the more... the more... Completa con *the + comparativo*. 1. ______ we automate, ______ we scale. (more / fast) 2. ______ we invest in R&D, ______ it becomes to stay competitive. (less / hard) 3. ______ we diversify suppliers, ______ our single-point risk. (more / low)
Ver solución 1. **The more** we automate, **the faster** we scale. 2. **The less** we invest in R&D, **the harder** it becomes to stay competitive. 3. **The more** we diversify suppliers, **the lower** our single-point risk.
### Ejercicio 4 — Superlativos reforzados Reescribe añadiendo refuerzo. 1. Cloud is the most profitable segment. (by far) 2. It is a fast-growing market. (one of the) 3. Enterprise is the largest contributor. (the single)
Ver solución 1. Cloud is **by far the most** profitable segment. 2. It is **one of the fastest-growing** markets in the region. 3. Enterprise is **the single largest** contributor.
### Ejercicio 5 — whereas / by contrast Reescribe usando *whereas* (cláusula) o *by contrast* (punto y coma + cláusula nueva). 1. Domestic growth stagnated. International revenue surged. 2. Costs rose. Margins widened thanks to efficiency gains.
Ver solución 1. Domestic growth stagnated, **whereas** international revenue surged. (o: Domestic growth stagnated; **by contrast**, international revenue surged.) 2. Costs rose, **whereas** margins widened thanks to efficiency gains. (o: Costs rose; **by contrast**, margins widened thanks to efficiency gains.)
### Ejercicio 6 — Concesivas (although / despite) Reescribe con *although* o *despite*. 1. The market contracted, but we gained share. → ______ the market contracted, we gained share. 2. There was a downturn, but margins held. → ______ the downturn, margins held.
Ver solución 1. **Although** the market contracted, we gained share. 2. **Despite** the downturn, margins held.
### Ejercicio 7 — Conectores de causa y consecuencia Inserta el conector adecuado (owing to / consequently / in order to / given). 1. ______ supply-chain disruptions, revenue fell. 2. Costs rose; ______, margins narrowed. 3. We diversified suppliers ______ reduce single-point risk. 4. ______ the volatility, a cautious forecast is warranted.
Ver solución 1. **Owing to** supply-chain disruptions, revenue fell. 2. Costs rose; **consequently**, margins narrowed. 3. We diversified suppliers **in order to** reduce single-point risk. 4. **Given** the volatility, a cautious forecast is warranted.
### Ejercicio 8 — Corrige los errores Cada frase tiene un error. Corrígelo. 1. Sales are more than last year. 2. We have less customers than Q1. 3. More we automate, faster we scale. 4. Sales are like way up. 5. Domestic stagnated whereas by contrast international surged.
Ver solución 1. Sales are **considerably higher** than last year. (modificador graduado) 2. We have **fewer customers** than Q1. (contable → fewer) 3. **The more** we automate, **the faster** we scale. 4. Sales **rose substantially**. (registro formal) 5. Domestic stagnated, **whereas** international surged. (un solo conector: whereas o by contrast, no ambos)
### Ejercicio 9 — Transformación (CAE-style) Reescribe empezando con las palabras dadas. 1. "International revenue grew faster than domestic." → *Domestic growth was...* 2. "Because of the downturn, margins narrowed." → *Owing to...* 3. "We gained share although the market contracted." → *Despite...* 4. "Investment should be reallocated to high-growth territories." → *It is recommended that...*
Ver solución 1. Domestic growth was **considerably slower than** international revenue. 2. **Owing to the downturn,** margins narrowed. 3. **Despite the contraction of the market,** we gained share. 4. **It is recommended that** investment **be reallocated** to high-growth territories.
### Ejercicio 10 — Vocabulario de tendencias Relaciona cada término con su definición. 1. Headwind a. Tasa de abandono de clientes. 2. Churn b. Factor adverso que frena el crecimiento. 3. Tailwind c. Resistente, que se recupera bien. 4. Resilient d. Factor favorable que impulsa el crecimiento.
Ver solución 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c.
### Ejercicio 11 — Colocaciones de informe Completa con el verbo adecuado (surged / narrowed / outperform / offset / weather). 1. Revenue ______ 14% year-on-year. 2. Rising costs caused margins to ______. 3. We managed to ______ the downturn without layoffs. 4. International gains ______ the domestic shortfall. 5. We continued to ______ the market benchmark.
Ver solución 1. Revenue **surged** 14% year-on-year. 2. Rising costs caused margins to **narrow**. 3. We managed to **weather** the downturn without layoffs. 4. International gains **offset** the domestic shortfall. 5. We continued to **outperform** the market benchmark.
### Ejercicio 12 — fewer vs. less Elige la forma correcta. 1. We had ______ churn events than Q1. (contable) 2. There was ______ volatility than expected. (incontable) 3. ______ customers upgraded this quarter. (contable) 4. The upgrade generated ______ revenue. (incontable)
Ver solución 1. **fewer** churn events (contable) 2. **less** volatility (incontable) 3. **fewer** customers (contable) 4. **less** revenue (incontable)
### Ejercicio 13 — Reading Lee el extracto y responde. > *Q3 revenue climbed 14% YoY, considerably outpacing the sector average of 6%. The more aggressively the firm expanded into emerging markets, the more its blended acquisition cost fell, so that operating margins widened by 230 basis points. Domestic growth, by contrast, remained only marginally positive. Although headwinds persist in supply, international momentum is expected to offset the domestic shortfall.* 1. By how much did revenue and the sector average grow? What does the comparison show? 2. What proportional relationship is described, and with what structure? 3. Identify one concesiva and one contrast connector.
Ver solución 1. Revenue climbed 14% YoY; the sector average, 6%. The comparison shows the firm outperformed the sector by a considerable margin (more than double). 2. The more aggressively it expanded into emerging markets, the more its blended acquisition cost fell. Structure: *the more... the more...* 3. Concesiva: *although headwinds persist*. Contrast: *by contrast*.
### Ejercicio 14 — Listening (paráfrasis) Parafrasea esta declaración del CFO en registro de informe. > "We made more money this quarter, way more than the market. Going abroad really helped bring costs down. Home market is basically flat though. Supply issues are still there but we'll cover the gap."
Ver solución Modelo: *Q3 revenue grew considerably faster than the sector average. International expansion materially lowered blended acquisition costs; by contrast, domestic growth remained only marginally positive. Although supply headwinds persist, international momentum is expected to offset the domestic shortfall.*
### Ejercicio 15 — Writing Escribe el cuerpo de un informe (80–100 palabras) comparando dos productos (Producto A y Producto B). Usa al menos: un comparativo con modificador, *the more... the more...*, un conector de contraste y un conector de consecuencia.
Ver solución Modelo: *Product A outperformed Product B considerably in Q3, generating 31% more revenue at a fraction of the support cost. The more aggressively we promoted Product A through targeted campaigns, the faster its adoption curve steepened, so that its margins widened by 180 basis points. Product B, by contrast, remained stagnant amid pricing pressure and rising churn. Consequently, it is recommended that marketing spend be reallocated toward Product A, and that a discontinuation review of Product B be commissioned for Q4.* (88 palabras)
### Ejercicio 16 — Speaking (monólogo) Prepara un monólogo de 2 minutos presentando los resultados trimestrales a un comité, usando comparativos y registro de informe.
Ver solución Modelo de inicio: *Turning to Q3 performance, revenue grew fourteen percent year-on-year, considerably outpacing the sector average of six percent. The more aggressively we expanded into emerging markets, the more our blended acquisition cost fell, so that operating margins widened by two hundred and thirty basis points. Domestic growth, by contrast, remained only marginally positive, stagnant amid pricing pressure. Although supply headwinds persist, international momentum is expected to offset the domestic shortfall; consequently, we recommend reallocating investment toward high-growth territories...*
### Ejercicio 17 — Registro: informe, memo o email Clasifica cada extracto. 1. *To: Board / From: CFO / Subject: Q3 Review. This report examines...* 2. *Hi team — quick note: the deck is ready for tomorrow's call.* 3. *Re: supplier policy. Please note that all new vendors must complete KYC within five business days.*
Ver solución 1. **Informe** (encabezado formal, propósito explícito, registro denso). 2. **Email profesional** (semiformal, conciso, primera persona). 3. **Memo** (formal-corto, propósito único, directriz).
### Ejercicio 18 — Consolidación Completa el párrafo con una palabra por hueco. > *Q3 revenue grew (1)______ faster than costs, and margins improved (2)______ on the previous year. The (3)______ we expanded abroad, the (4)______ our acquisition cost fell. Domestic growth, (5)______ contrast, remained only (6)______ positive.*
Ver solución 1. **considerably** (intensificador) 2. **markedly / substantially** (intensificador) 3. **more** (the more) 4. **lower / more** (the lower / the more... fell) 5. **by** (by contrast) 6. **marginally** (atenuador)
### Ejercicio 19 — Reescribe el párrafo con registro de informe Eleva el registro del párrafo coloquial con comparativos, *the more... the more...*, contraste y consecuencia. > *We did way better this quarter, like loads more than the market. Going abroad really cut costs. Home market is basically flat though. Supply is still a pain but we'll cover the gap.*
Ver solución Modelo: *Q3 revenue grew considerably faster than the sector average. The more aggressively we expanded into emerging markets, the more our blended acquisition cost fell, so that operating margins widened substantially. Domestic growth, by contrast, remained only marginally positive, stagnant amid pricing pressure. Although supply headwinds persist, international momentum is expected to offset the domestic shortfall; consequently, a cautious but optimistic forecast is warranted.*
## Resumen de la unidad - Los **comparativos con modificadores** gradúan la diferencia: intensificadores (*far, considerably, substantially, much, even, still*) y atenuadores (*marginally, slightly, narrowly, only modestly*); con sustantivos (*more/less/fewer ... than*) y *as...as* reforzado (*not nearly as, nothing like as, twice as*). - La estructura **the + comparativo ... the + comparativo** expresa proporcionalidad manteniendo el orden sujeto-verbo; los **superlativos** se refuerzan con *by far, one of the, the single*. - El **contraste** se reparte en subordinado (*whereas, while, whilst*), adverbial independiente (*by contrast, in contrast, conversely*) y argumentativo (*on the other hand, however, nevertheless*); las concesivas (*although/even though* con cláusula; *despite/in spite of* con sustantivo) añaden el matiz de obstáculo no impedidor. - Los **conectores de causa y consecuencia** (*owing to, due to, given / consequently, accordingly, therefore*) y la **estructura canónica del informe** (encabezado, introducción, secciones, conclusiones, recomendaciones) enmarcan el análisis. - El **vocabulario de tendencias** (*revenue, margin, forecast, downturn, scale, disrupt, benchmark, leverage, streamlined, volatile, resilient, stagnant, headwind, churn, YoY*) y sus colocaciones (*revenue surged, margins narrowed, gain/lose market share, outperform the market, offset the decline, weather the downturn, flat year-on-year*) permiten escribir informes que convierten datos en argumento accionable con la precisión y el registro que el C1 exige.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se estructura un pitch de emprendimiento en inglés C1?
faqs.answer: Con gancho (problema), solución, tamaño de mercado (TAM), tracción, modelo de negocio, equipo y petición (ask). El C1 eleva cada sección con condicionales de riesgo-oportunidad (should we secure funding, we will...), lenguaje persuasivo cuantificado y registro seguro pero no arrogante.

faqs.question: ¿Qué estructuras expresan riesgo y oportunidad en C1?
faqs.answer: Condicionales (if, unless, provided that, as long as, in the event that, assuming that), inversión con should (should you require further detail) y modales de proyección (we would, we could, we expect to). Combinadas, calibran la probabilidad y la contingencia del argumento de inversión.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre unless y if...not?
faqs.answer: Unless equivale a if...not pero es más formal y enfático: We will not scale unless we raise Series A = We will not scale if we do not raise Series A. Unless se prefiere en registro de pitch e informe; if...not es más neutro y coloquial.

faqs.question: ¿La Unidad 33 incluye ejercicios resueltos?
faqs.answer: Sí. Incluye práctica de condicionales y riesgo, unless/provided that, inversión con should, lenguaje persuasivo, vocabulario de startups, reading, listening, writing de pitch y speaking con soluciones y modelos.

content:
# Unidad 33 C1: pitch y riesgo-oportunidad, emprendimiento e innovación Un pitch es, en el fondo, un argumento condicional: *si* inviertes, *entonces* este futuro se realiza; *a menos que* resolvamos este cuello, el mercado queda desatendido. El inglés C1 maneja esa lógica de riesgo y oportunidad con un repertorio de **condicionales** y **conjunciones de contingencia** que ningún otro nivel despliega con la misma precisión. Comparemos tres versiones del mismo cierre de pitch: - *If you invest, we will grow. If you don't, we won't.* - *Provided we secure Series A funding, we will scale into three new markets within eighteen months; otherwise, growth will plateau.* - *Should we close this round at the proposed valuation, we would be positioned to capture a first-mover advantage in a market projected to reach twelve billion by 2030; in the event that funding falls short, however, we will pivot to a leaner model and conserve runway, so that downside risk remains bounded.* La primera usa un condicional básico; la segunda introduce *provided that* y un contraste; la tercera despliega el aparato completo: inversión con *should* (*should we close*), condicional compuesto (*we would be positioned*), proyección de mercado, contingencia formal (*in the event that*) y gestión de downside. La Unidad 33 C1 desarrolla estos recursos en el contexto de **entrepreneurship and innovation**: *startup, runway, pivot, scale, traction, bootstrapped, disrupt, Series A, valuation, runway, burn rate, MVP, go-to-market* y *moat*. El tema encaja de forma natural porque el emprendimiento es, por definición, el arte de argumentar bajo incertidumbre: el fundador debe proyectar un futuro posible, cuantificar su oportunidad y acotar su riesgo, todo en un registro que sea persuasivo sin perder credibilidad. Dominar las estructuras de riesgo-oportunidad es, en este género, tan decisivo como el modelo de negocio. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 33 C1](/curso-c1/unit-33)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 32 C1: negocios y tendencias](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-32-negocios-tendencias)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 34 C1: liderazgo y gestión](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-34-liderazgo-gestion)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. El pitch como argumento condicional Un pitch persuade mostrando que una inversión desbloquea un futuro valioso y que no invertir deja ese futuro en manos de otros. Toda su retórica es **condicional**: *if we... then we...*, *provided that...*, *unless...*. El C1 domina no solo los tres condicionales canónicos, sino las **conjunciones de contingencia** y la **inversión con should** que elevan el registro y matizan la probabilidad de cada escenario. ### 2. Los tres condicionales canónicos (repaso C1) - **Type 0 (hecho):** *If margins fall below 10%, the model breaks.* (general, real) - **Type 1 (futuro posible):** *If we close this round, we will scale into three markets.* - **Type 2 (hipotético/irreal):** *If we had more runway, we would expand faster.* (presente contrafactual) - **Type 3 (pasado irreal):** *If we had raised earlier, we would have launched by now.* (pasado contrafactual) - **Mixed:** *If we had raised earlier (pasado), we would be market leader today (presente).* ### 3. Unless: la negación condicional formal *Unless* equivale a *if...not* pero es más formal y enfático, típico del pitch y el informe: - *We will not scale **unless** we raise Series A.* (= *if we do not raise*) - *Unless we pivot, burn rate will outlast runway.* Se prefiere *unless* cuando se quiere subrayar que la condición es **necesaria**, no meramente posible. En registro coloquial, *if...not* es más neutro. ### 4. Provided that y as long as: condición suficiente - **Provided that / providing that:** formal, condición suficiente y estricta — *Provided we hit our Q4 targets, we will open the next round.* - **As long as:** más coloquial, condición suficiente pero más flexible — *As long as the team stays intact, we can ship on time.* En un pitch, *provided that* suena más serio y comprometido; *as long as*, más conversacional. ### 5. In the event that, assuming that, in case - **In the event that:** muy formal, escenario contingente — *In the event that funding falls short, we will pivot to a leaner model.* - **Assuming that:** presuposición — *Assuming the market grows at 8% CAGR, TAM reaches twelve billion by 2030.* - **In case:** precaución (no = if) — *We keep six months runway in case the round delays.* (no *in case the round delays* como condición futura, sino como precaución). ### 6. Inversión con should (formal, tipo 1) En registro formal, *if* puede invertirse con *should* + infinitivo: - *If you need further detail → **Should you need** further detail, do not hesitate to ask.* - *If we close this round → **Should we close** this round, we would be positioned to...* Es una forma elevada que aparece en pitches escritos, term sheets y cartas a inversores. El C1 debe reconocerla y usarla con sobriedad. ### 7. Inversión con were (tipo 2 formal) y had (tipo 3 formal) - **Were + sujeto + infinitivo (tipo 2):** *Were we to raise an additional five million, we would accelerate the roadmap.* (= *If we were to raise...*) - **Had + sujeto + participio (tipo 3):** *Had we launched six months earlier, we would have captured the segment.* (= *If we had launched...*) Estas inversiones densifican el registro y son la firma del pitch y el informe avanzados. ### 8. Modales de proyección: would, could, expect to - **Would:** proyección condicionada — *We would reach profitability by Q3 2027.* - **Could:** posibilidad abierta — *We could expand into Latin America within twelve months.* - **Expect to / anticipate:** proyección con compromiso — *We expect to hit $4M ARR by year-end.* - **Projected to / forecast to:** proyección de terceros — *The market is projected to reach $12B by 2030.* El arte del C1 está en calibrar la fuerza: *will* (compromiso fuerte), *expect to* (compromiso razonable), *would/could* (condicionado), *projected to* (atribuido a fuentes). ### 9. Lenguaje persuasivo cuantificado El pitch persuade con **cifras precisas**, no con adjetivos vagos: - *un 87% de los clientes renovaron* (no *la mayoría*). - *redujo el tiempo de onboarding a seis semanas* (no *mucho más rápido*). - *TAM de 12.000 millones a un CAGR del 8%* (no *mercado enorme*). - *burn rate de 180K al mes con 14 meses de runway* (no *dinero suficiente*). La cuantificación es la marca del pitch creíble; los adjetivos sin número suenan a humo. ### 10. Vocabulario de emprendimiento e innovación - **Startup** — empresa emergente. - **Runway** — meses de caja antes de needing más capital. - **Pivot** — cambio de estrategia o producto. - **Scale / scalable** — escalar / escalable. - **Traction** — tracción (señales de adopción o ingresos). - **Bootstrapped** — autofinanciado, sin capital externo. - **Disrupt / disruption** — disruptir / disrupción. - **Series A / B / C** — rondas de financiación sucesivas. - **Valuation** — valoración (pre-money / post-money). - **Burn rate** — ritmo de gasto mensual. - **MVP (minimum viable product)** — producto mínimo viable. - **Go-to-market** — estrategia de salida al mercado. - **Moat** — foso (ventaja competitiva defendible). - **CAGR** — tasa de crecimiento anual compuesta. - **TAM / SAM / SOM** — mercado total / servible / capturable. ### 11. Colocaciones de pitch - *raise a round / raise capital* — cerrar una ronda / levantar capital. - *extend runway / conserve runway* — alargar / conservar la caja. - *gain traction / build momentum* — ganar tracción / construir impulso. - *enter a market / expand into* — entrar en un mercado. - *capture market share* — captar cuota de mercado. - *build a moat / defend a moat* — construir / defender un foso competitivo. - *ship an MVP / launch a product* — lanzar un MVP / producto. - *pivot the model* — pivotar el modelo. - *achieve product-market fit* — alcanzar product-market fit. - *reach profitability / break even* — alcanzar rentabilidad / punto muerto. ### 12. Errores frecuentes con condicionales en pitches - **Confundir unless e if:** *We will scale if we don't raise* (sentido contrario) → *We will **not** scale **unless** we raise.* - **Usar would en tipo 1:** *If we will raise, we would scale* → *If we raise, we **will** scale.* - **Mezclar tiempos en mixed conditional:** *If we had raised, we would have be leader* → *...we would **be** leader today.* - **Olvidar inversión formal:** *If you need further detail* (aceptable) vs *Should you need further detail* (más formal). - **Sobrecargar con modales:** *We would could might scale* → un modal por cláusula. - **Confundir in case e if:** *In case we raise, we will scale* → *If we raise, we will scale.* (*in case* = por si acaso, precaución). ### 13. Registro: el cierre de pitch modelo > *Should we close this round at the proposed valuation, we would be positioned to capture a first-mover advantage in a market projected to reach twelve billion by 2030. Assuming a conservative 8% CAGR and our current traction, we expect to hit four million ARR within eighteen months. In the event that funding falls short, we will pivot to a leaner model and conserve runway, so that downside risk remains bounded. Provided that we secure eight million, we will scale into three new markets and build the data moat that makes us defensible.* Nótese: inversión con *should*, condicional compuesto, proyección de mercado con CAGR, *expect to* con cifra, contingencia formal (*in the event that*), condición suficiente (*provided that*) y gestión explícita del downside. ### 14. Diferencias de registro: pitch, term sheet, deck - **Pitch oral:** registro seguro pero conversacional, condicionales tipo 1, cuantificación, *we will / we expect to*. - **Pitch escrito / deck:** registro denso, inversión con *should*, *provided that*, proyecciones con CAGR. - **Term sheet:** registro legal-formal, *shall*, *subject to*, *in the event that*, *provided that*. El C1 debe moverse entre los tres sin perder la cuantificación que da credibilidad al argumento. ### 15. Síntesis: argumentar bajo incertidumbre El pitch combina cinco motores: **condicionales canónicos** (tipos 0–3 y mixed) para proyectar escenarios; **unless** para la negación condicional formal; **provided that / as long as** para condiciones suficientes; **inversiones con should / were / had** para elevar el registro; y **modales de proyección** (*would, could, expect to, projected to*) para calibrar el compromiso. A esto se suma la **cuantificación persuasiva** (cifras precisas, no adjetivos vagos) y un **léxico de startups** que permite hablar de emprendimiento con la credibilidad y el matiz que el C1 exige. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 — Los tres condicionales canónicos Completa con la forma verbal adecuada. 1. If we ______ (close) this round, we ______ (scale) into three markets. (tipo 1) 2. If we ______ (have) more runway, we ______ (expand) faster. (tipo 2) 3. If we ______ (raise) earlier, we ______ (launch) by now. (tipo 3) 4. If we ______ (raise) earlier, we ______ (be) market leader today. (mixed)
Ver solución 1. If we **close** this round, we **will scale** into three markets. 2. If we **had** more runway, we **would expand** faster. 3. If we **had raised** earlier, we **would have launched** by now. 4. If we **had raised** earlier, we **would be** market leader today.
### Ejercicio 2 — Unless vs. if...not Reescribe con *unless*. 1. We will not scale if we do not raise Series A. 2. If we do not pivot, burn rate will outlast runway.
Ver solución 1. We will **not scale unless** we raise Series A. 2. **Unless** we pivot, burn rate will outlast runway.
### Ejercicio 3 — Provided that vs. as long as Elige la forma más formal (*provided that*) o más coloquial (*as long as*). 1. ______ we hit Q4 targets, we will open the next round. (formal, estricta) 2. ______ the team stays intact, we can ship on time. (coloquial)
Ver solución 1. **Provided that** we hit Q4 targets, we will open the next round. 2. **As long as** the team stays intact, we can ship on time.
### Ejercicio 4 — Inversión con should (formal) Reescribe invirtiendo con *should*. 1. If you need further detail, do not hesitate to ask. 2. If we close this round, we will scale into three markets.
Ver solución 1. **Should you need** further detail, do not hesitate to ask. 2. **Should we close** this round, we will scale into three markets.
### Ejercicio 5 — Inversión con were y had Reescribe invirtiendo con *were* (tipo 2) o *had* (tipo 3). 1. If we were to raise five million more, we would accelerate the roadmap. 2. If we had launched six months earlier, we would have captured the segment.
Ver solución 1. **Were we to raise** five million more, we would accelerate the roadmap. 2. **Had we launched** six months earlier, we would have captured the segment.
### Ejercicio 6 — In the event that / assuming that / in case Elige la conjunción adecuada. 1. ______ funding falls short, we will pivot to a leaner model. (contingencia formal) 2. ______ the market grows at 8% CAGR, TAM reaches 12B by 2030. (presuposición) 3. We keep six months runway ______ the round delays. (precaución)
Ver solución 1. **In the event that** funding falls short, we will pivot to a leaner model. 2. **Assuming that** the market grows at 8% CAGR, TAM reaches 12B by 2030. 3. We keep six months runway **in case** the round delays.
### Ejercicio 7 — Modales de proyección Elige el modal que mejor calibra el compromiso (will / expect to / could / projected to). 1. We ______ hit $4M ARR by year-end. (compromiso razonable) 2. We ______ expand into Latin America within twelve months. (posibilidad abierta) 3. The market ______ reach $12B by 2030. (atribuido a fuentes) 4. We ______ scale into three markets if we close this round. (compromiso fuerte, condicionado)
Ver solución 1. We **expect to** hit $4M ARR by year-end. 2. We **could** expand into Latin America within twelve months. 3. The market **is projected to** reach $12B by 2030. 4. We **will** scale into three markets if we close this round.
### Ejercicio 8 — Corrige los errores Cada frase tiene un error. Corrígelo. 1. We will scale if we don't raise. 2. If we will raise, we would scale. 3. If we had raised, we would have be leader. 4. In case we raise, we will scale. (contexto: condición futura) 5. We would could might scale.
Ver solución 1. We will **not** scale **unless** we raise. (sentido contrario corregido) 2. If we **raise**, we **will** scale. (tipo 1, no *will* en el if-clause) 3. If we had raised, we would have **been** leader. (o *we would **be** leader today*, mixed) 4. **If** we raise, we will scale. (condición futura, no *in case*) 5. Un solo modal: *We **would** scale.* (o *We **could** scale.*)
### Ejercicio 9 — Transformación (CAE-style) Reescribe empezando con las palabras dadas. 1. "If we don't pivot, we'll run out of runway." → *Unless...* 2. "If we had launched earlier, we would have won the segment." → *Had we...* 3. "If you need further detail, call me." → *Should you...* 4. "We will scale provided that we secure eight million." → *Provided that...*
Ver solución 1. **Unless** we pivot, we'll run out of runway. 2. **Had we** launched earlier, we would have won the segment. 3. **Should you** need further detail, call me. 4. **Provided that** we secure eight million, we will scale.
### Ejercicio 10 — Vocabulario de startups Relaciona cada término con su definición. 1. Runway a. Ventaja competitiva defendible. 2. Moat b. Meses de caja antes de needing más capital. 3. MVP c. Producto mínimo viable. 4. Pivot d. Cambio de estrategia o producto. 5. Burn rate e. Ritmo de gasto mensual.
Ver solución 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, 4-d, 5-e.
### Ejercicio 11 — Colocaciones de pitch Completa con el verbo adecuado (raise / extend / gain / capture / build). 1. ______ a round at a fair valuation. 2. ______ runway by cutting non-essential spend. 3. ______ traction through a pilot programme. 4. ______ market share in the enterprise segment. 5. ______ a moat around proprietary data.
Ver solución 1. **Raise** a round at a fair valuation. 2. **Extend** runway by cutting non-essential spend. 3. **Gain** traction through a pilot programme. 4. **Capture** market share in the enterprise segment. 5. **Build** a moat around proprietary data.
### Ejercicio 12 — Lenguaje persuasivo cuantificado Mejora estas afirmaciones vagas con cifras precisas (inventa datos realistas). 1. Most of our clients renew. 2. We grew a lot last year. 3. The market is huge. 4. We have enough money.
Ver solución Modelo: 1. 87% of our enterprise clients renewed in 2025. 2. We grew ARR 140% year-on-year, from $1.2M to $2.9M. 3. The TAM is projected at $12B by 2030, growing at an 8% CAGR. 4. We have 14 months of runway at a burn rate of $180K per month.
### Ejercicio 13 — Reading Lee el extracto y responde. > *Should we close this round at the proposed valuation, we would be positioned to capture a first-mover advantage in a market projected to reach twelve billion by 2030. Assuming a conservative 8% CAGR and our current traction, we expect to hit four million ARR within eighteen months. In the event that funding falls short, we will pivot to a leaner model and conserve runway.* 1. Which inverted conditional opens the paragraph, and what does it mean in plain if-form? 2. What two projections are made, and with what modals? 3. What is the downside plan, and with what conjunction?
Ver solución 1. *Should we close this round...* = *If we close this round...* (inversión con should, tipo 1 formal). 2. (a) Market projected to reach $12B by 2030 (*is projected to*); (b) we expect to hit $4M ARR within 18 months (*expect to*). 3. Pivot to a leaner model and conserve runway, introduced by *in the event that* (contingencia formal).
### Ejercicio 14 — Listening (paráfrasis) Parafrasea esta declaración del fundador en registro de pitch C1. > "If you guys give us the money, we'll get really big. The market is massive. If we don't get the cash, we'll just do less and survive."
Ver solución Modelo: *Should we close this round, we would be positioned to scale aggressively in a market projected to reach twelve billion by 2030. In the event that funding falls short, we will pivot to a leaner model and conserve runway, so that downside risk remains bounded.*
### Ejercicio 15 — Writing Escribe el cierre de un pitch (80–100 palabras). Usa al menos: una inversión con *should*, una proyección con *expect to*, una contingencia con *in the event that* y una condición suficiente con *provided that*.
Ver solución Modelo: *Should we close this round at the proposed valuation, we would be positioned to capture a first-mover advantage in a market projected to reach twelve billion by 2030. Assuming a conservative 8% CAGR and our current traction, we expect to hit four million ARR within eighteen months. In the event that funding falls short, we will pivot to a leaner model and conserve runway, so that downside risk remains bounded. Provided that we secure eight million, we will scale into three new markets and build the data moat that makes us defensible.* (90 palabras)
### Ejercicio 16 — Speaking (monólogo) Prepara un monólogo de 2 minutos presentando un pitch ante inversores, usando condicionales e inversión formal.
Ver solución Modelo de inicio: *We're solving a twelve-billion-dollar problem with a product that already shows 140% year-on-year growth. Should we close this round at the proposed valuation, we would be positioned to capture a first-mover advantage and hit four million ARR within eighteen months. Assuming an 8% CAGR, our addressable market reaches twelve billion by 2030. In the event that funding falls short, we will pivot to a leaner model and conserve runway, so that downside risk remains bounded. Provided that we secure eight million, we will scale into three new markets and build the data moat that makes us defensible...*
### Ejercicio 17 — Registro: pitch oral, deck o term sheet Clasifica cada extracto. 1. *Should you require further detail, do not hesitate to request the data room.* 2. *Look, if you back us, we'll crush it — the market is massive.* 3. *Subject to satisfactory due diligence, the investment shall close within thirty days.*
Ver solución 1. **Pitch escrito / deck** (inversión con should, registro denso). 2. **Pitch oral** (coloquial, condicional tipo 1, adjetivo vago). 3. **Term sheet** (legal-formal, *subject to*, *shall*).
### Ejercicio 18 — Consolidación Completa el párrafo con una palabra por hueco. > *(1)______ we close this round, we would be positioned to capture a first-mover advantage. (2)______ an 8% CAGR, we (3)______ to hit $4M ARR. (4)______ the event that funding falls short, we will pivot. (5)______ that we secure eight million, we will scale.*
Ver solución 1. **Should** (inversión tipo 1) 2. **Assuming** (presuposición) 3. **expect** (expect to) 4. **In** (in the event that) 5. **Provided** (provided that)
### Ejercicio 19 — Reescribe el párrafo con registro de pitch Eleva el registro del párrafo coloquial con condicionales, inversión y cuantificación. > *If you give us money we'll get huge. The market is really big. If we don't get cash we'll just survive somehow.*
Ver solución Modelo: *Should we close this round at the proposed valuation, we would be positioned to capture a first-mover advantage in a market projected to reach twelve billion by 2030. Assuming a conservative 8% CAGR, we expect to hit four million ARR within eighteen months. In the event that funding falls short, we will pivot to a leaner model and conserve runway, so that downside risk remains bounded; provided that we secure eight million, we will scale into three new markets.*
## Resumen de la unidad - Los **condicionales canónicos** (tipos 0–3 y mixed) proyectan escenarios de hecho, futuro posible, hipotético e irreal; el C1 los combina con **unless** (negación condicional formal, condición necesaria) y **provided that / as long as** (condición suficiente, estricta vs. flexible). - Las **conjunciones de contingencia** (*in the event that, assuming that, in case*) matizan la probabilidad: *in the event that* (contingencia formal), *assuming that* (presuposición), *in case* (precaución, no condición futura). - Las **inversiones con should / were / had** elevan el registro formal (*should we close, were we to raise, had we launched*) y son la firma del pitch e informe avanzados. - Los **modales de proyección** calibran el compromiso: *will* (fuerte), *expect to / anticipate* (razonable), *would / could* (condicionado), *projected to / forecast to* (atribuido a fuentes). - El **lenguaje persuasivo cuantificado** (cifras precisas, no adjetivos vagos) y el **vocabulario de startups** (*startup, runway, pivot, scale, traction, bootstrapped, disrupt, Series A, valuation, burn rate, MVP, go-to-market, moat, CAGR, TAM*) con sus colocaciones (*raise a round, extend runway, gain traction, capture market share, build a moat, ship an MVP, pivot the model, achieve product-market fit*) permiten construir pitches que argumentan bajo incertidumbre con la credibilidad y el matiz que el C1 exige.
