excerpt: Guía C1 sobre reuniones, minutas y reported speech avanzado aplicados al liderazgo y la gestión, con vocabulario, teoría y ejercicios resueltos.
description: Aprende a redactar minutas y dirigir reuniones en inglés C1 con reported speech avanzado, verbos de reporte, registro de gestión, vocabulario de liderazgo y...
alt: Reuniones, minutas y reported speech aplicados al liderazgo y la gestión en inglés C1
keywords: Ejercicios de Reuniones y Minutas en Inglés C1

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se redacta una minuta formal en inglés C1?
faqs.answer: Con encabezado (date, attendees, apologies), sección de minutos anteriores ratificados, puntos del orden del día con reported speech y verbos de reporte (noted that, agreed to, undertook to, raised the issue of), acciones con responsable y plazo, y cierre con próxima reunión. El registro es impersonal, pasivo y con reported speech en pasado.

faqs.question: ¿Qué verbos de reporte se usan en minutas C1?
faqs.answer: Noted, highlighted, emphasised, queried, proposed, agreed, undertook, committed to, recommended, flagged, reiterated. Cada uno matiza la fuerza y el tipo de intervención: queried (preguntó con duda), flagged (señaló un problema), undertook (se comprometió a actuar).

faqs.question: ¿Qué cambios sufre el discurso al reportarlo en minutas?
faqs.answer: Retroceso de tiempos (present → past, will → would, can → could), cambio de pronombres (I → he/she, we → they), cambio de deícticos (tomorrow → the following day, here → there) y uso de verbos de reporte en pasado. Las preguntas reportadas llevan orden afirmativo.

faqs.question: ¿La Unidad 34 incluye ejercicios resueltos?
faqs.answer: Sí. Incluye práctica de reported speech, verbos de reporte, redacción de minutas, vocabulario de liderazgo, reading, listening, writing y speaking con soluciones y modelos.

content:
# Unidad 34 C1: reuniones y minutas, liderazgo y gestión La minuta es el género donde la palabra hablada se convierte en registro formal: lo que alguien *dijo* en la sala se transforma en lo que el comité *acordó*, *destacó* o *se comprometió a hacer*. Para hacerlo con precisión, el inglés C1 domina el **reported speech avanzado**, los **verbos de reporte** y el **registro de gestión**. Comparemos tres versiones del mismo acuerdo: - *John said we should cut costs and he will talk to finance.* - *John noted that costs should be reduced and undertook to speak with the finance team.* - *It was noted that, in light of the revised forecast, operating costs should be reduced by a further five percent; Mr. Chen undertook to liaise with the finance team and to present a revised budget by the end of the following week, and the committee recommended that the proposal be circulated for comment prior to the next meeting.* La primera reporta de forma directa; la segunda ya usa un verbo de reporte (*noted, undertook*) y retroceso de tiempos; la tercera despliega el aparato completo: pasiva impersonal (*it was noted*), cláusula causal (*in light of*), verbo de reporte con compromiso (*undertook to*), recomendación con subjuntivo mandativo (*be circulated*) y registro de minuta denso. La Unidad 34 C1 desarrolla estos recursos en el contexto de **leadership and management**: *agenda, minutes, chair, action item, stakeholder, delegate, accountable, escalate, ratify, mandate, buy-in, bottleneck* y *remediation*. El tema encaja de forma natural porque la gestión es, por definición, el arte de convertir la conversación en decisión y la decisión en acción registrada. Dominar el reported speech y el registro de minuta es, en este género, tan decisivo como la propia competencia directiva. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 34 C1](/curso-c1/unit-34)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 33 C1: emprendimiento e innovación](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-33-emprendimiento-innovacion)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 35 C1: ética corporativa](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-35-etica-corporativa)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. La minuta: por qué importa el reported speech Una minuta no transcribe; **reporta y condensa**. Convierte el flujo de una reunión en un registro jerárquico de acuerdos, compromisos y recomendaciones. Su motor gramatical es el **reported speech** en pasado, con **verbos de reporte** que matizan el tipo de intervención y **pasivas impersonales** que proyectan autoridad colectiva. Sin reported speech, la minuta se queda en *John said we should cut costs*; con él, llega a *It was noted that costs should be reduced; Mr. Chen undertook to present a revised budget*. ### 2. Reported speech: retroceso de tiempos Al reportar en pasado, los tiempos verbales retroceden un grado: - **Present → Past:** *She says the budget is tight* → *She said the budget **was** tight.* - **Present perfect → Past perfect:** *He has reviewed the proposal* → *He said he **had reviewed** the proposal.* - **Will → Would:** *We will circulate the draft* → *They said they **would** circulate the draft.* - **Can → Could:** *I can present next week* → *He said he **could** present the following week.* - **Must → Had to:** *We must act now* → *They said they **had to** act then.* El retroceso es obligatorio cuando el verbo de reporte está en pasado; se mantiene el tiempo original solo cuando la situación sigue siendo válida (*She said the earth revolves around the sun*). ### 3. Cambios de pronombres y deícticos - **Pronombres:** *I → he/she, we → they, my → his/her, our → their.* - **Deícticos temporales:** *today → that day, tomorrow → the following day, next week → the following week, yesterday → the previous day.* - **Deícticos espaciales:** *here → there, this → that.* *We will decide tomorrow* → *They said they would decide the following day.* ### 4. Verbos de reporte: matizar la intervención El C1 no se limita a *said*; elige el verbo según el tipo de intervención: - **Observación:** *noted, highlighted, emphasised, pointed out, observed.* - **Propuesta:** *proposed, suggested, recommended, put forward.* - **Acuerdo:** *agreed, accepted, endorsed, approved.* - **Compromiso:** *undertook to, committed to, pledged to, agreed to.* - **Duda o challenge:** *queried, questioned, raised concerns about, challenged.* - **Señalización de problema:** *flagged, raised the issue of, drew attention to.* - **Reiteración:** *reiterated, restated, reaffirmed.* Cada verbo carga un matiz: *queried* implica duda razonada; *flagged*, alerta de problema; *undertook to*, compromiso accionable con plazo. ### 5. Preguntas y órdenes reportadas - **Pregunta reportada (orden afirmativo):** *She asked, "When will the report be ready?"* → *She asked when the report **would be** ready.* (no *when would the report be*; orden afirmativo tras wh-word). - **Orden reportada (to + infinitivo):** *He said, "Circulate the draft."* → *He told them **to circulate** the draft.* / *He instructed them to circulate...* - **Sugerencia reportada:** *She said, "Let's defer the item."* → *She suggested deferring the item.* (o *that they defer*). ### 6. Pasivas impersonales en minutas La minuta prefiere la pasiva impersonal para proyectar autoridad colectiva y borrar el yo: - *It **was noted** that...* - *It **was agreed** that...* - *It **was recommended** that the proposal **be** circulated.* (subjuntivo mandativo) - *Concerns **were raised** about...* - *The minutes **were ratified**.* Esta impersonalización es la firma del registro de minuta: la entidad decide, no el individuo. ### 7. Estructura canónica de la minuta 1. **Encabezado:** *Date, Time, Location, Attendees, Apologies, Chair, Minute-taker.* 2. **Minutos anteriores:** *The minutes of the previous meeting were ratified.* 3. **Puntos del orden del día:** numerados, con reported speech y verbos de reporte. 4. **Action items:** con responsable y plazo — *Mr. Chen to present a revised budget by 30 October.* 5. **Cierre:** fecha de la próxima reunión. ### 8. Action items: responsable + plazo + verbo El action item es la unidad accionable de la minuta. Su patrón: **sujeto + to + infinitivo + plazo**. - *Ms. Patel to circulate the revised KPIs by Friday.* - *The finance team to present cost-saving options by 15 November.* - *All heads of department to confirm attendance at the strategy offsite by end of week.* La precisión del responsable y el plazo es lo que convierte un acuerdo en acción rastreable. ### 9. Conectores de secuencia y causalidad en minutas - **Secuencia:** *firstly, subsequently, thereafter, finally, in conclusion.* - **Causalidad:** *in light of, given, owing to, on account of.* - **Consecuencia:** *consequently, accordingly, therefore, as a result.* - **Adición:** *moreover, furthermore, in addition.* - **Contraste:** *however, nevertheless, on the other hand.* *In light of the revised forecast, costs should be reduced; consequently, Mr. Chen undertook to present a revised budget.* ### 10. Vocabulario de liderazgo y gestión - **Agenda** — orden del día. - **Minutes / minute-taker** — minuta / persona que toma la minuta. - **Chair (verb and noun)** — presidir / presidente de la reunión. - **Action item** — punto accionable. - **Stakeholder** — parte interesada. - **Delegate / delegation** — delegar / delegación. - **Accountable / accountability** — responsable de rendir cuentas. - **Escalate** — escalar (un problema a un nivel superior). - **Ratify** — ratificar, aprobar formalmente. - **Mandate** — mandato, autorización. - **Buy-in** — adhesión, compromiso de los implicados. - **Bottleneck** — cuello de botella. - **Remediation** — remediación, acción correctiva. - **Offsite** — reunión fuera de la oficina. - **AOB (any other business)** — ruegos y preguntas. ### 11. Colocaciones de gestión - *chair a meeting / call to order* — presidir una reunión / dar inicio. - *table an item / table a discussion* — poner un punto sobre la mesa / aplazarlo. - *defer an item / park an issue* — aplazar un punto / aparcar un asunto. - *drive an initiative / drive accountability* — impulsar una iniciativa / exigir responsabilidad. - *secure buy-in / build consensus* — lograr adhesión / construir consenso. - *assign an action item / track progress* — asignar un punto accionable / hacer seguimiento. - *escalate a concern* — escalar una preocupación. - *liaise with / report back to* — coordinarse con / informar de vuelta a. - *ratify the minutes* — ratificar las minutas. - *address a bottleneck* — abordar un cuello de botella. ### 12. Errores frecuentes en minutas y reported speech - **No retroceder el tiempo:** *She said the budget is tight* (si ya pasó) → *...the budget **was** tight.* - **Mantener orden interrogativo en pregunta reportada:** *She asked when would the report be ready* → *She asked when the report **would be** ready.* (orden afirmativo). - **Confundir tell y say:** *She said them to circulate* → *She **told** them to circulate.* (tell + objeto + to-infinitivo; say + that-clause). - **Olvidar el subjuntivo mandativo:** *It was recommended that the proposal is circulated* → *...that the proposal **be** circulated.* - **Usar presente en minutos anteriores:** *The minutes are ratified* → *The minutes **were** ratified.* - **Mezclar registro:** *John was like, we gotta cut costs* → *It was noted that costs should be reduced.* ### 13. Registro: extracto de minuta modelo > *3.2 Cost Reduction* > *It was noted that, in light of the revised forecast, operating costs should be reduced by a further five percent. Mr. Chen highlighted that procurement savings had already been identified, and undertook to liaise with the finance team and to present a revised budget by the end of the following week. Concerns were raised about the impact on staffing; however, the chair reiterated that no redundancies were contemplated at this stage. It was recommended that the proposal be circulated for comment prior to the next meeting.* > *Action: Mr. Chen to present a revised budget by 30 October.* Nótese: pasiva impersonal (*it was noted, were raised*), verbo de reporte con compromiso (*undertook to*), concesiva con contraste (*however*), recomendación con subjuntivo (*be circulated*), y action item con responsable y plazo. ### 14. Diferencias de registro: minuta, memo, email de seguimiento - **Minuta:** registro formal impersonal, reported speech en pasado, pasivas, action items. - **Memo de decisión:** formal, más conciso, registra una decisión concreta y su justificación. - **Email de seguimiento:** semiformal, primera persona, recapitula acuerdos y recuerda plazos. El C1 debe moverse entre los tres sin perder la precisión del responsable y el plazo que hace rastreable la gestión. ### 15. Síntesis: reportar para gobernar La minuta combina cuatro motores: **reported speech en pasado** (retroceso de tiempos, cambio de pronombres y deícticos), **verbos de reporte** que matizan la intervención (*noted, proposed, undertook, queried, flagged*), **pasivas impersonales** (*it was noted/agreed/recommended*) y **action items** con responsable y plazo. A esto se suman los **conectores de secuencia y causalidad** (*in light of, consequently, thereafter*), la **estructura canónica** (encabezado, ratificación, puntos, actions, cierre) y un **léxico de gestión** que permite convertir conversación en decisión rastreable con la precisión que el C1 exige. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 — Retroceso de tiempos Reporta estas frases en pasado (verbo de reporte en pasado). 1. "The budget is tight." → She said the budget ______. 2. "We will circulate the draft." → They said they ______. 3. "I can present next week." → He said he ______. 4. "We must act now." → They said they ______.
Ver solución 1. She said the budget **was** tight. 2. They said they **would** circulate the draft. 3. He said he **could** present the following week. 4. They said they **had to** act then.
### Ejercicio 2 — Cambios de deícticos Reporta cambiando los deícticos temporales y espaciales. 1. "We will decide tomorrow." → They said they would decide ______. 2. "I reviewed the proposal yesterday." → He said he had reviewed the proposal ______. 3. "Bring the report here." → She told them to bring the report ______.
Ver solución 1. They said they would decide **the following day**. 2. He said he had reviewed the proposal **the previous day**. 3. She told them to bring the report **there**.
### Ejercicio 3 — Verbos de reporte Elige el verbo más adecuado (noted / proposed / queried / undertook / flagged). 1. Mr. Chen ______ that procurement savings had been identified. 2. Ms. Patel ______ to present a revised budget by Friday. 3. A team member ______ whether the timeline was realistic. 4. The chair ______ a risk in the supply chain. 5. It was ______ that costs should be reduced by five percent.
Ver solución 1. Mr. Chen **noted** that procurement savings had been identified. 2. Ms. Patel **undertook** to present a revised budget by Friday. 3. A team member **queried** whether the timeline was realistic. 4. The chair **flagged** a risk in the supply chain. 5. It was **proposed / recommended** that costs should be reduced by five percent. (o *It was noted that...*)
### Ejercicio 4 — Preguntas reportadas (orden afirmativo) Reporta estas preguntas con orden afirmativo. 1. "When will the report be ready?" → She asked when ______. 2. "Has the budget been approved?" → He asked whether ______. 3. "Can we defer this item?" → She asked if ______.
Ver solución 1. She asked when the report **would be** ready. 2. He asked whether the budget **had been** approved. 3. She asked if they **could** defer that item.
### Ejercicio 5 — Órdenes reportadas (to + infinitivo) Reporta con *tell* o *instruct* + objeto + to-infinitivo. 1. "Circulate the draft." → He told them ______. 2. "Prepare a revised budget." → She instructed the team ______. 3. "Confirm attendance by Friday." → The chair asked all heads ______.
Ver solución 1. He told them **to circulate** the draft. 2. She instructed the team **to prepare** a revised budget. 3. The chair asked all heads **to confirm** attendance by Friday.
### Ejercicio 6 — Pasivas impersonales y subjuntivo mandativo Reescribe con pasiva impersonal + subjuntivo. 1. The committee recommends circulating the proposal. → It was recommended that the proposal ______. 2. They agreed to reduce costs by 5%. → It was agreed that costs ______. 3. Someone noted that the timeline was tight. → It was noted that the timeline ______.
Ver solución 1. It was recommended that the proposal **be circulated**. 2. It was agreed that costs **be reduced** by 5%. (o *should be reduced*) 3. It was noted that the timeline **was** tight. (reporte de hecho, no mandato)
### Ejercicio 7 — Action items (responsable + plazo) Redacta el action item para cada acuerdo. 1. Ms. Patel — circulate revised KPIs — by Friday. 2. Finance team — present cost-saving options — by 15 November. 3. All heads — confirm attendance at offsite — by end of week.
Ver solución 1. **Action: Ms. Patel to circulate the revised KPIs by Friday.** 2. **Action: The finance team to present cost-saving options by 15 November.** 3. **Action: All heads of department to confirm attendance at the strategy offsite by end of week.**
### Ejercicio 8 — Conectores de secuencia y causalidad Inserta el conector adecuado (in light of / consequently / thereafter / however / furthermore). 1. ______ the revised forecast, costs should be reduced. 2. Mr. Chen undertook to present a revised budget; ______, the committee endorsed the timeline. 3. Concerns were raised about staffing; ______, no redundancies were contemplated. 4. The minutes were ratified; ______, the chair moved to item 3.2. 5. Procurement savings were identified; ______, the proposal was circulated.
Ver solución 1. **In light of** the revised forecast, costs should be reduced. 2. Mr. Chen undertook to present a revised budget; **furthermore**, the committee endorsed the timeline. 3. Concerns were raised about staffing; **however**, no redundancies were contemplated. 4. The minutes were ratified; **thereafter**, the chair moved to item 3.2. 5. Procurement savings were identified; **consequently**, the proposal was circulated.
### Ejercicio 9 — Corrige los errores Cada frase tiene un error. Corrígelo. 1. She said them to circulate the draft. 2. She asked when would the report be ready. 3. It was recommended that the proposal is circulated. 4. The minutes are ratified at the start. 5. John was like, we gotta cut costs.
Ver solución 1. She **told** them to circulate the draft. (tell + objeto + to-infinitivo) 2. She asked when the report **would be** ready. (orden afirmativo) 3. It was recommended that the proposal **be** circulated. (subjuntivo mandativo) 4. The minutes **were** ratified at the start. (pasado) 5. It was noted that costs **should be reduced**. (registro de minuta)
### Ejercicio 10 — Transformación (CAE-style) Reescribe empezando con las palabras dadas. 1. "We will circulate the draft tomorrow," she said. → *She said they...* 2. "Let's defer the item," he proposed. → *He proposed deferring...* 3. "Can we reduce costs by 5%?" she asked. → *She asked whether...* 4. The committee recommends that the proposal be circulated. → *It was recommended...*
Ver solución 1. She said they **would circulate the draft the following day**. 2. He proposed **deferring the item**. (o *that they defer the item*) 3. She asked whether they **could reduce** costs by 5%. 4. It was recommended **that the proposal be circulated**.
### Ejercicio 11 — Vocabulario de gestión Relaciona cada término con su definición. 1. Ratify a. Cuello de botella. 2. Bottleneck b. Aprobar formalmente. 3. Escalate c. Subir un problema a nivel superior. 4. Buy-in d. Adhesión, compromiso de los implicados. 5. AOB e. Ruegos y preguntas.
Ver solución 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, 4-d, 5-e.
### Ejercicio 12 — Colocaciones de gestión Completa con el verbo adecuado (chair / table / defer / secure / escalate). 1. ______ a meeting and call it to order. 2. ______ an item for discussion. 3. ______ a point to the next meeting. 4. ______ buy-in from all stakeholders. 5. ______ a concern to the steering committee.
Ver solución 1. **Chair** a meeting and call it to order. 2. **Table** an item for discussion. 3. **Defer** a point to the next meeting. 4. **Secure** buy-in from all stakeholders. 5. **Escalate** a concern to the steering committee.
### Ejercicio 13 — Reading Lee el extracto de minuta y responde. > *3.2 Cost Reduction. It was noted that, in light of the revised forecast, operating costs should be reduced by a further five percent. Mr. Chen highlighted that procurement savings had already been identified, and undertook to liaise with the finance team and to present a revised budget by the end of the following week. Concerns were raised about staffing; however, the chair reiterated that no redundancies were contemplated.* 1. What two things did Mr. Chen do (verbos de reporte)? 2. What concern was raised, and how was it addressed? 3. Rewrite "It was noted that... costs should be reduced" as a direct quote from the chair.
Ver solución 1. He **highlighted** that procurement savings had been identified, and **undertook** to liaise with finance and present a revised budget by the end of the following week. 2. Concerns were raised about staffing (possible redundancies); the chair **reiterated** that no redundancies were contemplated. 3. The chair said, "Operating costs should be reduced by a further five percent." (o "In light of the revised forecast, we should reduce operating costs by a further five percent.")
### Ejercicio 14 — Listening (paráfrasis) Parafrasea esta conversación de reunión en registro de minuta. > "John said we need to cut costs. He'll talk to finance. Someone asked about layoffs but the boss said no redundancies for now."
Ver solución Modelo: *It was noted that operating costs should be reduced. Mr. Chen undertook to liaise with the finance team and to present a revised budget. Concerns were raised about staffing; however, the chair reiterated that no redundancies were contemplated at this stage.*
### Ejercicio 15 — Writing Escribe una sección de minuta (80–100 palabras) para el punto "3.3 Vendor Selection". Usa al menos: una pasiva impersonal, un verbo de reporte con compromiso, una concesiva con contraste y un action item con responsable y plazo.
Ver solución Modelo: *3.3 Vendor Selection. It was noted that three vendors had been shortlisted following the RFP process. Ms. Patel highlighted that Vendor A had scored highest on technical criteria, and undertook to conduct reference checks by the end of the following week. Concerns were raised about Vendor A's pricing structure; however, the committee agreed that the technical advantage offset the marginal cost premium. It was recommended that the final decision be deferred pending the reference checks. Action: Ms. Patel to report back on reference checks by 7 November.* (89 palabras)
### Ejercicio 16 — Speaking (monólogo) Prepara un monólogo de 2 minutos en el que, como chair, recapitules los acuerdos de una reunión al cierre, usando reported speech y registro de gestión.
Ver solución Modelo de inicio: *To summarise, it was noted that, in light of the revised forecast, operating costs should be reduced by a further five percent. Mr. Chen undertook to liaise with finance and to present a revised budget by the end of the following week. Concerns were raised about staffing; however, I would reiterate that no redundancies are contemplated at this stage. Regarding vendor selection, Ms. Patel agreed to conduct reference checks by 7 November, and it was recommended that the final decision be deferred pending those checks. Our next meeting is scheduled for...*
### Ejercicio 17 — Registro: minuta, memo o email de seguimiento Clasifica cada extracto. 1. *3.2 Cost Reduction. It was noted that... Action: Mr. Chen to present by 30 October.* 2. *Decision: the vendor contract is awarded to Supplier A, subject to satisfactory references.* 3. *Hi all — just to recap what we agreed: John's handling the budget, and we'll revisit vendor selection next week.*
Ver solución 1. **Minuta** (formal impersonal, reported speech, action items numerados). 2. **Memo de decisión** (formal conciso, registra una decisión y su condición). 3. **Email de seguimiento** (semiformal, primera persona, recapitula acuerdos).
### Ejercicio 18 — Consolidación Completa el extracto de minuta con una palabra por hueco. > *It was (1)______ that, in light of the revised forecast, costs should be reduced. Mr. Chen (2)______ to present a revised budget by the end of the (3)______ week. Concerns were raised about staffing; (4)______, no redundancies were contemplated. It was recommended that the proposal (5)______ circulated for comment.*
Ver solución 1. **noted** (pasiva impersonal) 2. **undertook** (verbo de reporte con compromiso) 3. **following** (deíctico temporal retrocedido) 4. **however** (concesiva con contraste) 5. **be** (subjuntivo mandativo)
### Ejercicio 19 — Reescribe el párrafo con registro de minuta Eleva el registro del párrafo coloquial a una sección de minuta con reported speech, pasivas y action item. > *John said we gotta cut costs and he'll talk to finance. Someone asked about layoffs but the boss said no redundancies for now. We'll send the proposal around before next time.*
Ver solución Modelo: *It was noted that, in light of the revised forecast, operating costs should be reduced by a further five percent. Mr. Chen undertook to liaise with the finance team and to present a revised budget by the end of the following week. Concerns were raised about staffing; however, the chair reiterated that no redundancies were contemplated at this stage. It was recommended that the proposal be circulated for comment prior to the next meeting. Action: Mr. Chen to present a revised budget by 30 October.*
## Resumen de la unidad - El **reported speech en pasado** retrocede los tiempos (*is→was, will→would, can→could, must→had to*), cambia pronombres (*I→he/she, we→they*) y deícticos (*tomorrow→the following day, here→there*); las preguntas reportadas llevan orden afirmativo y las órdenes, *to* + infinitivo. - Los **verbos de reporte** matizan la intervención: observación (*noted, highlighted, emphasised*), propuesta (*proposed, suggested, recommended*), acuerdo (*agreed, endorsed*), compromiso (*undertook to, committed to, pledged to*), duda (*queried, questioned, raised concerns*) y señalización (*flagged, raised the issue of*). - Las **pasivas impersonales** (*it was noted/agreed/recommended*) proyectan autoridad colectiva y, con el **subjuntivo mandativo** (*be circulated, be reduced*), formulan recomendaciones vinculantes. - Los **action items** (responsable + *to* + infinitivo + plazo) y los **conectores de secuencia y causalidad** (*in light of, consequently, thereafter, however*) estructuran la minuta canónica (encabezado, ratificación, puntos, actions, cierre). - El **vocabulario de gestión** (*agenda, minutes, chair, action item, stakeholder, delegate, accountable, escalate, ratify, mandate, buy-in, bottleneck, remediation, offsite, AOB*) y sus colocaciones (*chair a meeting, table an item, defer a point, secure buy-in, escalate a concern, liaise with, ratify the minutes, address a bottleneck*) permiten convertir conversación en decisión rastreable con la precisión y el registro que el C1 exige.

keywords: Ejercicios de Responsabilidad y Ética Corporativa C1
be accountable for liable for responsible for inglés
have a duty to ought to corporate ethics C1
have a duty to ought to

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre be responsible for, be accountable for y be liable for?
faqs.answer: Be responsible for indica la tarea o función asignada (the CFO is responsible for financial reporting); be accountable for indica rendición de cuentas, responder ante alguien del resultado (the CEO is accountable to the board); be liable for implica responsabilidad legal o financiera, con posible sanción (the company is liable for damages).

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se argumenta éticamente en inglés C1?
faqs.answer: Combinando estructuras de obligación moral (have a duty to, are obliged to, ought to), condicionales de consecuencia (if a company pollutes, it must remediate), hedges para no dogmatizar (it is widely held that), y conectores de causa y contraste. El registro es formal, impersonal y matizado, sin moralina retórica vacía.

faqs.question: ¿Qué son los stakeholders y por qué importan en ética corporativa?
faqs.answer: Son todas las partes afectadas por la actividad de una empresa: accionistas, empleados, clientes, proveedores, comunidades y medio ambiente. La ética corporativa moderna exige equilibrar sus intereses (stakeholder value), no solo maximizar el beneficio del accionista (shareholder value).

faqs.question: ¿La Unidad 35 incluye ejercicios resueltos?
faqs.answer: Sí. Incluye práctica de estructuras de responsabilidad, obligación moral, argumentación ética, vocabulario de stakeholders y CSR, reading, listening, writing y speaking con soluciones y modelos.

content:
# Unidad 35 C1: responsabilidad y stakeholders, ética corporativa La ética corporativa es el género donde el lenguaje se vuelve obligación moral: lo que una empresa *debe*, *es responsable de* y *responde por*. El inglés C1 distingue estos matices con un repertorio de **estructuras de responsabilidad** y **obligación ética** que ningún otro nivel maneja con la misma precisión. Comparemos tres versiones sobre el mismo hecho: - *The company did wrong and they should fix it.* - *The company is responsible for the spill and ought to bear the cost of remediation.* - *Insofar as the corporation knowingly discharged pollutants in breach of its own environmental policy, it is not merely responsible but fully accountable to the affected communities and liable for the cost of remediation; accordingly, it has a duty to compensate affected stakeholders and to implement safeguards against recurrence.* La primera es moralina vaga; la segunda introduce *responsible for* y *ought to*; la tercera despliega el aparato completo: causalidad formal (*insofar as*), distinción entre *responsible*, *accountable* y *liable*, conector de consecuencia (*accordingly*), obligación moral con *have a duty to* y un compromiso de remedio y prevención. La Unidad 35 C1 desarrolla estos recursos en el contexto de **corporate ethics and stakeholders**: *stakeholder, shareholder, accountability, liability, CSR, due diligence, whistleblowing, fiduciary duty, transparency, greenwashing, remediation, compliance* y *recurrence*. El tema encaja de forma natural porque la ética corporativa es, por definición, el arte de asignar responsabilidad y exigir obligación moral en un registro que sea formal sin ser retórico vacío. Dominar las estructuras de responsabilidad es, en este género, tan decisivo como el propio razonamiento ético. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 35 C1](/curso-c1/unit-35)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 34 C1: liderazgo y gestión](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-34-liderazgo-gestion)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 36 C1](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-36-economia-sociedad)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. La responsabilidad ética: por qué importan las estructuras La ética corporativa no se expresa con adjetivos morales sueltos (*good, bad, wrong*), sino con **estructuras gramaticales que asignan responsabilidad, gradúan la obligación y encadenan consecuencias**. El C1 domina tres familias: *be responsible for* (la tarea), *be accountable for/to* (la rendición de cuentas) y *be liable for* (la responsabilidad legal o financiera). Confundirlas no es un mero error gramatical: es una imprecisión ética que puede tergiversar quién debe qué a quién. ### 2. Be responsible for: la tarea o función *Be responsible for* indica la **tarea, función o ámbito asignado**: - *The CFO **is responsible for** financial reporting.* - *The procurement team **is responsible for** supplier due diligence.* Es la responsabilidad de rol: la persona o unidad tiene a su cargo una función, pero no necesariamente rinde cuentas ante un tribunal ni asume sanción legal por ella. ### 3. Be accountable for / to: la rendición de cuentas *Be accountable for* indica **rendición de cuentas por el resultado**, y *be accountable to* señala **ante quién** se responde: - *The CEO **is accountable for** the company's overall conduct.* - *The board **is accountable to** the shareholders.* La accountability añade el componente de respuesta: no solo se tiene la función, sino que se debe **explicar y responder** del resultado ante una autoridad o constituency. Es el núcleo del gobierno corporativo moderno. ### 4. Be liable for: la responsabilidad legal o financiera *Be liable for* implica **responsabilidad legal o financiera, con posible sanción**: - *The company **is liable for** the cost of remediation.* - *Directors may be **personally liable** for fraudulent misstatement.* La liability es la responsabilidad con diente: conlleva obligación de reparar, indemnizar o responder ante un tribunal. Confundir *responsible* con *liable* puede inflar o diluir la exigencia legal de un texto. ### 5. Obligación moral: have a duty to, are obliged to, ought to - **Have a duty to:** obligación ética o fiduciaria fuerte — *The board has a duty to act in the interest of all stakeholders.* - **Be obliged to:** obligación moral o contractual — *The company is obliged to honour its settlement agreement.* - **Ought to:** recomendación con tono moral — *The firm ought to have disclosed the conflict of interest.* - **Have a moral imperative to:** muy fuerte, retórico — *The corporation has a moral imperative to remediate the damage.* El C1 elige según la fuerza: *ought to* (consejo moral), *have a duty to* (obligación fiduciaria o ética), *be obliged to* (contractual), *be required to* (reglamentaria). ### 6. Fiduciary duty y el debate shareholder vs. stakeholder - **Fiduciary duty:** obligación legal de los directivos de actuar en el mejor interés del beneficiario — tradicionalmente, el accionista. - **Shareholder value:** la doctrina de que el fin de la empresa es maximizar el valor para el accionista. - **Stakeholder value:** la doctrina de que la empresa debe equilibrar los intereses de todas las partes afectadas (empleados, clientes, comunidades, medio ambiente). El debate se expresa con estructuras de obligación: *The board has a fiduciary duty to shareholders; nevertheless, a growing consensus holds that it also has a duty to stakeholders.* ### 7. Condicionales de consecuencia ética La argumentación ética encadena acciones y consecuencias con condicionales: - *If a company pollutes, it **must** remediate.* - *Should a breach occur, the firm **is obliged to** disclose it promptly.* - *Were a director to act in breach of fiduciary duty, they **would be** personally liable.* - *Unless the company reforms its supply chain, reputational damage **will** follow.* La inversión con *should* y *were* eleva el registro del razonamiento ético-formal. ### 8. Hedges y atribución en ética El registro ético evita el dogmatismo con *hedges* que atribuyen la postura: - *It is **widely held that** corporations owe duties beyond shareholders.* - *There is **a strong case for** holding boards accountable for ESG failures.* - *It is **arguable that** short-termism undermines long-term value.* - *A **growing consensus** holds that stakeholder value is not incompatible with shareholder returns.* Estos *hedges* proyectan prudencia y atribuyen la postura a la comunidad, evitando el tono de sermón. ### 9. Conectores de causa, consecuencia y contraste ético - **Causa:** *insofar as, in light of, given, owing to, on the grounds that.* - **Consecuencia:** *accordingly, consequently, therefore, as a result, hence.* - **Contraste:** *nevertheless, nonetheless, notwithstanding, yet, whereas.* - **Reformulación:** *that is to say, in other words, to put it differently.* *Insofar as the corporation knowingly breached its policy, it is liable; accordingly, it has a duty to remediate. Nevertheless, mitigating factors may reduce the penalty.* ### 10. Vocabulario de ética corporativa y stakeholders - **Stakeholder** — parte interesada. - **Shareholder** — accionista. - **Accountability** — rendición de cuentas. - **Liability** — responsabilidad legal o financiera. - **CSR (corporate social responsibility)** — responsabilidad social corporativa. - **Due diligence** — debida diligencia. - **Whistleblowing / whistleblower** — denuncia interna / denunciante. - **Fiduciary duty** — deber fiduciario. - **Transparency** — transparencia. - **Greenwashing** — lavado verde (falsa apariencia ecológica). - **Remediation** — remediación, reparación del daño. - **Compliance** — cumplimiento normativo. - **Recurrence** — recurrencia, repetición del daño. - **Conflict of interest** — conflicto de intereses. - **ESG (environmental, social, governance)** — criterios ASG. ### 11. Colocaciones éticas - *owe a duty to* — deber un deber a. - *act in the interest of* — actuar en interés de. - *bear the cost of* — asumir el coste de. - *disclose a conflict* — revelar un conflicto. - *remediate the damage* — remediar el daño. - *prevent recurrence* — prevenir la recurrencia. - *hold accountable / hold liable* — hacer rendir cuentas / hacer responsable legal. - *breach a policy / breach fiduciary duty* — incumplir una política / el deber fiduciario. - *implement safeguards* — implementar salvaguardas. - *compensate affected parties* — compensar a las partes afectadas. ### 12. Errores frecuentes en el registro ético - **Confundir responsible y liable:** *The CFO is liable for reporting* (no es ilegal, es su función) → *...is **responsible for** reporting.* - **Olvidar accountable to:** *The board is accountable* (¿ante quién?) → *...accountable **to** the shareholders.* - **Dogmatizar sin hedge:** *Companies must always put stakeholders first* (demasiado absoluto) → *A growing consensus holds that...* - **Usar moralina retórica vacía:** *It is of the utmost paramount crucial importance that utmost care be taken* → una estructura concreta (*has a duty to remediate*). - **Confundir ought to y must:** *ought to* es consejo moral; *must* es obligación fuerte; no son intercambiables en registro ético-formal. - **Mezclar registro:** *The company was really bad and should say sorry* → *The company is liable for the damage and has a duty to compensate affected stakeholders.* ### 13. Registro: argumento ético modelo > *Insofar as the corporation knowingly discharged pollutants in breach of its own environmental policy, it is not merely responsible but fully accountable to the affected communities and liable for the cost of remediation. Accordingly, it has a duty to compensate affected stakeholders and to implement safeguards against recurrence. Nevertheless, it is widely held that mitigating factors — notably the self-reporting of the breach — ought to be weighed when determining the scale of the penalty; that said, no mitigation absolves the board of its fiduciary duty to ensure compliance.* Nótese: causalidad formal (*insofar as*), distinción *responsible/accountable/liable*, conector de consecuencia (*accordingly*), obligación moral (*has a duty to*), *hedge* (*it is widely held that*), concesiva con contraste (*nevertheless, that said*) y cierre con *fiduciary duty*. ### 14. Diferencias de registro: código ético, informe de CSR, declaración pública - **Código ético (code of conduct):** normativo, con *shall, must, are required to* — *All employees shall disclose any conflict of interest.* - **Informe de CSR:** formal-expositivo, con pasiva, hedges y datos — *It is estimated that emissions were reduced by 18% year-on-year.* - **Declaración pública (apología o compromiso):** formal-retórico, con *we have a duty to, we are committed to* — *We are committed to remediating the damage and preventing recurrence.* El C1 debe moverse entre los tres sin confundir la directiva normativa del código con la exposición analítica del informe ni con el compromiso retórico de la declaración. ### 15. Síntesis: argumentar la responsabilidad La ética corporativa combina cinco motores: **estructuras de responsabilidad** (*be responsible for* la tarea, *be accountable for/to* la rendición, *be liable for* la sanción legal), **obligación moral** (*have a duty to, be obliged to, ought to*), **condicionales de consecuencia** (*if/should/were/unless*), **hedges de atribución** (*it is widely held that, there is a strong case for*) y **conectores de causa y contraste** (*insofar as, accordingly, nevertheless*). A esto se suma el debate **fiduciary duty / shareholder vs. stakeholder value** y un **léxico ético** que permite asignar responsabilidad con la precisión y el matiz que el C1 exige. ## Parte II — Ejercicios ### Ejercicio 1 — responsible for / accountable for / liable for Elige la estructura adecuada. 1. The CFO ______ financial reporting. (tarea de rol) 2. The CEO ______ the company's overall conduct. (rendición de cuentas por el resultado) 3. The company ______ the cost of remediation. (responsabilidad legal, con sanción) 4. The board ______ the shareholders. (responder ante)
Ver solución 1. The CFO **is responsible for** financial reporting. 2. The CEO **is accountable for** the company's overall conduct. 3. The company **is liable for** the cost of remediation. 4. The board **is accountable to** the shareholders.
### Ejercicio 2 — Obligación moral Elige la estructura que mejor gradúa la fuerza (ought to / have a duty to / be obliged to / be required to). 1. The board ______ act in the interest of all stakeholders. (obligación fiduciaria fuerte) 2. The company ______ honour its settlement agreement. (contractual) 3. The firm ______ have disclosed the conflict earlier. (consejo moral, reproche pasado) 4. All employees ______ disclose any conflict of interest. (reglamentaria, código)
Ver solución 1. The board **has a duty to** act in the interest of all stakeholders. 2. The company **is obliged to** honour its settlement agreement. 3. The firm **ought to have** disclosed the conflict earlier. 4. All employees **are required to** disclose any conflict of interest.
### Ejercicio 3 — Condicionales de consecuencia ética Completa con la forma verbal adecuada. 1. If a company pollutes, it ______ (must) remediate. 2. Should a breach ______ (occur), the firm is obliged to disclose it promptly. 3. Were a director to act in breach of fiduciary duty, they ______ (be) personally liable. 4. Unless the company reforms its supply chain, reputational damage ______ (follow).
Ver solución 1. If a company pollutes, it **must** remediate. 2. **Should** a breach **occur**, the firm is obliged to disclose it promptly. 3. **Were** a director to act in breach of fiduciary duty, they **would be** personally liable. 4. Unless the company reforms its supply chain, reputational damage **will** follow.
### Ejercicio 4 — Hedges de atribución Reescribe con un *hedging* de atribución. 1. Companies must put stakeholders first. → It is widely held that... 2. Boards should be accountable for ESG failures. → There is a strong case for... 3. Short-termism undermines long-term value. → It is arguable that...
Ver solución 1. It is **widely held that** companies should put stakeholders first. 2. There is **a strong case for** holding boards accountable for ESG failures. 3. It is **arguable that** short-termism undermines long-term value.
### Ejercicio 5 — Conectores de causa, consecuencia y contraste Inserta el conector adecuado (insofar as / accordingly / nevertheless / whereas / on the grounds that). 1. ______ the corporation knowingly breached its policy, it is liable. 2. The company is liable; ______, it has a duty to remediate. 3. Mitigating factors may reduce the penalty; ______, no mitigation absolves the board. 4. The board owes a duty to shareholders, ______ a growing consensus holds that it also owes a duty to stakeholders. 5. The claim was dismissed ______ the plaintiff lacked standing.
Ver solución 1. **Insofar as** the corporation knowingly breached its policy, it is liable. 2. The company is liable; **accordingly**, it has a duty to remediate. 3. Mitigating factors may reduce the penalty; **nevertheless**, no mitigation absolves the board. 4. The board owes a duty to shareholders, **whereas** a growing consensus holds that it also owes a duty to stakeholders. 5. The claim was dismissed **on the grounds that** the plaintiff lacked standing.
### Ejercicio 6 — Corrige los errores Cada frase tiene un error. Corrígelo. 1. The CFO is liable for reporting. (es su función, no ilegal) 2. The board is accountable. (¿ante quién?) 3. Companies must always put stakeholders first. (demasiado absoluto, sin atribución) 4. The company was really bad and should say sorry. 5. The firm ought to must disclose the conflict.
Ver solución 1. The CFO **is responsible for** reporting. (función de rol, no responsabilidad legal) 2. The board **is accountable to** the shareholders. 3. **A growing consensus holds that** companies should put stakeholders first. (hedge de atribución) 4. The company **is liable for the damage and has a duty to compensate** affected stakeholders. 5. The firm **ought to have disclosed** the conflict. (un solo modal; perfecto para reproche pasado)
### Ejercicio 7 — Transformación (CAE-style) Reescribe empezando con las palabras dadas. 1. "The company is responsible for the spill and should pay." → *Insofar as...* 2. "If a director breaches fiduciary duty, they will be personally liable." → *Were a director...* 3. "People think companies owe duties beyond shareholders." → *It is widely held that...* 4. "The company must remediate and prevent recurrence." → *The company has a duty...*
Ver solución 1. **Insofar as** the company is responsible for the spill, it should pay (for remediation). 2. **Were a director** to breach fiduciary duty, they would be personally liable. 3. **It is widely held that** companies owe duties beyond shareholders. 4. **The company has a duty** to remediate and to prevent recurrence.
### Ejercicio 8 — Vocabulario de ética corporativa Relaciona cada término con su definición. 1. Whistleblowing a. Falsa apariencia ecológica. 2. Greenwashing b. Denuncia interna de irregularidades. 3. Due diligence c. Debida diligencia (verificación previa). 4. Compliance d. Cumplimiento normativo. 5. ESG e. Criterios ambientales, sociales y de gobernanza.
Ver solución 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, 4-d, 5-e.
### Ejercicio 9 — Colocaciones éticas Completa con el verbo adecuado (owe / bear / disclose / remediate / prevent). 1. ______ a duty to all stakeholders. 2. ______ the cost of remediation. 3. ______ a conflict of interest promptly. 4. ______ the damage before it spreads. 5. ______ recurrence by implementing safeguards.
Ver solución 1. **Owe** a duty to all stakeholders. 2. **Bear** the cost of remediation. 3. **Disclose** a conflict of interest promptly. 4. **Remediate** the damage before it spreads. 5. **Prevent** recurrence by implementing safeguards.
### Ejercicio 10 — Fiduciary duty: shareholder vs. stakeholder Reescribe el enunciado equilibrando ambas doctrinas con un conector de contraste. > "The board has a fiduciary duty to shareholders. A growing consensus says it also has a duty to stakeholders."
Ver solución Modelo: *The board has a fiduciary duty to shareholders; **nevertheless**, a growing consensus holds that it also has a duty to stakeholders, and that the two are not irreconcilable.* (o con *whereas*: *The board has a fiduciary duty to shareholders, whereas a growing consensus holds that it also owes a duty to stakeholders.*)
### Ejercicio 11 — Reading Lee el extracto y responde. > *Insofar as the corporation knowingly discharged pollutants in breach of its own environmental policy, it is not merely responsible but fully accountable to the affected communities and liable for the cost of remediation. Accordingly, it has a duty to compensate affected stakeholders and to implement safeguards against recurrence. Nevertheless, it is widely held that mitigating factors — notably the self-reporting of the breach — ought to be weighed when determining the scale of the penalty.* 1. Distinguish the three levels of responsibility used in the text. 2. What two duties does the company have, according to the passage? 3. What mitigating factor is mentioned, and with what hedge?
Ver solución 1. *Responsible* (la tarea/incumplimiento), *accountable to* the affected communities (rendición de cuentas), *liable for* the cost of remediation (responsabilidad legal con sanción). 2. A duty to **compensate** affected stakeholders and a duty to **implement safeguards against recurrence**. 3. The self-reporting of the breach; introduced by the hedge *it is widely held that*.
### Ejercicio 12 — Listening (paráfrasis) Parafrasea esta declaración del CEO en registro ético-formal. > "We messed up with the spill. We'll pay to clean it and make sure it doesn't happen again. But we did tell on ourselves, so that should count for something."
Ver solución Modelo: *Insofar as the corporation discharged pollutants in breach of its environmental policy, it is liable for the cost of remediation. Accordingly, it has a duty to compensate affected stakeholders and to implement safeguards against recurrence. Nevertheless, it is widely held that the self-reporting of the breach ought to be weighed as a mitigating factor.*
### Ejercicio 13 — Writing Escribe un párrafo de argumentación ética (80–100 palabras) sobre un caso de greenwashing. Usa al menos: una estructura de responsabilidad (liable/accountable), una obligación moral (have a duty to), un condicional con *should* y un conector de contraste.
Ver solución Modelo: *Insofar as the firm marketed its product as carbon-neutral while knowingly relying on unverifiable offsets, it is accountable to consumers and liable for misleading claims. Accordingly, it has a duty to retract the campaign and to disclose its actual emissions transparently. Should the regulator find the practice systematic, the firm would face not only penalties but a lasting loss of trust; nevertheless, a prompt, good-faith correction may mitigate reputational damage and demonstrate genuine commitment to ESG principles.* (81 palabras)
### Ejercicio 14 — Speaking (monólogo) Prepara un monólogo de 2 minutos en el que argumentes, como miembro de un comité de ética, a favor de reforzar la whistleblower policy. Usa registro ético-formal.
Ver solución Modelo de inicio: *Insofar as the current whistleblower framework affords inadequate protection, the company is failing in its duty to employees and, by extension, to the stakeholders it claims to serve. It is widely held that robust whistleblowing channels are not a discretionary perk but a fiduciary safeguard: were a material breach to go unreported for fear of retaliation, the board would be accountable for the resulting harm. Accordingly, I would argue that we have a duty to strengthen protections, to guarantee anonymity, and to implement safeguards against recurrence. Should we fail to act, the reputational and legal exposure would, I believe, be considerable...*
### Ejercicio 15 — Registro: código ético, informe de CSR o declaración pública Clasifica cada extracto. 1. *All employees shall disclose any conflict of interest to the compliance officer without delay.* 2. *It is estimated that Scope 1 emissions were reduced by 18% year-on-year, owing to the electrification of the fleet.* 3. *We are committed to remediating the damage, to compensating affected communities, and to preventing recurrence.*
Ver solución 1. **Código ético** (normativo, *shall*). 2. **Informe de CSR** (formal-expositivo, pasiva, datos). 3. **Declaración pública** (formal-retórico, *we are committed to*).
### Ejercicio 16 — Consolidación Completa el párrafo con una palabra por hueco. > *(1)______ as the corporation knowingly breached its policy, it is (2)______ for the cost of remediation. (3)______, it has a duty to compensate affected stakeholders. (4)______, mitigating factors ought to be weighed. Should the breach (5)______ systematic, the firm would face severe penalties.*
Ver solución 1. **Insofar** (insofar as) 2. **liable** (be liable for) 3. **Accordingly** (consecuencia) 4. **Nevertheless** (contraste) 5. **prove** (should the breach prove systematic)
### Ejercicio 17 — Reescribe el párrafo con registro ético-formal Eleva el registro del párrafo coloquial con estructuras de responsabilidad, obligación moral y conectores. > *The company did a bad thing with the spill. They should pay to clean it and make sure it doesn't happen again. But they did tell on themselves so maybe go easy on them.*
Ver solución Modelo: *Insofar as the corporation knowingly discharged pollutants in breach of its environmental policy, it is accountable to the affected communities and liable for the cost of remediation. Accordingly, it has a duty to compensate affected stakeholders and to implement safeguards against recurrence. Nevertheless, it is widely held that the self-reporting of the breach ought to be weighed as a mitigating factor when determining the scale of the penalty.*
### Ejercicio 18 — Distinción fina: responsible vs. accountable vs. liable Para cada contexto, elige la estructura correcta y justifica. 1. Contexto: el CFO firma los informes financieros. (rol) 2. Contexto: el CEO explica ante el board por qué los ingresos cayeron. (rendición) 3. Contexto: la empresa paga una indemnización por un derrame. (sanción legal)
Ver solución 1. The CFO **is responsible for** financial reporting. (rol/tarea asignada) 2. The CEO **is accountable to** the board for the revenue decline. (rendición de cuentas, responder ante) 3. The company **is liable for** the cost of the spill. (responsabilidad legal con sanción)
### Ejercicio 19 — Debate shareholder vs. stakeholder (writing) Escribe un párrafo (80–100 palabras) que presente ambas doctrinas y postule una reconciliación, usando al menos un conector de contraste y una estructura de obligación.
Ver solución Modelo: *The board has a fiduciary duty to maximise shareholder value; nevertheless, a growing consensus holds that it also has a duty to stakeholders — employees, customers, communities and the environment. Insofar as short-termism erodes trust and, with it, long-term returns, the two doctrines are not irreconcilable but complementary. Accordingly, it is widely held that robust ESG governance serves not to dilute shareholder value but to safeguard it, so that a company accountable to all affected parties is, in the long run, also the one that best serves its shareholders.* (85 palabras)
## Resumen de la unidad - Las **estructuras de responsabilidad** se distinguen con precisión: *be responsible for* (la tarea o función asignada), *be accountable for/to* (la rendición de cuentas por el resultado y ante quién), *be liable for* (la responsabilidad legal o financiera, con posible sanción). Confundirlas tergiversa la exigencia ética y legal del texto. - La **obligación moral** se gradúa con *have a duty to* (fiduciaria/ética fuerte), *be obliged to* (contractual), *ought to* (consejo moral, con perfecto para reproche), *be required to* (reglamentaria). - Los **condicionales de consecuencia ética** (*if, should, were, unless*) encadenan acción y consecuencia; la **inversión con should/were** eleva el registro del razonamiento ético-formal. - Los **hedges de atribución** (*it is widely held that, there is a strong case for, it is arguable that, a growing consensus holds*) proyectan prudencia y evitan el dogmatismo; los **conectores de causa, consecuencia y contraste** (*insofar as, accordingly, nevertheless, whereas, on the grounds that*) estructuran el argumento. - El debate **fiduciary duty / shareholder vs. stakeholder value** y el **vocabulario ético** (*stakeholder, shareholder, accountability, liability, CSR, due diligence, whistleblowing, fiduciary duty, transparency, greenwashing, remediation, compliance, recurrence, conflict of interest, ESG*) con sus colocaciones (*owe a duty to, act in the interest of, bear the cost of, disclose a conflict, remediate the damage, prevent recurrence, hold accountable, breach fiduciary duty, implement safeguards, compensate affected parties*) permiten argumentar sobre ética corporativa con la precisión, el matiz y el registro que el C1 exige.
