faqs.answer: Sí. Incluye gramática, vocabulario de viajes, reading, listening, writing y speaking con respuestas y modelos.

content:
# Unidad 13 C1: participle clauses, viajes e intercambio cultural Las **participle clauses** permiten construir frases más compactas sin perder relaciones de tiempo, causa o contraste. En vez de escribir dos oraciones completas, podemos conectar sus ideas mediante un participio: - *She had never visited Japan before. She arrived in Tokyo with mixed feelings.* - *Having never visited Japan before, she arrived in Tokyo with mixed feelings.* La segunda frase indica claramente que la falta de experiencia ocurrió antes de la llegada. La estructura resulta especialmente útil en narraciones, informes, artículos de viajes y textos académicos. La Unidad 13 aplica estas formas al tema **Travel and Cultural Exchange**. Viajar puede ampliar la perspectiva, pero también plantea preguntas sobre turismo sostenible, desigualdad, aculturación y la relación entre visitantes y comunidades anfitrionas. El vocabulario de la unidad incluye *cultural conditioning, acculturation, overtourism, reverse culture shock, paternalistic, culturally sensitive* y *host community*. El objetivo no es reducir frases a cualquier precio. Una participle clause es buena cuando el sujeto está claro, la relación lógica se entiende y el texto gana fluidez. Si el sujeto implícito no coincide con el de la oración principal, aparece un **dangling modifier** y la frase deja de ser precisa. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 13 C1](/curso-c1/unit-13)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 12 C1: mixed conditionals y urbanismo](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-12-condicionales-urbanismo)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 14 C1: inversión condicional](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-21-clima-medioambiente)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. Qué es una participle clause Una participle clause es una cláusula reducida cuyo verbo aparece como participio. Normalmente no incluye un sujeto explícito ni un verbo conjugado, porque su sujeto se interpreta a partir de la oración principal. - **Present participle (-ing):** *Travelling through the region, she noticed several changes.* - **Past participle (-ed o V3):** *Surrounded by unfamiliar sounds, he felt disoriented.* - **Perfect participle:** *Having travelled extensively, he understood the cultural nuances.* - **Perfect passive participle:** *Having been warned about local restrictions, the visitors changed their plans.* Estas cláusulas pueden expresar tiempo, causa, condición, resultado, descripción o concesión. La relación exacta depende del contexto y de conectores como *while, when, after, having, although* o *though*. La ventaja principal es la concisión. La desventaja es que el lector debe identificar correctamente el sujeto implícito y la relación lógica. Por eso una participle clause exige más control que una simple coordinación con *and*. ### 2. Present participle: acción simultánea o causa El participio en **-ing** suele indicar que el sujeto realiza la acción y que esta ocurre al mismo tiempo que la acción principal o explica su causa: - *Walking through the old quarter, the visitors noticed the contrast between renovated buildings and abandoned homes.* - *Living abroad for a year, she developed a deeper appreciation of her own culture.* - *Looking at the map, the guide realised that the group had taken the wrong road.* Las versiones completas serían: - *While the visitors were walking...* - *Because she lived abroad for a year...* - *When the guide looked at the map...* No siempre hay una única traducción. El significado se infiere de la relación entre las dos acciones. Si quieres evitar ambigüedad, añade un conector: - *While travelling through the region, she collected interviews.* - *Because she had lived abroad, she understood the situation.* El participio en -ing también puede presentar una consecuencia: - *The group missed the last bus, forcing the guide to rearrange the itinerary.* En este caso, *forcing* no comparte exactamente el mismo sujeto; la construcción presenta el resultado de la primera acción. Es común en textos informativos, pero debe quedar claro qué hecho produce la consecuencia. ### 3. Having + past participle: anterioridad Usamos **having + past participle** cuando la acción de la participle clause terminó antes de la acción principal: - *Having visited the country several times, he understood its regional differences.* - *Having read the travel advisory, the family decided to postpone the trip.* - *Having never experienced reverse culture shock, she underestimated the difficulty of returning home.* La forma completa sería *After he had visited...*, *After the family had read...* o *Because she had never experienced...*. El perfect participle es útil cuando la anterioridad importa. Compara: - *Travelling through the country, she learned several expressions.* Las dos acciones pueden ser simultáneas. - *Having travelled through the country, she wrote a detailed report.* El viaje se presenta como terminado antes de escribir. La negación va delante de *having*: - *Not having booked accommodation, they had to sleep outside the city.* - *Having never studied the language, he relied on an interpreter.* Si la relación temporal no necesita énfasis, una cláusula completa puede ser más clara. El C1 no consiste en usar siempre la forma más comprimida. ### 4. Having been + past participle: pasiva anterior Cuando el sujeto recibe la acción anterior, usamos **having been + past participle**: - *Having been warned about overtourism, the visitors avoided the busiest district.* - *Having been invited by the host community, the researchers attended the ceremony.* - *Having been delayed by a strike, the train arrived after midnight.* La estructura contiene tres elementos: 1. *having* marca anterioridad. 2. *been* marca la voz pasiva. 3. El participio final expresa la acción recibida. No confundas: - *Having warned the visitors, the guide left.* El guía avisó. - *Having been warned, the visitors left.* Los visitantes recibieron el aviso. El sujeto implícito debe coincidir con el sujeto de la principal. *Having been delayed by a strike, the passengers waited* es correcto porque los pasajeros sufrieron el retraso. *Having been delayed by a strike, the station waited* sería ilógico si quieres decir que los pasajeros esperaron. ### 5. Past participle: relación pasiva o estado Una participle clause con **past participle** suele reducir una relativa pasiva o describir un estado: - *The route travelled by early traders is now a popular hiking trail.* - *Surrounded by mountains, the village attracts visitors throughout the year.* - *Built to accommodate seasonal workers, the houses are now expensive holiday rentals.* - *The documents collected during the exchange programme were archived.* Las versiones completas serían *the route that was travelled*, *the village which is surrounded* y *the houses that were built*. El participio pasado no significa necesariamente que la acción haya ocurrido inmediatamente antes; puede describir una característica estable. Compara el agente: - *The students travelling through Peru kept a journal.* Los estudiantes viajaban. - *The route travelled by the students was difficult.* La ruta fue recorrida. Un error común es usar -ing para una relación pasiva: *the route travelling by visitors* no es correcto. La ruta no viaja; es recorrida: *the route travelled by visitors*. ### 6. Participles y relativas reducidas Las relativas pueden reducirse en ciertos contextos: - *Tourists who are arriving today should register at the desk.* → *Tourists arriving today should register at the desk.* - *The artefacts that were found near the border were returned.* → *The artefacts found near the border were returned.* - *The researchers who have been invited to the conference will present their work.* → *The researchers invited to the conference will present their work.* La reducción es posible cuando el relativo funciona como sujeto y el verbo admite una forma participial adecuada. No elimines elementos si la relación se vuelve ambigua. En una relativa defining, el participio puede identificar el sustantivo: - *Visitors staying in the historic centre must pay a local tax.* En una non-defining, una cláusula adverbial puede ser más natural: - *The visitors, having completed the survey, returned to their hotel.* La puntuación importa. Una participle clause no restrictiva suele separarse con comas. Una forma restrictiva no lleva comas si identifica el referente. ### 7. Participles de concesión Las estructuras concesivas muestran que una situación no impide el resultado principal. El patrón **adjective/adverb + though + subject + be** es especialmente formal: - *Exhausted though they were, the travellers continued to explore the city.* - *Difficult though the journey was, it changed her understanding of the region.* - *Unfamiliar though the customs seemed, the visitors made an effort to adapt.* La estructura completa sería *Although they were exhausted...*. También puede aparecer **adjective + as + subject + be**: - *Young as he was, he had already lived in three countries.* No confundas esta construcción con una participle clause pura. Es una forma concesiva reducida con el verbo *be* explícito, pero pertenece al mismo repertorio de compactación y registro avanzado. También usamos **-ing** o **past participle** con valor concesivo cuando el contexto lo permite: - *Despite feeling disoriented, she remained culturally sensitive.* - *Though surrounded by unfamiliar customs, he avoided making assumptions.* ### 8. Participles de tiempo Los participios pueden sustituir cláusulas temporales: - *After leaving the airport, the group took a taxi.* - *On arriving in the village, the researchers met the host family.* - *While travelling abroad, she kept a record of local expressions.* - *Before returning home, he completed an intercultural training course.* **On + -ing** expresa una acción inmediatamente posterior o relacionada con el momento de llegar, ver o descubrir algo: - *On arriving in Tokyo, she felt both excited and apprehensive.* Con *after* y *before*, el sujeto debe ser el mismo en ambas partes: - Correcto: *After visiting the museum, the tourists had lunch.* - Incorrecto: *After visiting the museum, the rain began.* La lluvia no visitó el museo. Si los sujetos son diferentes, utiliza una cláusula completa: - *After the tourists visited the museum, the rain began.* ### 9. Participles de causa y resultado Una participle clause puede explicar por qué ocurre algo: - *Having misunderstood the instructions, the visitors missed the meeting point.* - *Feeling unwell, she returned to the hotel.* - *Unfamiliar with the local transport system, they hired a guide.* También puede presentar una consecuencia: - *The airline cancelled the flight, leaving hundreds of passengers stranded.* - *The route was closed, forcing the group to change its itinerary.* La diferencia semántica suele depender del orden. Al principio, la cláusula normalmente explica el contexto o la causa. Después de la principal, un participio puede introducir un resultado. Para que la consecuencia sea clara, usa verbos como *leaving, forcing, making, allowing*. ### 10. Dangling modifiers Un **dangling modifier** aparece cuando el sujeto implícito del participio no coincide con el sujeto de la principal: - Incorrecto: *Having travelled for twelve hours, the hotel looked inviting.* - Correcto: *Having travelled for twelve hours, the travellers found the hotel inviting.* En la frase incorrecta, parece que el hotel ha viajado. El problema no es solo estilístico; altera la lógica de la oración. Otros ejemplos: - Incorrecto: *Walking through the market, the smells became overwhelming.* - Correcto: *Walking through the market, I found the smells overwhelming.* - Incorrecto: *Having been delayed, the passengers missed the connection.* Correcto, porque los pasajeros sufrieron el retraso. - Incorrecto para el significado pretendido: *Having been delayed, the airport apologised.* El aeropuerto no fue necesariamente retrasado. Para corregir un dangling modifier puedes cambiar el sujeto principal, hacer explícito el sujeto del participio o utilizar una cláusula completa: - *Because the flight was delayed, the passengers missed the connection.* ### 11. Vocabulario de viajes e intercambio cultural - **cultural conditioning:** valores y supuestos adquiridos mediante educación y entorno. - **acculturation:** adopción gradual de elementos de otra cultura conservando parte de la propia. - **assimilation:** integración en otra cultura que puede implicar perder rasgos de origen. - **integration:** participación en la sociedad anfitriona sin borrar necesariamente la identidad propia. - **cultural shock:** desorientación ante normas, valores y prácticas nuevas. - **reverse culture shock:** dificultad emocional al regresar al propio país después de vivir fuera. - **culturally sensitive:** consciente y respetuoso con diferencias culturales. - **host community:** comunidad que recibe a visitantes o residentes extranjeros. - **overtourism:** exceso de visitantes que un destino no puede gestionar sosteniblemente. - **visitor cap:** límite al número de visitantes. - **short-term rental:** alquiler de corta duración. - **travel advisory:** recomendación o aviso oficial para viajeros. - **sustainable tourism:** turismo compatible con el bienestar local y la conservación. - **heritage site:** lugar de importancia histórica o cultural. - **paternalistic:** que asume saber qué es mejor para otros sin consultarles. - **agency:** capacidad de una comunidad o persona para tomar decisiones propias. - **voluntourism:** viaje que combina turismo y trabajo voluntario. - **intercultural competence:** capacidad de interactuar eficazmente entre culturas. - **local customs:** costumbres locales. - **cultural appropriation:** adopción de elementos culturales ajenos sin comprenderlos o respetar su contexto. Colocaciones útiles son **respect local customs**, **support host communities**, **manage visitor numbers**, **preserve cultural heritage**, **promote sustainable tourism**, **experience culture shock**, **develop intercultural competence**, **challenge cultural assumptions**, **broaden one’s perspective**, **avoid paternalistic behaviour**, **retain one’s identity** y **adapt to a host culture**. ### 12. Intercambio cultural con precisión Viajar no produce automáticamente comprensión intercultural. Una persona puede visitar muchos países y mantener las mismas ideas simplistas. Las participle clauses ayudan a presentar las condiciones del intercambio: - *Having listened to local residents, the volunteers revised their project.* - *Unfamiliar with the community’s priorities, they initially proposed an unsuitable solution.* - *Although welcomed by the host organisation, the visitors had to reconsider their assumptions.* La precisión léxica también importa. **Cultural sensitivity** no significa aceptar todas las prácticas sin reflexión; significa reconocer que los comportamientos tienen contextos y evitar juzgarlos desde una única norma. **Acculturation** no es sinónimo exacto de **assimilation**: la primera puede implicar intercambio y conservación de la identidad; la segunda suele sugerir una adaptación más completa. ### 13. Cómo elegir entre una cláusula completa y un participio Usa una participle clause cuando: - El sujeto es el mismo y evidente. - La relación temporal o causal es fácil de interpretar. - Quieres un estilo compacto y formal. - El texto ya ha establecido el contexto. Prefiere una cláusula completa cuando: - Los sujetos son diferentes. - La relación lógica podría interpretarse de dos maneras. - El participio crea una frase demasiado larga. - El lector necesita saber exactamente quién realizó la acción. Compara: - Compacta: *Having completed the survey, the researchers analysed the responses.* - Explícita: *After the researchers had completed the survey, they analysed the responses.* Las dos son correctas. La segunda es preferible si ya hay varios sujetos o si el orden temporal puede perderse. ### 14. Errores frecuentes - *Having been never abroad, she felt nervous.* → **Having never been abroad, she felt nervous.** - *Travelled extensively, he understands local customs.* → **Having travelled extensively, he understands local customs.** - *The route travelling by tourists is crowded.* → **The route travelled by tourists is crowded.** - *After visiting the museum, the rain started.* → **After the tourists visited the museum, the rain started.** - *Exhausted though were they, they continued.* → **Exhausted though they were, they continued.** - *Having lost the passport, the hotel helped her.* → **Having lost her passport, she asked the hotel for help.** - *The visitors were culturally sensitive, despite they misunderstood the ceremony.* → **Although they misunderstood the ceremony...** o **Despite misunderstanding the ceremony...** - *Having arrived, the luggage was collected.* → Si los viajeros llegaron: **Having arrived, the travellers collected their luggage.** ## Parte II — Ejercicios con soluciones ### Ejercicio 1 — Present participle Combina cada par con una cláusula en **-ing**. 1. He walked through the market. He noticed the contrast between old and new shops. 2. She lived abroad for a year. She developed a deeper appreciation of her own culture. 3. The guide looked at the map. She realised the group was lost.
Ver solución 1. **Walking through the market, he noticed the contrast between old and new shops.** 2. **Living abroad for a year, she developed a deeper appreciation of her own culture.** 3. **Looking at the map, the guide realised the group was lost.**
### Ejercicio 2 — Perfect participle Completa con **having + participio**. 1. ___ (travel) extensively, he understood the cultural nuances. 2. ___ (read) the travel advisory, the family postponed the trip. 3. ___ never ___ (experience) reverse culture shock, she underestimated the difficulty of returning home.
Ver solución 1. **Having travelled**. 2. **Having read**. 3. **Having never experienced**. La acción del participio es anterior a la acción principal.
### Ejercicio 3 — Pasiva Elige la forma correcta. 1. ___ (Having warned / Having been warned) about overtourism, the visitors avoided the busiest district. 2. ___ (Having invited / Having been invited) by the host community, the researchers attended the ceremony. 3. ___ (Having delayed / Having been delayed) by a strike, the train arrived after midnight.
Ver solución 1. **Having been warned**; 2. **Having been invited**; 3. **Having been delayed**. En los tres casos, el sujeto recibe la acción.
### Ejercicio 4 — Participio pasado o -ing Completa con **travelling** o **travelled**. 1. The students ___ through Peru kept a journal. 2. The route ___ by early traders is now a hiking trail. 3. Visitors ___ today should register at the desk. 4. The route ___ by visitors is difficult in winter.
Ver solución 1. **travelling** — los estudiantes realizan la acción. 2. **travelled** — la ruta recibe la acción. 3. **arriving** sería la forma natural en esta frase: *Visitors arriving today...*. 4. **travelled** — la ruta es recorrida.
### Ejercicio 5 — Concesión Reescribe con **adjective + though + subject + be**. 1. Although the travellers were exhausted, they continued. 2. Although the journey was difficult, it changed her perspective. 3. Although the customs seemed unfamiliar, the visitors adapted.
Ver solución 1. **Exhausted though the travellers were, they continued.** 2. **Difficult though the journey was, it changed her perspective.** 3. **Unfamiliar though the customs seemed, the visitors adapted.**
### Ejercicio 6 — Tiempo Combina con una participle clause. 1. After she arrived in Tokyo, she felt excited. 2. While he travelled abroad, he kept a language journal. 3. Before they returned home, they completed the survey.
Ver solución 1. **On arriving in Tokyo, she felt excited.** 2. **While travelling abroad, he kept a language journal.** 3. **Before returning home, they completed the survey.**
### Ejercicio 7 — Causa o resultado Indica si la cláusula expresa causa o resultado. 1. *Having misunderstood the instructions, the visitors missed the meeting point.* 2. *The airline cancelled the flight, leaving hundreds of passengers stranded.* 3. *Feeling unwell, she returned to the hotel.* 4. *The route was closed, forcing the group to change its itinerary.*
Ver solución 1. **Causa**: el malentendido explica por qué perdieron el punto de encuentro. 2. **Resultado**: los pasajeros quedaron varados como consecuencia. 3. **Causa**: sentirse mal explica el regreso. 4. **Resultado**: el cierre provocó un cambio de itinerario.
### Ejercicio 8 — Dangling modifiers Corrige las frases ilógicas. 1. *Having travelled for twelve hours, the hotel looked inviting.* 2. *Walking through the market, the smells became overwhelming.* 3. *After visiting the museum, the rain began.*
Ver solución 1. **Having travelled for twelve hours, the travellers found the hotel inviting.** 2. **Walking through the market, I found the smells overwhelming.** 3. **After the tourists visited the museum, the rain began.** En las versiones originales, el sujeto principal no podía realizar la acción del participio.
### Ejercicio 9 — Vocabulario cultural Completa con **acculturation, assimilation, overtourism, reverse culture shock** o **cultural conditioning**. 1. The gradual adoption of elements of a host culture while retaining aspects of one’s own is ___ . 2. The complete adaptation to another culture, sometimes involving loss of the original identity, is ___ . 3. The difficulty of returning home after years abroad is ___ . 4. Excessive visitor numbers that a destination cannot manage sustainably constitute ___ . 5. Unconscious values absorbed through upbringing are part of ___ .
Ver solución 1. **acculturation**; 2. **assimilation**; 3. **reverse culture shock**; 4. **overtourism**; 5. **cultural conditioning**.
### Ejercicio 10 — Reading Lee el texto y responde. > Having lived in Singapore for five years, Elena expected returning to her home country to feel simple. Instead, she experienced reverse culture shock. Walking through the streets of her old neighbourhood, she noticed that many shops had disappeared and that social conversations seemed less open than she remembered. Although welcomed by her family, she felt that she no longer fitted easily into the routines she had left behind. Her experience taught her that acculturation is not a one-way process: adapting to a host culture can change the expectations with which a person later views home. Elena now advises returning residents to allow themselves time to adjust rather than assuming that familiarity will remove every difficulty. 1. How long had Elena lived in Singapore? 2. What did she experience on returning? 3. What had changed in her neighbourhood? 4. What did she learn about acculturation? 5. What advice does she give returning residents?
Ver solución 1. **Five years.** 2. **Reverse culture shock.** 3. **Many shops had disappeared and conversations seemed less open.** 4. **That acculturation can change a person’s expectations of home; it is not one-way.** 5. **They should allow themselves time to adjust rather than assuming familiarity will remove every difficulty.**
### Ejercicio 11 — Listening guiado Guion: “Having been warned about overtourism, the visitors avoided the old town at midday. Travelling by train instead, they reached a smaller village, where they were welcomed by a host community that had developed sustainable tourism projects. Exhausted though they were after the journey, they attended a local workshop.” Identifica una pasiva perfecta, una cláusula en -ing y una concesión.
Ver solución Pasiva perfecta: **Having been warned about overtourism**. Cláusula en -ing: **Travelling by train instead**. Concesión: **Exhausted though they were after the journey**.
### Ejercicio 12 — Transformación Reescribe con una participle clause. 1. Because she was unfamiliar with local customs, she asked a guide for advice. 2. After the researchers had completed the interviews, they analysed the responses. 3. Although he was surrounded by unfamiliar languages, he remained calm.
Ver solución 1. **Unfamiliar with local customs, she asked a guide for advice.** 2. **Having completed the interviews, the researchers analysed the responses.** 3. **Though surrounded by unfamiliar languages, he remained calm.**
### Ejercicio 13 — Registro y precisión Reescribe de forma más formal: *The volunteers went to the village and then realised that their project was not useful.*
Modelo **Having consulted the host community, the volunteers realised that their initial project was not sufficiently relevant to local priorities.** La versión sustituye una secuencia simple por un participio perfecto y añade vocabulario más preciso.
### Ejercicio 14 — Writing Escribe 150–180 palabras sobre: **How can travellers avoid behaving paternalistically?** Incluye una participle clause de anterioridad, una pasiva, una concesión y vocabulario de intercambio cultural.
Modelo Having learned about the host community before travelling, visitors are more likely to recognise local priorities and avoid imposing their own solutions. The people living in the destination should be consulted before volunteer projects are designed, and their agency must be respected throughout the process. Welcomed by a community does not mean that every activity is automatically beneficial; the impact should be evaluated rather than assumed. Although travellers may arrive with good intentions, they can still behave paternalistically if they believe that their education or resources make them better qualified to decide what others need. Culturally sensitive visitors should therefore listen before proposing, support locally led initiatives and learn enough about local customs to avoid causing unnecessary offence. Having been invited to contribute, they should remain accountable to the host organisation and accept criticism when a project does not work. Exchange becomes meaningful when both sides share knowledge and make decisions, rather than when one side treats the other as a passive recipient of help.
### Ejercicio 15 — Speaking Habla durante un minuto sobre una experiencia de intercambio cultural. Usa **Having travelled**, **while living**, **though**, **culturally sensitive** y **host community**.
Pista y modelo **Having travelled through several countries, I have learned that cultural sensitivity requires more than memorising customs. While living with a host community, I had to ask questions and reconsider assumptions. Though some habits initially seemed unfamiliar, I gradually understood their context. The experience made me more careful about describing other cultures in simple terms.**
### Ejercicio 16 — Traducción controlada Traduce al inglés. 1. Habiendo viajado mucho, comprendía los matices culturales. 2. Aunque estaban agotados, los viajeros continuaron explorando la ciudad. 3. Rodeada de montañas, la aldea atrae visitantes todo el año.
Ver solución 1. **Having travelled extensively, he understood the cultural nuances.** 2. **Exhausted though they were, the travellers continued exploring the city.** 3. **Surrounded by mountains, the village attracts visitors all year round.**
### Ejercicio 17 — Edición avanzada Corrige el párrafo. > Having been never abroad, she was nervous. Walking through the airport, the announcements seemed confusing. After arriving, the luggage was collected by the guide. Exhausted though were the travellers, they attended the ceremony.
Ver solución **Having never been abroad, she was nervous. Walking through the airport, she found the announcements confusing. After arriving, the travellers collected their luggage from the guide. Exhausted though the travellers were, they attended the ceremony.** Se corrige la posición de *never*, el dangling modifier, el sujeto implícito de *arriving* y el orden de la concesión.
### Ejercicio 18 — Mini-test final Completa el texto. > ___ (live) abroad for a year, Maya developed greater cultural sensitivity. ___ (arrive) in the host country, she initially misunderstood several customs. ___ though she was, she continued asking respectful questions. The project ___ (design) by the host community helped her understand that acculturation is a mutual process.
Ver solución **Having lived; On arriving; Uncertain though; designed.** El texto completo es: **Having lived abroad for a year, Maya developed greater cultural sensitivity. On arriving in the host country, she initially misunderstood several customs. Uncertain though she was, she continued asking respectful questions. The project designed by the host community helped her understand that acculturation is a mutual process.**
## Resumen de la unidad Usa **-ing** para acciones simultáneas o causas cuando el sujeto realiza la acción. Usa **having + participio** para marcar que una acción terminó antes de la principal. Usa **having been + participio** cuando el sujeto recibe una acción anterior y un participio pasado para relaciones pasivas o estados. Las estructuras concesivas como **exhausted though they were** y **difficult though the journey was** aportan un registro formal y compacto. Antes de reducir una cláusula, comprueba que el sujeto implícito sea el mismo que el sujeto de la oración principal. Si no coincide, escribe una cláusula completa. El vocabulario también exige precisión: **acculturation** no es exactamente **assimilation**, **reverse culture shock** no es simple jet lag y **culturally sensitive** implica respeto contextual, no una colección de reglas superficiales. Cuando combines estas distinciones con colocaciones como *support host communities*, *preserve cultural heritage* y *develop intercultural competence*, podrás hablar de viajes e intercambio cultural con la riqueza y el control propios del C1.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es el subjuntivo mandativo en inglés?
faqs.answer: Es la forma base del verbo después de expresiones de recomendación, exigencia o importancia: It is essential that every chef know the ingredients’ provenance.

faqs.question: ¿Se dice recommend that he attend o attends?
faqs.answer: En el subjuntivo mandativo formal se usa la forma base: recommend that he attend. También existe recommend that he should attend.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma el subjuntivo pasivo?
faqs.answer: Se forma con be más participio: The standards require that inspections be carried out quarterly.

faqs.question: ¿La Unidad 14 incluye ejercicios resueltos?
faqs.answer: Sí. Incluye práctica de subjuntivo, vocabulario gastronómico, reading, listening, writing y speaking con respuestas y modelos.

content:
# Unidad 14 C1: subjuntivo, gastronomía y cultura En inglés formal, las recomendaciones, exigencias y condiciones importantes se pueden expresar con una estructura muy precisa: **that + sujeto + forma base del verbo**. Esta forma se conoce como **mandative subjunctive** o subjuntivo mandativo. - *The committee recommended that the standards be revised.* - *It is essential that every chef know the provenance of the ingredients.* - *The regulation requires that inspections be carried out quarterly.* La forma puede parecer sencilla porque el verbo no lleva `-s` en tercera persona y `be` aparece igual con todos los sujetos. Precisamente por eso contrasta con el inglés cotidiano, donde también son frecuentes estructuras con *should* o infinitivo. La Unidad 14 enseña a elegir el patrón según el registro y el verbo que lo introduce. El tema es **Food, Gastronomy and Culture**. La comida no es solo nutrición: transmite identidad, memoria, pertenencia y, en ocasiones, resistencia cultural. La unidad combina la gramática formal con vocabulario como *culinary identity, cultural heritage, food insecurity, culinary appropriation, provenance, sustainability* y *food waste*. También practica la escritura de reseñas, donde hay que describir sabor, textura, técnica y experiencia sin recurrir a adjetivos vagos. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 14 C1](/curso-c1/unit-14)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 13 C1: participle clauses y viajes](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-13-participle-clauses-viajes)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 15 C1: deporte y rendimiento](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-15-enfasis-deporte)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. El subjuntivo mandativo El subjuntivo mandativo aparece cuando una persona o institución recomienda, exige, solicita o considera necesario que otra persona haga algo. Su estructura es: > **verb/adjective + that + subject + base verb** - *The chef recommended that the restaurant source its vegetables locally.* - *The critic suggested that the menu include more seasonal dishes.* - *It is vital that diners understand the ingredients.* La forma base es igual para todas las personas: - *I recommend that he attend the workshop.* - *I recommend that she attend the workshop.* - *I recommend that they attend the workshop.* No añadimos `-s` en tercera persona: *I recommend that she attends* puede oírse en variedades que tratan la cláusula como indicativo, pero el subjuntivo formal es **I recommend that she attend**. ### 2. Verbos que introducen el subjuntivo Los verbos más frecuentes son **recommend, suggest, demand, insist, request, require, propose, urge, advise** y **stipulate**. No todos aceptan exactamente los mismos complementos, así que hay que aprender el patrón completo. - *The committee recommended that the standards be revised.* - *The inspector demanded that the kitchen close temporarily.* - *The law requires that food labels contain allergen information.* - *The chef insisted that the recipe remain unchanged.* - *The association proposed that restaurants reduce food waste.* - *The guide urged that visitors respect local customs.* Con **recommend, suggest, propose** también usamos **-ing** sin sujeto interno: - *The committee recommended revising the standards.* - *The chef suggested using seasonal ingredients.* - *The report proposed reducing packaging.* Si queremos mencionar quién debe realizar la acción, usamos *that + subject + base verb*: - *The committee recommended that restaurants revise the standards.* - *The chef suggested that the kitchen use seasonal ingredients.* No digas normalmente *suggest someone to do*. Usa *suggest that someone do* o *suggest doing*. ### 3. Adjetivos de importancia y necesidad El subjuntivo también aparece después de adjetivos como **essential, vital, important, necessary, crucial, imperative, advisable** y **desirable**: - *It is essential that every chef know the provenance of the ingredients.* - *It is vital that food be stored at the correct temperature.* - *It is important that restaurants disclose allergens clearly.* - *It is imperative that inspectors remain independent.* - *It is advisable that diners book in advance.* La estructura es: > **It + be + adjective + that + subject + base verb** El sujeto real aparece después de *that*. También podemos usar un infinitivo: - *It is essential to disclose allergens.* - *It is important for restaurants to train their staff.* La diferencia es que **for + object + to-infinitive** hace explícito el sujeto del infinitivo, mientras que el subjuntivo utiliza una cláusula con *that*. ### 4. El verbo be en subjuntivo El ejemplo más visible es **be**, que no cambia según el sujeto: - *It is essential that the dish be served immediately.* - *It is essential that the dishes be served immediately.* - *The regulation requires that the kitchen be inspected.* - *The regulations require that the kitchens be inspected.* No usamos *is* o *are* dentro de esta estructura formal: - Subjuntivo: *The rule requires that the kitchen be clean.* - Indicativo descriptivo: *The rule requires that the kitchen is clean.* La segunda puede aparecer en el habla y en algunas variedades, pero la primera es el patrón mandativo estándar y más claro en escritura formal. ### 5. Subjuntivo pasivo Para expresar que una acción debe ser realizada sobre un objeto, usamos **be + past participle**: - *The regulation requires that all inspections be carried out quarterly.* - *The committee recommended that the standards be revised immediately.* - *It is vital that ingredients be stored safely.* - *The law demands that allergens be listed on the menu.* La forma pasiva contiene el mismo `be` base para singular y plural. No añadas `-s` ni cambies a *are* dentro del subjuntivo: - Correcto: *It is essential that the labels be checked.* - Incorrecto para este patrón: *It is essential that the labels are checked.* La forma con *should* también es posible: - *It is essential that the labels should be checked.* El subjuntivo base suele ser más conciso y formal, especialmente en normas, contratos, informes y recomendaciones profesionales. ### 6. Negación La negación se forma con **not + base verb**: - *The chef insisted that the recipe not be changed.* - *It is important that customers not confuse tradition with authenticity.* - *The inspector demanded that the restaurant not reopen until repairs were complete.* En inglés británico también es frecuente **should not**: - *The chef insisted that the recipe should not be changed.* No uses *does not* o *did not* dentro del subjuntivo mandativo: - Correcto: *The report recommends that restaurants not waste food.* - No es el patrón: *The report recommends that restaurants do not waste food.* La segunda puede funcionar como una cláusula indicativa en algunos contextos, pero cambia el registro y la estructura. ### 7. Should como alternativa El patrón **that + subject + should + base verb** expresa la misma recomendación o necesidad en muchas variedades, especialmente en inglés británico: - *The committee recommended that the standards should be revised.* - *It is essential that every chef should know the provenance of ingredients.* - *The inspector demanded that the kitchen should close.* Compara: - **Mandative subjunctive:** *They demanded that the restaurant close.* - **Should construction:** *They demanded that the restaurant should close.* Ambas son gramaticales. La forma base es más compacta y aparece con frecuencia en inglés formal internacional; *should* hace visible la idea de recomendación u obligación. No confundas este *should* con el consejo independiente *The restaurant should close*, que no contiene *that*. ### 8. Verbo principal frente a cláusula mandativa El verbo que introduce la cláusula determina el patrón: - **recommend that + subject + base:** *They recommended that he attend.* - **recommend + -ing:** *They recommended attending.* - **advise + object + to-infinitive:** *They advised him to attend.* - **suggest that + subject + base:** *They suggested that he attend.* - **suggest + -ing:** *They suggested attending.* - **urge + object + to-infinitive:** *They urged him to attend.* - **insist that + subject + base:** *They insisted that he attend.* - **insist on + -ing:** *They insisted on attending.* Los errores nacen de traducir literalmente “recomendar que” o “sugerir a alguien que”. Aprende el marco completo, no solo el verbo. - Incorrecto: *The chef suggested the staff to change the menu.* - Correcto: *The chef suggested that the staff change the menu.* - Correcto: *The chef suggested changing the menu.* - Correcto con otro verbo: *The chef advised the staff to change the menu.* ### 9. Formalidad y elección estilística El subjuntivo mandativo es frecuente en: - Reglamentos: *The regulation requires that all kitchens be inspected.* - Propuestas: *We recommend that the council provide support to local producers.* - Informes: *The review suggests that food labels include clearer information.* - Comunicados: *It is imperative that the organisation remain transparent.* - Lenguaje legal: *The agreement stipulates that suppliers comply with safety standards.* En una conversación informal, es posible escuchar *The manager said that everyone should arrive early*. Esta forma es natural y no incorrecta. La elección depende del propósito. C1 implica poder pasar de una forma a otra con control: - Formal y concisa: *The manager requested that everyone arrive early.* - Neutral: *The manager asked everyone to arrive early.* - Conversacional: *The manager said everyone should arrive early.* ### 10. Gastronomía como cultura La comida puede describirse con precisión cultural y sensorial. **Cuisine** se refiere a un estilo o tradición culinaria; **dish** es un plato concreto; **recipe** son instrucciones; **ingredient** es un componente; **cuisine** no significa simplemente “comida”. - *The region’s cuisine reflects its climate and trading history.* - *The dish combines a smoky broth with pickled vegetables.* - *The recipe has been passed down through several generations.* **Culinary identity** describe el estilo distintivo de una persona o comunidad. **Cultural heritage** incluye prácticas, conocimientos y valores transmitidos. **Provenance** indica el origen documentado de un ingrediente o producto. Colocaciones importantes son **preserve culinary heritage**, **pass down a recipe**, **source ingredients locally**, **honour a tradition**, **adapt a recipe**, **marry flavours**, **balance textures**, **showcase seasonal produce**, **develop a culinary identity** y **acknowledge a dish’s origins**. ### 11. Cultura alimentaria y ética **Culinary appropriation** describe la adopción de prácticas o platos de otra cultura sin reconocer su origen, especialmente cuando existe una relación desigual de poder. No toda influencia culinaria es apropiación: el contexto, el reconocimiento, la compensación y la relación con la comunidad importan. - *The restaurant acknowledged the dish’s origins and worked with local cooks.* - *The debate concerns whether commercial success has been shared fairly.* - *It is important that culinary traditions not be detached from their history.* **Food insecurity** es el acceso poco fiable a alimentos suficientes, nutritivos y asequibles. Puede coexistir con **food waste** en países ricos, lo que muestra problemas de distribución, no necesariamente una falta absoluta de producción. - *The report recommends that supermarkets donate surplus food.* - *It is vital that food waste be reduced throughout the supply chain.* ### 12. Sabor, textura y técnica Una reseña C1 evita repetir *good, nice, tasty* y selecciona palabras según la experiencia: - **flavour:** sabor general o combinación de sabores. - **taste:** percepción gustativa o sabor concreto. - **aroma:** olor agradable o característico. - **texture:** sensación física, como *silky, crisp, chewy, tender*. - **aftertaste:** sabor que permanece. - **seasoning:** uso de sal, especias y otros elementos. - **presentation:** forma de servir y disponer el plato. - **technique:** procedimiento culinario. - **mouthfeel:** sensación del alimento en la boca. Adjetivos útiles son **subtle, intense, earthy, smoky, tangy, bitter, delicate, rich, refined, balanced, overpowered, under-seasoned, impeccably presented** y **technically precise**. - *The broth had a subtle smoky aroma and a remarkably clean aftertaste.* - *The acidity cut through the richness of the sauce.* - *The dish was technically precise, although its presentation felt overworked.* ### 13. Review writing Una reseña efectiva suele incluir: 1. Contexto: lugar, ocasión y tipo de experiencia. 2. Descripción: ingredientes, técnica, textura y presentación. 3. Evaluación: fortalezas y limitaciones concretas. 4. Veredicto: para quién sería adecuada la experiencia. La nominalisation puede ayudar: *the balance of flavours, the precision of the presentation, the originality of the pairing*. Pero alterna sustantivos y verbos para no crear una prosa rígida. Usa lenguaje evaluativo graduado: - **Muy positivo:** *exceptional, outstanding, accomplished, memorable*. - **Positivo con matiz:** *promising, accomplished, largely successful, well judged*. - **Crítico pero profesional:** *uneven, overcomplicated, underdeveloped, insufficiently balanced*. Evita convertir una preferencia personal en hecho universal. *I found the dish too salty* es más responsable que *The dish was objectively bad*. ### 14. Errores frecuentes - *The committee recommended that the standards are revised.* → **recommended that the standards be revised**. - *It is essential that every chef knows the provenance.* → En subjuntivo formal: **that every chef know**. - *The chef suggested the staff to change the recipe.* → **suggested that the staff change** o **suggested changing**. - *The inspector demanded the kitchen to close.* → **demanded that the kitchen close**. - *The regulation requires that inspections are carried out.* → **requires that inspections be carried out**. - *The recipe was passed from generation to generation down.* → **was passed down from generation to generation**. - *The flavours married together nicely.* → **The flavours married well** o **The ingredients complemented each other**. - *Food insecurity means people don’t like the food.* → **Food insecurity means unreliable access to sufficient, nutritious food.** ## Parte II — Ejercicios con soluciones ### Ejercicio 1 — Forma base Completa con la forma correcta del verbo. 1. The committee recommended that the standards ___ (be) revised. 2. It is essential that every chef ___ (know) the ingredients’ provenance. 3. The regulation requires that inspections ___ (be carried out) quarterly. 4. The inspector demanded that the kitchen ___ (close) temporarily.
Ver solución 1. **be**; 2. **know**; 3. **be carried out**; 4. **close**. El subjuntivo mandativo usa la forma base, también con sujetos en tercera persona.
### Ejercicio 2 — Recommend, suggest o advise Elige la opción correcta. 1. The chef recommended that the restaurant (*source / sources*) vegetables locally. 2. The guide suggested (*using / to use*) seasonal ingredients. 3. The inspector advised the staff (*to check / checking*) the temperature. 4. The report suggested that supermarkets (*donate / donates*) surplus food.
Ver solución 1. **source**; 2. **using**; 3. **to check**; 4. **donate**. *Suggest* acepta *-ing* o *that + subject + base*; *advise* acepta objeto + infinitivo.
### Ejercicio 3 — Subjuntivo pasivo Transforma. 1. The law requires restaurants to list allergens. 2. The committee recommended revising the safety standards. 3. It is vital for ingredients to be stored safely.
Ver solución 1. **The law requires that allergens be listed by restaurants.** 2. **The committee recommended that the safety standards be revised.** 3. **It is vital that ingredients be stored safely.**
### Ejercicio 4 — Should como alternativa Reescribe con **should** sin cambiar el significado. 1. It is essential that the labels be checked. 2. The committee insisted that the recipe remain unchanged. 3. The regulation requires that kitchens be inspected.
Ver solución 1. **It is essential that the labels should be checked.** 2. **The committee insisted that the recipe should remain unchanged.** 3. **The regulation requires that kitchens should be inspected.**
### Ejercicio 5 — Negación Completa con **not + verbo**. 1. The chef insisted that the recipe ___ ___ (change). 2. It is important that customers ___ ___ (confuse) tradition with authenticity. 3. The inspector demanded that the restaurant ___ ___ (reopen) before repairs were complete.
Ver solución 1. **not be changed**; 2. **not confuse**; 3. **not reopen**.
### Ejercicio 6 — Patrones de verbos Corrige las frases. 1. *The chef suggested the staff to change the menu.* 2. *The committee recommended to reduce food waste.* 3. *The inspector demanded the restaurant to close.* 4. *The association advised that diners to book early.*
Ver solución 1. **The chef suggested that the staff change the menu** o **suggested changing the menu**. 2. **The committee recommended reducing food waste** o **recommended that restaurants reduce food waste**. 3. **The inspector demanded that the restaurant close.** 4. **The association advised diners to book early** o **advised that diners book early**.
### Ejercicio 7 — Vocabulario culinario Completa con **culinary identity, provenance, cultural heritage, food insecurity** o **food waste**. 1. The documented origin of an ingredient is its ___ . 2. Recipes and rituals passed between generations form part of ___ . 3. A chef’s distinctive approach to flavour and technique is their ___ . 4. Unreliable access to sufficient nutritious food is ___ . 5. Discarded edible food contributes to ___ .
Ver solución 1. **provenance**; 2. **cultural heritage**; 3. **culinary identity**; 4. **food insecurity**; 5. **food waste**.
### Ejercicio 8 — Colocaciones Elige el verbo correcto: **preserve, source, marry, showcase** o **balance**. 1. ___ culinary heritage 2. ___ ingredients locally 3. ___ flavours 4. ___ seasonal produce 5. ___ textures
Ver solución 1. **preserve culinary heritage**; 2. **source ingredients locally**; 3. **marry flavours**; 4. **showcase seasonal produce**; 5. **balance textures**.
### Ejercicio 9 — Reading Lee el texto y responde. > The restaurant’s new menu draws on recipes that have been passed down through three generations. The chef insists that the origins of each dish be acknowledged, particularly when ingredients or techniques come from marginalised communities. She recommends that the restaurant source produce from small local farms and proposes that surplus food be donated to community kitchens. Critics have praised the menu’s culinary identity, although some argue that the tasting format makes the food inaccessible to lower-income diners. The chef concedes that cultural heritage should not become a luxury product and says that the restaurant will introduce a more affordable lunch menu. 1. How many generations have passed down the recipes? 2. What does the chef insist on? 3. What does she recommend regarding produce? 4. What criticism has the menu received? 5. What response does the chef propose?
Ver solución 1. **Three generations.** 2. **That the origins of each dish be acknowledged.** 3. **That the restaurant source produce from small local farms.** 4. **The tasting format may be inaccessible to lower-income diners.** 5. **Introducing a more affordable lunch menu.**
### Ejercicio 10 — Listening guiado Guion: “The food anthropologist argues that what we eat is a performance of identity. She recommends that culinary traditions be studied in their social context and insists that researchers not treat recipes as isolated objects. Although food can create a sense of belonging, the speaker warns that commercial success should not obscure questions of power and acknowledgement.” Identifica dos estructuras de subjuntivo, una concesión y el vocabulario ético principal.
Ver solución Subjuntivos: **recommends that culinary traditions be studied** e **insists that researchers not treat**. Concesión: **Although food can create a sense of belonging**. Vocabulario ético: **identity, social context, belonging, power, acknowledgement**.
### Ejercicio 11 — Review vocabulary Sustituye los adjetivos vagos por una opción precisa: **subtle, smoky, tangy, silky, under-seasoned**. 1. The sauce had a slightly sour, lively flavour. 2. The broth had a delicate flavour that did not dominate. 3. The soup tasted of wood and gentle fire. 4. The purée was smooth and soft in the mouth. 5. The dish lacked sufficient salt and seasoning.
Ver solución 1. **tangy**; 2. **subtle**; 3. **smoky**; 4. **silky**; 5. **under-seasoned**.
### Ejercicio 12 — Registro de reseña Reescribe de forma profesional: *The food was really good and the chef did cool things with old recipes.*
Modelo **The meal was largely successful, and the chef demonstrated considerable skill in adapting traditional recipes without losing their cultural character.**
### Ejercicio 13 — Corrección gramatical Corrige el párrafo. > It is essential that every restaurant lists allergens clearly. The committee recommended that labels are revised, and the chef suggested the staff to attend a workshop. Despite the training was useful, several employees needed further practice.
Ver solución **It is essential that every restaurant list allergens clearly. The committee recommended that labels be revised, and the chef suggested that the staff attend a workshop. Although the training was useful, several employees needed further practice.**
### Ejercicio 14 — Causa y evaluación Completa con una recomendación formal. The menu relies on imported ingredients. It is important that the restaurant ___ (source) more produce locally, and the chef recommends that suppliers ___ (be) selected according to transparent criteria.
Ver solución **source; be**. La versión completa es: **It is important that the restaurant source more produce locally, and the chef recommends that suppliers be selected according to transparent criteria.**
### Ejercicio 15 — Reading crítico Explica en 70–90 palabras por qué esta afirmación necesita matiz: *Cooking another culture’s food is always cultural appropriation.*
Modelo The statement is too absolute because the ethical question depends on context, power and acknowledgement. Cooking another culture’s food can form part of respectful exchange when the origins are recognised, local communities are involved and benefits are shared fairly. It may become appropriation when a business removes a dish from its history, claims ownership or profits while the originating community is ignored. The same recipe can therefore have different implications in different settings.
### Ejercicio 16 — Writing Escribe 150–180 palabras sobre: **How can restaurants preserve culinary heritage while remaining innovative?** Incluye tres estructuras de subjuntivo, dos colocaciones gastronómicas y una concesión.
Modelo It is essential that restaurants acknowledge the origins of the dishes they serve. Innovation can be valuable, but it should not detach culinary heritage from the communities that created it. I recommend that chefs work with local cooks and insist that traditional techniques be explained rather than presented as anonymous discoveries. Restaurants should also source ingredients responsibly and ensure that commercial benefits are shared where appropriate. Although recipes inevitably change over time, a new interpretation can still respect the memory and social meaning of the original dish. It is important that menus provide enough context for diners to understand what has been adapted and why. The committee should require that cultural references be checked carefully, particularly when a restaurant uses a tradition from a marginalised community. In this way, chefs can marry innovation with acknowledgement instead of treating heritage as a decorative resource. Creativity is strongest when it is informed by respect, research and a willingness to credit the people behind the food.
### Ejercicio 17 — Speaking Habla durante un minuto sobre una reseña de restaurante. Usa **I recommend that**, **it is essential that**, **although** y vocabulario de sabor y textura.
Pista y modelo **I recommend that the restaurant revise the balance of its tasting menu. Although the broth had a subtle smoky aroma and the purée was silky, it is essential that the seasoning be adjusted in the main course. I also recommend that the chef provide more context about the dish’s provenance. The technique was precise, but the presentation seemed overcomplicated.**
### Ejercicio 18 — Mini-test final Completa el texto. > The inspector requires that all ingredients ___ (be) labelled and that allergens ___ (list) clearly. The chef recommends that the kitchen ___ (source) local produce, although she insists that the budget ___ not ___ (increase) unnecessarily. The restaurant’s new menu ___ (marry) traditional techniques with contemporary presentation.
Ver solución **be; be listed; source; not be increased; marries.** Las tres primeras formas están en subjuntivo mandativo; la cuarta es un subjuntivo pasivo negativo; *marries* pertenece a la oración principal y por eso sí lleva `-s`.
### Ejercicio 19 — Revisión de patrones Reescribe cada recomendación usando el patrón indicado y explica qué cambia. 1. **recommend that + subject + base:** The chef wants the supplier to document the provenance. 2. **recommend + -ing:** The critic thinks restaurants should reduce packaging. 3. **advise + object + to-infinitive:** The inspector tells the manager to train the staff. 4. **insist that + subject + base:** The association wants menus to acknowledge culinary heritage.
Ver solución 1. **The chef recommends that the supplier document the provenance.** 2. **The critic recommends reducing packaging.** 3. **The inspector advises the manager to train the staff.** 4. **The association insists that menus acknowledge culinary heritage.** Las cuatro frases expresan una recomendación o exigencia, pero cada verbo selecciona un patrón diferente. *Recommend* puede llevar una cláusula mandativa o gerundio; *advise* necesita normalmente un objeto antes del infinitivo; *insist* combina bien con *that + subject + base* o con *on + -ing*. Esta diferencia de complementación es esencial en escritura C1: no basta con traducir “recomendar” o “aconsejar” palabra por palabra.
## Resumen de la unidad El subjuntivo mandativo se forma con **that + sujeto + verbo base** después de recomendaciones, exigencias y expresiones de importancia: *recommend that he attend*, *require that the labels be checked*, *it is essential that chefs know the provenance*. La forma no lleva `-s` en tercera persona y usa **be** igual en singular y plural. También puedes usar **should + base**, una estructura frecuente en inglés británico, o cambiar el patrón: *recommend doing*, *advise someone to do*, *suggest that someone do* y *urge someone to do*. No traduzcas literalmente; aprende qué complemento acepta cada verbo. En gastronomía, combina la gramática con colocaciones precisas como *preserve culinary heritage*, *source ingredients locally*, *marry flavours* y *acknowledge a dish’s origins*. Una reseña C1 no se limita a decir que algo está “bueno”: describe técnica, aroma, textura, presentación y contexto cultural, y distingue una preferencia personal de una conclusión general.
