faqs.question: ¿Qué estructuras se estudian en la Unidad 6 C1?
faqs.answer: La unidad trabaja estructuras impersonales con it, conectores de causa y resultado y modales avanzados para hablar de trabajo y economía con registro formal.

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo se usa it is widely argued that?
faqs.answer: Se usa para presentar una opinión o conclusión atribuida de forma impersonal, especialmente en informes, artículos y debates académicos.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre hence y owing to?
faqs.answer: Hence introduce normalmente un resultado o consecuencia; owing to introduce una causa y va seguido de un sustantivo o grupo nominal.

faqs.question: ¿La Unidad 6 incluye ejercicios resueltos?
faqs.answer: Sí. Incluye práctica de estructuras con it, conectores, modales, vocabulario, reading, listening, writing y speaking.

content:
# Unidad 6 C1: estructuras impersonales, conectores y modales La Unidad 6 cierra el primer módulo del curso C1 con tres herramientas esenciales para escribir y hablar sobre **trabajo y economía**: las estructuras impersonales con **it**, los conectores de **causa y resultado** y los **modales avanzados**. Juntas permiten presentar información con claridad, enlazar argumentos y expresar obligación, expectativa, probabilidad, crítica o necesidad sin depender siempre de frases directas y repetitivas. Compara estas versiones: - *People widely argue that remote work is changing management.* - *It is widely argued that remote work is changing management.* La segunda desplaza la atención desde las personas que opinan hacia la afirmación misma. Es una opción habitual en informes y textos académicos. Ahora observa la relación lógica: - *The stimulus was poorly targeted. Inequality widened.* - *The stimulus was poorly targeted; consequently, inequality widened.* El conector hace visible la relación entre causa y efecto. Finalmente, los modales añaden la postura del hablante: - *The figures must be interpreted carefully.* - *The figures may reflect regional differences.* - *The figures should have been published earlier.* La gramática C1 no consiste en elegir una forma más larga. Consiste en elegir la forma que representa mejor la evidencia, la relación lógica y el grado de responsabilidad del emisor. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 6 C1](/curso-c1/unit-6)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 5 C1: tiempos narrativos y nominalisation](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-5-tiempos-narrativos-arte)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 7 C1: inversión para énfasis](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-18-moda-identidad)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. It como sujeto gramatical En inglés una oración declarativa suele necesitar un sujeto explícito. Cuando la información importante es una cláusula larga, podemos colocar **it** al principio y desplazar el contenido hacia el final: - *It is important to understand the distinction.* - *It is clear that wage growth has slowed.* - *It surprised the board that costs had risen so quickly.* En estas frases, *it* no se refiere a un objeto concreto. Funciona como **dummy it** o sujeto anticipatorio. La información real aparece después, en forma de infinitivo o de *that-clause*. También es posible colocar la cláusula larga al principio: - *That wage growth has slowed is clear.* - *To understand the distinction is important.* Estas versiones son gramaticales, pero suelen resultar más pesadas. La estructura con *it* facilita el procesamiento y es muy frecuente en inglés profesional. ### 2. It is + adjective + that-clause El patrón más útil es: > **It + be + adjective + that + clause** - *It is obvious that the merger will affect employment.* - *It is unlikely that inflation will fall immediately.* - *It is essential that managers communicate the change clearly.* - *It was disappointing that the negotiations ended without agreement.* La elección del adjetivo expresa la evaluación del hablante: *obvious, clear, likely, unlikely, possible, essential, important, surprising, understandable, concerning*. La cláusula con *that* contiene la proposición evaluada. Si el contenido es una acción general, puede usarse un infinitivo: - *It is important to monitor cash flow.* - *It is difficult to recruit experienced staff.* - *It is possible to reduce costs without cutting essential services.* Cuando el sujeto de la acción es diferente, necesitamos *for + object + to-infinitive*: - *It is important for employees to understand the new policy.* - *It was difficult for the company to retain skilled workers.* No digas *It is important employees understand* en este patrón estándar. Usa *that employees understand* o *for employees to understand*. ### 3. It is + past participle + that Las estructuras impersonales con participio pasado permiten presentar opiniones, informes o expectativas sin mencionar un agente concreto: - *It is widely believed that the economy is entering a slowdown.* - *It has been suggested that the tax system needs reform.* - *It is generally accepted that training improves retention.* - *It was reported that several firms had frozen recruitment.* - *It is expected that interest rates will remain stable.* Los participios más frecuentes son **believed, argued, claimed, reported, suggested, assumed, estimated, expected, recognised, acknowledged**. El adverbio puede graduar el alcance: *widely, generally, increasingly, often, officially, wrongly*. Estas formas son útiles cuando la fuente es colectiva, irrelevante o deliberadamente no especificada. Si el autor importa, una estructura personal puede ser más concreta: - *It is believed that the merger will create jobs.* - *The merger is believed to create jobs.* La segunda enfoca la fusión; la primera enfoca la información. Con una acción anterior usamos el infinitivo perfecto: - *The company is believed to have overstated its profits.* - *The minister is reported to have rejected the proposal.* ### 4. It seems, appears y remains to be seen **It seems that** y **it appears that** presentan una impresión o conclusión con cierta distancia: - *It seems that smaller firms are adapting faster.* - *It appears that the policy has had an uneven effect.* También podemos usar *seem/appear + to-infinitive*: - *The policy seems to be working.* - *The policy appears to have reduced youth unemployment.* **It remains to be seen whether** significa que todavía no sabemos cuál será el resultado: - *It remains to be seen whether central banks can engineer a soft landing.* - *It remains to be seen how the merger will affect regional offices.* Otras expresiones útiles son: - *It is worth noting that...* — conviene señalar que. - *It should be noted that...* — debe observarse que. - *It goes without saying that...* — sobra decir que, aunque conviene no abusar. - *It is no surprise that...* — no sorprende que. - *It is difficult to determine whether...* — es difícil determinar si. ### 5. Find, make y consider + it Algunos verbos llevan **it** como objeto anticipatorio antes de un adjetivo y un infinitivo o una cláusula: - *The board found it difficult to reconcile the forecasts.* - *We consider it essential to protect entry-level jobs.* - *The auditors deemed it necessary to investigate the subsidiary.* - *She made it clear that the deadline could not be extended.* La estructura general es: > **verb + it + adjective + to-infinitive / that-clause** El adjetivo describe la acción o proposición que aparece después. No confundas *find it difficult* con *find difficult it*: el pronombre objeto va inmediatamente después del verbo. ### 6. Causa y resultado: dos tipos de relación Los conectores de causa explican por qué ocurre algo. Los de resultado muestran qué sucede como consecuencia. La categoría gramatical determina qué puede venir después. **Causa + sustantivo o grupo nominal:** - *because of the downturn* - *due to rising energy costs* - *owing to a shortage of staff* - *as a result of the merger* **Causa + oración completa:** - *because demand fell* - *since the firm lacked liquidity* - *as the market had changed* **Resultado + oración o consecuencia:** - *therefore, profits fell* - *consequently, recruitment slowed* - *as a result, several branches closed* - *hence, the company revised its forecast* Un error común es usar *due to* delante de una oración finita: *due to demand fell* es incorrecto. Di *due to falling demand* o *because demand fell*. ### 7. Conectores de causa **Because of**, **due to** y **owing to** son preposiciones y van seguidos de un sustantivo o gerundio: - *The delay occurred because of a technical problem.* - *The delay was due to a technical problem.* - *Owing to rising costs, the firm postponed the expansion.* *Due to* puede sonar más formal y aparece con frecuencia después de *be*: *The decline was due to lower demand*. *Owing to* suele introducir una causa al principio de una oración formal. *Because of* es neutral y muy común. **As a result of** presenta una causa con una consecuencia explícita: - *As a result of automation, some routine tasks have disappeared.* No confundas **thanks to** con una causa negativa. *Thanks to* suele presentar un resultado positivo, aunque puede usarse irónicamente: - *Thanks to better training, retention has improved.* ### 8. Conectores de resultado **Therefore**, **consequently** y **as a result** pueden aparecer al principio de una oración, después de punto y coma o entre comas: - *The subsidy was withdrawn; therefore, several projects were delayed.* - *The subsidy was withdrawn. Consequently, several projects were delayed.* - *The subsidy was withdrawn and, as a result, several projects were delayed.* **Hence** y **thus** son más formales y concisos: - *Demand fell sharply; hence, the revised forecast.* - *The data were incomplete; thus, no firm conclusion could be drawn.* *Thus* también puede indicar la manera en que se consigue algo: *The company reduced waste, thus lowering operating costs*. En esta estructura, *thus + -ing* equivale a “de ese modo”. **Thereby** significa “con ello” y suele ir seguido de gerundio: - *The firm centralised purchasing, thereby reducing duplication.* - *The policy simplified reporting, thereby making compliance easier.* ### 9. Puntuación y cohesión Los conectores formales necesitan puntuación correcta. No unas dos oraciones independientes solo con una coma: - Incorrecto: *Costs rose, consequently profits fell.* - Correcto: *Costs rose; consequently, profits fell.* - Correcto: *Costs rose. Consequently, profits fell.* - Correcto: *Costs rose, and consequently profits fell.* En textos largos, alterna conectores para evitar repetición. *Because* explica una causa; *therefore* introduce un resultado; *as a result of* empaqueta una causa nominal; *thereby* presenta un efecto derivado de una acción. La variedad no debe ocultar la lógica. ### 10. Modales avanzados de obligación y necesidad Además de *must* y *have to*, el C1 utiliza expresiones como: - **be required to:** obligación formal o reglamentaria. - **be obliged to:** deber impuesto por una norma o circunstancia. - **be expected to:** expectativa institucional o social. - **be supposed to:** acuerdo, instrucción o expectativa que puede no cumplirse. - **be meant to:** finalidad o intención prevista. - **had better:** consejo fuerte con posible consecuencia. - **would rather:** preferencia. - **needn't have + V3:** algo se hizo, pero no era necesario. - **didn't need to + infinitive:** no era necesario; no afirma si se hizo. - *Employees are required to disclose conflicts of interest.* - *The minister was expected to announce the reform.* - *You had better review the figures before publication.* - *We needn’t have hired an external consultant; the internal team solved the issue.* - *We didn’t need to hire one, so we handled the review ourselves.* La diferencia entre *needn't have done* y *didn't need to do* es especialmente importante. La primera indica que la acción sí ocurrió aunque era innecesaria. La segunda indica que no existía necesidad; el resultado de la acción debe aclararse por separado. ### 11. Modales de probabilidad y deducción Para interpretar datos económicos usamos: - **must:** conclusión muy probable. - **may/might/could:** posibilidad. - **can't/couldn't:** imposibilidad o contradicción con la evidencia. - **should/ought to:** expectativa razonable. - *The figures must reflect the seasonal adjustment.* - *The decline may be temporary.* - *The report could have overlooked informal employment.* - *The estimate can’t be accurate; it exceeds the population total.* - *The revised figures should be available next week.* En el pasado usamos **modal + have + participle**: - *The company must have underestimated demand.* - *The analysts might have misread the trend.* - *The policy could have reduced inequality.* - *The figures can’t have been calculated correctly.* En pasiva: - *The losses must have been underestimated.* - *The data may have been collected inconsistently.* - *The warning should have been communicated earlier.* ### 12. Modales para crítica y expectativa **Should have** puede expresar una expectativa no cumplida o una crítica: - *The report should have included regional data.* - *Managers should have consulted staff before changing the rota.* **Was/were supposed to** presenta una obligación o plan previo: - *The figures were supposed to be released on Friday.* - *The department was supposed to consult local offices.* **Would rather** expresa preferencia y puede llevar past perfect para criticar una decisión pasada: - *I would rather the company invested in training.* - *I would rather they had not announced the merger so early.* **Had better** es directo y suele implicar una consecuencia: - *You had better secure the contract before the deadline.* En informes formales, *would be advisable to* puede resultar menos personal y más diplomático: - *It would be advisable to review the redundancy policy.* ### 13. Vocabulario de trabajo y economía - **labour shortage:** escasez de mano de obra. - **wage bargaining:** negociación salarial. - **employee retention:** retención de empleados. - **staff turnover:** rotación de personal. - **job insecurity:** inseguridad laboral. - **fringe benefits:** beneficios adicionales al salario. - **redundancy:** despido por eliminación del puesto. - **layoffs:** despidos, especialmente por reducción de plantilla. - **subsidiary:** filial. - **off-balance-sheet liabilities:** pasivos fuera de balance. - **cash flow:** flujo de caja. - **liquidity:** liquidez. - **downturn:** desaceleración o periodo de caída. - **stimulus:** estímulo económico. - **inflation spike:** repunte de la inflación. - **fiscal policy:** política fiscal. - **interest rate:** tipo de interés. - **regional disparity:** desigualdad regional. - **headline unemployment:** desempleo general publicado. - **informal employment:** empleo informal. Colocaciones esenciales son **address a labour shortage**, **negotiate wages**, **improve retention**, **reduce turnover**, **secure funding**, **manage cash flow**, **engineer a soft landing**, **revise a forecast**, **raise productivity**, **freeze recruitment**, **flag a liability** y **widen regional disparities**. ### 14. Integrar las tres áreas Un párrafo C1 puede combinar estructura impersonal, causa, resultado y modal: > *It is widely argued that persistent labour shortages are reshaping wage bargaining. Owing to the difficulty of recruiting skilled workers, firms have increased fringe benefits; consequently, smaller employers may be facing additional pressure. It remains to be seen whether the policy will improve retention, although the first figures should be interpreted cautiously.* La primera oración presenta una opinión atribuida de forma impersonal. La segunda explica una causa y muestra una consecuencia. La tercera introduce incertidumbre y expectativa. El párrafo resulta más preciso porque cada forma cumple una función diferente. ### 15. Errores frecuentes - *It is important employees understand the change.* → **It is important that employees understand the change.** - *The decline was because of demand fell.* → **The decline was because demand fell** o **due to falling demand**. - *Costs rose, consequently profits fell.* → **Costs rose; consequently, profits fell.** - *The company must to revise its forecast.* → **The company must revise its forecast.** - *They needn’t have hired anyone* cuando no contrataron a nadie. → Si no contrataron: **They didn’t need to hire anyone.** - *It is believed the merger to create jobs.* → **It is believed that the merger will create jobs** o **The merger is believed to create jobs.** - *The board found difficult it to agree.* → **The board found it difficult to agree.** - *The policy has thereby improved because...* → **The policy has improved; thereby** no introduce una causa. Usa *because* para la causa y *thereby + -ing* para el efecto derivado. La revisión final debe comprobar cuatro cosas: si *it* anticipa correctamente una cláusula, si el conector admite el tipo de complemento utilizado, si el modal expresa la intención exacta y si la puntuación separa correctamente las proposiciones. ## Parte II — Ejercicios con soluciones ### Ejercicio 1 — Estructuras impersonales Completa con **It is**, **It was** o **It remains**. 1. ___ widely argued that remote work is changing management. 2. ___ obvious that the merger would affect employment. 3. ___ to be seen whether the policy will reduce inflation. 4. ___ important to monitor cash flow carefully.
Ver solución 1. **It is**; 2. **It was**; 3. **It remains**; 4. **It is**. El tiempo depende del momento de referencia y de si el resultado sigue abierto.
### Ejercicio 2 — It + adjective Elige la continuación correcta. 1. It is important ___ employees understand the change. (*that / for*) 2. It is difficult ___ recruit experienced staff. (*to / that*) 3. It was surprising ___ costs had risen so quickly. (*that / for*) 4. It is essential ___ managers to communicate clearly. (*that / for*)
Ver solución 1. **that employees understand**; 2. **to recruit**; 3. **that costs had risen**; 4. **for managers to communicate**. Usa *that + clause* con un sujeto y verbo completos; usa *for + object + to-infinitive* cuando el infinitivo tiene un sujeto explícito.
### Ejercicio 3 — Reporting impersonal Transforma las frases sin mencionar *people*. 1. People widely believe that the economy is slowing. 2. Analysts have suggested that the tax system needs reform. 3. The press reported that several firms had frozen recruitment.
Ver solución 1. **It is widely believed that the economy is slowing.** 2. **It has been suggested that the tax system needs reform.** 3. **It was reported that several firms had frozen recruitment.**
### Ejercicio 4 — Find it Completa con **it** y el adjetivo adecuado: *difficult, clear, necessary, impossible*. 1. The board found ___ ___ to reconcile the forecasts. 2. The director made ___ ___ that the deadline would not move. 3. Auditors deemed ___ ___ to investigate the subsidiary. 4. The figures make ___ ___ to compare the two regions.
Ver solución 1. **it difficult**; 2. **it clear**; 3. **it necessary**; 4. **it impossible**. El patrón es *verb + it + adjective + complement*.
### Ejercicio 5 — Causa o resultado Elige **because of, due to, consequently, hence** o **thereby**. 1. ___ rising energy costs, the firm postponed expansion. 2. Demand fell sharply; ___, profits declined. 3. The company centralised purchasing, ___ reducing duplication. 4. The delay was ___ a technical failure. 5. The currency weakened; ___ import prices increased.
Ver solución 1. **Owing to/Because of/Due to**; 2. **consequently**; 3. **thereby**; 4. **due to**; 5. **hence**. Los tres primeros conectores del ejercicio 1 requieren un sustantivo; los conectores de resultado enlazan con la consecuencia.
### Ejercicio 6 — Corrige el conector 1. *Due to demand fell, recruitment slowed.* 2. *Costs rose, consequently profits fell.* 3. *The firm reduced waste, because lowering operating costs.*
Ver solución 1. **Because demand fell, recruitment slowed** o **Due to falling demand, recruitment slowed.** 2. **Costs rose; consequently, profits fell.** 3. **The firm reduced waste, thereby lowering operating costs.**
### Ejercicio 7 — Modales avanzados Completa con **must, may, can’t** o **should**. 1. The figures ___ reflect seasonal adjustment; the pattern is very consistent. 2. The estimate ___ be accurate because it exceeds the total population. 3. The revised report ___ be available next week. 4. The decline ___ be temporary, but more data are needed.
Ver solución 1. **must**; 2. **can’t**; 3. **should**; 4. **may/might/could**. La fuerza depende de la evidencia y de si expresas conclusión, imposibilidad, expectativa o posibilidad.
### Ejercicio 8 — Modal perfecto Completa con la forma correcta. 1. The company ___ ___ ___ (underestimate) demand. 2. The analysts ___ ___ ___ (misread) the trend. 3. The data ___ ___ ___ (collect) inconsistently. 4. The warning ___ ___ ___ (communicate) earlier.
Ver solución 1. **must have underestimated**. 2. **might/may/could have misread**. 3. **may/might have been collected**. 4. **should have been communicated**.
### Ejercicio 9 — Needn’t have o didn’t need to Elige la opción correcta. 1. We ___ hire an external consultant; the internal team solved the issue. (*needn’t have / didn’t need to*) 2. We ___ hire an external consultant, but we did, so the expense was unnecessary. (*needn’t have / didn’t need to*) 3. They ___ submit a second form, so they stopped after the first. (*needn’t have / didn’t need to*)
Ver solución 1. **didn’t need to hire**; no lo hicieron. 2. **needn’t have hired**; sí lo hicieron, pero fue innecesario. 3. **didn’t need to submit**; la acción no se realizó.
### Ejercicio 10 — Vocabulario laboral Completa con **turnover, retention, redundancy, liquidity** o **wage bargaining**. 1. The company improved employee ___ by offering flexible schedules. 2. High staff ___ increased recruitment costs. 3. The firm faced a ___ after the factory closed. 4. The bank’s ___ position weakened during the downturn. 5. The union reopened ___ negotiations.
Ver solución 1. **retention**; 2. **turnover**; 3. **redundancy**; 4. **liquidity**; 5. **wage bargaining**.
### Ejercicio 11 — Reading Lee el texto y responde. > It is widely argued that the country’s labour shortage is partly responsible for rising wages. Owing to the difficulty of recruiting nurses and engineers, employers have increased salaries and improved fringe benefits. Consequently, smaller firms may be losing experienced staff to larger competitors. It remains to be seen whether the government’s training programme will improve retention. The first figures should be interpreted cautiously, since participation has been uneven across regions. The programme could have a stronger effect if local employers were involved in its design. 1. What is partly responsible for rising wages? 2. Why have employers improved salaries and benefits? 3. What may be happening to smaller firms? 4. Why should the first figures be treated cautiously? 5. What could strengthen the programme’s effect?
Ver solución 1. **The labour shortage.** 2. **Because recruiting nurses and engineers has been difficult.** 3. **They may be losing experienced staff to larger competitors.** 4. **Because participation has been uneven across regions.** 5. **Involving local employers in its design.**
### Ejercicio 12 — Listening guiado Guion: “It is important to distinguish headline unemployment from job insecurity. The official rate has fallen; nevertheless, many workers are on temporary contracts. This may explain why consumer confidence has not recovered. The figures could have been interpreted differently if informal employment had been measured more consistently.” Identifica un conector de contraste, dos modales y una estructura con *it*.
Ver solución Estructura con *it*: **It is important to distinguish...**. Conector de contraste: **nevertheless**. Modales: **may explain** expresa posibilidad y **could have been interpreted** expresa una posibilidad alternativa en el pasado.
### Ejercicio 13 — Reformulación impersonal Reescribe con **It is believed that** o **X is believed to**. *Analysts believe that the subsidiary overstated its profits.*
Ver solución **It is believed that the subsidiary overstated its profits.** También: **The subsidiary is believed to have overstated its profits.** La segunda enfoca la filial y usa infinitivo perfecto para la acción anterior.
### Ejercicio 14 — Registro y cohesión Une las frases con un conector adecuado: *The stimulus was poorly targeted. Inequality widened despite headline growth.*
Modelo **The stimulus was poorly targeted; consequently, inequality widened despite headline growth.** También son posibles **therefore** o **as a result**. *Despite* introduce el contraste entre crecimiento general y desigualdad.
### Ejercicio 15 — Writing Escribe 140–170 palabras sobre: **Should governments intervene when labour shortages push up wages?** Incluye una estructura impersonal con *it*, dos conectores de causa o resultado, dos modales y vocabulario de trabajo.
Modelo It is widely argued that governments should intervene when labour shortages threaten essential services. Owing to the difficulty of recruiting qualified nurses, hospitals may have to improve wages and fringe benefits. Consequently, public funding could be needed, particularly in regions where smaller employers cannot compete with large institutions. It is important, however, to distinguish a temporary shortage from a structural failure in training. The government should support apprenticeships and might offer incentives for workers who move to underserved areas. Such measures would not necessarily solve every problem, since employee retention also depends on management, workload and job security. It remains to be seen whether higher wages alone will reduce staff turnover. A balanced policy should therefore combine investment in training with better working conditions and reliable data about regional disparities.
### Ejercicio 16 — Speaking Habla durante un minuto sobre una decisión económica controvertida. Usa *It is often argued that*, *because of*, *consequently*, *must/might* y una limitación.
Pista y modelo **It is often argued that the company should freeze recruitment because of falling demand. Consequently, costs might be controlled in the short term, but the firm must consider the effect on employee retention. A freeze could protect liquidity, although it may also worsen the labour shortage when demand recovers.**
### Ejercicio 17 — Corrección avanzada Corrige el párrafo. > It is believed the merger to create jobs, but due to the integration was delayed, costs rose, consequently the forecast must have revised. The managers didn’t need to have hired consultants, although they did.
Ver solución **It is believed that the merger will create jobs, but because the integration was delayed, costs rose; consequently, the forecast must have been revised. The managers needn’t have hired consultants, although they did.** *Due to* necesita un grupo nominal, no una oración finita. *Must have been revised* es la pasiva modal perfecta. *Needn’t have hired* indica que la contratación ocurrió, pero no era necesaria.
### Ejercicio 18 — Mini-test final Completa el texto. > ___ remains to be seen whether the merger will improve productivity. ___ to the shortage of engineers, the company may outsource some work; ___, its cash flow could become more difficult to manage. The board ___ have anticipated the shortage, and it ___ important for managers to revise the recruitment plan.
Ver solución **It; Owing/Due/Because of; consequently/as a result; should; is.** La respuesta completa puede ser: **It remains to be seen whether the merger will improve productivity. Owing to the shortage of engineers, the company may outsource some work; consequently, its cash flow could become more difficult to manage. The board should have anticipated the shortage, and it is important for managers to revise the recruitment plan.**
### Ejercicio 19 — Integración de gramática y argumento Completa el párrafo con una estructura impersonal, un conector de causa, uno de resultado y un modal adecuado. Después explica por qué has elegido cada forma. > ___ widely accepted that automation is changing routine work. ___ the speed of technological change, some employees may need retraining; ___, firms should invest in professional development. It ___ to be seen whether productivity gains will improve job security, but the transition ___ be managed more fairly if workers were consulted earlier.
Ver solución Una respuesta posible es: **It is widely accepted that automation is changing routine work. Owing to the speed of technological change, some employees may need retraining; consequently, firms should invest in professional development. It remains to be seen whether productivity gains will improve job security, but the transition could be managed more fairly if workers were consulted earlier.** **It is widely accepted** presenta una opinión sin señalar una fuente concreta. **Owing to** introduce el grupo nominal *the speed of technological change*. **Consequently** introduce el resultado y **could be managed** expresa una posibilidad condicionada, no una garantía. La frase final mantiene un registro prudente porque reconoce que la consulta previa habría cambiado el proceso, pero no afirma que ese resultado sea seguro.
## Resumen de la unidad Usa **it + be + adjective + that-clause** para evaluar una proposición y **it + be + adjective + to-infinitive** para presentar una acción de forma compacta. Usa **it is believed/reported/suggested that** para atribuir información impersonalmente y **find/make/consider + it + adjective** para valorar una acción o situación. Distingue la gramática de los conectores: **because of, due to, owing to** y **as a result of** introducen nombres; **because, since** y **as** introducen oraciones; **therefore, consequently, hence, thus** presentan resultados; **thereby + -ing** muestra un efecto derivado de una acción. Finalmente, elige los modales según la intención: **must** para una conclusión fuerte, **may/might/could** para posibilidades, **can’t** para imposibilidad, **should** para expectativa o crítica y **needn’t have** para una acción realizada innecesariamente. Cuando combines estas formas con colocaciones como *address a labour shortage*, *manage cash flow* y *improve employee retention*, podrás escribir sobre trabajo y economía con la precisión, distancia y cohesión propias del nivel C1.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es una nominal clause?
faqs.answer: Es una cláusula que funciona como sustantivo dentro de otra oración, por ejemplo That stress affects sleep is well established o What matters is recovery.

faqs.question: ¿Qué reporting verbs se estudian en la Unidad 7?
faqs.answer: Se practican acknowledge, recommend, contend, concede, maintain, insist, dispute y otros verbos que permiten atribuir opiniones con precisión.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre although y despite?
faqs.answer: Although introduce una oración con sujeto y verbo; despite e in spite of introducen un sustantivo, pronombre o gerundio.

faqs.question: ¿La Unidad 7 incluye ejercicios resueltos?
faqs.answer: Sí. Incluye gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, writing y speaking con respuestas y modelos.

content:
# Unidad 7 C1: nominal clauses, reporting verbs y concesión La Unidad 7 C1 enseña a construir argumentos complejos sobre **health and mind**. En un artículo científico o en una conversación académica no siempre basta con decir *stress affects sleep*. Necesitamos convertir una idea completa en el sujeto o complemento de otra oración, atribuirla a una fuente concreta y reconocer que una conclusión puede mantenerse aunque exista una dificultad. Para eso usamos **nominal clauses**, **reporting verbs** y estructuras de **concession**. Observa la progresión: - *Chronic stress remodels neural circuits.* - *That chronic stress remodels neural circuits is no longer controversial.* - *The authors acknowledge that chronic stress may remodel neural circuits, although the evidence remains heterogeneous.* La primera frase comunica una proposición. La segunda la convierte en el sujeto de una oración más amplia. La tercera identifica la postura de los autores, introduce un grado de cautela y añade una concesión. Esta capacidad de empaquetar ideas y relacionarlas con precisión es una característica del nivel C1. > **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 7 C1](/curso-c1/unit-7)
> **Unidad anterior:** [Unidad 6 C1: estructuras con it](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-6-estructuras-it-economia)
> **Siguiente unidad:** [Unidad 8 C1: comparatives y concession](/blog/curso-c1/unidad-24-oceanos-vida-marina)
> **Curso completo:** [Inglés C1](/blog/metodos/ingles-c1) ## Parte I — Teoría ### 1. Qué es una nominal clause Una nominal clause, también llamada noun clause, es una cláusula que funciona como un sustantivo. Puede actuar como sujeto, objeto, complemento o parte de una expresión preposicional. En lugar de una sola palabra, contiene un sujeto y un verbo propios: - *That the treatment works is encouraging.* - *The researchers agree that the treatment works.* - *What the treatment changes is still uncertain.* - *The debate concerns whether the treatment is affordable.* La cláusula completa puede ocupar la posición que ocuparía *the result*, *the fact* o *the question*. Esta flexibilidad permite expresar relaciones abstractas sin encadenar muchas frases simples. Las nominal clauses más frecuentes en la unidad empiezan con **that, whether, what, the fact that** y palabras interrogativas como **how, why, where**. No funcionan todas de la misma manera, por lo que conviene identificar si hablamos de una proposición, una incertidumbre o la información que falta. ### 2. That-clause como sujeto Una cláusula introducida por **that** puede ser el sujeto de la oración: - *That chronic stress remodels neural circuits is no longer controversial.* - *That early intervention can alter illness trajectories is supported by longitudinal studies.* - *That the trial was not preregistered should give readers pause.* La estructura es: > **That + subject + verb + main verb** El verbo principal suele ser *is, was, remains, seems, matters, suggests* o una forma pasiva como *is supported*. La cláusula con *that* presenta una proposición completa, no una pregunta. En escritura formal es correcta, pero puede ser pesada si contiene mucha información. Por eso a menudo la sustituimos por **it**: - *It is no longer controversial that chronic stress remodels neural circuits.* - *It should give readers pause that the trial was not preregistered.* La versión con *that-clause* al principio pone énfasis en la proposición; la versión con *it* facilita el procesamiento. Ambas son útiles en C1. No confundas **that** relativo con **that** conjuntivo. En *The study that examined sleep was large*, *that* introduce una relative clause y modifica *study*. En *That the study examined sleep is important*, *that* introduce una nominal clause que funciona como sujeto. ### 3. Whether-clause para incertidumbre **Whether** introduce una cuestión abierta o una alternativa. Puede funcionar como sujeto, objeto o complemento: - *Whether digital therapy will prove cost-effective at scale is still an open question.* - *The researchers examined whether participants had improved.* - *It is unclear whether the effect will last.* Como sujeto, **whether** suele sonar más natural que *if*: - Natural y formal: *Whether the intervention works remains uncertain.* - Menos natural como sujeto: *If the intervention works remains uncertain.* En una cláusula objeto, tanto *whether* como *if* pueden ser posibles, aunque *whether* es preferible cuando hay alternativas explícitas o un registro formal: - *The study investigated whether patients improved.* - *The study investigated if patients improved.* - *The study investigated whether patients improved or deteriorated.* Después de preposición usamos **whether**, no normalmente *if*: - *The decision depends on whether the participants consent.* - *There is uncertainty about whether the effect is clinical or statistical.* ### 4. What-clause: “lo que” y la información focalizada **What** significa aproximadamente “lo que” y contiene dentro de sí el elemento que falta. Por eso no se combina normalmente con un sustantivo inmediatamente después: - *What is most striking is the gap between symptom scores and functional recovery.* - *What the intervention changes is still being studied.* - *What matters most is whether people can function in daily life.* La estructura típica es: > **What + clause + be + focus** La parte con *what* puede ser el sujeto; la información posterior identifica el resultado. Compara: - *What concerns the clinicians is the lack of long-term data.* - *The thing that concerns the clinicians is the lack of long-term data.* No digas *What the clinicians concern is...* si quieres expresar “lo que preocupa a los clínicos”. El verbo necesita su patrón: *What concerns them is...* o *What they are concerned about is...*. La concordancia suele seguir al elemento focalizado después de *be*, aunque existen variaciones. En escritura académica, mantén la estructura sencilla: *What matters is the evidence*, *What matters are the practical consequences* puede aparecer cuando el foco es plural. ### 5. The fact that **The fact that + clause** convierte un hecho o proposición en un grupo nominal explícito: - *The fact that effects were heterogeneous complicates the meta-analysis.* - *The fact that participants withdrew affected the final sample.* - *The fact that symptoms improved does not prove that the treatment caused the change.* Esta forma es útil cuando queremos hacer visible que tratamos una proposición como información. Sin embargo, no la repitas innecesariamente: *The fact that the fact that...* es pesado. Alternativas son *That effects were heterogeneous...* o *Because effects were heterogeneous...*, según la relación que quieras expresar. La cláusula con *that* después de un sustantivo puede ser complementaria o relativa: - *The fact that the trial was small matters.* Aquí especifica el contenido del hecho. - *The trial that was small ended early.* Aquí modifica *trial*. El contexto y la posición ayudan a distinguirlas. ### 6. Nominal clauses como objetos Muchos verbos de pensamiento, conocimiento, investigación y comunicación aceptan una nominal clause como objeto: - *The study demonstrates that sleep quality predicts recovery.* - *The authors acknowledge that residual confounding cannot be excluded.* - *The team investigated whether the intervention improved concentration.* - *The review examines how social isolation affects wellbeing.* - *The clinicians discussed what the scores meant in practice.* El inglés académico usa estas cláusulas para expresar contenido sin convertir cada proposición en una oración independiente. No uses inversión interrogativa dentro de una nominal clause: - Correcto: *The researchers asked whether the participants had improved.* - Incorrecto: *The researchers asked whether had the participants improved.* Una pregunta directa tiene inversión (*Had the participants improved?*); una pregunta integrada mantiene el orden declarativo (*whether the participants had improved*). ### 7. Reporting verbs: atribuir ideas con precisión Los reporting verbs indican qué dijo, pensó o sostuvo una persona o institución y, a menudo, muestran cómo se relaciona con la proposición. No todos tienen el mismo patrón gramatical. **Verb + that-clause:** - *acknowledge that* — reconocer, a menudo una limitación. - *argue that* — defender una posición. - *contend that* — sostener formalmente. - *claim that* — afirmar, sin garantizar que sea verdad. - *concede that* — admitir un punto, normalmente parcialmente. - *maintain that* — mantener una postura. - *note that* — señalar. - *observe that* — observar. - *suggest that* — sugerir. - *demonstrate/show that* — mostrar o demostrar. - *The authors acknowledge that the sample was heterogeneous.* - *The review contends that prevention should begin earlier.* - *The researchers concede that the effect is small.* **Verb + object + that-clause:** - *The therapist reminded participants that recovery is non-linear.* - *The report warned readers that the results were preliminary.* **Verb + gerund:** - *The witness denied having ignored the warning.* - *The researchers admitted having underestimated attrition.* - *The review recommends improving access to support.* **Verb + that + subject + base form:** - *The committee recommended that the intervention be offered early.* - *The clinicians insisted that every participant receive follow-up care.* Después de *recommend, insist, propose* y algunos adjetivos como *essential*, el inglés formal puede usar el subjuntivo mandativo: *that the team collect more data*, no *that the team collects more data*. En británico también es posible *should collect*. **Verb + to-infinitive / object + to-infinitive:** - *The clinician advised patients to keep a sleep diary.* - *The committee urged the hospital to revise its protocol.* - *The speaker claimed to have identified a new risk factor.* No combines patrones al azar: *recommend to improve* es incorrecto cuando no hay objeto; usa *recommend improving* o *recommend that the team improve*. *Suggest someone to do* tampoco es el patrón estándar; usa *suggest that someone do* o *suggest doing*. ### 8. El matiz de los reporting verbs La selección del verbo cambia la relación con la información: - *The authors claim that the intervention works.* Puede haber duda o distancia. - *The authors demonstrate that the intervention works.* Presentan evidencia que apoya la conclusión. - *The authors acknowledge that the evidence is limited.* Reconocen una restricción. - *The authors concede that the effect is modest.* Admiten un punto que quizá reduce la fuerza de su argumento. - *The authors maintain that the effect is clinically meaningful.* Continúan defendiendo la posición. - *The authors dispute that the result is due to chance.* Rechazan una interpretación. En una reseña rigurosa, evita repetir *say*. Usa un verbo que describa la función exacta de la frase y añade un hedge cuando sea necesario: *The authors suggest that..., but they do not establish that...*. ### 9. Concession: admitir sin abandonar la tesis Una estructura de concesión reconoce una idea que podría parecer contraria a la principal y, aun así, mantiene o matiza la conclusión. Las formas principales son: - **although/even though + subject + verb**: *Although the sample was small, the pattern was consistent.* - **despite/in spite of + noun or -ing**: *Despite the small sample, the pattern was consistent.* - **despite the fact that + clause**: *Despite the fact that the sample was small, the pattern was consistent.* - **while/whereas + clause**: *While symptom scores improved, functional recovery remained limited.* - **nevertheless/nonetheless/however + sentence**: *The sample was small. Nevertheless, the pattern was consistent.* - **yet/still + clause**: *The evidence is preliminary, yet the finding deserves attention.* No mezcles estructuras: - Incorrecto: *Despite the sample was small...* - Correcto: *Although the sample was small...* o *Despite the small sample...* **Even though** suele presentar un contraste fuerte. **Although** es neutral y frecuente en escritura. **Despite** e **in spite of** son preposiciones y necesitan un nombre, pronombre o gerundio. ### 10. Concesión y puntuación Una cláusula concesiva inicial suele separarse con coma: - *Although the intervention was brief, participants reported less distress.* Si va después, normalmente no hace falta coma cuando está estrechamente ligada a la principal: - *Participants reported less distress although the intervention was brief.* Los adverbios conjuntivos como *however, nevertheless* no unen por sí solos dos oraciones independientes con una coma: - Incorrecto: *The sample was small, nevertheless the result was interesting.* - Correcto: *The sample was small; nevertheless, the result was interesting.* - Correcto: *The sample was small. Nevertheless, the result was interesting.* ### 11. Vocabulario de health and mind - **chronic stress:** estrés crónico. - **neural circuit:** circuito neuronal. - **threat detection:** detección de amenazas. - **symptom score:** puntuación de síntomas. - **functional recovery:** recuperación funcional. - **clinical outcome:** resultado clínico. - **treatment trajectory:** evolución del tratamiento. - **digital therapy:** terapia digital. - **cost-effective:** rentable o coste-efectiva. - **longitudinal cohort:** cohorte longitudinal. - **meta-analysis:** metaanálisis. - **effect size:** tamaño del efecto. - **residual confounding:** confusión residual. - **preregister a trial:** preregistrar un ensayo. - **attrition:** abandono de participantes. - **wellbeing:** bienestar. - **self-regulation:** autorregulación. - **emotional resilience:** resiliencia emocional. - **cognitive load:** carga cognitiva. - **social isolation:** aislamiento social. - **sleep quality:** calidad del sueño. - **functional impairment:** deterioro funcional. - **evidence-based intervention:** intervención basada en la evidencia. - **follow-up care:** atención de seguimiento. Colocaciones útiles son **assess symptom severity**, **improve functional recovery**, **reduce cognitive load**, **monitor treatment outcomes**, **experience chronic stress**, **develop emotional resilience**, **address social isolation**, **collect longitudinal data**, **estimate an effect size**, **account for confounding**, **provide follow-up care** y **support mental wellbeing**. ### 12. Nominal clauses en textos de salud En investigación, una nominal clause puede ocupar distintas funciones dentro del mismo párrafo: > *That chronic stress affects sleep is well established. The fact that sleep quality predicts recovery has encouraged clinicians to assess it routinely. Researchers are investigating whether digital therapy can improve sleep at scale. What remains uncertain is how long the benefit lasts. Although the early evidence is promising, the authors acknowledge that attrition may have biased the results.* La primera oración presenta un punto de partida. La segunda añade una consecuencia. La tercera formula una pregunta de investigación. La cuarta focaliza la incertidumbre. La quinta introduce concesión y limitación. La variedad sintáctica evita una lista de frases coordinadas y muestra cómo progresa un argumento. ### 13. Errores frecuentes - *What the study shows it is unclear.* → **What the study shows is unclear.** - *The researchers asked whether did the patients improve.* → **... whether the patients improved.** - *The committee recommended to improve access.* → **The committee recommended improving access** o **recommended that the team improve access**. - *The author suggested participants to rest.* → **The author suggested that participants rest** o **suggested resting**. - *Despite the evidence was limited...* → **Although the evidence was limited** o **Despite the limited evidence**. - *The sample was small, however the result was useful.* → **The sample was small; however, the result was useful.** - *That the results are mixed mean...* → **That the results are mixed means...**; la nominal clause es singular. - *The fact that the fact that...* → Elimina la repetición o usa una cláusula directa. La revisión final debe responder: ¿la cláusula funciona como nombre?, ¿el reporting verb admite el patrón que he usado?, ¿la concesión lleva cláusula o grupo nominal?, ¿la puntuación separa correctamente las ideas?, ¿el verbo expresa exactamente la postura de la fuente? ## Parte II — Ejercicios con soluciones ### Ejercicio 1 — That, whether o what Completa. 1. ___ chronic stress affects sleep is well established. 2. ___ digital therapy will prove cost-effective remains uncertain. 3. ___ is most striking is the gap between symptom scores and recovery. 4. The study investigated ___ participants had improved.
Ver solución 1. **That** — presenta una proposición como sujeto. 2. **Whether** — introduce una incertidumbre. 3. **What** — significa “lo que” y focaliza la información posterior. 4. **whether** — funciona como objeto de *investigated*.
### Ejercicio 2 — Nominal clause como sujeto Combina las frases. 1. The trial was not preregistered. This should give readers pause. 2. Early intervention can alter illness trajectories. Longitudinal studies support this. 3. Effects were heterogeneous across sites. This complicates the meta-analysis.
Ver solución 1. **That the trial was not preregistered should give readers pause.** 2. **That early intervention can alter illness trajectories is supported by longitudinal studies.** 3. **The fact that effects were heterogeneous across sites complicates the meta-analysis.**
### Ejercicio 3 — Orden indirecto Corrige las preguntas integradas. 1. *The researchers asked whether had the participants improved.* 2. *The review examines how does social isolation affect wellbeing.* 3. *It is unclear what did the intervention change.*
Ver solución 1. **The researchers asked whether the participants had improved.** 2. **The review examines how social isolation affects wellbeing.** 3. **It is unclear what the intervention changed.** Una nominal clause mantiene el orden declarativo: sujeto antes del verbo.
### Ejercicio 4 — Reporting verbs Elige **acknowledged, contended, conceded, disputed** o **maintained**. 1. The authors ___ that the sample was too small to support a definitive conclusion. 2. The review ___ that prevention should begin before symptoms become severe. 3. The researchers ___ that the effect was modest but clinically relevant. 4. The critics ___ that the correlation proved causation. 5. Despite the criticism, the team ___ that the intervention remained useful.
Ver solución 1. **acknowledged** — reconocieron una limitación. 2. **contended** — defendieron una posición formal. 3. **conceded** — admitieron un punto parcialmente desfavorable. 4. **disputed** — rechazaron una interpretación. 5. **maintained** — siguieron defendiendo su postura.
### Ejercicio 5 — Patrones de reporting Completa con la forma correcta. 1. The committee recommended ___ (offer) the intervention early. 2. The clinicians insisted that every participant ___ (receive) follow-up care. 3. The therapist advised patients ___ (keep) a sleep diary. 4. The witness denied ___ (ignore) the warning. 5. The speaker claimed ___ (identify) a new risk factor.
Ver solución 1. **offering** o **that the intervention be offered**. 2. **receive** — subjuntivo mandativo; también *should receive*. 3. **to keep**. 4. **having ignored**. 5. **to have identified**.
### Ejercicio 6 — Concesión con cláusula Completa con **although, even though, while** o **whereas**. 1. ___ the sample was small, the pattern was consistent. 2. ___ symptom scores improved, functional recovery remained limited. 3. ___ the treatment was brief, participants reported less distress. 4. The digital group improved quickly, ___ the control group changed gradually.
Ver solución 1. **Although/Even though**. 2. **While**. 3. **Although/Even though**. 4. **whereas**. *While* puede señalar contraste entre dos resultados; *whereas* contrasta grupos o proposiciones de forma explícita.
### Ejercicio 7 — Despite e in spite of Reescribe sin cambiar el significado. 1. Although the evidence was limited, the finding deserved attention. 2. Although participants experienced attrition, the analysis remained informative. 3. Although the intervention was expensive, it improved follow-up care.
Ver solución 1. **Despite the limited evidence, the finding deserved attention.** 2. **Despite participant attrition, the analysis remained informative.** 3. **In spite of the intervention’s expense, it improved follow-up care.** Después de *despite/in spite of* usamos un sustantivo, posesivo o gerundio, no una oración finita sin *the fact that*.
### Ejercicio 8 — However y nevertheless Puntúa correctamente. 1. *The cohort was small however the data were valuable.* 2. *The evidence was preliminary nevertheless the policy changed.* 3. *The treatment was demanding. However participants completed it.*
Ver solución 1. **The cohort was small; however, the data were valuable.** 2. **The evidence was preliminary; nevertheless, the policy changed.** 3. **The treatment was demanding. However, participants completed it.**
### Ejercicio 9 — Vocabulario Completa con **attrition, wellbeing, cognitive load, effect size** o **follow-up care**. 1. The study measured the ___ rather than relying only on symptom scores. 2. High ___ made the digital exercises difficult to complete. 3. Participant ___ reduced the final sample. 4. The researchers reported a small but meaningful ___ . 5. Patients received structured ___ after the intervention.
Ver solución 1. **wellbeing**; 2. **cognitive load**; 3. **attrition**; 4. **effect size**; 5. **follow-up care**.
### Ejercicio 10 — Reading Lee el texto y responde. > That chronic stress affects sleep is well established, but the relationship is not simple. A longitudinal cohort found that participants reporting poor sleep also showed lower emotional resilience six months later. The authors acknowledged that the study could not establish causation, since unmeasured social factors may have influenced both outcomes. What is most striking is that functional impairment persisted even when symptom scores had improved. Although the digital programme reduced reported distress, its effect size was modest. The researchers nevertheless contend that the intervention may be cost-effective because it can provide support to people who cannot attend regular appointments. 1. What is well established? 2. What did the cohort find? 3. What limitation did the authors acknowledge? 4. What remained even when symptom scores improved? 5. Why do the researchers defend the programme?
Ver solución 1. **That chronic stress affects sleep.** 2. **Participants with poor sleep also showed lower emotional resilience six months later.** 3. **The study could not establish causation because unmeasured social factors may have affected both outcomes.** 4. **Functional impairment persisted.** 5. **They contend that it may be cost-effective because it can support people who cannot attend regular appointments.**
### Ejercicio 11 — Listening guiado Guion: “The committee conceded that the intervention was demanding, yet it maintained that the benefits justified the effort. It recommended that participants receive additional support, although it disputed the claim that everyone needed weekly sessions. What matters most, the chair argued, is whether people can function more independently after treatment.” Identifica dos reporting verbs, una concesión y una nominal clause.
Ver solución Reporting verbs: **conceded, maintained, recommended, disputed, argued**. Concesión: **although it disputed the claim...** o **yet it maintained...**. Nominal clause: **whether people can function more independently after treatment**; también **What matters most** funciona como sujeto focalizado.
### Ejercicio 12 — Completa un argumento Completa con una nominal clause adecuada. 1. ___ the trial was not preregistered should give readers pause. 2. The main question is ___ the benefits will last. 3. ___ the intervention changes in daily life is still unclear. 4. The fact ___ effects varied across sites complicates interpretation.
Ver solución 1. **That**; 2. **whether**; 3. **What**; 4. **that**. Las respuestas construyen respectivamente una proposición como sujeto, una incertidumbre, una what-clause y el complemento de *the fact*.
### Ejercicio 13 — Reformulación académica Reescribe con distancia y precisión: *The treatment works for everyone, even though the study only had twenty participants.*
Modelo **Although the study included only twenty participants, the authors suggest that the treatment may benefit a wider population; however, the available evidence does not establish that it works for everyone.** La versión distingue la afirmación de los autores de lo que los datos permiten concluir y evita una generalización absoluta.
### Ejercicio 14 — Writing Escribe 150–180 palabras sobre: **Should digital mental-health interventions be offered as a first-line option?** Incluye una that-clause, una whether-clause, dos reporting verbs y dos estructuras de concesión.
Modelo That digital interventions can improve access to support is increasingly recognised, particularly for people who live far from specialist services. Several reviews suggest that guided programmes may reduce mild distress, and one committee has recommended that patients receive professional follow-up when necessary. Nevertheless, whether these tools should be offered as a first-line option remains debatable. Although digital therapy can be cost-effective, it may not meet the needs of people experiencing severe symptoms or limited digital access. Despite the convenience of remote sessions, some users may require a relationship that is easier to establish face to face. The authors acknowledge that the evidence is heterogeneous, but they maintain that carefully designed programmes can complement, rather than replace, clinical care. It is therefore reasonable to expand access gradually while monitoring outcomes, protecting privacy and ensuring that users can move to more intensive support when required.
### Ejercicio 15 — Speaking Habla durante un minuto sobre un hábito que puede mejorar el bienestar. Usa *What matters is...*, *although*, *despite* y un reporting verb.
Pista y modelo **What matters is whether the habit can be maintained in daily life. Although short walks may seem simple, they can reduce cognitive load and support wellbeing. Despite the limited evidence for one individual, researchers suggest that regular movement may improve sleep. I would nevertheless acknowledge that people have different health needs.**
### Ejercicio 16 — Traducción controlada Traduce al inglés. 1. Que los efectos fueran distintos complica el metaanálisis. 2. Los autores reconocieron que no podían demostrar causalidad. 3. A pesar de que la muestra era pequeña, el resultado merece atención.
Ver solución 1. **That the effects were different complicates the meta-analysis.** 2. **The authors acknowledged that they could not demonstrate causation.** 3. **Despite the fact that the sample was small, the result deserves attention.**
### Ejercicio 17 — Corrección avanzada Corrige el párrafo. > What the study shows it is uncertain. The researchers suggested participants to complete more sessions, despite the evidence was limited. They claimed that the intervention helped everyone, however they acknowledged the attrition was high.
Ver solución **What the study shows is uncertain. The researchers suggested that participants complete more sessions, although the evidence was limited. They claimed that the intervention helped everyone; however, they acknowledged that attrition was high.** Se elimina el *it* innecesario, se corrige el patrón de *suggest*, se cambia *despite* por *although* ante una cláusula y se puntúa *however* correctamente.
### Ejercicio 18 — Mini-test final Completa el texto. > ___ early psychological intervention can alter illness trajectories is supported by longitudinal cohorts. The committee ___ that the evidence remains heterogeneous, ___ it recommends that services expand access. ___ matters most is whether patients receive appropriate follow-up care. It remains unclear ___ the benefits will last, and the researchers ___ that further data are needed.
Ver solución **That; acknowledges; although; What; whether; maintain/contend.** Una versión completa es: **That early psychological intervention can alter illness trajectories is supported by longitudinal cohorts. The committee acknowledges that the evidence remains heterogeneous, although it recommends that services expand access. What matters most is whether patients receive appropriate follow-up care. It remains unclear whether the benefits will last, and the researchers maintain that further data are needed.**
## Resumen de la unidad Usa **that-clauses** para presentar proposiciones, **whether-clauses** para expresar incertidumbre y **what-clauses** para focalizar “lo que” importa o sigue sin explicarse. Usa **the fact that** cuando quieras convertir un hecho explícito en el sujeto o complemento de la oración. Elige los reporting verbs por su significado y por su patrón: *acknowledge that*, *recommend doing* o *recommend that someone do*, *advise someone to do*, *deny having done* y *claim to have done*. No combines estructuras por traducción literal. Para la concesión, recuerda la diferencia formal: **although/even though + clause**, **despite/in spite of + noun o gerund**, y **however/nevertheless + oración independiente**. Estas formas te permiten admitir una limitación sin abandonar una conclusión matizada. En un texto sobre salud y mente, la precisión gramatical debe ir acompañada de prudencia. Una muestra pequeña, un efecto modesto o una posible variable de confusión no invalidan necesariamente un estudio, pero sí condicionan lo que podemos afirmar. El inglés C1 te permite expresar exactamente esa relación entre evidencia, postura y límite.
