content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 36 del curso A1** (*Musical Instruments*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Instrumentos musicales A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-36-instrumentos-musicales)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 36 — Musical Instruments](/curso-a1/unit-36)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Play the + instrument](/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/a1-unit36-play-the.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: play the](#leccion-1--gramatica-play-the)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: instrumentos](#leccion-2--vocabulario-instrumentos)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Noah](#leccion-3--reading-noah)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Instruments](#leccion-4--listening-instruments)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: My instruments](#leccion-5--writing-my-instruments)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: play the

**Objetivo:** *play the + instrument*, *plays*, *can play*, *the drums*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I play ____ piano. → *the / a / —*  
2. She plays ____ guitar. → *the / a / —*  
3. He plays ____ violin. → *the / a / —*  
4. Can you ____ the flute? → *play / plays / playing*  
5. They play ____ drums. → *the / a / —*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **the** — *play the piano*.  
2. **the**  
3. **the**  
4. **play** — *can + play*.  
5. **the** — *the drums* (plural).

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige

6. The pattern is ____. → a) play the + instrument · b) play instrument · c) do the instrument  
7. Correct sentence: ____. → a) I play the piano. · b) I play piano. · c) I play a piano always  
8. She ____ guitar. → a) plays the · b) play the · c) playing the  
9. I can ____ the flute. → a) play · b) plays · c) playing  
10. With drums we say ____. → a) the drums · b) the drum · c) a drums

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) play the + instrument**  
7. **a) I play the piano.**  
8. **a) plays the**  
9. **a) play**  
10. **a) the drums**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Ordena

11. I / play / the / piano.  
12. She / plays / the / guitar.  
13. He / can / play / the / flute.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. I play the piano.  
12. She plays the guitar.  
13. He can play the flute.

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. In A1 we usually say *play the piano* (with *the*). → True / False  
15. *Drums* takes *the* and is plural: *play the drums*. → True / False

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **True**  
15. **True**

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: instrumentos

**Objetivo:** piano, guitar, drums, violin, flute.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige el significado

1. *Piano* = ____. → a) keyboard instrument · b) wind instrument · c) only drums  
2. *Guitar* = ____. → a) string instrument with six strings · b) wind instrument · c) keyboard only  
3. *Drums* = ____. → a) You hit them with sticks. · b) You blow them. · c) You only press keys.  
4. *Violin* = ____. → a) small string instrument with a bow · b) a big flute · c) a piano  
5. *Flute* = ____. → a) wind instrument you blow · b) string instrument · c) drums

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) keyboard instrument**  
2. **a) string instrument with six strings**  
3. **a) You hit them with sticks.**  
4. **a) small string instrument with a bow**  
5. **a) wind instrument you blow**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–7 — Empareja

6. Empareja: piano / guitar / drums / violin / flute → play the piano · play the guitar · play the drums · play the violin · play the flute  
7. Empareja EN → ES: piano / guitar / drums / violin / flute → piano · guitarra · batería · violín · flauta

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **piano → play the piano** · **guitar → play the guitar** · **drums → play the drums** · **violin → play the violin** · **flute → play the flute**  
7. **piano → piano** · **guitar → guitarra** · **drums → batería** · **violin → violín** · **flute → flauta**

</details>

### Ejercicios 8–10 — Completa

8. I play ____ piano. → *the / a / —*  
9. She ____ the guitar. → *plays / play / playing*  
10. He plays ____ drums. → *the / a / —*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

8. **the**  
9. **plays**  
10. **the**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Definiciones

11. The pattern is ____. → a) play the + instrument · b) play + instrument without the · c) make the instrument  
12. Which is a wind instrument? → a) flute · b) piano · c) drums  
13. Which is a keyboard instrument? → a) piano · b) violin · c) flute

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) play the + instrument**  
12. **a) flute**  
13. **a) piano**

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Ordena

14. I / play / the / piano / and / the / guitar.  
15. She / can / play / the / violin.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. I play the piano and the guitar.  
15. She can play the violin.

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Noah

**Objetivo:** leer sobre los instrumentos de la familia de Noah.

### Texto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/reading-noah.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Noah"></audio>

> My name is Noah. I play the piano and the guitar. I started when I was eight. My sister plays the violin. She is very good. My brother plays the drums in a band. We sometimes play together at home. My mum can play the flute but she doesn't practice often. Music is important in our family.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. What is the writer's name? → a) Noah · b) Nick · c) Neil  
2. What does Noah play? → a) The piano and the guitar · b) Only the drums · c) Only the flute  
3. When did he start? → a) When he was eight · b) When he was seven · c) Two years ago  
4. What does his sister play? → a) The violin · b) The drums · c) The flute  
5. What does his brother play? → a) The drums · b) The piano · c) The violin

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Noah**  
2. **a) The piano and the guitar**  
3. **a) When he was eight**  
4. **a) The violin**  
5. **a) The drums**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Comprensión

6. Where does his brother play the drums? → a) In a band · b) Only at school · c) Never  
7. What can mum play? → a) The flute · b) The piano · c) The drums  
8. Does mum practice often? → a) No · b) Yes · c) Every day  
9. When do they play together? → a) Sometimes at home · b) Every day at school · c) Never  
10. We say play ____ piano. → a) the · b) a · c) —

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) In a band**  
7. **a) The flute**  
8. **a) No**  
9. **a) Sometimes at home**  
10. **a) the**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Detalles

11. The text is about ____. → a) music and instruments in the family · b) free time shopping · c) sports  
12. Which word means "batería"? → a) drums · b) flute · c) violin  
13. His sister ____ the violin. → a) is very good at · b) hates · c) never plays  
14. Music ____ in their family. → a) is important · b) is boring · c) is not important  
15. Noah can also ____. → a) play the guitar · b) play the drums · c) play the flute

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) music and instruments in the family**  
12. **a) drums**  
13. **a) is very good at**  
14. **a) is important**  
15. **a) play the guitar**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Instruments

**Objetivo:** escuchar un diálogo sobre instrumentos.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/listening-instruments.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Instruments"></audio>

> **A:** Do you play any instrument?  
> **B:** Yes, I play the piano and the guitar.  
> **A:** How long?  
> **B:** I started the piano when I was seven. I started the guitar two years ago.  
> **A:** Can your sister play any instrument?  
> **B:** She plays the violin. She is very good. My brother plays the drums. We all like music.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. What does B play? → a) The piano and the guitar · b) Only the drums · c) Only the flute  
2. When did B start the piano? → a) When he was seven · b) When he was eight · c) Last year  
3. When did B start the guitar? → a) Two years ago · b) When he was seven · c) Yesterday  
4. What does his sister play? → a) The violin · b) The drums · c) The piano  
5. What does his brother play? → a) The drums · b) The flute · c) The guitar

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) The piano and the guitar**  
2. **a) When he was seven**  
3. **a) Two years ago**  
4. **a) The violin**  
5. **a) The drums**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Is his sister good? → a) Yes, she is very good. · b) No · c) The audio doesn't say  
7. The dialogue is ____. → a) about musical instruments · b) about shopping · c) about sports  
8. She ____ the violin. He ____ the drums. → a) plays; plays · b) play; play · c) playing; playing  
9. We say play ____ piano. → a) the · b) a · c) —  
10. They ____ music. → a) all like · b) don't like · c) hate

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) Yes, she is very good.**  
7. **a) about musical instruments**  
8. **a) plays; plays**  
9. **a) the**  
10. **a) all like**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. A ____ about instruments. → a) asks · b) ask · c) asking  
12. "How long?" asks about ____. → a) How long (ago) · b) Where · c) Who  
13. B started ____ when he was seven. → a) the piano · b) the drums · c) the flute  
14. How many instruments are mentioned? → a) Four: piano, guitar, violin and drums · b) Two · c) One  
15. His brother can ____. → a) play the drums · b) play the flute · c) play the piano

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) asks**  
12. **a) How long (ago)**  
13. **a) the piano**  
14. **a) Four: piano, guitar, violin and drums**  
15. **a) play the drums**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: My instruments

**Objetivo:** escribir sobre instrumentos con *play the*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I play ____ piano. → *the / a / —*  
2. She ____ the guitar. → *plays / play / playing*  
3. He plays ____ drums. → *the / a / —*  
4. Can you ____ the flute? → *play / plays / playing*  
5. They play ____ violin. → *the / a / —*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **the**  
2. **plays**  
3. **the**  
4. **play**  
5. **the**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. I / play / the / piano.  
7. She / plays / the / guitar / and / the / violin.  
8. He / can / play / the / flute.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. I play the piano.  
7. She plays the guitar and the violin.  
8. He can play the flute.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Escribe qué instrumentos tocas (usa *play the*).  
10. Pregunta y respuesta: *Do you play any instrument?*  
11. Escribe: algo que tocas + algo que te gustaría tocar.  
12. Escribe sobre un familiar: *My sister/brother plays…*  
13. Párrafo corto (4 frases) sobre música en tu familia o sobre ti.  
14. Tres frases: *I / She / He play(s) the…*  
15. Pregunta con *Can you…?* y respuesta corta.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. I play the piano and the guitar.  
10. Do you play any instrument? Yes, I play the piano.  
11. I play the guitar. I would like to play the piano.  
12. My sister plays the violin.  
13. I play the piano. I started when I was eight. My brother plays the drums. We like music.  
14. I play the piano. She plays the guitar. He plays the drums.  
15. Can you play the guitar? No, I can't.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Patrón | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **play the + instrument** | I play **the** piano. |
| **plays** (he/she) | She **plays** the guitar. |
| **can play** | He **can play** the flute. |
| **the drums** | They play **the drums**. |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Continúa con la [**Unidad 37 — Talent & Skills**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-37-talent-skills): *good at*, *talent*, *skill*.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe 6–8 frases sobre instrumentos: *I play the…*, *She plays the…*, *Can you play…?*

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 37 del curso A1** (*Talent & Skills*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Talent & Skills A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-37-talent-skills)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 37 — Talent & Skills](/curso-a1/unit-37)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Skill levels](/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/a1-unit37-skill-levels.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: very well / quite well / not at all](#leccion-1--gramatica-very-well--quite-well--not-at-all)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: talentos](#leccion-2--vocabulario-talentos)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Lisa](#leccion-3--reading-lisa)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Skills](#leccion-4--listening-skills)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: My skills](#leccion-5--writing-my-skills)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: very well / quite well / not at all

**Objetivo:** niveles de habilidad con *can* + *very well / quite well / not at all*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I can sing ____. → *very well / not at all / quite slow*  
2. She cooks ____. → *quite well / at all / very bad*  
3. He can't dance ____. → *at all / very well / quite well*  
4. I play the guitar ____. → *quite well / at all / very nothing*  
5. She speaks English ____. → *well / wells / at*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **very well**  
2. **quite well**  
3. **at all** — *can't … at all*.  
4. **quite well**  
5. **well**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige

6. High ability = ____. → a) very well · b) not at all · c) never well  
7. Medium ability = ____. → a) quite well · b) not at all · c) very never  
8. I ____ very well. → a) can draw · b) drawing · c) draws  
9. *Not at all* means ____. → a) nothing / no ability · b) medium · c) high  
10. She can ____ English very well. → a) speak · b) speaks · c) speaking

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) very well**  
7. **a) quite well**  
8. **a) can draw**  
9. **a) nothing / no ability**  
10. **a) speak**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Ordena

11. I / can / sing / very well.  
12. She / cooks / quite well.  
13. He / can't / dance / at all.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. I can sing very well.  
12. She cooks quite well.  
13. He can't dance at all.

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. *Very well* = high level; *quite well* = medium; *not at all* = zero. → True / False  
15. We say *I can't dance at all* (not *I can't dance not at all*). → True / False

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **True**  
15. **True**

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: talentos

**Objetivo:** *creative, hardworking, skill, talent, good at, bad at*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige el significado

1. *Creative* = ____. → a) has new ideas · b) works slowly · c) can't do anything  
2. *Hardworking* = ____. → a) works a lot · b) lazy · c) only creative  
3. *Fast* = ____. → a) quick · b) slow · c) creative  
4. *Skill* = ____. → a) something you can do well · b) only music · c) only sport  
5. *Talent* = ____. → a) natural ability · b) homework · c) a room

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) has new ideas**  
2. **a) works a lot**  
3. **a) quick**  
4. **a) something you can do well**  
5. **a) natural ability**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–7 — Empareja

6. Empareja: very well / quite well / not at all / creative / hardworking → high · medium · no ability · new ideas · works hard  
7. Empareja actividad → área: sing / draw / cook / drive / swim → music · art · food · car · water

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **very well → high** · **quite well → medium** · **not at all → no ability** · **creative → new ideas** · **hardworking → works hard**  
7. **sing → music** · **draw → art** · **cook → food** · **drive → car** · **swim → water**

</details>

### Ejercicios 8–10 — Completa

8. She is ____ — she has new ideas. → *creative / slow / bad*  
9. He works ____. → *hard / hardly never / soft*  
10. I can't ____ at all. → *dance / dancing / dances*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

8. **creative**  
9. **hard**  
10. **dance**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Definiciones

11. *Slow* means ____. → a) not fast · b) creative · c) hardworking  
12. *Good at* means ____. → a) can do well · b) can't do · c) never try  
13. *Bad at* means ____. → a) can't do well · b) excellent · c) creative

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) not fast**  
12. **a) can do well**  
13. **a) can't do well**

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Ordena

14. She / is / good / at / drawing.  
15. He / can / run / very / fast.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. She is good at drawing.  
15. He can run very fast.

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Lisa

**Objetivo:** leer sobre talentos en la familia de Lisa.

### Texto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/reading-lisa.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Lisa"></audio>

> My name is Lisa. I can sing very well and I play the piano quite well. My brother can cook very well — he is creative. I can't draw at all. My sister is hardworking and she speaks English very well. We all have different skills.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. What is the writer's name? → a) Lisa · b) Lara · c) Lucy  
2. Can Lisa sing? → a) Yes, very well. · b) No · c) Quite well only  
3. How well does she play the piano? → a) Quite well. · b) Not at all. · c) Very badly.  
4. Who can cook very well? → a) Her brother. · b) Her sister. · c) Lisa  
5. Can Lisa draw? → a) No, not at all. · b) Yes, very well. · c) Quite well.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Lisa**  
2. **a) Yes, very well.**  
3. **a) Quite well.**  
4. **a) Her brother.**  
5. **a) No, not at all.**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Comprensión

6. How is her sister? → a) Hardworking. · b) Lazy. · c) Bad at English.  
7. Does her sister speak English well? → a) Yes, very well. · b) No · c) Not at all  
8. The text is about ____. → a) different skills in a family · b) shopping · c) instruments only  
9. Her brother is ____. → a) creative · b) bad at cooking · c) not creative  
10. Which word means "creativo"? → a) creative · b) hardworking · c) slow

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) Hardworking.**  
7. **a) Yes, very well.**  
8. **a) different skills in a family**  
9. **a) creative**  
10. **a) creative**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Detalles

11. We all ____ different skills. → a) have · b) has · c) having  
12. Lisa ____ draw at all. → a) can't · b) can · c) cans  
13. Lisa sings ____. → a) Very well. · b) Not at all. · c) Never  
14. How many people are mentioned? → a) Three: Lisa, her brother, and her sister. · b) One · c) Five  
15. *Skills* means ____. → a) things you can do well · b) only sports · c) only music

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) have**  
12. **a) can't**  
13. **a) Very well.**  
14. **a) Three: Lisa, her brother, and her sister.**  
15. **a) things you can do well**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Skills

**Objetivo:** escuchar un diálogo sobre habilidades.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/listening-skills.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Skills"></audio>

> **A:** Can you sing?  
> **B:** Yes, I can. I sing very well.  
> **A:** What about cooking?  
> **B:** I cook quite well. My brother can't dance at all. He is good at drawing, though.  
> **A:** Are you creative?  
> **B:** Yes, we are. We all have different skills.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Can B sing? → a) Yes, very well. · b) No · c) Not at all  
2. How well does B cook? → a) Quite well. · b) Not at all. · c) Very badly.  
3. Can B's brother dance? → a) No, not at all. · b) Yes, very well. · c) Quite well.  
4. What is the brother good at? → a) Drawing. · b) Singing. · c) Cooking.  
5. Are they creative? → a) Yes. · b) No. · c) The audio doesn't say.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Yes, very well.**  
2. **a) Quite well.**  
3. **a) No, not at all.**  
4. **a) Drawing.**  
5. **a) Yes.**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. We all ____ different skills. → a) have · b) has · c) having  
7. The dialogue is ____. → a) about skills and abilities · b) about food only · c) about school  
8. B sings ____. → a) Very well. · b) Not at all. · c) Never  
9. A ____ about singing, cooking and creativity. → a) asks · b) ask · c) asking  
10. The brother is good at ____. → a) drawing · b) dancing · c) singing

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) have**  
7. **a) about skills and abilities**  
8. **a) Very well.**  
9. **a) asks**  
10. **a) drawing**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. B cooks ____. → a) quite well · b) at all · c) very never  
12. The brother can't ____ at all. → a) dance · b) dancing · c) dances  
13. Which word adds contrast? → a) Though. · b) And only. · c) Because.  
14. Does B give ability levels? → a) Yes; “very well” and “quite well.” · b) No · c) Only “not at all”  
15. They all have different ____. → a) skills · b) skillses · c) skillful

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) quite well**  
12. **a) dance**  
13. **a) Though.**  
14. **a) Yes; “very well” and “quite well.”**  
15. **a) skills**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: My skills

**Objetivo:** escribir sobre tus habilidades y las de otros.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I can sing ____. → *very well / at all / quite never*  
2. She cooks ____. → *quite well / at all / very nothing*  
3. He ____ draw very well. → *can / cans / canning*  
4. I am ____ at drawing. → *good / well / goods*  
5. She can't ____ at all. → *dance / dancing / dances*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **very well**  
2. **quite well**  
3. **can**  
4. **good**  
5. **dance**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. I / can / cook / quite well.  
7. She / is / creative / and / hardworking.  
8. He / can't / swim / at all.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. I can cook quite well.  
7. She is creative and hardworking.  
8. He can't swim at all.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Escribe algo que haces *very well*.  
10. Escribe algo que *can't … at all*.  
11. Dos frases: *very well* + *quite well*.  
12. Usa *good at* y *bad at*.  
13. Párrafo corto (4–5 frases) sobre tus skills.  
14. Dos preguntas *Can you…?* con respuesta.  
15. Escribe sobre un amigo/a.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. I can sing very well.  
10. I can't dance at all.  
11. I can cook very well. I play the guitar quite well.  
12. I am good at drawing. I am bad at singing.  
13. I can speak English quite well. I can cook very well. I can't sing at all. I am good at drawing. I am creative.  
14. Can you swim? Yes, I can. Can you drive? No, I can't.  
15. My friend can play the piano very well. He is good at sports.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Nivel | Frase |
| :--- | :--- |
| Alto | I can sing **very well**. |
| Medio | I cook **quite well**. |
| Cero | I can't dance **at all**. |
| Adjetivo | I am **good at** drawing. |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Continúa con la [**Unidad 38 — Pedir permiso**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso): *Can I…?*, *May I…?*.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe 6–8 frases reales sobre ti y tu familia con *very well*, *quite well* y *not at all*.

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 38 del curso A1** (*Asking for Permission*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Pedir permiso A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 38 — Asking for Permission](/curso-a1/unit-38)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Can I / May I](/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/a1-unit38-can-may.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: Can I…? May I…?](#leccion-1--gramatica-can-i-may-i)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: frases educadas](#leccion-2--vocabulario-frases-educadas)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Permission](#leccion-3--reading-permission)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: In class](#leccion-4--listening-in-class)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: Polite requests](#leccion-5--writing-polite-requests)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: Can I…? May I…?

**Objetivo:** pedir permiso con *Can I…?* y *May I…?*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. ____ I use the phone? → *Can / Do / Am*  
2. May I ____ the window? → *open / opens / opening*  
3. Can I borrow ____ pen? → *your / you / yours*  
4. ____ I ask a question? → *May / Do / Am*  
5. No, ____ can't right now. → *you / your / yours*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Can** (*May* también vale).  
2. **open** — *May I* + verbo base.  
3. **your**  
4. **May** (*Can* también vale).  
5. **you**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige

6. More formal permission: ____. → a) May I…? · b) I want · c) Give me  
7. After *Can I / May I* we use ____. → a) base verb (open, borrow) · b) -ing only · c) past tense  
8. *No, you can't* is a ____. → a) denial/refusal · b) greeting · c) thank you  
9. *Can I sit here?* — *sit* ____ correct. → a) is · b) are · c) am  
10. *Can I…?* is a ____. → a) request · b) order always · c) past story

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) May I…?**  
7. **a) base verb (open, borrow)**  
8. **a) denial/refusal**  
9. **a) is**  
10. **a) request**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Ordena

11. Can / I / use / the / phone?  
12. May / I / ask / a / question?  
13. No, / you / can't / right / now.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. Can I use the phone?  
12. May I ask a question?  
13. No, you can't right now.

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. *Can I…?* and *May I…?* both ask for permission. → True / False  
15. After *Can I / May I* we use the base verb (*open*, not *opens*). → True / False

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **True**  
15. **True**

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: frases educadas

**Objetivo:** *please, excuse me, borrow, of course, permission*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige el significado

1. *Please* = ____. → a) polite word for requests · b) a refusal · c) a goodbye  
2. *Excuse me* = ____. → a) to get attention politely · b) to say no · c) to say thank you  
3. *Borrow* = ____. → a) use and return · b) keep forever · c) break  
4. *Of course* = ____. → a) yes, sure · b) no · c) maybe never  
5. *Permission* = ____. → a) allowed to do something · b) a school subject · c) a book

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) polite word for requests**  
2. **a) to get attention politely**  
3. **a) use and return**  
4. **a) yes, sure**  
5. **a) allowed to do something**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–7 — Empareja

6. Empareja: Can I…? / May I…? / Please / Of course / Excuse me → informal request · formal request · polite · yes, sure · get attention  
7. Empareja verbo → objeto típico: borrow / use / open / sit / ask → pen, book · bathroom, phone · door, window · here · question

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **Can I…? → informal request** · **May I…? → formal request** · **Please → polite** · **Of course → yes, sure** · **Excuse me → get attention**  
7. **borrow → pen, book** · **use → bathroom, phone** · **open → door, window** · **sit → here** · **ask → question**

</details>

### Ejercicios 8–10 — Completa

8. Can I use the bathroom, ____? → *please / pleaseing / pleased*  
9. ____ me, may I come in? → *Excuse / Excuses / Excused*  
10. Yes, ____ course. → *of / off / on*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

8. **please**  
9. **Excuse**  
10. **of**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Definiciones

11. A *request* is ____. → a) asking for something · b) saying goodbye · c) a number  
12. *Right now* means ____. → a) at this moment · b) yesterday · c) never  
13. Which is more formal? → a) May I ask a question? · b) Give me a question · c) I want question

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) asking for something**  
12. **a) at this moment**  
13. **a) May I ask a question?**

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Ordena

14. Can / I / borrow / your / eraser?  
15. Excuse / me, / may / I / come / in?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. Can I borrow your eraser?  
15. Excuse me, may I come in?

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Permission

**Objetivo:** leer sobre frases educadas en clase y en el trabajo.

### Texto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/reading-permission.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Permission"></audio>

> In class we use polite phrases. Can I use the bathroom? May I ask a question? At work we say please and thank you. Excuse me—can I borrow your pen? Of course. When we ask for permission, we are polite.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. Where do we use polite phrases first in the text? → a) In class · b) At home · c) At the park  
2. Which question is about the bathroom? → a) Can I use the bathroom? · b) May I ask a question? · c) Can I borrow your pen?  
3. Which question is more formal in the text? → a) May I ask a question? · b) Give me a question · c) I want a question  
4. At work we say ____. → a) please and thank you · b) only goodbye · c) nothing  
5. *Excuse me* helps to ____. → a) start a polite request · b) say no · c) close a door

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) In class**  
2. **a) Can I use the bathroom?**  
3. **a) May I ask a question?**  
4. **a) please and thank you**  
5. **a) start a polite request**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Comprensión

6. What does someone want to borrow? → a) a pen · b) a car · c) a house  
7. The answer to borrowing the pen is ____. → a) Of course · b) Never · c) No  
8. The text is about ____. → a) polite requests and permission · b) sports · c) food  
9. When we ask for ____, we are polite. → a) permission · b) money only · c) food only  
10. The last sentence says we are ____. → a) polite · b) angry · c) late

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) a pen**  
7. **a) Of course**  
8. **a) polite requests and permission**  
9. **a) permission**  
10. **a) polite**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Detalles

11. *Borrow* means ____. → a) use and return · b) keep forever · c) break  
12. We ____ permission. → a) ask for · b) ask to · c) ask of  
13. A friendly yes is ____. → a) Of course · b) Go away · c) Never  
14. The text shows examples ____. → a) both in the text · b) only at home · c) only in parks  
15. *Polite* means ____. → a) respectful; having good manners · b) rude · c) loud

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) use and return**  
12. **a) ask for**  
13. **a) Of course**  
14. **a) both in the text**  
15. **a) respectful; having good manners**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: In class

**Objetivo:** escuchar peticiones educadas en clase.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/listening-classroom.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: In class"></audio>

> **A:** Excuse me. Can I use the bathroom?  
> **B:** Yes, of course.  
> **A:** May I borrow your pen, please?  
> **B:** Sure. Here you are.  
> **A:** Thank you.  
> **B:** Can you close the door, please?  
> **A:** Of course. We use please and thank you in class.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. What does A ask first? → a) to use the bathroom · b) to open a window · c) to leave school  
2. What is B's first answer? → a) Yes, of course. · b) No · c) Maybe later  
3. What does A ask next? → a) to borrow a pen · b) to borrow a book · c) to sit down  
4. What does B say about the pen? → a) Sure. Here you are. · b) Never · c) Buy one  
5. What does A say after getting the pen? → a) Thank you. · b) Goodbye · c) Sorry

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) to use the bathroom**  
2. **a) Yes, of course.**  
3. **a) to borrow a pen**  
4. **a) Sure. Here you are.**  
5. **a) Thank you.**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. What does B ask A to do? → a) to close the door · b) to open the window · c) to leave  
7. Where do they use please and thank you? → a) in class · b) only at home · c) never  
8. How does A start? → a) Excuse me · b) Hey you · c) Give me  
9. *May I…?* is ____ than *Can I…?* in many situations. → a) more formal · b) less polite · c) incorrect  
10. *Here you are* means ____. → a) giving something · b) saying goodbye · c) refusing

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) to close the door**  
7. **a) in class**  
8. **a) Excuse me**  
9. **a) more formal**  
10. **a) giving something**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. May I borrow your pen, ____? → a) please · b) pleased · c) pleasing  
12. The dialogue is about ____. → a) polite requests in class · b) sports · c) food  
13. *Of course* means ____. → a) yes, of course · b) no · c) never  
14. How many permission requests does A make? → a) two: the bathroom and a pen · b) one · c) five  
15. Polite words in the dialogue include ____. → a) please, thank you, and excuse me · b) only goodbye · c) only no

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) please**  
12. **a) polite requests in class**  
13. **a) yes, of course**  
14. **a) two: the bathroom and a pen**  
15. **a) please, thank you, and excuse me**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: Polite requests

**Objetivo:** escribir peticiones de permiso y respuestas educadas.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. ____ I sit here? → *Can / Do / Am*  
2. May I ____ a question? → *ask / asks / asking*  
3. Yes, ____ course. → *of / off / on*  
4. Excuse ____, can I come in? → *me / my / I*  
5. Can I borrow ____ book? → *your / you / yours*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Can** (*May* también vale).  
2. **ask**  
3. **of**  
4. **me**  
5. **your**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. Can / I / sit / here?  
7. No, / you / can't / right / now.  
8. May / I / open / the / window?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. Can I sit here?  
7. No, you can't right now.  
8. May I open the window?

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Escribe una petición con *Can I…?*  
10. Escribe una petición más formal con *May I…?*  
11. Mini diálogo: pedir un boli + respuesta positiva.  
12. Empieza con *Excuse me* + *please*.  
13. Diálogo corto (4–5 líneas) en clase.  
14. Tres peticiones diferentes.  
15. Una negativa educada + una petición de ayuda.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. Can I use the bathroom?  
10. May I ask a question?  
11. Can I borrow your pen? Yes, of course. Here you are.  
12. Excuse me, can I use the computer, please?  
13. Can I open the window? Yes, of course. Thank you. Can you close it, please? Sure.  
14. Can I use the bathroom? May I ask a question? Can I borrow your book?  
15. No, you can't right now. Can you help me, please?

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Forma | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Can I…?** | permiso (común) | Can I use the bathroom? |
| **May I…?** | permiso (más formal) | May I ask a question? |
| **Please / Thank you** | cortesía | …please? / Thank you. |
| **Of course / Sure** | sí | Yes, of course. |
| **No, you can't** | no | No, you can't right now. |

---

Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 39 del curso A1** (*Outdoor Activities*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Outdoor Activities A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-39-outdoor-activities)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 39 — Outdoor Activities](/curso-a1/unit-39)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Present Continuous for plans](/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/a1-unit39-present-continuous-plans.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: planes futuros](#leccion-1--gramatica-planes-futuros)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: outdoor](#leccion-2--vocabulario-outdoor)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Family outdoors](#leccion-3--reading-family-outdoors)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Weekend plans](#leccion-4--listening-weekend-plans)

## Lección 1 — Gramática: planes futuros

**Objetivo:** Present Continuous para planes ya decididos (*I'm going camping…*).

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I ____ going camping next week. → *'m / is / are*  
2. She is ____ hiking on Saturday. → *going / go / goes*  
3. We are ____ cycling on Sunday. → *going / go / goes*  
4. He ____ fishing tomorrow. → *'s going / go / going*  
5. They are ____ to the mountains. → *going / go / goes*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **'m** (*am*)  
2. **going**  
3. **going**  
4. **'s going** (*is going*)  
5. **going**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige

6. Present Continuous here talks about ____. → a) plans already decided · b) past habits · c) only now this second  
7. The tense for these plans is ____. → a) Present Continuous · b) Past Simple · c) Present Perfect  
8. *I'm going camping next week* is ____. → a) a future plan · b) a past story · c) a command  
9. After *going* we often use ____. → a) an activity ending in -ing · b) only past verbs · c) nothing  
10. Correct: ____. → a) We're going hiking next week. · b) We going hike. · c) We goes hiking.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) plans already decided**  
7. **a) Present Continuous**  
8. **a) a future plan**  
9. **a) an activity ending in -ing**  
10. **a) We're going hiking next week.**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Ordena

11. I'm / going / camping / next week.  
12. She / is / going / cycling / on Sunday.  
13. They / are / going / fishing / tomorrow.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. I'm going camping next week.  
12. She is going cycling on Sunday.  
13. They are going fishing tomorrow.

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. *I'm going camping next week* can mean a future plan. → True / False  
15. We often add a time word: *tomorrow, on Saturday, next week*. → True / False

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **True**  
15. **True**

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: outdoor

**Objetivo:** *hiking, camping, cycling, fishing, tent, trail, backpack*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige el significado

1. *Hiking* = ____. → a) walking in nature or the mountains · b) sleeping in a tent · c) riding a bike  
2. *Camping* = ____. → a) sleeping outdoors in a tent · b) catching fish · c) driving a car  
3. *Cycling* = ____. → a) riding a bicycle · b) walking · c) swimming  
4. *Fishing* = ____. → a) catching fish · b) camping only · c) hiking only  
5. *Outdoor* = ____. → a) outside, in nature · b) inside a house · c) only at school

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) walking in nature or the mountains**  
2. **a) sleeping outdoors in a tent**  
3. **a) riding a bicycle**  
4. **a) catching fish**  
5. **a) outside, in nature**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–7 — Empareja

6. Empareja: hiking / camping / cycling / fishing / next week → walk in the mountains · tent · bicycle · fish · future  
7. Empareja objeto → actividad: tent / trail / bike / rod / backpack → camping · hiking · cycling · fishing · hiking/camping

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **hiking → walk in the mountains** · **camping → tent** · **cycling → bicycle** · **fishing → fish** · **next week → future**  
7. **tent → camping** · **trail → hiking** · **bike → cycling** · **rod → fishing** · **backpack → hiking/camping**

</details>

### Ejercicios 8–10 — Completa

8. I am ____ camping next week. → *going / go / goes*  
9. She is going ____ on Saturday. → *hiking / hike / hikes*  
10. We are ____ cycling next week. → *going / go / goes*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

8. **going**  
9. **hiking**  
10. **going**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Definiciones

11. A *trail* is ____. → a) a path for walking · b) a car · c) a fish  
12. A *tent* is ____. → a) a shelter used for camping · b) a bike · c) a book  
13. *Next weekend* is ____. → a) future time · b) past time · c) never

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) a path for walking**  
12. **a) a shelter used for camping**  
13. **a) future time**

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Ordena

14. I / am / going / hiking / on Saturday.  
15. We / are / going / cycling / next week.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. I am going hiking on Saturday.  
15. We are going cycling next week.

</details>

## Lección 3 — Reading: Family outdoors

**Objetivo:** leer planes outdoor de una familia.

### Texto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/reading-outdoors.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Family outdoors"></audio>

> I'm going camping next week with my family. We love outdoor activities. My brother is going hiking on Saturday, and my sister is going cycling on Sunday. My dad is going fishing tomorrow. We have a tent and backpacks. Next weekend, we are all going to the mountains.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. What is the writer doing next week? → a) Going camping · b) Going shopping · c) Staying home  
2. Who is the writer going with? → a) With the family · b) Alone · c) With classmates only  
3. What is the brother doing on Saturday? → a) Going hiking · b) Going fishing · c) Going cycling  
4. What is the sister doing on Sunday? → a) Going cycling · b) Going hiking · c) Going camping  
5. When is dad going fishing? → a) Tomorrow · b) Next year · c) Never

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Going camping**  
2. **a) With the family**  
3. **a) Going hiking**  
4. **a) Going cycling**  
5. **a) Tomorrow**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Comprensión

6. What equipment do they have? → a) A tent and backpacks · b) Only a car · c) Nothing  
7. Where are they going next weekend? → a) To the mountains · b) To the beach only · c) To school  
8. The text is about ____. → a) outdoor activities and future plans · b) food · c) work  
9. Which activity is walking in nature? → a) Hiking · b) Fishing · c) Cycling  
10. They ____ outdoor activities. → a) love · b) hate · c) ignore

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) A tent and backpacks**  
7. **a) To the mountains**  
8. **a) outdoor activities and future plans**  
9. **a) Hiking**  
10. **a) love**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Detalles

11. A *backpack* is ____. → a) a bag carried on your back · b) a tent · c) a bike  
12. Plans use ____. → a) I'm going / He is going · b) I go always past · c) I went only  
13. When are they all going to the mountains? → a) Next weekend · b) Yesterday · c) Never  
14. How many outdoor activities are named? → a) Four: camping, hiking, cycling, and fishing · b) One · c) Ten  
15. *Outdoor* means ____. → a) outside, in nature · b) indoors · c) underwater only

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) a bag carried on your back**  
12. **a) I'm going / He is going**  
13. **a) Next weekend**  
14. **a) Four: camping, hiking, cycling, and fishing**  
15. **a) outside, in nature**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Weekend plans

**Objetivo:** escuchar planes outdoor del fin de semana.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/listening-plans.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Weekend plans"></audio>

> **A:** What are you doing next weekend?  
> **B:** I'm going camping with my friends.  
> **A:** Nice! I'm going hiking on Saturday.  
> **B:** My brother is going cycling on Sunday. We love outdoor activities.  
> **A:** Me too. Next week, I'm going fishing.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. What is B doing next weekend? → a) Going camping · b) Going shopping · c) Working  
2. Who is B going with? → a) With friends · b) Alone · c) With teachers  
3. What is A doing on Saturday? → a) Going hiking · b) Going fishing · c) Going cycling  
4. What is B's brother doing on Sunday? → a) Going cycling · b) Going hiking · c) Going camping  
5. When is A going fishing? → a) Next week · b) Yesterday · c) Never

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Going camping**  
2. **a) With friends**  
3. **a) Going hiking**  
4. **a) Going cycling**  
5. **a) Next week**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. They ____ outdoor activities. → a) love · b) hate · c) ignore  
7. A says ____ after hearing they love outdoor activities. → a) Me too. · b) Never · c) Goodbye  
8. A's first reaction to camping is ____. → a) Nice! · b) Boring · c) No  
9. The dialogue is about ____. → a) future outdoor plans · b) past jobs · c) food only  
10. *I'm going camping* here is ____. → a) a future plan · b) a past habit · c) a command

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) love**  
7. **a) Me too.**  
8. **a) Nice!**  
9. **a) future outdoor plans**  
10. **a) a future plan**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. A's first question is ____. → a) What are you doing next weekend? · b) Where were you? · c) Who are you?  
12. *Cycling* means ____. → a) riding a bicycle · b) walking · c) sleeping  
13. How many activities are mentioned? → a) Four: camping, hiking, cycling, and fishing · b) One · c) Zero  
14. B says I ____ camping. → a) 'm going · b) go always · c) went  
15. *Me too* means ____. → a) I agree / the same for me · b) I disagree · c) goodbye

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) What are you doing next weekend?**  
12. **a) riding a bicycle**  
13. **a) Four: camping, hiking, cycling, and fishing**  
14. **a) 'm going**  
15. **a) I agree / the same for me**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: My outdoor plans

**Objetivo:** escribir planes outdoor con Present Continuous.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I ____ going camping next week. → *'m / is / are*  
2. She is ____ hiking on Saturday. → *going / go / goes*  
3. We are ____ fishing tomorrow. → *going / go / goes*  
4. We love ____ activities. → *outdoor / indoors / indoor*  
5. He ____ going cycling on Sunday. → *'s / am / are*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **'m**  
2. **going**  
3. **going**  
4. **outdoor**  
5. **'s**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. I'm / going / camping / next week.  
7. They / are / going / to the mountains / next weekend.  
8. My dad / is / going / fishing / tomorrow.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. I'm going camping next week.  
7. They are going to the mountains next weekend.  
8. My dad is going fishing tomorrow.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Escribe tu plan: *I'm going… next week.*  
10. Escribe sobre un familiar: *My brother/sister is going…*  
11. Dos planes: mañana + próximo fin de semana.  
12. Frase con *love outdoor activities* + un hobby.  
13. Párrafo corto (4 frases) sobre planes outdoor.  
14. Tres personas: *He / She / They are going…*  
15. Pregunta y respuesta: *What are you doing next weekend?*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. I'm going camping next week.  
10. My brother is going hiking on Saturday.  
11. I'm going cycling tomorrow. We are going camping next weekend.  
12. We love outdoor activities. I like hiking.  
13. I'm going camping next weekend. My friend is going hiking on Saturday. We have a tent. We love outdoor activities.  
14. He is going fishing tomorrow. She is going cycling on Sunday. They are going camping next week.  
15. What are you doing next weekend? I'm going hiking.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Actividad | Plan |
| :--- | :--- |
| **camping** | I'm going camping next week. |
| **hiking** | She's going hiking on Saturday. |
| **cycling** | He's going cycling on Sunday. |
| **fishing** | Dad is going fishing tomorrow. |
| Tiempo | tomorrow / on Saturday / next week |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Continúa con la [**Unidad 40 — Repaso Módulo 4**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-40-repaso-modulo-4): *can*, *play/go/do*, frecuencia, conectores, free time, instrumentos, skills y permiso.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe 6–8 frases de planes outdoor con Present Continuous y un tiempo futuro.

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 40 del curso A1** (*Module 4 Review — Abilities & Interests*) con **soluciones comentadas**.

> **Guía teórica:** [Repaso Módulo 4 A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-40-repaso-modulo-4)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 40 — Module 4 Review](/curso-a1/unit-40)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Module 4 map](/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/a1-unit40-module-map.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: repaso](#leccion-1--gramatica-repaso)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: repaso](#leccion-2--vocabulario-repaso)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Tom](#leccion-3--reading-tom)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Review](#leccion-4--listening-review)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: Module 4](#leccion-5--writing-module-4)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: repaso

**Objetivo:** *can*, *play/go/do*, frecuencia, *and/but/because*, planes (*I'm going…*).

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I ____ swim very well. → *can / cans / canning*  
2. She ____ football every Saturday. → *plays / play / playing*  
3. We ____ swimming every week. → *go / goes / going*  
4. He ____ yoga in the morning. → *does / do / doing*  
5. I ____ going camping next week. → *'m / is / are*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **can**  
2. **plays**  
3. **go**  
4. **does**  
5. **'m** (*am*)

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige

6. I ____ have breakfast at 8. → a) always · b) never never · c) at all  
7. I like tea ____ I don't like coffee. → a) but · b) and · c) because  
8. We ____ football (ball sport). → a) play · b) go · c) do  
9. Future plan form: ____. → a) am/is/are going + -ing · b) only past · c) will always required here  
10. *Because* introduces a ____. → a) reason · b) contrast · c) greeting

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) always**  
7. **a) but**  
8. **a) play**  
9. **a) am/is/are going + -ing**  
10. **a) reason**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Ordena

11. I / can / play / the / guitar / very well.  
12. She / always / goes / running / on Mondays.  
13. I / am / going / camping / next weekend / because / I / love / nature.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. I can play the guitar very well.  
12. She always goes running on Mondays.  
13. I am going camping next weekend because I love nature.

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. *Play* + ball sports; *go* + -ing activities; *do* + yoga/exercise. → True / False  
15. *Can I…?* asks for permission; *I'm going camping* can be a future plan. → True / False

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **True**  
15. **True**

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: repaso

**Objetivo:** deportes, frecuencia, permiso, conectores y planes.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige el significado

1. *Play* often goes with ____. → a) sports with a ball · b) only yoga · c) only camping  
2. *Go* often goes with ____. → a) activities ending in -ing · b) only football · c) only piano  
3. *Do* often goes with ____. → a) yoga / exercise / gymnastics · b) only tennis · c) only drums  
4. *Always* means ____. → a) 100% of the time · b) 0% · c) never  
5. *May I…?* is often ____ than *Can I…?*. → a) more formal · b) less polite · c) incorrect

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) sports with a ball**  
2. **a) activities ending in -ing**  
3. **a) yoga / exercise / gymnastics**  
4. **a) 100% of the time**  
5. **a) more formal**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–7 — Empareja

6. Empareja: play / go / do / can / going → football, tennis · swimming, camping · yoga · ability · future plan  
7. Empareja: and / but / because / very well / of course → addition · contrast · reason · high level · yes, sure

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **play → football, tennis** · **go → swimming, camping** · **do → yoga** · **can → ability** · **going → future plan**  
7. **and → addition** · **but → contrast** · **because → reason** · **very well → high level** · **of course → yes, sure**

</details>

### Ejercicios 8–10 — Completa

8. I ____ have breakfast at 8. → *always / never never / at*  
9. Can I ____ your pen? → *borrow / borrows / borrowing*  
10. We are ____ camping next week. → *going / go / goes*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

8. **always**  
9. **borrow**  
10. **going**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Definiciones

11. *Never* means ____. → a) 0% · b) 100% · c) sometimes  
12. *Excuse me* is ____. → a) a polite way to start a request · b) a refusal · c) a sport  
13. Outdoor activities include ____. → a) hiking, camping, fishing · b) only homework · c) only TV

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) 0%**  
12. **a) a polite way to start a request**  
13. **a) hiking, camping, fishing**

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Ordena

14. I / usually / go / swimming / on Fridays.  
15. We / are / going / camping / because / we / love / nature.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. I usually go swimming on Fridays.  
15. We are going camping because we love nature.

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Tom

**Objetivo:** leer un texto que mezcla habilidad, deportes, frecuencia, planes y permiso.

### Texto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/reading-tom.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Tom"></audio>

> My name is Tom. I can play the guitar quite well and I play football every Saturday. I always do yoga in the morning because I like it. Next week I'm going camping with my friends. Can I use the bathroom? Yes, of course — we use polite phrases every day.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. What is the writer's name? → a) Tom · b) Tim · c) Ted  
2. Can he play the guitar? → a) Yes, quite well. · b) No · c) Not at all  
3. When does he play football? → a) Every Saturday. · b) Never · c) Every Monday  
4. When does he do yoga? → a) Always in the morning. · b) Never · c) Only at night  
5. Why does he do yoga? → a) Because he likes it. · b) Because he hates it. · c) The text doesn't say

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Tom**  
2. **a) Yes, quite well.**  
3. **a) Every Saturday.**  
4. **a) Always in the morning.**  
5. **a) Because he likes it.**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Comprensión

6. What is he doing next week? → a) Going camping. · b) Going shopping. · c) Staying home  
7. Who is he going with? → a) With friends. · b) Alone · c) With teachers  
8. Which permission question appears? → a) Can I use the bathroom? · b) May I leave forever? · c) Can I drive?  
9. *Because* introduces ____. → a) a reason · b) a contrast · c) a greeting  
10. With football we use ____. → a) play · b) go · c) do

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) Going camping.**  
7. **a) With friends.**  
8. **a) Can I use the bathroom?**  
9. **a) a reason**  
10. **a) play**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Detalles

11. *And* connects ____. → a) “I can play…” and “I play football”; two positive ideas · b) only contrast · c) only refusal  
12. *Of course* means ____. → a) yes, sure · b) no · c) never  
13. The text reviews ____. → a) several Module 4 topics · b) only past tense · c) only food  
14. *I'm going camping* is ____. → a) a future plan · b) a past habit · c) a command  
15. Polite phrases include ____. → a) please, thank you, Can I…? · b) only goodbye · c) only no

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) “I can play…” and “I play football”; two positive ideas**  
12. **a) yes, sure**  
13. **a) several Module 4 topics**  
14. **a) a future plan**  
15. **a) please, thank you, Can I…?**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Review

**Objetivo:** escuchar un diálogo de repaso del Módulo 4.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/listening-review.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Review"></audio>

> **A:** Can you swim?  
> **B:** Yes, I can. I go swimming every week.  
> **A:** I always play tennis on Saturdays, but I don't like football.  
> **B:** I'm going camping next weekend because I love nature. May I borrow your torch?  
> **A:** Of course.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Can B swim? → a) Yes. · b) No. · c) The audio doesn't say  
2. How often does B go swimming? → a) Every week. · b) Never. · c) Once a year  
3. What does A always play on Saturdays? → a) Tennis. · b) Football. · c) Yoga  
4. Does A like football? → a) No. · b) Yes. · c) Always  
5. Which connector shows contrast? → a) but · b) and · c) because

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Yes.**  
2. **a) Every week.**  
3. **a) Tennis.**  
4. **a) No.**  
5. **a) but**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. What is B doing next weekend? → a) Going camping. · b) Going shopping. · c) Working  
7. Why is B going camping? → a) Because B loves nature. · b) Because B hates nature. · c) The audio doesn't say  
8. What does B want to borrow? → a) A torch. · b) A car. · c) A house  
9. Which permission form does B use? → a) May I borrow…? · b) Give me · c) I take  
10. A's answer is ____. → a) Of course. · b) Never. · c) Goodbye

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) Going camping.**  
7. **a) Because B loves nature.**  
8. **a) A torch.**  
9. **a) May I borrow…?**  
10. **a) Of course.**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. With swimming we often use ____. → a) go + swimming · b) play swimming · c) do football  
12. *Always* is ____. → a) an adverb of frequency · b) a sport · c) a place  
13. A *torch* is ____. → a) a light used for camping or in the dark · b) a ball · c) a book  
14. The dialogue reviews ____. → a) can, play/go, frequency, but/because, plans, permission · b) only past · c) only food  
15. *I'm going camping* uses ____. → a) Present Continuous for the future · b) Past Simple · c) Present Perfect

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) go + swimming**  
12. **a) an adverb of frequency**  
13. **a) a light used for camping or in the dark**  
14. **a) can, play/go, frequency, but/because, plans, permission**  
15. **a) Present Continuous for the future**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: Module 4

**Objetivo:** escribir frases que combinen los temas del Módulo 4.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I ____ cook very well. → *can / cans / canning*  
2. She ____ football every Saturday. → *plays / play / playing*  
3. We ____ swimming on Mondays. → *go / goes / going*  
4. I ____ do yoga in the morning. → *always / never never / at*  
5. I like tea ____ I don't like coffee. → *but / and / because*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **can**  
2. **plays**  
3. **go**  
4. **always**  
5. **but**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. I'm / going / camping / next week.  
7. Can / I / borrow / your / pen, / please?  
8. I / do / yoga / in the morning / because / I / like / it.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. I'm going camping next week.  
7. Can I borrow your pen, please?  
8. I do yoga in the morning because I like it.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Escribe una habilidad con *can* + *very/quite well*.  
10. Escribe un deporte con *play* + frecuencia.  
11. Dos frases: *and* + *but*.  
12. Un plan outdoor con Present Continuous.  
13. Párrafo corto (4–5 frases) mezclando can, frecuencia, plan y permiso.  
14. Mini diálogo de permiso.  
15. Frase con *because*.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. I can cook very well.  
10. I play football every Saturday.  
11. I like tea and coffee. I play tennis, but I don't like football.  
12. I'm going camping next week.  
13. I can swim well. I always go swimming on Mondays because I love it. Next weekend I'm going hiking. Can I use the bathroom? Yes, of course.  
14. Can I borrow your book? Yes, of course. Here you are.  
15. I do yoga because I like it and it is relaxing.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **can** | I can swim very well. |
| **play / go / do** | play football · go swimming · do yoga |
| **frecuencia** | always / usually / often / sometimes / never |
| **conectores** | and / but / because |
| **planes** | I'm going camping next week. |
| **permiso** | Can I…? / May I…? Of course. |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Continúa con la [**Unidad 41 — At the Airport**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-41-aeropuerto-must-should): *must*, *should*, check-in, passport, boarding pass.

Antes de pasar de módulo, escribe un párrafo de 8–10 frases que combine al menos cinco temas del Módulo 4.

faqs.question: ¿Qué ejercicios incluye la Unidad 1 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: Cinco lecciones con 15 actividades cada una: gramática (to be con I/you), vocabulario de saludos y datos personales, reading (María), listening (Carlos) y writing (completar, ordenar y presentarte).

faqs.question: ¿Cómo uso este artículo?

faqs.question: ¿I am o You are?
faqs.answer: Con I siempre am (I am a student). Con you siempre are (You are from Spain). My name va con is (My name is Ana).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico en el curso?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 1 del curso A1 de Linguafly: ejercicios interactivos de gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 1 del curso A1** (*Saludos e información personal*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Saludos y presentarse A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-1-saludos-presentarse)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 1 — Saludos e información personal](/curso-a1/unit-1)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![I am / You are](/blog/curso-a1/unit-1/a1-unit1-to-be-i-you.png)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: verbo *to be* (I / You)

### 1. Completa: I ____ Maria.

Opciones: am · are · is

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**am** — Con *I* siempre usamos **am**: *I am Maria.*
</details>

### 2. ¿Qué frase es correcta?

a) I am twenty years old.  
b) I twenty am years old.  
c) I years old am twenty.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**a) I am twenty years old.** — En inglés: *I am* + edad + *years old* (no *have*).
</details>

### 3. Completa: I ____ a student.

Opciones: am · are · is

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**am** — *I am a student.*
</details>

### 4. Elige la forma correcta para “My name is…”

a) My name am Carlos.  
b) My name is Carlos.  
c) My name are Carlos.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) My name is Carlos.** — Después de *My name* va **is**.
</details>

### 5. Completa: You ____ my friend.

Opciones: am · are · is

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**are** — Con *you* usamos **are**: *You are my friend.*
</details>

### 6. ¿Qué frase es correcta?

a) You is from Spain.  
b) You are from Spain.  
c) You am from Spain.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) You are from Spain.** — *are* con *you*; *am* solo con *I*; *is* con *he/she/it*.
</details>

### 7. Completa: I ____ from Madrid.

Opciones: am · are · is

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**am** — *I am from Madrid.*
</details>

### 8. Completa: I ____ a teacher.

Opciones: am · is · are

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**am** — *I am a teacher.*
</details>

### 9. Completa: You ____ twenty-five years old.

Opciones: am · are · is

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**are** — *You are twenty-five years old.*
</details>

### 10. ¿Qué frase es correcta?

a) You are my friend.  
b) You am my friend.  
c) You is my friend.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**a) You are my friend.**
</details>

### 11. Ordena: name / My / is / Ana.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**My name is Ana.**
</details>

### 12. Ordena: am / I / from / Barcelona.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**I am from Barcelona.**
</details>

### 13. Ordena: years old / thirty / am / I

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**I am thirty years old.**
</details>

### 14. ¿Es correcta la frase *You am my teacher*?

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Falso.** Debe ser *You **are** my teacher.*
</details>

### 15. ¿Es correcta la frase *I am from Spain*?

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Verdadero.** *I am from* + país es correcto.
</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: presentación y saludos

### 1. ¿Cómo se dice «nombre» en inglés?

a) age · b) name · c) city · d) country

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) name**
</details>

### 2. Completa: I am thirty ____ .

a) year · b) years · c) years old · d) age

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) years old** — *I am thirty years old.*
</details>

### 3. ¿Qué palabra significa «de» (origen)?

a) to · b) from · c) in · d) at

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) from** — *I am from Madrid.*
</details>

### 4. ¿Qué dices para saludar por la mañana?

a) Hello · b) Good morning · c) Goodbye · d) Good night

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) Good morning** (también puedes decir *Hello*, pero el saludo típico de la mañana es *Good morning*).
</details>

### 5. ¿Qué palabra significa «trabajo» / «empleo»?

a) name · b) age · c) job · d) city

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) job**
</details>

### 6. ¿Cómo se dice «Encantado de conocerte»?

a) Hello · b) Goodbye · c) Nice to meet you · d) How are you?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) Nice to meet you**
</details>

### 7. Empareja

| Inglés | Español |
| :--- | :--- |
| Hello | Hola |
| Name | Nombre |
| Friend | Amigo |
| Student | Estudiante |
| Teacher | Profesor |

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

Hello → Hola · Name → Nombre · Friend → Amigo · Student → Estudiante · Teacher → Profesor
</details>

### 8. Empareja

| Inglés | Español |
| :--- | :--- |
| From | De (origen) |
| City | Ciudad |
| Country | País |
| Years old | años (edad) |
| Goodbye | Adiós |

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

From → De (origen) · City → Ciudad · Country → País · Years old → años (edad) · Goodbye → Adiós
</details>

### 9. Empareja (saludos según la hora)

| Inglés | Español |
| :--- | :--- |
| Good morning | Buenos días |
| Good afternoon | Buenas tardes |
| Good evening | Buenas tardes/noches (al llegar) |
| Good night | Buenas noches (al despedirse) |

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

Good morning → Buenos días · Good afternoon → Buenas tardes · Good evening → Buenas tardes/noches · Good night → Buenas noches
</details>

### 10. Empareja

| Inglés | Español |
| :--- | :--- |
| My | Mi |
| Your | Tu |
| Happy | Feliz |
| Nice | Encantado / agradable |

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

My → Mi · Your → Tu · Happy → Feliz · Nice → Encantado / agradable
</details>

### 11. Completa: My ____ is Ana.

Opciones: name · age · city

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**name** — *My name is Ana.*
</details>

### 12. Completa: I am ____ Madrid.

Opciones: from · in · at

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**from** — *I am from Madrid.*
</details>

### 13. Enseñas inglés en una escuela. Completa: I am a ____ .

Opciones: teacher · student · doctor

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**teacher**
</details>

### 14. Alguien dice “Hi!”. ¿Qué respondes?

a) Goodbye · b) Hi or Hello · c) Good night · d) My name is …

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) Hi or Hello**
</details>

### 15. Conoces a alguien por primera vez. ¿Qué frase encaja mejor?

a) Goodbye · b) Nice to meet you · c) I am twenty. · d) From Madrid.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) Nice to meet you**
</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: María

Lee el texto y responde.

> Hello! My name is María. I am twenty-eight years old. I am from Madrid, Spain. I am a teacher. I teach English at a small school. I am happy today because it is my birthday. Nice to meet you!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-1/reading-maria.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: María"></audio>

### 1. What is her name?

a) Ana · b) María · c) Carmen · d) Elena

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) María** — *My name is María.*
</details>

### 2. How old is María?

a) twenty · b) twenty-five · c) twenty-eight · d) thirty

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) twenty-eight**
</details>

### 3. Where is María from?

a) London · b) Barcelona · c) Madrid · d) Mexico City

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) Madrid**
</details>

### 4. What is her job?

a) student · b) doctor · c) teacher · d) nurse

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) teacher**
</details>

### 5. What does she teach?

a) Spanish · b) Math · c) English · d) Science

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) English**
</details>

### 6. Where does she work?

a) At a big school. · b) At a small school. · c) At home. · d) In a hospital.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) At a small school.**
</details>

### 7. Why is María happy today?

a) Because she is on holiday.  
b) Because it is her birthday.  
c) Because she has a new job.  
d) Because she is from Madrid.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) Because it is her birthday.**
</details>

### 8. What phrase does María use to end the text?

a) Goodbye · b) How are you? · c) Nice to meet you · d) Thank you

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) Nice to meet you**
</details>

### 9. María is from Barcelona.

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Falso** — Es de Madrid.
</details>

### 10. María is a student.

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Falso** — Es *teacher*.
</details>

### 11. Today is her birthday.

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Verdadero**
</details>

### 12. María teaches at a big school.

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Falso** — *small school*.
</details>

### 13. What is the main topic of this text?

a) A day at school.  
b) A person introducing herself.  
c) A birthday party.  
d) A trip to Madrid.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) A person introducing herself.**
</details>

### 14. Who wrote this text?

a) A friend of María. · b) María herself. · c) A teacher. · d) A student.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) María herself.** (primera persona: *My name is…*, *I am…*)
</details>

### 15. In what city does María teach?

a) Barcelona · b) Madrid · c) Valencia · d) Seville

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) Madrid**
</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Carlos

Escucha (o lee la transcripción) y responde.

> Hi! My name is Carlos. I am from Barcelona, Spain. I am twenty-five years old. I am a student. I study at the university. I am happy to be here. Nice to meet you!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-1/listening-carlos.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Carlos"></audio>

### 1. What is his name?

a) Pedro · b) Carlos · c) Pablo · d) Antonio

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) Carlos**
</details>

### 2. Where is Carlos from?

a) Madrid · b) Valencia · c) Barcelona · d) Seville

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) Barcelona**
</details>

### 3. How old is Carlos?

a) twenty · b) twenty-three · c) twenty-five · d) thirty

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) twenty-five**
</details>

### 4. What is Carlos? (job / role)

a) teacher · b) doctor · c) student · d) engineer

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) student**
</details>

### 5. Where does he study?

a) At school. · b) At the university. · c) At home. · d) In a library.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) At the university.**
</details>

### 6. How does Carlos feel?

a) tired · b) sad · c) happy · d) angry

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) happy** — *I am happy to be here.*
</details>

### 7. What country does he mention?

a) Italy · b) France · c) Spain · d) Portugal

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) Spain**
</details>

### 8. What phrase does Carlos use at the end?

a) Goodbye · b) Thank you · c) Nice to meet you · d) How are you?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**c) Nice to meet you**
</details>

### 9. Carlos is from Madrid.

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Falso** — Es de Barcelona.
</details>

### 10. Carlos is a teacher.

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Falso** — Es *student*.
</details>

### 11. Carlos studies at the university.

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Verdadero**
</details>

### 12. Carlos is thirty years old.

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Falso** — Tiene veinticinco.

### 13. What is the main topic of this audio?

a) A class at university.  
b) A person introducing himself.  
c) A trip to Barcelona.  
d) A job interview.

**b) A person introducing himself.**
</details>

### 14. Who is speaking in the audio?

a) A teacher. · b) Carlos himself. · c) A friend of Carlos. · d) A student from another country.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b) Carlos himself.**
</details>

### 15. Does Carlos say he is happy?

Verdadero · Falso

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Verdadero** — *I am happy to be here.*
</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing

### Completa (1–5)

1. My ____ is Ana.  
2. I ____ from Madrid.  
3. You ____ my friend.  
4. I am twenty ____ old.  
5. I am ____ a student.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **name** · 2. **am** · 3. **are** · 4. **years** · 5. **a**
</details>

### Ordena (6–8)

6. is / My / name / Carlos  
7. am / I / from / Barcelona  
8. are / You / a / teacher

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **My name is Carlos.**  
7. **I am from Barcelona.**  
8. **You are a teacher.**
</details>

### Redacción guiada (9–12) — modelos

9. Nombre y edad  

<details>
<summary>Ver modelo</summary>

My name is Sofía. I am twenty-two years old.
</details>

10. Origen  

<details>
<summary>Ver modelo</summary>

I am from Valencia.
</details>

11. Estudios / trabajo  

<details>
<summary>Ver modelo</summary>

I am a student. / I am a teacher.
</details>

12. Saludo + presentación  

<details>
<summary>Ver modelo</summary>

Hello! My name is Sofía. Nice to meet you!
</details>

### Redacción libre (13–15) — modelo completo

<details>
<summary>Ver modelo (4–6 frases)</summary>

Hello! My name is Sofía. I am twenty-two years old. I am from Valencia, Spain. I am a student. I am happy to be here. Nice to meet you!
</details>

---

## Clave rápida

| Regla | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| I + **am** | I am a student. |
| You + **are** | You are from Spain. |
| My name + **is** | My name is Ana. |
| Edad | I am 20 **years old**. |
| Origen | I am **from** Madrid. |
| Primera vez | **Nice to meet you!** |

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 10 del curso A1** (*Rutinas diarias y la hora*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Rutinas diarias y la hora A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-10-rutinas-diarias-hora)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 10 — Rutinas diarias y la hora](/curso-a1/unit-10)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Rutinas diarias](/blog/curso-a1/unit-10/a1-unit10-routines.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: Present Simple y *What time…?*](#leccion-1--gramatica-present-simple-y-what-time)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: rutinas y la hora](#leccion-2--vocabulario-rutinas-y-la-hora)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Mark's day](#leccion-3--reading-marks-day)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Anna's routine](#leccion-4--listening-annas-routine)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: My daily routine](#leccion-5--writing-my-daily-routine)
