content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 7 del curso A1** (*Colores y descripciones físicas*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Colores y descripciones físicas A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-7-colores-descripciones-fisicas)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 7 — Colores y descripciones físicas](/curso-a1/unit-7)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Colores básicos](/blog/curso-a1/unit-7/a1-unit7-colors.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: adjetivos y *have got*](#leccion-1--gramatica-adjetivos-y-have-got)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: colores y rasgos físicos](#leccion-2--vocabulario-colores-y-rasgos-fisicos)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: My best friend](#leccion-3--reading-my-best-friend)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Lisa and Tom](#leccion-4--listening-lisa-and-tom)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: Physical descriptions](#leccion-5--writing-physical-descriptions)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: adjetivos y *have got*

**Objetivo:** Adjetivo delante del nombre; *to be* + adjetivo; *have/has* para pelo y ojos.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. She ____ tall. → *is / are / am*  
2. He ____ got long brown hair. → *has / have / is*  
3. My car ____ red. → *is / are / am*  
4. She is ____ for her age. → *young / tall / short / old*  
5. They ____ blue eyes. → *have / has / is*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **is** — *to be* + adjetivo con *she*.  
2. **has** — *he/she/it* → *has (got)*.  
3. **is**  
4. **young**  
5. **have** — *they* → *have*.

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige la opción correcta

6. Which sentence is correct?  
   a) She has long hair. · b) She has hair long. · c) She is long hair.  
7. Where do adjectives go in English?  
   a) After the noun. · b) Before the noun. · c) At the end.  
8. He ____ short black hair.  
   a) has · b) is · c) have  
9. The sky ____ blue.  
   a) is · b) are · c) have  
10. She ____ green eyes.  
    a) has · b) is · c) are

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) She has long hair.**  
7. **b) Before the noun.**  
8. **a) has**  
9. **a) is**  
10. **a) has**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Ordena las palabras

11. He / is / tall.  
12. She / has / long / brown / hair.  
13. The / car / is / blue.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. He is tall.  
12. She has long brown hair.  
13. The car is blue.

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. In English we put adjectives before nouns. → ?  
15. We use have got for hair and eyes in descriptions. → ?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **Verdadero**  
15. **Verdadero**

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: colores y rasgos físicos

**Objetivo:** Colores básicos y adjetivos de descripción física.

### Ejercicios 1–6 — Elige la palabra correcta

1. What color is the sky on a sunny day? → a) red · b) blue · c) green · d) yellow  
2. The opposite of tall is ____. → a) young · b) short · c) old · d) long  
3. We use ____ to describe hair length. → a) tall · b) long · c) old · d) blue  
4. The opposite of young is ____. → a) short · b) tall · c) old · d) long  
5. What word describes the colour of grass? → a) red · b) blue · c) green · d) yellow  
6. Brown hair is ____ in Spanish. → a) rubio · b) castaño · c) negro · d) pelirrojo

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b) blue**  
2. **b) short**  
3. **b) long**  
4. **c) old**  
5. **c) green**  
6. **b) castaño**

</details>

### Ejercicios 7–10 — Une con su significado

**7.** tall · short · young · old · long  
→ alto · bajo · joven · mayor/viejo · largo

**8.** red · blue · green · yellow · black  
→ rojo · azul · verde · amarillo · negro

**9.** white · brown · hair · eyes · dark  
→ blanco · marrón/castaño · pelo · ojos · oscuro

**10.** She has long hair. · He is tall. · Her eyes are blue. · My brother is young. · The car is red.  
→ Ella tiene el pelo largo. · Él es alto. · Sus ojos son azules. · Mi hermano es joven. · El coche es rojo.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

7. tall→alto · short→bajo · young→joven · old→mayor/viejo · long→largo  
8. red→rojo · blue→azul · green→verde · yellow→amarillo · black→negro  
9. white→blanco · brown→marrón/castaño · hair→pelo · eyes→ojos · dark→oscuro  
10. She has long hair.→Ella tiene el pelo largo. · He is tall.→Él es alto. · Her eyes are blue.→Sus ojos son azules. · My brother is young.→Mi hermano es joven. · The car is red.→El coche es rojo.

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Completa

11. She has ____ hair. It is not short. → *long / tall / old / blue*  
12. My grandfather is ____. He is seventy years old. → *young / tall / old / short*  
13. His ____ are green. → *hair / eyes / hand / face*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **long**  
12. **old**  
13. **eyes**

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Contexto

14. You describe a person who is not short. She ____.  
    a) is short · b) is tall · c) is old · d) is young  
15. You say the colour of snow. It is ____.  
    a) red · b) blue · c) white · d) black

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **b) is tall**  
15. **c) white**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: My best friend

**Objetivo:** Leer una descripción física corta de una amiga.

### Texto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-7/reading-friend.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: My best friend"></audio>

> Can you describe your best friend? Sure! She is tall with long brown hair. What color are her eyes? Her eyes are green. She is very beautiful. How old is she? She is young — only twenty years old.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. What is the friend's height? → a) short · b) medium · c) tall  
2. What color is the friend's hair? → a) black · b) brown · c) blonde  
3. What color are the friend's eyes? → a) blue · b) brown · c) green  
4. How old is the friend? → a) thirty · b) twenty · c) eighteen  
5. Is the hair long or short? → a) short · b) long · c) medium

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **c) tall**  
2. **b) brown**  
3. **c) green**  
4. **b) twenty**  
5. **b) long**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–9 — Verdadero o falso

6. The person described is a man. → ?  
7. She has green eyes. → ?  
8. She is forty years old. → ?  
9. The text describes a person with physical details. → ?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **Falso**  
7. **Verdadero**  
8. **Falso** (twenty)  
9. **Verdadero**

</details>

### Ejercicios 10–15 — Comprensión

10. Main topic:  
    a) A school · b) A description of a friend · c) A doctor · d) Football  
11. Which words describe hair in the text?  
    a) tall and short · b) long and brown · c) green and blue  
12. What colour is the friend's hair?  
    a) Brown · b) Black · c) Blonde  
13. What verb do we use for hair and eyes?  
    a) is · b) have · c) go  
14. The friend is described as ____.  
    a) old · b) young · c) short  
15. Which adjective is NOT in the text?  
    a) tall · b) beautiful · c) short

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

10. **b) A description of a friend**  
11. **b) long and brown**  
12. **a) Brown**  
13. **b) have**  
14. **b) young**  
15. **c) short**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Lisa and Tom

**Objetivo:** Escuchar un diálogo con descripciones físicas de familiares.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-7/listening-lisa-tom.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Lisa and Tom"></audio>

> **Lisa:** Who is that woman with the long red hair?  
> **Tom:** She is my sister Emma.  
> **Lisa:** She is very tall. How old is she?  
> **Tom:** She is twenty-five years old. She has blue eyes too.  
> **Lisa:** My brother is short and he has brown hair.  
> **Tom:** Is he young?  
> **Lisa:** Yes, he is only eighteen.

### Ejercicios 1–8 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. What color is Emma's hair? → a) brown · b) red · c) black · d) blonde  
2. Who is Emma? → a) Tom's friend · b) Tom's sister · c) Tom's mother · d) Lisa's sister  
3. Is Emma tall or short? → a) short · b) tall · c) medium  
4. How old is Emma? → a) twenty · b) twenty-five · c) thirty · d) eighteen  
5. What color are Emma's eyes? → a) green · b) brown · c) blue · d) black  
6. Lisa's brother is ____. → a) tall · b) short · c) old  
7. What color is Lisa's brother's hair? → a) black · b) red · c) brown · d) blonde  
8. How old is Lisa's brother? → a) twenty-five · b) twenty · c) eighteen · d) thirty

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b) red**  
2. **b) Tom's sister**  
3. **b) tall**  
4. **b) twenty-five**  
5. **c) blue**  
6. **b) short**  
7. **c) brown**  
8. **c) eighteen**

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–12 — Verdadero o falso

9. Emma has black hair. → ?  
10. Tom and Lisa talk about physical descriptions. → ?  
11. Lisa's brother is tall. → ?  
12. Emma is Tom's sister. → ?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

9. **Falso** (red)  
10. **Verdadero**  
11. **Falso** (short)  
12. **Verdadero**

</details>

### Ejercicios 13–15 — Comprensión global

13. Main topic:  
    a) School and work · b) Two people describe family members physically · c) Sports  
14. What do they describe about the people?  
    a) Hair, eyes, height (and age) · b) Work · c) School  
15. Which details are mentioned?  
    a) Only names · b) Height, hair color, eyes, age · c) Job and city

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

13. **b) Two people describe family members physically**  
14. **a) Hair, eyes, height (and age)**  
15. **b) Height, hair color, eyes, age**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: Physical descriptions

**Objetivo:** Escribir descripciones cortas con *to be*, colores y *have/has*.

### Modelo

> I have long brown hair.  
> My eyes are green. / I have green eyes.  
> I am tall. I am twenty-two years old.  
> My sister is tall. She has long black hair and brown eyes.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. The sky is ____. (*blue*)  
2. She ____ long brown hair. (*has / have*)  
3. My brother is ____. He is not tall. (*short*)  
4. Her eyes ____ green. (*is / are*)  
5. She is ____ — only twenty years old. (*young*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **blue**  
2. **has**  
3. **short**  
4. **are**  
5. **young**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena las palabras

6. and / beautiful. / She / is / tall  
7. He / has / blue / eyes.  
8. My / car / is / red.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. She is tall and beautiful.  
7. He has blue eyes.  
8. My car is red.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–12 — Escribe frases guiadas (ejemplos)

9. Describe your hair (*I have … hair*).  
10. Describe your eyes (*My eyes are … / I have … eyes*).  
11. Height + age (*I am … / I am … years old*).  
12. A family member or friend: height, hair, eyes.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. I have long brown hair.  
10. My eyes are brown. / I have green eyes.  
11. I am tall. I am twenty-two years old.  
12. My sister is tall. She has long black hair and brown eyes.

</details>

### Ejercicios 13–15 — Párrafos cortos (ejemplos)

13. Describe your best friend (4–6 sentences).  
14. Describe two family members.  
15. Colours you like and colours of things you have.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

**13.**  
My best friend is Ana. She is tall and young. She has long brown hair. Her eyes are green. She is twenty years old. She is very beautiful.

**14.**  
My mother is tall. She has short brown hair and blue eyes. My brother is short. He has black hair and brown eyes. He is young — only eighteen years old.

**15.**  
I like blue and green. My room is white. My bag is black. I have brown hair and green eyes. My favourite colour is blue.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Recuerda |
|------|----------|
| Altura / edad | *She is tall.* · *He is young.* |
| Pelo / ojos | *She has long hair.* · *He has blue eyes.* |
| Orden | adjetivo + nombre (*long brown hair*) |
| Colores | *red, blue, green, yellow, black, white, brown* |

---

## Siguiente paso

1. Repasa la [guía teórica de la Unidad 7](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-7-colores-descripciones-fisicas).  
2. Practica en la [Unidad 7 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-7).

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 8 del curso A1** (*Números, edad y precios*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Números, edad y precios A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-8-numeros-edad-precios)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 8 — Números, edad y precios](/curso-a1/unit-8)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Números 20–100](/blog/curso-a1/unit-8/a1-unit8-numbers.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: edad y precio](#leccion-1--gramatica-edad-y-precio)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: números, precios y edad](#leccion-2--vocabulario-numeros-precios-y-edad)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: At the supermarket](#leccion-3--reading-at-the-supermarket)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: At the shop](#leccion-4--listening-at-the-shop)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: Ages and prices](#leccion-5--writing-ages-and-prices)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: edad y precio

**Objetivo:** *How old…?* para la edad, *How much…?* para el precio y números 20–100.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. How ____ are you? → *old / much / many*  
2. How ____ is the coffee? → *old / much / many*  
3. I am ____ years old. → *twenty-five / twenty / five*  
4. The book ____ forty-five euros. → *is / are / am*  
5. How old ____ she? → *are / is / am*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **old** — *How old are you?*  
2. **much** — *How much is…?*  
3. **twenty-five**  
4. **is** — singular.  
5. **is** — *How old is she?*

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige la opción correcta

6. Which question do we use for age?  
   a) How much is it? · b) How old are you? · c) How many?  
7. Which question do we use for price?  
   a) How old are you? · b) How much is it? · c) Where is it?  
8. My sister ____ 30 years old.  
   a) has · b) is · c) have  
9. These shoes ____ £50.  
   a) is · b) are · c) am  
10. 100 = ____.  
    a) one hundred · b) ten · c) one thousand

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **b) How old are you?**  
7. **b) How much is it?**  
8. **b) is**  
9. **b) are**  
10. **a) one hundred**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Ordena las palabras

11. How / old / are / you?  
12. I / am / twenty-eight / years / old.  
13. How / much / is / this / book?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. How old are you?  
12. I am twenty-eight years old.  
13. How much is this book?

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. We use "How old" to ask about age in English. → ?  
15. We use "How much" to ask the price of something. → ?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **Verdadero**  
15. **Verdadero**

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: números, precios y edad

**Objetivo:** Números 20–100, monedas, *cheap/expensive* y preguntas de edad/precio.

### Ejercicios 1–6 — Elige la opción correcta

1. Forty = ____. → a) 14 · b) 40 · c) 44  
2. Eighty = ____. → a) eighteen · b) eighty · c) eight  
3. What symbol is for dollars? → a) £ · b) $ · c) €  
4. What word means *barato*? → a) expensive · b) cheap · c) small  
5. How do you say 90 in English? → a) nineteen · b) ninety · c) nine  
6. The opposite of cheap is ____. → a) expensive · b) small · c) old

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b) 40**  
2. **b) eighty**  
3. **b) $**  
4. **b) cheap**  
5. **b) ninety**  
6. **a) expensive**

</details>

### Ejercicios 7–10 — Une con su significado

**7.** twenty · fifty · seventy · one hundred · thirty → 20 · 50 · 70 · 100 · 30  

**8.** How old are you? · How much is it? · years old · expensive · cheap  
→ Pregunta por edad · Pregunta por precio · Expresión para edad · Precio alto · Precio bajo

**9.** £ · $ · € · cents · bill → Libra (UK) · Dólar · Euro · Parte de dólar/euro · La cuenta  

**10.** sixty-four · twenty-one · ninety-nine · fifteen · eighty → 64 · 21 · 99 · 15 · 80

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

7. twenty→20 · fifty→50 · seventy→70 · one hundred→100 · thirty→30  
8. How old are you?→edad · How much is it?→precio · years old→edad · expensive→precio alto · cheap→precio bajo  
9. £→libra · $→dólar · €→euro · cents→céntimos · bill→cuenta  
10. sixty-four→64 · twenty-one→21 · ninety-nine→99 · fifteen→15 · eighty→80

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Completa

11. I am ____ years old. (25) → *twenty-five / fifty-two / fifteen*  
12. The total ____ ninety-nine pounds. → *is / are / am*  
13. How ____ are these apples? → *much / many / old*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **twenty-five**  
12. **is**  
13. **much**

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Contexto

14. You want to ask the price of a coffee. You ____.  
    a) say "How old are you?" · b) say "How much is it?" · c) say "Where is it?"  
15. Someone asks your age. You answer: ____.  
    a) I am twenty-five years old. · b) I have twenty-five euros. · c) The book is twenty-five.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **b) say "How much is it?"**  
15. **a) I am twenty-five years old.**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: At the supermarket

**Objetivo:** Leer un texto corto de compras con cantidades y precios.

### Texto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-8/reading-supermarket.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Supermarket"></audio>

> I am at the supermarket. I need twenty apples and ten oranges. The apples are five euros. The oranges are three euros. I also need a bottle of milk. The milk is one euro and fifty cents. The total is nine euros and fifty cents. I have twenty euros. I am happy.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. How many apples does the person need? → a) ten · b) twenty · c) five  
2. How much are the oranges? → a) five euros · b) three euros · c) one euro  
3. How much is the milk? → a) 1.00€ · b) 1.50€ · c) 2.00€  
4. What is the total? → a) nine euros · b) nine euros fifty · c) twenty euros  
5. How much money does the person have? → a) ten euros · b) twenty euros · c) nine fifty

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b) twenty**  
2. **b) three euros**  
3. **b) 1.50€**  
4. **b) nine euros fifty**  
5. **b) twenty euros**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–9 — Verdadero o falso

6. The apples cost five euros. → ?  
7. The person is at the restaurant. → ?  
8. The total is more than ten euros. → ?  
9. The person has enough money to pay. → ?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **Verdadero**  
7. **Falso** (supermarket)  
8. **Falso** (9.50€)  
9. **Verdadero** (20€ > 9.50€)

</details>

### Ejercicios 10–15 — Comprensión

10. Main topic:  
    a) A restaurant · b) Shopping at the supermarket with prices · c) A family  
11. Which numbers appear in the text?  
    a) Only five and three · b) Twenty, ten, five, three, one, fifty, nine, twenty · c) One hundred  
12. How much money do they have?  
    a) 20€ · b) 9.50€ · c) 10€  
13. How many oranges does the person need?  
    a) twenty · b) ten · c) five  
14. What does the person need besides fruit?  
    a) A bottle of milk · b) Bread · c) Water  
15. How does the person feel at the end?  
    a) Sad · b) Happy · c) Tired

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

10. **b) Shopping at the supermarket with prices**  
11. **b) Twenty, ten, five, three, one, fifty, nine, twenty**  
12. **a) 20€**  
13. **b) ten**  
14. **a) A bottle of milk**  
15. **b) Happy**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: At the shop

**Objetivo:** Escuchar un diálogo de tienda sobre precios y edades.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-8/listening-shop.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Shop"></audio>

> **Maria:** How much is this book?  
> **Shop:** It is twenty-five euros.  
> **Maria:** And how much are the notebooks?  
> **Shop:** They are three euros each.  
> **Maria:** How old is your daughter?  
> **Shop:** She is twelve years old.  
> **Maria:** My son is fifteen. I need two books and one notebook.  
> **Shop:** That is fifty-three euros in total.

### Ejercicios 1–6 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. How much is the book? → a) twenty euros · b) twenty-five euros · c) thirty euros  
2. How much are the notebooks? → a) one euro each · b) three euros each · c) five euros each  
3. How old is the shop assistant's daughter? → a) ten · b) twelve · c) fifteen  
4. How old is Maria's son? → a) twelve · b) fifteen · c) twenty-five  
5. What does Maria need? → a) One book and one notebook · b) Two books and one notebook · c) Two notebooks and one book  
6. What is the total? → a) fifty-three euros · b) thirty-three euros · c) twenty-eight euros

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b) twenty-five euros**  
2. **b) three euros each**  
3. **b) twelve**  
4. **b) fifteen**  
5. **b) Two books and one notebook**  
6. **a) fifty-three euros**

</details>

### Ejercicios 7–10 — Verdadero o falso

7. Maria asks about the price of the book. → ?  
8. The daughter is fifteen years old. → ?  
9. The notebooks cost five euros each. → ?  
10. The dialogue is about prices and ages. → ?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

7. **Verdadero**  
8. **Falso** (twelve)  
9. **Falso** (three)  
10. **Verdadero**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Comprensión global

11. Main topic:  
    a) Sports · b) A customer asks prices and talks about ages with shop · c) Food  
12. What does the woman buy?  
    a) Books and a notebook · b) Only a notebook · c) Only books  
13. Which questions are asked?  
    a) Only How much · b) How much is the book, how much are the notebooks, how old is your daughter · c) Where is the shop  
14. How many books does Maria buy?  
    a) one · b) two · c) three  
15. In what currency are the prices?  
    a) Dollars · b) Euros · c) Pounds

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **b) A customer asks prices and talks about ages with shop**  
12. **a) Books and a notebook**  
13. **b) How much is the book, how much are the notebooks, how old is your daughter**  
14. **b) two**  
15. **b) Euros**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: Ages and prices

**Objetivo:** Escribir frases sobre edad y precio con números en inglés.

### Modelo

> I am twenty-five years old.  
> How much is this book? It is twenty euros. It is cheap.  
> How old is your sister? She is thirty years old.  
> The total is twenty-five euros.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. ____ old are you? (*How*)  
2. How ____ is the coffee? (*much / many / old*)  
3. The book is ____ euros. (40) → *forty / fourteen / four*  
4. The total ____ fifty euros. (*is / are / am*)  
5. I ____ twenty-eight years old. (*am / is / are*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **How**  
2. **much**  
3. **forty**  
4. **is**  
5. **am**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena las palabras

6. How / much / is / this / book?  
7. I / am / thirty / years / old.  
8. The / total / is / twenty-five / euros.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. How much is this book?  
7. I am thirty years old.  
8. The total is twenty-five euros.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–12 — Escribe frases guiadas (ejemplos)

9. Say your age (*I am … years old*).  
10. Ask the price of something (*How much is this …?*).  
11. Price + expensive/cheap.  
12. Ask someone's age + answer.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. I am twenty-five years old.  
10. How much is this book?  
11. It is twenty euros. It is cheap.  
12. How old is your sister? She is thirty years old.

</details>

### Ejercicios 13–15 — Párrafos cortos (ejemplos)

13. A shopping trip: what you bought, prices, total.  
14. Ages of family or friends.  
15. Mix prices and ages (something you bought + ages + expensive/cheap).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

**13.**  
I go to the shop. How much is this book? It is twenty euros. How much are the notebooks? They are three euros. The total is twenty-three euros. It is cheap.

**14.**  
I am twenty-eight years old. How old is your brother? He is thirty years old. How old is your sister? She is twenty-five years old. My friend is twenty-two years old.

**15.**  
I am twenty-five years old. My sister is thirty years old. I buy a book. How much is this book? It is forty euros. It is expensive. The total is forty euros.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Recuerda |
|------|----------|
| Edad | *How old are you?* · *I am twenty-five years old.* |
| Precio | *How much is it?* · *It is forty euros.* |
| Plural | *How much are these shoes?* · *They are £50.* |
| Números | *twenty, thirty, forty… one hundred* |
| Opinión | *cheap / expensive* |

faqs.question: ¿Qué ejercicios incluye la Unidad 9 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: Cinco lecciones con 15 actividades cada una: gramática (to be + a/an + profesión), vocabulario de trabajos, reading (Laura), listening (Tom) y writing.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo uso este artículo?
faqs.answer: Haz cada ejercicio sin mirar la solución. Después abre «Ver solución» y lee la explicación. Si fallas, repasa la guía teórica y vuelve a intentarlo en el curso interactivo.

faqs.question: ¿A o an con profesiones?
faqs.answer: Usa a delante de consonante (a teacher, a doctor). Usa an delante de vocal (an engineer, an artist). Pregunta el lugar: Where do you work?

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 9 del curso A1** (*Profesiones y ocupaciones*) con **soluciones comentadas**. Corresponde a las lecciones del curso: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

> **Guía teórica:** [Profesiones y ocupaciones A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-9-profesiones-ocupaciones)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 9 — Profesiones y ocupaciones](/curso-a1/unit-9)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Profesiones](/blog/curso-a1/unit-9/a1-unit9-jobs.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática: *to be*, *a/an* y *Where do you work?*](#leccion-1--gramatica-to-be-aan-y-where-do-you-work)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario: profesiones y lugares](#leccion-2--vocabulario-profesiones-y-lugares)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Laura's family](#leccion-3--reading-lauras-family)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Tom the teacher](#leccion-4--listening-tom-the-teacher)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing: Jobs](#leccion-5--writing-jobs)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: *to be*, *a/an* y *Where do you work?*

**Objetivo:** Decir la profesión (*I am a teacher*), elegir *a/an* y preguntar el lugar de trabajo.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I ____ a teacher. → *am / is / are*  
2. She is ____ engineer. → *a / an / the*  
3. He ____ a doctor. → *am / is / are*  
4. My brother is ____ teacher. → *a / an / the*  
5. Where ____ you work? → *do / does / are*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am** — *I am a teacher.*  
2. **an** — *engineer* empieza por vocal.  
3. **is**  
4. **a** — *teacher* empieza por consonante.  
5. **do** — *Where do you work?*

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige la opción correcta

6. Which article before engineer? → a) a · b) an · c) the  
7. Which article before doctor? → a) a · b) an · c) the  
8. They ____ students. → a) am · b) is · c) are  
9. Where ____ she work? → a) do · b) does · c) is  
10. I work ____ a school. → a) in · b) at · c) on

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **b) an**  
7. **a) a**  
8. **c) are**  
9. **b) does**  
10. **a) in**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Ordena las palabras

11. I / am / a / teacher.  
12. Where / do / you / work?  
13. She / works / in / a / hospital.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. I am a teacher.  
12. Where do you work?  
13. She works in a hospital.

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. We use "a" before professions that start with a consonant. → ?  
15. We ask "Where do you work?" to know the place of work. → ?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **Verdadero**  
15. **Verdadero**

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: profesiones y lugares

**Objetivo:** Nombrar trabajos básicos y relacionarlos con lugares de trabajo.

### Ejercicios 1–6 — Elige la palabra correcta

1. Someone who works in a school is ____. → a) teacher · b) doctor · c) waiter  
2. Someone who helps sick people in a hospital is ____. → a) chef · b) doctor · c) driver  
3. A ____ works in a restaurant kitchen. → a) waiter · b) chef · c) nurse  
4. A ____ drives buses or taxis. → a) engineer · b) driver · c) pilot  
5. A ____ studies at school or university. → a) student · b) teacher · c) engineer  
6. A ____ helps doctors in a hospital. → a) nurse · b) waiter · c) chef

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) teacher**  
2. **b) doctor**  
3. **b) chef**  
4. **b) driver**  
5. **a) student**  
6. **a) nurse**

</details>

### Ejercicios 7–10 — Une con su significado

**7.** teacher · doctor · chef · waiter · engineer  
→ school · hospital · restaurant · restaurant · office

**8.** nurse · driver · student · pilot · teacher  
→ hospital · bus · university · airport · school

**9.** engineer · waiter · artist · pilot · doctor  
→ Ingeniero · Camarero · Artista · Piloto · Médico

**10.** I work in a school · I work in a hospital · I work in a restaurant · I study at university · I drive a bus  
→ I am a teacher · I am a doctor or nurse · I am a chef or waiter · I am a student · I am a driver

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

7. teacher→school · doctor→hospital · chef→restaurant · waiter→restaurant · engineer→office  
8. nurse→hospital · driver→bus · student→university · pilot→airport · teacher→school  
9. engineer→Ingeniero · waiter→Camarero · artist→Artista · pilot→Piloto · doctor→Médico  
10. school→teacher · hospital→doctor/nurse · restaurant→chef/waiter · university→student · bus→driver

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Completa

11. My mother is ____ teacher. She works in a school. → *a / an / the*  
12. He is ____ engineer. He works in an office. → *a / an / the*  
13. Where ____ your sister work? She works in a hospital. → *do / does / is*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a**  
12. **an**  
13. **does**

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Contexto

14. Someone asks your job. You say: ____.  
    a) I am a teacher. · b) I work. · c) How old are you?  
15. You want to ask where someone works. You ____.  
    a) say "What is your name?" · b) say "Where do you work?" · c) say "How old are you?"

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **a) I am a teacher.**  
15. **b) say "Where do you work?"**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Laura's family

**Objetivo:** Leer un texto corto sobre las profesiones de una familia.

### Texto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-9/reading-laura.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Laura"></audio>

> My name is Laura. I am a teacher. I work in a school in Madrid. My brother is an engineer. He works in an office. My sister is a nurse. She works in a hospital. My father is a doctor. He works in the same hospital as my sister. We are a family of workers.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. What is Laura's job? → a) Teacher · b) Engineer · c) Nurse  
2. Where does Laura work? → a) In a hospital · b) In a school · c) In an office  
3. What is Laura's brother's job? → a) Teacher · b) Engineer · c) Doctor  
4. Where does the brother work? → a) In a school · b) In an office · c) In a hospital  
5. What is Laura's sister's job? → a) Nurse · b) Doctor · c) Teacher

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Teacher**  
2. **b) In a school**  
3. **b) Engineer**  
4. **b) In an office**  
5. **a) Nurse**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–9 — Verdadero o falso

6. Laura's father is a doctor. → ?  
7. The sister works in a school. → ?  
8. The father and the sister work in the same hospital. → ?  
9. Laura works in Barcelona. → ?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **Verdadero**  
7. **Falso** (hospital)  
8. **Verdadero**  
9. **Falso** (Madrid)

</details>

### Ejercicios 10–15 — Comprensión

10. Main topic:  
    a) A family and their jobs · b) A school in Madrid · c) Hospitals  
11. Which professions are mentioned?  
    a) Only teacher · b) Teacher, engineer, nurse, doctor · c) Waiter and chef  
12. What does Laura introduce?  
    a) Her family and their jobs · b) Schools · c) A hospital  
13. Where does Laura's sister work?  
    a) In a school · b) In a hospital · c) In an office  
14. What does "a family of workers" mean?  
    a) Everyone has a job · b) No one works · c) Only one person works  
15. How many people in Laura's family have a job mentioned?  
    a) Two · b) Three · c) Four

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

10. **a) A family and their jobs**  
11. **b) Teacher, engineer, nurse, doctor**  
12. **a) Her family and their jobs**  
13. **b) In a hospital**  
14. **a) Everyone has a job**  
15. **c) Four**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Tom the teacher

**Objetivo:** Escuchar una entrevista corta sobre profesiones.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-9/listening-tom.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Tom"></audio>

> **Interviewer:** What do you do?  
> **Tom:** I am a teacher. I work in a primary school.  
> **Interviewer:** Where is the school?  
> **Tom:** It is in the centre of town.  
> **Interviewer:** Do you like your job?  
> **Tom:** Yes, I love it. My sister is a nurse. She works in a hospital. We both like our jobs.

### Ejercicios 1–6 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. What is Tom's job? → a) Doctor · b) Teacher · c) Engineer  
2. Where does Tom work? → a) In a hospital · b) In a primary school · c) In an office  
3. Where is the school? → a) In the centre of town · b) In a village · c) Near the hospital  
4. Does Tom like his job? → a) Yes · b) No · c) He doesn't say  
5. What is Tom's sister's job? → a) Teacher · b) Nurse · c) Doctor  
6. Where does Tom's sister work? → a) In a school · b) In a hospital · c) In an office

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b) Teacher**  
2. **b) In a primary school**  
3. **a) In the centre of town**  
4. **a) Yes**  
5. **b) Nurse**  
6. **b) In a hospital**

</details>

### Ejercicios 7–10 — Verdadero o falso

7. Tom is a secondary school teacher. → ?  
8. Tom and his sister like their jobs. → ?  
9. The interviewer asks "What do you do?". → ?  
10. Tom's sister works in a school. → ?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

7. **Falso** (primary school)  
8. **Verdadero**  
9. **Verdadero**  
10. **Falso** (hospital)

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Comprensión global

11. Main topic:  
    a) Food · b) A person talks about his job and his sister's job · c) Sports  
12. What is Tom's job?  
    a) Teacher · b) Nurse · c) Doctor  
13. Which questions does the interviewer ask?  
    a) Only Where do you work? · b) What do you do?, Where is the school?, Do you like your job? · c) How old are you?  
14. What type of school does Tom work in?  
    a) Secondary · b) Primary · c) University  
15. Does Tom mention his sister?  
    a) No · b) Yes, she is a nurse · c) Yes, she is a teacher

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **b) A person talks about his job and his sister's job**  
12. **a) Teacher**  
13. **b) What do you do?, Where is the school?, Do you like your job?**  
14. **b) Primary**  
15. **b) Yes, she is a nurse**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing: Jobs

**Objetivo:** Escribir frases y párrafos sobre profesiones y lugares de trabajo.

### Modelo

> I am a teacher. I work in a school.  
> He is an engineer. She is a doctor.  
> Where do you work? I work in a hospital.  
> My mother is a nurse. She likes her job.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I ____ a teacher. (*am / is / are*)  
2. He is ____ engineer. (*a / an*)  
3. She is ____ doctor. (*a / an*)  
4. Where ____ you work? (*do / does*)  
5. I work ____ a hospital. (*in / at / on*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am**  
2. **an**  
3. **a**  
4. **do**  
5. **in**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena las palabras

6. I / am / a / teacher.  
7. Where / do / you / work?  
8. She / works / in / a / hospital.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. I am a teacher.  
7. Where do you work?  
8. She works in a hospital.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–12 — Escribe frases guiadas (ejemplos)

9. Say a job (*I am a/an …* or *My … is a/an …*).  
10. Say a workplace (*I work in a/an …*).  
11. Job + workplace (two sentences).  
12. Question + answer (*What do you do?* / *Where do you work?*).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. I am a teacher. / My sister is a nurse.  
10. I work in a school. / She works in a hospital.  
11. I am a teacher. I work in a school.  
12. What do you do? I am a doctor. / Where do you work? I work in a hospital.

</details>

### Ejercicios 13–15 — Párrafos cortos (ejemplos)

13. Your job or a family member's job (4–6 sentences).  
14. Jobs of 2–3 people you know.  
15. Short presentation: name, job, workplace, like.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

**13.**  
My mother is a nurse. She works in a hospital. She likes her job. My father is an engineer. He works in an office. I am a student.

**14.**  
My brother is a driver. He works on a bus. My friend is a chef. She works in a restaurant. My uncle is a doctor. He works in a hospital.

**15.**  
My name is Ana. I am a teacher. I work in a school. I like my job. My sister is a nurse. She works in a hospital.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Recuerda |
|------|----------|
| Profesión | *I am a teacher.* · *He is an engineer.* |
| *a / an* | *a* + consonante · *an* + vocal |
| Lugar | *I work in a school / hospital / office.* |
| Preguntas | *What do you do?* · *Where do you work?* |

---

3. Siguiente unidad: [rutinas diarias y la hora](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-10-rutinas-diarias-hora).

title: Futuro en Inglés B1: Will vs Going to con Ejemplos
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía del futuro en inglés B1: compara will, going to y present continuous con ejemplos y ejercicios para practicar.
description: Aprende el futuro en inglés B1 con will, going to y present continuous: diferencias, predicciones, planes y ejemplos para elegir cada forma.
alt: Contraste will, going to y present continuous para el futuro B1

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo debo usar will para hablar del futuro?
faqs.answer: Usa **will** en cuatro situaciones muy concretas: predicciones de opinión sin evidencia visible (*I think it will rain*), promesas (*I will call you*), decisiones espontáneas que tomas en el momento de hablar (*Wait, I will help you*) y planes inciertos con *probably* o *perhaps* (*I will probably stay at home*). Si tu frase encaja en alguna de estas cuatro categorías, casi seguro necesitas *will*.

faqs.question: ¿En qué se diferencia going to de will si ambos hablan del futuro?
faqs.answer: **Going to** se usa para planes o intenciones que **ya has decidido** antes del momento de hablar (*I am going to visit my parents next weekend*) y para predicciones con **evidencia visible ahora mismo** (*Look at the clouds! It is going to rain*). *Will*, en cambio, no implica ninguna decisión previa: es espontáneo o es solo una opinión. La diferencia clave está en si ya habías pensado el plan antes o lo decides en ese instante.

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso el present continuous para hablar del futuro?
faqs.answer: Cuando existe un **arreglo fijo** con hora y lugar concretos, normalmente respaldado por un billete, una cita o un acuerdo con otra persona: *She is meeting her boss at 3 PM*, *We are flying to Rome on Friday*. La diferencia con *going to* es sutil pero importante: *going to* es una intención, mientras que el present continuous implica que ya existe un compromiso concreto y confirmado.

faqs.question: ¿Por qué a veces se usa el Present Simple para hablar del futuro, como en "the flight departs"?
faqs.answer: Porque hablamos de un **horario oficial**, no de un plan personal: *The flight departs at 10 AM*, *The plane takes off at 8 o'clock*. El avión "sale" según una programación fija, ajena a tu voluntad, así que no tendría sentido usar *will* o *going to* aquí. Este uso del Present Simple para el futuro se limita casi siempre a horarios de transporte, cines o eventos con programación oficial.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde puedo practicar todo lo de la Unidad 6 del curso B1?
faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-6-future-will-going-to-ejercicios-soluciones) tienes actividades adicionales comentadas, y en la [Unidad 6 del curso B1 de Linguafly](/curso-b1/unit-6) encontrarás will/going to/continuous, vocabulario de travel & transport, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
Tras el [Repaso 1–4](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-5-repaso-1-4), la **Unidad 6 del curso B1** (*Future: will, going to, present continuous*) abre el bloque de futuros del curso y te enseña a **elegir la forma futura correcta** según lo que realmente quieras comunicar: una predicción de opinión, un plan ya decidido o un arreglo fijo con hora y lugar. Todo ello con vocabulario de **travel & transport** (viajes y transporte), un contexto perfecto para practicar las tres formas a la vez.

En español usamos casi siempre el mismo futuro simple para todo ("iré", "voy a ir", "salgo mañana"), así que este contraste es uno de los puntos donde más cuesta automatizar la elección correcta en inglés. La buena noticia es que, igual que en la Unidad 4, existen señales muy claras que te ayudarán a decidir sin dudar: la presencia de evidencia visible, de un billete o una cita concreta, o simplemente de una opinión sin plan previo.

Esta guía incluye explicaciones detalladas, tablas de referencia, audios de pronunciación, errores típicos, un texto de lectura sobre un viaje de negocios a Tokio, un diálogo modelo, un plan de práctica de diez a quince minutos y ocho ejercicios con soluciones comentadas.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 6 — Future forms](/curso-b1/unit-6)  
> **Cuaderno de ejercicios (con soluciones):** [Ejercicios Unidad 6 B1](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-6-future-will-going-to-ejercicios-soluciones)  
> **Antes:** [U5 — Repaso 1–4](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-5-repaso-1-4) · [will vs going to](/blog/gramatica/will-going-to-diferencia)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 6 (B1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar **will** para predicciones de opinión, promesas y decisiones espontáneas.
- Usar **going to** para planes, intenciones y predicciones con evidencia visible.
- Usar el **present continuous** para arreglos fijos con hora y lugar confirmados.
- Reconocer el **Present Simple** en horarios oficiales (*The flight departs…*).
- Aplicar toda la gramática al vocabulario de **viajes y transporte**.

![Tres formas de futuro](/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/future-forms.png)

---

## 1. Mapa rápido de las cuatro formas

Antes de entrar en detalle, conviene ver las cuatro formas juntas para entender su relación. Cada una responde a una pregunta distinta: ¿es una opinión?, ¿es un plan ya decidido?, ¿hay una cita confirmada? o ¿es un horario oficial?

| Forma | Uso principal | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **will** | opinión, promesa, decisión espontánea | I think it **will** rain. · Wait, I **will** help you. |
| **going to** | plan / intención / evidencia | I **am going to** visit my parents. · It **is going to** rain. |
| **am/is/are + -ing** | arreglo fijo | We **are flying** to Rome on Friday. |
| **Present Simple** | horario oficial | The flight **departs** at 10 AM. |

---

## 2. *going to*: planes e intenciones

*Going to* se usa cuando ya tienes una **decisión tomada** antes de hablar, o cuando ves una **evidencia clara** de que algo va a ocurrir. Es la forma más común para hablar de planes de viaje, porque casi siempre implica que ya has pensado en ello con antelación.

> I **am going to** visit my parents next weekend.  
> He **is going to** take the train tomorrow.  
> I **am going to** book the tickets next week.  
> What **are you going to** do this weekend?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/am-going-to-visit.mp3" title="🔊 I am going to visit my parents next weekend."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/is-going-to-take.mp3" title="🔊 He is going to take the train tomorrow."></audio>

Cuando la evidencia es visible **en el momento de hablar**, también usamos *going to*, incluso si no hay ningún plan de por medio:

> Look at the clouds! It **is going to** rain.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/going-to-rain.mp3" title="🔊 Look at the clouds! It is going to rain."></audio>

---

## 3. *will*: predicciones, promesas y decisiones espontáneas

*Will* se usa cuando no hay ningún plan previo: es una opinión sin evidencia concreta, una promesa que haces en ese instante, o una decisión que tomas de forma completamente espontánea mientras hablas.

> I think it **will** rain tomorrow.  
> Wait, I **will** help you.  
> I promise I **will** call you when I arrive.  
> I **will** probably stay at home tonight.  
> Perhaps we **will** see you there.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/will-rain.mp3" title="🔊 I think it will rain tomorrow."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/will-help.mp3" title="🔊 Wait, I will help you."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/will-call.mp3" title="🔊 I promise I will call you when I arrive."></audio>

Un truco muy fiable: si en la frase aparecen palabras como *I think*, *probably* o *perhaps*, casi siempre necesitas **will**, porque estas expresiones señalan opinión, no un plan decidido de antemano.

---

## 4. Present continuous: arreglos fijos

Cuando existe una **cita, un billete o un acuerdo concreto** con otra persona, el inglés prefiere el present continuous en lugar de *going to*, aunque en la práctica ambas formas a veces se solapan.

> She **is meeting** her boss at 3 PM.  
> We **are flying** to Rome on Friday.  
> They **are having** a meeting tomorrow at 9.  
> She **is meeting** her sister at the airport at 5 PM.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/is-meeting.mp3" title="🔊 She is meeting her boss at three PM."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/are-flying.mp3" title="🔊 We are flying to Rome on Friday."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/are-having-meeting.mp3" title="🔊 They are having a meeting tomorrow at nine."></audio>

La señal más clara para reconocer este uso es la combinación de **hora + lugar** en la misma frase: *at the airport at 5 PM*, *on Friday*, *at 3 PM*. Cuantos más detalles concretos, más probable es que necesites el present continuous.

---

## 5. Present Simple: horarios oficiales

> The flight **departs** at 10 AM.  
> The plane **takes off** at 8 o'clock.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/flight-departs.mp3" title="🔊 The flight departs at ten AM."></audio>

Aquí no hablas de tu plan personal, sino del **horario** oficial de un vuelo, un tren o un evento programado. Este uso del Present Simple para el futuro es muy limitado en la práctica —casi siempre aparece con transporte, cines o programas de televisión— pero es importante reconocerlo porque suena muy natural en contextos de viaje.

---

## 6. Vocabulario: Travel & transport

![Vocabulario de viajes](/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/travel-vocab.png)

| Palabra | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| airport | aeropuerto | We are meeting at the **airport** at six. |
| passport | pasaporte | Don't forget your **passport** at check-in. |
| take off / land | despegar / aterrizar | The plane will **take off** soon and **land** in Tokyo. |
| station | estación | He is going to the train **station** this afternoon. |
| check in / check out | registrarse / salir del hotel | We will **check in** at the hotel around noon. |
| flight | vuelo | Our **flight** departs at ten in the morning. |
| suitcase | maleta | I am going to pack my **suitcase** tonight. |
| set off | partir / empezar el viaje | We will **set off** early to avoid traffic. |
| traveller | viajero/a | Every experienced **traveller** checks the weather first. |
| book | reservar | I am going to **book** the tickets tomorrow. |
| delay | retraso | There is a two-hour **delay** at the airport today. |
| get on / get off | subir / bajar (bus, tren) | We will **get on** the train at platform four. |
| hotel | hotel | We are staying at a small **hotel** near the centre. |
| business trip | viaje de negocios | She is going on a **business trip** next month. |
| colleague | compañero/a de trabajo | I am meeting a **colleague** at the airport tomorrow. |

---

## 7. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I will to go.* | *I **will go** / I **am going to** go.* | *Will* nunca lleva *to* antes del verbo. |
| *She meeting her boss tomorrow.* | *She **is meeting** her boss tomorrow.* | El present continuous necesita el verbo *be* auxiliar. |
| *The flight is depart at 10.* | *The flight **departs** at 10.* | Los horarios usan Present Simple, no present continuous. |
| *I think it is going to rain.* (sin evidencia, solo opinión) | *I think it **will** rain.* | Una opinión sin evidencia visible pide *will*, no *going to*. |
| Usar *will* para todo el futuro | Mira si hay **plan**, **arreglo** o solo **opinión** | Cada forma responde a una situación distinta; no son intercambiables. |
| *I am going to visiting my parents.* | *I am **going to visit** my parents.* | Tras *going to* necesitas el infinitivo sin *to* adicional, no *-ing*. |
| *We will flying to Rome on Friday.* | *We **are flying** to Rome on Friday.* | Un arreglo fijo con fecha y lugar pide present continuous, no *will*. |
| *The plane will depart at 10 AM tomorrow* (horario oficial) | *The plane **departs** at 10 AM tomorrow.* | Los horarios oficiales prefieren Present Simple, aunque *will* no sea incorrecto del todo. |

---

## 8. Reading: viaje de negocios a Tokio

![Viaje a Tokio](/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/tokyo-trip.png)

> Next month I am flying to Tokyo for a business trip, and I am really looking forward to it. I have already booked my flight and hotel, and I am meeting my colleagues at the airport at 6 AM before we check in together. The plane takes off at 8 o'clock, so we need to arrive early to avoid any last-minute stress. I think I will enjoy the trip a lot, because I love travelling and discovering new cultures. I am going to visit some temples if I have enough free time between meetings, and I will probably try some traditional Japanese food in the evenings. My colleague says the flight is usually on time, but there is sometimes a short delay because of the weather.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/reading-tokyo.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Tokyo trip"></audio>

Marca las cuatro formas: *am flying* / *am meeting* (arreglos con present continuous), *takes off* (horario con Present Simple), *will enjoy* / *will probably try* (predicción con *will*), *am going to visit* (intención con *going to*).

---

## 9. Diálogo: planes de viaje

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/dialogue-travel.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: travel plans"></audio>

> **Nora:** What are you going to do next month?  
> **Iván:** I am flying to Tokyo for work.  
> **Nora:** Are you meeting anyone there?  
> **Iván:** Yes — I am meeting my colleagues at the airport at six.  
> **Nora:** What time does the flight take off?  
> **Iván:** It takes off at eight, so we need to arrive early.  
> **Nora:** Do you think you will enjoy the trip?  
> **Iván:** I think I will enjoy it a lot. I love travelling.  
> **Nora:** Are you going to visit any temples?  
> **Iván:** Yes — I am going to visit some if I have time between meetings.

---

## 10. Plan de práctica (10–15 minutos)

1. **3 min — Repaso auditivo.** Escucha los audios de las secciones 2 a 5 en orden y, antes de cada frase, decide si es *will*, *going to*, present continuous u horario.
2. **4 min — Lectura activa.** Lee el texto del viaje a Tokio en voz alta y clasifica cada verbo en futuro según las cuatro categorías del mapa rápido.
3. **4 min — Producción oral.** Practica el diálogo con otra persona y cámbialo para hablar de tu próximo viaje real, usando al menos tres formas distintas de futuro.
4. **4 min — Autoevaluación.** Escribe cuatro frases sobre tus propios planes: una con *will* (opinión), una con *going to* (plan), una con present continuous (arreglo) y una con Present Simple (horario, si aplica).

### Practica con el audio de la unidad

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

Escucha esta combinación de frases dos veces: la primera solo para identificar de oído qué forma futura aparece en cada una; la segunda repitiendo cada frase completa en voz alta.

---

## 11. Practica más: listening y reading extra

Este segundo texto repite las cuatro formas de futuro en un contexto distinto —un fin de semana en la playa— para que sigas entrenando el reconocimiento con más variedad.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/listening-future.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: future in context"></audio>

> This weekend the weather forecast says it is going to be sunny, so we are going to the beach on Saturday. We are meeting our friends there at eleven, right after the bus arrives at the station. I think we will stay until sunset if everyone is having a good time. The last bus back to the city leaves at nine in the evening.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/reading-future.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: future in context"></audio>

---

## 12. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige la forma

1. I \_\_\_\_ visit my parents next weekend. (plan)
2. I think it \_\_\_\_ rain tomorrow.
3. She \_\_\_\_ meeting her boss at 3 PM.
4. Wait — I \_\_\_\_ help you.
5. Look at the clouds! It \_\_\_\_ rain.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am going to** · 2. **will** · 3. **is** · 4. **will** · 5. **is going to**

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Arreglos y horarios

1. We \_\_\_\_ flying to Rome on Friday.
2. They \_\_\_\_ having a meeting tomorrow at 9.
3. The flight \_\_\_\_ at 10 AM. (*departs*)
4. She \_\_\_\_ meeting her sister at the airport at 5.
5. I promise I \_\_\_\_ call you when I arrive.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **are** · 2. **are** · 3. **departs** · 4. **is** · 5. **will**

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Travel vocab

1. Where you wait for a plane = \_\_\_\_
2. Document to travel abroad = \_\_\_\_
3. Plane leaves the ground = \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_
4. Reserve a room = \_\_\_\_
5. Delay in departure = \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **airport** · 2. **passport** · 3. **takes off** · 4. **book** · 5. **delay**

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrección

1. *I will visiting my parents next weekend.* → \_\_\_\_
2. *Look! It will rain* (nubes negras) → más natural: \_\_\_\_
3. *The flight is depart at 10.* → \_\_\_\_
4. *I think I am going to enjoy* (solo opinión, sin evidencia) → también: \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **am going to visit**… / I **am visiting**…
2. It **is going to** rain.
3. The flight **departs** at 10.
4. I think I **will** enjoy…

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading (Tokyo)

1. The person is flying next \_\_\_\_.
2. They are meeting colleagues at the airport at \_\_\_\_ AM.
3. The plane takes off at \_\_\_\_.
4. They think they \_\_\_\_ enjoy the trip.
5. They \_\_\_\_ going to visit temples if they have time.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **month** · 2. **6** · 3. **8** · 4. **will** · 5. **are**

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Listening extra (beach weekend)

1. The forecast says it is going to be \_\_\_\_.
2. They are going to the \_\_\_\_ on Saturday.
3. They are meeting friends there at \_\_\_\_.
4. The last bus back leaves at \_\_\_\_ in the evening.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **sunny** · 2. **beach** · 3. **eleven** · 4. **nine**

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Produce tus propias frases

Escribe una frase con *will* (opinión), una con *going to* (plan) y una con present continuous (arreglo fijo).

<details>
<summary>Modelo</summary>

I think it **will** be a great trip. I **am going to** book my flight this week. We **are meeting** at the station at nine tomorrow.

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Traducción al inglés

1. Creo que va a llover mañana.
2. Voy a visitar a mis padres el próximo fin de semana.
3. Nos vemos en el aeropuerto a las seis.
4. El vuelo sale a las diez.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I think it will rain tomorrow.**
2. **I am going to visit my parents next weekend.**
3. **We are meeting at the airport at six.**
4. **The flight departs at ten.**

</details>

---

## Tip del profesor

Antes de elegir la forma futura, pregúntate: ¿esto es solo una **opinión** sin plan (→ *will*), un **plan** que ya decidí antes de hablar o algo que **veo venir ahora mismo** (→ *going to*), una **cita concreta** con hora y lugar (→ present continuous), o un **horario oficial** ajeno a mi voluntad (→ Present Simple)? Practica con tu próximo viaje real: seguro que puedes construir al menos una frase con cada una de las cuatro formas.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Forma | Señal |
| :--- | :--- |
| will | I think · promise · Wait… · probably |
| going to | plan · intention · Look! (evidencia) |
| present continuous | Friday at 3 · airport at 6 · fixed |
| Present Simple | timetable · departs · takes off |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso B1

En la **Unidad 7** estudiarás **was/were going to**: planes e intenciones del pasado que **no ocurrieron**, con vocabulario de *plans & intentions*.

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 6 B1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-6-future-will-going-to-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 6 — Future forms](/curso-b1/unit-6)

Curso:

- [Unidad 7 — Was/were going to](/curso-b1/unit-7)

Guías relacionadas:

- [will vs going to](/blog/gramatica/will-going-to-diferencia)
- [U5 — Repaso 1–4](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-5-repaso-1-4)
- [Cursos online de inglés B1](/blog/metodos/cursos-online-ingles-b1)

---

title: Subject & Object Questions A2: Who saw you? / Who did you see?
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 34 del curso A2: preguntas de sujeto (sin do/does/did) y de objeto, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende preguntas de sujeto y objeto en inglés A2: Who saw you? vs Who did you see?. Sin do/does/did en sujeto. Guía Unidad 34 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema de preguntas de sujeto y objeto A2

faqs.question: ¿Qué es una subject question?
faqs.answer: Pregunta por el sujeto de la frase. No usa do/does/did: Who called you? What happened? El verbo va en forma normal (called, happens…).

faqs.question: ¿Qué es una object question?
faqs.answer: Pregunta por el objeto (o complemento). Usa do/does/did + infinitivo: Who did you call? What do you want?

faqs.question: ¿Cómo sé si es sujeto u objeto?
faqs.answer: Mira la respuesta. Si la respuesta hace la acción (Tom called me → Who called you?), es sujeto. Si recibe la acción (I called Tom → Who did you call?), es objeto.

faqs.question: ¿Who y What sirven para ambos tipos?
faqs.answer: Sí. Who saw you? / Who did you see? y What happened? / What did you see? Which también aparece en ambos contextos.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 34 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-34-subject-object-questions-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 34 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 33](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-33-gerunds-infinitives) practicaste gerundios e infinitivos. En la **Unidad 34 del curso A2** (*Subject & Object Questions*) aprendes a preguntar por el **sujeto** o por el **objeto** — y a no mezclar las dos estructuras.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 34 — Subject & Object Questions](/curso-a2/unit-34)  
> **Antes:** [U33 — Gerundios e infinitivos](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-33-gerunds-infinitives)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 34 (A2)

- Hacer **subject questions** (*Who called you?*) **sin** *do/does/did*.
- Hacer **object questions** (*Who did you call?*) **con** *do/does/did*.
- Usar **who, what, which** en ambos tipos.
- Entender entrevistas y cuestionarios simples.
- Evitar el error típico: ~~Who did call you?~~ / ~~Who you saw?~~

![Subject and object questions](/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/a2-unit34-subject-object.png)

---

## 1. Idea clave: ¿preguntas por quién/qué hace, o por quién/qué recibe?

Frase base: **Tom called Ana.**

| Preguntas por… | Pregunta | Respuesta |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sujeto** (quién llamó) | **Who called** Ana? | Tom. |
| **Objeto** (a quién llamó) | **Who did** Tom **call**? | Ana. |

Misma idea con *what*:

| | Pregunta | Respuesta |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Sujeto | **What happened?** | An accident. |
| Objeto | **What did** you **see**? | An accident. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/who-called-you.mp3" title="🔊 Who called you?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/who-did-you-call.mp3" title="🔊 Who did you call?"></audio>

---

## 2. Subject questions (sin *do/does/did*)

Preguntas por el **sujeto**. El orden es como una frase afirmativa, pero empieza con *Who / What / Which…*

| Tiempo | Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Present Simple | Who/What + verbo (-s si 3ª) | **Who lives** here? **What causes** this? |
| Past Simple | Who/What + pasado | **Who saw** you? **What happened?** |
| Present Continuous | Who/What + is/are + -ing | **Who is calling**? |
| with *be* | Who/What + am/is/are/was/were | **Who is** the teacher? |

> **Who works** in this office?  
> **What makes** you happy?  
> **Which train** goes to London?

**Importante:** no pongas *do/does/did* delante del verbo principal.

~~Who did call you?~~ → **Who called you?**  
~~Who does live here?~~ → **Who lives here?**

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/who-lives-here.mp3" title="🔊 Who lives here?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/what-happened.mp3" title="🔊 What happened yesterday?"></audio>

---

## 3. Object questions (con *do/does/did*)

Preguntas por el **objeto** (o un complemento). Aquí sí usas auxiliar + infinitivo:

| Tiempo | Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Present | Who/What + do/does + sujeto + infinitivo | **Who do** you **know**? **What does** she **want**? |
| Past | Who/What + did + sujeto + infinitivo | **Who did** you **see**? **What did** they **buy**? |

> **Who did** you **call** last night?  
> **What do** you **need**?  
> **Which film did** you **watch**?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/what-did-you-buy.mp3" title="🔊 What did you buy?"></audio>

![Who / What two patterns](/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/a2-unit34-who-what.png)

---

## 4. Truco rápido para elegir

1. Piensa en la **respuesta**.  
2. Si la respuesta **hace** la acción → **subject question** (sin *did*).  
3. Si la respuesta **recibe** la acción / es el objeto → **object question** (con *did*).

| Situación | Pregunta |
| :--- | :--- |
| Alguien te llamó; quieres saber quién | **Who called you?** |
| Tú llamaste a alguien; quieres saber a quién | **Who did you call?** |
| Pasó algo; quieres el suceso | **What happened?** |
| Tú viste algo; quieres el objeto | **What did you see?** |

---

## 5. *Who, what, which*

| Palabra | Uso típico | Subject | Object |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Who** | personas | Who phoned you? | Who did you phone? |
| **What** | cosas / hechos | What happened? | What did you say? |
| **Which** | elección (de un grupo) | Which bus stops here? | Which bus did you take? |

> **Which** students **passed** the exam? *(subject)*  
> **Which** students **did** you **help**? *(object)*

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/which-bus.mp3" title="🔊 Which bus did you take?"></audio>

---

## 6. Present Simple: *does* solo en object questions

Con *he/she/it* en **object questions**:

> **What does** she **want**?  
> **Who does** Tom **like**?

En **subject questions**, la *-s* va en el verbo principal:

> **Who wants** coffee?  
> **What makes** that noise?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/who-wants-coffee.mp3" title="🔊 Who wants coffee?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/what-does-she-want.mp3" title="🔊 What does she want?"></audio>

---

## 7. Lectura y diálogo

### Lectura: un mensaje

Someone called me yesterday. **Who called** me? It was Ana. She asked about the party. **What did** she **want**? She wanted my address. **Who did** I **tell**? I told my brother. **What happened** later? We went to the café together.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/reading-message.mp3" title="🔊 Someone called me yesterday…"></audio>

### Diálogo: entrevista corta

**A:** **Who lives** in that flat?  
**B:** My cousin.  
**A:** **Who did** you **visit** last weekend?  
**B:** My cousin! **What happened** there?  
**A:** Nothing special — but **what did** you **eat**?  
**B:** Homemade pizza. **Who made** it? My cousin's partner.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/dialogue-interview.mp3" title="🔊 Who lives in that flat?"></audio>

![Interview questions](/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/a2-unit34-interview.png)

### Mini práctica (4 frases)

Who called you? Who did you call? What happened? What did you see?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Who called you? Who did you call?"></audio>

---

## 8. Errores frecuentes

1. **Subject + did:** ~~Who did call you?~~ → **Who called you?**  
2. **Object sin auxiliar:** ~~Who you saw?~~ → **Who did you see?**  
3. **Doble pasado:** ~~Who did you saw?~~ → **Who did you see?**  
4. ***-s* + does juntos mal:** ~~Who does wants coffee?~~ → **Who wants coffee?** / **What does she want?**  
5. **Confundir sentido:** *Who saw you?* ≠ *Who did you see?*

---

## 9. Ejercicios (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — ¿Subject (S) u Object (O)?

1. Who called you? ___  
2. Who did you call? ___  
3. What happened? ___  
4. What did you buy? ___  
5. Who lives here? ___  
6. Who do you live with? ___

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. S  
2. O  
3. S  
4. O  
5. S  
6. O  

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa (*did* o nada + forma verbal)

1. Who ___ (call) you yesterday?  
2. Who ___ you ___ (call) yesterday?  
3. What ___ (happen) at school?  
4. What ___ you ___ (see)?  
5. Who ___ (want) tea?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. called  
2. did / call  
3. happened  
4. did / see  
5. wants  

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Reescribe como pregunta correcta

Respuesta → pregunta:

1. Tom called me. → Who _______________?  
2. I called Tom. → Who _______________?  
3. An accident happened. → What _______________?  
4. I saw an accident. → What _______________?  
5. Maria lives here. → Who _______________?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Who called you?  
2. Who did you call?  
3. What happened?  
4. What did you see?  
5. Who lives here?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Elige la opción correcta

1. ___ you yesterday evening?  
   a) Who called  b) Who did call  c) Who you called  
2. ___ at the party?  
   a) Who you see  b) Who did you see  c) Who saw you did  
3. ___ this noise?  
   a) What does make  b) What makes  c) What did makes  
4. ___ she want?  
   a) What  b) What does  c) What do  
5. ___ the blue bus or the red one?  
   a) Which did you take  b) Which you took  c) Which took you did  

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. a  
2. b  
3. b  
4. b  
5. a  

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Corrige el error

1. Who did call you?  
2. Who you saw at the cinema?  
3. What did happened?  
4. Who does lives here?  
5. What she want?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Who called you?  
2. Who did you see at the cinema?  
3. What happened?  
4. Who lives here?  
5. What does she want?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Traduce al inglés

1. ¿Quién te llamó?  
2. ¿A quién llamaste?  
3. ¿Qué pasó?  
4. ¿Qué compraste?  
5. ¿Quién vive aquí?  
6. ¿Qué quiere ella?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Who called you?  
2. Who did you call?  
3. What happened?  
4. What did you buy?  
5. Who lives here?  
6. What does she want?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Completa el diálogo

**A:** ___ (Who / phone) you this morning?  
**B:** My boss.  
**A:** ___ (What / he / want)?  
**B:** He wanted the report.  
**A:** ___ (Who / you / call) after that?  
**B:** Ana. ___ (What / happen) then? We finished the report together.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

Who phoned  
What did he want  
Who did you call  
What happened  

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — *Which*

1. ___ train goes to Oxford? *(subject)*  
2. ___ train did you take? *(object)*  
3. ___ students passed? *(subject)*  
4. ___ students did you help? *(object)*

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Which  
2. Which  
3. Which  
4. Which  

*(La diferencia está en el resto de la pregunta: goes vs did you take; passed vs did you help.)*

</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Empareja

1. Who broke the window?  
2. Who did you invite?  
3. What caused the delay?  
4. What did the delay cause?  

a) The snow.  
b) Many cancellations.  
c) Tom (he broke it).  
d) My classmates (I invited them).

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1 → c  
2 → d  
3 → a  
4 → b  

</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tu entrevista (8–10 preguntas)

Escribe un mini cuestionario con:

- 3 **subject questions**  
- 3 **object questions**  
- al menos un *what* y un *which*

**Modelo:** el diálogo de la sección 7.

---

## 10. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Tabla sujeto vs objeto.  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha lectura y diálogo; marca S/O.  
4. **5–8 min** — Escribe el cuestionario (Ejercicio 10) y léelo en voz alta.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sé qué es subject vs object question  
- [ ] No uso *did* en *Who called you?*  
- [ ] Uso *did* + infinitivo en *Who did you call?*  
- [ ] Domino *who / what / which* en ambos tipos  
- [ ] Puedo corregir ~~Who did call you?~~ y ~~Who you saw?~~

---

## 11. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Practica **pares**: *Who saw you?* / *Who did you see?*  
2. Mira siempre la **respuesta** para elegir la estructura.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 34](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-34-subject-object-questions-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 34 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-34).

La **Unidad 35** revisa **some, any, much, many** (y cantidades A2).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tipo | ¿Auxiliar? | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Subject | No *do/does/did* | Who called you? What happened? |
| Object | Sí *do/does/did* + base | Who did you call? What did you see? |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 35** verás **Some, Any, Much, Many (revisión)**.

Guía blog:

- [Unidad 35 — Some, any, much, many](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-35-some-any-much-many)

Curso:

- [Unidad 35 — Some, Any, Much, Many](/curso-a2/unit-35)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 34 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-34-subject-object-questions-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 34 — Subject & Object Questions](/curso-a2/unit-34)

Guías relacionadas:

- [U33 — Gerundios e infinitivos](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-33-gerunds-infinitives)

- [U19 — How questions](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-19-how-questions)

---

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A2: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- Cambridge English — A2 Key: https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/key/
