title: ¿Cómo Repasar el Módulo 2 de A2? Present Perfect y Más
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Present Perfect, Past Continuous, for/since y How questions: repasa el Módulo 2 de A2 con audios y ejercicios (Unidad 20).
description: Integra el Módulo 2 del curso A2: Present Perfect, Past Continuous, for/since y How questions. Guía Unidad 20 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema de repaso del Módulo 2 del curso A2

faqs.question: ¿Qué se repasa en la Unidad 20 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: El Módulo 2 completo (unidades 11–19): Present Perfect (ever, never, already, yet, just), contraste con Past Simple, Past Continuous, when/while, for/since y How questions.

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso Present Perfect y cuándo Past Continuous?
faqs.answer: Present Perfect para experiencias o resultados ligados al presente (I have been to Paris / I have already finished). Past Continuous para una acción en curso en el pasado (I was walking when…).

faqs.question: ¿For o since?
faqs.answer: For + duración (for three years). Since + punto de inicio (since 2021). Ambos con Present Perfect cuando la situación sigue.

faqs.question: ¿Qué preguntas How debo dominar?
faqs.answer: How long (duración), How often (frecuencia), How much (incontable), How many (contable) y How long ago (pasado + ago).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 20 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones y en la Unidad 20 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En las [unidades 11–19](/blog/curso-a2) construiste el Módulo 2. En la **Unidad 20 del curso A2** (*Module 2 Review*) **combinas** todo: experiencias, escenas en pasado, duración y preguntas *How…?* en un mismo relato.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 20 — Repaso Módulo 2](/curso-a2/unit-20)  
> **Antes:** [U19 — How Questions](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-19-how-questions)

---

## Qué repasará la Unidad 20 (A2)

| Bloque | Unidades | Forma clave |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Present Perfect intro | [U11](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-11-present-perfect-introduccion) | *have/has + past participle* |
| Ever & Never | [U12](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-12-present-perfect-ever-never) | *Have you ever…? / I have never…* |
| Already & Yet | [U13](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-13-present-perfect-already-yet) | *already / yet* |
| Just | [U14](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-14-present-perfect-just) | *have just…* |
| PP vs Past Simple | [U15](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-15-present-perfect-vs-past-simple) | *ever* vs *yesterday / ago* |
| Past Continuous | [U16](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-16-past-continuous) | *was/were + -ing* |
| PS + PC | [U17](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-17-past-simple-past-continuous) | *when / while* |
| For & Since | [U18](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-18-for-since) | *for* duración / *since* punto |
| How questions | [U19](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-19-how-questions) | *How long / often / much / many* |

![Repaso Módulo 2 A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/a2-unit20-module2-review.png)

---

## 1. Formas rápidas (cheat sheet)

![Formas rápidas del Módulo 2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/a2-unit20-quick-forms.png)

| Tema | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Present Perfect | have/has + PP | I **have been** to Paris. |
| Ever / Never | ever…? / never + PP | Have you **ever**…? I have **never**… |
| Already / Yet | already mid · yet final | I have **already** finished. / I haven't… **yet**. |
| Just | have/has + just + PP | I have **just** arrived. |
| PP vs PS | sin fecha vs con fecha | I have been to Japan. / Last year I **went**… |
| Past Continuous | was/were + -ing | I **was walking**… |
| When / While | fondo + interrupción | I was walking **when** I met… |
| For / Since | duración / punto | **for** three years / **since** 2021 |
| How…? | long / often / much / many | How **often** do you exercise? |

---

## 2. Present Perfect (U11–U14)

> I **have been** to Paris twice.  
> Have you **ever** been to Japan?  
> I have **never** been to Australia.  
> I have **already** finished my course.  
> I haven't found a new job **yet**.  
> I have **just** arrived.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/have-been-paris.mp3" title="🔊 I have been to Paris twice"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/already-finished-course.mp3" title="🔊 I have already finished my course this year"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/havent-found-job-yet.mp3" title="🔊 I haven't found a new job yet"></audio>

---

## 3. Present Perfect vs Past Simple (U15)

> I **have lived** in Barcelona for three years. *(sigue)*  
> Last week I **met** an old friend. *(fecha concreta)*  
> I **have already visited** five countries this year.  
> I haven't been to Japan **yet**.

Regla: ¿hay momento concreto (*last week, yesterday, ago*)? → Past Simple. ¿Experiencia / resultado / *already-yet-just-ever-never-for-since*? → Present Perfect.

---

## 4. Past Continuous + when/while (U16–U17)

> Last week I **was walking** in the park when I **met** an old friend.  
> We **were talking** while we walked.  
> Yesterday I **was cooking** dinner when my sister **called**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/was-walking-when-met.mp3" title="🔊 I was walking in the park when I met an old friend"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/was-cooking-when-called.mp3" title="🔊 I was cooking dinner when my sister called"></audio>

Fondo = *was/were + -ing*. Interrupción = Past Simple.

---

## 5. For & Since + How questions (U18–U19)

> I have lived here **for** three years.  
> I have worked as a teacher **since** 2021.  
> **How long** have you lived in Barcelona?  
> **How often** do you go to the gym? — Three times a week.  
> **How many** countries have you visited? — Five.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/lived-for-three-years.mp3" title="🔊 I have lived in Barcelona for three years"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/worked-since-2021.mp3" title="🔊 I have worked as a teacher since 2021"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/how-often-gym.mp3" title="🔊 How often do you go to the gym?"></audio>

---

## 6. Texto modelo: David

> My name is David. I have lived in Barcelona for three years. I have worked as a teacher since 2021. Last week I was walking in the park when I met an old friend. We were talking while we walked. How often do I exercise? I go to the gym three times a week. I have already finished my course this year but I haven't found a new job yet. I feel good because I have a stable life with good friends.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/reading-david.mp3" title="🔊 My name is David. I have lived in Barcelona…"></audio>

![Historia de David — Módulo 2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/a2-unit20-david-story.png)

| Estructura | Ejemplo en David |
| :--- | :--- |
| for | lived… **for** three years |
| since | worked… **since** 2021 |
| was … when | **was walking** when I **met**… |
| while | **were talking** while we walked |
| How often | gym **three times a week** |
| already / yet | **already** finished / haven't found… **yet** |

---

## 7. Listening: Maria

> Hi! I am Maria. I have lived in Valencia for four years. I have worked at a hospital since 2020. Yesterday I was cooking dinner when my sister called. We were talking while I was finishing the food. How often do I exercise? I go swimming twice a week. I have already visited five countries this year but I haven't been to Japan yet. I feel happy because I have a good job and a wonderful family.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/dialogue-maria.mp3" title="🔊 Hi! I am Maria. I have lived in Valencia…"></audio>

Preguntas rápidas:

1. ¿Cuánto tiempo en Valencia? → *for four years*  
2. ¿Desde cuándo en el hospital? → *since 2020*  
3. ¿Qué hacía cuando llamó su hermana? → *cooking dinner*  
4. ¿Ha estado en Japón? → *No, not yet*

---

## 8. Mini práctica oral

> I have lived here for three years.  
> I was walking when I met a friend.  
> How often do you go to the gym?  
> I have already finished, but I haven't started yet.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 I have lived here for three years…"></audio>

1. 2 frases Present Perfect (*ever/never/already/yet/just/for/since*).  
2. 2 frases *was/were … when …*  
3. 2 preguntas *How…?* + respuestas.

---

## 9. Errores frecuentes del módulo

| Incorrecto | Correcto |
| :--- | :--- |
| I have been to Paris last year. | I **went** to Paris last year. |
| I was walk when I met him. | I was **walking** when I met him. |
| I have lived here since three years. | I have lived here **for** three years. |
| How many water…? | How **much** water…? |
| I have already finished yet. | I have **already** finished. / I haven't finished **yet**. |
| How long ago have you arrived? | How long ago **did** you arrive? |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/visited-five-countries.mp3" title="🔊 I have already visited five countries this year"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/havent-been-japan-yet.mp3" title="🔊 I haven't been to Japan yet"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-20/swimming-twice-week.mp3" title="🔊 I go swimming twice a week"></audio>

---

## 10. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige la forma

1. I ____ been to Paris twice. *(have / went)*  
2. She ____ watching TV when I called. *(was / were)*  
3. I have lived here ____ five years. *(for / since)*  
4. I have worked here ____ 2021. *(for / since)*  
5. How ____ do you go to the gym? *(long / often / many)*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **have** · 2. **was** · 3. **for** · 4. **since** · 5. **often**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa a David

I have lived in Barcelona ____ three years. I have worked as a teacher ____ 2021. Last week I ____ walking when I ____ an old friend. I go to the gym three times a ____. I have ____ finished my course but I haven't found a new job ____.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**for** · **since** · **was** · **met** · **week** · **already** · **yet**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Completa a Maria

I have lived in Valencia ____ four years. I have worked at a hospital ____ 2020. Yesterday I ____ cooking when my sister ____. I go swimming ____ a week. I have ____ visited five countries but I haven't been to Japan ____.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**for** · **since** · **was** · **called** · **twice** · **already** · **yet**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Empareja tema → unidad

1. ever / never  
2. was/were + -ing  
3. for / since  
4. How much / How many  
5. already / yet  

a) U13 · b) U12 · c) U16 · d) U18 · e) U19

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **c** · 3 → **d** · 4 → **e** · 5 → **a**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Corrige

1. *I have been to Japan last year.*  
2. *I was walk when I met him.*  
3. *I have lived here since three years.*  
4. *How many water do you drink?*  
5. *I have already finished yet.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **went** to Japan last year.  
2. I was **walking** when I met him.  
3. I have lived here **for** three years.  
4. How **much** water do you drink?  
5. I have **already** finished. / I haven't finished **yet**.
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Elige la correcta

1. ____  
   a) I was walking when I met him. · b) I walked when I was meeting him. · c) I was walk when I met him.  
2. ____  
   a) I have lived here for three years. · b) I have lived here since three years. · c) I live here for three years.  
3. ____  
   a) How often do you exercise? · b) How long do you exercise a week? *(frecuencia)* · c) How many do you exercise?  
4. ____  
   a) I have already finished. · b) I have finished already the course. · c) I have already finish.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a** · 2. **a** · 3. **a** · 4. **a**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Traduce

1. He vivido en Barcelona durante tres años.  
2. Trabajo como profesor desde 2021.  
3. Estaba caminando cuando conocí a un amigo.  
4. Voy al gimnasio tres veces a la semana.  
5. Ya he terminado el curso.  
6. Aún no he encontrado un nuevo trabajo.  
7. ¿Con qué frecuencia haces ejercicio?  
8. Ya he visitado cinco países este año.  
9. Aún no he estado en Japón.  
10. Ayer estaba cocinando cuando llamó mi hermana.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I have lived in Barcelona for three years.  
2. I have worked as a teacher since 2021.  
3. I was walking when I met a friend.  
4. I go to the gym three times a week.  
5. I have already finished the course.  
6. I haven't found a new job yet.  
7. How often do you exercise?  
8. I have already visited five countries this year.  
9. I haven't been to Japan yet.  
10. Yesterday I was cooking when my sister called.
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Tu texto integrado

Escribe 10–14 frases que incluyan:

- 2 × Present Perfect (*already/yet/ever/never/just*)  
- 1 × *for* · 1 × *since*  
- 2 × *was/were … when …*  
- 2 × *How…?* (pregunta o respuesta)  

**Modelo:** David o Maria.

---

## 11. Plan de estudio (30–35 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Recorre el mapa U11–U19.  
2. **10 min** — Ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **8 min** — Escucha a David y Maria; marca cada estructura.  
4. **8–10 min** — Escribe y graba tu texto integrado.

### Checklist final del Módulo 2

- [ ] Uso Present Perfect para experiencias y resultados (*ever/never/already/yet/just*)  
- [ ] Eligo Present Perfect vs Past Simple según el marcador  
- [ ] Describo escenas con *was/were + -ing*  
- [ ] Combino con *when/while*  
- [ ] Uso *for* (duración) y *since* (punto)  
- [ ] Pregunto con *How long / often / much / many*  
- [ ] Puedo escribir un párrafo que combine **todo**

---

## 12. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. No estudies cada tema aislado: **fuerza la mezcla** (como David).  
2. Mínimos: *have been, already, yet, just, was walking when, for, since, How often*.  
3. Grábate 60–90 segundos sobre tu vida ahora + algo que pasó la semana pasada.  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 20](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-20-repaso-modulo-2-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 20 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-20).

La **Unidad 21** abre el **Módulo 3** con **Going to**: planes e intenciones (*I'm going to…*).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Forma |
| :--- | :--- |
| Present Perfect | *have/has + PP* |
| Ever / Never / Already / Yet / Just | marcadores PP |
| PP vs PS | sin fecha vs *yesterday/ago* |
| Past Continuous | *was/were + -ing* |
| When / While | interrupción / fondo |
| For / Since | duración / punto |
| How…? | long / often / much / many |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 21** empezarás **Going to: Plans & Intentions**: *I'm going to travel next summer*.

Guía blog:

- [Unidad 21 — Going to: planes e intenciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-21-going-to-planes-intenciones)

Curso:

- [Unidad 21 — Going to](/curso-a2/unit-21)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 20 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-20-repaso-modulo-2-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 20 — Module 2 Review](/curso-a2/unit-20)

Guías del Módulo 2 (repaso):

- [U11 — Present Perfect: Introducción](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-11-present-perfect-introduccion)
- [U12 — Ever & Never](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-12-present-perfect-ever-never)
- [U13 — Already & Yet](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-13-present-perfect-already-yet)
- [U14 — Just](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-14-present-perfect-just)
- [U15 — Present Perfect vs Past Simple](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-15-present-perfect-vs-past-simple)
- [U16 — Past Continuous](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-16-past-continuous)
- [U17 — Past Simple + Past Continuous](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-17-past-simple-past-continuous)
- [U18 — For & Since](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-18-for-since)

- [Inglés A2: guía del nivel](/blog/metodos/ingles-a2)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Present Perfect: usos principales](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-usos-principales)
- [Present Perfect vs Past Simple](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-vs-past-simple)
- [Past Simple vs Past Continuous](/blog/gramatica/past-simple-vs-past-continuous)
- [Present Perfect: since / for](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-since-for)

title: Present Perfect A2: Already, Yet y Usos
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 13 del curso A2: Present Perfect con already y yet, listas de tareas, audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende already y yet con Present Perfect A2: posición, significado y ejemplos para hablar de lo ya hecho y lo que aún falta, con audio y ejercicios prácticos.
alt: Esquema already y yet del Present Perfect A2

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso already con Present Perfect?
faqs.answer: En afirmativas para decir que algo ya está hecho (a menudo antes de lo esperado): I have already finished my homework. Already va entre have/has y el past participle.

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso yet?
faqs.answer: En negativas e interrogativas: I haven't done the shopping yet. Have you washed the dishes yet? Yet suele ir al final de la frase.

faqs.question: ¿Already y yet significan lo mismo que ever/never?
faqs.answer: No. Ever/never hablan de experiencias en la vida. Already/yet hablan del progreso de tareas: lo ya completado o lo que aún no.

faqs.question: ¿Puedo poner yet en medio de la frase?
faqs.answer: En A2 prioriza yet al final: I haven't finished yet. Have you finished yet? Evita I haven't yet finished como forma principal del curso.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 13 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones y en la Unidad 13 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 12](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-12-present-perfect-ever-never) preguntaste *Have you ever…?*. En la **Unidad 13 del curso A2** (*Present Perfect: Already & Yet*) hablas de **progreso**: lo que **ya** has hecho y lo que **aún no**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 13 — Present Perfect: Already & Yet](/curso-a2/unit-13)  
> **Antes:** [U12 — Ever & Never](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-12-present-perfect-ever-never)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 13 (A2)

- Usar **already** en afirmativas: *I have already finished…*
- Usar **yet** en negativas: *I haven't… yet*
- Preguntar con **yet**: *Have you… yet? / Has she… yet?*
- Colocar bien las palabras (*already* en medio · *yet* al final).
- Hablar de tareas y obligaciones del día.

![Already y yet Present Perfect A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/a2-unit13-already-yet.png)

---

## 1. Idea clave

| Palabra | Significado A2 | Tipo de frase |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **already** | ya (antes de ahora / antes de lo esperado) | afirmativa |
| **yet** | aún / todavía (no ha pasado hasta ahora) | negativa e interrogativa |

No confundas con *ever/never* (experiencias de vida). Aquí: **lista de tareas**.

---

## 2. *Already* en afirmativas

**Already** va **entre** *have/has* y el past participle:

> I **have already** finished my homework.  
> He **has already** eaten breakfast.  
> I **have already** cleaned my room.  
> I **have already** done my chores.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/have-already-finished.mp3" title="🔊 I have already finished my homework"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/has-already-eaten.mp3" title="🔊 He has already eaten breakfast"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/have-already-cleaned.mp3" title="🔊 I have already cleaned my room"></audio>

Estructura: **have/has + already + past participle**

---

## 3. *Yet* en negativas

**Yet** va **al final** de la negativa:

> I **haven't** done the shopping **yet**.  
> I **haven't** finished **yet**.  
> She **hasn't** called **yet**.  
> I **haven't** paid the electricity bill **yet**.  
> I **haven't** sent the emails **yet**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/havent-done-shopping-yet.mp3" title="🔊 I haven't done the shopping yet"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/havent-finished-yet.mp3" title="🔊 I haven't finished yet"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/havent-called-yet.mp3" title="🔊 She hasn't called yet"></audio>

Estructura: **haven't/hasn't + past participle + … + yet**

---

## 4. *Yet* en preguntas

También al **final**:

> **Has she cleaned** her room **yet**?  
> **Have you washed** the dishes **yet**?  
> Have you finished yet?  
> Has he called yet?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/has-she-cleaned-yet.mp3" title="🔊 Has she cleaned her room yet?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/have-you-washed-yet.mp3" title="🔊 Have you washed the dishes yet?"></audio>

Respuestas típicas:

- *Yes, I have.* / *Yes, she has.* *(a menudo + already)*  
- *No, I haven't.* / *No, not yet.*

---

## 5. Posición: *already* vs *yet*

![Posición already y yet](/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/a2-unit13-word-position.png)

| Palabra | Posición prioritaria A2 | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **already** | entre *have/has* y el participio | I have **already** finished… |
| **yet** | al final | I haven't finished **yet**. / Have you finished **yet**? |

| Correcto | Incorrecto / menos prioritario A2 |
| :--- | :--- |
| I have already finished. | *I already have finished.* |
| I haven't finished yet. | *I haven't yet finished.* |
| Have you finished yet? | *Have you yet finished?* |

---

## 6. Texto modelo: Sofia

> My name is Sofia. I have many tasks every day. This morning I have already cleaned my room and done the washing. I have already finished my homework too. But I haven't paid the electricity bill yet. I must do it today. I also haven't called my grandmother yet. She is waiting for my call. I feel good because I have already completed most of my obligations today.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/reading-sofia.mp3" title="🔊 My name is Sofia. I have many tasks…"></audio>

![Lista de tareas con already y yet](/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/a2-unit13-chores-list.png)

| Ya hecho (*already*) | Aún no (*yet*) |
| :--- | :--- |
| cleaned my room | paid the electricity bill |
| done the washing | called my grandmother |
| finished my homework | |

---

## 7. Listening: Lucas

> Hi! I am Lucas. I have a busy week. Today I have already done my chores and finished the shopping. I have already cleaned the kitchen too. But I haven't sent the emails yet. I must do that before dinner. I also haven't called my boss yet. He is waiting for my call. I feel relaxed because I have already completed most of my tasks for today.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/dialogue-lucas.mp3" title="🔊 Hi! I am Lucas. I have a busy week…"></audio>

Preguntas rápidas:

1. ¿Qué ha hecho ya? → *chores, shopping, kitchen*  
2. ¿Qué falta? → *emails, call his boss*  
3. ¿Cómo se siente? → *relaxed* (ha completado la mayor parte)

---

## 8. Mini práctica oral

> I have already finished my homework.  
> I haven't done the shopping yet.  
> Has she cleaned her room yet?  
> He has already eaten breakfast.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-13/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 I have already finished my homework…"></audio>

1. Di 3 cosas que **ya** has hecho hoy (*already*).  
2. Di 3 cosas que **aún no** (*haven't… yet*).  
3. Haz 2 preguntas *Have you… yet?*

---

## 9. Vocabulario de tareas (del curso)

| Inglés | Idea |
| :--- | :--- |
| clean my room / the kitchen | limpiar |
| do the washing / the shopping / my chores | hacer la colada / compras / tareas |
| finish my homework | terminar deberes |
| wash the dishes | lavar los platos |
| pay a bill | pagar una factura |
| send emails | enviar correos |
| call my grandmother / my boss | llamar |

---

## 10. Errores frecuentes

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I already have finished. | I have **already** finished. | *already* tras *have* |
| I haven't yet finished. *(prioridad A2)* | I haven't finished **yet**. | *yet* al final |
| I have finished yet. | I have **already** finished. / I haven't finished **yet**. | *yet* no va en afirmativas A2 |
| I haven't already finished. | I haven't finished **yet**. | negativa → *yet* |
| Have you already finished yet? | Have you finished **yet**? / Have you **already** finished? | no mezclar las dos |
| Did you finish yet? *(si quieres Present Perfect A2)* | **Have** you finished **yet**? | Present Perfect + *yet* |

---

## 11. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — *already* o *yet*

1. I have ____ finished my homework.  
2. I haven't done the shopping ____.  
3. Has she cleaned her room ____?  
4. He has ____ eaten breakfast.  
5. Have you washed the dishes ____?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **already** · 2. **yet** · 3. **yet** · 4. **already** · 5. **yet**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Posición

Elige la correcta:

1. ____  
   a) I already have finished. · b) I have already finished. · c) I have finished already. *(prioridad A2: mid)*  
2. ____  
   a) I haven't finished yet. · b) I haven't yet finished. · c) I yet haven't finished.  
3. ____  
   a) Have you yet washed the dishes? · b) Have you washed the dishes yet? · c) Yet have you washed the dishes?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b** · 2. **a** · 3. **b**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Completa a Sofia

I have ____ cleaned my room and done the washing. I have ____ finished my homework. But I haven't paid the electricity bill ____. I also haven't called my grandmother ____.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**already** · **already** · **yet** · **yet**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Completa a Lucas

Today I have ____ done my chores and finished the shopping. I have ____ cleaned the kitchen. But I haven't sent the emails ____. I also haven't called my boss ____.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**already** · **already** · **yet** · **yet**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Transforma

1. I finished my homework. *(already + Present Perfect)*  
2. I didn't do the shopping. *(haven't… yet)*  
3. Ask about the dishes. *(Have you… yet?)*  
4. He ate breakfast. *(already)*  
5. She didn't call. *(hasn't… yet)*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I have **already** finished my homework.  
2. I **haven't** done the shopping **yet**.  
3. **Have you washed** the dishes **yet**?  
4. He **has already** eaten breakfast.  
5. She **hasn't** called **yet**.
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Corrige

1. *I already have finished my homework.*  
2. *I haven't yet done the shopping.* *(prioridad A2)*  
3. *I have finished yet.*  
4. *Have you yet cleaned your room?*  
5. *I haven't already called her.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I have **already** finished my homework.  
2. I haven't done the shopping **yet**.  
3. I have **already** finished. / I haven't finished **yet**.  
4. Have you cleaned your room **yet**?  
5. I haven't called her **yet**.
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Empareja

1. already  
2. yet (negativa)  
3. yet (pregunta)  
4. have + already + PP  
5. haven't + PP + yet  

a) I haven't paid the bill yet. · b) Has she cleaned yet? · c) I have already finished. · d) “ya” en afirmativa · e) “aún” en negativa/pregunta

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **d** · 2 → **e** (neg.) · 3 → **e** (preg.) / **b** · 4 → **c** · 5 → **a**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la correcta

1. *Already* se usa sobre todo en: ____  
   a) afirmativas · b) solo negativas · c) solo con *never*  
2. *Yet* en A2 va normalmente: ____  
   a) al principio · b) al final · c) antes de *have*  
3. ____  
   a) I have already cleaned the kitchen. · b) I have cleaned already the kitchen. · c) I already cleaned have the kitchen.  
4. ____  
   a) I haven't sent the emails yet. · b) I haven't sent yet the emails. · c) I haven't already sent the emails.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a** · 2. **b** · 3. **a** · 4. **a**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. Ya he terminado mis deberes.  
2. Aún no he hecho la compra.  
3. ¿Ha limpiado ella su habitación ya/aún?  
4. Él ya ha desayunado.  
5. ¿Has lavado los platos ya?  
6. Aún no he terminado.  
7. Ella aún no ha llamado.  
8. Ya he limpiado mi habitación.  
9. Aún no he pagado la factura de la luz.  
10. Ya he hecho casi todas mis tareas.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I have already finished my homework.  
2. I haven't done the shopping yet.  
3. Has she cleaned her room yet?  
4. He has already eaten breakfast.  
5. Have you washed the dishes yet?  
6. I haven't finished yet.  
7. She hasn't called yet.  
8. I have already cleaned my room.  
9. I haven't paid the electricity bill yet.  
10. I have already completed most of my tasks. / I have already done most of my chores.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tu lista de hoy

Escribe 8–12 frases:

- 4 × *I have already…*  
- 3 × *I haven't… yet*  
- 1 × pregunta *Have you… yet?*  

**Modelo:** Sofia o Lucas.

---

## 12. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Repasa: *already* (medio) · *yet* (final).  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–7.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha a Sofia y Lucas; marca *already/yet*.  
4. **5–8 min** — Escribe y graba tu lista del día.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *already* en afirmativas entre *have/has* y el participio  
- [ ] Uso *yet* al final en negativas y preguntas  
- [ ] No mezclo *already* + *yet* en la misma frase  
- [ ] Puedo describir tareas hechas y pendientes  
- [ ] Distingo *already/yet* de *ever/never*

---

## 13. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Plantilla del día: *I have already… But I haven't… yet.*  
2. Lista: *homework, shopping, dishes, emails, bill, call, clean, chores*.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 13](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-13-present-perfect-already-yet-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 13 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-13).

La **Unidad 14** añade **just**: *I have just…* (acabo de…).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Caso | Forma |
| :--- | :--- |
| Ya hecho | **have/has + already + PP** |
| Aún no | **haven't/hasn't + PP + yet** |
| Pregunta | **Have/Has + sujeto + PP + yet?** |
| Posición *already* | entre *have/has* y el participio |
| Posición *yet* | al final |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 14** estudiarás **Present Perfect: Just**: *I have just finished* / *She has just arrived*.

Guía blog:

- [Unidad 14 — Present Perfect: Just](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-14-present-perfect-just)

Curso:

- [Unidad 14 — Present Perfect: Just](/curso-a2/unit-14)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 13 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-13-present-perfect-already-yet-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 13 — Present Perfect: Already & Yet](/curso-a2/unit-13)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Present Perfect: just / already / yet](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-just-already-yet)
- [Present Perfect: usos principales](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-usos-principales)
- [Present Perfect: ever / never](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-ever-never)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A2: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- Cambridge English — A2 Key: https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/key/
- British Council — Present Perfect: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar/present-perfect

title: Direcciones en Inglés A1: Turn Left y Go Straight
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 26 del curso A1: dar direcciones con imperativos Turn left, Turn right, Go straight y Past the…, más on the left/right y diálogos.
description: Aprende a dar direcciones en inglés A1 con Turn left, Turn right y Go straight, frases útiles, mapas, audio y ejercicios para practicar.
alt: Esquema imperativos Turn left Go straight para direcciones en inglés A1
keywords: on the left on the right

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma el imperativo para dar direcciones en A1?
faqs.answer: Usas la forma base del verbo sin sujeto: Turn left. Go straight. Past the bank. No dices You turn left en indicaciones normales de calle.

faqs.question: ¿Qué significan Turn left, Go straight y Past the…?
faqs.answer: Turn left = gira a la izquierda. Turn right = gira a la derecha. Go straight = sigue recto. Past the bank = pasa el banco (por delante).

faqs.question: ¿Cómo pregunto cómo llegar a un sitio?
faqs.answer: How do I get to the library? / Where is the pharmacy? Respuestas típicas: Go straight… Turn left at the corner… It’s on the left.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es You can’t miss it?
faqs.answer: Significa que el lugar es fácil de ver / no te puedes perder. Se usa al final de unas indicaciones claras.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 26 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 26 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 25](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-25-barrio-the-a-an-some-any) describiste tu barrio. En la **Unidad 26 del curso A1** (*Giving Directions*) aprendes a **indicar el camino** con **imperativos**: ***Turn left, Turn right, Go straight, Past the…***.

Combina lugares de las [Unidades 11](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-11-lugares-ciudad) y [24](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-24-preposiciones-lugar-next-to-between) (*on the left, next to…*). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 26 — Giving Directions](/curso-a1/unit-26)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 25 — Barrio](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-25-barrio-the-a-an-some-any) · [Unidad 24 — Preposiciones](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-24-preposiciones-lugar-next-to-between)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 26 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar imperativos: ***Turn left / right***, ***Go straight***, ***Past the…***.
- Situar el destino: ***on the left / on the right***.
- Preguntar: ***How do I get to…?*** / ***Where is…?***.
- Usar puntos de referencia: *corner, traffic lights, bank, supermarket…*.
- Cerrar con ***You can’t miss it*** y cortesía (*Thanks / You’re welcome*).

---

## 1. El imperativo para direcciones

En indicaciones de calle usas la **forma base** del verbo **sin sujeto**:

```
Turn left.
Go straight.
Past the bank.
Cross the street.
```

No hace falta *you*: *Turn left* (no *You turn left*) es lo natural en A1 para dar el camino.

| Imperativo | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Turn left** | Gira a la izquierda | Turn left at the corner. |
| **Turn right** | Gira a la derecha | Turn right at the traffic lights. |
| **Go straight** | Sigue recto | Go straight for 100 metres. |
| **Past the…** | Pasa el/la… | Past the bank and then turn right. |
| **Cross** | Cruza | Cross the street. |

![Esquema imperativos Turn left Go straight Past the A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/a1-unit26-imperatives.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/turn-left-corner.mp3" title="🔊 Turn left at the corner"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/go-straight-100.mp3" title="🔊 Go straight for 100 metres"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/past-the-bank.mp3" title="🔊 Past the bank and then turn right"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/turn-right-lights.mp3" title="🔊 Turn right at the traffic lights"></audio>

### Tip

*Past the bank* = *go past the bank* (pasa por delante). En el curso aparece mucho la forma corta ***Past the…***.

---

## 2. *Turn left / Turn right*

| Frase | Uso |
| :--- | :--- |
| Turn left **at the corner** | Gira a la izquierda **en la esquina**. |
| Turn right **at the traffic lights** | Gira a la derecha **en el semáforo**. |
| Turn left **at the bank** | Gira a la izquierda **en el banco** (punto de referencia). |

> Turn left at the corner.  
> Turn right at the traffic lights.  
> Go straight and turn right at the bank.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/go-straight-turn-right.mp3" title="🔊 Go straight and turn right at the bank"></audio>

### No digas

| ❌ | ✅ |
| :--- | :--- |
| *Turn to the left* (demasiado largo en A1 calle) | *Turn left* |
| *Turn in left* | *Turn left* |
| *Turn left in the corner* | *Turn left **at** the corner* |

---

## 3. *Go straight*

*Go straight* = sigue en la misma dirección (no gires).

> Go straight for 100 metres.  
> Go straight for about 200 metres.  
> Go straight along this street.  
> Go straight past the bank.  
> Go straight out of the station.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/go-straight-street.mp3" title="🔊 Go straight along this street"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/go-straight-past.mp3" title="🔊 Go straight past the bank"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/library-directions.mp3" title="🔊 Go straight for about 200 metres. Turn left at the corner"></audio>

### Combinaciones útiles

| Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Go straight **for** + distancia | Go straight for 200 metres. |
| Go straight **along** + calle | Go straight along this street. |
| Go straight **past** + lugar | Go straight past the supermarket. |
| Go straight **out of** + lugar | Go straight out of the station. |

---

## 4. *Past the…* y puntos de referencia

*Past the bank* = pasa el banco (no entres; continúa).

> Past the bank and then turn right.  
> Past the supermarket and the cinema is on the right.  
> Past the bank on your right.  
> Go straight past the supermarket.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/past-supermarket.mp3" title="🔊 Past the supermarket and the cinema is on the right"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/past-bank-right.mp3" title="🔊 Past the bank on your right"></audio>

### Vocabulario de calle

| Inglés | Español |
| :--- | :--- |
| corner | esquina |
| traffic lights | semáforo |
| crossing | cruce / paso |
| street | calle |
| station | estación |
| on the left | a la izquierda |
| on the right | a la derecha |
| on your left / right | a tu izquierda / derecha |

Más lugares que ya conoces: *bank, supermarket, cinema, library, pharmacy, park*.

---

## 5. *On the left / On the right*

Al final de las indicaciones **localizas** el destino:

> The pharmacy is **on the left**.  
> The cinema is **on the right**.  
> It’s on the left, next to the pharmacy.  
> Past the bank **on your right**.

![Esquema on the left on the right A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/a1-unit26-left-right.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/on-the-left.mp3" title="🔊 The pharmacy is on the left"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/on-the-right.mp3" title="🔊 The cinema is on the right"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/library-left-pharmacy.mp3" title="🔊 It's on the left, next to the pharmacy"></audio>

### Con U24

| U24 | U26 |
| :--- | :--- |
| The library is **next to** the pharmacy. | Go straight… The library is **on the left**, next to the pharmacy. |
| The cinema is **opposite** the park. | Past the supermarket… The cinema is **on the right**. |

Primero **mueves** a la persona (*Turn / Go / Past*); luego **anclas** el lugar (*on the left / next to…*).

---

## 6. Preguntar el camino

| Pregunta | Uso |
| :--- | :--- |
| **How do I get to** the library? | ¿Cómo llego a la biblioteca? |
| **Where is** the pharmacy? | ¿Dónde está la farmacia? |
| Excuse me. How do I get to the cinema? | Versión educada |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/how-get-library.mp3" title="🔊 How do I get to the library?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/how-get-cinema.mp3" title="🔊 How do I get to the cinema?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/where-pharmacy.mp3" title="🔊 Where is the pharmacy?"></audio>

### Diálogo modelo (cine)

> **A:** How do I get to the cinema?  
> **B:** Go straight along this street. Turn left at the corner. Past the supermarket and the cinema is on the right.  
> **A:** Thanks!  
> **B:** You’re welcome.

![Diálogo How do I get to the cinema A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/a1-unit26-dialogue.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/thanks-welcome.mp3" title="🔊 Thanks! You're welcome"></audio>

### Texto modelo (estación → biblioteca)

> To get to the library from the station, go straight out of the station. Go straight for about 200 metres. Turn left at the corner. Past the bank on your right. The library is on the left, next to the pharmacy. You can’t miss it.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/full-directions.mp3" title="🔊 Go straight out of the station. Turn left at the corner. Past the bank. The library is on the left"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/cant-miss-it.mp3" title="🔊 You can't miss it"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-26/cross-the-street.mp3" title="🔊 Cross the street and the bank is there"></audio>

---

## 7. Frases de cierre y cortesía

| Frase | Significado |
| :--- | :--- |
| **You can’t miss it.** | No te puedes perder / es fácil de ver. |
| **Thanks!** / **Thank you.** | Gracias. |
| **You’re welcome.** | De nada. |
| **Excuse me.** | Perdona / Disculpa (para preguntar). |

Úsalas al final: dan naturalidad al diálogo de calle.

---

## 8. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *You turn left at the corner* (demasiado “frase completa”) | *Turn left at the corner* | Imperativo sin sujeto |
| *Turn left in the corner* | *Turn left **at** the corner* | *at* + esquina/semáforo |
| *Go to straight* | *Go straight* | Sin *to* |
| *Pass the bank* (calco) | *Past the bank* / *Go past the bank* | Forma del curso |
| *The cinema is in the right* | *The cinema is **on** the right* | *on the left/right* |
| *How I get to the library?* | *How **do** I get to the library?* | Auxiliar *do* |
| *Turn to left* | *Turn left* | Sin *to* |

---

## 9. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Turn left / right** | *tern left* · *right* con /r/ suave o fuerte según acento. |
| **Go straight** | *streit* (el grupo *str-*). |
| **Past the** | *past thə* (the débil). |
| **traffic lights** | acento en *TRA-* · *lights* = /laɪts/. |
| **corner** | *KOR-ner*. |
| **You can’t miss it** | *kant* (UK) / *kænt* (US) · *miss it* enlazado. |

Practica la secuencia: *Go straight → Turn left → Past the… → It’s on the right.*

---

## 9b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Excuse me. How do I get to the park?  
> **B:** Go straight. Turn left at the corner. The park is on the right.  
> **A:** Thanks!  
> **B:** You’re welcome.

> **A:** Where is the pharmacy?  
> **B:** Go straight past the supermarket. The pharmacy is on the left, next to the library. You can’t miss it.

> **A:** How do I get to the library from the station?  
> **B:** Go straight out of the station. Go straight for about 200 metres. Turn left at the corner. Past the bank on your right. The library is on the left.

Cambia solo el destino: fijas el patrón de imperativos.

---

## 9c. Plantillas para copiar

1. Turn left / right at the \_\_\_\_.  
2. Go straight for \_\_\_\_ metres.  
3. Go straight along this street.  
4. Past the \_\_\_\_ and then turn \_\_\_\_.  
5. The \_\_\_\_ is on the left / right.  
6. How do I get to the \_\_\_\_?  
7. It’s on the left, next to the \_\_\_\_.  
8. You can’t miss it.

### Más frases para memorizar

> Turn left at the corner.  
> Turn right at the traffic lights.  
> Go straight for 100 metres.  
> Go straight along this street.  
> Go straight past the bank.  
> Past the bank and then turn right.  
> Past the supermarket and the cinema is on the right.  
> The pharmacy is on the left.  
> The cinema is on the right.  
> It’s on the left, next to the pharmacy.  
> How do I get to the library?  
> How do I get to the cinema?  
> Cross the street and the bank is there.  
> You can’t miss it.  
> Thanks! You’re welcome.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego da **4 pasos** para ir de tu casa a un lugar cercano.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 2 × *Turn left/right at…*.  
2. Di 2 × *Go straight…*.  
3. Di 1 × *Past the…* + 1 × *on the left/right*.  
4. Pregunta y responde: *How do I get to…?*

Si lo haces con un mapa dibujado, el orden de los pasos se vuelve automático.

### Tour guiado (modelo estación → biblioteca)

> Go straight out of the station. Go straight for about 200 metres. Turn left at the corner. Past the bank on your right. The library is on the left, next to the pharmacy. You can’t miss it.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego cambia el destino a *cinema* o *pharmacy* sin mirar el texto.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> Excuse me. How do I get to the supermarket?  
> Go straight along this street.  
> Turn right at the traffic lights.  
> Past the bank and the supermarket is on the left.  
> Where is the cinema?  
> Go straight. Turn left at the corner. Past the supermarket. The cinema is on the right.  
> Cross the street.  
> Thanks! You’re welcome.

Personaliza con **tu** calle. Cuanto más concreto el punto de referencia, más claras las indicaciones.

### Checklist mental

- Imperativo = forma base, sin *you*  
- Girar → *Turn left / right* + *at the…*  
- Recto → *Go straight* (+ *for / along / past*)  
- Pasar → *Past the…*  
- Destino → *on the left / on the right*  
- Pregunta → *How do I get to…?*  
- Cierre → *You can’t miss it* · *Thanks / You’re welcome*

### Mapa rápido U24 → U26

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U24 | Dónde está (*next to, opposite…*) |
| U25 | Describir el barrio (*a/the, some/any*) |
| **U26** | Cómo llegar (imperativos) |
| U27 | Pets & Animals |

### Secuencia típica de 4 pasos

1. **Sal / sigue:** Go straight out of the station / along this street.  
2. **Gira:** Turn left at the corner.  
3. **Pasa:** Past the bank on your right.  
4. **Localiza:** The library is on the left. You can’t miss it.

Si memorizas solo esta plantilla, ya puedes dar indicaciones A1 en la calle.

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige el imperativo

1. \_\_\_\_ left at the corner. (gira)  
2. \_\_\_\_ straight for 100 metres. (sigue)  
3. \_\_\_\_ the bank and then turn right. (pasa)  
4. \_\_\_\_ right at the traffic lights. (gira)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Turn**  
2. **Go**  
3. **Past**  
4. **Turn**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa

1. Turn left \_\_\_\_ the corner.  
2. Go straight \_\_\_\_ 200 metres.  
3. The cinema is \_\_\_\_ the right.  
4. Past the bank \_\_\_\_ your right.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **at**  
2. **for**  
3. **on**  
4. **on**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Gira a la izquierda en la esquina.  
2. Sigue recto 100 metros.  
3. Pasa el banco y entonces gira a la derecha.  
4. El cine está a la derecha.  
5. ¿Cómo llego a la biblioteca?  
6. No te puedes perder.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Turn left at the corner.  
2. Go straight for 100 metres.  
3. Past the bank and then turn right.  
4. The cinema is on the right.  
5. How do I get to the library?  
6. You can’t miss it.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige

1. *You turn left at the corner.* (versión de indicación de calle)  
2. *Turn left in the corner.*  
3. *Go to straight.*  
4. *The pharmacy is in the left.*  
5. *How I get to the cinema?*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Turn** left at the corner.  
2. Turn left **at** the corner.  
3. **Go straight.**  
4. The pharmacy is **on** the left.  
5. How **do** I get to the cinema?
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Ordena los pasos (estación → biblioteca)

a) Past the bank on your right.  
b) Go straight out of the station.  
c) The library is on the left, next to the pharmacy.  
d) Turn left at the corner.  
e) Go straight for about 200 metres.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**b → e → d → a → c**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Empareja

1. Turn left  
2. Go straight  
3. Past the bank  
4. on the right  
5. You can’t miss it  

a) sigue recto  
b) a la derecha  
c) gira a la izquierda  
d) es fácil de encontrar  
e) pasa el banco

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **a** · 3 → **e** · 4 → **b** · 5 → **d**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe indicaciones

Escribe 5–7 frases para ir de un punto A a un punto B (reales o inventados). Usa al menos:

- *Go straight*  
- *Turn left* o *Turn right*  
- *Past the…*  
- *on the left* o *on the right*

**Modelo:**

> Go straight along this street. Turn left at the corner. Past the supermarket and the cinema is on the right. You can’t miss it.

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. Turn right \_\_\_\_ the traffic lights. (at / on / in)  
2. Go straight \_\_\_\_ this street. (along / at / to)  
3. The library is \_\_\_\_ the left. (on / in / at)  
4. How \_\_\_\_ I get to the park? (do / does / am)  
5. Past \_\_\_\_ supermarket. (the / a / —)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **at**  
2. **along**  
3. **on**  
4. **do**  
5. **the**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Repite 8 imperativos en voz alta.  
2. **3 min** — Diálogo *How do I get to…?* (pregunta + 4 pasos).  
3. **4 min** — Dibuja un mapa y escribe indicaciones.  
4. **5 min** — Grábate y comprueba *at / on / for / along*.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *Turn left / right* + *at the…*  
- [ ] Uso *Go straight* (+ *for / along / past*)  
- [ ] Uso *Past the…*  
- [ ] Localizo con *on the left / right*  
- [ ] Pregunto *How do I get to…?*  
- [ ] Cierro con *You can’t miss it* / *Thanks*

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Mapa en papel:** 6 edificios; escribe el camino de A a B.  
2. **Pareja:** uno pregunta, el otro da 4 pasos.  
3. **Combina** U25: *There is a cinema on the right. Go straight past the supermarket.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 27](/curso-a1/unit-27): *Pets & Animals*.  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 26](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-26-direcciones-imperativos-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 26 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-26).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Imperativo | Forma base, sin sujeto |
| Girar | Turn left / right **at** the… |
| Recto | Go straight (**for / along / past**) |
| Pasar | Past the + lugar |
| Destino | on the left / on the right |
| Pregunta | How do I get to…? |
| Cierre | You can’t miss it · Thanks |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

En la **Unidad 27** aprenderás vocabulario de **mascotas y animales**.

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 26 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-26-direcciones-imperativos-ejercicios-soluciones)

Guía dedicada:

- [Unidad 27 — Pets & Animals](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-27-mascotas-animales)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Preposiciones de movimiento](/blog/gramatica/preposiciones-movimiento-ingles)
- [Inglés para viajar](/blog/viajes/ingles-para-viajar)
- [Inglés en trenes y metro](/blog/viajes/ingles-trenes-metro-transporte)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- British Council — Giving directions: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/skills/speaking/a1-speaking/giving-directions
- British Council — Imperatives: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar/imperatives

title: Animales en Inglés A1: Mascotas, Granja y Salvajes
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 27 del curso A1: pets, farm y wild animals, más adjetivos dangerous, friendly y cute, con audios, esquemas y ejercicios.
description: Aprende animales en inglés A1: pets, farm animals y wild animals, con vocabulario, adjetivos para describirlos y ejercicios prácticos.
alt: Esquema pets farm wild animals en inglés nivel A1

faqs.question: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre pet, farm y wild animals?
faqs.answer: Pets viven con personas (dog, cat, fish). Farm animals viven en la granja (cow, horse, chicken). Wild animals viven en la naturaleza (lion, tiger, bear).

faqs.question: ¿Qué adjetivos practico en la Unidad 27?
faqs.answer: Dangerous (peligroso), friendly (amigable) y cute (mono/adorable), más big/small. Ejemplo: My dog is very friendly. A lion is dangerous. The kitten is so cute.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde va el adjetivo en inglés A1?
faqs.answer: Antes del sustantivo (a friendly dog) o después de be (My dog is friendly). Con can: A snake can be dangerous.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo hablo de mis mascotas?
faqs.answer: I have two pets. My dog is called Max. He is very friendly. My cat is small and very cute. She likes sleeping on the sofa.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 27 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 27 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 26](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-26-direcciones-imperativos) diste direcciones. En la **Unidad 27 del curso A1** (*Pets & Animals*) cambias de tema: **mascotas y animales**, clasificados en ***pets / farm / wild***, y adjetivos como ***dangerous, friendly, cute***.

Repasas descripciones de la [Unidad 7](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-7-colores-descripciones-fisicas) y *like + -ing* de la [Unidad 18](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-18-gustos-like-ing-because). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 27 — Pets & Animals](/curso-a1/unit-27)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 7 — Descripciones](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-7-colores-descripciones-fisicas) · [Unidad 18 — Gustos](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-18-gustos-like-ing-because)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 27 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Clasificar animales: ***pet / farm / wild***.
- Nombrar mascotas, animales de granja y salvajes.
- Describir con ***dangerous, friendly, cute*** (+ *big / small*).
- Hablar de tus mascotas: *I have… My dog is called…*.
- Contrastar: *We don’t have wild animals at home*.

---

## 1. Tres grupos: *pets, farm, wild*

| Grupo | Significado | Ejemplos |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **pet** | mascota (vive con personas) | dog, cat, fish, rabbit, hamster |
| **farm animal** | animal de granja | cow, horse, sheep, pig, chicken, duck |
| **wild animal** | animal salvaje | lion, tiger, bear, wolf, elephant, snake |

![Esquema pets farm wild animals A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/a1-unit27-pets-farm-wild.png)

> A cat is a **pet** animal.  
> A cow lives on a **farm**.  
> A **wild** animal lives in the forest.  
> Pigs and chickens are **farm** animals.  
> Lions are **wild** and dangerous.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/cat-is-a-pet.mp3" title="🔊 A cat is a pet animal"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/cow-on-farm.mp3" title="🔊 A cow lives on a farm"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/wild-in-forest.mp3" title="🔊 A wild animal lives in the forest"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/pigs-chickens-farm.mp3" title="🔊 Pigs and chickens are farm animals"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/lions-wild-dangerous.mp3" title="🔊 Lions are wild and dangerous"></audio>

### Tip

Algunos animales pueden ser **pet o wild** según el contexto (p. ej. *rabbit*). En A1, clasifica por el uso más habitual del ejercicio.

---

## 2. Vocabulario esencial

### Pets

| Inglés | Español |
| :--- | :--- |
| dog | perro |
| cat | gato |
| fish | pez |
| rabbit | conejo |
| hamster | hámster |
| kitten | gatito |
| pet | mascota |

### Farm

| Inglés | Español |
| :--- | :--- |
| farm | granja |
| cow | vaca |
| horse | caballo |
| sheep | oveja |
| pig | cerdo |
| chicken | gallina |
| duck | pato |

### Wild

| Inglés | Español |
| :--- | :--- |
| lion | león |
| tiger | tigre |
| bear | oso |
| wolf | lobo |
| elephant | elefante |
| snake | serpiente |
| forest / jungle | bosque / selva |
| zoo | zoo |

---

## 3. Adjetivos: *dangerous, friendly, cute*

| Adjetivo | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **dangerous** | peligroso | A lion is dangerous. |
| **friendly** | amigable / simpático | My dog is very friendly. |
| **cute** | mono / adorable | The kitten is so cute. |
| **big / small** | grande / pequeño | The elephant is very big. |

![Esquema adjetivos animals A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/a1-unit27-adjectives.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/lion-dangerous.mp3" title="🔊 A lion is dangerous"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/dog-friendly.mp3" title="🔊 My dog is very friendly"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/kitten-cute.mp3" title="🔊 The kitten is so cute"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/tigers-dangerous.mp3" title="🔊 Tigers are dangerous"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/rabbits-cute.mp3" title="🔊 Rabbits are cute"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/elephant-big.mp3" title="🔊 The elephant is very big"></audio>

### Dos posiciones del adjetivo

```
be + adjective → My dog is friendly.
adjective + noun → a friendly dog
```

> My hamster is **cute** and **friendly**.  
> My pet is a **friendly** dog.  
> A snake can be **dangerous**.  
> The horse is **big** but **friendly**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/hamster-cute-friendly.mp3" title="🔊 My hamster is cute and friendly"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/my-pet-dog.mp3" title="🔊 My pet is a friendly dog"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/snake-dangerous.mp3" title="🔊 A snake can be dangerous"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/horse-big-friendly.mp3" title="🔊 The horse is big but friendly"></audio>

### Tip para hispanohablantes

En inglés el adjetivo **no cambia** de género ni número: *a cute cat / cute cats* (no *cutes*).

---

## 4. Hablar de tus mascotas

| Función | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Tener | I have two pets. |
| Nombre | My dog is called Max. |
| Descripción | He is very friendly. |
| Gustos | He loves to play. / She likes sleeping on the sofa. |
| Contraste | Wild animals are dangerous — we don’t have them at home. |

![Ilustración My Pets A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/a1-unit27-my-pets.png)

### Texto modelo del curso

> I have two pets. My dog is called Max. He is very friendly and he loves to play. My cat is small and very cute. She likes sleeping on the sofa. At my grandma’s farm there are cows, chickens and a horse. The horse is big but friendly. Wild animals like lions and tigers are dangerous — we don’t have them at home.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/two-pets.mp3" title="🔊 I have two pets. My dog is called Max"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/dog-loves-play.mp3" title="🔊 He is very friendly and he loves to play"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/cat-cute-sofa.mp3" title="🔊 My cat is small and very cute. She likes sleeping on the sofa"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/farm-animals.mp3" title="🔊 At my grandma's farm there are cows, chickens and a horse"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-27/wild-not-home.mp3" title="🔊 Wild animals like lions and tigers are dangerous. We don't have them at home"></audio>

### Diálogo modelo

> **Ana:** Do you have any pets?  
> **Luis:** Yes. I have two pets: a dog and a cat.  
> **Ana:** What’s your dog like?  
> **Luis:** He’s very friendly. He loves to play.  
> **Ana:** And your cat?  
> **Luis:** She’s small and cute. She likes sleeping on the sofa.  
> **Ana:** Cool! Do you like wild animals?  
> **Luis:** I like elephants at the zoo, but lions are dangerous. We don’t have them at home!

---

## 5. *He / she* con animales

En inglés es habitual usar ***he/she*** con mascotas (sobre todo si conoces el sexo o tienes vínculo emocional):

> My dog is called Max. **He** is friendly.  
> My cat is cute. **She** likes sleeping.

Con animales genéricos o salvajes suele usarse ***it***:

> A lion is dangerous. **It** lives in the wild.

En A1 ambas formas aparecen; prioriza *he/she* con *my dog / my cat*.

---

## 6. Combinar con gramática previa

| Unidad | Cómo se conecta |
| :--- | :--- |
| U7 | Adjetivos de descripción (*big, small…*) |
| U17–18 | *like / love* + *-ing* / *to* |
| U23 | *There are cows on the farm* |
| U25 | *I have some pets* / *Do you have any pets?* |

> There are cows, chickens and a horse on the farm.  
> Do you have any pets? — Yes, I have a dog.  
> I like sleeping cats. / He loves to play.

---

## 7. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *My dog is very friend* | *My dog is very **friendly*** | Adjetivo = *friendly* |
| *a dog friendly* | *a **friendly** dog* | Adj. antes del nombre |
| *The lion are dangerous* | *The lion **is** / Lions **are*** | Concordancia |
| *Sheeps* | *sheep* (plural igual) | Plural irregular |
| *a cute* (sin nombre) | *a cute cat / It is cute* | Falta sustantivo o *be* |
| *dangerouss animals* | *dangerous animals* | Sin -s en el adj. |
| *I have a pet dog friendly* | *I have a **friendly** pet dog* / *My pet is a friendly dog* | Orden |

---

## 8. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **dangerous** | *DEIN-jer-əs* (3 sílabas). |
| **friendly** | *FREND-li*. |
| **cute** | *kiuut* /kjuːt/. |
| **lion / tiger** | *LAI-ən* · *TAI-gə*. |
| **elephant** | *E-lə-fənt*. |
| **chicken** | *CHI-kən*. |
| **sheep** | igual en singular y plural. |

Practica el contraste: *friendly dog* vs *dangerous lion* — cambia solo el adjetivo y el animal.

---

## 8b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Do you have a pet?  
> **B:** Yes. I have a dog. He’s very friendly.  
> **A:** Is he cute?  
> **B:** Yes! And he loves to play.

> **A:** What’s on your grandma’s farm?  
> **B:** There are cows, chickens and a horse.  
> **A:** Is the horse friendly?  
> **B:** Yes. It’s big but friendly.

> **A:** Are lions pets?  
> **B:** No. Lions are wild and dangerous. We don’t have them at home.

Cambia solo el animal y el adjetivo: fijas la estructura.

---

## 8c. Plantillas para copiar

1. I have a / two \_\_\_\_.  
2. My \_\_\_\_ is called \_\_\_\_.  
3. He / She is very \_\_\_\_.  
4. A \_\_\_\_ is a pet / farm / wild animal.  
5. \_\_\_\_ are cute / friendly / dangerous.  
6. A snake can be \_\_\_\_.  
7. At the farm there are \_\_\_\_.  
8. Wild animals like \_\_\_\_ are dangerous.

### Más frases para memorizar

> A lion is dangerous.  
> My dog is very friendly.  
> The kitten is so cute.  
> A cat is a pet animal.  
> A cow lives on a farm.  
> A wild animal lives in the forest.  
> Tigers are dangerous.  
> Rabbits are cute.  
> Pigs and chickens are farm animals.  
> The elephant is very big.  
> My hamster is cute and friendly.  
> A snake can be dangerous.  
> My pet is a friendly dog.  
> Lions are wild and dangerous.  
> I have two pets. My dog is called Max.  
> My cat is small and very cute.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego describe **tus** mascotas (o inventadas) con 6 frases.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 3 animales *pet*, 3 *farm*, 3 *wild*.  
2. Di 3 frases con *friendly / cute / dangerous*.  
3. Di 2 frases *I have…* + descripción.  
4. Di 1 contraste: *Wild animals… we don’t have them at home.*

Si usas fotos reales de animales, el vocabulario se pega más rápido.

### Tour guiado (modelo)

> I have two pets. My dog is called Max. He is very friendly and he loves to play. My cat is small and very cute. She likes sleeping on the sofa. At my grandma’s farm there are cows, chickens and a horse. The horse is big but friendly. Wild animals like lions and tigers are dangerous — we don’t have them at home.

Grábate leyéndolo y luego improvísalo con **tus** animales.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> Do you have any pets?  
> Yes, I have a rabbit. It’s cute and friendly.  
> What’s your favourite wild animal?  
> I like elephants. They’re very big.  
> Are snakes dangerous?  
> Yes. A snake can be dangerous.  
> Are chickens pets?  
> No. Chickens are farm animals.  
> The zoo has wild animals.

Personaliza con animales que te gusten. Cuanto más personal, mejor recuerdas *pet / farm / wild*.

### Checklist mental

- Mascota → *pet*  
- Granja → *farm animal*  
- Naturaleza / zoo → *wild*  
- Peligroso → *dangerous*  
- Amigable → *friendly*  
- Mono → *cute*  
- Adj. + noun **o** *be* + adj.  
- Mascotas: a menudo *he/she*

### Mapa rápido del módulo

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U7 | Adjetivos físicos |
| U18 | *like + -ing* |
| U25–26 | Barrio y direcciones |
| **U27** | Pets & animals + adjetivos |
| U28 | Body parts (*have/has got*) |

---

## 9. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — *pet / farm / wild*

1. dog → \_\_\_\_  
2. cow → \_\_\_\_  
3. lion → \_\_\_\_  
4. chicken → \_\_\_\_  
5. hamster → \_\_\_\_  
6. tiger → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **pet**  
2. **farm**  
3. **wild**  
4. **farm**  
5. **pet**  
6. **wild**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Elige el adjetivo

1. A lion is \_\_\_\_. (dangerous / cute)  
2. My dog is very \_\_\_\_. (friendly / wild)  
3. The kitten is so \_\_\_\_. (cute / dangerous)  
4. The elephant is very \_\_\_\_. (big / small)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **dangerous**  
2. **friendly**  
3. **cute**  
4. **big**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Un gato es una mascota.  
2. Una vaca vive en una granja.  
3. Mi perro es muy amigable.  
4. El gatito es tan mono.  
5. Los leones son salvajes y peligrosos.  
6. Tengo dos mascotas.  
7. Una serpiente puede ser peligrosa.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. A cat is a pet. / A cat is a pet animal.  
2. A cow lives on a farm.  
3. My dog is very friendly.  
4. The kitten is so cute.  
5. Lions are wild and dangerous.  
6. I have two pets.  
7. A snake can be dangerous.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige

1. *My dog is very friend.*  
2. *a dog friendly*  
3. *The lion are dangerous.*  
4. *I have two pet.*  
5. *Sheeps are farm animals.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. My dog is very **friendly**.  
2. a **friendly** dog  
3. The lion **is** dangerous. / Lions **are** dangerous.  
4. I have two **pets**.  
5. **Sheep** are farm animals.
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Empareja

1. dangerous  
2. friendly  
3. cute  
4. farm  
5. wild  

a) mono / adorable  
b) granja  
c) peligroso  
d) salvaje  
e) amigable

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **e** · 3 → **a** · 4 → **b** · 5 → **d**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el texto

I have two \_\_\_\_. My dog is called Max. He is very \_\_\_\_. My cat is small and very \_\_\_\_. At the farm there are cows and a horse. Lions are \_\_\_\_ animals — we don’t have them at home.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**pets** · **friendly** · **cute** · **wild** (o **dangerous**)
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe sobre animales

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- al menos 1 *pet*, 1 *farm*, 1 *wild*  
- los adjetivos *friendly*, *cute* y *dangerous*  
- *I have…* o *There is/are…*

**Modelo:**

> I have two pets. My dog is called Max. He is very friendly and he loves to play. My cat is small and very cute. At my grandma’s farm there are cows, chickens and a horse. The horse is big but friendly. Lions are wild and dangerous. We don’t have them at home.

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. A cat is a \_\_\_\_ animal. (pet / wild / farm)  
2. Chickens are \_\_\_\_ animals. (farm / wild / pet)  
3. Tigers are \_\_\_\_. (dangerous / cute)  
4. My pet is a \_\_\_\_ dog. (friendly / friend)  
5. A snake \_\_\_\_ be dangerous. (can / is can)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **pet**  
2. **farm**  
3. **dangerous**  
4. **friendly**  
5. **can**
</details>

---

## 10. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Lista 5 pets + 5 farm + 5 wild en voz alta.  
2. **3 min** — 6 frases con *dangerous / friendly / cute*.  
3. **4 min** — Escribe tu párrafo *I have…*.  
4. **5 min** — Grábate y comprueba *he/she* y plurales (*sheep*).

### Checklist

- [ ] Clasifico *pet / farm / wild*  
- [ ] Uso *dangerous, friendly, cute*  
- [ ] Pongo el adjetivo en el lugar correcto  
- [ ] Hablo de mascotas con *I have / is called*  
- [ ] Sé que *sheep* no añade *-s*

---

## 11. Consejos para practicar

1. **Flashcards** de 15 animales → di el grupo (*pet/farm/wild*).  
2. **Foto** de tu mascota: 5 frases descriptivas.  
3. **Combina** U18: *My dog loves playing. My cat likes sleeping.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 28](/curso-a1/unit-28): *Body Parts* (*have/has got*).  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 27](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-27-mascotas-animales-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 27 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-27).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| **pet** | vive con personas |
| **farm** | cow, horse, chicken… |
| **wild** | lion, tiger, bear… |
| **dangerous** | peligroso |
| **friendly** | amigable |
| **cute** | mono / adorable |
| **Orden** | *a friendly dog* / *is friendly* |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

En la **Unidad 28** aprenderás **partes del cuerpo** con ***have / has got***.

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 27 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-27-mascotas-animales-ejercicios-soluciones)

Guía dedicada:

- [Unidad 28 — Body Parts (have/has got)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-28-partes-cuerpo-have-got)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)
- [Gramática inglesa: guía por niveles](/blog/gramatica/gramatica-inglesa-guia)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- British Council — Animals vocabulary: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/vocabulary/a1-a2-vocabulary
- British Council — Adjectives: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar/adjectives

title: Partes del Cuerpo A1: Have Got, This/These y Vocabulario
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 28 del curso A1: partes del cuerpo con have got / has got, this/these y vocabulario head, arms, legs, hands, feet, face.
description: Aprende partes del cuerpo en inglés A1 con have got / has got, this/these y vocabulario head, arms, legs, hands, feet y face, con ejemplos y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema body parts have got this these en inglés nivel A1

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso have got y cuándo has got?
faqs.answer: Have got con I, you, we, they (I have got two arms). Has got con he, she, it (She has got long legs). También verás have/has sin got en A1; el curso practica la forma con got.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre this y these?
faqs.answer: This = singular (This is my hand). These = plural (These are my feet). This is / These are.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se dice pies en inglés?
faqs.answer: Singular foot, plural feet (no foots). Ejemplo: I have got two feet. These are my feet.

faqs.question: ¿Qué partes del cuerpo practico en la Unidad 28?
faqs.answer: Head, face, eyes, nose, mouth, arms, hands, fingers, legs y feet. Con adjetivos como long, short, big, blue y tall.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 28 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 28 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 27](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-27-mascotas-animales) hablaste de animales. En la **Unidad 28 del curso A1** (*Body Parts*) aprendes a nombrar **partes del cuerpo** y a usar ***have got / has got*** con ***this / these***.

Conecta con descripciones de la [Unidad 7](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-7-colores-descripciones-fisicas) y demostrativos de la [Unidad 4](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-4-articulos-plurales-demostrativos). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 28 — Body Parts](/curso-a1/unit-28)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 7 — Descripciones](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-7-colores-descripciones-fisicas) · [Unidad 4 — This/that](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-4-articulos-plurales-demostrativos)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 28 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***have got*** y ***has got*** para el cuerpo.
- Distinguir ***this*** (singular) y ***these*** (plural).
- Nombrar: ***head, face, arms, legs, hands, feet*** (+ eyes, nose, mouth, fingers).
- Describir: *long legs, blue eyes, big feet, tall…*.
- Recordar el plural irregular ***foot → feet***.

---

## 1. Vocabulario: partes del cuerpo

| Singular | Plural | Español |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **head** | heads | cabeza |
| **face** | faces | cara |
| **eye** | eyes | ojo / ojos |
| **nose** | noses | nariz |
| **mouth** | mouths | boca |
| **arm** | arms | brazo / brazos |
| **hand** | hands | mano / manos |
| **finger** | fingers | dedo / dedos |
| **leg** | legs | pierna / piernas |
| **foot** | **feet** | pie / pies |

![Esquema body parts etiquetado A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/a1-unit28-body-parts.png)

### Tip clave

***Foot → feet*** (no *foots*). Es uno de los plurales irregulares más importantes de A1.

> I have got two **feet**.  
> These are my **feet**.  
> My **feet** are big.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/my-feet-are-big.mp3" title="🔊 My feet are big"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/these-are-my-feet.mp3" title="🔊 These are my feet"></audio>

---

## 2. *Have got / Has got*

| Sujeto | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they | **have got** | I have got two arms. |
| he / she / it | **has got** | She has got long legs. |

```
I/you/we/they + have got + …
he/she/it + has got + …
```

![Esquema have got has got A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/a1-unit28-have-has-got.png)

> I **have got** two arms.  
> We **have got** two hands.  
> She **has got** long legs.  
> He **has got** blue eyes.  
> I **have got** a head and a face.  
> She **has got** long arms.  
> I **have got** two arms and two legs.  
> She **has got** a beautiful face.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/i-have-got-two-arms.mp3" title="🔊 I have got two arms"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/she-has-got-long-legs.mp3" title="🔊 She has got long legs"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/he-has-got-blue-eyes.mp3" title="🔊 He has got blue eyes"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/we-have-got-two-hands.mp3" title="🔊 We have got two hands"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/head-and-face.mp3" title="🔊 I have got a head and a face"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/she-has-got-long-arms.mp3" title="🔊 She has got long arms"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/two-arms-two-legs.mp3" title="🔊 I have got two arms and two legs"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/beautiful-face.mp3" title="🔊 She has got a beautiful face"></audio>

### *Have got* ≈ *have*

En A1 verás las dos:

| Con *got* | Sin *got* (también correcta) |
| :--- | :--- |
| I have got two arms. | I have two arms. |
| She has got long legs. | She has long legs. |

El curso practica sobre todo ***have got / has got*** (muy frecuente en UK).

### Negativa y pregunta (intro rápida)

| Tipo | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Negativa | I **haven’t got** blue eyes. / She **hasn’t got** long arms. |
| Pregunta | **Have** you **got** long legs? / **Has** she **got** blue eyes? |

En esta unidad el foco principal es la **afirmativa** + vocabulario del cuerpo.

---

## 3. *This / These*

| Forma | Número | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **This** | singular | This is my hand. |
| **These** | plural | These are my feet. |

```
This + is + singular
These + are + plural
```

![Esquema this these body parts A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/a1-unit28-this-these.png)

> **This** is my hand.  
> **This** is my head.  
> **These** are my feet.  
> **These** are my arms.  
> This is my hand and these are my feet.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/this-is-my-hand.mp3" title="🔊 This is my hand"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/this-is-my-head.mp3" title="🔊 This is my head"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/these-are-my-arms.mp3" title="🔊 These are my arms"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-28/this-hand-these-feet.mp3" title="🔊 This is my hand and these are my feet"></audio>

### Tip

Señala una sola parte → *This is…*. Señala dos o más → *These are…*.

---

## 4. La cara: *eyes, nose, mouth*

En la **face** tienes:
