### Combina con *can* (U31)

> I **can** swim. I **go** swimming every Sunday.  
> She **can** play tennis. She **plays** tennis twice a week.

---

## 7. Texto modelo (familia activa)

> My name is Jake. I love sport. I play football every Saturday with my team. On Sundays I go swimming at the pool. My sister does yoga every morning. She doesn’t like football but she likes reading and painting. My mum plays tennis twice a week. We are an active family.

![Active family sports hobbies A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/a1-unit32-active-family.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/jake-football.mp3" title="🔊 I play football every Saturday with my team"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/active-family.mp3" title="🔊 We are an active family"></audio>

### Diálogo modelo

> **A:** What sports do you play?  
> **B:** I play football every Saturday. And you?  
> **A:** I go swimming on Sundays. Does your sister play football?  
> **B:** No, she doesn’t. She does yoga and she likes reading and painting.  
> **A:** Nice! Does your mum play tennis?  
> **B:** Yes, she does — twice a week. We’re an active family.

---

## 8. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *play swimming* | ***go** swimming* | -ing → go |
| *go football* | ***play** football* | pelota → play |
| *do tennis* | ***play** tennis* | pelota → play |
| *play yoga* | ***do** yoga* | yoga → do |
| *She go swimming* | *She **goes** swimming* | 3.ª persona |
| *I play the football* | *I play football* | Sin *the* (A1 general) |
| *I do painting* (A1) | *I **like** painting* | Hobby → like + -ing |

---

## 9. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **play / plays** | *plei* · *pleiz*. |
| **go / goes** | *gou* · *gouz*. |
| **do / does** | *duː* · *daz*. |
| **swimming** | *SWI-ming* (doble m). |
| **football** | UK *FUT-bool*. |
| **yoga** | *IOU-ga*. |

Practica el trío: *play football → go swimming → do yoga*.

---

## 9b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Do you play football?  
> **B:** Yes, I do. Every Saturday.  
> **A:** Do you go swimming?  
> **B:** Yes — on Sundays.

> **A:** Does she do yoga?  
> **B:** Yes, she does. Every morning.  
> **A:** Does she like football?  
> **B:** No. She likes reading and painting.

> **A:** What sports do you play?  
> **B:** Football and tennis. My mum plays tennis twice a week.

Cambia solo el deporte: fijas *play / go / do*.

---

## 9c. Plantillas para copiar

1. I play \_\_\_\_ every \_\_\_\_.  
2. She / He goes \_\_\_\_ing on \_\_\_\_.  
3. We do \_\_\_\_ in the morning.  
4. I like \_\_\_\_ing and \_\_\_\_ing.  
5. What sports do you play?  
6. Do you go swimming? — Yes, I do.  
7. Does she do yoga? — Yes, she does.  
8. We are an active family.

### Más frases para memorizar

> I play football every Saturday.  
> She goes swimming on Mondays.  
> We do yoga in the morning.  
> They play tennis at the club.  
> My sister likes painting and reading.  
> I play football with my friends.  
> She goes swimming every weekend.  
> He likes painting and reading.  
> I play tennis and football.  
> She likes reading and painting.  
> I go running in the park.  
> We do exercise every day.  
> They play basketball at school.  
> I play football every Saturday with my team.  
> On Sundays I go swimming at the pool.  
> My sister does yoga every morning.  
> My mum plays tennis twice a week.  
> We are an active family.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego describe **tu** semana deportiva en 8 frases.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 2 frases *play…*.  
2. Di 2 frases *go …ing*.  
3. Di 2 frases *do…*.  
4. Di 2 hobbies con *like + -ing*.

Si lo unes a días (*on Monday, every Saturday*), practicas U12 + U32 a la vez.

### Combinar *can* (U31) con *play / go / do* (U32)

En la unidad anterior practicaste habilidad (*I can swim*). Aquí hablas de **hábito**: *I go swimming*. Las dos ideas van juntas en la vida real:

| Habilidad (can) | Hábito (play/go/do) |
| :--- | :--- |
| I can swim. | I go swimming on Sundays. |
| She can play tennis. | She plays tennis twice a week. |
| We can do yoga. | We do yoga in the morning. |
| He can run. | He goes running in the park. |

Modelo corto:

> I can swim very well. On Sundays I go swimming at the pool.  
> My mum can play tennis. She plays tennis twice a week.  
> My sister can paint. She likes painting and reading.

Así unes **capacidad** + **rutina** sin mezclar las formas: *can* no lleva *-s*; *plays / goes / does* sí.

### Mini-historia para reescribir

Lee y sustituye los deportes por los tuyos:

> Every Saturday I play football with my friends. On Sunday I go swimming. On Monday I do exercise at home. In the evening I like reading. My brother plays basketball at school. My dad goes cycling at the weekend. We are an active family.

Cambia *football → tennis*, *swimming → running*, *exercise → yoga*, y vuelve a decirlo en voz alta. El verbo (*play / go / do*) debe quedarse bien elegido.

### Tour guiado (modelo)

> My name is Jake. I love sport. I play football every Saturday with my team. On Sundays I go swimming at the pool. My sister does yoga every morning. She doesn’t like football but she likes reading and painting. My mum plays tennis twice a week. We are an active family.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tu** familia.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> What sports do you play?  
> I play football and tennis.  
> Do you go swimming?  
> Yes, I do — every weekend.  
> Does she do yoga?  
> Yes, she does.  
> I go running in the park.  
> We do exercise every day.  
> She likes reading and painting.  
> We’re an active family.

Personaliza con tus hobbies reales. Cuanto más concreto el día, mejor.

### Checklist mental

- Pelota → **play**  
- Actividad *-ing* (swim/run/cycle) → **go**  
- Yoga / exercise → **do**  
- Painting / reading → **like + -ing**  
- he/she → *plays / goes / does*  
- Pregunta → *What sports do you play?*

### Combina U18 + U31 + U32

| Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Gusto | I **like** swimming. |
| Habilidad | I **can** swim. |
| Actividad | I **go** swimming on Sundays. |

Las tres juntas dan un speaking A1 completo sobre ocio.

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U18 | like + -ing |
| U31 | can / can't |
| **U32** | play / go / do |
| U33 | Adverbs of frequency |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — *play / go / do*

1. I \_\_\_\_ football every Saturday.  
2. She \_\_\_\_ swimming on Mondays. (goes)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ yoga in the morning.  
4. They \_\_\_\_ tennis at the club.  
5. We \_\_\_\_ exercise every day.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **play**  
2. **goes**  
3. **do**  
4. **play**  
5. **do**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Elige el verbo

1. swimming → play / **go** / do  
2. football → **play** / go / do  
3. yoga → play / go / **do**  
4. running → play / **go** / do  
5. basketball → **play** / go / do

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **go** · 2. **play** · 3. **do** · 4. **go** · 5. **play**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Juego al fútbol cada sábado.  
2. Ella va a nadar los lunes.  
3. Hacemos yoga por la mañana.  
4. Le gusta leer y pintar.  
5. ¿Qué deportes practicas?  
6. Mi madre juega al tenis dos veces a la semana.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I play football every Saturday.  
2. She goes swimming on Mondays.  
3. We do yoga in the morning.  
4. She likes reading and painting.  
5. What sports do you play?  
6. My mum plays tennis twice a week.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige

1. *I play swimming.*  
2. *She go swimming every week.*  
3. *We play yoga.*  
4. *I go football.*  
5. *He do exercise.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **go** swimming.  
2. She **goes** swimming every week.  
3. We **do** yoga.  
4. I **play** football.  
5. He **does** exercise.
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Empareja

1. play  
2. go  
3. do  
4. like  

a) yoga, exercise  
b) football, tennis  
c) painting, reading  
d) swimming, running

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **d** · 3 → **a** · 4 → **c**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el texto

My name is Jake. I \_\_\_\_ football every Saturday. On Sundays I \_\_\_\_ swimming at the pool. My sister \_\_\_\_ yoga every morning. She likes \_\_\_\_ and painting. My mum \_\_\_\_ tennis twice a week. We are an \_\_\_\_ family.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**play** · **go** · **does** · **reading** · **plays** · **active**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe tu semana

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- 2 × *play*  
- 2 × *go …ing*  
- 1 × *do*  
- 2 hobbies con *like*  
- al menos 2 días o frecuencias (*every Saturday, twice a week*)

**Modelo:** el texto de Jake (sección 7).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. She \_\_\_\_ swimming every weekend. (go / goes / play)  
2. I \_\_\_\_ football with my friends. (play / go / do)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ yoga in the morning. (do / play / go)  
4. He likes \_\_\_\_. (painting / paint / paints)  
5. What sports \_\_\_\_ you play? (do / does / are)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **goes**  
2. **play**  
3. **do**  
4. **painting**  
5. **do**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Tabla mental: 5 *play*, 5 *go*, 3 *do*.  
2. **3 min** — Preguntas *Do you play/go/do…?*  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el texto de Jake.  
4. **5 min** — Grábate y comprueba 3.ª persona (*plays/goes/does*).

### Checklist

- [ ] Sé elegir *play / go / do*  
- [ ] Uso *goes / plays / does* con he/she  
- [ ] Hablo de painting/reading con *like*  
- [ ] Pregunto *What sports do you play?*  
- [ ] Combino con días y frecuencia

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Calendario semanal:** escribe un deporte/hobby por día.  
2. **Pareja:** entrevista con 6 preguntas *Do you…?*  
3. **Combina** U31: *I can swim → I go swimming.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 33](/curso-a1/unit-33): *Adverbs of Frequency*.  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 32 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-32).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Verbo | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **play** | pelota | play football |
| **go** | -ing | go swimming |
| **do** | yoga / exercise | do yoga |
| **like** | hobbies | like reading |
| **Tip** | he/she | plays / goes / does |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Continúa con la [**Unidad 33 — Adverbios de frecuencia**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-33-adverbios-frecuencia): *always, usually, often, sometimes, never*.

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 32 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do-ejercicios-soluciones)

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe ocho frases reales sobre tu semana: dos con *play*, dos con *go …ing*, dos con *do*, y dos hobbies con *like + -ing*. Léelas en voz alta y comprueba la *-s* de la tercera persona.

Guías relacionadas:

- [Inglés para deportes](/blog/metodos/ingles-para-deportes)
- [Inglés en playas y deportes acuáticos](/blog/viajes/ingles-playas-deportes-acuaticos)
- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- British Council — Play, go, do: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar/play-go-do
- British Council — Sports vocabulary: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/vocabulary/a1-a2-vocabulary

title: Adverbios de Frecuencia A1: Always, Usually y Never
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 33 del curso A1: always, usually, often, sometimes, never y su posición, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende always, usually, often, sometimes y never en inglés A1, su posición con Present Simple y be, con audios, esquemas y ejercicios prácticos.

faqs.question: ¿Cuáles son los adverbios de frecuencia en A1?
faqs.answer: Los cinco básicos son always (siempre), usually (normalmente), often (a menudo), sometimes (a veces) y never (nunca).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde va el adverbio con Present Simple?
faqs.answer: Antes del verbo principal: I always get up at 7. She often goes running.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde va el adverbio con am/is/are?
faqs.answer: Después de be: She is never late. They are always busy.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 33?
faqs.answer: Always, usually, often, sometimes, never, get up, have breakfast, go running, meet friends, eat late, relax, read books, how often.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 33 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 33 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do) hablaste de deportes y hobbies (*I play football, I go swimming*). En la **Unidad 33 del curso A1** (*Adverbs of Frequency*) aprendes a decir **con qué frecuencia** haces esas cosas: ***always, usually, often, sometimes, never***.

Encaja con la [rutina diaria](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-13-rutina-diaria) y el [Present Simple](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-5-present-simple-rutinas). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 33 — Adverbs of Frequency](/curso-a1/unit-33)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 32 — Sports & Hobbies](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do) · [Unidad 13 — Rutina diaria](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-13-rutina-diaria)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 33 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***always, usually, often, sometimes, never***.
- Colocar el adverbio **antes del verbo** en Present Simple.
- Colocar el adverbio **después de** *am / is / are*.
- Hablar de hábitos: *get up, have breakfast, go running…*.
- Preguntar frecuencia: ***How often…?*** (introducción A1).

---

## 1. La escala de frecuencia

De más a menos frecuente:

| Adverbio | Significado | % aproximado |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **always** | siempre | 100% |
| **usually** | normalmente / casi siempre | ~80–90% |
| **often** | a menudo / muchas veces | ~60–70% |
| **sometimes** | a veces | ~30–40% |
| **never** | nunca | 0% |

![Escala adverbios de frecuencia A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/a1-unit33-frequency-scale.png)

```
always > usually > often > sometimes > never
```

### Tip

No memorices solo la traducción: asocia cada adverbio a **tu** vida (*I always… / I never…*).

---

## 2. Posición con Present Simple (verbo normal)

Regla A1: **sujeto + adverbio + verbo + …**

> I **always** get up at 7.  
> I **usually** have breakfast with my family.  
> I **often** go running before work.  
> I **sometimes** meet friends for lunch.  
> I **never** eat late at night.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/always-get-up.mp3" title="🔊 I always get up at 7 in the morning"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/usually-breakfast.mp3" title="🔊 I usually have breakfast with my family"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/often-go-running.mp3" title="🔊 I often go running before work"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/sometimes-meet-friends.mp3" title="🔊 I sometimes meet friends for lunch"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/never-eat-late.mp3" title="🔊 I never eat late at night"></audio>

### Más ejemplos

> I **always** have breakfast at 8.  
> I **usually** get up at 7.  
> I **often** watch TV in the evening.  
> We **sometimes** go to the cinema.  
> She **never** eats meat.  
> I **usually** drink coffee in the morning.  
> She **never** forgets her keys.  
> I **often** go to the gym.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/i-always-have-breakfast.mp3" title="🔊 I always have breakfast at 8"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/i-usually-get-up.mp3" title="🔊 I usually get up at 7"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/i-often-watch-tv.mp3" title="🔊 I often watch TV in the evening"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/we-sometimes-cinema.mp3" title="🔊 We sometimes go to the cinema"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/she-never-eats-meat.mp3" title="🔊 She never eats meat"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/we-usually-drink-coffee.mp3" title="🔊 I usually drink coffee in the morning"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/never-forget-keys.mp3" title="🔊 She never forgets her keys"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/i-often-go-gym.mp3" title="🔊 I often go to the gym"></audio>

### Cuidado con la 3.ª persona

El adverbio **no** lleva *-s*. El verbo sí:

| Incorrecto | Correcto |
| :--- | :--- |
| She always **get** up | She always **gets** up |
| He never **eat** meat | He never **eats** meat |
| She often **go** running | She often **goes** running |

---

## 3. Posición con *be* (*am / is / are*)

Con *be*, el adverbio va **después**: **sujeto + am/is/are + adverbio + …**

> She **is never** late.  
> He **is never** late.  
> They **are always** busy.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/she-is-never-late.mp3" title="🔊 She is never late"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/he-is-never-late.mp3" title="🔊 He is never late"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/they-are-always-busy.mp3" title="🔊 They are always busy"></audio>

![Posición del adverbio A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/a1-unit33-adverb-position.png)

```
I always get up.     → adverbio ANTES del verbo
She is never late.   → adverbio DESPUÉS de be
```

### Contraste rápido

| Tipo | Orden | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Verbo normal | subject + **adv** + verb | I **often** go running |
| *be* | subject + **be** + adv | She **is** never late |

No digas *She never is late* ni *I get always up* en A1 estándar.

---

## 4. Vocabulario útil de hábitos

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| get up | levantarse | I always get up at 7. |
| have breakfast | desayunar | I usually have breakfast. |
| go running | ir a correr | I often go running. |
| meet friends | quedar con amigos | I sometimes meet friends. |
| eat late | cenar / comer tarde | I never eat late at night. |
| relax | relajarse | I always relax at weekends. |
| read books | leer libros | I always read books. |
| watch TV | ver la tele | I often watch TV. |
| go to the cinema | ir al cine | We sometimes go to the cinema. |
| go to the gym | ir al gimnasio | I often go to the gym. |

Combina con U32: *I often **play** football. / I usually **go** swimming. / I always **do** yoga.*

---

## 5. Preguntar *How often…?*

Pregunta A1 muy útil:

> **How often** do you go running?  
> I **often** go running. / Three times a week.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/how-often-do-you.mp3" title="🔊 How often do you go running?"></audio>

### Respuestas posibles

| Pregunta | Respuesta con adverbio | Respuesta con tiempo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| How often do you play football? | I **always** play on Saturdays. | Every Saturday. |
| How often do you go swimming? | I **sometimes** go swimming. | Twice a week. |
| How often do you eat meat? | I **never** eat meat. | Never. |

*Every day / twice a week / at weekends* (U10–U13) + adverbios (U33) = hábitos claros.

---

## 6. Reading modelo: Emma

![Rutina de Emma A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/a1-unit33-emma-routine.png)

> My name is Emma. I **always** get up at 7 in the morning. I **usually** have breakfast with my family. I **often** go running before work. I **sometimes** meet friends for lunch. I **never** eat late at night because I like to sleep early. At weekends I **always** relax and read books.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/emma-routine.mp3" title="🔊 I always get up at 7. I usually have breakfast with my family"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/always-relax-weekends.mp3" title="🔊 At weekends I always relax and read books"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/always-usually-often.mp3" title="🔊 I always get up early. I usually have breakfast. I often go running"></audio>

### Comprueba

1. ¿A qué hora se levanta? → **At 7** (*always*).  
2. ¿Desayuna con la familia? → **Usually**.  
3. ¿Qué hace a menudo antes del trabajo? → **Go running**.  
4. ¿Come tarde por la noche? → **Never**.  
5. ¿Qué hace los fines de semana? → **Always relax and read books**.

---

## 7. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** How often do you get up early?  
> **B:** I **always** get up at 7. And you?  
> **A:** I **usually** get up at 8. Do you go running?  
> **B:** Yes — I **often** go running before work.  
> **A:** Nice! Do you eat late at night?  
> **B:** No, I **never** eat late. I like to sleep early.  
> **A:** At weekends I **always** relax and read books.  
> **B:** Me too sometimes… but I **often** meet friends!

---

## 8. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I get always up* | *I **always** get up* | Adv. antes del verbo |
| *She never is late* | *She **is never** late* | Adv. después de *be* |
| *I am always get up* | *I always get up* | No mezcles *be* + verbo |
| *She always go* | *She always **goes*** | 3.ª persona en el verbo |
| *I never don't eat* | *I **never** eat* | *Never* ya es negativo |
| *Always I get up* | *I always get up* | Orden A1 estándar |

### Tip *never*

*Never* = negativo. No uses *don't/doesn't* juntos en A1 básico:

> I **never** eat meat. ✅  
> I don’t never eat meat. ❌

---

## 9. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **always** | *OL-weiz* (2 sílabas). |
| **usually** | *IU-zhu-li* (cuidado con /ʒ/). |
| **often** | UK a menudo *OF-ən* (t muda frecuente). |
| **sometimes** | *SAM-taimz*. |
| **never** | *NE-və*. |

Practica la cadena: *always → usually → often → sometimes → never*.

---

## 9b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Do you always have breakfast?  
> **B:** Yes, I usually have breakfast with my family.  
> **A:** How often do you go running?  
> **B:** I often go running before work.

> **A:** Is she ever late?  
> **B:** No. She is never late.  
> **A:** Are they busy?  
> **B:** Yes — they are always busy.

> **A:** Do you eat late at night?  
> **B:** Never. I like to sleep early.  
> **A:** What do you do at weekends?  
> **B:** I always relax and read books.

Cambia solo el adverbio: fijas la **posición**.

---

## 9c. Plantillas para copiar

1. I always \_\_\_\_ at \_\_\_\_.  
2. I usually \_\_\_\_ with \_\_\_\_.  
3. I often \_\_\_\_ before \_\_\_\_.  
4. I sometimes \_\_\_\_.  
5. I never \_\_\_\_.  
6. She / He is never \_\_\_\_.  
7. They are always \_\_\_\_.  
8. How often do you \_\_\_\_?

### Más frases para memorizar

> I always get up at 7 in the morning.  
> I usually have breakfast with my family.  
> I often go running before work.  
> I sometimes meet friends for lunch.  
> I never eat late at night.  
> At weekends I always relax and read books.  
> She is never late.  
> They are always busy.  
> I usually get up at 7.  
> We sometimes go to the cinema.  
> He is never late.  
> I always have breakfast at 8.  
> I often watch TV in the evening.  
> She never eats meat.  
> I usually drink coffee in the morning.  
> She never forgets her keys.  
> I often go to the gym.  
> How often do you go running?

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego escribe **tu** rutina con los cinco adverbios.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 1 frase con *always*.  
2. Di 1 con *usually*.  
3. Di 1 con *often*.  
4. Di 1 con *sometimes*.  
5. Di 1 con *never*.  
6. Di 1 con *be* (*is/are* + adverbio).

Si lo unes a deportes (U32), practicas *I often play football / I usually go swimming*.

### Combinar U32 + U33

| Deporte / hobby | + frecuencia |
| :--- | :--- |
| I play football | I **always** play football on Saturdays. |
| I go swimming | I **usually** go swimming on Sundays. |
| I do yoga | I **often** do yoga in the morning. |
| I like reading | I **always** read books at weekends. |

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> I always get up at 7. I usually have breakfast. I often go running. I sometimes meet friends. I never eat late. At weekends I always relax.

Cambia los verbos por los tuyos y mantén los adverbios en el sitio correcto.

### Tour guiado (modelo Emma)

> My name is Emma. I always get up at 7 in the morning. I usually have breakfast with my family. I often go running before work. I sometimes meet friends for lunch. I never eat late at night because I like to sleep early. At weekends I always relax and read books.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tu** día.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> How often do you get up early?  
> I always get up at 7.  
> I usually have breakfast with my family.  
> I often go running before work.  
> I sometimes meet friends for lunch.  
> I never eat late at night.  
> She is never late.  
> They are always busy.  
> At weekends I always relax and read books.  
> How often do you go to the gym?

Personaliza horas y actividades. Cuanto más real, mejor.

### Checklist mental

- Escala: always → usually → often → sometimes → never  
- Verbo normal → adverbio **antes**  
- *be* → adverbio **después**  
- 3.ª persona: *-s* en el **verbo**, no en el adverbio  
- *never* = sin *don't*  
- Pregunta: *How often…?*

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U5 / U13 | Present Simple + rutina |
| U32 | play / go / do |
| **U33** | Adverbs of frequency |
| U34 | and / but / because |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige el adverbio

1. I \_\_\_\_ get up at 7. (100%)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ eats meat. (0%)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ go to the cinema. (a veces)  
4. I \_\_\_\_ go running before work. (a menudo)  
5. I \_\_\_\_ have breakfast with my family. (normalmente)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **always**  
2. **never**  
3. **sometimes**  
4. **often**  
5. **usually**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Posición (ordena)

1. always / I / get up / at 7  
2. never / she / is / late  
3. often / I / go / running  
4. are / they / always / busy  
5. sometimes / we / go / to the cinema

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I always get up at 7.**  
2. **She is never late.**  
3. **I often go running.**  
4. **They are always busy.**  
5. **We sometimes go to the cinema.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Siempre me levanto a las 7.  
2. Ella nunca llega tarde.  
3. A menudo voy a correr.  
4. A veces quedo con amigos.  
5. Normalmente desayuno con mi familia.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I always get up at 7.**  
2. **She is never late.**  
3. **I often go running.**  
4. **I sometimes meet friends.**  
5. **I usually have breakfast with my family.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — *be* o verbo normal

1. He \_\_\_\_ never late. (*is*)  
2. They \_\_\_\_ always busy. (*are*)  
3. I \_\_\_\_ always get up early. (— / adverbio solo)  
4. She \_\_\_\_ never eats meat.  
5. We \_\_\_\_ sometimes go to the cinema.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **is**  
2. **are**  
3. (nada: *I always get up early*)  
4. (nada: *She never eats meat*)  
5. (nada: *We sometimes go…*)
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de Emma (sección 6). Contesta:

1. What time does she get up?  
2. Does she usually have breakfast alone?  
3. What does she often do before work?  
4. Does she eat late at night?  
5. What does she always do at weekends?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **At 7**  
2. **No — with her family**  
3. **Go running**  
4. **No — never**  
5. **Relax and read books**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa con *always / usually / often / sometimes / never*

1. I \_\_\_\_ drink coffee in the morning. (casi siempre)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ forgets her keys. (nunca)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ eat out at weekends. (a veces)  
4. He \_\_\_\_ goes to the gym. (a menudo)  
5. At weekends I \_\_\_\_ relax. (siempre)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **usually**  
2. **never**  
3. **sometimes**  
4. **often**  
5. **always**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe sobre ti

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- los cinco adverbios  
- al menos una frase con *be*  
- una pregunta *How often…?*  
- un deporte de la U32

**Modelo:** el texto de Emma (sección 6).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. She \_\_\_\_ late. (never is / is never / never)  
2. I \_\_\_\_ get up at 7. (always / am always / get always)  
3. They \_\_\_\_ busy. (always are / are always / always)  
4. He never \_\_\_\_ meat. (eat / eats / eating)  
5. How often \_\_\_\_ you go running? (do / does / are)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **is never**  
2. **always**  
3. **are always**  
4. **eats**  
5. **do**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Escala en voz alta: always → never.  
2. **3 min** — 5 frases verbo + 3 frases con *be*.  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el texto de Emma.  
4. **5 min** — Preguntas *How often…?* + respuestas.

### Checklist

- [ ] Conozco always / usually / often / sometimes / never  
- [ ] Pongo el adverbio antes del verbo  
- [ ] Pongo el adverbio después de *be*  
- [ ] Uso *-s* en 3.ª persona del verbo  
- [ ] Pregunto *How often…?*

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Tabla personal:** una columna por adverbio, 2 hábitos en cada una.  
2. **Pareja:** 6 × *How often do you…?*  
3. **Combina** U32: *I often play football / I usually go swimming.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 34](/curso-a1/unit-34): *and, but, because*.  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 33](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-33-adverbios-frecuencia-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 33 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-33).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Escala | always → usually → often → sometimes → never |
| Verbo | subject + **adv** + verb |
| *be* | subject + **be** + adv |
| Negativo | *never* (sin *don't*) |
| Pregunta | How often…? |
| Tip | *-s* en el verbo, no en el adverbio |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

Continúa con la [**Unidad 34 — And, but, because**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-34-and-but-because): suma ideas, contraste y razones.

title: And, but, because A1: conectar ideas en inglés
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 34 del curso A1: and, but y because para unir ideas, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende a unir frases con and, but y because en inglés A1 para sumar ideas, contrastar y dar razones. Guía Unidad 34 con audios, esquemas y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema and but because para conectar ideas en inglés A1

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso and, but y because?
faqs.answer: And suma ideas (I like coffee and tea). But marca contraste (I like tea but I don't like coffee). Because da una razón (I stay home because I am tired).

faqs.question: ¿Because va con sujeto y verbo?
faqs.answer: Sí. En A1 usamos because + oración: because I am tired, because it is healthy. No digas solo because tired.

faqs.question: ¿Puedo empezar una frase con Because?
faqs.answer: En speaking informal a veces se oye. En A1 del curso, lo más seguro es unir dos ideas en la misma frase: I stay home because I am tired.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 34?
faqs.answer: And, but, because, reason, contrast, like, don't like, tired, healthy, tasty, sport, music, pizza, fish, cinema.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 34 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 34 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 33](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-33-adverbios-frecuencia) dijiste **con qué frecuencia** haces las cosas (*I always get up at 7*). En la **Unidad 34 del curso A1** (*Using And, But, Because*) aprendes a **unir ideas** para hablar con frases más largas y naturales.

Encaja con gustos de la [Unidad 18](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-18-gustos-like-ing-because) y con deportes de la [Unidad 32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 34 — Using And, But, Because](/curso-a1/unit-34)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 33 — Adverbios de frecuencia](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-33-adverbios-frecuencia) · [Unidad 18 — Gustos](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-18-gustos-like-ing-because)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 34 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***and*** para **sumar** ideas.
- Usar ***but*** para **contrastar**.
- Usar ***because*** para dar una **razón**.
- Unir dos oraciones cortas en una más larga.
- Hablar de gustos y hábitos con más detalle (Leo: sport, music, pizza…).

---

## 1. Tres conectores, tres trabajos

| Conector | Trabajo | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **and** | suma / añade | I like coffee **and** tea. |
| **but** | contraste | I like tea **but** I don't like coffee. |
| **because** | razón / causa | I stay at home **because** I am tired. |

![Esquema and but because A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/a1-unit34-and-but-because.png)

```
and      → + (same direction)
but      → ≠ (contrast)
because  → why (reason)
```

### Tip

Pregúntate: ¿estoy **añadiendo**, **oponiéndome** o **explicando por qué**? Esa pregunta elige el conector.

---

## 2. *And* — sumar ideas

Une dos cosas del mismo “sentido”:

> I like coffee **and** tea.  
> I like pizza **and** pasta.  
> I like dogs **and** cats.  
> I like sport **and** music.  
> At weekends I meet friends **and** we go to the cinema.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/like-coffee-and-tea.mp3" title="🔊 I like coffee and tea"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/like-pizza-and-pasta.mp3" title="🔊 I like pizza and pasta"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/like-dogs-and-cats.mp3" title="🔊 I like dogs and cats"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/like-sport-and-music.mp3" title="🔊 I like sport and music"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/meet-friends-and-cinema.mp3" title="🔊 At weekends I meet friends and we go to the cinema"></audio>

### Patrones útiles

| Patrón | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| noun **and** noun | pizza and pasta |
| verb phrase **and** verb phrase | I meet friends and we play video games |
| adjective **and** adjective | easy and tasty |

No hace falta repetir el sujeto si es el mismo y el verbo es paralelo: *I like tea and coffee.*

---

## 3. *But* — contraste

Une dos ideas que **no van en la misma dirección**:

> I play football **but** I don't like watching it on TV.  
> I like tea **but** I don't like coffee.  
> I like swimming **but** I don't like running.  
> She is tall **but** her brother is short.  
> He is fast **but** he doesn't like running.  
> I don't like fish **but** I eat it sometimes…

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/football-but-dont-watch.mp3" title="🔊 I play football but I don't like watching it on TV"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/like-tea-but-not-coffee.mp3" title="🔊 I like tea but I don't like coffee"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/swimming-but-not-running.mp3" title="🔊 I like swimming but I don't like running"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/tall-but-brother-short.mp3" title="🔊 She is tall but her brother is short"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/fast-but-dont-like-running.mp3" title="🔊 He is fast but he doesn't like running"></audio>

### Tip

Tras *but* suele aparecer un **cambio**: positivo → negativo, o al revés.

> I like it **but** it's expensive.  
> It's difficult **but** I like it.

---

## 4. *Because* — dar una razón

Responde a ***Why…?***

> I stay at home **because** I am tired.  
> We eat pasta **because** we like it.  
> I like pizza **because** it is easy to make and tasty.  
> I'm tired **because** I didn't sleep well.  
> We are happy **because** we passed the exam.  
> I like it **because** it's cheap.  
> She is sad **because** she lost her phone.  
> I eat fish sometimes **because** it's healthy.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/stay-home-because-tired.mp3" title="🔊 I stay at home because I am tired"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/eat-pasta-because-like.mp3" title="🔊 We eat pasta because we like it"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/like-pizza-because-tasty.mp3" title="🔊 I like pizza because it is easy to make and tasty"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/tired-because-no-sleep.mp3" title="🔊 I'm tired because I didn't sleep well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/happy-because-passed.mp3" title="🔊 We are happy because we passed the exam"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/like-it-because-cheap.mp3" title="🔊 I like it because it's cheap"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/sad-because-lost-phone.mp3" title="🔊 She is sad because she lost her phone"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/dont-like-fish-but.mp3" title="🔊 I don't like fish but I eat it sometimes because it's healthy"></audio>

### Regla A1

***Because* + sujeto + verbo** (oración completa):

| ❌ | ✅ |
| :--- | :--- |
| because tired | because **I am** tired |
| because healthy | because **it is** healthy |
| because like it | because **I like** it |

Ya viste *because* con gustos en la [Unidad 18](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-18-gustos-like-ing-because). Aquí lo generalizas a cualquier razón.

---

## 5. De dos frases cortas a una larga

![Diagrama de conectores A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/a1-unit34-connectors-diagram.png)

| Frases cortas | Conector | Frase unida |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I like coffee. I like tea. | **and** | I like coffee **and** tea. |
| I like tea. I don't like coffee. | **but** | I like tea **but** I don't like coffee. |
| I stay at home. I am tired. | **because** | I stay at home **because** I am tired. |

### Mini-práctica mental

1. ¿Misma dirección? → **and**  
2. ¿Contraste? → **but**  
3. ¿Por qué? → **because**

---

## 6. Vocabulario útil del texto de Leo

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| sport | deporte | I like sport and music. |
| music | música | I like sport and music. |
| watch on TV | ver en la tele | I don't like watching it on TV. |
| prefer | preferir | I prefer to play outside. |
| tasty | rico / sabroso | …easy to make and tasty. |
| healthy | sano | …because it's healthy. |
| meet friends | quedar con amigos | I meet friends at weekends. |
| cinema | cine | we go to the cinema |
| video games | videojuegos | we play video games |

---

## 7. Reading modelo: Leo

![Gustos de Leo A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/a1-unit34-leo-likes.png)

> My name is Leo. I like sport **and** music. I play football **but** I don't like watching it on TV. I prefer to play outside. I like pizza **because** it is easy to make **and** tasty. I don't like fish **but** I eat it sometimes **because** it's healthy. At weekends I meet friends **and** we go to the cinema or we play video games.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/leo-intro.mp3" title="🔊 My name is Leo. I like sport and music"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-34/prefer-play-outside.mp3" title="🔊 I prefer to play outside"></audio>

### Comprueba

1. ¿Qué le gusta? → **Sport and music**.  
2. ¿Le gusta ver fútbol en la tele? → **No**.  
3. ¿Por qué le gusta la pizza? → **Easy to make and tasty**.  
4. ¿Come pescado? → **Sometimes, because it's healthy**.  
5. ¿Qué hace el fin de semana? → **Meet friends; cinema or video games**.

Cuenta los conectores del texto: verás **and**, **but** y **because** trabajando juntos.

---

## 8. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** Do you like football?  
> **B:** Yes, I play football **but** I don't like watching it on TV.  
> **A:** Why?  
> **B:** **Because** I prefer to play outside.  
> **A:** And food? Do you like pizza?  
> **B:** Yes, **because** it's easy to make **and** tasty.  
> **A:** Do you like fish?  
> **B:** No, **but** I eat it sometimes **because** it's healthy.  
> **A:** Nice. At weekends I meet friends **and** we go to the cinema.

---

## 9. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I like tea and I don't like coffee* (sin contraste claro) | *I like tea **but** I don't like coffee* | Contraste → **but** |
| *I stay home because tired* | *…because **I am** tired* | *because* + oración |
| *Because I am tired. I stay home.* (dos frases sueltas A1) | *I stay home **because** I am tired.* | Une en una frase |
| *I like pizza but is tasty* | *I like pizza **because** it is tasty* | Razón ≠ contraste |
| *I like coffee but tea* | *I like coffee **and** tea* | Suma → **and** |

### *Why…? / Because…*

> **Why** do you stay at home?  
> **Because** I am tired. / I stay at home **because** I am tired.

En writing A1, la segunda opción (frase completa) es más clara.

---

## 9b. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **and** | a menudo /ən/ débil entre palabras: *tea and coffee*. |
| **but** | /bʌt/; no alargues la *u*. |
| **because** | *bi-COZ* (acento en la 2.ª). |
| **tasty** | *TEIS-ti*. |
| **healthy** | *HEL-zi* (th sonora). |

Practica el trío: *and → but → because* en tres frases seguidas.

---

## 9c. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Do you like tea and coffee?  
> **B:** I like tea but I don't like coffee.  
> **A:** Why do you stay at home?  
> **B:** Because I am tired.

> **A:** Do you like swimming?  
> **B:** Yes, but I don't like running.  
> **A:** Why do you eat fish?  
> **B:** Because it's healthy.

> **A:** What do you like?  
> **B:** Sport and music.  
> **A:** And at weekends?  
> **B:** I meet friends and we go to the cinema.

Cambia solo los sustantivos: fijas el **conector**.

---

## 9d. Plantillas para copiar

1. I like \_\_\_\_ and \_\_\_\_.  
2. I like \_\_\_\_ but I don't like \_\_\_\_.  
3. I \_\_\_\_ because I am / it is \_\_\_\_.  
4. She is \_\_\_\_ but her brother is \_\_\_\_.  
5. Why do you \_\_\_\_? — Because \_\_\_\_.  
6. I don't like \_\_\_\_ but I \_\_\_\_ sometimes because \_\_\_\_.  
7. At weekends I \_\_\_\_ and we \_\_\_\_.

### Más frases para memorizar

> I like coffee and tea.  
> I like pizza and pasta.  
> I like dogs and cats.  
> I like sport and music.  
> I play football but I don't like watching it on TV.  
> I like tea but I don't like coffee.  
> I like swimming but I don't like running.  
> She is tall but her brother is short.  
> I stay at home because I am tired.  
> We eat pasta because we like it.  
> I like pizza because it is easy to make and tasty.  
> I'm tired because I didn't sleep well.  
> We are happy because we passed the exam.  
> I don't like fish but I eat it sometimes because it's healthy.  
> At weekends I meet friends and we go to the cinema.  
> I like it because it's cheap.  
> He is fast but he doesn't like running.  
> She is sad because she lost her phone.  
> I prefer to play outside.  
> My name is Leo. I like sport and music.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego escribe **tu** versión con and / but / because.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 2 frases con *and*.  
2. Di 2 frases con *but*.  
3. Di 2 frases con *because*.  
4. Une las tres en un mini-texto (como Leo).

Si lo combinas con U33: *I often play football but I never watch it on TV because I prefer to play outside.*

### Combinar U18 + U32 + U33 + U34

| Unidad | Aporta | Ejemplo unido |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U18 | like + -ing | I like swimming |
| U32 | play/go/do | I play football |
| U33 | frequency | I often play football |
| **U34** | connectors | …**but** I don't watch it **because** I prefer to play outside |

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> I like sport and music. I play football but I don't watch it on TV. I like pizza because it's tasty. I don't like fish but I eat it sometimes because it's healthy. At weekends I meet friends and we go to the cinema.

Cambia *football → tennis*, *pizza → pasta*, *cinema → gym*, y mantén los conectores.

### Tour guiado (modelo Leo)

> My name is Leo. I like sport and music. I play football but I don't like watching it on TV. I prefer to play outside. I like pizza because it is easy to make and tasty. I don't like fish but I eat it sometimes because it's healthy. At weekends I meet friends and we go to the cinema or we play video games.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tus** gustos.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> Why do you stay at home?  
> Because I am tired.  
> I like tea but I don't like coffee.  
> I like pizza because it's tasty.  
> She is tall but her brother is short.  
> We are happy because we passed the exam.  
> I meet friends and we play video games.  
> I prefer to play outside.

Personaliza comida, deporte y fin de semana.

### Checklist mental

- Suma → **and**  
- Contraste → **but**  
- Razón → **because** + sujeto + verbo  
- *Why…?* → *Because…* / frase completa  
- Puedes combinar dos conectores: *…but… because…*

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U18 | like + -ing + because |
| U33 | adverbs of frequency |
| **U34** | and / but / because |
| U35 | Free time activities |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige el conector

1. I like coffee \_\_\_\_ tea.  
2. I like tea \_\_\_\_ I don't like coffee.  
3. I stay at home \_\_\_\_ I am tired.  
4. She is tall \_\_\_\_ her brother is short.  
5. We eat pasta \_\_\_\_ we like it.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **and**  
2. **but**  
3. **because**  
4. **but**  
5. **because**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Une las frases

1. I like pizza. I like pasta. → …  
2. I like swimming. I don't like running. → …  
3. I stay at home. I am tired. → …  
4. He is fast. He doesn't like running. → …  
5. We are happy. We passed the exam. → …

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I like pizza and pasta.**  
2. **I like swimming but I don't like running.**  
3. **I stay at home because I am tired.**  
4. **He is fast but he doesn't like running.**  
5. **We are happy because we passed the exam.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Me gusta el deporte y la música.  
2. Juego al fútbol pero no me gusta verlo en la tele.  
3. Me quedo en casa porque estoy cansado.  
4. Me gusta la pizza porque es rica.  
5. No me gusta el pescado pero lo como a veces porque es sano.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I like sport and music.**  
2. **I play football but I don't like watching it on TV.**  
3. **I stay at home because I am tired.**  
4. **I like pizza because it is tasty. / …because it's tasty.**  
5. **I don't like fish but I eat it sometimes because it's healthy.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — ¿And, but o because?

1. I like dogs \_\_\_\_ cats. (suma)  
2. I'm tired \_\_\_\_ I didn't sleep well. (razón)  
3. I like it \_\_\_\_ it's cheap. (razón)  
4. She is sad \_\_\_\_ she lost her phone. (razón)  
5. I prefer to play outside \_\_\_\_ I don't like watching football on TV. (contraste — elige con sentido)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **and**  
2. **because**  
3. **because**  
4. **because**  
5. **but** / o reescribe: *I don't like watching football on TV because I prefer to play outside.*
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de Leo (sección 7). Contesta:

1. What does Leo like?  
2. Does he like watching football on TV?  
3. Why does he like pizza?  
4. Why does he eat fish sometimes?  
5. What does he do at weekends?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Sport and music**  
2. **No**  
3. **Because it is easy to make and tasty**  
4. **Because it's healthy**  
5. **Meet friends; cinema or video games**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa *because* con oración

1. I stay at home because \_\_\_\_. (cansado)  
2. We eat pasta because \_\_\_\_. (nos gusta)  
3. She is sad because \_\_\_\_. (perdió el móvil)  
4. I like it because \_\_\_\_. (barato)  
5. We are happy because \_\_\_\_. (aprobamos)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I am tired**  
2. **we like it**  
3. **she lost her phone**  
4. **it's cheap / it is cheap**  
5. **we passed the exam**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe sobre ti

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- 2 × *and*  
- 2 × *but*  
- 2 × *because*  
- un deporte (U32) y un adverbio de frecuencia (U33)

**Modelo:** el texto de Leo (sección 7).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. I like tea \_\_\_\_ I don't like coffee. (and / but / because)  
2. I stay home \_\_\_\_ I am tired. (and / but / because)  
3. I like coffee \_\_\_\_ tea. (and / but / because)  
4. Because tired. → ¿Correcto? (sí / **no**)  
5. Why do you eat fish? — \_\_\_\_ it's healthy. (And / But / Because)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **but**  
2. **because**  
3. **and**  
4. **no** → *because I am tired*  
5. **Because**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Tabla: 3 *and*, 3 *but*, 3 *because*.  
2. **3 min** — Une 5 pares de frases cortas.  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el texto de Leo.  
4. **5 min** — Preguntas *Why…?* + respuestas *Because…*.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *and* para sumar  
- [ ] Uso *but* para contrastar  
- [ ] Uso *because* + sujeto + verbo  
- [ ] Respondo *Why…?* con razón  
- [ ] Combino conectores en un mini-texto

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Diario de 5 líneas:** cada día una frase con *and*, una con *but*, una con *because*.  
2. **Pareja:** *Why do you…?* × 6.  
3. **Combina** U33: *I often play football but I never watch it on TV.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 35](/curso-a1/unit-35): *Free Time Activities*.  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 34](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-34-and-but-because-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 34 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-34).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Conector | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **and** | suma | coffee and tea |
| **but** | contraste | tea but not coffee |
| **because** | razón | because I am tired |
| **Tip** | *because* + oración | because it is healthy |
| **Why?** | Because… | Why? Because… |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 34 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-34-and-but-because-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 34 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-34)

Continúa con la [**Unidad 35 — Free Time Activities**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-35-free-time-activities): *go for a walk*, *go shopping*, *like watching TV*.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe un párrafo de 6–8 frases sobre ti usando *and*, *but* y *because* al menos una vez cada uno.

Guías relacionadas:

- [Gramática inglesa: guía por niveles](/blog/gramatica/gramatica-inglesa-guia)
- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)

---

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- British Council — And, but, or, so, because: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar

title: Free Time Activities A1: go for a walk, go shopping y like + -ing
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 35 del curso A1: tiempo libre con go for a walk, go shopping y like + -ing, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende a hablar de tu tiempo libre en inglés A1: go for a walk, go shopping, watching TV y playing video games. Guía Unidad 35 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema go for a walk go shopping y like + -ing en inglés A1

faqs.question: ¿Cómo digo ir de paseo e ir de compras?
faqs.answer: Go for a walk (ir de paseo) y go shopping (ir de compras). Con he/she: goes for a walk / goes shopping.

faqs.question: ¿Uso like + -ing con actividades de ocio?
faqs.answer: Sí. I like watching TV. He likes playing video games. We enjoy walking in the park.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es free time?
faqs.answer: Free time es el tiempo libre: cuando no trabajas ni estudias. What do you do in your free time?

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 35?
faqs.answer: Go for a walk, go shopping, watching TV, video games, walking, free time, films, park, social media, walk the dog.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 35 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 35 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 34](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-34-and-but-because) uniste ideas con *and / but / because*. En la **Unidad 35 del curso A1** (*Free Time Activities*) aprendes a hablar de tu **tiempo libre**: ***go for a walk***, ***go shopping***, ***watching TV***, ***playing video games***.

Repasas *go + -ing* de la [Unidad 32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do) y *like + -ing* de la [Unidad 18](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-18-gustos-like-ing-because). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 35 — Free Time Activities](/curso-a1/unit-35)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 34 — And, but, because](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-34-and-but-because) · [Unidad 32 — Sports & Hobbies](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 35 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***go for a walk*** e ***go shopping***.
- Hablar de gustos con ***like / enjoy + -ing***.
- Usar vocabulario: *watching TV, video games, walking, free time*.
- Preguntar ***What do you do in your free time?***.
- Combinar con frecuencia (U33) y conectores (U34).

---

## 1. Dos patrones clave

| Patrón | Uso | Ejemplos |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **go + frase** | actividades con *go* | go for a walk, go shopping |
| **like / enjoy + -ing** | gustos de ocio | like watching TV, enjoy walking |

![Patrones free time A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/a1-unit35-free-time-patterns.png)

```
go for a walk / go shopping
like + watching / playing / walking / going…
```

### Tip

*Go shopping* (sin *to the*). *Go for a walk* (con *for a*). Memoriza las dos frases enteras.

---

## 2. *Go for a walk* — ir de paseo

> I **go for a walk** every evening.  
> I **go for a walk** in the park.  
> We **go for a walk** every Sunday.  
> She **goes for a walk** every day.  
> At weekends we sometimes **go for a walk** together.  
> In my free time I **go for a walk**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/go-for-a-walk-evening.mp3" title="🔊 I go for a walk every evening"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/go-for-a-walk-park.mp3" title="🔊 I go for a walk in the park"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/go-for-a-walk-sunday.mp3" title="🔊 We go for a walk every Sunday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/she-goes-for-a-walk.mp3" title="🔊 She goes for a walk every day"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/i-go-for-a-walk.mp3" title="🔊 In my free time I go for a walk"></audio>

### 3.ª persona

| Sujeto | Forma |
| :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they | go for a walk |
| he / she / it | **goes** for a walk |

También: *like **going** for a walk* (= te gusta ir de paseo).

---

## 3. *Go shopping* — ir de compras

> She **goes shopping** on Saturdays.  
> We **go shopping** at weekends.  
> They like **going shopping** on Saturdays.  
> I don't like **going shopping** because it is too busy.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/goes-shopping-saturdays.mp3" title="🔊 She goes shopping on Saturdays"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/go-shopping-weekends.mp3" title="🔊 We go shopping at weekends"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/likes-going-shopping.mp3" title="🔊 They like going shopping on Saturdays"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/dont-like-shopping.mp3" title="🔊 I don't like going shopping because it is too busy"></audio>

### Contraste útil

| ✅ | ❌ |
| :--- | :--- |
| go shopping | go to shopping |
| go for a walk | go to a walk |
| go to the shops | go the shops |

*Go to the shops* también es correcto (ir a las tiendas). En esta unidad priorizamos ***go shopping***.

---

## 4. *Like / enjoy + -ing* — gustos de ocio

> I **like watching** TV.  
> She **likes watching** TV.  
> She **likes watching** TV at night.  
> He **likes playing** video games.  
> I **like watching** TV and **playing** video games.  
> We **enjoy walking** in the park.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/like-watching-tv.mp3" title="🔊 I like watching TV"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/she-likes-watching-tv.mp3" title="🔊 She likes watching TV"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/likes-watching-tv-night.mp3" title="🔊 She likes watching TV at night"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/like-playing-video-games.mp3" title="🔊 He likes playing video games"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/like-watching-and-playing.mp3" title="🔊 I like watching TV and playing video games"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/enjoy-walking-park.mp3" title="🔊 We enjoy walking in the park"></audio>

### Regla (repaso U18)

Tras *like / love / enjoy / don't like* → **verbo + -ing**.

| ❌ | ✅ |
| :--- | :--- |
| I like watch TV | I like **watching** TV |
| He likes play video games | He likes **playing** video games |
| We enjoy walk | We enjoy **walking** |

---

## 5. Vocabulario de tiempo libre

![Vocabulario free time A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/a1-unit35-free-time-vocab.png)

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| free time | tiempo libre | In my free time… |
| go for a walk | ir de paseo | I go for a walk in the park. |
| go shopping | ir de compras | She goes shopping on Saturdays. |
| watching TV | ver la tele | I like watching TV. |
| video games | videojuegos | He likes playing video games. |
| walking | pasear / caminar | We enjoy walking. |
| walk the dog | pasear al perro | …walking the dog. |
| films | películas | I often watch films at home. |
| park | parque | in the park |
| social media | redes sociales | I sometimes check social media. |
| busy | concurrido / ocupado | It's too busy. |

---

## 6. Preguntar por el tiempo libre

> **What do you do in your free time?**  
> In my free time I go for a walk.  
> I like watching TV and playing video games.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/what-do-you-do.mp3" title="🔊 What do you do in your free time?"></audio>

### Otras preguntas útiles

| Pregunta | Respuesta modelo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Do you go for a walk? | Yes, every evening. |
| Do you like going shopping? | No, because it's too busy. |
| How often do you watch TV? | I often watch films at home. |
| Does he like video games? | Yes, he likes playing video games. |

---

## 7. Reading modelo: Mia

![Tiempo libre de Mia A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/a1-unit35-mia-free-time.png)

> My name is Mia. In my free time I like **going for a walk** in the park and **watching** TV. I often **watch** films at home. I don't like **going shopping** because it is too busy. My brother likes **playing** video games and **walking** the dog. At weekends we sometimes **go for a walk** together in the morning.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/mia-free-time.mp3" title="🔊 In my free time I like going for a walk in the park and watching TV"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/often-watch-films.mp3" title="🔊 I often watch films at home"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/brother-games-dog.mp3" title="🔊 My brother likes playing video games and walking the dog"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-35/sometimes-walk-together.mp3" title="🔊 At weekends we sometimes go for a walk together in the morning"></audio>

### Comprueba

1. ¿Qué le gusta a Mia? → **Going for a walk and watching TV**.  
2. ¿Le gusta ir de compras? → **No — too busy**.  
3. ¿Qué ve a menudo? → **Films at home**.  
4. ¿Qué le gusta a su hermano? → **Video games and walking the dog**.  
5. ¿Cuándo pasean juntos? → **Sometimes at weekends in the morning**.

Fíjate: *like going / watching / playing* + *go for a walk* + *often / sometimes* (U33) + *because* (U34).

---

## 8. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** What do you do in your free time?  
> **B:** I like going for a walk in the park and watching TV. And you?  
> **A:** I often watch films at home. Do you like going shopping?  
> **B:** No, I don't — because it's too busy.  
> **A:** What about your brother?  
> **B:** He likes playing video games and walking the dog.  
> **A:** Nice! At weekends we sometimes go for a walk together.

---

## 9. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *go to shopping* | ***go shopping*** | Sin *to* |
| *go to a walk* | ***go for a walk*** | *for a walk* |
| *I like watch TV* | *I like **watching** TV* | *like + -ing* |
| *She go shopping* | *She **goes** shopping* | 3.ª persona |
| *I like play video games* | *I like **playing** video games* | *-ing* |
| *in my free times* | *in my **free time*** | Singular habitual |

---

## 9b. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **walk / walking** | *wok* · *WO-king* (l muda en muchos acentos). |
| **shopping** | *SHO-ping* (doble p). |
| **watching** | *WO-ching*. |
| **video games** | *VI-di-ou geimz*. |
| **free time** | une: *freeˈtime*. |

Practica: *go for a walk → go shopping → like watching TV*.

---

## 9c. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Do you go for a walk?  
> **B:** Yes, every evening in the park.  
> **A:** Do you go shopping at weekends?  
> **B:** Sometimes — but I don't like it when it's busy.

> **A:** What do you like doing at home?  
> **B:** Watching TV and playing video games.  
> **A:** How often do you watch films?  
> **B:** I often watch films at night.

> **A:** What does your brother like?  
> **B:** Playing video games and walking the dog.  
> **A:** Do you go for a walk together?  
> **B:** Yes — sometimes at weekends.

Cambia solo el día o el lugar: fijas las **estructuras**.

---

## 9d. Plantillas para copiar

1. I go for a walk every \_\_\_\_.  
2. She / He goes shopping on \_\_\_\_.  
3. I like watching \_\_\_\_.  
4. He likes playing \_\_\_\_.  
5. We enjoy walking in \_\_\_\_.  
6. What do you do in your free time?  
7. I don't like going shopping because \_\_\_\_.  
8. At weekends we sometimes go for a walk together.

### Más frases para memorizar

> I go for a walk every evening.  
> She goes shopping on Saturdays.  
> We go shopping at weekends.  
> I go for a walk in the park.  
> We go for a walk every Sunday.  
> I like watching TV.  
> She likes watching TV.  
> She likes watching TV at night.  
> He likes playing video games.  
> I like watching TV and playing video games.  
> We enjoy walking in the park.  
> I often watch films at home.  
> I don't like going shopping because it is too busy.  
> My brother likes playing video games and walking the dog.  
> At weekends we sometimes go for a walk together in the morning.  
> In my free time I like going for a walk in the park and watching TV.  
> What do you do in your free time?  
> In my free time I go for a walk.  
> She goes for a walk every day.  
> They like going shopping on Saturdays.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego describe **tu** free time en 8 frases.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 2 frases *go for a walk*.  
2. Di 2 frases *go shopping*.  
3. Di 2 *like + -ing*.  
4. Responde *What do you do in your free time?*

Si lo unes a U33: *I often go for a walk. I sometimes go shopping. I never play video games.*

### Combinar U32 + U33 + U34 + U35

| Unidad | Aporta | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U32 | play/go/do | I go swimming |
| U33 | frequency | I often… |
| U34 | connectors | …but / because… |
| **U35** | free time phrases | I go for a walk / like watching TV |

Modelo largo:

> In my free time I often go for a walk in the park **but** I don't like going shopping **because** it's too busy. I like watching TV **and** playing video games.

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> In my free time I like going for a walk and watching TV. I often watch films at home. I don't like going shopping because it's too busy. My brother likes playing video games. At weekends we sometimes go for a walk together.

Cambia *park → beach*, *films → series*, *brother → sister*, y mantén *go / like + -ing*.

### Tour guiado (modelo Mia)

> My name is Mia. In my free time I like going for a walk in the park and watching TV. I often watch films at home. I don't like going shopping because it is too busy. My brother likes playing video games and walking the dog. At weekends we sometimes go for a walk together in the morning.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tu** familia.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> What do you do in your free time?  
> I go for a walk every evening.  
> She goes shopping on Saturdays.  
> I like watching TV and playing video games.  
> We enjoy walking in the park.  
> I often watch films at home.  
> I don't like going shopping because it's too busy.  
> At weekends we sometimes go for a walk together.

Personaliza parque, día y actividad.

### Checklist mental

- *go for a walk* / *go shopping*  
- he/she → *goes*  
- *like / enjoy + -ing*  
- *What do you do in your free time?*  
- Combina con *often / sometimes* y *because*

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U18 | like + -ing |
| U32 | play / go / do |
| U34 | and / but / because |
| **U35** | Free time activities |
| U36 | Musical instruments |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa

1. I \_\_\_\_ for a walk every evening.  
2. She \_\_\_\_ shopping on Saturdays.  
3. I like \_\_\_\_ TV.  
4. He likes \_\_\_\_ video games.  
5. We enjoy \_\_\_\_ in the park.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **go**  
2. **goes**  
3. **watching**  
4. **playing**  
5. **walking**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Elige la forma correcta

1. go / goes shopping → She \_\_\_\_ shopping.  
2. like watch / like watching → I \_\_\_\_ TV.  
3. go for a walk / go to a walk → I \_\_\_\_ every Sunday.  
4. go shopping / go to shopping → We \_\_\_\_ at weekends.  
5. enjoy walking / enjoy walk → We \_\_\_\_ in the park.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **goes**  
2. **like watching**  
3. **go for a walk**  
4. **go shopping**  
5. **enjoy walking**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Voy de paseo cada tarde.  
2. Ella va de compras los sábados.  
3. Me gusta ver la tele.  
4. Le gusta jugar a videojuegos.  
5. ¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I go for a walk every evening.**  
2. **She goes shopping on Saturdays.**  
3. **I like watching TV.**  
4. **He/She likes playing video games.**  
5. **What do you do in your free time?**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — *go* o *like + -ing*

1. I \_\_\_\_ for a walk in the park. (actividad habitual)  
2. I like \_\_\_\_ for a walk in the park. (gusto)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ shopping at weekends.  
4. They like \_\_\_\_ shopping on Saturdays.  
5. She \_\_\_\_ for a walk every day.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **go**  
2. **going**  
3. **go**  
4. **going**  
5. **goes**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de Mia (sección 7). Contesta:

1. What does Mia like in her free time?  
2. Does she like going shopping? Why / why not?  
3. What does she often watch?  
4. What does her brother like?  
5. When do they go for a walk together?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Going for a walk and watching TV**  
2. **No, because it's too busy**  
3. **Films at home**  
4. **Playing video games and walking the dog**  
5. **Sometimes at weekends in the morning**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Une con conectores (U34)

1. I like watching TV. I like playing video games. → …  
2. I don't like going shopping. It is too busy. → …  
3. I go for a walk. I don't go shopping. → …

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I like watching TV and playing video games.**  
2. **I don't like going shopping because it is too busy.**  
3. **I go for a walk but I don't go shopping.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe sobre ti

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- *go for a walk* y *go shopping*  
- 2 × *like / enjoy + -ing*  
- 1 adverbio de frecuencia  
- 1 *because* o *but*

**Modelo:** el texto de Mia (sección 7).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. She \_\_\_\_ shopping on Saturdays. (go / goes / going)  
2. I like \_\_\_\_ TV. (watch / watching / watches)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ for a walk every Sunday. (go / goes / going)  
4. He likes \_\_\_\_ video games. (play / playing / plays)  
5. What \_\_\_\_ you do in your free time? (do / does / are)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **goes**  
2. **watching**  
3. **go**  
4. **playing**  
5. **do**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Di en voz alta: *go for a walk / go shopping / like watching / like playing*.  
2. **3 min** — Responde 5 × *What do you do in your free time?*  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el texto de Mia.  
4. **5 min** — Combina con *often / but / because*.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *go for a walk* y *go shopping*  
- [ ] Formo *goes* con he/she  
- [ ] Uso *like / enjoy + -ing*  
- [ ] Pregunto por el free time  
- [ ] Combino con frecuencia y conectores

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Lista de 8 actividades** de tu semana y dilas con *I go… / I like…*.  
2. **Pareja:** entrevista *What do you do…?* + *How often…?*  
3. **Combina** U32: *I go swimming and I go for a walk.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 36](/curso-a1/unit-36): *Musical Instruments* (*play the piano…*).  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 35](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-35-free-time-activities-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 35 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-35).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Paseo | go for a walk |
| Compras | go shopping |
| Gustos | like / enjoy + -ing |
| Pregunta | What do you do in your free time? |
| 3.ª pers. | goes for a walk / goes shopping |
| Tip | no *go to shopping* |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 35 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-35-free-time-activities-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 35 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-35)

Continúa con la [**Unidad 36 — Instrumentos musicales**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-36-instrumentos-musicales): *play the piano*, *play the guitar*, *play the drums*.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe un párrafo de 6–8 frases sobre tu free time usando *go for a walk* o *go shopping*, más dos *like + -ing*.

Guías relacionadas:

- [Inglés para deportes](/blog/metodos/ingles-para-deportes)
- [Inglés en playas y deportes acuáticos](/blog/viajes/ingles-playas-deportes-acuaticos)
- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)

---

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- British Council — Free time activities: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/vocabulary/a1-a2-vocabulary
