title: Musical Instruments A1: play the piano, guitar, drums…
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 36 del curso A1: play the + instrumento (piano, guitar, drums, violin, flute), con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende play the + instrumento en inglés A1: piano, guitar, drums, violin y flute. Guía Unidad 36 con audios, esquemas y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema play the + instrumento musical en inglés A1

faqs.question: ¿Se dice play piano o play the piano?
faqs.answer: En inglés británico A1 del curso usamos play the + instrumento: play the piano, play the guitar, play the drums.

faqs.question: ¿Play football y play the guitar son iguales?
faqs.answer: No. Con deportes de pelota: play football (sin the). Con instrumentos: play the guitar (con the).

faqs.question: ¿Cómo pregunto si alguien toca un instrumento?
faqs.answer: Do you play the piano? / Can you play the violin? Yes, I do. / Yes, I can.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 36?
faqs.answer: Piano, guitar, drums, violin, flute, band, practice, music, play the + instrument.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 36 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 36 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 35](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-35-free-time-activities) hablaste de tiempo libre (*go for a walk, watching TV*). En la **Unidad 36 del curso A1** (*Musical Instruments*) aprendes a hablar de **instrumentos** con la fórmula ***play the + instrument***.

Conecta con *can* de la [Unidad 31](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad) y con *play* de la [Unidad 32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do) (¡ojo con *the*!). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 36 — Musical Instruments](/curso-a1/unit-36)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 35 — Free Time](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-35-free-time-activities) · [Unidad 31 — Can](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 36 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***play the*** + instrumento.
- Nombrar: ***piano, guitar, drums, violin, flute***.
- Formar 3.ª persona: *She **plays** the guitar*.
- Combinar con ***can***: *Can you play the violin?*
- Hablar de música en familia (texto de Noah).

---

## 1. La regla *play the + instrument*

| Patrón | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **play the** + instrument | I play **the** piano. |
| he/she **plays the** + instrument | She plays **the** guitar. |
| **can play the** + instrument | He can play **the** flute. |

![Esquema play the A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/a1-unit36-play-the.png)

```
play the piano
play the guitar
play the drums
play the violin
play the flute
```

### Tip clave: *the*

Con instrumentos musicales en A1 (estilo británico del curso): **casi siempre *the***.

| ✅ | ❌ (A1 del curso) |
| :--- | :--- |
| play the piano | play piano |
| play the guitar | play a guitar |
| play the drums | play drums |

---

## 2. Contraste: deportes vs instrumentos

En la U32 viste *play football* **sin** *the*. Aquí es al revés:

| Tipo | Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Deporte (pelota) | play + sport | play football, play tennis |
| Instrumento | play **the** + instrument | play **the** guitar |

> I **play football** on Saturdays.  
> I **play the piano** every evening.

No mezcles: *play the football* ❌ · *play guitar* ❌ (en este curso).

---

## 3. Vocabulario: cinco instrumentos

![Vocabulario instrumentos A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/a1-unit36-instruments-vocab.png)

| Inglés | Español | Tipo (extra) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **piano** | piano | teclado |
| **guitar** | guitarra | cuerda |
| **drums** | batería | percusión (plural) |
| **violin** | violín | cuerda + arco |
| **flute** | flauta | viento |

### *Drums* es plural

Decimos ***the drums*** (no *the drum* en A1 habitual):

> He plays **the drums** in a band.

---

## 4. Ejemplos con audio

> I **play the piano**.  
> She **plays the guitar**.  
> He **plays the drums**.  
> We **play the violin**.  
> They **play the flute**.  
> I **play the piano and the guitar**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/play-the-piano.mp3" title="🔊 I play the piano"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/plays-the-guitar.mp3" title="🔊 She plays the guitar"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/plays-the-drums.mp3" title="🔊 He plays the drums"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/play-the-violin.mp3" title="🔊 We play the violin"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/play-the-flute.mp3" title="🔊 They play the flute"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/play-piano-and-guitar.mp3" title="🔊 I play the piano and the guitar"></audio>

### Más frases de la familia de Noah

> My sister **plays the violin**. She is very good.  
> My brother **plays the drums** in a band.  
> We sometimes **play** together at home.  
> My mum **can play the flute** but she doesn't practice often.  
> Music is important in our family.  
> I started when I was eight.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/sister-plays-violin.mp3" title="🔊 My sister plays the violin. She is very good"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/brother-drums-band.mp3" title="🔊 My brother plays the drums in a band"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/sometimes-play-together.mp3" title="🔊 We sometimes play together at home"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/mum-flute-practice.mp3" title="🔊 My mum can play the flute but she doesn't practice often"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/music-important.mp3" title="🔊 Music is important in our family"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/started-when-eight.mp3" title="🔊 I started when I was eight"></audio>

---

## 5. Combinar con *can* (U31)

> **Can** you **play** the violin?  
> He **can play** the flute.  
> She **can play** the violin.  
> My mum **can play** the flute.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/can-you-play-violin.mp3" title="🔊 Can you play the violin?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/he-can-play-flute.mp3" title="🔊 He can play the flute"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/she-can-play-violin.mp3" title="🔊 She can play the violin"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/can-play-the-flute.mp3" title="🔊 My mum can play the flute"></audio>

### *Do you play…?* vs *Can you play…?*

| Pregunta | Matiz A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Do you play** the piano? | ¿Lo tocas (hábito / sí o no)? |
| **Can you play** the piano? | ¿Sabes tocarlo (habilidad)? |

Ambas son útiles. Respuestas:

> Yes, I do. / No, I don't.  
> Yes, I can. / No, I can't.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/do-you-play.mp3" title="🔊 Do you play the piano?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/yes-i-play.mp3" title="🔊 Yes, I play the guitar"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/i-dont-play.mp3" title="🔊 No, I don't play any instruments"></audio>

---

## 6. Vocabulario extra útil

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| band | grupo / banda | in a band |
| practice | practicar | she doesn't practice often |
| music | música | Music is important. |
| together | juntos | play together |
| start | empezar | I started when I was eight. |
| good (at) | bueno/a | She is very good. |

---

## 7. Reading modelo: Noah

![Familia musical de Noah A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/a1-unit36-noah-family.png)

> My name is Noah. I play **the piano** and **the guitar**. I started when I was eight. My sister plays **the violin**. She is very good. My brother plays **the drums** in a band. We sometimes play together at home. My mum can play **the flute** but she doesn't practice often. Music is important in our family.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-36/noah-intro.mp3" title="🔊 My name is Noah. I play the piano and the guitar"></audio>

### Comprueba

1. ¿Qué toca Noah? → **The piano and the guitar**.  
2. ¿Cuándo empezó? → **When he was eight**.  
3. ¿Qué toca su hermana? → **The violin**.  
4. ¿Dónde toca la batería su hermano? → **In a band**.  
5. ¿Qué puede tocar su madre? → **The flute** (pero no practica a menudo).

Cuenta los *the*: verás que **cada instrumento** lo lleva.

---

## 8. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** Do you play the piano?  
> **B:** Yes, I do — and the guitar. And you?  
> **A:** I can play the flute, but I don't practice often.  
> **B:** Nice! Does your sister play an instrument?  
> **A:** Yes, she plays the violin. She's very good.  
> **B:** My brother plays the drums in a band.  
> **A:** Cool. We sometimes play together at home.

---

## 9. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I play piano* | *I play **the** piano* | *the* + instrumento |
| *I play a guitar* | *I play **the** guitar* | No *a* en A1 del curso |
| *She play the violin* | *She **plays** the violin* | 3.ª persona |
| *play the football* | *play football* | Deporte ≠ instrumento |
| *He plays the drum* | *He plays **the drums*** | Plural habitual |
| *Can you plays…?* | *Can you **play**…?* | Tras *can* → base |

---

## 9b. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **piano** | *pi-A-nou* (3 sílabas). |
| **guitar** | *gui-TAR* (acento al final). |
| **drums** | *dramz*. |
| **violin** | *vai-o-LIN*. |
| **flute** | *fluut*. |
| **the** | /ðə/ antes de consonante: *the piano*. |

Practica: *the piano → the guitar → the drums → the violin → the flute*.

---

## 9c. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Do you play the guitar?  
> **B:** Yes, I play the guitar and the piano.  
> **A:** Can you play the drums?  
> **B:** No, I can't — but my brother can.

> **A:** What does your sister play?  
> **B:** She plays the violin. She's very good.  
> **A:** And your mum?  
> **B:** She can play the flute but she doesn't practice often.

> **A:** Do you play any instruments?  
> **B:** No, I don't play any instruments.  
> **A:** Do you like music?  
> **B:** Yes — music is important to me.

Cambia solo el instrumento: fijas ***play the***.

---

## 9d. Plantillas para copiar

1. I play the \_\_\_\_.  
2. She / He plays the \_\_\_\_.  
3. I play the \_\_\_\_ and the \_\_\_\_.  
4. Can you play the \_\_\_\_?  
5. My brother plays the drums in a band.  
6. We sometimes play together at home.  
7. Do you play the piano? — Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

### Más frases para memorizar

> I play the piano.  
> She plays the guitar.  
> He plays the drums.  
> We play the violin.  
> They play the flute.  
> I play the piano and the guitar.  
> My mum can play the flute.  
> Can you play the violin?  
> He can play the flute.  
> She can play the violin.  
> My brother plays the drums in a band.  
> My sister plays the violin. She is very good.  
> We sometimes play together at home.  
> Music is important in our family.  
> My name is Noah. I play the piano and the guitar.  
> I started when I was eight.  
> My mum can play the flute but she doesn't practice often.  
> Do you play the piano?  
> Yes, I play the guitar.  
> No, I don't play any instruments.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego habla de **tu** familia musical (o inventa una).

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di los 5 instrumentos con *the*.  
2. Di 3 frases *I play the…*.  
3. Di 2 con *plays*.  
4. Pregunta *Can you play the…?* y responde.

Si lo unes a U33: *I often play the piano. She sometimes plays the violin.*

### Combinar U31 + U32 + U36

| Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Deporte | I play football. |
| Instrumento | I play **the** guitar. |
| Habilidad | I **can** play the piano. |
| Free time | In my free time I play the guitar. |

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> I play the piano and the guitar. My sister plays the violin. My brother plays the drums. My mum can play the flute. We sometimes play together at home. Music is important in our family.

Cambia los instrumentos y mantén ***the***.

### Tour guiado (modelo Noah)

> My name is Noah. I play the piano and the guitar. I started when I was eight. My sister plays the violin. She is very good. My brother plays the drums in a band. We sometimes play together at home. My mum can play the flute but she doesn't practice often. Music is important in our family.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tu** familia.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> Do you play the piano?  
> Yes, I play the guitar.  
> Can you play the violin?  
> She plays the flute.  
> He plays the drums in a band.  
> We sometimes play together at home.  
> Music is important in our family.  
> I don't play any instruments.

Personaliza con los instrumentos que conozcas.

### Checklist mental

- Instrumento → **play the** …  
- Deporte (pelota) → **play** … (sin *the*)  
- he/she → **plays**  
- *drums* → plural  
- *Can you play the…?*

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U31 | can / can't |
| U32 | play football (sin *the*) |
| U35 | free time |
| **U36** | play **the** + instrument |
| U37 | Talent & Skills |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Añade *the* si hace falta

1. I play \_\_\_\_ piano.  
2. She plays \_\_\_\_ guitar.  
3. I play \_\_\_\_ football.  
4. He plays \_\_\_\_ drums.  
5. They play \_\_\_\_ flute.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **the**  
2. **the**  
3. (nada)  
4. **the**  
5. **the**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa *play / plays*

1. I \_\_\_\_ the piano.  
2. She \_\_\_\_ the guitar.  
3. He \_\_\_\_ the drums.  
4. We \_\_\_\_ the violin.  
5. Can you \_\_\_\_ the flute?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **play**  
2. **plays**  
3. **plays**  
4. **play**  
5. **play**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Toco el piano.  
2. Ella toca la guitarra.  
3. Él toca la batería en un grupo.  
4. ¿Sabes tocar el violín?  
5. Mi madre puede tocar la flauta.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I play the piano.**  
2. **She plays the guitar.**  
3. **He plays the drums in a band.**  
4. **Can you play the violin?**  
5. **My mum can play the flute.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Deporte o instrumento

1. play \_\_\_\_ tennis  
2. play \_\_\_\_ piano  
3. play \_\_\_\_ football  
4. play \_\_\_\_ violin  
5. play \_\_\_\_ drums

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. (nada)  
2. **the**  
3. (nada)  
4. **the**  
5. **the**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de Noah (sección 7). Contesta:

1. What instruments does Noah play?  
2. What does his sister play?  
3. Where does his brother play the drums?  
4. Can his mum play an instrument?  
5. Do they play together?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **The piano and the guitar**  
2. **The violin**  
3. **In a band**  
4. **Yes — the flute**  
5. **Sometimes at home**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Une con conectores (U34)

1. I play the piano. I play the guitar. → …  
2. My mum can play the flute. She doesn't practice often. → …  
3. My sister plays the violin. She is very good. → …

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I play the piano and the guitar.**  
2. **My mum can play the flute but she doesn't practice often.**  
3. **My sister plays the violin and she is very good.** / *… She is very good.*
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe sobre ti / tu familia

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- 3 instrumentos con *the*  
- 1 × *plays* (3.ª persona)  
- 1 × *can play*  
- 1 pregunta *Do you…?* o *Can you…?*

**Modelo:** el texto de Noah (sección 7).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. I play \_\_\_\_ guitar. (the / a / —)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ the violin. (play / plays / playing)  
3. Can you \_\_\_\_ the flute? (play / plays / playing)  
4. He plays \_\_\_\_ drums. (the / a / —)  
5. I play \_\_\_\_ football. (the / a / —)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **the**  
2. **plays**  
3. **play**  
4. **the**  
5. **—** (nada)
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Lista en voz alta: *the piano, the guitar, the drums, the violin, the flute*.  
2. **3 min** — 5 frases *I play the…* + 3 *She/He plays…*.  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el texto de Noah.  
4. **5 min** — Mini-entrevista *Do/Can you play the…?*

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *play the* + instrumento  
- [ ] No pongo *the* con football/tennis  
- [ ] Formo *plays* con he/she  
- [ ] Uso *the drums* (plural)  
- [ ] Pregunto con *Do/Can you play…?*

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Etiquetas en casa:** pega *the piano / the guitar* en flashcards.  
2. **Pareja:** adivina el instrumento (*Do you play the…?*).  
3. **Combina** U35: *In my free time I play the guitar.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 37](/curso-a1/unit-37): *Talent & Skills* (*very well / quite well*).  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 36](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-36-instrumentos-musicales-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 36 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-36).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Fórmula | play **the** + instrument |
| Vocab | piano · guitar · drums · violin · flute |
| 3.ª pers. | plays the… |
| Habilidad | can play the… |
| Contraste | play football (sin *the*) |
| Tip | *the drums* (plural) |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 36 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-36-instrumentos-musicales-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 36 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-36)

Continúa con la [**Unidad 37 — Talent & Skills**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-37-talent-skills): *very well*, *quite well*, *not at all*.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe un párrafo de 6–8 frases sobre instrumentos en tu familia (reales o inventados), siempre con *the*.

Guías relacionadas:

- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)
- [Can / Could en inglés](/blog/gramatica/can-could-ingles)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- British Council — Musical instruments: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/vocabulary/a1-a2-vocabulary
- British Council — Articles (a/an/the): https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar

title: Habilidades en Inglés A1: Very Well, Quite Well y Práctica
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 37 del curso A1: very well, quite well, not at all y adjetivos de talento, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende a describir habilidades en inglés A1 con very well, quite well y not at all, además de creative y hardworking, con ejemplos y ejercicios.
alt: Escala very well quite well not at all para habilidades en inglés A1
keywords: very well quite well not at all

faqs.question: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre very well y quite well?
faqs.answer: Very well = muy bien (nivel alto). Quite well = bastante bien (nivel medio-bueno). Not at all = nada / en absoluto.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde va very well en la frase?
faqs.answer: Después del verbo (o del objeto): I can sing very well. She plays the piano quite well.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo uso not at all?
faqs.answer: Suele ir con can't o don't: I can't draw at all. He can't dance at all.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 37?
faqs.answer: Very well, quite well, not at all, creative, hardworking, fast, skill, talent, good at, sing, draw, cook.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 37 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 37 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 36](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-36-instrumentos-musicales) dijiste *I play the piano*. En la **Unidad 37 del curso A1** (*Talent & Skills*) aprendes a decir **cómo de bien** lo haces: ***very well***, ***quite well***, ***not at all***.

Repasas *can* de la [Unidad 31](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad) y deportes/hobbies de la [Unidad 32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 37 — Talent & Skills](/curso-a1/unit-37)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 36 — Instrumentos](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-36-instrumentos-musicales) · [Unidad 31 — Can](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 37 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***very well / quite well / not at all***.
- Colocarlos **después del verbo**.
- Describir personas: ***creative, hardworking, fast***.
- Usar ***good at + -ing***.
- Preguntar ***How well can you…?***

---

## 1. La escala de habilidad

| Expresión | Significado | Nivel |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **very well** | muy bien | alto |
| **quite well** | bastante bien | medio-alto |
| **well** | bien | básico positivo |
| **not at all** | nada / en absoluto | cero |

![Escala very well quite well not at all A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/a1-unit37-skill-levels.png)

```
very well  >  quite well  >  well  >  not at all
```

### Tip

Estas expresiones van **al final** de la idea verbal: *I can sing **very well**.* No digas *I very well can sing*.

---

## 2. *Very well* — muy bien

> I can speak English **very well**.  
> I can sing **very well**.  
> She can draw **very well**.  
> My brother can cook **very well**.  
> My sister speaks English **very well**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/speak-english-very-well.mp3" title="🔊 I can speak English very well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/can-sing-very-well.mp3" title="🔊 I can sing very well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/can-draw-very-well.mp3" title="🔊 She can draw very well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/very-well.mp3" title="🔊 Very well"></audio>

---

## 3. *Quite well* — bastante bien

> She cooks **quite well**.  
> I play the guitar **quite well**.  
> I play the piano **quite well**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/cooks-quite-well.mp3" title="🔊 She cooks quite well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/play-guitar-quite-well.mp3" title="🔊 I play the guitar quite well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/quite-well-thanks.mp3" title="🔊 Quite well, thanks"></audio>

### *Very* vs *quite*

| Frase | Matiz |
| :--- | :--- |
| I sing **very well**. | Excelente / muy alto. |
| I sing **quite well**. | Bien, pero no perfecto. |

---

## 4. *Not at all* — nada

> He can't dance **at all**.  
> I can't draw **at all**.  
> Not at all.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/cant-dance-at-all.mp3" title="🔊 He can't dance at all"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/cant-draw-at-all.mp3" title="🔊 I can't draw at all"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/not-at-all.mp3" title="🔊 Not at all"></audio>

### Patrones

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| can't + verb + **at all** | I can't swim at all. |
| don't / doesn't + verb + **well** | They don't sing well. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/dont-sing-well.mp3" title="🔊 They don't sing well"></audio>

Con *not at all* el foco es **cero habilidad**. Con *don't … well* es “no lo hago bien” (puede ser un poco, pero mal).

---

## 5. Adjetivos: *creative, hardworking, fast…*

![Vocabulario skills A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/a1-unit37-skills-vocab.png)

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| creative | creativo/a | He is creative. |
| hardworking | trabajador/a | She is hardworking. |
| fast | rápido/a | He can run very fast. |
| slow | lento/a | I'm slow at maths. |
| skill | habilidad | We have different skills. |
| talent | talento | She has a talent for music. |
| good at | bueno/a en | She is good at drawing. |
| bad at | malo/a en | I'm bad at dancing. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/brother-cook-creative.mp3" title="🔊 My brother can cook very well — he is creative"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/sister-hardworking.mp3" title="🔊 My sister is hardworking and she speaks English very well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/she-is-creative.mp3" title="🔊 She is creative — she paints beautifully"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/he-works-hard.mp3" title="🔊 He works hard"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/good-at-drawing.mp3" title="🔊 She is good at drawing"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/can-run-very-fast.mp3" title="🔊 He can run very fast"></audio>

### *Good at + -ing*

> She is **good at drawing**.  
> He is **good at cooking**.  
> I'm **bad at dancing**.

Tras *good at / bad at* → **verbo + -ing** (como *like + -ing* en U18).

---

## 6. Preguntar *How well…?*

> **How well** can you cook?  
> Very well. / Quite well, thanks. / Not at all.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/how-well-do-you.mp3" title="🔊 How well can you cook?"></audio>

### Mini-tabla de respuestas

| Pregunta | Respuesta |
| :--- | :--- |
| How well can you sing? | Very well. |
| How well do you play the piano? | Quite well. |
| How well can you draw? | Not at all. / I can't draw at all. |

---

## 7. Reading modelo: Lisa

![Familia de Lisa y sus skills A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/a1-unit37-lisa-family.png)

> My name is Lisa. I can sing **very well** and I play the piano **quite well**. My brother can cook **very well** — he is **creative**. I can't draw **at all**. My sister is **hardworking** and she speaks English **very well**. We all have different **skills**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/lisa-intro.mp3" title="🔊 My name is Lisa. I can sing very well and I play the piano quite well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-37/different-skills.mp3" title="🔊 We all have different skills"></audio>

### Comprueba

1. ¿Canta Lisa bien? → **Very well**.  
2. ¿Cómo toca el piano? → **Quite well**.  
3. ¿Quién cocina muy bien? → **Her brother** (creative).  
4. ¿Sabe dibujar? → **Not at all**.  
5. ¿Cómo es su hermana? → **Hardworking**; speaks English very well.

---

## 8. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** How well can you sing?  
> **B:** Very well — and I play the piano quite well. And you?  
> **A:** I can't sing at all! But my brother can cook very well.  
> **B:** Is he creative?  
> **A:** Yes, he is. My sister is hardworking and she speaks English very well.  
> **B:** Nice. We all have different skills.

---

## 9. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I very well can sing* | *I can sing **very well*** | Adv. al final |
| *I can to sing very well* | *I can **sing** very well* | Sin *to* tras *can* |
| *She is good at draw* | *She is good at **drawing*** | *good at + -ing* |
| *I can't draw not at all* | *I can't draw **at all*** | Un solo negativo |
| *quite very well* | *very well* **o** *quite well* | No combines ambos |

---

## 9b. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **very well** | *VE-ri wel* — une las dos palabras. |
| **quite well** | *kwait wel*. |
| **at all** | *ət OL* (acento en *all*). |
| **creative** | *kri-EI-tiv*. |
| **hardworking** | *HARD-wer-king*. |

Practica la escala: *very well → quite well → not at all*.

---

## 9c. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** How well can you cook?  
> **B:** Quite well, thanks.  
> **A:** Can you draw?  
> **B:** Not at all.

> **A:** Does she sing well?  
> **B:** Yes — very well.  
> **A:** And the piano?  
> **B:** She plays the piano quite well.

> **A:** Is your brother creative?  
> **B:** Yes. He can cook very well.  
> **A:** Is your sister hardworking?  
> **B:** Yes — and she speaks English very well.

Cambia solo la habilidad: fijas ***very well / quite well / not at all***.

---

## 9d. Plantillas para copiar

1. I can \_\_\_\_ very well.  
2. I \_\_\_\_ quite well.  
3. I can't \_\_\_\_ at all.  
4. She / He is creative / hardworking.  
5. She is good at \_\_\_\_ing.  
6. How well can you \_\_\_\_?  
7. We all have different skills.

### Más frases para memorizar

> I can speak English very well.  
> She cooks quite well.  
> He can't dance at all.  
> I play the guitar quite well.  
> They don't sing well.  
> I can sing very well.  
> She can draw very well.  
> I can't draw at all.  
> My brother can cook very well — he is creative.  
> My sister is hardworking and she speaks English very well.  
> She is good at drawing.  
> He can run very fast.  
> My name is Lisa. I can sing very well and I play the piano quite well.  
> We all have different skills.  
> How well can you cook?  
> Quite well, thanks.  
> Not at all.  
> Very well.  
> She is creative — she paints beautifully.  
> He works hard.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego escribe **tus** skills con la escala completa.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 2 frases *very well*.  
2. Di 2 *quite well*.  
3. Di 2 *not at all* / *can't … at all*.  
4. Di 1 *good at + -ing* y 1 adjetivo (*creative / hardworking*).

Si lo unes a U36: *I play the piano quite well. She plays the violin very well.*

### Combinar U31 + U36 + U37

| Unidad | Aporta | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U31 | can / can't | I can sing |
| U36 | play the + instrument | I play the piano |
| **U37** | degree | …**very well** / **quite well** |

Modelo: *I can play the piano quite well. I can't draw at all.*

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> I can sing very well. I play the piano quite well. My brother can cook very well — he is creative. I can't draw at all. My sister is hardworking and she speaks English very well. We all have different skills.

Cambia las habilidades y mantén la escala.

### Tour guiado (modelo Lisa)

> My name is Lisa. I can sing very well and I play the piano quite well. My brother can cook very well — he is creative. I can't draw at all. My sister is hardworking and she speaks English very well. We all have different skills.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tu** familia.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> How well can you cook?  
> Very well.  
> Quite well, thanks.  
> Not at all.  
> I can sing very well.  
> I play the guitar quite well.  
> I can't dance at all.  
> She is good at drawing.  
> He is creative.  
> She is hardworking.

Personaliza con tus talentos reales.

### Checklist mental

- Escala: very well → quite well → not at all  
- Posición: **después** del verbo  
- *can't … at all*  
- *good at + -ing*  
- Adjetivos: creative, hardworking, fast  

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U31 | can / can't |
| U36 | play the + instrument |
| **U37** | very well / quite well / not at all |
| U38 | Asking for Permission |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige el nivel

1. I can sing \_\_\_\_. (muy bien)  
2. She cooks \_\_\_\_. (bastante bien)  
3. He can't dance \_\_\_\_. (nada)  
4. I play the guitar \_\_\_\_. (bastante bien)  
5. They don't sing \_\_\_\_. (bien)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **very well**  
2. **quite well**  
3. **at all**  
4. **quite well**  
5. **well**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Ordena

1. very well / I / can / sing  
2. quite well / she / cooks  
3. at all / he / can't / dance  
4. drawing / she / is / good at  
5. fast / he / can / run / very

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I can sing very well.**  
2. **She cooks quite well.**  
3. **He can't dance at all.**  
4. **She is good at drawing.**  
5. **He can run very fast.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Puedo cantar muy bien.  
2. Cocina bastante bien.  
3. No sé dibujar nada.  
4. Es creativo.  
5. Es trabajadora y habla inglés muy bien.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I can sing very well.**  
2. **She/He cooks quite well.**  
3. **I can't draw at all.**  
4. **He/She is creative.**  
5. **She is hardworking and she speaks English very well.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — *Good at* o *very well*

1. She is good at \_\_\_\_. (draw)  
2. She can draw \_\_\_\_.  
3. He is good at \_\_\_\_. (cook)  
4. He can cook \_\_\_\_.  
5. I'm bad at \_\_\_\_. (dance)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **drawing**  
2. **very well** / **quite well**  
3. **cooking**  
4. **very well** / **quite well**  
5. **dancing**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de Lisa (sección 7). Contesta:

1. How well can Lisa sing?  
2. How well does she play the piano?  
3. Who is creative?  
4. Can Lisa draw?  
5. How well does her sister speak English?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Very well**  
2. **Quite well**  
3. **Her brother**  
4. **No — not at all**  
5. **Very well**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Une con conectores (U34)

1. I can sing very well. I play the piano quite well. → …  
2. My brother can cook very well. He is creative. → …  
3. I can't draw. (nada) → …

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I can sing very well and I play the piano quite well.**  
2. **My brother can cook very well — he is creative.** / *…because he is creative.*  
3. **I can't draw at all.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe sobre ti

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- *very well*, *quite well*, *not at all*  
- 1 adjetivo (*creative / hardworking / fast*)  
- 1 × *good at + -ing*  
- 1 pregunta *How well…?*

**Modelo:** el texto de Lisa (sección 7).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. I can sing \_\_\_\_. (very well / well very / at all)  
2. He can't dance \_\_\_\_. (very well / at all / quite)  
3. She is good at \_\_\_\_. (draw / drawing / draws)  
4. How well \_\_\_\_ you cook? (can / cans / are)  
5. She cooks \_\_\_\_. (quite well / well quite / quite)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **very well**  
2. **at all**  
3. **drawing**  
4. **can**  
5. **quite well**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Escala en voz alta: very well → quite well → not at all.  
2. **3 min** — 6 frases con *can* + grado.  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el texto de Lisa.  
4. **5 min** — Entrevista *How well can you…?* × 6.

### Checklist

- [ ] Distingo very well / quite well / not at all  
- [ ] Los pongo después del verbo  
- [ ] Uso *can't … at all*  
- [ ] Uso *good at + -ing*  
- [ ] Describo con creative / hardworking

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Tabla personal:** 3 skills *very well*, 3 *quite well*, 3 *not at all*.  
2. **Pareja:** *How well can you…?* + respuesta corta.  
3. **Combina** U36: *I play the guitar quite well.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 38](/curso-a1/unit-38): *Asking for Permission* (*Can I…? / May I…?*).  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 37](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-37-talent-skills-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 37 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-37).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Alto | very well |
| Medio | quite well |
| Cero | not at all |
| Posición | después del verbo |
| Persona | creative · hardworking |
| Tip | good at + -ing |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 37 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-37-talent-skills-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 37 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-37)

Continúa con la [**Unidad 38 — Pedir permiso**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso): *Can I…?*, *May I…?*, *please*, *of course*.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe un párrafo de 6–8 frases sobre tus skills usando los tres niveles de la escala.

Guías relacionadas:

- [Can / Could en inglés](/blog/gramatica/can-could-ingles)
- [Verbos modales: guía](/blog/gramatica/verbos-modales-ingles-guia)
- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- British Council — Can / ability: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar/can-cant
- British Council — Describing people: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/vocabulary/a1-a2-vocabulary

title: Asking for Permission A1: Can I…? y May I…?
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 38 del curso A1: Can I…? y May I…? para pedir permiso, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende a pedir permiso en inglés A1 con Can I…? y May I…?, más please, excuse me y of course. Guía Unidad 38 con audios, esquemas y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema Can I y May I para pedir permiso en inglés A1

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre Can I y May I?
faqs.answer: Ambos piden permiso. Can I…? es más informal y frecuente. May I…? suena más formal (clase, trabajo, situaciones educadas).

faqs.question: ¿Cómo respondo a Can I…?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can. / No, you can't. También Of course. o Sorry, not right now.

faqs.question: ¿Can I have…? es lo mismo que Can I use…?
faqs.answer: Ambos usan Can I, pero Can I have…? (U16) suele pedir algo en un pedido; Can I use / borrow…? pide permiso para hacer o usar algo.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 38?
faqs.answer: Can I, May I, please, excuse me, of course, borrow, use, open, sit, ask a question, bathroom, pen, permission.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 38 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 38 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 37](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-37-talent-skills) dijiste *cómo de bien* haces algo (*I can sing very well*). En la **Unidad 38 del curso A1** (*Asking for Permission*) usas ***Can I…?*** y ***May I…?*** para **pedir permiso**.

Conecta con *can* de la [Unidad 31](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad) y con *Can I have…?* de la [cafetería (U16)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-16-cafeteria-can-i-have-id-like). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 38 — Asking for Permission](/curso-a1/unit-38)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 37 — Talent & Skills](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-37-talent-skills) · [Unidad 31 — Can](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 38 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Pedir permiso con ***Can I…?*** (informal).
- Pedir permiso con ***May I…?*** (más formal).
- Responder: ***Yes, you can / No, you can't / Of course***.
- Usar frases educadas: ***please, excuse me, thank you***.
- Pedir en clase y en el trabajo: *borrow a pen, ask a question, come in…*.

---

## 1. Dos fórmulas, mismo objetivo

| Fórmula | Registro | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Can I** + verb…? | informal / cotidiano | Can I use the bathroom? |
| **May I** + verb…? | más formal / educado | May I ask a question? |

![Esquema Can I May I A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/a1-unit38-can-may.png)

```
Can I + base verb…?
May I + base verb…?
→ Yes, you can. / No, you can't. / Of course.
```

### Tip

Tras *Can I / May I* va el **verbo en forma base** (sin *-s*, sin *to*): *open, borrow, use, sit, ask*.

---

## 2. *Can I…?* — permiso informal

> **Can I** use the bathroom?  
> **Can I** borrow your pen?  
> **Can I** use the phone?  
> **Can I** sit here?  
> **Can I** please use the computer?  
> **Can I** borrow your eraser?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-use-bathroom.mp3" title="🔊 Can I use the bathroom?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-borrow-pen.mp3" title="🔊 Can I borrow your pen?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-use-phone.mp3" title="🔊 Can I use the phone?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-sit-here.mp3" title="🔊 Can I sit here?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-please-computer.mp3" title="🔊 Can I please use the computer?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-borrow-eraser.mp3" title="🔊 Can I borrow your eraser?"></audio>

### Tres usos de *can* (no los mezcles)

| Unidad | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U31 | habilidad | Can you swim? |
| U16 | pedido | Can I have a coffee? |
| **U38** | permiso | Can I use the bathroom? |

---

## 3. *May I…?* — más formal

> **May I** open the door?  
> **May I** come in?  
> **May I** ask a question?  
> Excuse me, **may I** come in?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/may-i-open-door.mp3" title="🔊 May I open the door?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/may-i-come-in.mp3" title="🔊 May I come in?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/may-i-ask-question.mp3" title="🔊 May I ask a question?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/excuse-me-come-in.mp3" title="🔊 Excuse me, may I come in?"></audio>

### ¿Cuándo usar *May I*?

- En **clase** con el profesor.  
- En el **trabajo** o con desconocidos.  
- Cuando quieres sonar **más educado**.

En conversación cotidiana, *Can I…?* es perfectamente correcto.

### Extra A1: *Could I…?*

Más suave/educado que *Can I*:

> **Could I** please open the window?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/could-i-please.mp3" title="🔊 Could I please open the window?"></audio>

---

## 4. Respuestas

| Respuesta | Significado |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Yes, you can.** | Sí, puedes. |
| **No, you can't.** | No, no puedes. |
| **No, you can't right now.** | Ahora no. |
| **Of course.** | Por supuesto. |
| **Of course. Here you are.** | Claro. Aquí tienes. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/yes-you-can.mp3" title="🔊 Yes, you can"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/no-you-cant.mp3" title="🔊 No, you can't right now"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/of-course.mp3" title="🔊 Of course. Here you are"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/of-course-short.mp3" title="🔊 Of course"></audio>

---

## 5. Frases educadas

![Frases educadas A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/a1-unit38-polite-phrases.png)

| Inglés | Español | Uso |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| please | por favor | Can I **please**…? |
| excuse me | perdón / con permiso | para llamar la atención |
| of course | por supuesto | respuesta positiva |
| thank you | gracias | después del permiso |
| borrow | pedir prestado | borrow your pen |
| permission | permiso | ask for permission |
| right now | ahora mismo | not right now |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/excuse-me-borrow.mp3" title="🔊 Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/please-and-thank-you.mp3" title="🔊 Please and thank you"></audio>

### Verbos útiles de petición

| Verbo | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| use | Can I use the bathroom / phone / computer? |
| borrow | Can I borrow your pen / eraser / book? |
| open | May I open the door / window? |
| sit | Can I sit here? |
| ask | May I ask a question? |
| come in | May I come in? |

---

## 6. En clase y en el trabajo

![Escenas de permiso A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/a1-unit38-permission-scenes.png)

> In class we use polite phrases.  
> At work we say please and thank you.  
> When we ask for permission we are polite.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/in-class-polite.mp3" title="🔊 In class we use polite phrases"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/at-work-please.mp3" title="🔊 At work we say please and thank you"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/when-ask-permission.mp3" title="🔊 When we ask for permission we are polite"></audio>

### Mini-guía rápida

| Situación | Frase modelo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Baño (clase) | Can I use the bathroom? |
| Pregunta (clase) | May I ask a question? |
| Entrar | Excuse me, may I come in? |
| Bolígrafo | Excuse me — can I borrow your pen? |
| Ordenador | Can I please use the computer? |

---

## 7. Reading modelo

> In class we use polite phrases. **Can I** use the bathroom? **May I** ask a question? At work we say **please** and **thank you**. **Excuse me** — can I borrow your pen? **Of course**. When we ask for **permission** we are polite.

### Comprueba

1. ¿Dónde se usan primero las frases educadas? → **In class**.  
2. Ejemplo de baño → **Can I use the bathroom?**  
3. Ejemplo de pregunta → **May I ask a question?**  
4. ¿Qué se dice en el trabajo? → **Please and thank you**.  
5. Respuesta a *borrow your pen* → **Of course**.

---

## 8. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?  
> **B:** Of course. Here you are.  
> **A:** Thank you! May I ask a question?  
> **B:** Yes, you can.  
> **A:** Can I use the bathroom?  
> **B:** Yes, you can.  
> **A:** And later… may I come in after the break?  
> **B:** Of course.

---

## 9. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *Can I to use…?* | *Can I **use**…?* | Sin *to* |
| *Can I using…?* | *Can I **use**…?* | Forma base |
| *Yes, I can.* (como permiso a otro) | *Yes, **you** can.* | Respondes al oyente |
| *May I opens…?* | *May I **open**…?* | Sin *-s* |
| *Borrow me your pen* | *Can I **borrow your** pen?* | Estructura inglesa |

---

## 9b. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Can I** | a menudo /kən aɪ/ débil. |
| **May I** | *mei aɪ*. |
| **borrow** | *BO-rou*. |
| **excuse me** | *ik-SKIUZ mi*. |
| **of course** | *əv KORS*. |

Practica: *Can I…? → May I…? → Of course.*

---

## 9c. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Can I use the bathroom?  
> **B:** Yes, you can.  
> **A:** May I ask a question?  
> **B:** Of course.

> **A:** Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?  
> **B:** Of course. Here you are.  
> **A:** Thank you!  
> **B:** You're welcome.

> **A:** May I come in?  
> **B:** Yes, you can.  
> **A:** Can I sit here?  
> **B:** Sorry — no, you can't right now.

Cambia solo el verbo/objeto: fijas la **estructura**.

---

## 9d. Plantillas para copiar

1. Can I \_\_\_\_?  
2. May I \_\_\_\_?  
3. Excuse me — can I borrow your \_\_\_\_?  
4. Can I please use the \_\_\_\_?  
5. Yes, you can. / No, you can't. / Of course.  
6. May I ask a question?  
7. May I come in?

### Más frases para memorizar

> Can I use the bathroom?  
> May I open the door?  
> Can I borrow your pen?  
> May I come in?  
> Yes, you can.  
> No, you can't right now.  
> Can I use the phone?  
> May I ask a question?  
> Can I sit here?  
> Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?  
> Of course. Here you are.  
> Excuse me, may I come in?  
> Can I borrow your eraser?  
> Can I please use the computer?  
> Please and thank you.  
> In class we use polite phrases.  
> At work we say please and thank you.  
> When we ask for permission we are polite.  
> Of course.  
> Could I please open the window?

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego improvisa 8 peticiones de tu día (clase, casa, trabajo).

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 3 × *Can I…?*  
2. Di 3 × *May I…?*  
3. Di 3 respuestas (*Yes, you can / No, you can't / Of course*).  
4. Une con *Excuse me — …*

Si lo combinas con U16: *Can I have a coffee?* (pedido) vs *Can I use the bathroom?* (permiso).

### Combinar U16 + U31 + U38

| Uso de *can* | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Habilidad | I can swim. |
| Pedido | Can I have a tea? |
| Permiso | Can I borrow your pen? |

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> In class I say: Can I use the bathroom? May I ask a question? Excuse me — can I borrow your pen? Of course. At work we say please and thank you. When we ask for permission we are polite.

Cambia *pen → book*, *bathroom → phone*, y mantén *Can I / May I*.

### Tour guiado (modelo del reading)

> In class we use polite phrases. Can I use the bathroom? May I ask a question? At work we say please and thank you. Excuse me — can I borrow your pen? Of course. When we ask for permission we are polite.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego inventa un diálogo de 6 líneas.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> Excuse me.  
> Can I borrow your pen?  
> May I ask a question?  
> Can I sit here?  
> May I come in?  
> Yes, you can.  
> No, you can't right now.  
> Of course. Here you are.  
> Thank you.  
> Could I please open the window?

Personaliza objetos y lugares de tu rutina.

### Checklist mental

- *Can I* + verbo base  
- *May I* = más formal  
- Respuestas: *you can / you can't / of course*  
- *Excuse me* + petición  
- *please / thank you*

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U16 | Can I have…? (pedido) |
| U31 | can / can't (habilidad) |
| **U38** | Can I / May I (permiso) |
| U39 | Outdoor Activities |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa *Can / May*

1. \_\_\_\_ I use the bathroom? (informal)  
2. \_\_\_\_ I ask a question? (formal / clase)  
3. \_\_\_\_ I borrow your pen?  
4. \_\_\_\_ I come in? (educado)  
5. \_\_\_\_ I sit here?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Can**  
2. **May** (también *Can*)  
3. **Can**  
4. **May** (también *Can*)  
5. **Can**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Forma base del verbo

1. May I \_\_\_\_ the door? (open)  
2. Can I \_\_\_\_ your pen? (borrow)  
3. May I \_\_\_\_ a question? (ask)  
4. Can I \_\_\_\_ the phone? (use)  
5. May I \_\_\_\_ in? (come)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **open**  
2. **borrow**  
3. **ask**  
4. **use**  
5. **come**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. ¿Puedo usar el baño?  
2. ¿Puedo hacer una pregunta?  
3. ¿Puedo pedir prestado tu bolígrafo?  
4. Sí, puedes.  
5. Por supuesto. Aquí tienes.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Can I use the bathroom?**  
2. **May I ask a question?**  
3. **Can I borrow your pen?**  
4. **Yes, you can.**  
5. **Of course. Here you are.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Respuestas

1. Can I sit here? → \_\_\_\_ (sí)  
2. Can I use the computer now? → \_\_\_\_ (ahora no)  
3. Can I borrow your eraser? → \_\_\_\_ (por supuesto)  
4. May I come in? → \_\_\_\_ (sí)  
5. Can I open the window? → \_\_\_\_ (no)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Yes, you can.**  
2. **No, you can't right now.**  
3. **Of course.**  
4. **Yes, you can. / Of course.**  
5. **No, you can't.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de la sección 7. Contesta:

1. Where do we use polite phrases first in the text?  
2. Give one *Can I…* example.  
3. Give one *May I…* example.  
4. What do we say at work?  
5. What does *Of course* mean here?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **In class**  
2. **Can I use the bathroom?** / **Can I borrow your pen?**  
3. **May I ask a question?**  
4. **Please and thank you**  
5. **Yes / sure**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Une con *Excuse me*

1. can I borrow your pen  
2. may I come in  
3. can I pass

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?**  
2. **Excuse me, may I come in?**  
3. **Excuse me — can I pass?**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe diálogos

Escribe 2 mini-diálogos (4–6 líneas cada uno):

1. En **clase** (*May I ask…? / bathroom / borrow*).  
2. En el **trabajo** o con un desconocido (*Excuse me / please / of course*).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. Can I \_\_\_\_ the bathroom? (use / uses / using)  
2. May I \_\_\_\_ a question? (ask / asks / asking)  
3. Yes, \_\_\_\_ can. (you / I / we)  
4. \_\_\_\_ me — can I borrow your pen? (Excuse / Please / Sorry)  
5. Which is more formal? (Can I / **May I** / Do I)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **use**  
2. **ask**  
3. **you**  
4. **Excuse**  
5. **May I**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — 5 × *Can I…?* + 5 × *May I…?*  
2. **3 min** — Respuestas rápidas.  
3. **4 min** — Diálogo clase + diálogo trabajo.  
4. **5 min** — Reescribe el reading con tus objetos.

### Checklist

- [ ] Formo *Can I + verbo base*  
- [ ] Uso *May I* en contextos formales  
- [ ] Respondo *you can / you can't / of course*  
- [ ] Uso *excuse me* y *please*  
- [ ] Distingo permiso (U38) de habilidad (U31) y pedido (U16)

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Lista del día:** 8 cosas para las que pediste (o pedirías) permiso.  
2. **Pareja:** uno pide, el otro concede o niega.  
3. **Combina** U16: *Can I have…?* vs *Can I use…?*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 39](/curso-a1/unit-39): *Outdoor Activities*.  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 38](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 38 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-38).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Informal | Can I + verb…? |
| Formal | May I + verb…? |
| Sí | Yes, you can. / Of course. |
| No | No, you can't. |
| Educación | please · excuse me · thank you |
| Tip | verbo en forma base |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 38 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 38 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-38)

Continúa con la [**Unidad 39 — Outdoor Activities**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-39-outdoor-activities): *I'm going camping*, *hiking*, *cycling*, *fishing*.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe 10 frases de permiso reales (casa, clase, trabajo) con *Can I* y *May I*.

Guías relacionadas:

- [Can / Could en inglés](/blog/gramatica/can-could-ingles)
- [May / Might en inglés](/blog/gramatica/may-might-ingles)
- [Verbos modales: guía](/blog/gramatica/verbos-modales-ingles-guia)

---

## Fuentes

- British Council — Making requests: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/skills/speaking

title: Outdoor Activities A1: Actividades y Planes
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 39 del curso A1: actividades al aire libre y Present Continuous para planes, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende outdoor activities en inglés A1 y usa el present continuous para hablar de camping, hiking, cycling y fishing, con vocabulario y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema Present Continuous para planes outdoor en inglés A1

faqs.question: ¿Cómo hablo de planes futuros en A1 con outdoor activities?
faqs.answer: Con Present Continuous + marcador de futuro: I'm going camping next week. She is going hiking on Saturday.

faqs.question: ¿Es lo mismo que el Present Continuous de ropa (U29)?
faqs.answer: Misma forma (am/is/are + -ing), distinto uso: U29 describe ahora (ropa); U39 habla de planes ya decididos para el futuro cercano.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario outdoor practico?
faqs.answer: Hiking, camping, cycling, fishing, tent, backpack, trail, mountains, outdoor, next week, tomorrow.

faqs.question: ¿Se dice go camping o going camping?
faqs.answer: Para planes: I'm going camping. Para hábitos también existe I go camping every summer; en esta unidad priorizamos going + activity para planes.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 39 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 39 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 38](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso) pediste permiso (*Can I…?*). En la **Unidad 39 del curso A1** (*Outdoor Activities*) hablas de **planes al aire libre** con ***Present Continuous***: *I'm going camping next week*.

Repasas la forma de la [Unidad 29](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-29-ropa-present-continuous) y *go + -ing* de la [Unidad 32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 39 — Outdoor Activities](/curso-a1/unit-39)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 38 — Pedir permiso](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso) · [Unidad 29 — Present Continuous](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-29-ropa-present-continuous)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 39 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***am / is / are + going + activity*** para planes.
- Hablar de ***camping, hiking, cycling, fishing***.
- Usar marcadores: ***tomorrow, on Saturday, next week, next weekend***.
- Preguntar: ***What are you doing next weekend?***
- Describir planes familiares outdoor.

---

## 1. Present Continuous para planes futuros

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| I **'m going** + activity | I'm going camping next week. |
| She / He **is going** + activity | She is going hiking on Saturday. |
| We / They **are going** + activity | We are going cycling tomorrow. |

![Present Continuous planes A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/a1-unit39-present-continuous-plans.png)

```
am / is / are + going + camping / hiking / cycling / fishing
+ tomorrow / on Saturday / next week / next weekend
```

### Tip

No es “ahora mismo”: es un **plan ya decidido**. La clave está en el tiempo futuro (*next week*, *tomorrow*…).

Con un marcador claro, el oyente entiende que hablas del futuro aunque la forma sea Present Continuous. Sin marcador (*I'm going camping*), a veces suena a “ahora / en camino”; por eso en A1 conviene añadir **cuándo**.

### Marcadores de tiempo útiles

| Marcador | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| tomorrow | We're going cycling **tomorrow**. |
| on Saturday / on Sunday | She's going hiking **on Saturday**. |
| next week | I'm going camping **next week**. |
| next weekend | We're going to the mountains **next weekend**. |
| in July | They're going camping **in July**. |

Memoriza 4 marcadores y reutilízalos con las 4 actividades outdoor.

---

## 2. Ejemplos con audio

> **I'm going camping** next week.  
> She **is going hiking** on Saturday.  
> We **are going cycling** tomorrow.  
> **He's going fishing** next weekend.  
> They **are going camping** in July.  
> I **am going hiking** on Saturday.  
> We **are going cycling** next week.  
> They **are going fishing** tomorrow.  
> She **is going cycling** on Sunday.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/im-going-camping.mp3" title="🔊 I'm going camping next week"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/going-hiking-saturday.mp3" title="🔊 She is going hiking on Saturday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/going-cycling-tomorrow.mp3" title="🔊 We are going cycling tomorrow"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/hes-going-fishing.mp3" title="🔊 He's going fishing next weekend"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/going-camping-july.mp3" title="🔊 They are going camping in July"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/going-hiking-saturday-i.mp3" title="🔊 I am going hiking on Saturday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/going-cycling-next-week.mp3" title="🔊 We are going cycling next week"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/going-fishing-tomorrow.mp3" title="🔊 They are going fishing tomorrow"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/shes-going-cycling-sunday.mp3" title="🔊 She is going cycling on Sunday"></audio>

### Contraste rápido

| Uso | Ejemplo | Unidad |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Ahora (ropa) | She **is wearing** a dress. | U29 |
| Plan futuro | She **is going hiking** on Saturday. | **U39** |
| Hábito | I **go** cycling every Sunday. | U32 / Present Simple |

---

## 3. Vocabulario outdoor

![Vocabulario outdoor A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/a1-unit39-outdoor-vocab.png)

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| outdoor | al aire libre | outdoor activities |
| hiking | senderismo | going hiking |
| camping | camping / acampar | going camping |
| cycling | ir en bici | going cycling |
| fishing | pesca | going fishing |
| tent | tienda de campaña | We have a tent. |
| backpack | mochila | backpacks |
| trail | sendero | on the trail |
| mountains | montañas | to the mountains |
| next week | la próxima semana | next week |
| next weekend | el próximo fin de semana | next weekend |
| tomorrow | mañana | tomorrow |

---

## 4. Preguntas y respuestas

> **What are you doing** next weekend?  
> **I'm going hiking.**

> **Are you going camping** next week?  
> **Yes, we are.**

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/what-are-you-doing.mp3" title="🔊 What are you doing next weekend?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/im-going-hiking.mp3" title="🔊 I'm going hiking"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/are-you-going-camping.mp3" title="🔊 Are you going camping next week?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/yes-we-are.mp3" title="🔊 Yes, we are"></audio>

### Tabla de preguntas

| Pregunta | Respuesta corta |
| :--- | :--- |
| Are you going camping? | Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. |
| Is she going hiking? | Yes, she is. / No, she isn't. |
| Are they going fishing? | Yes, they are. / No, they aren't. |
| What are you doing tomorrow? | I'm going cycling. |

---

## 5. Reading modelo: planes en familia

![Familia outdoor A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/a1-unit39-family-outdoors.png)

> **I'm going camping** next week with my family. We love outdoor activities. My brother **is going hiking** on Saturday and my sister **is going cycling** on Sunday. My dad **is going fishing** tomorrow. We have a tent and backpacks. Next weekend we are all **going to the mountains**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/im-going-camping-family.mp3" title="🔊 I'm going camping next week with my family"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/love-outdoor.mp3" title="🔊 We love outdoor activities"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/brother-hiking.mp3" title="🔊 My brother is going hiking on Saturday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/sister-cycling.mp3" title="🔊 My sister is going cycling on Sunday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/dad-fishing.mp3" title="🔊 My dad is going fishing tomorrow"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/tent-backpacks.mp3" title="🔊 We have a tent and backpacks"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/going-mountains.mp3" title="🔊 Next weekend we are all going to the mountains"></audio>

### Comprueba

1. ¿Qué hace el narrador la próxima semana? → **Going camping**.  
2. ¿Con quién? → **Family**.  
3. ¿Hermano el sábado? → **Hiking**.  
4. ¿Hermana el domingo? → **Cycling**.  
5. ¿Padre mañana? → **Fishing**.  
6. ¿Próximo finde? → **To the mountains**.

---

## 6. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** What are you doing next weekend?  
> **B:** I'm going camping with my family. And you?  
> **A:** I'm going hiking on Saturday.  
> **B:** Nice! Is your sister going too?  
> **A:** No — she's going cycling on Sunday.  
> **B:** And your dad?  
> **A:** He's going fishing tomorrow. We love outdoor activities.

---

## 7. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I going camping* | *I**'m** going camping* | Falta *am* |
| *She going hiking* | *She **is** going hiking* | Falta *is* |
| *We go camping next week* (plan fijo A1) | *We **are going** camping next week* | PC para planes |
| *I'm go camping* | *I'm **going** camping* | *-ing* |
| *next week I camping* | *I'm going camping **next week*** | Orden + *going* |

---

## 8. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **I'm going** | une: *aimˈgoing*. |
| **hiking** | *HAI-king*. |
| **camping** | *KAM-ping*. |
| **cycling** | *SAI-kling*. |
| **fishing** | *FI-shing*. |
| **outdoor** | *AUT-dor*. |

Practica: *camping → hiking → cycling → fishing*.

---

## 9. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Are you going camping next week?  
> **B:** Yes, we are — with my family.  
> **A:** What are you doing on Saturday?  
> **B:** I'm going hiking.

> **A:** Is she going cycling on Sunday?  
> **B:** Yes, she is.  
> **A:** Is he going fishing tomorrow?  
> **B:** Yes — my dad loves fishing.

> **A:** What are you doing next weekend?  
> **B:** We're going to the mountains. We have a tent and backpacks.

Cambia solo el día o la actividad: fijas ***am/is/are going***.

---

## 9b. Plantillas para copiar

1. I'm going \_\_\_\_ next week.  
2. She / He is going \_\_\_\_ on \_\_\_\_.  
3. We are going \_\_\_\_ tomorrow.  
4. What are you doing next weekend?  
5. Are you going camping? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.  
6. Next weekend we are going to the mountains.

### Más frases para memorizar

> I'm going camping next week.  
> She is going hiking on Saturday.  
> We are going cycling tomorrow.  
> He's going fishing next weekend.  
> They are going camping in July.  
> I am going hiking on Saturday.  
> We are going cycling next week.  
> They are going fishing tomorrow.  
> My brother is going hiking on Saturday.  
> My sister is going cycling on Sunday.  
> My dad is going fishing tomorrow.  
> We have a tent and backpacks.  
> Next weekend we are all going to the mountains.  
> We love outdoor activities.  
> I'm going camping next week with my family.  
> What are you doing next weekend?  
> I'm going hiking.  
> Are you going camping next week?  
> Yes, we are.  
> She is going cycling on Sunday.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego escribe **tus** planes outdoor de la semana.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 4 frases *I'm going…* con actividades distintas.  
2. Di 3 con *he/she is going…*.  
3. Pregunta *What are you doing next weekend?* y responde.  
4. Añade *tent / backpack / mountains*.

Si lo unes a U33: *I'm often going hiking at weekends* (más natural: *I often go hiking* para hábitos; *I'm going hiking on Saturday* para un plan concreto).

### Combinar U29 + U32 + U39

| Unidad | Aporta | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U29 | am/is/are + -ing | form |
| U32 | go + -ing activities | go cycling |
| **U39** | plans | I'm **going** cycling **tomorrow** |

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> I'm going camping next week with my family. My brother is going hiking on Saturday. My sister is going cycling on Sunday. My dad is going fishing tomorrow. Next weekend we are going to the mountains.

Cambia días y actividades; mantén *am/is/are going*.

### Tour guiado (modelo)

> I'm going camping next week with my family. We love outdoor activities. My brother is going hiking on Saturday and my sister is going cycling on Sunday. My dad is going fishing tomorrow. We have a tent and backpacks. Next weekend we are all going to the mountains.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tus** planes.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> What are you doing next weekend?  
> I'm going camping.  
> Are you going hiking on Saturday?  
> Yes, I am.  
> She's going cycling on Sunday.  
> He's going fishing tomorrow.  
> We're going to the mountains.  
> We have a tent and backpacks.

Personaliza lugares y días reales.

### Checklist mental

- *am/is/are + going + activity*  
- Marcador de futuro (*tomorrow / next week…*)  
- Vocab: camping · hiking · cycling · fishing  
- Pregunta: *What are you doing…?*  
- Respuestas cortas: *Yes, I am / No, I'm not*

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U29 | Present Continuous (ahora) |
| U32 | go + -ing (hábitos/ocio) |
| **U39** | PC para planes outdoor |
| U40 | Module 4 Review |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa *am / is / are*

1. I \_\_\_\_ going camping next week.  
2. She \_\_\_\_ going hiking on Saturday.  
3. We \_\_\_\_ going cycling tomorrow.  
4. He \_\_\_\_ going fishing next weekend.  
5. They \_\_\_\_ going camping in July.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am** / **'m**  
2. **is**  
3. **are**  
4. **is** / **'s**  
5. **are**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Elige la actividad

1. sleeping in a tent → \_\_\_\_  
2. walking in the mountains → \_\_\_\_  
3. riding a bicycle → \_\_\_\_  
4. catching fish → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **camping**  
2. **hiking**  
3. **cycling**  
4. **fishing**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Voy de camping la próxima semana.  
2. Ella va de senderismo el sábado.  
3. Vamos en bici mañana.  
4. Él va a pescar mañana.  
5. ¿Qué haces el próximo fin de semana?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I'm going camping next week.**  
2. **She is going hiking on Saturday.**  
3. **We are going cycling tomorrow.**  
4. **He is going fishing tomorrow.**  
5. **What are you doing next weekend?**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Ordena

1. camping / I'm / next week / going  
2. hiking / is / she / on Saturday / going  
3. fishing / going / dad / is / tomorrow / my  
4. mountains / going / we / are / to the

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I'm going camping next week.**  
2. **She is going hiking on Saturday.**  
3. **My dad is going fishing tomorrow.**  
4. **We are going to the mountains.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de la sección 5. Contesta:

1. What is the writer doing next week?  
2. What is the brother doing on Saturday?  
3. What is the sister doing on Sunday?  
4. What is dad doing tomorrow?  
5. Where are they going next weekend?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Going camping (with family)**  
2. **Hiking**  
3. **Cycling**  
4. **Fishing**  
5. **To the mountains**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Preguntas sí/no

1. Are you going camping next week? → Yes, \_\_\_\_.  
2. Is she going hiking? → No, \_\_\_\_.  
3. Are they going fishing tomorrow? → Yes, \_\_\_\_.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I am** / **we are**  
2. **she isn't** / **she's not**  
3. **they are**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe tus planes

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- las 4 actividades (*camping, hiking, cycling, fishing*)  
- *tomorrow / on Saturday / next week / next weekend*  
- 1 pregunta *What are you doing…?*  
- *tent* o *backpack*

**Modelo:** el texto de la sección 5.

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. I \_\_\_\_ going camping next week. ('m / is / are)  
2. She is \_\_\_\_ hiking on Saturday. (go / going / goes)  
3. What \_\_\_\_ you doing next weekend? (are / is / do)  
4. We \_\_\_\_ going to the mountains. (are / is / am)  
5. He \_\_\_\_ going fishing tomorrow. (is / are / am)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **'m**  
2. **going**  
3. **are**  
4. **are**  
5. **is**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Di las 4 actividades con *I'm going…*.  
2. **3 min** — Cambia sujeto (*he/she/we*).  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el reading.  
4. **5 min** — Mini-entrevista *What are you doing…?*

### Checklist

- [ ] Formo *am/is/are going + activity*  
- [ ] Uso marcadores de futuro  
- [ ] Conozco hiking / camping / cycling / fishing  
- [ ] Pregunto planes con Present Continuous  
- [ ] Distingo hábito (I go…) vs plan (I'm going…)

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Agenda de la semana:** un plan outdoor por día en inglés.  
2. **Pareja:** planes del finde + preguntas sí/no.  
3. **Combina** U32: *I go cycling every Sunday* vs *I'm going cycling tomorrow*.  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 40](/curso-a1/unit-40): *Module 4 Review*.  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 39](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-39-outdoor-activities-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 39 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-39).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Forma | am/is/are + going + activity |
| Uso | planes futuros decididos |
| Vocab | camping · hiking · cycling · fishing |
| Tiempo | tomorrow · next week · on Saturday |
| Pregunta | What are you doing…? |
| Tip | no olvides *am/is/are* |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 39 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-39-outdoor-activities-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 39 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-39)

En la **Unidad 40** harás el **repaso del Módulo 4** (*Abilities & Interests*): *can*, *play/go/do*, frecuencia, conectores, free time, instrumentos, skills y permiso.

Guía dedicada:

- [Unidad 40 — Repaso Módulo 4](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-40-repaso-modulo-4)

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe un párrafo de 6–8 frases con tus planes outdoor de la próxima semana.

Guías relacionadas:

- [Inglés para naturaleza y senderismo](/blog/viajes/mochileros-ingles-naturaleza-senderismo-seguridad)
- [Inglés en playas y deportes acuáticos](/blog/viajes/ingles-playas-deportes-acuaticos)
- [Inglés para deportes](/blog/metodos/ingles-para-deportes)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- British Council — Present continuous (future): https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar/present-continuous
- British Council — Free time / outdoor: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/vocabulary/a1-a2-vocabulary
